children.translated_text: Composed by <s>Ratnākaraśānti</s>
The commentary called <s>Sāratamā</s> on the Noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom in Eight Thousand Lines)

body.text: 1. sarvākārajñatācaryāparivarto nāma prathamaḥ //
body.translated_text: 1. The chapter called the Practice of Omniscience in All Aspects is the first.

body.text: namaḥ sarvabuddhabodhisattvebhyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Homage to all <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>!

children.translated_text: He whose [light] in the world, though the suns are many, is superior,
with prosperity at the rise of day, and night at [its] setting;
whose lineage, spreading to every object, is endowed with purity (?),
may the <s>Buddha</s>-awakening of that treasure of the guru's qualities arise for you!

body.text: .............namaḥ śaraṇaṃ daśabalāste vā (?) //
body.translated_text: ............Homage, I take refuge in the <s>Daśabala</s> (Ten-Powered One), or those (?)

body.text:
yasyāḥ katipayavarṇā dhṛtāḥ karṇapuṭairapi /
bodherbhavanti bījāni jinamātā pyatyasau /

children.translated_text: For the Lord <s>Maitreya</s>, the ship that is the ornament in the ocean of her meaning,
has been determined by [commentaries] equal in form to the extensive version, through her own portions;

children.text: vyācaṣṭe vacasā sphuṭena laghunā mando 'pi ratnākāraḥ
children.translated_text: even the slow-witted <s>Ratnākara</s> expounds with clear and concise words
that <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>... of the great ones... that <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā</s> (Eight Thousand).

body.translated_text:
She whose few syllables, even [merely] held in the hollows of the ears,
become seeds of awakening — she is the Mother of the <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones), and she surpasses [all];

body.text: atha kasmādiyaṃ vyākhyāyate?
body.translated_text: Now, why is this [text] commented upon?

body.text: sūtraṃ geyaṃ vyākaraṇaṃ gāthā udānaṃ nidānaṃ avadānaṃ itivṛttakaṃ jātakaṃ vaipulyaṃ adbhutā dharmāḥ upadeśāśceti /
body.translated_text: <s>Sūtra</s>, <s>geya</s> (verse), <s>vyākaraṇa</s> (prophecy), <s>gāthā</s> (stanza), <s>udāna</s> (inspired utterance), <s>nidāna</s> (occasion), <s>avadāna</s> (narrative), <s>itivṛttaka</s> (legend), <s>jātaka</s> (birth-story), <s>vaipulya</s> (extensive), <s>adbhuta-dharma</s> (marvels), and <s>upadeśa</s> (instruction) — [these are the twelve divisions of scripture].

body.text: tatra sūtraṃ katamat? yatra gambhīrapadairarthasūcanam / geyaṃ katamat? sūtrameva [yadgīyate] / yacca neyārthaṃ sūtraṃ tadapi geyaṃ gamyatvāt / vyākaraṇaṃ [katamat? yatra] śrāvako 'bhyatītaḥ kālagata upapattau vyākriyate / yacca nītārthaṃ sūtraṃ tena hi [sphuṭābhiprāyeṇa] vyākhyānāt / gāthā katamā? yatra [dvipadā tripadā catuṣpadā pañcapadā] ṣaṭpadā ca / udānaṃ katamat? yaduddiśya bhāṣitam / sotpattiśikṣāprajñaptibhāṣitaṃ vā / avadānaṃ katamat? sadṛṣṭāntakabhāṣitam / itivṛttakaṃ katamat? pūrvayogapratisaṃyuktam / [jātakaṃ katamat? bodhisattvacaryāpratisaṃyuktam / vaipulyaṃ katamat?] yadbodhisattvapiṭakapratisaṃyuktam / sarvasattvahitasukhādhiṣṭhānatvāt / adbhūtā dharmāḥ katame? yatra śrāvakabodhisattvabuddhānāmāścaryādbhutā dharmā deśyante / upadeśāḥ katame? yatrāviparītaṃ dharmalakṣaṇamupadiśyate [tatropadeśe 'ntargateyaṃ bhagavatī sūtraratnam /]
body.translated_text: Among these, what is a <s>sūtra</s>? That in which the meaning is indicated through profound words. What is a <s>geya</s>? That which is a <s>sūtra</s> itself [when] sung. And a <s>sūtra</s> of indirect meaning is also <s>geya</s>, because it is to be understood [through interpretation]. What is a <s>vyākaraṇa</s>? That in which a <s>śrāvaka</s> (disciple) who has passed away is prophesied regarding his rebirth. And a <s>sūtra</s> of definitive meaning [is also so], since it explains with clear intent. What is a <s>gāthā</s>? That which has two, three, four, five, or six lines. What is an <s>udāna</s>? That which is spoken with reference to [a specific topic]. Or what is spoken as the teaching of the arising, training, and designation. What is an <s>avadāna</s>? That which is spoken with illustrations. What is an <s>itivṛttaka</s>? That which is connected with former events. What is a <s>jātaka</s>? That which is connected with the practice of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. What is a <s>vaipulya</s>? That which is connected with the <s>Bodhisattva</s> collection (piṭaka), because it is the basis for the welfare and happiness of all beings. What are <s>adbhuta-dharmas</s>? Those in which the marvelous and wondrous qualities of <s>śrāvakas</s>, <s>bodhisattvas</s>, and <s>Buddhas</s> are taught. What are <s>upadeśas</s>? Those in which the characteristics of <s>dharma</s> are correctly taught. Among these, within <s>upadeśa</s>, this Noble Sūtra-jewel is included.

body.text: paramapuruṣārthasādhanasya paramagambhīrasya dharmasya sarvairākāraiḥ sūcanāt / athaiṣā katibhiḥ padārthairabhidheyairdarśitā? katame vata iti praśne śāstram-
body.translated_text: Because it indicates through all modes the supremely profound <s>Dharma</s> which is the means to the highest human goal. Now, by how many categories of meaning is this [sūtra] expounded? In response to the question 'What are they?' — the treatise [states]:

children.translated_text: The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is expressed through eight categories of meaning:
<s>Sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience in all aspects), <s>mārgajñatā</s> (knowledge of paths), <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience), [and then] // 1-3 //
Full awakening in all aspects, the culmination, the sequential [awakening],
instantaneous awakening, and the <s>dharmakāya</s> (truth-body) — these are eight. // 1-4 //

body.text: iti / svārthe 'dhā' pratyayaḥ / ime te 'ṣṭāvityarthaḥ / bodhyabhimukhaḥ samyagbodhi' 'bhisambodhaḥ' / ata evā....... / abhisamīyate saptabhiḥ prāpyate yataḥ / mūrdhā prakarṣaḥ / taṃ prāpto 'mūrdhaprāptaḥ' / anupūrvamanukramaḥ / tadyogāt 'anupūrvikaḥ' / ubhayatrāpi 'sambodha' iti vartate /
body.translated_text: The suffix '-dhā' is used in its own sense [of division]. The meaning is: these are [the] eight. 'Directed toward awakening, full and correct awakening' is <s>abhisambodha</s>. Therefore... Because it is attained — realized — through seven [stages]. The peak is the highest degree. One who has reached that is '<s>mūrdhaprāpta</s>' (one who has reached the peak). <s>Anupūrva</s> is sequential order. By connection with that, it is '<s>anupūrvika</s>' (sequential). In both cases, the word '<s>sambodha</s>' (awakening) is understood.

body.text: punaḥ śāstram-
body.translated_text: Further, the treatise [states]:

body.text: lakṣaṇaṃ [tatprayogastatprakarṣastadanukramaḥ /]
body.translated_text: The characteristic, its application, its excellence, its sequence,

body.text: tanniṣṭhā tadvipākaścetyanyaḥ ṣoḍhārtha
body.translated_text: its completion, and its result — this is another sixfold summary of meaning. // 9-1 //

body.text: saṃgrahaḥ // 9-1 //
athavā........ṣaḍarthāḥ / yata ādau trividhā sarvajñatā tat 'lakṣaṇaṃ' prajñāpāramitāyāḥ / tataścatvāro 'syāḥ prayogaḥ prayogaprakarṣaḥ prayogānukramaḥ prayoganiṣṭhā ceti / ........ /
body.translated_text: Alternatively... six meanings. Since the threefold omniscience comes first, that is the 'characteristic' of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Then there are four: its application, the excellence of application, the sequence of application, and the completion of application... ...

body.text: punaḥ śāstram-
body.translated_text: Further, the treatise [states]:

children.translated_text: The threefold object, the cause, and the fourfold application,
the <s>dharmakāya</s> (truth-body) as the result, and activity — this is another threefold summary of meaning. // 9-2 //

body.text: athavātisaṃkṣepato 'syāṃ trayo 'rthāḥ / tathā hi trividhaḥ prayogaviṣayaḥ sarvajñatātrayaśca[taddhetuḥ] 'viṣayaḥ' / 'prayogaścaturātmaka' / sarvākārā hi sambodhādiḥ / tasya hetoḥ 'phalaṃ dharmakāyaḥ' tat 'karma' ca /
body.translated_text: Alternatively, in extreme summary, there are three meanings in this [text]. For the threefold object of application — the triad of omniscience — [and] its cause is the 'object.' 'The application is fourfold.' For the full awakening in all aspects and so on [constitute it]. 'The result is the <s>dharmakāya</s>' of that cause. And that is 'activity.'

body.text: tadevamaṣṭau ṣaṭ trayo vāsya sūtrasyārthāḥ sākalyena / prādhānyena punareka eva vārthaḥ / anyathā ekavākyatāpi na syāt / daśadāḍimādipasamūhavat / avayavārthaiḥ parasparo[para]ktasya svārthena (?) ekatvādupasaṃhārāt / tasmāt sambaddhān(nu)guṇopāyāt / samyaksambodhiratra
body.translated_text: Thus the meanings of this <s>sūtra</s> are eight, six, or three in their totality. But primarily, there is even one meaning. Otherwise, there would be no unity of statement either — like a heap of ten pomegranates. Because of the unification through one's own meaning of what is connected with each other through component meanings (?). Therefore, through coherent and suitable means, the perfect and complete awakening is here

body.text: prādhānyenocyata ityeke / tadasat / yataḥ samyaksambodhiḥ śrāvakapiṭake 'pyatipratītatvādajijñāsitā / prajñāpāramitā tu tatrāviditatvājjijñāsiteti / saiva [śāstre prādhānyena]abhidhīyate / [duradhimokṣā] gambhīratvāt / bhagavatastu vacanāt [pratilabdhād] adhimucyate.............. / tato 'pīyaṃ prādhānyena bhagavatā vaktavyā / yathā yathā ceyamadhimacyate tathā tathā bodherāsannībhavati / tato 'pīyaṃ prādhānyena vacanīyā / aṣṭāsu cābhisamayeṣu yathā [sāraṃ tatheyaṃ] vistareṇocyamānā kathaṃ prādhānyena nocyate? prajñāpāramitaiva mārgaḥ sambodheḥ / śeṣāṇāmapi tathaiva mārgīkaraṇāt / ityevamiyamucyamānā sutarāṃ prādhānyenocyata ityalamativistareṇa / ata eva prādhānyena vyapadeśādetatsūtraṃ prajñāpāramitā / [na samyaksambodhi]riti / tasmātprajñāpāramitaivaḥ....... /
body.translated_text: stated primarily, according to some. But that is wrong. Because <s>samyaksambodhi</s> (perfect awakening), being well-known even in the <s>Śrāvaka</s> collection, is not inquired about. But <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, being unknown there, is inquired about. It is she that is primarily spoken of in the treatise. [She is] difficult to assent to, because of her profundity. But through the <s>Bhagavat</s>'s words, one assents [to her]... Therefore, she too is primarily to be spoken by the <s>Bhagavat</s>. And as much as she is assented to, that much closer one becomes to awakening. Therefore too, she is primarily to be spoken. And in the eight <s>abhisamayas</s> (realizations), as she is spoken extensively according to [their] essence, how is she not spoken primarily? <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> itself is the path of awakening. Because the others too are made into path in the same way. Thus, being spoken [in this manner], she is all the more spoken primarily — enough of excessive elaboration. Therefore, because of the primary designation, this <s>sūtra</s> is [called] <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, not <s>Samyaksambodhi</s>. Therefore, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> alone is...

body.text: evaṃ mayetyādi / atha kasyedaṃ vacanam? saṃṅgītikārasya / saṅgītatvena loke saṃpratyayārtham / tatkiṃ ........prakṣepaḥ? naivam / bhagavadājñayaivaṃ tena pāṭhāt / uktaṃ hi bhagavatā [śrutaṃ mayā] iti saṅgītikāraḥ aḍakavatīnivāsī vajrapāṇirmahābodhisattvaḥ / sa hi bhādrakalpikānāṃ tathāgatānāṃ rūpakāyasya dharmakāyasya ca rakṣādhikṛtaḥ pṛṣṭhato 'vagataḥ / evaṃ te (taiḥ?) pratyarpitaśāsanaśca....... / ............. .......... yato 'syāmacyu (?)tasamādhiniśrito mahān dharmāvabhāsastasmāt prabhākarī / yato 'syāṃ bodhipakṣyaiḥ saṃkleśendhanadahanaṃ tasmādarciṣmatī / yato 'syāṃ laukikalokottarayorvidyāsatyajñānayoranyonyavirodhādduṣkaraḥ parijayastasmātsudurjayā / yato 'syāṃ pratītyasamutpādapravicayādabhimukho bhavatyasaṅgamukhākhyaḥ prajñāpāramitāvihārastasmādabhimukhī / yato 'syāṃ bodhipakṣyasatya[pratītya] samutpādālambano nirnimittavihāra ābhogavāhī tasmāddūraṃgamā / yato 'syāṃ sa eva svarasavāhitvādacalaḥ tasmādacalā / yato 'syāṃ pratisaṃvibhdirdhārmakathikatvādbodhisattvaḥ sādhustasmāt sādhumatī / yato 'syāṃ bodhisattvo 'bhiṣicyate yau[va]rājyāya tasmāddharmameghā / ..........etāḥ pratyekaṃ ṣaḍbhiḥ pāramitābhiḥ saṃgṛhītāḥ yathākramam / etāsu daśa pāramitā atiricyate /
body.translated_text: 'Thus have I [heard]' and so on. Now, whose is this statement? Of the compiler (<s>saṅgītikāra</s>). For the sake of confidence in the world, through compilation. Is this then... an interpolation? Not so. By the <s>Bhagavat</s>'s command itself, through that recitation. For the <s>Bhagavat</s> has said, 'I have heard' — thus the compiler is <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the great <s>Bodhisattva</s> dwelling in <s>Aḍakavatī</s>. For he is entrusted with the protection of the form-body and <s>dharmakāya</s> of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> of the <s>Bhadrakalpa</s> (Fortunate Age), following [them] from behind. And the teaching has been entrusted to him by them... Because in this [stage] there is a great illumination of <s>Dharma</s> based on the unfallen <s>samādhi</s>, therefore [it is called] <s>Prabhākarī</s> (Luminous). Because in this [stage] the fuel of defilements is burned by the factors of awakening, therefore <s>Arciṣmatī</s> (Blazing). Because in this [stage] the difficult mastery of the mutual opposition of worldly and supramundane knowledge, truth, and wisdom [is achieved], therefore <s>Sudurjayā</s> (Very Difficult to Conquer). Because in this [stage], through the analysis of dependent arising, one becomes face-to-face [with reality], being the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> abiding called <s>Asaṅgamukha</s> (Unattached Presence), therefore <s>Abhimukhī</s> (Facing). Because in this [stage] the same signless abiding, based on the factors of awakening, truth, and dependent arising, is carried by effort, therefore <s>Dūraṃgamā</s> (Far-Going). Because in this [stage] that same [abiding], being carried spontaneously, is immovable, therefore <s>Acalā</s> (Immovable). Because in this [stage] the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is good due to analytical knowledge and being a <s>Dharma</s>-preacher, therefore <s>Sādhumatī</s> (Good Intelligence). Because in this [stage] the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is consecrated for the crown-prince [position], therefore <s>Dharmameghā</s> (Cloud of <s>Dharma</s>). These are each comprised by six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) in sequence. Among these, ten <s>pāramitās</s> are distinguished.

body.text: katamā daśa?
body.translated_text: What are the ten?

children.text: "dānaṃ śīlaṃ kṣamā vīrya dhyānaṃ prajñā upāyatā /
children.translated_text: Giving, morality, patience, vigor, meditation, wisdom, skillful means,
aspiration, power, and knowledge — these are the ten <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections).

body.text: tatra yatpāramitopacitasya kuśalamūlasyānuttarāyāṃ samyaksambodhau samyakpariṇāmanamupādāya pāramitā tenopāyena tasyākṣayīkaraṇāt / āha ca / "ābodhe kṣayamiti svalpamapi na bodhipariṇataṃ kuśalam / āsamantātpatitaḥ payonidhau salilabidnuriva" iti / bhadracaryādikaṃ praṇidhānapāramitā yayā pratijanma yatpāramitāścarati / bhāvanābalaṃ pratisaṃkhyānabalaṃ ca balapāramitā / yayā pratyahaṃ pratikṣaṇaṃ tāścarati / yathābhiprāyamayathārutaṃ mahāyānasya parijñānaṃ jñānapāramitā /
body.translated_text: Among these, the <s>pāramitā</s> (perfection) of skillful means consists in the correct dedication of the wholesome root accumulated through the [other] <s>pāramitās</s> to unsurpassed perfect awakening, because through that means it is made inexhaustible. And it is said: 'Even a small amount of wholesome [merit] dedicated to awakening does not diminish until [the attainment of] awakening — like a drop of water [that does not diminish when] fallen into the great ocean.' The <s>pāramitā</s> of aspiration is the aspiration beginning with the <s>Bhadracarī</s> (Noble Conduct), by which one practices the [other] <s>pāramitās</s> in each birth. The <s>pāramitā</s> of power is the power of cultivation and the power of analysis, by which one practices those [perfections] every day and every moment. The <s>pāramitā</s> of knowledge is the understanding of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle) as intended and not according to the literal [meaning].

body.text: bhūmīnāṃ vistara āryadaśabhūmakādau / parikarmāṇi punarāsāṃ mahatyorbhagavatyoruddiṣṭāni nirdiṣṭāni ca bhūmīnāṃ parikarmāṇyadhikṛtya śāstre trayoviṃśatiḥ ślokāḥ / tāni yathābhūmi pṛthakkṛtya vakṣyāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: The details of the <s>bhūmis</s> (stages) are in the Noble <s>Daśabhūmaka</s> and elsewhere. The preparatory practices for these are indicated and taught in the two great Noble [texts]. The treatise has twenty-three verses concerning the preparatory practices with respect to the <s>bhūmis</s>. We shall state those separately for each <s>bhūmi</s>.

children.translated_text: The tenth (first) <s>bhūmi</s> is attained through tenfold preparatory practice:
Intention, being a beneficial entity, and equanimity toward beings, // 1-48 //
Generosity, attending upon spiritual friends, seeking the support of the true <s>Dharma</s>,
constant mental disposition toward renunciation, and aspiration directed toward the <s>Buddha</s>-body, // 1-49 //
Teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>, and truthfulness is said to be the tenth;
the preparatory practice for these should be understood through the non-apprehension of their intrinsic nature. // 1-50 //

body.text: 'daśadhā' iti daśavidhena / taccāśayādi // 'āśayaḥ' śraddhāchandau / 'hitavastutvaṃ' sarvasattvahitaiṣitā / heturasyāḥ 'sattveṣu praśamacittatā' / 'tyāgo ' dānapāramitā / 'eṣaṇā' paryeṣaṇā / sā ca 'saddharmālambanā' dharmaparyeṣṭirityarthaḥ / gṛhavāsānniṣkramaṇaṃ niṣkramaḥ / svārthe ṣyañ 'naiṣkramyaṃ' taccittatā / 'spṛhā' ityatra sadeti vartate / 'satyaṃ' coktamiti satyavacanaṃ taddaśamam / 'eṣāṃ' ityāśayādīnām //
body.translated_text: 'Tenfold' means of ten kinds. And that consists of intention and so on. 'Intention' is faith and aspiration. 'Being a beneficial entity' is the wish for the welfare of all beings. Its cause is 'equanimity toward beings.' 'Generosity' is the <s>pāramitā</s> of giving. 'Seeking' means searching. And that is 'supported by the true <s>Dharma</s>' — meaning the search for <s>Dharma</s>. Renunciation from household life is <s>niṣkrama</s>; in the reflexive sense, with the <s>ṣyañ</s> suffix, '<s>naiṣkramya</s>' (renunciation) — that disposition of mind. 'Aspiration' — here the word 'sat' (true/good) is understood. 'Truthfulness' means truthful speech — that is the tenth. 'Of these' means of intention and the rest.

children.text: śīlaṃ kṛtajñatā kṣāntiḥ prāmodyaṃ mahatī kṛpā /
children.translated_text: Morality, gratitude, patience, joy, great compassion,
respect, service to the guru, and vigor in giving and the like is the eighth. // 1-51 //

body.text: 'śīlaṃ' śīlapariśuddhiḥ / 'kṣāntiḥ' kṣāntibalam / pramoda eva 'prāmodyam' 'mahatī' sarvasattvāparityāgitayā / 'gauravaṃ' gauravārheṣu / 'gurūśuśrūṣā' kalyāṇamitreṣa śāstṛsaṃjñā / 'dānādike ' iti pāramitāsu / 'aṣṭama' grahaṇādaṣṭāveva parikarmāṇi dvitīyāyām /
body.translated_text: 'Morality' is the purity of moral conduct. 'Patience' is the power of forbearance. <s>Prāmodya</s> is simply joy — 'great' because of not abandoning any being. 'Respect' toward those deserving respect. 'Service to the guru' means regarding spiritual friends as teachers. 'In giving and the like' means in the <s>pāramitās</s>. Because of the word 'eighth,' there are exactly eight preparatory practices for the second [<s>bhūmi</s>].

children.text: atṛptatā śrute dānaṃ dharmasya ca nirāmiṣam /
children.translated_text: Insatiability in learning, giving of <s>Dharma</s> without material [reward],
purification of the <s>Buddha</s>-field, and unwearied [perseverance] in <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), // 1-52 //

body.text: hrīrapatrāpyamityetat pañcadhāmananātmakam /
body.translated_text: Sense of shame and moral dread — this is fivefold, consisting of reflection.

body.text: 'śrutaṃ' bāhuśrutyam / 'saṃśuddhiḥ' pariśuddhiḥ / sā tasyāmeva puṇyapariṇāmanāt / 'amananātmakaṃ' tenāmananāt / 'pañcadhā' iti vacanāt pañcaiva parikarmāṇi tṛtīyāyām /
body.translated_text: 'Learning' is extensive learning. 'Purification' is complete purification — that [is achieved] through the dedication of merit in that very [practice]. 'Consisting of reflection' means through such reflection. Because of the word 'fivefold,' there are exactly five preparatory practices for the third [<s>bhūmi</s>].

body.text: vanāśālpecchatā tuṣṭirdhutasaṃlekhasevanam // 1-53 //
body.translated_text: Desire for forest [dwelling], contentment of few desires, and the practice of ascetic purification, // 1-53 //

children.translated_text: Non-abandonment of the training, disgust toward sensual pleasures,
weariness [with saṃsāra], renunciation of all possessions, [and] non-withdrawal and non-attachment. // 1-54 //

body.text: vanasya ('vānāśā) araṇyavāsastatkāryatvāt / 'tuṣṭiḥ' santuṣṭiḥ / 'dhuta' guṇa 'saṃlekhasya' 'sevanaṃ' anutsargaḥ / 'nirvitsarvāstisaṃtyāgau' iti nirvedaḥ sarvasatāṃ tyāgaśca / 'anavalīnatvānapekṣate ' iti / anavalīnacittatā sarvavastunirapekṣatā ca / anavalīnatvaṃ asaṃkucutatvam / daśeti vakṣyamāna(ṇa)manuvartate / tato daśaiva parikarmāṇi caturthyām /
body.translated_text: 'Forest-desire' (<s>vanāśā</s>) is forest-dwelling, because of being its effect. 'Contentment' is satisfaction. 'Practice of ascetic purification' (<s>dhuta-saṃlekha</s>) — 'practice' means non-abandonment. 'Weariness and renunciation of all possessions' — that is, spiritual weariness and the abandonment of all belongings. 'Non-withdrawal and non-attachment' — non-withdrawn mindedness and non-attachment to all things. Non-withdrawal means non-contraction. 'Ten' is supplied from what will follow. Therefore there are exactly ten preparatory practices for the fourth [<s>bhūmi</s>].

children.translated_text: Intimacy [with householders], jealousy toward [noble] families, [providing] an occasion for idle chatter,
Self-exaltation, contempt for others — [these are] the ten unwholesome paths of action. // 1-55 //
Pride, arrogance, wrong perception, doubt, tolerance of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) —
By abandoning these, one attains the fifth <s>bhūmi</s> (stage). // 1-56 //

body.text: 'saṃstavo ' gṛhipravrajitaiḥ / 'kuleṣu' upasaṃ[kra]maṇīyāgṛheṣu 'mātsaryam' / 'saṅgaṇikā' apratirūpakathā / 'utkarṣaṇam' / 'avajñā'
body.translated_text: 'Intimacy' is [contact] with householders and renunciants. 'Jealousy toward families' is [jealousy regarding] households worthy of visiting. '<s>Saṅgaṇikā</s>' is improper conversation. 'Exaltation' [is self-aggrandizement]. 'Contempt'

body.text: paṃsanam / 'karmamārgāḥ' 'karmapathāḥ' / 'mānaḥ' cittonnatiḥ / 'stambho ' gurūṣvapraṇatakāyatā / 'viparyāso ' viparātārthagrāhaḥ / 'vimatiḥ' vicikitsā / 'kleśamarṣaṇaṃ' rāgadveṣamohādhivāsanam / 'etān' iti saṃstavādīn /
body.translated_text: is disparagement. 'Paths of action' means '<s>karmapathāḥ</s>' (courses of action). 'Pride' is mental elation. 'Arrogance' is not bowing the body before teachers. 'Wrong perception' is grasping a meaning in a reversed way. 'Doubt' is uncertainty. 'Tolerance of <s>kleśas</s>' is harboring attachment, hatred, and delusion. 'These' refers to intimacy and the rest.

children.translated_text: One who fulfills the [six] <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) — generosity, morality, patience, vigor, meditation, and wisdom,
And who abandons the minds of disciples, <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>-aspirants, and those beset by fear, // 1-57 //
Who, when asked, does not shrink back, who is not disheartened even in total renunciation,

children.text: kṛśo 'pi nārthināṃ kṣeptā ṣaṣṭhīṃ bhūmiṃ samaśnute // 1-58 //
children.translated_text: Who, even when impoverished, does not reject petitioners — attains the sixth <s>bhūmi</s> (stage). // 1-58 //

body.text: ṣaṇṇāṃ pāramitānāṃ pratyekaṃ pūraka iti ṣaḍdharmāḥ / śrāvakaspṛhāyāḥ pratyekabuddhaspṛhāyāḥ parita(tra)sanacittasya ca parivarjaka iti trayaḥ / yācitasyānabalīnacittatā, sarvasvatyāge 'pyadaurmanasya, daurbalyepi na yācakānāṃ kṣepa iti trayaḥ / ebhirdvādaśabhirdharmaiḥ ṣaṣṭhiṃ bhūmiṃ prāpnoti /
body.translated_text: Being a fulfiller of each of the six <s>pāramitās</s> individually makes six qualities. Being an abandoner of the desire for the <s>Śrāvaka</s> [path], the desire for the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> [path], and the terrified mind makes three. Not shrinking when asked, not being disheartened even in renouncing all possessions, and not rejecting petitioners even when weakened makes three. By these twelve qualities one attains the sixth <s>bhūmi</s>.

children.translated_text: Grasping at self, being, soul, person; [views of] annihilation and eternalism;
Signs and causes; in the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases); // 1-59 //
Clinging to the three realms; attachment; a sunken mind;
Adherence to the view of the Three Jewels and morality; // 1-60 //
And despair regarding <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), and opposition to it — these twenty
Blemishes, when severed in a person, [that person] reaches the seventh <s>bhūmi</s> (stage). // 1-61 //
Knowledge of the three gates of liberation; purity of the threefold sphere;
Compassion, reflection, seeing the equality of all <s>dharmas</s>, and knowledge of the one approach; // 1-62 //
Knowledge of the <s>anutpādakṣānti</s> (patient acceptance of the non-arising of dharmas); seeing all <s>dharmas</s> as one;
The elimination of conceptualization; abandonment of perception, views, and <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions); // 1-63 //

children.text: śamathasya ca nidhyaptiḥ kauśalaṃ ca vidarśane /
children.translated_text: And the application of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding); skill in <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight);
The taming of the mind; knowledge that is unobstructed everywhere; // 1-64 //
Having mastered the stages, going at will to other realms simultaneously,
And seeing one's own existence everywhere — these [make] twenty. // 1-65 //

body.text: dvitīyāt 'viṃśati' śabdādūrdhvaṃ guṇāḥ......ātmagrahādayo 'viṃśatiḥ' / 'kalaṅkāḥ' doṣāḥ / yasya 'vicchinnāḥ' prahīṇāḥ / trivimokṣamukhajñānādayaśca viṃśatiḥ gunāḥ (ṇāḥ) paripūrṇāḥ sa saptamīṃ bhūmiṃ prāpnotīti samāsato 'rthaḥ /
body.translated_text: From the second [verse], the word 'twenty' and above refers to the qualities... The graspings beginning with self-grasping are the 'twenty blemishes.' When 'severed' means 'abandoned.' The qualities beginning with knowledge of the three gates of liberation, twenty in number, are fulfilled — one who [has accomplished this] attains the seventh <s>bhūmi</s>. This is the meaning in brief.

body.text: ' graho ''bhiniveṣaḥ(śaḥ) / tasya viśeṣaṇamātmādirāyatanaparyantaḥ / śāśvatoccheda..........................ratnādi (?) dṛṣṭiḥ / tasyāṃ 'abhiniveṣi (śi)tā' niśrayaḥ / 'viṣādaḥ' khedaḥ / 'tadvirodhaḥ' śūnyatāyā bādhanam / 'samaṃ' iti sahetyarthaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Grasping' means 'adherence.' Its specification extends from 'self' through '<s>āyatana</s>.' The views of eternalism and annihilation... are 'views.' 'Adherence' thereto is 'commitment.' 'Despair' is dejection. 'Opposition to it' is the rejection of <s>śūnyatā</s>. 'Simultaneously' means 'together.'

body.text: tatra kalaṅkanirdeśānāmā(ma)rthaḥ / ātmagrāhaḥ / sattvagrāhaḥ / jīvagrāhaḥ / pudgalagrāhaḥ / ucchedagrāhaḥ / śāśvatagrāhaḥ / nimittagrāhaḥ / hetugrāhaḥ / skandhagrāhaḥ / [dhātugrāhaḥ / āyatanagrāhaḥ /] traidhātuke adhyavasānam / traidhātuke ālayaḥ / buddhidṛṣṭiniśrayaḥ / dharmadṛṣṭiniśrayaḥ / saṅghadṛṣṭiniśrayaḥ / śīladṛṣṭiniśrayaḥ / śūnyā dharmā iti viṣāḍhaḥ / śanyatāvirodhaśceti /
body.translated_text: Here the meaning of the enumeration of blemishes: Self-grasping. Being-grasping. Soul-grasping. Person-grasping. Annihilationism-grasping. Eternalism-grasping. Sign-grasping. Cause-grasping. Aggregate-grasping. [Element-grasping. Sense-base-grasping.] Fixation on the three realms. Abiding in the three realms. Adherence to the view of the <s>Buddha</s>. Adherence to the view of the <s>Dharma</s>. Adherence to the view of the <s>Saṅgha</s>. Adherence to the view of morality. Despair that <s>dharmas</s> are empty. And opposition to emptiness.

body.text: guṇānirdeśānāmarthaḥ / śūnyatāparipūrtiḥ / ānimittasākṣātkriyā / apraṇihitajñānam / [trimaṇḍalaviśuddhitā / karuṇā / mananā] / sarvadharmasamatādarśanam / bhūtanayaprativedhaḥ / anutpādakṣāntijñānam / ekanayanirdeśaḥ / sarvadharmāṇāṃ kalpanāsamuddhātaḥ / saṃjñādṛṣṭivivartaḥ / kleśavivartaḥ / śamathanidhyaptiḥ / vipaśyanākauśalyam / dātucittatā / anunayasyābhūmiḥ / yathecchakṣetragamanam / tatra cabuddhaparṣanmaṇḍe[svātmabhāva]darśanamiti //
body.translated_text: The meaning of the enumeration of qualities: Fulfillment of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness). Direct realization of the signless. Knowledge of the wishless. [Purity of the threefold sphere. Compassion. Reflection.] Seeing the equality of all <s>dharmas</s>. Penetration of the true approach. Knowledge of <s>anutpādakṣānti</s> (patient acceptance of non-arising). The instruction of the one approach. The elimination of conceptualization in all <s>dharmas</s>. Turning away from perception. Turning away from views. Turning away from <s>kleśas</s>. Application of <s>śamatha</s>. Skill in <s>vipaśyanā</s>. A mind given to [the three forms of] giving. Mastery of the stages. Going at will to any realm. And seeing one's own existence therein, in the assemblies of the <s>Buddhas</s>.

children.translated_text: Knowledge of the minds of all beings, play with the <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), the auspicious
Accomplishment of the <s>Buddha-kṣetra</s> (Buddha-field), and examination in the service of the <s>Buddhas</s>; // 1-66 //
Knowledge of the faculties, purification of the <s>Buddha-kṣetra</s>, an illusory abiding,
And intentional birth in existence — these activities are taught as eightfold. // 1-67 //

body.text: iti / 'śubhā niṣpattiḥ' iti sambandhaḥ / pariśuddhetyarthaḥ / 'aṣṭādhā' iti vacanāt āṣṭaveva parikarmāṇyaṣṭamyām / tadyathā / sarvasattvacittānupraveśaḥ / abhijñācittā [nukriḍanam /] / buddhakṣetraniṣpādanam / buddhānāṃ sevā ca parīkṣaṇaṃ cetyekīkriyate / indriyaparāparajñānam / buddhakṣetrapariśodhanam /
body.translated_text: Thus. The construction is: 'the auspicious accomplishment.' The meaning is: 'purified.' Since the statement says 'eightfold,' there are exactly eight preparations for the eighth [<s>bhūmi</s>]. Namely: entry into the minds of all beings; play of the mind with the <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges); accomplishment of the <s>Buddha-kṣetra</s>; service and examination of the <s>Buddhas</s> — these are combined as one; knowledge of the superior and inferior among the faculties; purification of the <s>Buddha-kṣetra</s>;

body.text: māyopamasya samādherabhīkṣṇaṃ samāpattiḥ sañcitya bhavo[pa]pattiśca / dvividhaṃ buddhakṣetram / ādau bhājanalokaḥ paścāt sattvaloka iti /
body.translated_text: Repeated attainment of the <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) that is like an illusion, and intentional rebirth. The <s>Buddha-kṣetra</s> is twofold: first, the world of the container; second, the world of beings.

children.translated_text: Infinite <s>praṇidhānas</s> (vows), knowledge of the speech of gods and others,
A river-like [flow] of eloquence, supreme entry into the womb; // 1-68 //
And the excellences of clan, birth, lineage,
Retinue, birth, going forth, <s>Bodhi</s>-tree, and the fullness of qualities. // 1-69 //

body.text: aṣṭamānantaraṃ navamī / tasyāḥ parikarmāṇi dvādaśa / anantaṃ praṇidhānam / devādirutajñānam / paripūrṇaṃ pratibhānam / garbhāvakrāntisampat / kulasaṃpat / jātisaṃpat / gotrasaṃpat / parivārasaṃpat / janmasaṃpat / naiṣkramyasaṃpat / bodhivṛkṣasaṃpat / guṇapūrisampacca /
body.translated_text: After the eighth comes the ninth [<s>bhūmi</s>]. Its preparations are twelve: infinite <s>praṇidhāna</s>; knowledge of the speech of gods and others; perfect eloquence; excellence of womb-entry; excellence of clan; excellence of birth; excellence of lineage; excellence of retinue; excellence of [actual] birth; excellence of going forth; excellence of the <s>Bodhi</s>-tree; and excellence of the fullness of qualities.

children.translated_text: Having transcended the nine stages, one is established on the <s>Buddha-bhūmi</s> (Buddha-stage).

children.text: yena jñānena sā jñeyā daśamī bodhisattvabhūḥ // 1-70 //
children.translated_text: By the knowledge through which that is known, that is the tenth <s>Bodhisattva-bhūmi</s>. // 1-70 //

body.text: 'navabhūmīḥ' iti gotrādibhūmiḥ / tatra gotrabhūmiḥ nirvāṇagotrakāṇam / aṣṭamakabhūmiḥ śrotaāpattiphalapratipannakasya / darśanabhūmiḥ śrotaāpannasya / tanubhūmiḥ sakṛdāgaminaḥ / vītarāgabhūmiranāgāminaḥ / "kṛtaṃ karaṇīyaṃ" iti jñānāt kṛtāvī arhan / tasya bhūmiḥ kṛtāvibhūmiḥ / śrāvakabhūmiḥ śrāvakasya / saiva ṣaḍvidhā pratyekabuddhasya / bodhisattvabhūmiḥ bodhisattvasya / pūrvoktā navabhūmayaḥ / etā navabhūmīratikramya yena jñānena bodhisattvo buddhabhūmau pratiṣṭhito bhavati sā daśami bodhisattvabhūmiḥ / iti bhūmisambharaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'The nine stages' means the stages beginning with the <s>gotra</s> (family) stage. There, the <s>gotra-bhūmi</s> is for those of the <s>nirvāṇa</s>-lineage. The eighth-person stage is for the aspirant to the fruit of stream-entry. The stage of seeing is for the stream-enterer. The thin stage is for the once-returner. The passionless stage is for the non-returner. The stage of 'the task is done' — from the knowledge that 'what was to be done has been done' — the <s>arhat</s>, whose stage is the stage of the accomplished. The <s>Śrāvaka</s>-stage is for the <s>Śrāvaka</s>. The same sixfold [division applies] for the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>. The <s>Bodhisattva</s>-stage is for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. The aforementioned are the nine stages. Having transcended these nine stages, the knowledge by which a <s>Bodhisattva</s> is established on the <s>Buddha-bhūmi</s> — that is the tenth <s>Bodhisattva-bhūmi</s>. Thus the collection of stages.

body.text: prati[pakṣa]madhikṛtya śāstram-
body.translated_text: With regard to the antidotes, the treatise [states] —

children.translated_text: The antidote should be known as eightfold, on the paths of seeing and cultivation,
For the pacification of eight conceptualizations regarding the grasped and the grasper. // 1-71 //

body.text: 'abhyāso ' bhāvanā / grāhyo, grāhakaḥ / darśanamārge dvau grāhyavikalpau / vastumātrādhiṣṭhānaḥ pratipakṣadhiṣṭhānaśca / dvau grāhakavikalpau / pudgaladravyādhiṣṭhānaḥ pudgalaprajñaptyadhiṣṭhānaśca / [evaṃ bhāvanāmārge vikalpa]prahāṇāya aṣṭau pratipakṣāḥ / pratipakṣasambhāraḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Cultivation' means '<s>bhāvanā</s>' (meditative development). 'Grasped' [means the object]; 'grasper' [means the subject]. On the path of seeing there are two conceptualizations of the grasped: one based on the mere object; one based on the antidote. Two conceptualizations of the grasper: one based on the person as substance; one based on the person as designation. [Similarly on the path of cultivation, for the abandonment of conceptualizations] there are eight antidotes. Thus the collection of antidotes.

body.text: tatra darśanamārge tathatādīnāṃ rūpādīnāṃ svapnādīnāṃ ca grāhyavastūnāmupalambho vikalpaḥ / taddharmatopalambhalakṣaṇo 'nupalambhaḥ pratipakṣaḥ / dānādīnāṃ buddhadharmaparyantānāṃ pratipakṣavastūnāmupalambho vikalpaḥ / anupalambhaḥ pratipakṣaḥ / a................anupalambhapratipakṣaḥ / nāmasaṃketavyavahārāderupalambho vikalpaḥ / anupalambhaḥ pratipakṣaḥ / bhāvanāmārge tu na sthitā nāsthitāḥ sarvadharmā asthānayogena / dharmadhātuyogenetyarthaḥ / iti grāhyavastūnāmanupalambhaḥ / dānādīnāṃ pratipakṣavastūnāmanupalambhaḥ / śrota āpanna.......pudgalaprajñaptyāśrayāṇāṃ śrotaāpattiphalādīnāmanupalambhaḥ / iti pratipakṣasaṃbhāraḥ / samāptā ca saṃbhārapratipattiḥ //
body.translated_text: On the path of seeing, the conceptualization is the apprehension of grasped objects such as <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) and the like, forms and the like, dreams and the like. Its antidote is non-apprehension, characterized by non-apprehension of those very qualities. The conceptualization regarding antidote objects is the apprehension of <s>dāna</s> (generosity) and the rest up to the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>. Its antidote is non-apprehension... The antidote of non-apprehension. The conceptualization is the apprehension of names, conventions, and designations. Its antidote is non-apprehension. On the path of cultivation, however, all <s>dharmas</s> are neither established nor not established, through the method of non-establishment — meaning through the method of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>. Thus the non-apprehension of grasped objects. The non-apprehension of antidote objects such as <s>dāna</s> and the rest. The non-apprehension of the stream-enterer... the non-apprehension of the fruits of stream-entry and the rest, which depend on the designation of the person. Thus the collection of antidotes. And the practice of the collection is complete.

body.text: niryāsyatītyetena niryāṇapratipattiḥ prastāvitā / tāmadhikṛtya śāstram-
body.translated_text: By the phrase 'will go forth,' the practice of going forth is introduced. With regard to that, the treatise [states] —

children.translated_text: In the teaching, in equality,
In the welfare of beings, in the abandonment of effort, and for the ultimate — going forth; going forth characterized by attainment; // 1-72 //
And going forth within the scope of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience) —
The practice of going forth should be known as eightfold. // 1-73 //

body.text: etadāha / evamukte ityādinā subhūtiravocaditi / kimavocata? mahāyānamityādi / yasmādanena sadevamānuṣāsuraṃ lokamabhibhūya bodhisattvo niryāsyati / tasmādidaṃ yānaṃ mahāyānamityucyate / abhibhūya niryāsyatīti samānakāle ktvāpratyayaḥ / saṃmīlya hasatītyādivat / kasmādasau sarvalokamabhibhavati? tadalabhyasya māhātmyasya lābhāt / kiṃ punastat? sattvarāśeragratāsaṃpādanam / sattvarāśimahattayā prahāṇamahattayā adhigamamahattayā ca mahat / itīdamuddeśaniryāṇam //
body.translated_text: He states this beginning with 'Having thus spoken' and so on. <s>Subhūti</s> spoke. What did he say? '<s>Mahāyāna</s>' and so on. Since, having overcome the world with its gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> will go forth — therefore this vehicle is called '<s>Mahāyāna</s>' (Great Vehicle). 'Having overcome and going forth' — the <s>ktvā</s>-suffix [indicates] simultaneous action, as in 'having closed [the eyes], he laughs.' Why does he overcome the entire world? Through the attainment of a greatness not otherwise obtainable. What is that? The achievement of being foremost among the multitudes of beings. It is great through the greatness of the multitude of beings, the greatness of abandonment, and the greatness of realization. This is the going forth of the teaching.

body.text: ākāśamahattayā tanmahāyānamiti / tad yānaṃ mahaducyata iti sambandhaḥ / ākāśasamatayeti / kathaṃ samatā? yathākāśaṃ na digbhirbhidyate / avarṇasaṃsthānamapratighamanirdarśanamanantamamadhyanna hīyate na vardhate notpadyate na nirudhyate na kāmadhātuparyāpannaṃ na rūpadhātuparyāpannaṃ nārūpyadhatuparyāpannam / tathaiva mahāyānam / tasmādyathākāśasamatayā mahattadyānam / iti samatāniryāṇam /
body.translated_text: Through the greatness of space, that is the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. 'That vehicle is called great' — this is the construction. 'Through equality with space' — how is there equality? Just as space is not divided by directions, is without color, shape, resistance, demonstrability — is infinite, without middle, does not decrease, does not increase, does not arise, does not cease, is not included in the desire realm, not included in the form realm, not included in the formless realm — so too is the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. Therefore, through equality with space, that vehicle is great. This is the going forth of equality.

body.text: yathā ākāśe ityādi / ākāśa avakāśo 'ntarbhāvāt / mahāyāne avakāśaḥ / tena teṣāmarthakaraṇāt / lokadhātubhiḥ saṃkhyābhirdigbhiścāparicchinnatvāt / aprameyā asaṃkhyeyā aparimāṇāḥ / paryāyeṇeti prakāreṇa / kathaṃ ca tāvatāmavakāśaḥ yataḥ sattvāsattayā ākāśāsattā / ākāśāsattayā mahāyānāsattā / mahāyānāsattayā sarvadharmāsattā / iti hi sattvāścākāśaṃ ca mahāyānaṃ ca sarvadharmāścārūpiṇo 'nidarśanā apratighā ekalakṣaṇā yadutālakṣaṇāḥ / evamiyatā sattvānāṃ mahāyāne avakāśaḥ / iti sattvārthaniryāṇam //
body.translated_text: Beginning with 'just as in space' and so on. Space means room, from the inclusion [of everything]. In the <s>Mahāyāna</s> there is room. Because it serves the purpose of those [beings]. Because it is unlimited by world-systems, numbers, and directions. Immeasurable, innumerable, incalculable. 'In various ways' means 'in various modes.' And how is there room for that many? Because the non-existence of beings [equals] the non-existence of space. The non-existence of space [equals] the non-existence of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. The non-existence of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> [equals] the non-existence of all <s>dharmas</s>. For beings, space, the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, and all <s>dharmas</s> are formless, non-demonstrable, non-resistant, of one characteristic — namely, no characteristic. To this extent, there is room for beings in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. This is the going forth for the welfare of beings.

body.text: naivāsyetyādi / āgamaḥ āgamanam / nirgamaḥ nirgamanam / sthānaṃ gatinivṛttiḥ / trayaṃ mahāyānasya nāsti / acalā hi sarvadharmāḥ / yatasteṣāṃ prakṛtirna kvacidgacchati na kutaścidāgacchati na kvacittiṣṭhati / pariṣyandaścābhogaḥ / iti anābhoganiryāṇam /
body.translated_text: Beginning with 'not of this' and so on. '<s>Āgama</s>' is arrival. '<s>Nirgama</s>' is departure. '<s>Sthāna</s>' is the cessation of movement. These three do not exist for the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. For all <s>dharmas</s> are immovable. Since their nature neither goes anywhere, nor comes from anywhere, nor abides anywhere. And '<s>pariṣyanda</s>' is effortlessness. This is the going forth without effort.

body.text: evamasyetyādi / evamityākāśasyaiva / asyeti mahāyānasya / pūrvānta ityatīto 'rthaḥ / aparānta ityanāgato 'rthaḥ / madhyaḥ pratyutpannaḥ / trayamapyetanmahāyānasya nopalabhyate / trayadhvasamaṃ tadyānaṃ tasmānmahāyānam / kathaṃ tryadhvasamam? yato 'tīto 'rthotītārthenā (na) śūnyaḥ / anāgato 'rtho 'nāgatārthenā(na) śūnyaḥ / anāgato 'rtho 'nāgatārthenā(na) śūnyaḥ / pratyutpannaḥ pratyutpannena / tryadhvasamatā tryadhvasamatayā / mahāyānaṃ mahāyānena / bodhisattvo bodhisattvena śūnyaḥ / na ca śūnyatā atītā va anāgatā vā pratyutpannā vā / na tasyāṃ saṃkleśa upalabhyate na vyavadānam / na saṃsāro na nirvāṇam / tasmāt trayadhvasamaṃ tadyānam / ityantābhāvādatyantaniryāṇam /
body.translated_text: Regarding 'thus of this' and so on: 'thus' refers to space itself. 'Of this' refers to the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle). '<s>Pūrvānta</s>' means the past. '<s>Aparānta</s>' means the future. '<s>Madhya</s>' means the present. All three of these are not apprehended in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. That vehicle is equal to the three times; therefore it is <s>Mahāyāna</s>. How is it equal to the three times? Because the past object is not empty of [being a] past object; the future object is not empty of [being a] future object; the future object is not empty of [being a] future object; the present [is not empty] of the present; the equality of the three times [is not empty] of the equality of the three times; the <s>Mahāyāna</s> [is not empty] of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>; the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is empty of [being a] <s>Bodhisattva</s>. And <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) is neither past, nor future, nor present. In it, neither defilement (<s>saṃkleśa</s>) nor purification (<s>vyavadāna</s>) is apprehended; neither <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) nor <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Therefore that vehicle is equal to the three times. Since there is no end, [it is] the ultimate departure (<s>atyantaniryāṇa</s>).

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān ityādi / atra bhagavānāha / yānaśabdārthanirdeśe subhūteḥ sādhukāraṃ datvā atra śikṣitvetyādinā prāptiniryāṇaṃ praratauti / atra sarvajñateti sarvākārajñatā / atha khalvityādinā pūrṇasya praśnaḥ / prajñāpāramitādhikāre mahāyānasya pareṣāmaprastutatvāśaṅkānivṛttyarthaḥ / buddhānubhāvād bhagavan ityetatparyantena parihāraḥ / anulomaṃ nirdiśasi iti tvaṃ hi arvadharmān mahāyānaniḥsvabhāvān nirdiśasi / niḥsvabhāvatājñānaṃ ca teṣāṃ prajñāpāramitaiva / tasmādanulomaṃ nirdiśasīti bhāvaḥ / api tu khalu punarityādinā prakṛtameva prāptiniryāṇamadhikṛtya tasyāṃ pāptau dvādaśaviśeṣān dvādaśabhirvākyairāha / ata eva viśeṣadyotanārtho 'pituśabdaḥ / tatra api tu khalvityādi prathamam / tatkasyetyādi dvitīyam / rūpaṃ bodhisattva ityādi tṛtīyam / evaṃ bhagavannityādi caturtham / buddha
body.translated_text: Regarding 'Now then, the Blessed One' and so on: Here the Blessed One speaks. Having given approval to <s>Subhūti</s> regarding the exposition of the meaning of the word 'vehicle,' he sets forth the attainment-departure (<s>prāptiniryāṇa</s>) through 'having trained here' and so on. '<s>Sarvajñatā</s>' here means <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience in all aspects). With 'Now then' and so on is <s>Pūrṇa</s>'s question. Its purpose is to remove the doubt that in the domain of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>Mahāyāna</s> of others is not the topic. The resolution [extends] up to 'through the Buddha's power, O Blessed One.' 'You teach in accordance' means: you teach all <s>dharmas</s> as being without inherent nature (<s>niḥsvabhāva</s>) in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. And the knowledge of their lack of inherent nature is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> itself. Therefore the meaning is: 'you teach in accordance.' With 'Moreover, furthermore' and so on, taking up the attainment-departure regarding the very subject at hand, he states twelve distinctions through twelve sentences. Hence the word <s>api tu</s> (moreover) is for the purpose of indicating the distinctions. Of these, 'moreover, furthermore' and so on is the first; 'of what' and so on is the second; 'form is <s>Bodhisattva</s>' and so on is the third; 'thus, O Blessed One' and so on is the fourth; '<s>Buddha</s>'

body.text: ityādi pañcamam / yathā ātmetyādi ṣaṣṭham / evamabhāvasvabhāvāḥ sarvadharmā iti saptamam / katamattadityādyaṣṭamam / evameteṣāmityādi navamam / tatkimityādi daśamam / na cetyādyekādaśam / sa cetyādi dvādaśam / kalpiteṣu anabhiniveśābhyāsaniṣṭhāyāṃ tadabhiniveśajanmanaḥ parantatrasya sarvathā nivṛttau sarvākarajñatā bodhisattvena prāpyata iti samudāyārthaḥ /
body.translated_text: and so on is the fifth; 'just as the self' and so on is the sixth; 'thus all <s>dharmas</s> are of the nature of non-existence' is the seventh; 'which is that' and so on is the eighth; 'thus, of these' and so on is the ninth; 'then what' and so on is the tenth; 'and not' and so on is the eleventh; 'and he' and so on is the twelfth. The collective meaning is: when, through the practice of non-attachment toward conceptually constructed [entities], there is the complete cessation of the clinging that gives rise to the other [defilements], <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience in all aspects) is attained by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

body.text: avayavārthastūcyate / uktaṃ bhagavatā "atra mahāyāne śikṣitvā atītānāgatapratyutpannā bodhisattva mahāsattvāḥ sarvākārajñatāmanuprāptā anuprāpsyanti anuprāpnuvanti ceti / tatra na pūrvānta upalabhyate nāparānto na madhyaḥ / tato na sattvā na sarvadharmā na bodhisattvaḥ" iti / sattvāśca sarvadharmāśca bodhisattvaśca pūrvāntāparāntamadhyāni ca sarvametadadvaidhīkāram / tasmātpūrvāntādiṣu bodhisattvo nopaitīti prathamasyārthaḥ / tatkasya hetoriti / tatpūrvāntādīnāmasattvaṃ kutaḥ? hetumāha / rūpāparyantatayetyādi / rūpādaya ākāśa(śa)samāḥ / rūpādiśūnyatāmupādāya / ata ete 'paryantāḥ / pūrvāntāparāntamadhyarahitāḥ / evaṃ bodhisattva iti dvitīyasyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: The meaning of the parts is now stated. The Blessed One has said: 'Having trained here in this <s>Mahāyāna</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> of the past, future, and present have attained, will attain, and are attaining <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>. Therein, neither the past end, nor the future end, nor the middle is apprehended. Therefore neither beings, nor all <s>dharmas</s>, nor the <s>Bodhisattva</s> [are apprehended].' Beings, all <s>dharmas</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, and the past, future, and middle — all of this is non-duality (<s>advaidhīkāra</s>). Therefore, the meaning of the first [sentence] is that the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not approach the past and so on. 'For what reason?' — why are the past and so on non-existent? He states the reason: 'because of the endlessness of form' and so on. Form and the rest are equal to space, by virtue of their emptiness. Therefore they are 'endless' (<s>aparyanta</s>) — devoid of past, future, and middle. 'Likewise the <s>Bodhisattva</s>' — this is the meaning of the second [sentence].

body.text: rūpādikaṃ bodhisattva iti nopaiti nāvagacchati / yasmāt idamapi na vidyate nopalabhyate rūpādi śūnyatāmupādāya / na hi śūnyatāyā rūpādikamasti nāpi bodhisattva iti tṛtīyasyārthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Form and the rest are <s>Bodhisattva</s> — [this means] one does not approach, does not comprehend [them as such]. Because even this does not exist — form and the rest are not apprehended, by virtue of emptiness. For in <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), form and the rest do not exist, nor does the <s>Bodhisattva</s> — this is the meaning of the third [sentence].

body.text: evamiti pratibhāsamānena rūpeṇa / bodhisattvadharmamiti / bodhisattvākhyarūpādi / sarveṇeti skandhadhātvādivargabhedena / sarveṇa sarvamiti sarvayathā bhavati pūrṇāvayavatvād vargāṇām / punaḥ sarvamiti teṣu vargeṣvekaikam / sarvaṃ sarvatheti svena svena itaretaraiśca sarvairanupalabhamānaḥ / taiḥ śūnyatvāt / sarvajñatāmapīti sarvākārabhūtāmapi / so 'ham ityādi / taṃ dharmamiti bodhisattvākhyam / prakaraṇādgamyate prajñāpāramitāmapi sarvākārajñatāmapīti / dharmamiti bodhisattvākhyam / dharmeṇeti prajñāpāramitākhyena / dharme iti sarvākārajñatākhye prāptasya / avavadiṣyāmi prāptaye / naiva kaścitkenacitkvacidityarthaḥ / evameva vādābhāva anuṣṭhānābhāvānna kascinna kenacinna kvacitprāpnotīti caturthasyārthaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Thus' means by form as it appears. '<s>Bodhisattva-dharma</s>' means form and the rest called '<s>Bodhisattva</s>.' 'By all' means through the division into groups such as <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and so on. 'All of all' means as fully as it exists, because of the completeness of the groups' parts. Again, 'all' means each one among those groups. 'All in every way' means not apprehended through its own, through each other's, and through all collectively — because of being empty of them. '<s>Sarvajñatā</s> also' means even that which consists of all aspects. 'I am that' and so on — 'that <s>dharma</s>' means called '<s>Bodhisattva</s>.' It is understood from the context that [this also refers to] <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>. '<s>Dharma</s>' means called '<s>Bodhisattva</s>'; 'by <s>dharma</s>' means by that called '<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>'; 'in <s>dharma</s>' means in that called '<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>' — 'of the one who has attained, I shall instruct for attainment.' Not at all, by no one, anywhere — this is the meaning. Thus, due to the absence of speech and the absence of practice, no one, by no means, nowhere attains — this is the meaning of the fourth [sentence].

body.text: buddha iti buddhatvaṃ sarvākārajñatetyarthaḥ / nāmadheyamātramiti / arthaśūnyaṃ nāma / tathāhi nārthasya svabhāvo nāma prāksaṅketārthamātradarśanāt /
body.translated_text: '<s>Buddha</s>' means Buddhahood, i.e. <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience in all aspects). 'A mere name' means a name empty of referent. For indeed, the referent does not have a name as its inherent nature, since before the convention, only the referent is perceived.

body.text: nāpi nāmnaḥ svabhāvoārthaḥ / aviditārthasya nāmnaḥ kevalasyaiva pratīteḥ / asatyepi cārthe śabdaprayogāt / nirarthakaṃ nāma / ata eva tacca nāmadheyamanabhinivṛttaṃ nāmadheyatvenāsiddham / ato 'nabhinivṛttena bodhisattvanāmnā anabhinirvṛttaṃ sarvākārajñatā nāma na prāpyata iti pañcamasyārthaḥ /
body.translated_text: Nor does the name have the referent as its inherent nature, since the name alone, without knowing the referent, is cognized. And because words are used even when the referent does not exist, the name is without referent. Therefore that name is unproduced — not established as a name. Thus, through the unproduced name '<s>Bodhisattva</s>,' the unproduced <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> called 'name' is not attained — this is the meaning of the fifth [sentence].

body.text: evaṃ tāvatpañcabhirvākyairdharmanairātmyamukhena nāmadheyamukhena ca kalpitasya prāptiḥ pratiṣiddhā / pugalanairātmyamukhenāpi tatpratiṣedhāya ṣaṣṭhaṃ coktam / yathā ātmā ātmeti ca bhagavannucyate ātyantatayā ca bhagavannanabhinirvṛtta ātmeti / atyantatayetyekāntena / anabhinirvṛtta ityasadbhūtaḥ / yathālakṣaṇamasattvāt / yathāśabdāt prakaraṇācca gamyate tatha sarvadharmā bodhisattvaśceti //
body.translated_text: Thus, through five sentences, the attainment of the conceptually constructed is refuted through the approach of <s>dharma-nairātmya</s> (selflessness of phenomena) and through the approach of names. To refute that [attainment] through the approach of <s>pudgala-nairātmya</s> (selflessness of persons) as well, the sixth [sentence] is stated: 'Just as the self — "self, self" is spoken, O Blessed One, but ultimately, O Blessed One, the self is unproduced.' 'Ultimately' means absolutely. 'Unproduced' means non-existent, because it does not possess the defining characteristic, due to non-existence. From the word 'just as' and from the context, it is understood [that this applies to] all <s>dharmas</s> and the <s>Bodhisattva</s> as well.

body.text: paratantrasvabhāvamadhikṛtya saptamaṃ coktam / evamabhāvasvabhāvāḥ sarvadharmaḥ iti / kutaḥ etat? yato mahatyorbhagavatyordvādaśabhirebhirvākyairuddeśaḥ subhūtinā kṛte tata eṣāṃ dvādaśānāmabhidhānakāraṇapraśneṣu śariputreṇa kṛteṣu thavirasubhūtiḥ kāraṇāni krameṇa bruvāṇaḥ saptamasthānakena kāraṇena 'abhāvasvabhāvāḥ sarvadharmā iti' praśnamanudyābhāvasvabhāvatāyāṃ kāraṇamuktvā 'anena paryāyeṇa, śāriputra, abhāvasvabhāvāḥ sarvadharmāḥ' ityupasaṃhāraṃ kṛtavān / tata eṣa pāṭhaḥ pratīyate / subhūteḥ praśnānuvādakāraṇākhyānatadupasaṃhārā iha jñāpakā na tūddeśaḥ / uddeśe 'pi saptamavākyasya prāyeṇa pāṭhabhraṃsā(śā)t / yataḥ saptamavākye trayo viplavāḥ kālena jātāḥ / uttareṇa granthena sahaikavākyatā prathamo viplavaḥ / ekavākyatārthe prathamāṃ vibhaktimapanīya ṣaṣṭhivibhaktiḥ kṛteti dvitīyo viplavaḥ / abhāvasvabhāvatāṃ cāpanīya asvabhāvata paṭhiteti tṛtīyo viplavaḥ / arthaṃ brūmaḥ / evamiti paratantreṇa svabhāvena abhāvasvabhāva eṣāmiti abhāvasvabhāvāḥ sarvadharmāḥ / yadāha / nāsti samyogikaḥ svabhāvaḥ pratītyasamutpannatvāditi / kāraṇasaṃnidhiḥ saṃyogastasmin satyeva bhavatīti saṃyogikaḥ / saṃyogiko yaḥ svabhāvaḥ so 'bhāvaḥ kāraṇaviyoge satyabhāvāt / api ca / yaḥ pratītyasamutpannaḥ so 'nityatvāt paścādabhāvaḥ / na ca vidyamānasya paścādabhāvo ghaṭate virodhāt / tasmādekakṣaṇa eva yo bhāvaḥ sa ekakṣaṇāntareṣvabhāvaḥ / tasmādabhāva eṣāṃ svabhāvaḥ / kiṃ ca, yadanityaṃ tat duḥkhaṃ duḥkhaṃ ca prahātavyam / tato 'pyabhāvasvabhāva eṣām / tasmātparatantreṇāpi svabhāvena bodhisattvo na prāpnotīti saptamasyārthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Taking up the <s>paratantra-svabhāva</s> (dependent nature), the seventh [sentence] is also stated: 'Thus, all <s>dharmas</s> are of the nature of non-existence (<s>abhāva-svabhāva</s>).' Whence is this? Because when, in the presence of the two great [interlocutors], the twelve enunciations are made by <s>Subhūti</s>, then, when questions about the reason for stating these twelve are posed by <s>Śāriputra</s>, the Elder <s>Subhūti</s>, stating the reasons in order, at the seventh position states the reason 'all <s>dharmas</s> are of the nature of non-existence,' and having stated the reason for their nature of non-existence, makes the conclusion: 'By this explanation, <s>Śāriputra</s>, all <s>dharmas</s> are of the nature of non-existence.' From this, this reading is understood. <s>Subhūti</s>'s repetition of the question, statement of reason, and conclusion thereof are indicative here, but not the enunciation [itself]. Even in the enunciation, the seventh sentence has mostly suffered textual corruption. For three corruptions have occurred over time in the seventh sentence: the merging into a single sentence with the following text is the first corruption; removing the first [nominative] case ending and replacing it with the sixth [genitive] case is the second corruption; removing <s>abhāva-svabhāvatā</s> and reading <s>asvabhāvata</s> is the third corruption. We state the meaning: 'thus' means by the dependent nature; 'of the nature of non-existence of these' means all <s>dharmas</s> are of the nature of non-existence. As stated: there is no conjoined inherent nature, because of being dependently arisen. Conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>) is the presence of the cause; what exists only when that is present is 'conjoined' (<s>sāṃyogika</s>). The conjoined inherent nature is non-existent (<s>abhāva</s>), because of non-existence when the cause is absent. Moreover, what is dependently arisen, being impermanent, is subsequently non-existent. And the subsequent non-existence of what exists is not tenable, due to contradiction. Therefore, an entity that exists in a single moment is non-existent in all other single moments. Therefore non-existence is the inherent nature of these [dharmas]. Furthermore, what is impermanent is suffering; and suffering is to be abandoned. Therefore too, their inherent nature is non-existence. Therefore, even through the dependent nature, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not attain [anything] — this is the meaning of the seventh [sentence].

body.text: nanviyamabhāvasvabhāvatā kalpitasyāpi rūpādeḥ prāpnoti / yataḥ kulālāda ghaṭaḥ kuvindātpaṭa utpadyamāno dṛśyate / ata āha / katamattadityādi / katamattatkalpitam / rūpādi yat a[na]bhinirdhūttam / naiva kiñcit sarvaṃ kalpitamasaṃskṛtamityarthaḥ / ata eva nirdeśavākye subhūtinā yuktiruktā- asaṃskṛtāḥ sarvadharmāḥ saṃskarturabhāvāditi / kulālakuvindāderapi kalpitasyāsatvādityarthaḥ / tasmātkalpitasyotpādanirodhādipratiṣedho 'ṣṭamasyārthaḥ /
body.translated_text: But does this nature of non-existence not also apply to conceptually constructed form and the rest? Since a pot is seen to arise from a potter, a cloth from a weaver. Therefore he says: 'Which is that' and so on. Which is that conceptually constructed form and the rest that is unproduced? None whatsoever — everything conceptually constructed is unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>) — this is the meaning. Hence, in the explanatory sentence, <s>Subhūti</s> states the reasoning: 'All <s>dharmas</s> are unconditioned, because of the non-existence of a producer.' Because even the potter, weaver, and so on are conceptually constructed and non-existent — this is the meaning. Therefore, the refutation of production, cessation, and so on of the conceptually constructed is the meaning of the eighth [sentence].

body.text: asyāṃ tu bhagavatyāṃ grāhyatāpi kalpitasya pratiṣiddhā / bālagrāhyatvāt tasya / aṣṭamādūrdhvaṃ trīṇī vākyāni pariniṣpannaṃ svabhāvamadhikṛtya evamityādi / evamiti kalpitena svabhāvena eteṣāmiti paratnatrarūpāṇāṃ yā asvabhāvatā śūnyatā sānabhinirvṛttiriti / sa pariniṣpannasvabhāva ityarthaḥ / yadyevaṃ tadā dharmatāyā dharmādavyatirekād bhrāntikṣaye śūnyatāpi kṣīyeta / atha śūnyatā śāśvatī tadā tadavyatirekād bhrāntikṣaye śūnyatāpi kṣīyeta / atha śūnyatā śāśvatī tadā tadavyatirekād bhrāntirapi śāsva(śva)tī bhavedityata āha / yā cetyādi / yatpariniṣpannaṃ rūpaṃ na te bhrāntisvabhāvāḥ paratantrā dharmā ityarthaḥ / tadevaṃ śūnyatāyāḥ paratantrādavyatirekapratiṣedho navamasyārthaḥ //
body.translated_text: But in this [<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>], even the graspability of the conceptually constructed is refuted, because it is grasped by the childish. The three sentences from the eighth onward take up the <s>pariniṣpanna-svabhāva</s> (perfected nature): 'thus' and so on. 'Thus' means by the conceptually constructed nature; 'of these' means of the dependent forms; 'that which is their lack of inherent nature, their <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), that is the unproduced' — this is the <s>pariniṣpanna-svabhāva</s> (perfected nature), this is the meaning. If so, then since <s>dharmatā</s> (the nature of reality) is not different from <s>dharmas</s>, when delusion ceases, <s>śūnyatā</s> too would cease. But if <s>śūnyatā</s> is eternal, then because of non-difference from it, delusion too would be eternal. Therefore he says: 'and that which' and so on. That which is the perfected form — those dependent <s>dharmas</s> of the nature of delusion are not it — this is the meaning. Thus, the refutation of non-difference of <s>śūnyatā</s> from the dependent [nature] is the meaning of the ninth [sentence].

body.text: tatkimityādi / avyatireke niṣiddhe vyatirekaḥ syāt / tatkimiti tadā katham / anabhinirvṛttimiti śūnyatāmātraṃ bodhisattvam / anabhinirvṛttyāmiti śūnyatāmātraṃ prajñāpāramitāyāmavavadiṣyāmi / na kathaṃcit / nahi jāta śakyo 'vavaditum / nāpi jāto 'rthaḥ prajñāpāramiteti vyatirekapratiṣedho daśamasyārthaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Then what' and so on. When non-difference has been refuted, there might be difference. 'Then what' means 'then how.' 'The unproduced' means <s>śūnyatā</s> alone as <s>Bodhisattva</s>. 'In the unproduced' means in <s>śūnyatā</s> alone as <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, 'I shall instruct.' Not in any way. For what is produced cannot be instructed. Nor has any referent been produced [called] <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> — the refutation of difference is the meaning of the tenth [sentence].

body.text: nanu paratantrarūpaṃ bhrāntireva / nirvṛttāyāṃ ca bhrāntau prāptistadā ka āśrayaḥ śūnyatāyāḥ? atha nirāśrayā na tarhi kasyacit dharmatā / ko vā tasyāḥ śaśaviṣāṇādviśeṣa? śaśaviṣāṇakalpasya ca bodhisattvasya kutaḥ prāptirityāha / na cetyādi / sarvadharmā iti jñeyāḥ skandhādayaḥ / buddhadharmā iti prāptavyā daśabalavaiśāradyādayaḥ / bodhisattvadharmā iti pūrvalabdhā guṇāḥ / yo vā bodhāya carediti bodhisattvaḥ / sarva ete prāptikāle 'nabhinrivṛtito 'nyatreti śūnyatāvyatirekeṇa nopalabhyante / suviśuddhajñānāvyatirekiṇī sarvaśūnyataiva tadānīṃ khyātītyarthaḥ / idamapyanena sūcitam / ya eṣa buddhabodhisattvapṛthagjanāvasthānagāmitvāddharmadhātuvadeva śāsva(śva)taprakāśastasyāsau dharmatā / yāvatparatantrastāvatparatantradharmatā ucyate / parato buddhadharmatā / svābhāvikaśca kāyo buddhānāmucyata ityamekadaśasyārthaḥ /
body.translated_text: Objection: The <s>paratantra</s> (dependent) nature is nothing but delusion itself. And when delusion has ceased, what then is the support of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness)? If it is without support, then it is not a property of anything. What difference is there between it and the horn of a hare? And how can a <s>bodhisattva</s> who is like a hare's horn attain [anything]? To this he says: 'Not so' and the rest. '<s>Sarvadharmāḥ</s>' (all dharmas) means the knowable things such as the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) and so on. '<s>Buddhadharmāḥ</s>' (buddha-qualities) means the attainable qualities such as the ten powers, the fearlessnesses, and so forth. '<s>Bodhisattvadharmāḥ</s>' (bodhisattva-qualities) means the previously acquired virtues. Or, 'one who practices for <s>bodhi</s> (awakening)' is a <s>bodhisattva</s>. All of these, at the time of attainment, 'are not found apart from non-arising' — that is, they are not apprehended apart from <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness). The meaning is: at that time, <s>śūnyatā</s> alone, non-different from supremely pure <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), shines forth. This is also implied by this: that which, because it pervades the stages of <s>Buddha</s>, <s>bodhisattva</s>, and ordinary beings, is like <s>dharmadhātu</s> (the realm of dharmas) itself, eternally luminous — that is its <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature). Insofar as it is <s>paratantra</s> (dependent), it is called the dharmatā of the dependent nature. Beyond that, it is <s>buddhadharmatā</s> (the nature of buddha-qualities). And the <s>svābhāvika kāya</s> (essential body) of the <s>Buddhas</s> is declared — this is the meaning of the eleventh [section].

body.text: dvādaśaṃ vyaktam / sa cedityata ārabhya tatkasya hetorityataḥ prāk / atra cittaṃ nāvalīyata ityādibhiḥ pañcabhiḥ padaiḥ śamathasya pañcākārā ucyante / na bhagnapṛṣṭhī bhavatīti / ekapadena catvāra ākārāḥ / śamayati vyupaśamayati ekotīkaroti cittaṃ samādadhātīti / eṣāmabhāve samādhaye cittasya paścābhdaṅgaprasaṅgāt / atastaireva caturbhiḥ pṛṣṭhabhaṅgapratiṣedhāt na bhagnapṛṣṭhībhavati mānasam / evaṃ ṣaḍbhiḥ padairnavākāraḥ śamatha uktaḥ / bhūtapratyavekṣaṇālokaḥ udyotaḥ / udyotāt trāsastadakaraṇam / akaraṇe[na] pratiṣedhakaraṇāt / tato nottasyatītyekena padena vipaśyanā / na santrasyati na santrāsamāpadyata iti padadvayena yuganaddho mārgaḥ / tathā hi na saṃtrasyatīti na samādhestrasyati tadatyāgāditi śamathāṅgaḥ / saṃprajñānāt trāsaḥ saṃtrāsaḥ / tannāpadyata iti vipaśyanāṅgaḥ / carati prajñāpāramitāyāmiti uddeśaḥ / śeṣeṇa nirdeśaḥ / bhāvayatīti śamathena / upaparīkṣata iti vipaśyanayā / upanidhyāyatītyupanirīkṣamāṇo nipuṇaṃ dhyāyati yuganaddhena mārgeṇeti / dvādaśasyārthaḥ /
body.translated_text: The twelfth [section] is clear. [It runs] from 'If so' through to just before 'For what reason.' Here, by five phrases beginning with 'The mind does not sink,' five aspects of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) are stated. 'One does not become broken-backed' — by this single phrase, four aspects [are indicated]: [the mind] calms, pacifies, becomes one-pointed, and enters into <s>samādhi</s> (concentration). For if these were absent, the mind's entry into concentration would be a later development [i.e., impossible]. Therefore, by these very four [aspects], since the breaking of the back is negated, the mind does not become broken-backed. Thus by six phrases, nine aspects of <s>śamatha</s> are stated. 'The light of examining things as they are' is illumination. From illumination comes fear; the non-performance of that [fear is what is meant]. By non-performance, the preventive action [is accomplished]. Therefore, 'one does not startle' — by this single phrase, <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) [is indicated]. 'Does not become frightened, does not fall into terror' — by this pair of phrases, the <s>yuganaddha mārga</s> (conjoined path) [is indicated]. For 'does not become frightened' means one does not fear <s>samādhi</s>, since one does not abandon it — this is the <s>śamatha</s> component. 'Terror' is the dread arising from discernment; 'does not fall into that' — this is the <s>vipaśyanā</s> component. 'Practices the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>' is the outline. The remainder is the detailed exposition. 'Cultivates' means through <s>śamatha</s>. 'Examines' means through <s>vipaśyanā</s>. 'Contemplates' means 'while closely investigating, meditates keenly through the conjoined path' — this is the meaning of the twelfth [section].

body.text: asyopapattaye trayodaśaṃ coktam / tatkasya hetorityata ārabhya prāk sarvākārajñatāniryāṇā(ṇā)t / tatkasya hetoriti praśnaḥ / uttaraṃ yasminhītyādi / imān dharmāniti sarvadharmān prajñāpāramitāyāṃ saṃmukhībhūtāyām / rūpaṃ kalpitaṃ yāvadvijñānaṃ yāvadbuddhadharmān nopaitīti nopalabhate, tadapratibhāsāt / nopagacchati na vikalpayati nirvikalpatvāt prajñāpāramitāyaḥ / iti svabhāvavikalpau pratiṣiddhau / viśeṣavikalpau pratiṣeddhumāhaḥ / na rūpāderutpādanirodhau / pūrvvamutpanno rūpādiridānīṃ niruddha iti na paśyati / kalpitasya hi yathālakṣaṇamasatvādutpādanirodhau na staḥ / tasmādubhau na paśyati / nanu paratantrasyānivṛttau duṣpariharaḥ kalpitasya pratibhāsaḥ / tatkutastannopeti? atha ṣaḍbhirvākyaiḥ kalpiteṣvanabhiniveśābhyāsāttadabhiniveśajanmanaḥ paratantrasya tadānīṃ nirvṛtiriṣyate / apūrvasyānutpadātpūrvasya ca svarasena vyayāt / tau tarhyanutpādavyayau tasya svabhāvau abhāvasvabhāvāḥ sarvadharmā iti paratantraṃ svabhāvamadhikṛtya vacanāt / sarvametaccetasi nidhāya pṛcchati tatkasya hetoriti / uttaraṃ tathā hityādi / yau hi rūpāderanutpādavyayau tau tasyābhāvau / abhāvau ca na bhāvau virodhāt / yatpunaruktamabhāvasvabhāvāḥ paratantrā iti / abhāvadvayavyabhicārastatra svabhāvārtho na punastādātmyaṃ virodhāt / evamabhedaṃ pratiṣidhya bhedapratiṣedhāyāha / ityanutpādavyayau ca rūpādiśca advayametad advaidhīkāramiti / nanu tadānīṃ rūpāderabhāvādadvayībhāvo na yukta ityata
body.translated_text: The thirteenth [section] is also stated in support of this. [It runs] from 'For what reason?' through to just before 'the exit toward <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience in all aspects).' 'For what reason?' is the question. The answer is 'Because in this' and so forth. 'These dharmas' means all dharmas, when <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> has become directly present. 'Form is conceptually constructed, up to consciousness, up to buddha-qualities — one does not approach' means one does not apprehend them, because they do not appear [as such]. 'Does not resort to, does not conceptualize' — because <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is free from conceptual construction. Thus the own-nature and conceptual constructions are negated. To negate specific conceptual constructions, he says: 'There is no arising or ceasing of form and so on.' 'Previously arisen form and so on has now ceased' — this is not seen. For since what is conceptually constructed does not truly exist according to its characteristics, arising and ceasing do not apply to it. Therefore both are not seen. Objection: If the <s>paratantra</s> (dependent nature) has not ceased, the appearance of the conceptually constructed is difficult to avoid. Then how does one not approach it? By six sentences, through habitual non-attachment to conceptually constructed [things], the cessation of the <s>paratantra</s>, which is born from attachment to them, is accepted at that time — because no new [paratantra] arises and the old one naturally decays. Then those non-arising and non-decay are its own-nature; 'all dharmas are of the nature of non-existence' is stated with reference to the <s>paratantra</s> own-nature. Keeping all this in mind, [<s>Subhūti</s>] asks 'For what reason?' The answer is 'Indeed thus' and so forth. The non-arising and non-decay of form and so on are the non-existence of those [dharmas]. And non-existences are not existences, due to contradiction. As for the statement 'the dependent [things] are of the nature of non-existence,' the meaning of 'own-nature' there is non-divergence from the two types of non-existence, not identity, due to contradiction. Having thus negated non-difference, to negate difference he says: 'Thus non-arising and non-decay and form and so on — this is non-dual, this is non-duality.' Objection: Since form and so on do not exist at that time, non-duality is not appropriate. To this

body.text: āha / yatpunarityādi / naṭra paratantraṃ rūpādi gṛhyate / kiṃ tarhi? yadadvayamutpādavyayavirahāt pariniṣpannamityarthaḥ / pariniṣpanno hi svabhāvo dharmāṇāṃ kalpitābhāvalakṣaṇaḥ / anutpādavyayāvapi dharmāṇāmabhāvalakṣaṇau / tata ekarasatvādeṣāṃ trayāṇāmadvayībhāva iti bhāvaḥ / iti prāptiniryāṇam //
body.translated_text: he says: 'That which is' and so forth. Here, form and so on as the <s>paratantra</s> (dependent nature) is not what is meant. What then? That which is non-dual, due to being free from arising and ceasing, is the <s>pariniṣpanna</s> (perfected nature) — this is the meaning. For the perfected nature of <s>dharmas</s> is characterized by the absence of the conceptually constructed. Non-arising and non-ceasing are also characterized by the absence of dharmas. Therefore, because of the single-taste nature of these three, their non-duality [is established] — this is the intention. Thus [concludes] the exit toward attainment.

body.text: sarvākārajñātāniryāṇamidānīṃ vaktavyam / tatrādau catvāro dharmā upaparīkṣaṇīyāḥ / katamo bodhisattvaḥ katamā sarvākārajñatā katamā prajñāpāramitā katamā upaparīkṣaṇeti / tatra bodhireva sattvastenocyate bodhisattvaḥ / tayā bodhyā yatsarvadharmāṇāṃ sarvākārajñānaṃ nirabhiniveśaṃ sā tatra sarvākārajñatā / āratā āramitā / grasitaskabhitādivacchāndasa ihāgamaḥ / vikalpādyaḥ (dye)pāntīti pāḥ / vikalpapratipakṣā dharmāḥ / tebhyo 'pyāratā viratā yā prajñā seha prajñāpāramitā / yatsarvadharmānnityasukhātmaśāntaśūnyanimittapraṇihitaviviktānāṃ pratyekaṃ tadviparītānāṃ ca ṣoḍaṣānāmārāṇāṃ pratiṣedhena vyupaparīkṣate / tadatropaparīkṣaṇaṃ mahatyorbhagavatyoruktam / tatrordhvamadharamupaparīkṣaṇaṃ tayoruktam / tadevāsyāṃ darśayitumāha / evaṃ bhagavannityataḥ prabhṛti atha khalvāyuṣmān ityataḥ prāk / arthaḥ pūrvavat / atha khalvāyuṣmānityadi / tena hīti yenādvayasyaiṣā gaṇānā kṛtā / advayaśca dharmadhātuḥ / tena kāraṇena bodhisattvopyanutpādaḥ / utpādavirahāddharmadhāturityarthaḥ / paratantrastu svabhāvo neha gaṇyate / tasya paramārthatvāt / paramārthasya nehādhikārāt / kotra doṣa iti cedāha / yadi cet ityādi / duṣkarasya karmaṇaścārikā caraṇam / tāṃ kiṃ kasmāccarati? prayogavīryeṇa / āsṭāṃ prayogavīryam / yāni duḥkhāni karacaraṇaśiraḥ śarīradānāni satvānāṃ kṛtaśaḥ sattvānāmarthāya tāni vā pratyanubhavituṃ kasmādutsaheta / saṃnāhavīryeṇāpi tadā duṣkaracārikāṃ na carenna vādyavaset / tathā hi kāraṇaparatantratvenāparamārthatvāt / aparamārthasya cānabhyasanīyatvāt / viśeṣato duṣkarasyeti codyam / evamukta ityādinā subhūteḥpariṣkārāḥ / tatrānabhyupagamena prathamo nāhamityādinā / yo hi duṣkaracārikāmicchati tasya sā na syādityaniṣṭāpādanaṃ doṣaḥ syāt / na hīti / kuto necchasīti cet / duṣkarasaṃjñayā duṣkaraṃ carato vipratisāriṇaḥ samyaksambodhervyāvṛttiprasaṅgāt / nāpītyādinā dvitīyaḥ parihāraḥ / na bhavatīti na niṣpadyata ityarthaḥ / api tu ityādinā tṛtīyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Now the exit toward <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience in all aspects) is to be stated. Therein, first four dharmas are to be examined: What is a <s>bodhisattva</s>? What is <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>? What is <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>? What is 'examination'? Therein, <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) itself is the being (<s>sattva</s>), hence '<s>bodhisattva</s>' is said. By that <s>bodhi</s>, the knowledge of all <s>dharmas</s> in all their aspects, free from attachment — that is <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> therein. '<s>Āratā</s>' means '<s>āramitā</s>' (having reached the far shore) — like '<s>grasita</s>' and '<s>skabhita</s>' and the like, the grammatical form is Vedic. '<s>Pā</s>' means dharmas that are the antidote to conceptual construction — they 'go to the far shore' [of such constructs]. <s>Prajñā</s> (wisdom) that has 'reached the far shore,' having desisted from even those [antidotal dharmas], is here <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>. That which examines all dharmas by negating each of the sixteen 'delights' (<s>āraṇa</s>) — namely, the attributes of permanent, blissful, self, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, and solitary, along with their respective opposites — that is the 'examination' spoken of by the two venerable ones [<s>Bhagavān</s> and another]. Therein, the higher and lower examination [was explained] by them. To show that very thing in this [text], he says: 'Thus, O <s>Bhagavān</s>' and so forth, from that point up to just before 'Then indeed, the venerable one.' The meaning is as before. 'Then indeed, the venerable one' and so forth. 'By this' means by this reckoning of non-duality that was made. And <s>dharmadhātu</s> (the realm of dharmas) is non-dual. For that reason, a <s>bodhisattva</s> too is non-arising. Being free from arising, [he] is <s>dharmadhātu</s> — this is the meaning. But the <s>paratantra</s> own-nature is not here reckoned, because it is ultimate. And the ultimate is not the subject here. If one asks what the fault is, he says: 'If indeed' and so forth. The practice of difficult conduct is its performance. Why does one perform that? Through exertional vigor. Setting aside exertional vigor — would one endure experiencing the sufferings of giving away hands, feet, head, and body to beings, repeatedly for the sake of beings? Through armor-like vigor too, one would then neither practice the difficult conduct nor abandon it. For it is non-ultimate, being dependent on a cause. And what is non-ultimate is not to be practiced. Especially what is difficult — this is the objection. By 'Thus spoken' and so on, <s>Subhūti's</s> responses [are given]. Therein, the first [response], by non-acceptance, [starting with] 'I do not' and so forth. For one who desires the practice of difficult conduct, that [conduct] would not arise — this would produce the undesired consequence, which would be a fault. 'Not so' [he says]. If asked 'Why do you not desire it?' — because if one practicing the difficult with the notion 'this is difficult' were to experience remorse, there would be the consequence of turning away from <s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (perfect awakening). 'Nor' and so forth is the second response. 'Does not occur' means 'is not produced' — this is the meaning. 'Moreover' and so forth is the third.

body.text:
punaraparamityādinā caturthaḥ / yathā ātmetyādi / sarvaduḥkhāni sarvasāśravāḥ pañcaskandhāḥ / tebhyaḥ sarvebhyaḥ parimocayitavyāḥ / sarveṇeti dhātugatiyonyādibhedena / sarveṇa sarvamiti sarva yathā bhavati tisṛbhirduḥkhātābhiḥ / sarvatheti sarvavyavasāyaiḥ sarvamiti niravaśeṣaṃ mocayitavyāḥ / duḥkhaskandhāditi duḥkharāśeḥ / cittapradoṣaḥ pratighaḥ / yathā ātmā na vidyate sarveṇeti ātmasattvajīvapoṣapuruṣādibhedena / sarveṇa sarva yathā bhavati dṛśyādṛśyabhedāt / sarvatheti skandhadhātvādibhyo bhedena / abhedena ca / kathamabhedena sarvaṃ yathā bhavati? prativargaṃ samastebhyo vyastebhyaśca yathā ātmā tathā sarvadharmā na vidyante / sarveṇeti skandhadhātvādivargabhedena sarveṇa sarva yathā bhavati / vargāṇāṃ paripūrṇāvayavatvāt / punaḥsarva yathā bhavati prativarga te sarva ityarthaḥ / sarvatheti
/ sarveṣu prabhedeṣu ātmani pareṣu ca samastavyasteṣvityarthaḥ / tadevaṃ duṣkaracārikācaraṇā bhāvaprasaṅga(ṅgāḥ) catvāra uktāḥ / caturthena parihāreṇaitadapi sūcitam / duṣkaracārikāyā apyanutpāda eva tattvaṃ tadeva tattvaṃ paśyatā sā caritavyā yatāsau śaktā ca bhavenmahāphalā ca / anutpāde sarvaduḥkhānāmapratibhāsanāt tattvadarśanācca / sarvākārasarvadharmavikalpaprabiṣedhāya hetuḥ sthaviro yadapyāyuṣmān ityetadārabhya sannihitādevamuktaḥśabdāt prāk / atra sarvajñatāpīti sarvākārajñatāpi buddhopītyarthaḥ / tataḥ prāptivikalpapratiṣedhārthamāha / evamukta ityata ārabhya atyaṃtaṃ pratibhātīti yāvat / sarvajñateti sarvākārajñatā anuprāptaiva bhavatītyādita eva sarveṣāṃ dharmadhātumātratvāt dharmadhātośca prakṛtyaiva sarvathā viśuddhatvāditi bhāvaḥ / evamukta ityādinā subhūteruttaram / anutpannasya dharmasyeti bodhisattvākhyasya dharmadhātoḥ / prāptimiti prāptatvaṃ / nāhamicchāmi nāpyabhisamayamiti nāpi prāptābhisamayam / yadihīccheyaṃ tadānutpādamicchato me prāptiḥ prasajyeta / naiva tvicchāmīti na yuktaḥ prāptiprasaṅgaḥ / yuktimapyāha nāpītyādinā / sarva eva dharmo 'nutpāda ityasmin pakṣe hyeṣaḥ prasaṅgaḥ / tatra anutpannena bodhisattvena anutpannā sarvākārajñatā nāpi prāpyate / ayuktatvāditi bhāvaḥ / ubhayoraṇā[nā]dimattvena prāptyayogāt / āheti śāriputra āha / kiṃ punarityādi / yastūbhayoranutpannatve prāptirayuktā / tatkimanyatarotpattau yuktetyarthaḥ / āheti subhūtiranyatarotpattipakṣaṃ vimocayitumāha kiṃ punarityādi / evakāro bhinnakramatvādantaṃ netavyaḥ / anutpanno dharmaḥ
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore' and so forth is the fourth. 'Just as the self' and so on. 'All sufferings' are the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) that are tainted. All beings are to be liberated from all of those. 'By all' means by the classification of <s>dhātus</s> (elements), <s>gatis</s> (destinies), <s>yonis</s> (modes of birth), and so forth. 'All in every way' means all as they exist through the three forms of <s>duḥkhatā</s> (suffering). 'In every manner' means by all determinations.
