'All' means without remainder — they are to be liberated. 'From the mass of suffering' means from the heap of suffering. '<s>Cittapradoṣa</s>' (corruption of mind) is <s>pratigha</s> (aversion). 'Just as the self does not exist, by all' means by the classification of <s>ātman</s> (self), <s>sattva</s> (being), <s>jīva</s> (life-force), <s>poṣa</s> (nourisher), <s>puruṣa</s> (person), and so forth. 'All in every way' means because of the distinction between visible and invisible. 'In every manner' means by the distinction from <s>skandhas</s>, <s>dhātus</s>, and so on — and by non-distinction too. How is it 'all in every way' by non-distinction? Group by group, from both the collective and the individual [perspectives] — just as the self, so all dharmas do not exist. 'By all' means by the classification of groups such as <s>skandhas</s>, <s>dhātus</s>, and so on. 'All in every way' means because of the completeness of the members of each group. Again 'all in every way' means group by group, 'all those' — this is the meaning. 'In every manner' means in all sub-divisions, in self and others, both collectively and individually — this is the meaning. Thus four consequences of practicing difficult conduct have been stated. By the fourth response, this too is implied: even the practice of difficult conduct has non-arising as its reality; one who sees that very reality should practice it, for thereby it becomes both effective and greatly fruitful — because in non-arising, all sufferings do not appear, and because of the vision of reality. [The passage] serving as the cause for the negation of conceptualization regarding all dharmas in all aspects [runs from] 'Elder, that which the venerable one' through to just before 'Thus spoken.' Here, '<s>sarvajñatā</s>' means <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>, and '<s>buddha</s>' is implied. Then, to negate the conceptual construction of attainment, he says: from 'Thus spoken' through to 'appears ultimately.' '<s>Sarvajñatā</s>' means <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> — 'is already attained' and so on, because from the very beginning all dharmas are nothing but <s>dharmadhātu</s>, and because <s>dharmadhātu</s> is by its very nature pure in every way — this is the intention. 'Thus spoken' and so forth is <s>Subhūti's</s> reply. 'Of an unarisen dharma' means of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> designated as '<s>bodhisattva</s>.' 'Attainment' means the state of having attained. 'I do not desire it, nor do I [desire] realization' means 'nor [do I desire] realization that has been attained.' For if I were to desire, then for me who desires non-arising, the consequence of attainment would follow. But since I do not desire at all, the consequence of attainment is not valid. He also states the reasoning: 'Nor' and so forth. For in the position that every dharma whatsoever is non-arising, this consequence [would arise]: the unarisen <s>bodhisattva</s> does not attain even the unarisen <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> — because it is inappropriate — this is the intention. Because of the beginninglessness of both, the conjunction of attainment is impossible. '<s>Āha</s>' (he said) means <s>Śāriputra</s> said. 'What then?' and so forth. If attainment is inappropriate when both are unarisen, then is it appropriate when one of them arises? — this is the meaning. '<s>Āha</s>' means <s>Subhūti</s> says [the following] in order to resolve the position of one-sided arising: 'What then?' and so forth. The particle '<s>eva</s>' should be taken at the end because of its displaced order. 'An unarisen dharma'

body.text:
paścādutpanno vā syāt paścādanutpanna eva vā / tatra dvītīyavikalpe kathamanyatarotpatiḥ? ādye tu vikalpe dharmadhātorutpattivirodha iti bhāvaḥ / tasmādubhayoranutpādāt sādhūktaṃ nāpyanutpannena dharmeṇānutpannā prāptiḥ prāpyata iti yuktaḥ prāptivikalpapratiṣedhaḥ / tasmātsarvadharmāṇāṃ paramārtho dharmadhātuḥ / sa ca prakṛtiprabhāsvaratvādanādinidhanatvācca na prāpyate nāpi prāpnoti, kevalaṃ draṣṭavyaḥ / yattasya darśanaṃ saiva kalpitānāṃ sarvadharmāṇāmanupalabdhiḥ / saiva niratiśayā prajñāpāramitā / tayā parikalpitadharmābhiniveśakṣayāttadabhiniveśahetukāḥ sarvāvaraṇasaṃgrāhiṇaḥ sarvābhūtaparikalpāḥ paratantrākhyāḥ kriyante / pūrveṣāṃ svarasanirodhāt / kāraṇābhāvena pareṣāmanutpādāt / tataḥ prakṛtiprabhāsvaropi bodhisattvākhyo dharmadhāturāgantukairāvaraṇamalairmalinīkṛtaḥ / tena teṣāṃ kṣaye sati tatra kṣayalakṣaṇā viśuddhirapūrvatvāt prāpyate / tadyathā prakṛtyā viśuddhamākāśamāgantukaistuhinarajastamo
'bhradhūmādibhirāvaraṇairmalinīkriyate / paścāttadapāye [kṣaya?]lakṣaṇā viśuddhistena prāpyate / sarvavibhramanivṛttau ca suviśuddhasarvadharmadharmatājñānalakṣaṇā sarvākārajñatā yāpūrvatvāvdodhisattvena labhyate / saiva tasyā viśuddherātmabhūtāyāḥ saṃvedanāprāptyabhisamayaḥ saṃpadyata iti siddhāntaḥ /
body.translated_text: or it may arise afterward, or not arise afterward at all. In the second alternative, how can either one arise? In the first alternative, the meaning is that there is a contradiction with the arising of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of phenomena). Therefore, since both do not arise, it is well said that 'attainment is not attained by an unarisen <s>dharma</s> (phenomenon) with an unarisen attainment' — the refutation of the alternative of attainment is reasonable. Therefore, the ultimate reality of all <s>dharmas</s> is the <s>dharmadhātu</s>. And since it is luminous by nature and without beginning or end, it is neither attained nor does it attain; it is merely to be seen. That seeing of it is itself the non-apprehension of all constructed <s>dharmas</s>. That itself is the unsurpassed <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom). Through it, by the exhaustion of attachment to constructed <s>dharmas</s>, all the false constructions called <s>paratantra</s> (other-dependent), which include all obscurations and are caused by that attachment, cease. Through the natural cessation of the former, and through the non-arising of the latter due to the absence of their cause. Hence, the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, called <s>bodhisattva</s>, though luminous by nature, is defiled by adventitious obscuration-stains. Therefore, when those are exhausted, purification characterized by that exhaustion is attained therein, being unprecedented. Just as space, pure by nature, is defiled by adventitious obscurations such as snow, dust, darkness, clouds, and smoke, and later, upon their removal, purification characterized by [their] exhaustion is attained thereby. And when all confusion has ceased, the knowledge of the true nature of all <s>dharmas</s> in its perfectly pure form — <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience in all aspects) — is obtained by the <s>bodhisattva</s>, being unprecedented. That itself constitutes the realization-attainment-experience of that purification which is its essential nature — this is the established doctrine.

body.text: tatredānīmāgantukāvaraṇaviśuddhiḥ sthavirābhyāṃ vaktavyā / tāṃ śāriputra ārabhate / āheti śāriputra āha / kiṃ punarityādi / utpadyata ityutpādaḥ / para[ta]ntraḥ svabhāvaḥ / kiṃ punaḥ paścādanutpādaḥ? kāraṇābhāvādanutpatterityeka pakṣaḥ / utāho 'nutpādaḥ? sarvākārajñatā teṣāṃ dharmaḥ / pūrvamanutpannatvādyaḥ paścādutpadyata iti dvitīyapakṣaḥ / tatrādye pakṣe anutpannāyāḥ sarvākārajñatāyāḥ kutaḥ prāptiḥ? dvitīyapakṣe sarvākārajñatāyāḥ kāraṇaṃ vaktavyam / abhūtaparikalpaśca śāśvato bhavet kṣayābhāvāditi bhāvaḥ / subhūtirāheti parihāramāha / utpāda utpattiḥ dharmaḥ sarvākārajñatāyāḥ / anutpādo 'nutpattiḥ dharmo 'bhūtaparikalpasyeti ya eṣa bhedaḥ / nāsau pratibhāti jalpituṃ na rocate vaktum / sarvadharmaśūnyatālambane cittasantāne yaiva sarvabhrāntīnāṃ nivṛttiḥ saiva sarvākārajñatāyā utpattiḥ / ato 'syā na kāraṇaṃ vaktavyam / nāpyabhūtaparikalpaḥ śāśvato bhavatīti bhāvaḥ / śāriputra āheti / jalpavikalpapratiṣedhāyāha / anutpādopītyādi / anutpādaḥ pramāna(ṇā)siddhatvātpratibhātyeva rocata eva vaktum / kuto na pratibhātīti kāṅkṣā praśnaḥ / āheti subhūtiruttaramāha / anutpāda evetyādi / jalpa iti mānasaḥ śabdaḥ / pratibhātīti jalpābhidheyaṃ vastu / pratibhānamiti sajalpā buddhiḥ / trayametadanutpāda eva sarvākārajñatāyāṃ dharmatāśarīreṇaiva
body.translated_text: Now, the purification from adventitious obscurations is to be stated by the two elders. <s>Śāriputra</s> begins it. 'Said' means <s>Śāriputra</s> said. 'What then' and so forth. '<s>Utpāda</s>' (arising) means arising; the <s>paratantra</s> (other-dependent) nature. 'What then is non-arising afterward?' — one position is that there is no arising due to the absence of a cause. 'Or is it non-arising?' — <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience) is their <s>dharma</s>. The second position is that which was previously unarisen arises afterward. In the first position, whence is there attainment of the unarisen <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>? In the second position, a cause for <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> must be stated; and the false construction would be eternal, due to the absence of its exhaustion — this is the meaning. '<s>Subhūti</s> said' — he states the resolution. '<s>Utpāda</s>' (arising) means the arising-nature of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>; '<s>anutpāda</s>' (non-arising) means the non-arising-nature of false construction — this is the distinction. 'It does not appear' means 'it is not pleasing to state.' In the mind-stream resting on the emptiness of all <s>dharmas</s>, the very cessation of all confusions is the arising of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>. Therefore, no cause for it need be stated, nor does the false construction become eternal — this is the meaning. '<s>Śāriputra</s> said' — he speaks to refute discursive conceptualization. 'Even non-arising' and so forth. Non-arising, being established by valid cognition, certainly appears, certainly is pleasing to state. 'Why does it not appear?' — this is the question of doubt. 'He said' — <s>Subhūti</s> gives the answer. 'Non-arising itself' and so forth. 'Speech' is the mental word. 'Appears' is the object denoted by speech. 'Appearance' is cognition together with speech. All three are just non-arising within <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>, through the very body of <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature of reality)

body.text: sarvadharmāṇāṃ tasyāṃ pratibhāsāditi bhāvaḥ / evameva atyantaṃ pratibhātītyupasaṃhāraḥ / iti sarvākārajñatāniryāṇam //
body.translated_text: — since all <s>dharmas</s> appear in it — this is the meaning. 'Just so, it thoroughly appears' is the conclusion. Thus ends the exposition of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience in all aspects).

body.text: evamukta ityādinā śāriputraḥ prakṛtameva subhūtervacanaṃ praśaṃsanmārganiryāṇaprastāvanāṃ karoti / sthāpayitavyo niḥsaṃśayaṃ gaṇayitavyaḥ / yato yata eveti yatra yatraiva sthāne niḥsarati uttarati na calati na bhraśyati na vi[ro]dhayati na vyākulayati / evamukta iti / evaṃ prastāvanāyāṃ kṛtāyāṃ etad iti mārganiryāṇe / aniśritā anabhiniviṣṭā dharmā yaistathoktāḥ / na vyativartanta iti na bhrasya(śya)nti / evamukta iti sarvadharmāniśritatāyāmuktayām / atreti anantaroktā sarvadharmāniśritā cāsau paramatvātpāramitā ca / katameti ṣaṇṇāṃ pāramitānāṃ madhye katamā / sārvayānikī yānatrayasādhāraṇī / yaścaiṣā prajñāpāramitaiva / na taharyasyetyata āha / sarvadharmetyādi sugamam / iti hīti yata evaṃ tasmāt / avalīnatvaṃ viṣādaḥ kāṃkṣāyitatvaṃ saṃśayālutā / dandhāyitatvamapratipattiḥ / anyathātvaṃ parāṅmukhībhāvaḥ manasikāreṇeti nirvikalpena manasā / kathamāyuṣmannityādi vikalpakaṃ manasikāraṃ matvā śāriputrasyāyaṃ praśno manasikāreṇa viharantīti yāvat /
body.translated_text: With 'thus spoken' and so forth, <s>Śāriputra</s>, praising the very statement of <s>Subhūti</s> on the main topic, introduces the exposition of the path. 'To be established' means certainly to be reckoned. 'From whatever, from that very' means in whatever place one emerges, transcends, does not waver, does not fall, does not obstruct, does not confuse. 'Thus spoken' — when the introduction has been made thus, 'this' refers to the path exposition. '<s>Dharmas</s> that are unsupported, non-attached' — those described as such. 'Do not transgress' means 'do not fall away.' 'Thus spoken' — when the non-dependence of all <s>dharmas</s> has been stated, 'here' means the just-mentioned non-dependence of all <s>dharmas</s>, which is itself the supreme <s>pāramitā</s> (perfection). 'Which one?' — among the six <s>pāramitās</s>, which one? 'Common to all vehicles' — common to the three vehicles. And that is this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> itself. 'Not then of this' — therefore he says, 'all <s>dharmas</s>' and so forth — easily understood. 'Thus indeed' — since it is so, therefore. 'Non-shrinking' means dejection; 'hesitation' means being full of doubt; 'sluggishness' means indecision; 'alteration' means turning away. 'With mental attention' means with a non-conceptual mind. 'How, O <s>Āyuṣman</s>' and so forth — considering this to be conceptual mental attention, this is <s>Śāriputra</s>'s question, meaning 'dwelling in mental attention.'

body.text: tata ūrdhvaṃ evamukta ityādinā subhūteḥ sādhukārapūrvakaṃ vacanam / tatra vistareṇa codyakaraṇāt sādhukāraḥ / api tvityādinā parihāraḥ / artha eveti / asmadiṣṭameva / icchālakṣaṇatvādarthasya / bhūtapadābhidhāneneti vikalpamanasikārasya viparyayo bhūtapadaṃ bhūtaṃ vastu / tasyābhidhānena savistareṇa / aniṣṭāpādanaṃ hi / codyam / neṣṭābhidhānamityupālambhaḥ / yuktitaśceyamicchati darśayituṃ svayameva pṛcchati / tatkasyetyādi / tabhdū tapadaṃ kutaḥ? sattva ātmā sa iha dṛṣṭāntaḥ / manasikāro vikalpaḥ / sa dārṣṭāntikaḥ / asvabhāvatādirvaiditavyeti sādhāraṇaṃ hetukaṃ netavyaḥ / tatra asvabhāvatā svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā / lakṣaṇamanayorgrāhakatvam / ataśca yathā ātmano 'svabhāvatā tathā manasikārasyāpi / grāhakatvāyogāditi hetuḥ / śeṣeṣu asvabhāvatvāditi hetuḥ / sabhdāvo bhāvatvaṃ tadviraho 'sadbhāvatā / viviktatā abhāvatā acintyatā tadīyacintāyāṃ nirviṣayatvāt / anabhisaṃbodhanatā samyagjñānāviṣayata / ayathābhūtārthatvena mithyāvastutvenā bhisaṃbodhanaṃ saṃyagjñānamasyeti ayathābhutārthābhisaṃbodhanatā / aneneti
body.translated_text: After that, with 'thus spoken' and so forth, is <s>Subhūti</s>'s statement preceded by approval. Therein, the approval is due to the detailed raising of objections. With 'but' and so forth is the resolution. 'The very purpose' — what we intend. Since purpose has the character of intention. 'By the designation of the real' — the opposite of conceptual mental attention is the real, the actual entity. By its designation, in detail. For the objection is the production of the unintended. Not the statement of the intended — this is the criticism. And wishing to show this through reasoning, he himself asks. 'Of what then' and so forth. 'The real' — from where? 'Being' is the self; it is the example here. 'Mental attention' is conceptualization; that is the exemplified. Non-self-nature and the like should be understood as the common reason to be drawn. Therein, 'non-self-nature' is emptiness of own-characteristic. 'Characteristic' of both is [their being] graspers. And therefore, just as there is non-self-nature of the self, so too of mental attention, because of the impossibility of being a grasper — this is the reason. In the remaining cases, 'because of non-self-nature' is the reason. '<s>Sadbhāva</s>' is the state of being; its absence is '<s>asadbhāvatā</s>' (non-existence). 'Distinctness' means non-being; 'inconceivability' means that there is no object in thinking about it. 'Non-fully-awakening' means not being an object of right knowledge; 'non-fully-awakening to things as they really are' means full awakening to falsely constituted entities as false things — this is right knowledge of that. 'By this' means

body.text: yathoktena / evaṃrūpeṇeti bhūtārthapratyavekṣakeṇa / vihāreṇeti śamatharūpeṇa / itiśabdaḥ parivartaparisamāptyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: by what has been stated. 'Of such a form' means by one who examines the real meaning. 'By dwelling' means in the form of <s>śamatha</s> (tranquility). The word 'thus' serves the purpose of concluding the chapter.

body.text: sarvākārajñatāyāṃ caryā caraṇam / cittotpādādayo daśārthāḥ / taddyotakaḥ parivartastatparivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Caryā</s> (practice) in <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> means conduct. The ten topics beginning with the generation of the mind (<s>cittotpāda</s>). The chapter that illuminates that is this chapter.

body.text: āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ
body.translated_text: End of the first chapter of the commentary called <s>Sāratama</s>, composed by <s>Ratnākaraśānti</s>, on the Noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

body.text: sāratamānāmni pañjikāyāṃ ratnākaraśāntiviracitāyāṃ prathamaḥ parivartaḥ //
2. śakraparivarto nāma dvitīyaḥ /
body.translated_text: 2. The second chapter, called the <s>Śakra</s> Chapter.

body.text: uktā sarvākārajñatā / itaḥ prabhṛti mārgajñatā vaktavyā / tasyāmekādaśavastūni / yataḥ śāstram-
body.translated_text: The <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience in all aspects) has been stated. From here onward, <s>mārgajñatā</s> (knowledge of the paths) is to be stated. In that, there are eleven topics. Because the treatise [states] —

children.translated_text: The quality of being outshone and the like, the paths of disciples and solitary realizers,
the great benefit, the path of seeing, with qualities pertaining to this life and the next, // 1-7 //
conduct, aspiration, and the praised, lauded, and commended,
and the supreme dedication and rejoicing-mental attention, // 1-8 //
accomplishment, purity utterly — this is the path of meditation;
the knowledge of the <s>bodhisattvas</s> — thus is <s>mārgajñatā</s> declared. // 1-9 //

body.text: 'dhyāmīkaraṇatādi' śrāvakamārgaḥ / 'mahānuśaṃso ' bodhisattvasya darśanamārgaḥ / bhāvanāmārgasya 'kāritram' / 'adhimukti'manaskāraḥ / 'stutastobhitasaṃ(śaṃ)sitāḥ' / 'pariṇāmanā'manaskāraḥ / 'anumodanā'manaskāraḥ / 'abhinirhāraḥ' / 'atyantaśuddhiśce 'ti / ekādaśavastūni 'mārgajñatā' sā ca 'bodhisattvānāṃ' ityarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: Among those, first, 'the quality of being outshone and the like,' because the treatise [states] —
The quality of being outshone, by the radiances, the fitness of the gods,

children.text: viṣayo niyato vyāptiḥ svabhāvastasya karma ca // 2-1 //
children.translated_text: the determined object, pervasion, the nature, and its function. // 2-1 //

body.translated_text: 'The quality of being outshone and the like' is the <s>śrāvaka</s> (disciple) path. 'The great benefit' is the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s path of seeing. 'Conduct' is of the path of meditation. 'Aspiration' is mental attention. 'Praised, lauded, and commended.' 'Dedication' is mental attention. 'Rejoicing' is mental attention. 'Accomplishment.' 'And utter purity.' These are the eleven topics. '<s>Mārgajñatā</s>' (knowledge of the paths), and that belongs to the '<s>bodhisattvas</s>' — this is the meaning.

body.text: asyāṃ 'yogyatāṃ' cittotpādaḥ dvitīyo (prathamo)'rthaḥ / 'tāṃ prati' tadartham / 'dhyāmīkaraṇatā' mandacchāyīkaraṇaṃ 'devānām' / 'bhābhiḥ' iti bhagavataḥ prakṛtiprabhayā sā dvitīyo 'rthaḥ / 'viṣayo niyataḥ' iti / tasyā eva viṣayapratiniyamastṛtīyo 'rthaḥ / viṣaya'vyāpti'ścaturthaḥ / 'svabhāvaḥ' pañcamaḥ / 'kāritraṃ' ṣaṣṭhaḥ / yadyamī ṣaḍarthāḥ kathametadekaṃ vastu? iha mārgajñatāyā mūlaṃ cittotpādaḥ / tada(d) rahitānāṃ tasyāmayogyatvāt / ata evāsau yogyatocyate / tata evāsau pradhānam / śeṣastasyāḥ paricchedaḥ / pradhānena ca vyapadeśādekavastūcyate /
body.translated_text: In this, 'fitness' is <s>cittotpāda</s> (generation of the mind of awakening), the second (first) topic. 'For that purpose' means for that end. 'The quality of being outshone' means being made dim, 'of the gods.' 'By the radiances' means by the natural radiance of the <s>Bhagavat</s> (Blessed One) — that is the second topic. 'The determined object' — the restriction of the object of that very [radiance] is the third topic. 'Pervasion' of the object is the fourth. 'Nature' is the fifth. 'Function' is the sixth. If these are six topics, how is this one topic? Here, the root of <s>mārgajñatā</s> is <s>cittotpāda</s>, since without it there is no fitness for it. Hence it is called 'fitness.' Therefore it is the principal [topic]; the rest is its specification. And since the designation is by the principal, it is called one topic.

body.text: tatra dhyāmīkaraṇatāmadhikṛtyāha / tena khalu punarityādi / tena samayeneti tasmin kāle / vivakṣātaḥ kārakāṇi bhavantīti karaṇatvam / khalu śabdo vākyālaṅkāre / punaḥ śabdo viśeṣārthaḥ / abhisamayabhedo viśeṣaḥ / sannipatitaḥ samāgamāt / sanniṣaṇṇo niṣadanāt / trayastriṃśānāṃ kāyo nikāyaḥ / tasmin bhavā iti ṭhal / catvāro mahārājā vaiśravaṇadhṛtarāṣṭravirūḍhakavirūpākṣā caturādiṣu dikṣu / teṣāṃ kāyaḥ / tasmin bhavāḥ / eṣa eva trisāhasro lokadhātuḥ sahā / tasyāḥ patiḥ / brahmaṇaḥ kāyastasmin bhavāḥ / iha tūttarapadavṛddhiḥ / caturthasya dhyānasyāśrayaṃ ca śuddhāvāsāḥ / avṛhā atapāḥ sudṛśāḥ sudarśanā akaniṣṭhāśceti / kutaḥ śuddhāvāsāḥ? āryāṇāmeva teṣūtpādāt / teṣāṃ pañcānāṃ nikāyānāṃ pañcaiva sahastrāṇi / etāvanta eta rūpiṇo devanikāyā yathodhvamutkṛṣṭāḥ prabhāprabhāvādibhiḥ / yopītyādi / tepi sanniṣaṇṇāḥ / yopi teṣāṃ avabhāsaḥ sopyabhibhūto dhyāmīkṛto 'bhūt / samakālameveti yopisopi śabdārthaḥ / yogyatā hi cittotpādastadartha dhyāmīkaraṇam / sarvābhibhūrbhagavāniti viditvā tabhdāve spṛhotpādanāt / avabhāsaḥ prabhā / svakarmaṇo vipaktirvipākaḥ / tasmājjātaḥ sahajo nābhisaṃskārika ityarthaḥ / kena kāraṇenābhibhūtaḥ? buddhādhiṣṭhānena buddhasannidhānena / kena kartrā? buddhatejasā buddhasya bhagavataḥ prakṛtiprabhayā / nanu tepi mahānubhāvāḥ kasmānna praticakrurityata āha buddhānubhāveneti / buddhānubhāvena sarvānubhāvaḥ pratihanyataḥ iti bhāvaḥ / dhyāmīkaraṇatā //
body.translated_text: Regarding the quality of being outshone, he says 'at that time' and so forth. 'At that time' means at that moment; instrumentality arises from the intention to speak, hence it is [in] the instrumental. The word 'indeed' is a sentence-ornament. The word 'again' serves the purpose of distinguishing — the distinction being the division of <s>abhisamaya</s> (realization). 'Assembled' means through gathering. 'Seated' means through sitting. The body (<s>kāya</s>) of the Thirty-three — their group (<s>nikāya</s>); 'those born in it' takes the <s>ṭhal</s> suffix. The Four Great Kings are <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, and <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, in the four directions. Their host; those born in it. This very three-thousandfold world-realm is <s>Sahā</s>; its lord. The host of <s>Brahmā</s>; those born in it. Here however, the compound takes augmentation of the final member. And the <s>Śuddhāvāsas</s> (Pure Abodes) are the support of the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation): <s>Avṛha</s>, <s>Atapa</s>, <s>Sudṛśa</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, and <s>Akaniṣṭha</s>. Why <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s>? Because only <s>āryas</s> (noble ones) are born there. Of those five groups, there are five thousand each. So many are these form-realm divine groups, increasingly excellent upward in radiance, glory, and the like. 'Those who also' and so forth — they too were seated. 'Whichever radiance of theirs — that too was outshone, made dim.' 'At the very same time' — this is the meaning of the words 'whoever' and 'whatever.' For the fitness is the <s>cittotpāda</s>; for its sake is the outshining — since knowing 'the <s>Bhagavat</s> outshines all,' aspiration is produced in [their] being. 'Radiance' means light. 'Born from the ripening of one's own <s>karma</s>' — <s>vipāka</s> means ripening; born from that means innate, not fabricated — this is the meaning. By what cause was [the radiance] outshone? By the <s>Buddha</s>'s empowerment, by the <s>Buddha</s>'s presence. By what agent? By the <s>Buddha</s>'s splendor, by the natural radiance of the Blessed <s>Buddha</s>. Now, they too are of great power — why did they not resist? To this he says 'by the <s>Buddha</s>'s might' — all might is overcome by the <s>Buddha</s>'s might — this is the meaning. [This is] the quality of being outshone.

body.text: atha khalvityādi / antikāditi sakāśāt / prajñāpāramitāmiti bodhisatvānāṃ mahāsatvānāmityanena sambandhaḥ / mārgajñatāmityarthaḥ /
body.translated_text: Now, 'at that time' and so forth. 'From the presence of' means from the proximity. '<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>' — this connects with 'of the <s>bodhisattvas</s> <s>mahāsattvas</s>.' The meaning is <s>mārgajñatā</s> (knowledge of the paths).

body.text: upadiśyata iti upadeśaḥ / tasyā evārthasyāvagamāya vādo 'vavādaḥ tadanubandhāya śāsanī tatsahitā seti samāsaḥ /
body.translated_text: That which is taught is an instruction (<s>upadeśa</s>). The counsel (<s>avavāda</s>) is discourse for the understanding of that very meaning; the precept (<s>śāsanī</s>) is for its continuation — thus is the compound [formed].

body.text: sthātavyaṃ śrutamayyā prajñayā / śikṣitavyaṃ cintāmayyā / yogamāpattavyaṃ bhāvanāmayyā /
body.translated_text: One should abide in wisdom born of hearing (<s>śrutamayī prajñā</s>). One should train in wisdom born of reflection (<s>cintāmayī</s>). One should apply oneself to yoga through wisdom born of meditation (<s>bhāvanāmayī</s>).

body.text: ānubhāvādayaḥ prabhāvaparyāyāḥ / tadānubhavenetyuddeśaḥ / itarābhyāṃ nirdeśaḥ / tejaseti pratibhānaśakte rodhāya / kena prabhāvena? adhiṣṭhāneneti prabodhakena / iyatā granthena yogyatāyāḥ prastāvanāṃ kṛtāyāṃ tāmāha / yairityādinā utpāditavyāntena iti yogyatā //
body.translated_text: Words like <s>ānubhāva</s> (power) and so on are synonyms of <s>prabhāva</s> (influence). 'By that influence' is the general statement. The other two [terms] are the detailed explanation. '<s>Tejas</s>' (brilliance) serves to counteract the power of eloquence. By what influence? 'By empowerment (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>)' — meaning by the awakening [power]. Having thus made the introduction of fitness with this extent of text, he states that [fitness] with the passage beginning 'by those' — the fitness being [expressed by the passage] ending with 'to be generated.'

body.text: yetvityādi / hīnamārgalabhyaṃ nirvāṇaṃ samyaktvam tasmin niyamaḥ samyaktvaniyāmaḥ / taṃ avakrāntāḥ prāptāḥ / baddhasīmāno baddhasetavaḥ / tadyathā śrotaāpannasaptaktabhdavaparamaḥ / dvitrijanmā kulaṃkulaḥ / anuttarā (ra)samyaksaṃbodhinimittaṃ yat punaḥ punaḥ saṃsaraṇaṃ tasmai cittamutpādāyatumabhavyāḥ / iti śamaikayānaiḥ śrāvakairuttamabodheḥ kadācidapyakāmanādyogyatāyā viṣayapratiniyamaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Those who' and so on. <s>Nirvāṇa</s> attainable by the lesser path is '<s>samyaktva</s>' (correctness); the fixed determination toward it is '<s>samyaktva-niyāma</s>' (the certainty of correctness). 'Entered' means attained. 'Of fixed boundaries, of fixed bridges' — that is, for example, the <s>Śrotaāpanna</s> (stream-enterer) with seven births as the maximum; the <s>Kulaṃkula</s> (family-to-family) with two or three births. They are unable to generate the mind [directed] toward unsurpassed perfect awakening, which requires repeated transmigration. Thus, by the <s>Śrāvakas</s> of the one vehicle of quiescence, the determination of the domain of unfitness even at any time for the highest awakening [is established].

body.text: api tvityādi utpādayerannityetadantena vyāptiḥ / śrāvakairapi bodhipariṇatikaiḥ samyaksambodhau cittasyotpādanāt / te hi svāṃ bodhimadhigamyāpi buddhabodhisattvānāṃ lokottarāṃ vibhūtiṃ dṛṣṭvā vañcitamivātmānaṃ manyamānāstathāgatairadhiṣṭhitāstadvodhau cittamutpādyācalyabhūmikabodhisattvavannirmitābhirupapattibhirbodhicaryāṃ caritvā parāṃ bodhimadhigacchantīti vyāptiḥ //
body.translated_text: 'But' and so on — with the passage ending 'they would generate,' there is the [statement of] pervasion. Because even by <s>Śrāvakas</s> who dedicate [merit] toward awakening, the mind is generated for perfect complete awakening. For they, even having realized their own awakening, seeing the supramundane glory of the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, considering themselves as if deceived, being empowered by the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, generate the mind toward that awakening, and like <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of the immovable stage, practicing the <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct through emanated rebirths, they attain the supreme awakening — thus the pervasion.

body.text: nāhaṃ kuśalamūlasyāntarāyaṃ karomīti / svabhāvaḥ kuśalarāśiḥ / sarvakuśaladharmasaṃgrāhakatvāccittotpādasyeti kuśalapakṣatvaṃ yogyatāyāḥ svabhāvaḥ / viśiṣṭebhyo hi dharmebhyo viśiṣṭatamā dharmā adhyālambitavyā iti kāritram / viśiṣṭebhya iti bodhicittasaṃgṛhītebhyaḥ / hetau pañcamā / viśiṣṭatamā dharmā iti mahāyānasaṃgṛhītāḥ phalahetubhūtāḥ / adhyālambitavyā iti prāptavyāḥ / tasmānnāntarāyaṃ karomīti śabdārthaḥ / iti dvividhamahāyānaprāpaṇaṃ bodhicittasya kāritram //
body.translated_text: 'I do not create an obstacle to the wholesome root.' The intrinsic nature [of the wholesome root] is the accumulation of wholesome [merit]. Because the generation of the mind [of awakening] gathers all wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, the nature of fitness is its belonging to the wholesome class. The function [of this fitness] is that from distinguished <s>dharmas</s>, even more distinguished <s>dharmas</s> are to be aspired to. 'From distinguished' means from those comprised by <s>bodhicitta</s> (the awakening mind). The fifth [case-ending is used] in the causal sense. 'More distinguished <s>dharmas</s>' means those comprised by the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, which are both result and cause. 'To be aspired to' means to be attained. Therefore, 'I do not create an obstacle' — this is the literal meaning. Thus, the twofold leading to the <s>Mahāyāna</s> is the function of <s>bodhicitta</s>.

body.text: tadevaṃ kecidvodhicittotpādanārthamutsāhitāḥ purvamutpāditabodhicittāstu saṃpraharṣitāḥ / evamutpāditabodhicittvatvādubhayepi te bodhisattvā
body.translated_text: Thus, some have been encouraged to generate <s>bodhicitta</s> (the awakening mind), while those who had previously generated <s>bodhicitta</s> have been delighted. Having thus generated <s>bodhicitta</s>, both groups, being <s>Bodhisattvas</s>

body.text: mahāsattvāḥ santo mārgajñatāyāmutsāhitāḥ / ata āha / atha khalvityādi / sādhustvamiti mahataḥ parārthasya karaṇāt / bhagavataḥ kṛtajñairit / yathā pūrvaṃ jinaputrasya bhagavatastacchrāvakairbahukṛtaṃ tathāsmābhirbhagavataḥ śrāvakairbhagavatputrāṇāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ bahukartavyamiti kṛtajñatārthaḥ / tatkasya hetoriti / tatkṛtajñatvaṃ kena prakāreṇa? pūrvakā eva paurvakāḥ / brahma nirvāṇaṃ tasmai caraṇaṃ brahmacaryam / taccaraṇaṃ bodhāyeti bodhaye / bodhicaryāṃ caratīti yāvat / yairiti vibhaktipratirūpako nipāto yathārthaḥ avodita iti samprasāraṇam / vada vyaktāyāṃ vācityasya yajāditvāt / avavadita iti kvacitpāṭhaḥ / tatra vada sthairya ityayaṃ dhāturanekārthatvāt / anuparigrahītavyā ityavavaditavyāḥ / anuparivārayitavyā iti anuśāsitavyāḥ / uttarayoḥ padayoḥ saṃśabdaḥ samyagarthaḥ / asmābhirapīti śrāvakairapi / ātmasa [jā]tīyeṣvapyātmavyavahārāt / sādhu cetyavahitaśrotratayā / suṣṭhu cetyavahitamanaskatayā / manasikurviti cintābhāvanābhyām / prajñāpāramitāyāṃ sthātavyamiti mārgajñatāyāṃ veditavyam /
body.translated_text: and <s>Mahāsattvas</s> (great beings), are encouraged in <s>mārgajñatā</s> (knowledge of paths). Therefore he says, 'Now then' and so on. 'Well done, you' — because of performing the great benefit of others. 'Of the <s>Bhagavat</s>, being grateful' — means: just as formerly much was done by the <s>Bhagavat</s>'s <s>Śrāvakas</s> for the son of the Victorious One, so we, being <s>Śrāvakas</s> of the <s>Bhagavat</s>, have much to do for the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who are the <s>Bhagavat</s>'s children — this is the meaning of gratitude. 'For what reason?' — by what manner is there this gratitude? 'Former' means 'of earlier times.' <s>Brahma</s> is <s>Nirvāṇa</s>; the conduct toward it is <s>brahmacarya</s> (holy life); that conduct toward awakening is [expressed as] 'for awakening' — meaning they practice the <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct. 'By those' — the particle <s>yair</s> resembles a case-ending but means 'in the manner that.' '<s>Avodita</s>' — with vowel strengthening. From the root <s>vad</s> meaning 'clear speech,' because it belongs to the <s>yaj</s>-class. Some read '<s>avavadita</s>.' There the root <s>vad</s> means 'steadfastness,' because of multiple meanings. 'To be tended to' means to be counseled. 'To be attended to' means to be instructed. In the last two words, the prefix '<s>sam</s>' means 'correctly.' 'By us also' — even by <s>Śrāvakas</s>, because of the use of the word 'self' even for those of one's own kind. 'Well' — with attentive ears. 'Excellently' — with attentive mind. 'Attend to' — through reflection and meditation. 'One should abide in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>' should be understood as [abiding] in <s>mārgajñatā</s> (knowledge of paths).

body.text: tatrādau śrāvakamārgaḥ / tatra darśanamārgamadhikṛtyāha / śūnyatāyāmityādi / aviparītatvāccatvāri satyāni / āryāṇāṃ satyatvena pratibhānti na bālānāṃ tasmāttānyevāryasatyāni / duḥkha samudayo nirodho mārgaśca / tatra duḥkhaṃ saṃsāriṇaḥ skandhāḥ / duḥkhahetuḥ samadayaḥ / duḥkhakṣayo nirodhaḥ / tatprāpakaṃ jñānaṃ mārgaḥ / eṣāṃ caturṇāmāryasatyānāṃ ya ākārāsteṣāṃ śūnyatāyāṃ tiṣṭhatā śūnyatāṃ paśyatā prajñāpāramitāyāmiti śrāvakīye darśanamārge sthātavyaṃ samāhitena cetasā / śūnyatādarśanaṃ cānupalambha eva / tataḥ śāstram-
body.translated_text: There, first is the <s>Śrāvaka</s> path. Regarding the path of seeing (<s>darśana-mārga</s>), he says 'in emptiness' and so on. Because they are unerring, [they are] the four truths (<s>satyas</s>). They appear as truths to the <s>Āryas</s> (Noble Ones), not to the childish — therefore they are called <s>Āryasatyas</s> (Noble Truths). [They are:] suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>), origination (<s>samudaya</s>), cessation (<s>nirodha</s>), and path (<s>mārga</s>). Among these, suffering is the aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>) of the one in <s>saṃsāra</s>. The cause of suffering is origination. The cessation of suffering is <s>nirodha</s>. The knowledge that leads to it is the path. One should abide in the path of seeing of the <s>Śrāvaka</s> by contemplating the aspects of these four Noble Truths while abiding in emptiness, seeing emptiness, in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> — with a concentrated mind. And the seeing of emptiness is precisely non-apprehension. Therefore the treatise [states]:

children.translated_text: Through the non-apprehension of the aspects of the four Noble Truths,
this path of the <s>Śrāvakas</s> should be known as belonging to the method of <s>mārgajñatā</s> (knowledge of paths). // 2-2 //

body.text: śrāvakapiṭake ca satyanāṃ ṣoḍaśākārāḥ paṭhayante / duḥkhamanityato duḥkhato 'nātmataḥ śūnyataśca parijñeyam / samadayo hetutaḥ samudayataḥ prabhavataḥ pratyayataśca / nirodho nirodhataḥ śāntataḥ praṇītato niḥśa(sa)raṇataśca / mārgo mārgato nyāyataḥ pratipattito niryāṇikataśceti // amī neha gṛhyante / ye tu mahatyorbhagavatyoḥ paṭhitāsta iha gṛhyante / pratyāsatteḥ śrāvakabodheśca lāghaveneti
body.translated_text: In the <s>Śrāvaka</s> collection, sixteen aspects of the truths are recited. Suffering is to be fully known as: impermanent, suffering, non-self, and empty. Origination: as cause, as arising, as production, and as condition. Cessation: as cessation, as peace, as excellence, and as escape. Path: as path, as method, as practice, and as leading out. These are not taken here. But those recited in the two great Noble [sūtras] are taken here — because of proximity, and because the <s>Śrāvaka</s>'s awakening is easily

body.text: prāpaṇāt / tatra duḥkhaṃ caturbhirākārairmanasikaroti pūrvavat / anityato duḥkhato 'nātmataḥ śāntataśca yathākramamudayavyayayogitvāt pratikūlatvāt ātmavilakṣaṇatvāt / ātmaśūnyatvācca / ātmaśūnyo hi śāntaḥ / tadyathā kuṇapaḥ / samudayamekādaśabhirākāraiḥ / tatra caturbhirākāraiḥ prahāṇārhattvajñāpanārtham / rogato gaṇḍataḥ śalyato 'ghataśca duḥkhahetutvāddaḥkhotkarṣahetutvāduruddharatvāt / aihikāmatrikaduḥkhahetutvena pāpasādharmyācca / punaścaturbhiḥ śa(sa)kya(tya)tvaparijñāpanārtham / parataḥ pralobhadharmataścalataḥ prabhaḍgurataśca / ātmā hi hātumaśakto 'yaṃ tu paraḥ / pratikṣaṇavināśitvāt / pralopadharmā ca / arhabhdirunmūlitatvāt / calaśca prakṛtena mārgeṇa bhaṅgitvāt prabhaṅguraśca / ātaptakāritārtha punastribhiḥ / bhayata upadravata upasargataśca / aśanipātādivabhdayahetutvāt / bhūtarākṣasādisādharmyāt durbhikṣaparacakrādisādharmyācceti / pratilomaḥ pratītyasamutpādo avidyānirodhāt saṃskāranirodha ityata ārabhya evamasya kevalasya mahato duḥkhaskandhasya nirodho bhavatīti yāvat / tatra niruddhirnirodha iti nirodhasatyam / nirudhyate 'neneti nirodho mārgasatyaṃ saptabhirākāraiḥ / anātmataḥ śāntato viviktataḥ śūnyata ānimittataḥ apraṇihitato 'nabhisaṃskārataśca / ātmā hi yogino duḥkhātmanaḥ skandhāḥ / ato duḥkhābhāvādanātmā kleśopaśamācchāntaḥ / duḥkhakleśāvaśucī tayorūpaśamādviviktaḥ / śūcirityarthaḥ / ātmātmīyavirahācchūnyaḥ / sarvasaṃskṛtanimittābhāvādānimittaḥ / traidhātuke praṇidhānaṃ praṇihitam / tat kṣayādapraṇihitaḥ / āyatyāṃ karmābhisaṃskārābhāvādanabhisaṃskāraḥ / mārgasatyamapyebhireva saptabhirākāraiḥ / nirodhaprāpako hi mārgaḥ / tato 'nātmaśāntaviviktādiprāpakatvānmārgopyanātmā śānto viviktaḥ śūnya ānimitto 'praṇihito 'nabhisaṃskāraśca / evamekonatriṃśadākāra iha śrāvakamārga āsu tabdodhiprāpaṇāt / sa caiṣāmākārāṇāmanupalambhena mārgajñatāyāṃ praviśati /
body.translated_text: attained. There, one contemplates suffering through four aspects, as before: as impermanent, as suffering, as non-self, and as peaceful — respectively because of being subject to arising and destruction, because of being disagreeable, because of being unlike the self, and because of being empty of self. For what is empty of self is peaceful — like a corpse. Origination [is contemplated] through eleven aspects. Of these, through four aspects to indicate the worthiness of abandonment: as disease, as boil, as thorn, and as affliction — because of being the cause of suffering, the cause of extreme suffering, and being difficult to remove; and because of being the cause of suffering in this life and the next, and of resemblance to evil. Again through four to indicate that it can be fully known: as other, as subject to decay, as unstable, and as fragile — for the self is impossible to abandon, but this [origination] is 'other'; because of perishing from moment to moment; subject to decay; and by the noble path of uprooting, unstable; and because of breaking by its natural path, fragile. The purpose of the heated [contemplation] again through three: as fear, as calamity, and as disaster — because of being a cause of fear like thunderbolts, because of resemblance to <s>bhūtas</s> and <s>rākṣasas</s>, and because of resemblance to famine, foreign invasion, and the like. The reverse dependent origination — from the cessation of ignorance comes the cessation of formations, beginning thus, up to 'thus there is the cessation of this entire great mass of suffering.' There, the state of being ceased is cessation — this is the truth of cessation. That by which [things] are ceased is cessation — this is the truth of the path, [contemplated] through seven aspects: as non-self, as peaceful, as secluded, as empty, as signless, as wishless, and as non-fabricated. For the self of the practitioner is the aggregates that are the nature of suffering; therefore, from the absence of suffering, [it is] non-self; from the pacification of defilements, peaceful; since suffering and defilements are impure, from their pacification, secluded — meaning pure; from being devoid of self and what belongs to self, empty; from the absence of all conditioned signs, signless; since aspiration toward the three realms is <s>praṇihita</s> (wishful intention), from its exhaustion, wishless; from the absence of karmic fabrications in the future, non-fabricated. The truth of the path too [is contemplated] through these same seven aspects — for the path leads to cessation; therefore, being the means to attain non-self, peaceful, secluded, and so on, the path too is non-self, peaceful, secluded, empty, signless, wishless, and non-fabricated. Thus the <s>Śrāvaka</s> path has twenty-nine aspects here, because it leads to their [the Śrāvakas'] awakening. And through the non-apprehension of these aspects, it enters into <s>mārgajñatā</s> (knowledge of paths).

body.text: tena hītyādi / yena hīnamārgaṃ bhāvayato bodhisattvasyānupāyakuśalasya hīnabodhau pāta āśaṃkyate / tena hi kāraṇenāsyāṃ mārgajñatāyāṃ mahāsannāho mahadupāyakauśalam / sannaddhena taddharmitena bhavitavyamātmarakṣārtham / tatrāyaṃ mahān sannāho yaduta sarvākārajñatāpratisaṃyuktairmanasikārairbhāvanā karttavyā / vyutthitena ca sarvaṃ tatkuśalamūlamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayitavyam / taccānupalambhayogeneti / iti śrāvakāṇāṃ darśanamārgaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Therefore' and so on. Because for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who cultivates the lesser path without skillful means, there is the danger of falling into the lesser awakening — therefore, in this <s>mārgajñatā</s>, great armor is [needed], great skillful means. One endowed with that quality must [be equipped] for the protection of oneself. And this great armor is that the cultivation should be done with mental attention connected with <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience in all aspects). And when one arises [from meditation], all that wholesome root should be dedicated to unsurpassed perfect awakening. And that should be through the method of non-apprehension. Thus is the <s>Śrāvaka</s> path of seeing.

body.text: ita ūrdhvaṃ nirodhabhāgīyāni / na rūpe sthātavyamityetadārabhyānena manasikāreṇeti yāvat / tatra na buddhatve sthātavyamityetadante ūṣmā / tata ūrdhva iti hi buddhatvamiti na sthātavyamityetadantena mūrdhā / tato vijñānaṃ śūnyamupalabhyate vetyetadantena kṣānti / śeṣāṇyagradharmaḥ / tatra rūpādiṣvasthānama [na] bhiniveśa ūṣmā / rūpādīnāmidantayā svalakṣaṇānupalambho mūrdhā / rūpādīnāṃ dvayānupalambhaḥ kṣāntiḥ / śūnyaṃ ityanupalambha upalabhyata iti upalambhaḥ / tasmāt śūnyamupalabhyatevetyapi dvayam / śrotaāpattiphalādīnāṃ viśeṣeṣvasthānamagradharmaḥ / tasmādasyāṃ bhagavatyāmanyathaiva śāstrapāṭha unneyaḥ-
body.translated_text: From here onward are the factors conducive to cessation (<s>nirodha-bhāgīya</s>). Beginning with 'one should not abide in form' up to 'by this mental attention.' There, up to 'one should not abide in Buddhahood' is <s>ūṣmā</s> (warmth). From there onward, up to 'for Buddhahood is not something to abide in' is <s>mūrdhan</s> (summit). Up to 'is consciousness empty or is it apprehended?' is <s>kṣānti</s> (acceptance). The remainder is <s>agradharma</s> (supreme dharma). There, non-attachment to form and such — that is, non-grasping — is <s>ūṣmā</s> (warmth). The non-apprehension of the specific characteristics of form and such in terms of 'this-ness' is <s>mūrdhan</s> (summit). The non-apprehension of duality in form and such is <s>kṣānti</s> (acceptance). 'Empty' is non-apprehension; 'is apprehended' is apprehension — therefore 'is consciousness empty or apprehended?' is also duality. Non-abiding in the distinctions of the fruit of stream-entry and so on is <s>agradharma</s> (supreme dharma). Therefore, in this Noble [sūtra], the reading of the treatise should be inferred differently:

children.text: asthānamūṣmā rūpādau mūrdhā taditi hīti yat /
children.translated_text: Non-attachment to form and such is <s>ūṣmā</s> (warmth); <s>mūrdhan</s> (summit) is [the contemplation] 'this, thus';
<s>kṣānti</s> (acceptance) is [the contemplation] 'form and such are neither permanent nor impermanent' — non-abiding in duality.
And that which is non-abiding in the distinctions of the fruits of the Noble Ones here,
that is to be known as <s>agradharma</s> (supreme dharma) on the path of the Noble <s>Śrāvaka</s>.

body.text: atra na cakṣuḥ saṃsparśe sthātavyamiti / indriyaviṣayavijñānasannipāte sati yaḥ sukhādivedanotpattyanukūlasyendriyavikārasya paricchedakaḥ sādṛśyamātreṇa sa sukhādivedanājanakaḥcaitasikaḥ sparśa ityucyate / indriyavikāraṃ sādṛśyena spṛśatīti kṛtvā / ata indriyabhedāccakṣuḥsaṃsparśo yāvanmanaḥsaṃsparśaḥ / ukta cābhidharme "trikasannipāte idriyavikāraparicchedaḥ sparśaḥ vedanotpattisanniśrayadānakarmakaḥ" iti / śubhaṃ śuci aśubhamaśuci / asaṃskṛtaprabhāvitaṃ kleśāvidyākṣayasyāsaṃskṛtatvāt / imaṃ lokamitikāmadhātum / tatraiveti akāmini loke / ihaivetyasminneva janmani / anupadhiśeṣa iti upadhayaḥ skandhāḥ / ta eva śeṣāḥ sopadhiṣeśe tadviparyayādanupadhiśeṣaḥ / buddhaparinirvāṇeti / saṃsāranirvāṇayorapratiṣṭhitena / yathākramaṃ sarveṣāṃ kleśikadharmaparikṣayāt, anāśravāṇāṃ ca dharmāṇāmanantānāṃ jagadarthāya yāvadākāśamavasthānāt / na ca tato vyutthita iti prāptāparihāṇitaḥ / na sthito nāsthita ityapratiṣṭhitamānasattvādavyutthānācca / na viṣṭhito naviṣṭhita iti pravāhayogena pūrvavat / śeṣaṃ subodhamityagradharmaḥ / ityuktāni śrāvakamārganirvedhabhāgīyāni //
body.translated_text: Here, regarding 'one should not abide in eye-contact' — when there is the conjunction of sense faculty, object, and consciousness, that which determines the modification of the sense faculty that is conducive to the arising of pleasant and other <s>vedanā</s> (feelings), by mere resemblance, that mental factor which produces pleasant and other <s>vedanā</s> is called <s>sparśa</s> (contact) — because it 'touches' the modification of the sense faculty by resemblance. Therefore, due to the differentiation of sense faculties, there is <s>cakṣuḥ-saṃsparśa</s> (eye-contact) up to <s>manaḥ-saṃsparśa</s> (mind-contact). And it is stated in the <s>Abhidharma</s>: '<s>Sparśa</s> is the determination of sense-faculty modification upon the conjunction of the triad, having the function of providing the basis for the arising of <s>vedanā</s>.' '<s>Śubha</s>' means pure; '<s>aśubha</s>' means impure. 'Produced by the unconditioned' — because the destruction of <s>kleśa</s> (afflictions) and <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) is unconditioned. 'This world' means the <s>kāmadhātu</s> (desire realm). 'There itself' means in the world without desire. 'Here itself' means in this very birth. Regarding '<s>anupadhiśeṣa</s>' (without remainder of substrata) — <s>upadhis</s> are the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates); they themselves are the remainder in <s>sopadhiśeṣa</s> (with remainder); by its opposite, <s>anupadhiśeṣa</s>. 'The <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of the <s>Buddha</s>' — by the non-abiding in either <s>saṃsāra</s> or <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Respectively, because of the complete exhaustion of all afflicted <s>dharmas</s>, and because the infinite undefiled <s>dharmas</s> remain as long as space for the benefit of beings. 'And not risen from that' — because of non-deterioration of what has been attained. 'Neither abiding nor not abiding' — because the mind is non-abiding and because of non-arising. 'Neither established nor not established' — as before, through the continuity of the stream. The rest is easy to understand — thus <s>agradharma</s> (supreme dharma). Thus the <s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s> (penetration) stages of the <s>śrāvaka</s> path have been explained.

body.text: buddhānubhāvāt khaṅgamārgaprastāvanāya keṣāñciddevaputrāṇāṃ vitarko 'bhūt tamāha / atha khalu tatretyādinā / keṣāñciditi ye śrāvakamārgamapi subhūtinā deśyamānaṃ gaṃbhīraṃ menire / kathaṃ yakṣāṇām? tairuccāraṇāt / kathaṃ yakṣarutādīni? tabhdāṣātvāt / tatra rutānītyuddeśaḥ / śeṣeṇa nirdeśaḥ / mantritāni vākyāni / pravyāhṛtāni vākyasamūhāḥ / bhāṣate padavākyaiḥ / pravyāharati vākyasamūhaiḥ / deśayatītyavavadatī / upadiśatītyanuśāsti / atha khalvāyuṣmānityādi / idamitilabdhāvasaratvāduddiṣṭaṃ khaṅgajñānam parāmṛṣati / na vijñāyate na vijñāyata iti dvirvacanamavadhāraṇārtham / parato na vijñāyate eva caramabhavakhaṅgaiḥkhaṅgajñānam / paropadeśasya teṣu vaiyarthyāt / yataḥ svayaṃbhūtvena teṣāṃ svayameva tatsaṃmukhībhavatīti paropadeśavaiyarthyam //
body.translated_text: Through the power of the <s>Buddha</s>, in order to introduce the <s>khaḍga-mārga</s> (rhinoceros path), a thought arose in certain <s>devaputras</s> (sons of gods) — this is stated with 'atha khalu tatra' and so on. 'Certain' refers to those who considered even the <s>śrāvaka</s> path being taught by <s>Subhūti</s> to be profound. How [is it the speech] of <s>yakṣas</s>? Because they utter it. How are they <s>yakṣa</s>-sounds and so on? Because they are of their language. There, 'sounds' is the heading; the rest is the exposition. '<s>Mantrita</s>' means sentences. '<s>Pravyāhṛta</s>' means groups of sentences. 'Speaks' means through words and sentences. 'Expounds' means through groups of sentences. 'Teaches' means instructs. 'Advises' means guides. 'Then the venerable' and so on — 'this' refers to the <s>khaḍga-jñāna</s> (rhinoceros knowledge) that is indicated, being taken up since the occasion has been obtained. The repetition 'is not known, is not known' is for the purpose of emphasis. The <s>khaḍga-jñāna</s> is definitely not known from others by the rhinoceros-practitioners in their final existence, because instruction from others is useless for them, since through their self-born nature, they themselves directly encounter that — thus instruction from others is futile.

body.text: tathāhīti / īdṛśyeva hi dharmatā dharmāṇām / kīdṛśītyāha nātretyādi / atreti skandhadhātvāyatanādau / na kiñciditi na kaściddharmaḥ sūcyata iti deśyate / śrūyate śrotrā niḥśvabhāvatvātsarvadharmāṇām / tadyathā nirmitabuddhena nirmitānāṃ pariṣadāṃ dharma deśyamāne na kiñciddeśyate na kaściddeśayitā na kaścicchroteti / atha khalu tesāmityādi / uttānamagambhīraharṣādvivecanam / itītyevamasmābhirvitarkite / anāryāṇāmagocaratvena dūrāt / niṣprapañcatvena sūkṣmāt / dukhagāhatvena gambhīrācchrāva (ka) mārgā dūrataraṃ sūkṣmataraṃ gambhīrataraṃ jñānam / praviśati cetasā / deśayati granthataḥ / bhāṣate arthataḥ / tathā hi nātretyādinā / iti jñānagambhīratā / ataḥ śāstram-
body.translated_text: 'For so it is' — for such indeed is the <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature) of <s>dharmas</s>. What kind? This is stated with 'not here' and so on. 'Here' means among the <s>skandhas</s>, <s>dhātus</s>, <s>āyatanas</s>, and so on. 'Nothing' means no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever is indicated, i.e., taught, or heard — because all <s>dharmas</s> are devoid of intrinsic nature. Just as when a magically created <s>Buddha</s> teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to magically created assemblies, nothing is taught, there is no teacher, and there is no listener. 'Then of those' and so on — the discrimination is straightforward, arising from joy at profundity. 'Thus' means 'when we had thus reflected.' 'From afar' — because it is inaccessible to the ignoble. 'Subtle' — because it is free from conceptual elaboration. 'Profound' — because it is hard to fathom. The knowledge of the <s>śrāvaka</s> path is farther, subtler, and more profound. 'Enters with the mind' — 'teaches' means through the text; 'speaks' means according to the meaning. As stated with 'not here' and so on — thus the profundity of knowledge. Therefore the treatise states:

children.translated_text: Verse 36
The futility of instruction from others, due to the self-awakening of the self-born ones,
and the profundity of knowledge — these are said to characterize the <s>khaḍga</s> (rhinoceros) practitioners. [2-6]

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmāniti / nemāṃkṣāntimanāgamyeti / tathāhi nātretyādinoktam / grāhyābhāvajñānaṃ nāprāpya prāpyaivetyarthaḥ / ataśca śrāvakairapi tajjñānaṃ tathāgatairapyupādeyaṃ sutarāṃ khaṅgairadhigantavyāmiti bhāvaḥ / iti khaṅgānāṃ grāhyavikalpaprahāṇam //
body.translated_text: 'Then the venerable' and so on. 'Without having attained this <s>kṣānti</s> (patient acceptance)' — as stated with 'not here' and so on. The meaning is that the knowledge of the non-existence of the graspable is not attained without attaining [it], but rather by attaining it. Therefore, since even <s>śrāvakas</s> must adopt that knowledge, and <s>Tathāgatas</s> as well, all the more must <s>khaḍga</s> practitioners realize it — this is the purport. Thus the abandonment of the conceptual construction of the graspable by the <s>khaḍga</s> practitioners.

body.text: atha khalu punarapītyādi / mantrādibalena pratibhāsamāno mithyāpuruṣo māyā / ṛddhisandarśito nirmitaḥ / tābhyāṃ sadṛśāḥ / māyopamāste sattvā na māyeti / mithyātvameva māyātvaṃ manyante / subhūtistu manyate mithyāviśeṣo māyā ca svapnaṃ ca tābhyāṃ sādṛśyaṃ mithyātvameva / tasmānmāyā ca sattvāścetyadvayaṃ mithyātvena nirviśeṣatvāditi / tadevaṃ māyāpuruṣavat puruṣadravyāṇāmasattvamuktam / sarvadharmā apīti / puruṣadharmā api sarve māyopamāḥ / asati puruṣadravye taddharmāṇāmapyabhāvāt / atha khalvāyuṣmān śāriputra ityādi nāsyā āyuṣmanta ityādinā na kaścitpratyeṣako bhaviṣyatyetadantena sthavirasubhūtirdhārmaśravaṇikavat pratyeṣakānāmapyabhāvamāha / pratīkṣantīti pratyeṣakāḥ / teṣāmabhāvaḥ pratyeṣakapuruṣadravyābhāvāt / sūcyata ityasphuṭaṃ bhāṣyate / paridīpyata iti sphuṭam / prajñapyata iti vaktṛśrotṛbhirvyavahriyate / tasmātsarvathā na santi puruṣadravyāṇi / kevalamadhyātmikeṣu ca skandhādiṣu puruṣaprajñaptiḥ / tataḥ puruṣaprajñaptyāśraye skandhādau grāhaka grāhameṣāmastīti khaṅgānāṃ grāhakavikalpāprahāṇam /
body.translated_text: 'Then again' and so on. A false person appearing through the power of <s>mantras</s> and the like is <s>māyā</s> (illusion); one displayed through supernatural power is <s>nirmita</s> (magically created). They are similar to these two. 'Those beings are like illusion, not illusion' — they consider that falsity alone constitutes being illusory. But <s>Subhūti</s> holds that illusion and dream are a particular kind of falsity, and the resemblance to them is falsity itself; therefore illusion and beings are non-dual, being without distinction in their falsity. Thus, like an illusory person, the non-existence of person-substances has been stated. 'All <s>dharmas</s> too' — even all the <s>dharmas</s> of a person are like illusion, because when person-substance does not exist, its properties also do not exist. 'Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>' and so on — with 'Not of this, O venerable one' up to 'there will be no seeker,' the elder <s>Subhūti</s> states the non-existence of seekers as well, like <s>Dharma</s>-listeners. 'Those who expect' are seekers. Their non-existence is because person-substance of seekers does not exist. 'Is indicated' means spoken indistinctly. 'Is illuminated' means spoken clearly. 'Is designated' means used conventionally by speakers and listeners. Therefore, in no way do person-substances exist; there is merely the designation of a person upon the internal <s>skandhas</s> and so on. Hence, grasping exists in the basis of person-designation, namely the <s>skandhas</s> and so on — thus the non-abandonment of the conceptual construction of the grasper by the <s>khaḍga</s> practitioners.

body.text: atha khalu śakrasyetyādinā na tat puṣpamityetadantena khaṅgānāṃ gotramucyate / atra dharmaparyāyo dharmaprabhedaḥ / khaṅgamārgaḥ / yannuśabdo / vākyālaṅkāre / subhūtimiti / dharmabhāṇakapūjayā dharmapūjanāt / etaditivakṣyamānaṃ(ṇaṃ) vitarkitaṃ abhūt / śakramanu śakraṃ prati vyāharaṇāyeti vitarkaṃ viditvā bhāṣaṇāya / imānīti prakṛtāni / puṣpāṇītyamalatvena puṣpasādharmyāt khaḍgamārgasaṃgṛhītāni kuśalāni / deveṣu pracarantīti avacaranti na dṛṣṭāni, anāśravatvena dhātupatitatvābhāvāditi bhāvaḥ / abhyavakīrṇānīti pariṣadi nirmitapuṣpaiḥ sūcitāni / nirmitāni yathādarśanamasattvāt / kuta ityāha / naitānītyādi / manomayānītyupasaṃhāraḥ / manonirji(rmi) tānītyarthaḥ / śakrastu manomayatvamapi niṣeddhumāha / anirjātānīti / yathā hi grāhyatvādvṛkṣādayo na santīti na tebhyo nirjātāni tāni / tathā manopi nāsti grāhakatvāditi tatopyanirjātāni subhūtirāha / yatkauśikānirjātaṃ na tatpuṣpamiti yattayornityābhisambandhānna tatpuṣpaṃ na sa khaḍmārgaḥ syādityarthaḥ / evaṃ manyate / nirviśeṣaṃ jātaṃ nirjātam / ataḥ sajātīyaṃ kāryamāśritam / kāraṇamāśrayaḥ / khaḍgamārgaśca khaḍgāśritaḥ / na ca khaḍgasya saṃskṛto dharmo mārgasyāśrayo yujyate sāsravasya vijātīyatvāt / anāsravasyāpi saṃskṛtasyādimatvādādita eva nirāśrayasyānutpattiprasaṅgāt / tasmādanāsravatvena sajātīyaḥ khaḍgasya dharmadhātureva khaḍmārgasyāśraya ādhāraḥ pratiṣṭhāgotramiti khaḍgamārgasyādhāraḥ // ataḥ śāstram-
body.translated_text: With 'Then <s>Śakra</s>' and so on, up to 'that is not a flower,' the <s>gotra</s> (lineage) of the <s>khaḍga</s> practitioners is explained. Here '<s>dharmaparyāya</s>' means a division of the <s>Dharma</s> — the <s>khaḍga-mārga</s>. The word 'nanu' is a figure of speech. '<s>Subhūti</s>' — because of honoring the <s>Dharma</s> through honoring the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher. 'This' refers to what is about to be stated — the thought that arose. 'Following <s>Śakra</s>' means in order to address <s>Śakra</s> — having known the thought, for the purpose of speaking. 'These' refers to those under discussion. 'Flowers' — because of their similarity to flowers through being pure, the wholesome qualities included in the <s>khaḍga-mārga</s>. 'They pervade among the gods' means they descend and are not seen, because being undefiled they do not fall into any realm — this is the purport. 'Scattered about' means indicated in the assembly through magically created flowers. 'Created' — because of non-existence as perceived; how so? This is stated with 'these are not' and so on. 'Mind-made' is the conclusion — meaning produced by the mind. But <s>Śakra</s>, wishing to deny even their mind-made nature, says 'not produced' — just as trees and such do not exist because they are graspable objects, and so [the flowers] are not produced from them, likewise the mind also does not exist because it is a grasping subject, and so they are not produced from it either. <s>Subhūti</s> says: 'O <s>Kauśika</s>, what is not produced is not a flower' — by the perpetual connection of those two, that is not a flower, meaning it would not be the <s>khaḍga-mārga</s>. He thinks thus: what is produced without distinction is 'nirjāta' (arisen). Therefore it depends on a cause of the same class; the cause is the basis. The <s>khaḍga-mārga</s> depends on the <s>khaḍga</s> practitioner. But a conditioned <s>dharma</s> of the <s>khaḍga</s> practitioner is not suitable as the basis of the path, because being defiled it is of a different class. Even an undefiled conditioned [dharma], being initial, would entail the absurdity of non-arising from the very start for that which is without basis. Therefore, as undefiled and thus of the same class, the <s>dharmadhātu</s> alone of the <s>khaḍga</s> practitioner is the basis, foundation, and <s>gotra</s> (lineage) of the <s>khaḍga-mārga</s> — thus the foundation of the <s>khaḍga-mārga</s>. Therefore the treatise states:

children.translated_text: Verse 37
Through the abandonment of the conceptual construction of graspable objects, through the non-abandonment of the grasper,
and through the foundation — thus should the summary of the <s>khaḍga-mārga</s> (rhinoceros path) be understood. [2-8]

body.text: atha khaḍgānāṃ kathaṃ parārthakriyāṃ? icchāmātreṇa tatsiddheḥ / kathaṃ tebhyaḥ śravaṇam? sūśrūṣāmātreṇa / yataḥ śāstram-
body.translated_text: Now, how do <s>khaḍga</s> practitioners accomplish the benefit of others? Through mere wish, that is accomplished. How is there hearing from them? Through mere desire to listen. Therefore the treatise states:

children.translated_text: Verse 38

children.text: suśrūṣā yatra yatrārthe yasya yasya yathā yathā /
children.translated_text: Wherever there is desire to listen, regarding whatever subject, of whomever, in whatever manner,

children.text: sa so 'rthaḥ khyātyaśabdopi tasya tasya tathā tathā //
children.translated_text: that very meaning becomes known, even without words, to that person, in that manner.

body.text: 'yasya yasya' vineyasya / 'yatra yatrārthe ' iti nirvedhabhāgīyeṣvāryamārge vā / 'yathā yathā' iti yena yenākāreṇa / atha khalu śakretyādi / dvitīyād atha khalu śakraśabdāt prāk nirvedhabhāgīyāni vaktavyāni / tatra buddhadharmeṣu śikṣata ityetadantena ūṣmā / nāmapadaiḥ prajñaptiḥ vyavahāraḥ / tān nirdiśati / na ca virodhayati tāṃ cottānīkaroti / tāmeva copadiśati / tathā hi prajñaptimātraṃ rūpaṃ prajñaptimātrameva dharmatetyupadiśati ityūṣmā /
body.translated_text: 'Of whomever' means of whichever disciple to be trained. 'Regarding whatever subject' means in the <s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s> (penetration) stages or in the <s>āryamārga</s> (noble path). 'In whatever manner' means in whatever aspect. 'Then <s>Śakra</s>' and so on — from the second occurrence of 'then <s>Śakra</s>,' the <s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s> stages are to be explained. There, with 'trains in the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>' and so on up to that extent is <s>ūṣman</s> (warmth). 'Through names and words' means designation, conventional usage. He indicates those; and does not contradict that [designation], and clarifies it, and teaches that very thing. For he teaches that form is mere designation, and that <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature) is mere designation itself — thus <s>ūṣman</s>.

body.text: yo 'prameyeṣvityādinā na parihāṇāyetyetadantena mūrdhā / kathaṃ na śikṣate, anupalambhāditi / iti mūrdhā / yo na rūpasya vivṛddhaya ityādinā atha khalvāyuṣmānityataḥ prāk kṣāntiḥ / atra rūpāderaparigrahayuktirmahatyorbhagavatyoruktā 'adhyātmaśūnyatāṃ yāvadabhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatāmupādāya' iti / iti kṣāntiḥ / atha khalvāyuṣmānityādinā atha khalu śakra ityataḥ prāgagradharmaḥ / evaṃ ceti buddhisthaṃ hetuḥ parāmṛśati / mahatyorbhagavatyorya uktaḥ tathā hi "na sa rūpasyotpādaṃ paśyati na nirodhaṃ nodgrahaṃ notsargaṃ na saṃkleśaṃ nāvadānaṃ na cayaṃ nāpacayaṃ no hānirna vṛddhim" ityagradharmāḥ / ataḥ śāstram-
body.translated_text: With 'whoever regarding the immeasurable' and so on, up to 'not for deterioration,' is <s>mūrdhan</s> (summit). How does one not train? Because of non-apprehension — thus <s>mūrdhan</s>. With 'whoever does not [seek] the increase of form' and so on, up to before 'then the venerable,' is <s>kṣānti</s> (patient acceptance). Here the reasoning for the non-grasping of form and the rest has been stated in the two great [<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>] scriptures: 'taking up <s>adhyātma-śūnyatā</s> (internal emptiness) up to <s>abhāva-svabhāva-śūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the nature of non-existence)' — thus <s>kṣānti</s>. With 'then the venerable' and so on, up to before 'then <s>Śakra</s>,' is <s>agradharma</s> (supreme dharma). 'And thus' — the reasoning established in the <s>Buddha</s> is examined. As stated in the two great [scriptures]: 'He does not perceive the arising of form, nor its cessation, nor its grasping, nor its abandonment, nor its defilement, nor its purification, nor its accumulation, nor its diminution, nor its decrease, nor its increase' — thus <s>agradharma</s>. Therefore the treatise states:

children.translated_text: Verse 39
Through non-contradiction with designation, having the nature of indicating <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature),
that which pertains to <s>ūṣman</s> (warmth) and <s>mūrdhan</s> (summit) is characterized by the non-decrease and so on of form and the rest. [2-9]
Verse 40
Through <s>adhyātma-śūnyatā</s> (internal emptiness) and the other [emptinesses], because of the non-grasping of form and the rest,
is <s>kṣānti</s> (patient acceptance); through the aspects of non-arising and so on of form and the rest is <s>agradharmatā</s> (supreme dharma). [2-10]

body.text: ityuktaḥ pratyekabuddhamārgaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus the <s>pratyekabuddha-mārga</s> (path of the solitary buddha) has been explained.

body.text: bodhisattvasya mārgo vaktavyaḥ / tamadhikṛtya śāstram-
body.translated_text: The path of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is to be explained. With reference to that, the treatise states:

children.translated_text: Verse 41
Through the moments of <s>kṣānti</s> (patient acceptance) and <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), fourfold with respect to each truth,
the path of seeing in <s>mārgajñatā</s> (knowledge of paths) is said to be this, together with its auxiliaries. [2-11]

body.text: iti saṃkṣepeṇa sūtrārthaḥ / dve kṣāntī dve ca jñāne pratisatyam / duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāntirduḥkhe dharmajñānam / duḥkhe anvayajñānakṣāntirduḥkhe anvayajñānam / evaṃ samudayanirodhe mārge ca / ebhiḥ pratisatyaṃ caturvidhaiḥ kṣaṇairbodhisattvasya darśanamārgajñatāyāmucyate sahānusaṃ(śaṃ)syaiḥ / eṣāṃ tu kṣaṇānāṃ viśeṣalakṣaṇamadhikṛtya śāstre pañca ślokāḥ-
body.translated_text: Thus is the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> in brief. There are two <s>kṣāntis</s> and two <s>jñānas</s> for each truth: <s>duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣānti</s> (patient acceptance of knowledge of the dharma regarding suffering), <s>duḥkhe dharmajñāna</s> (knowledge of the dharma regarding suffering), <s>duḥkhe anvayajñānakṣānti</s> (patient acceptance of subsequent knowledge regarding suffering), <s>duḥkhe anvayajñāna</s> (subsequent knowledge regarding suffering). Likewise for <s>samudaya</s> (origination), <s>nirodha</s> (cessation), and <s>mārga</s> (path). Through these fourfold moments for each truth, the path of seeing of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in <s>mārgajñatā</s> (knowledge of paths) is explained, together with its auxiliaries. But regarding the specific characteristics of these moments, there are five verses in the treatise:

children.translated_text: Verse 42
Because of the absence of the relation of support and supported between <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) and awakening, mutually,
the non-endorsement by turns, the greatness, and the immeasurability. [2-12]
Verse 43
Because of measurement, the non-existence of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness); the ascertainment of form and the rest;
for one established in that [suchness], the blessing and coming forth toward Buddhahood, and so on. [2-13]
Verse 44
<s>Maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) and the rest, the pervading of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), the embracing of Buddhahood,
the pacification of all afflictions and diseases of all that is purified. [2-14]
Verse 45
The quelling of grasping at <s>nirvāṇa</s>, the protection and so on from the <s>Buddhas</s>,
beginning with the <s>apramāṇas</s> (immeasurables) and non-killing, [these are] <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience in all aspects) in the method. [2-15]
Verse 46
For one who is himself established, the establishing of beings, the dedication of merit,
and the [perfections of] <s>dāna</s> (generosity) and the rest toward perfect awakening — these are the moments of <s>mārgajñatā</s> (knowledge of paths). [2-16]

body.text: mārgajñatāyāṃ bodhisattvasya darśanamārgakṣaṇā ityarthaḥ /
body.translated_text: The meaning is: these are the moments of the path of seeing of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in <s>mārgajñatā</s> (knowledge of paths).

body.text: imāṃ tu bhagavatīmadhikṛtyādyaṃ pādatrayamanyathā kartavyam / tatrādyaḥ kṣaṇaḥ pādadvayena-
body.translated_text: However, with regard to this <s>Bhagavatī</s> [Prajñāpāramitā], the first three quarters [of the verse] must be understood differently. There, the first moment [is expressed] by two quarters —

body.text: rūpādito dhīrnānanyā na cānyā paramārthataḥ /
body.translated_text: The cognition of form and so on is neither non-different nor different in the ultimate sense.

body.text: dhīḥ prajñāpāramitā sā rūpādibhyo nābhinnā lakṣaṇabhedāt / na ca bhinnā paramārthataḥ / tathā hi / yā prajñāpāramitā yadrūpādi yā rūpāditathatā yā ca gaveṣaṇā sarva ete dharmā na saṃyuktā na visaṃyuktā arūpiṇo 'nidarśanāpratighā ekalakṣaṇā yadutālakṣaṇāḥ, na saṃyuktā na visaṃyuktā iti / nābhinnāḥ na bhinnāḥ kalpitā nāmatvāt / bhedābhedayośca bhāvadharmatvāt / ata eva rūpaskandhābhāvādarūpiṇaḥ / cakṣurvijñānābhāvādanidarśanāḥ / svadeśe parasyotpatteravibandhanādapratighāḥ / bhedapratibhāsānāmastaṅgamādekalakṣaṇāḥ / yadutālakṣaṇā iti tathatāmātralakṣaṇāḥ / ata ādyasya kṣaṇasya prastāvanā / atha khalu śakra ityādinā tatkasya hetorityataḥ prāk / tata urdhvamādyakṣaṇa evamukta ityataḥ prāk / iti duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāntiḥ /
body.translated_text: The cognition (<s>dhī</s>) is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. It is not undifferentiated from form and the like, because of the difference in characteristics. Nor is it different in the ultimate sense. For thus: that which is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, that which is form and so on, that which is the <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) of form and so on, and that which is the investigation — all these <s>dharmas</s> are neither conjoined nor disjoined, formless, non-demonstrable, non-resistant, of one characteristic — namely, no characteristic. 'Neither conjoined nor disjoined' means: not undifferentiated, not differentiated — [their difference is] imagined, being merely nominal. And because both difference and non-difference are properties of [real] entities. Hence, due to the non-existence of the form-aggregate, they are formless. Due to the non-existence of visual consciousness, they are non-demonstrable. Due to no obstruction of the arising of another at one's own location, they are non-resistant. Due to the cessation of the appearances of difference, they are of one characteristic. 'Namely, no characteristic' means characterized by <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) alone. Thus the introduction of the first moment. [The text] from 'Now then, O <s>Śakra</s>' up to 'for what reason.' And above that, the first moment [runs] from 'having thus spoken' until the [next section]. This is the <s>dharmajñānakṣānti</s> (patient acceptance of knowledge of the truth) regarding suffering.

body.text: caturṇāṃ kṣaṇānāṃ viśeṣalakṣaṇaṃ śāstreṇa-
body.translated_text: The specific characteristics of the four moments, by the treatise —

body.text:
tasyā [:] catuṣṭayaṃ yattu mahattā sāpramāṇatā /
parimāṇāntatābhāvau rūpādeḥ
body.translated_text: Its fourfold [nature] is: greatness, immeasurability, being beyond measurement, and endlessness — of form and so on.

body.text: saha apramāṇatayā 'sā'pramāṇatā' / 'mahattā' apramāṇatā cetyarthaḥ / anta evāntatā / parimāṇaścāntatā / ca tayorabhāvau aparimāṇatā / anantatā cetyarthaḥ / 'tasyāḥ' iti prajñāpāramitāyāstanmahattādi 'catuṣṭayaṃ yat rūpādeḥ' iti sambandhaḥ / rūpādermahattvādinā tadālambanāyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyā mahattvādi / mahāpāramitā / apramāṇapāramitā / aparimāṇapāramitā / anantapāramitā cetyarthaḥ / etacca mahāpāramitāvijñānaṃ nirabhiniveśaṃ draṣṭavyam / evaṃ mahāpāramiteti kauśika nābhiniviśata ityādeḥ sūtrapāṭhāt / ata evamukte śakreṇa teṣāmuddeśaḥ / sthavira ityādikaḥ subhūtinā saślādhānuvādaḥ / tataḥ subhūtinaiva nirdeśaḥ tatkasyetyādi / tatra rūpādīnāṃ mahattā- amuṣmin kāle bhāvo 'muṣminnabhāvaḥ- ityevaṃ kālato 'paricchedāt tadālambanatvāttasya mahattvam / iti duḥkhe dharmajñānam //
body.translated_text: 'Together with immeasurability' [means] '<s>sā-apramāṇatā</s>' (that-which-is-immeasurable). The meaning is: 'greatness' and 'immeasurability.' '<s>Antatā</s>' is limitedness. '<s>Parimāṇa</s>' is also limitedness. And the absence of both is 'being beyond measurement' and 'endlessness.' The construction is: 'of that' — of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> — 'the fourfold' — greatness and so on — 'of form and so on.' Through the greatness and so on of form and the like, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> that has them as its object [also has] greatness and so on. The meaning is: the great <s>pāramitā</s>, the immeasurable <s>pāramitā</s>, the <s>pāramitā</s> beyond measurement, and the endless <s>pāramitā</s>. And this knowledge of the great <s>pāramitā</s> should be seen as free from clinging. [This is known] from the <s>sūtra</s> reading: 'Thus, O <s>Kauśika</s>, one does not cling to [the notion of] great <s>pāramitā</s>.' Therefore, when this was said, <s>Śakra</s> made the enumeration. The passage beginning with 'Elder' is <s>Subhūti's</s> approbatory repetition. Then by <s>Subhūti</s> himself the exposition [follows] beginning with 'of what.' There, the greatness of form and so on: 'at such a time there is existence, at such a time non-existence' — thus, because there is no delimitation in terms of time, and because [<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>] takes those as its object, there is greatness. This is the <s>dharmajñāna</s> (knowledge of the truth) regarding suffering.

body.text: ākāso(śo)pamena tathatāśarīreṇa pramāṇato 'paricchedādapramāṇateti / duḥkhe 'nvayajñānakṣāntiḥ //
body.translated_text: Because there is no delimitation by measure, through the body of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) that is comparable to space, there is immeasurability. This is the <s>anvayajñānakṣānti</s> (patient acceptance of subsequent knowledge) regarding suffering.

body.text: saṃkhyayā aparicchedādaparimāṇateti duḥkhe 'nvayajñānam //
body.translated_text: Because there is no delimitation by number, there is being beyond measurement. This is the <s>anvayajñāna</s> (subsequent knowledge) regarding suffering.

body.text: deśato 'paricchedādanantatā ārambaṇanantatayā ca / ārambaṇaṃ sarvadharmā na ca teṣāmantato(tā)'sti gaṇanātikrāntatvāt / api ca sarvadharmā anantā asattvena teṣāmutpādavināśāntayorabhāvāt / sattvā apyālambanamubhayanairātmyajñāne / te cānantāḥ / śakra āha / tatkathamanantā iti / subhūtirāha / na gaṇanā ayogena gaṇanābahutvena veti / na gaṇanātikrāntatvena / nāpyanantākhyayā saṃkhyayetyarthaḥ / kathaṃ tarhīti tarhi śabdo 'kṣamāyām / na dharmādhivacanamiti dharma ātmadravyaṃ na tasyādhivacanaṃ tasyābhāvāt / dharmatvena svārthābhidhānāt nādharmādhivacanam / prakṣiptamiti sūtraiḥ prayuktam / kutaḥ? yata āgaṃtukaṃ sati vicāre calatvāt / yato 'vastukaṃ ātmadravyābhāvāt / ātmasambandhādapyātmeti kiñciducyate / tadapi nāstyātmano 'tyantamasattvādityanātmīyam / athavā ātmaprajñaptiviṣayaḥ skandhādirātmīyastasyāpyabhāvādanātmīyam / athavā nāma saṃjñā tasyātmīyaḥ saṃjñī / tadabhāvādanātmīyam / ārambaṇaṃ viṣayastadabhāvāt ānārambaṇam / atreti śāstṛśāsane /
body.translated_text: Because there is no delimitation by location, there is endlessness, and also due to the endlessness of the object. The object is all <s>dharmas</s>, and there is no end to them, because they surpass calculation. Moreover, all <s>dharmas</s> are endless because, through their non-existence as entities, there is no [end defined by] the limits of arising and cessation. Beings too are the object in the knowledge of the twofold selflessness. And they are endless. <s>Śakra</s> says: 'How then are they endless?' <s>Subhūti</s> says: 'Not by surpassing calculation, not by the multiplicity of calculation.' Not by surpassing calculation, nor by the number called 'endless' — this is the meaning. 'How then?' — the word 'then' [expresses] exasperation. 'Not a designation of <s>dharma</s>' — <s>dharma</s> is substantial self; there is no designation of it, due to its non-existence. Since it denotes its own meaning through the nature of being a <s>dharma</s>, it is not a designation of non-<s>dharma</s>. 'Introduced' means employed in the <s>sūtras</s>. Why? Because it is adventitious — being unstable when investigated. Because it is without substance — due to the absence of a substantial self. Even 'self' is spoken of in relation to the self. But even that does not exist — because of the absolute non-existence of the self — therefore it is 'without self.' Alternatively, the <s>skandhas</s> and the like, which are the referents of the designation of 'self,' are 'belonging to the self'; due to their non-existence too, 'without self.' Alternatively, name and designation — the 'possessor of designation' (<s>saṃjñī</s>) belongs to that; due to its non-existence, 'without self.' The object (<s>ārambana</s>) is the domain; due to its non-existence, 'without object.' 'Here' means in the teaching of the Teacher.

body.text: etaccāptavacanādapi nairātmyasiddhiṃ darśayitumāha / kā satvānantateti / gaṇanāti krāntatvena na kācitpramāṇasiddhepi nairātmyeāptavacanādapi nātmasiddhiriti darśayitumāha / sacetyādi / svareṇeti vacanena / anantasya lokasya vijñaptirarthajñāpano ghoṣaḥ śabdo 'syeti tathoktena / tathāpyatimāṃsalatvāt gambhīro nirghoṣastūryanirghoṣavadvicitraḥ śabdosyeti tathoktena / avitiṣṭhamāna iti aviśrāmyena / api nviti kinnu / ādiśuddhatvamādita evāsattvapariśuddhatvaṃ sarvatrāsattvam / anenāpi paryāyeṇa prakāreṇa / anantapāramiteyam / katamenetyata āha / evaṃ sattvānantayeti / satvānāmutpādanirodhāntavirahāt sattvānantatayeti / evaṃ cetyevameva / na gaṇānatikrāntatveneti samudaye dharmajñānakṣāntiḥ //
body.translated_text: And this is stated to show the establishment of selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>) even from authoritative testimony. 'What is the endlessness of beings?' — not by surpassing calculation is there any [endlessness]; to show that even though selflessness is established by valid cognition, there is no establishment of self even from authoritative testimony, [the text] says beginning with 'if.' 'By voice' means 'by speech.' The sound that conveys the meaning of the endless world — thus stated. Yet, because it is exceedingly dense, the profound soundless [reality], described as having a sound like a musical instrument — various [in nature]. 'Not abiding' means 'without rest.' 'Is it not?' means 'indeed.' 'Purity from the beginning' means purity as non-being from the very start — non-being everywhere. 'By this way' means 'by this method.' 'This is the endless <s>pāramitā</s>.' 'By which?' — to this he replies: 'Thus, by the endlessness of beings.' Because beings lack the limits of arising and cessation, through the endlessness of beings. 'Thus' means 'in just this way.' 'Not by surpassing calculation' — this is the <s>dharmajñānakṣānti</s> regarding the origin [of suffering].

body.text: avadhāraṇam //
body.translated_text: Ascertainment.

body.text: tasyāṃ sthitasya buddhatve,
body.translated_text: For one established in that [<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>], regarding <s>Buddhahood</s>,

body.text: 'tasyāṃ' prajñāpāramitāyāṃ sthitāyāṃ yad 'buddhatve 'vadhāraṇaṃ' buddha eva sa dṛṣṭavya iti sa ṣaṣṭhaḥ kṣaṇaḥ / tasya prastāvanā / atha khalu sendrakā ityādinā / indra śakraḥ / brahmā sahāpatiḥ / prajāpatayaścatvāro lokapālāḥ / viśiṣṭa dharmaśravaṇapraharṣādaprayatnajaṃ vacanaṃ udānaṃ tat udānayanti sma / udīratavantaḥ / aho ityāścarye / dharma iti deśanādharmaḥ / punaḥ dharma iti dharmaprakāśito darśanamārgaḥ / tasyaiva dharmasya dharmatā prakṛtistathā gatotpādanam / ata evāhuḥ ya ityādi / prādurbhāva utpādo 'nāśravalakṣaṇaḥ sūcyate / tadvacanātkilādau pratīteḥ / tataḥ kramena(ṇa) sphuṭena sphuṭataraṃ sphuṭatamaṃ ca pratīteḥ / deśyate prakāśyate prabhāvyate ca / tathāgatamityādinā tameva ṣaṣṭhaṃ kṣaṇamāhuḥ / adyāgreṇeti / adya prabhṛti dhārayiṣyāmaḥ / avirahito prāptāparihāṇāt / vihariṣyati saṃmukhībhāvāt / tathāgataṃ tu svayamavadhārayiṣyāma iti yaduktaṃ tattathāgatatve niyatamaviśeṣalābhāt / tallābhe ca vyākaraṇam / tata āha yadāhamityādi / alpavayo hi śrotriyo māṇavaka ityucyate / tasyāmantraṇaṃmāṇavaka, bhaviṣyasi buddho bhagavān svayamabhisaṃbodhāt / buddhiratiśayenāsyāstīti buddhaḥ / tādṛśaṃ pratyekabuddhopīti / tadvayavacchedārthaṃ bhagavad grahaṇam / ṣaḍivadhena bhagārthena tasya yogāt / bhagavān bodhisattvopi / tadvayavacchedārthaṃ buddhagrahaṇaṃ tasyānabhisambodhāt / yathā dharmāstathaiva gadanāt tathāgataḥ / gadeḥ pacādyac / nairuktastakāraḥ / arayaḥ kleśāstān hatavāniti arhan / samyagaviparītaṃ samastaṃ buddhamaneneti samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ / etena
body.translated_text: 'In that' — in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>; for one established therein, the 'ascertainment regarding <s>Buddhahood</s>' is: 'he should be seen as a <s>Buddha</s> indeed' — this is the sixth moment. Its introduction [runs] from 'Now then, together with <s>Indra</s>' and so on. '<s>Indra</s>' is <s>Śakra</s>. '<s>Brahmā</s>' is <s>Sahāpati</s>. The '<s>Prajāpatis</s>' are the four world-guardians. An <s>udāna</s> (inspired utterance) is a spontaneous statement arising from the joy of hearing the distinguished <s>Dharma</s>; they uttered [it]. They exclaimed. 'Aho!' [expresses] wonder. '<s>Dharma</s>' means the <s>Dharma</s> of the teaching. Again, '<s>dharma</s>' means the path of seeing manifested by the <s>Dharma</s>. The 'true nature' (<s>dharmatā</s>) of that very <s>dharma</s> is its inherent nature — the production of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Therefore they say beginning with 'he who' and so on. 'Manifestation' means arising, characterized by the absence of defilements — this is indicated. From that statement, at first there is understanding.
