Then gradually, more clearly, still more clearly, and most clearly there is understanding. '[The <s>Dharma</s>] is taught, illuminated, and made manifest.' With 'the <s>Tathāgata</s>' and so on, they declare that very sixth moment. 'From today onward' — from today we shall uphold [it]. 'Not separated' — because of non-loss of what has been attained. 'Will abide' — through direct encounter. 'We shall ascertain the <s>Tathāgata</s> ourselves' — what was said about ascertainment regarding <s>Tathāgata</s>-hood is definite because of the inevitable attainment of the distinction. And with that attainment comes the prediction (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>). Therefore [the text] says beginning with 'When I' and so on. A young student of the <s>Vedas</s> is called a <s>māṇavaka</s>. The address is: 'O <s>māṇavaka</s>, you shall become a <s>Buddha</s>, a <s>Bhagavān</s>' — through perfect self-awakening. '<s>Buddha</s>' means one who possesses supreme understanding. A <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> also [has understanding] like that. To distinguish from him, the word '<s>Bhagavān</s>' is used — through his connection with the six kinds of 'fortunate' meaning. A <s>Bodhisattva</s> is also a <s>Bhagavān</s>; to distinguish from him, the word '<s>Buddha</s>' is used, since [the <s>Bodhisattva</s>] has not [yet] attained perfect awakening. '<s>Tathāgata</s>' means one who has gone (<s>gata</s>) just as (<s>tathā</s>) the <s>dharmas</s> are, [i.e.,] speaking in accordance with them. The 'ta'-suffix from the root 'gad' (to speak). The etymological 'ta'-sound. '<s>Arhat</s>' — '<s>arayaḥ</s>' are the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions); he has destroyed them, hence '<s>arhan</s>.' '<s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>' — 'correctly' means without error; 'completely' — he has awakened to [all <s>dharmas</s>] by means of that. By this, the excellence of being a teacher is stated. For one who does not speak, or who speaks incorrectly, cannot be a teacher. And incorrect speech would arise from the force of <s>kleśas</s> or from ignorance. Both of these are absent in him, because he is respectively an <s>Arhat</s> and a <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>. 'How can a <s>saṃsāric</s> being have such power?' — to this he says '<s>Sugata</s>.' 'Gone' means liberated from rebirth. The word 'su-' means 'excellent,' 'without return,' 'without remainder' — like 'well-formed,' 'well-cured of fever,' 'well-filled pot.' For the exclusion of non-Buddhists, trainees, and those beyond training, respectively. Having gone by the supramundane path, he has gone excellently. Non-Buddhists have not, because their liberation is not [true] liberation, being finite.

body.text: śāstṛtvasaṃpaduktā / na hyavaktā viparītavaktā vā śāstā bhavati / viparītavacanaṃ ca kleśavaśādajñānādvā bhavet / taccobhayamasya nāsti yathākramamarhatvāt samyaksambuddhatvācc / saṃsāriṇaḥ kathamī[dṛśī] śaktiriti cedāha sugata iti / gataḥ punarbhavāt muktaḥ / suśabdaḥ prasa (śa)stāpunarāvṛttiniḥśeṣārthaḥ, surūpavat sunaṣṭajvaravat supūrṇaghaṭavacca / bāhyaśaikṣāśaikṣāṇāṃ vyavacchedāya yathākramam / tatra lokottareṇa mārgeṇa gatatvāt praśastaṃ gataḥ / naivaṃ bāhyāḥ / sāvadhikatvena tanmokṣasyāmokṣatvāt /
body.translated_text: By this, the excellence of being a teacher is stated. For one who does not speak, or who speaks incorrectly, cannot be a teacher. And incorrect speech would arise from the force of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) or from ignorance. Both of these are absent in him, because — respectively — he is an <s>Arhat</s> and a <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>. If it be asked, 'How can a <s>saṃsāric</s> being have such power?', he says '<s>Sugata</s>.' 'Gone' (<s>gata</s>) means liberated from rebirth. The word 'su-' [in <s>Sugata</s>] has the senses of 'excellent,' 'without return,' and 'without remainder' — like 'well-formed' (<s>surūpa</s>), 'well-cured of fever' (<s>sunaṣṭajvara</s>), and 'well-filled pot' (<s>supūrṇaghaṭa</s>) — respectively, in order to exclude non-Buddhists, trainees (<s>śaikṣa</s>), and those beyond training (<s>aśaikṣa</s>). Therein, because he has gone by the supramundane path, he has 'gone excellently.' Non-Buddhists [have] not so [gone], because their liberation, being finite (having a limit), is not [true] liberation.

body.text: "punarāvṛttirityuktau janmadoṣasamubhdavau /"
body.translated_text: "'Without return' refers to those two [defects] arising from birth and its faults."

body.text: tau ca śaikṣāṇām / aśaikṣastu bhagavāṃstasmādapunarāvṛttyā gataḥ / śeṣamakleśanirjvaraṃ /
body.translated_text: And those [defects] pertain to trainees. But the <s>Bhagavān</s>, being beyond training, has therefore gone without return. The remainder [concerns] the absence of affliction and fever.

body.text: "kāyavākbuddhivaiguṇyaṃ mārgākṣapaṭutāpi vā /"
body.translated_text: "Deficiency of body, speech, or mind; or the dullness of the path and faculties."

body.text: tadaśaikṣāṇāmapi hīnayānarhatāṃ yathāsambhavamasti / na tu bhagavataḥ / tato niḥśeṣagamanāt sugataḥ / kathamekaḥ suśabdastrīnarthānāha? tantreṇa nyāyena / tadyathā śveto dhāvati / alambumāṇāṃ yāteti / śvetaḥ śuklaḥ śvā itaḥ śvetaḥ / alambumā nāma grāmaḥ / tasya yātā gantā bumā api grāmaḥ / tasyālaṅganteti / kathaṃ sugataḥ? yato vidyācaraṇasampannaḥ / vidyā adhiprajñaṃ śikṣā, adhiśīlamadhicittaṃ ca / śikṣācaraṇaṃ vidyā puraścaraṇatvāttayoḥ / ato vidyayā cakṣuṣeva paśyan / itarābhyāṃ caraṇābhyāmiva tathā gamanāt sugataḥ / tadanena padadvayena śāstṛtvasampado heturūktaḥ / lokaviditi lokasya vinayanakālākālādiparijñānāllokavit / puruṣā eva damyā damanīyā vineyatvāt / teṣāṃ sārathiḥ samyagvinetā / tasya sadṛśaḥ sārathirastyeva / tadanyaḥ sugatastatodhikastu / nāstīti anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ / anena padadvayena śāstṛtvasampado heturuktaḥ / athāsya karmaṇo viṣayaḥ / kiṃ durgatiṃ gatā api? netyāha / śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ceti / iti samudaye dharmajñānam //
body.translated_text: These exist even for <s>Arhats</s> of the lesser vehicle, as applicable. But not for the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Therefore, from his going without remainder, he is <s>Sugata</s>. How does one word 'su-' convey three meanings? By systematic method. Just as 'the white one runs' [can mean the white dog runs], and '<s>Alambumānā</s> goes' [has double meaning] — 'white' means the white dog; '<s>Alambumā</s>' is a village name; its traveler is one going to that [village]; '<s>bumā</s>' is also a village, and one going to it. How is he <s>Sugata</s>? Because he is 'endowed with knowledge and conduct.' 'Knowledge' is the training in higher wisdom; 'conduct' is the training in higher morality and higher mind. 'Knowledge-conduct' [means knowledge precedes], because knowledge goes before them. Therefore, seeing with knowledge as if with eyes, and walking with the other two as if with feet — from going in that way, he is <s>Sugata</s>. By these two terms, the cause of the excellence of being a teacher is stated. '<s>Lokavid</s>' (knower of the world) — because of knowing the right and wrong times for disciplining the world. '<s>Puruṣas</s>' are the ones to be disciplined, being trainable. Their '<s>sārathi</s>' (charioteer) is one who guides them rightly. There exists a charioteer comparable to him. But a <s>Sugata</s> different from him, and superior — there is none, hence '<s>anuttara puruṣadamyasārathi</s>' (unsurpassed charioteer of persons to be tamed). By these two terms, the cause of the excellence of being a teacher is stated. Now, the domain of his activity — does it include even those gone to evil destinies? No — hence 'teacher of gods and humans.' This is the <s>dharmajñāna</s> regarding the origin [of suffering].

body.text: atha khalu ta ityādinā saptamaṃ kṣaṇamāhuḥ / āścaryamāhārikārthe / paramāścaryamanuparigrāhikāthe / yāvacchabdaḥ paryantārthaḥ / dānapāramitāyā śīlapāramitāyā yāvat sarvajñatāyāḥ sarvākārajñatāyā ityarthaḥ / āhāriketyākarṣikā / anuparigrāhiketyanuśabdo 'nvayārthaḥ / anvayo yuktirnyāyaḥ / aparigrahonutsargayogaḥ / aparigrahānutsargayogayoḥ sāhityam / anvayena parigrāhikā yathā na parigṛṇhāti na cotsṛjati tathā parigrāhiketyarthaḥ / atra śāstram-
body.translated_text: With 'now then those' and so on, they declare the seventh moment. 'Wonder' is in the sense of appropriating. 'Supreme wonder' is in the sense of encompassing. The word '<s>yāvat</s>' has the sense of 'up to.' [Up to] the <s>dāna-pāramitā</s> (perfection of generosity), the <s>śīla-pāramitā</s> (perfection of morality), up to <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience) and <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects) — this is the meaning. 'Appropriating' means 'attracting.' 'Encompassing' — the word 'anu' means 'conformity,' conformity being reason or method. '<s>Aparigraha</s>' is the method of non-grasping. The combination of non-grasping and non-abandoning. 'Encompassing through conformity' means: it encompasses in such a way that it neither grasps nor abandons — this is the meaning. Here the treatise [says] —

body.text: anugrahātyāgatādayaḥ //
body.translated_text: Favoring, non-abandoning, and the rest.

body.text: iti / ādānamādiparigrahaḥ / anugraho 'vikalpanam / ayamaparigrahārthaḥ / atyāga eva atyāgatā / ayamanutsargārthaḥ / bodhisattvāḥ parigṛṇhanti / bhagavatī tān parigrāhayatīti samudaye 'nvayajñānakṣāntiḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus. 'Receiving' is the initial grasping. 'Favoring' is non-conceptualization. This is the meaning of non-grasping. 'Non-abandonment itself' is 'non-abandoning.' This is the meaning of non-forsaking. <s>Bodhisattvas</s> grasp. The <s>Bhagavatī</s> (<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>) causes them to grasp — this is the <s>anvayajñānakṣānti</s> (patient acceptance of subsequent knowledge) regarding the origin [of suffering].

body.text: śakreṇa prastāvakatvādupalakṣitaḥ parivartaḥ śakraparivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: The chapter marked by <s>Śakra</s> as the introducer is the <s>Śakra</s> Chapter.

body.text: āryāṣṭasāhastrikāyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ sāratamānāmni pañjikāyāṃ ratnākaraśāntiviracitāyāṃ dvitīyaḥ parivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: In the <s>Pañjikā</s> commentary named <s>Sāratama</s>, composed by <s>Ratnākaraśānti</s>, on the noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s> — this is the Second Chapter.

body.text: 3. aprameyaguṇadhāraṇapāramitāstūpasatkāro nāma tṛtīyaḥ /
body.translated_text: 3. The third [chapter] is named 'Veneration of the <s>Stūpa</s> of the <s>Pāramitā</s> of Upholding Immeasurable Qualities.'

body.text: 'maitryādi' iti śāstram / maitrī karuṇāmuditopekṣāścatvāryapramāṇāni maitryādi / tadātmakaṃ darśanamaṣṭamaḥ kṣaṇa ityarthaḥ / taddeśanā nidānam / atha khalu bhagavānityādinā āmantrayate smetyetadantena saṃgītikāra āha / sākṣīkaraṇamaṣṭame kṣaṇe hīnayānapatanapratipakṣagauravātiśayotpādanāya / tameva kṣaṇam / bhagavānāha / yo hītyādinā prajñāpāramitāmiti prakaraṇāddarśanakṣaṇaḥ / prajñā saiva pāraṃgateti pāramitā / kasya pāram? hīnayānapatanabhūmeḥ / kā cāsau? yā catur(rṇāṃ) apramāṇātmakaṃ darśanam / tathāhi tatprāpto bodhisattvaḥ sarvasattveṣvātmasamatādarśī tānaśaraṇān hitvā nātmanaḥ kevalasya hitamīhate yena hīnayāne nipatet / tasmānmaitryādirūpaṃ darśanamatra prajñāpāramitā / saiva cāṣṭamaḥ kṣaṇaḥ / tāṃ yaḥ kaścid grahīṣyati yāvat paryavāpsyati sākṣātkaraṇāt / pravartayiṣyatīti parebhyaḥ prakāśitāyāstasyāstairudgrahaṇāt / yāvatpravartanāt / na tasyetyādiranuśaṃstaḥ (saḥ) pravartayiṣyatīti yāvat / iti samudaye anvayajñānam /
body.translated_text: '<s>Maitrī</s> and so on' — thus says the treatise. <s>Maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), <s>muditā</s> (sympathetic joy), and <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity) — the four <s>apramāṇas</s> (immeasurables) are what is meant by '<s>maitrī</s> and so on.' The vision whose nature consists of these is the eighth moment — this is the meaning. The teaching of that is the occasion. By 'Then indeed the <s>Bhagavān</s>' and so forth, with the address, up to 'said' — the compiler of the council states. The direct realization in the eighth moment is for the purpose of generating exceptional reverence as the antidote to falling into the lesser vehicle. That very moment: the <s>Bhagavān</s> said 'For whoever' and so forth — by the context of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, it is the moment of vision. <s>Prajñā</s> (wisdom) itself has 'gone to the far shore' — hence <s>pāramitā</s>. The far shore of what? Of the ground of falling into the lesser vehicle. And what is that? That which is the vision consisting of the four <s>apramāṇas</s>. For a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has attained that, seeing equality of self and all beings, does not abandon the refugeless beings to seek the welfare of himself alone, whereby he would fall into the lesser vehicle. Therefore, the vision in the form of <s>maitrī</s> and so forth is here <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>. And that itself is the eighth moment. 'Whoever will grasp it' up to 'will master it' — through direct realization. 'Will propagate it' — through the taking up by others of that which has been taught to them. Up to 'will propagate' — the benefit is stated through to 'will propagate.' Thus [this is] the knowledge of positive concomitance regarding the aggregate [of the path of seeing].

body.text: 'śūnyatāvyāptiḥ' iti śāstram / ṣoḍaśānāṃ śūnyatānāṃ darśanena yā vyāptiḥ sarvāsāṃ darśanaṃ sa navamaḥ kṣaṇaḥ ityarthaḥ / tamāha / na ca khalvityādinā /
body.translated_text: 'The pervasion of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness)' — thus says the treatise. The pervasion that occurs through the vision of the sixteen <s>śūnyatās</s> — the vision of all of them — that is the ninth moment — this is the meaning. This he states: 'Not indeed' and so forth.

body.text: ihāpi darśanakṣaṇaḥ prajñāpāraṃgateti pāramitā / kasya pāram? śūnyatānāṃ ṣoḍaśānāmapi / tāsāṃ darśanāt / atrānuśaṃsaḥ / ādvitīyādatha / khalu śabdāt / acchannaḥ pradeśo avakāśaḥ / nipannaḥ śayitaḥ / bhaviṣyati prabandhena pravakṣyati / rakṣāvaraṇasahitā guptiḥ / tatra śastrādinā rakṣā rakṣaniyogādāvaraṇam / svayamupasaṃkramya tasyādhiṣṭhānāt guptiḥ / athavā śarīrasya sarvasukhopasaṃharaṇaṃ rakṣā / bāhyopakramanivāraṇamāvaraṇam / ādhyātmikarogādinivāraṇaṃ guptiḥ / teṣāṃ saṃvidhānaṃ samyak prayogo vā vā manasā vā / iti nirodhe dharmajñānakṣāntiḥ //
body.translated_text: Here too, the moment of vision is <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> — '<s>prajñā</s> has gone to the far shore' hence <s>pāramitā</s>. The far shore of what? Of the sixteen <s>śūnyatās</s> as well — through the vision of those. Here the benefit [is stated]. From the second [phrase] onward, from the word '<s>khalu</s>' (indeed). '<s>Acchanna</s>' means an open area; '<s>avakāśa</s>' means space. '<s>Nipanna</s>' means lying down. 'Will become' means will continue to teach in succession. 'Protection' together with 'shielding' is guarding. Therein, protection by weapons and the like is 'shielding' through the duty of protection; guarding is the personal approach and blessing. Alternatively, the gathering of all comforts for the body is protection; the prevention of external harm is shielding; the prevention of internal diseases and the like is guarding. Their arrangement is the proper practice through body, speech, or mind. Thus [this constitutes] the <s>dharmajñānakṣānti</s> (patient acceptance of the knowledge of dharmas) regarding cessation.

body.text: 'buddhatvasya parigrahaḥ' iti / buddhasya bhāvo buddhatvam / yena buddho bhavati tasya parigrahalakṣaṇaḥ prabhāsvarasamādhidhāraṇāsampat / abuddhakeṣu ca buddhakṣetreṣu buddharūpasyātmanaḥ saṃdarśanam / tamāha / atha khalu śakra ityādinā / imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmitiṃ darśanakṣaṇam / imān guṇāniti lakṣaṇasampadādīn / iyata ityabhyunnatān / dṛṣṭadhārmikāniti dṛṣṭo dharmaḥ prāptaṃ janma / tatrabhavān / pratilabhata ityuddeśaḥ / parigṛṇhātīti nirdeśaḥ / iti nirodhe dharmajñānam //
body.translated_text: 'The grasping of <s>buddhatva</s> (buddhahood)' — thus [says the treatise]. The state of a <s>Buddha</s> is <s>buddhatva</s>. The grasping of that by which one becomes a <s>Buddha</s>, characterized by comprehension — [this involves] the luminous <s>samādhi</s>

body.text: 'sarvasya vyavadānasya' ityekādaśaḥ / vyavadāyantyaneneti vyavadānam / dānapāramitādi / tasya sarvasya parigrahaḥ / tamāha / kiṃ punarityādinā punaraparamityataḥ prāk / iti nirodhe anvayajñānakṣāntiḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Of all purification' — this is the eleventh [moment]. That by which one purifies is purification — the <s>dāna-pāramitā</s> (perfection of generosity) and so on. The grasping of all of that — this he states

body.text: 'sarvādhivyādhiśātanaṃ' iti / ādhayo vyasanāni / tīrthikairābhimānikaiśca saha vigrahavivādani(vi)rodhāsteṣāṃ śātanam / tathā ca tacchatanaṃ yathā teṣāṃ paścāttata imāṃ śrutavatāṃ tribhiryānaiḥ kleśadurgatisaṃsārāruyā vyādhayaḥ kṣīyante / tasmāt sarvādhiśātanam / darśanaṃ dvādaśaḥ kṣaṇaḥ / tamāha punaraparamityādinā saṃsthāpyanta ityetadantena / dharmamiti śāsanam / vigrahītavyaṃ tāḍanena / vivaditavyaṃ kalahena / virodhayitavyaṃ parasparadveṣeṇa / te 'bhiprāyā iti vigrahādyabhiprāyāḥ / evaṃ hyetabhdavatīti / eṣaiva hi dharmatetyarthaḥ imāmiti dvādaśakṣaṇalakṣaṇām / [oṣadhī] oṣaḥ prabhāvaḥ / sa dhīyate 'syāmiti dadhāteḥ kvip pratyayaḥ / jātireṣā tata oṣadherajātāvityaṇa bhavati / strīliṅgaścāyaṃ tataḥ kṛdikārādaktiṅ iti dīrghavikalpaḥ / āśīḥ sarpasya daṃṣṭrā / tasyāṃ viṣamasyeti āśīviṣaḥ sarpaḥ / janturdehī /
body.translated_text: 'The destruction of all afflictions and calamities' — thus [says the treatise]. '<s>Ādhis</s>' are misfortunes; the conflicts, disputes, and quarrels with <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist teachers) and the self-conceited — their destruction.

body.text: prāṇakajāta iti tiryagviśeṣaḥ / tejaseti prabhāvena / baleneti bādhakatvena / sthāmata ityabādhyatvena / balādhāneneti tadyogena sāmarthyādhānāt / iti nirodhe anvayajñānam /
body.translated_text: '<s>Prāṇaka-jāta</s>' is a specific type of animal. 'By radiance' means through influence. 'By strength' means through the power to subdue. 'By steadfastness' means through being unsurmountable. 'By a foundation of strength' means

body.text: 'nirvāṇagrāhaśāntatvaṃ' iti / grāho 'bhiniveśaḥ / etadāha tatkasya hetorityādinā / prajñāpāramiteti trayodaśaḥ kṣaṇaḥ / iti mārge dharmajñānakṣāntiḥ //
body.translated_text: 'The pacification of grasping at <s>nirvāṇa</s>' — thus [says the treatise]. 'Grasping' is attachment. This he states with 'For what reason' and so forth. '<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>' — this is the thirteenth moment.

body.text: 'buddhebhyo rakṣaṇādikaṃ' iti buddhebhyo rakṣaṇam / ādiśabdāddevādibhyaḥ / etadāha / catvāraścetyādinā bhaviṣyatītyetadantena / prajñāpārami[tāmi]ti caturdaśakṣaṇaḥ / iti mārge dharmajñānam //
body.translated_text: 'Protection and so on from the <s>Buddhas</s>' — thus [says the treatise]: protection from the <s>Buddhas</s>. By the word 'and so on' — also from <s>devas</s> (gods) and others. This he states with 'And four' and so forth, up to 'will become.'

body.text:
'aprāṇivadhamārabhya sarvākārajñatā naye /
svayaṃ sthitasya sattvānāṃ sthāpanaṃ'
body.translated_text: 'Beginning with non-killing of living beings, established in the path to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience in all aspects), the establishment of beings by one who is oneself established [therein]' —

body.text: iti prāṇātipātaviratiraprāṇivadhaḥ / tamādiṃ kṛtvā yatpāramitādau yāvatsarvākārajñatāyāṃ sthitasya tatraiva yatpareṣāṃ sthāpanaṃ sa pañcadaśakṣaṇaḥ / etadāha punaraparamityādinā / prajñāpāramitādīnāṃ parebhya upadeśo vacanam / ādeyaṃ grāhyam / tadasya svayamapi teṣu sthitatvādityādeyavacanaḥ / mṛdu priyaṃ vacanamasyeti mṛduvacanaḥ / dānādīnāṃ teṣu ca sthitānāṃ varṇabhāṣaṇāt / mitavacano hitasyaiva vacanāt / aprakīrṇavacano hitasyāpyahitamiśrasyāvacanāt / iti mārge anvayajñānakṣāntiḥ //
body.translated_text: thus, abstention from taking life is 'non-killing.' Taking that as the beginning, for one who is established in the <s>pāramitās</s> and so on up to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>, the establishment of others therein as well

body.text: 'pariṇāmanaṃ' 'dānādīnāṃ ca sambodhau' iti ṣoḍaśa kṣaṇa / tamāha / na ca krodhābhibhūta ityā[ra]bhya svādhyāsyatītyetadantena / paridamayati krodhāsaṃśamanāt / pariṇāmayati unnatilakṣaṇasya mānasya kṣayanayanāt / upanāho vairam / vyāpādaḥ sattvavidveṣaḥ / anuśayo vairānubandhaḥ / smṛtirmaitrī ceti / tayoḥ smṛtimāha / tasyaivamityādinā / teneti vyāpādena / paribhedo vikāraḥ / dhakṣyata iti daheḥ prayogaḥ / etena saparivāyordveṣamānayoḥ prahāṇamuktam / dveṣeṇa hi pareṣāmanugrahaṃ na kurvīta / tasmāttāvubhau prahāya dānādīnāmātmanaḥ kuśalānāmanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau tribhiryānaiḥ sarvasattvaparinirvāpaṇāya pariṇāmena paraṃ darśanaṃ ṣoḍaśa kṣaṇa ityuktaṃ bhavati / ityukto bodhisattvānāṃ darśanamārgaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Dedication' — 'of generosity and so on toward <s>saṃbodhi</s> (complete awakening)' — this is the sixteenth moment. This he states from 'Not overcome by anger' through to 'will master.'

body.text: lokottara eva darśa[na]mārgo bhāvanāmārgastu dvidhā laukiko lokottaraśca / tāvubhau yathākramaṃ paścādvaktavyau / ādita eva lokottarasya bhāvanāmārgasya kāritraṃ granthalābhavādabhidheyam / tatra śāstram-
body.translated_text: The <s>darśana-mārga</s> (path of seeing) alone is supramundane; but the <s>bhāvanā-mārga</s> (path of cultivation) is twofold: mundane and supramundane. Both of these, in order, are to be explained later. First

children.translated_text: 'Universal taming is obeisance; universal conquest of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions);
invulnerability to assault; <s>bodhi</s> (awakening); and filling of the foundation.' // 2-17 //

body.text: namanaṃ 'nāmaḥ' sarvata iti vartate / 'sarvataḥ' iti pariśubdārthaḥ / paridamanaṃ pariṇamanaṃ cetyarthaḥ / te ubhe yathākramaṃ dveṣamānayoḥ parikṣayāt / te dve / evamukte śakra ityādinā mahāsattvānāmityetadantenāha / eṣu ṣaṭsu kāritreṣu prajñāpāramitāśabdena bodhisattvānāṃ bhāvanāmārga ucyate / yatheyamityarthaḥ / iti paridamanapariṇāmanakāritre /
body.translated_text: 'Bowing' is '<s>nāma</s>' (obeisance); '<s>sarvataḥ</s>' (universally) continues [to apply]. '<s>Sarvataḥ</s>' has the meaning of 'completely purified.' '<s>Paridamana</s>' (universal taming) and '<s>pariṇamana</s>' (dedication) — this is the meaning. Both of those, as

body.text: 'sarvataḥ kleśanirjayaḥ' iti / svaparakleśānāmatyantajayāt / tamāha bhagavānityādinā naitat sthānaṃ vidyata ityetadantena / jīvitāntarāyo veti / tatraiva śastrasampāte paropakrameṇa veti / mṛgayādimadhyagatopi parasyaiṣa upakramaḥ / pareṣāṃ tena / svaparakleśārjanayā bhagavatyā tena nirjitāstasyaiṣa niṣyanda iti bhāvaḥ / iti kleśanirjayākāritram //
body.translated_text: 'Universal conquest of <s>kleśas</s>' — through the ultimate conquest of one's own and others' afflictions. This he states from '<s>Bhagavān</s>' and so forth up to 'this situation does not exist.'

body.text: jīvitāntarāyāya kṛtāḥ parairupakramāstasminna prabhavantīti 'upakramāviṣahyatvam" / tadāha / sacedityādinā nobhayavyābādhāya cetayata ityetadantena / tatreti śarīre / tatkasya hetoriti tadapatanaṃ kutaḥ? uttaraṃ mahāvidyetyādinā / sarvakālaṃ sarvatra deśe sarvavipakṣeṣu vāpratihataprabhāvatvādyathākramaṃ mahatī / apramāṇā aparimāṇā ca / tato 'dhikābhāvād anuttarā / samābhāvād asamā / samena samaḥ samasamaḥ / kiñcidūnajātī[ya]tvāt samasamā / tasyā apyabhāvād asamasamā / ātmano ābādhaḥ / upaghātaḥ / evaṃ pareṣāmubhayasya ca tadartha na cetayate / na cittaṃ vyāpārayati / tasmātparopakramairaviṣahyatvamasyāḥ karmeti / upakramāviṣahyatvakāritram //
body.translated_text: 'Invulnerability to assault' — assaults are attempts made by others to endanger one's life; these cannot prevail against him. This he states from 'If indeed' and so forth: 'the harm from both does not [prevail].'

body.text: 'bodhiḥ' iti / anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhiḥ / pañcamaṃ kāritram / tadāha / acaitanyeṣu sarvajñajñānena / vyavalokayiṣyatīti / vinayanādyartham / tatkasya hetoriti tat sarvajñajñānaṃ kutaḥ? na taktiñcidasti yanna prāptamiti / sarve hi buddhadharmāḥ prāptavyāḥ / te ca pratyātmavedyāḥ / tato yadyanena prāptā na syurnāyaṃ sarvavibhdavet / tasmānna tatkiñcidasti yadasya na prāptaṃ syāt / tataḥ prāpyamitaracca sarvaṃ jānātīti na tatkiñcidasti yadasya na jñātaṃ syāt / prakarṣagataṃ ca sākṣātkārijñānamiha gṛhyate / tata āha / na
body.translated_text: '<s>Bodhi</s>' (awakening) — the unsurpassed perfect awakening. This is the fifth accomplishment. This he states: 'Among the insentient, through the knowledge of the omniscient. Will illuminate' means

body.text: kiñcidasti yadasākṣātkṛtaṃ syāt? iti vāśabdāḥ parasparāpekṣayā vikalpārthāḥ / tasmādasau sarvajñaḥ / tasya jñānaṃ sarvajñajñānam / saiva samyaksambodhiḥ / tathā hi samyagjñānaṃ sambodhiḥ / samyagiti sākṣāt / saiva bodhivivakṣātaḥ sarvotkarṣagataḥ samyaksambodhiḥ sarvajñānaṃ ceti / vyavahārato bhedo na vastutaḥ / abhisaṃbhotsyata iti pratilapsyate / iti sambodhikāritram //
body.translated_text: 'Is there anything that has not been directly realized?' — the particles '<s>vā</s>' (or) convey the sense of alternatives in mutual relation. Therefore, that one is omniscient. His knowledge is <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience).

body.text: 'ādhārapūjyatā' iti / dvividha ādhāraḥ / eka pustakagatāyāḥ tasyā apara udgṛhyamānāyā yāvaduddiśyamānāyāḥ tasya pūjyatā tadvadeva dvividhā / tatra gatānāṃ sattvānāṃ parairaviheṭhanīyatā / te dve yathākramaṃ punaraparabāhyadvayena parigṛṇhātītyetadantenāha / antaśa iti paramāpacaye / na satkariṣyata iti sthāpanādūrdhvam / avatāro randhramavakāśaḥ / sthāpayitveti bahiṣkṛtya / pūrvajanmano 'paraparyāyavedanīyaṃ niyatavipākamakuśalaṃ pūrvakarma / tasya vipāko 'niṣṭaphalam / imamiti yathoktam / tadyathetyādinā dṛṣṭāntaḥ / evamevetyādinā dārṣṭāntikaḥ / bodhimaṇḍagata iti / maṇḍaḥ sāraḥ / bodhyarthe maṇḍo bodhimaṇḍaḥ / tasminniṣadha bodheradhigamāt / kasya sāraḥ? kāñcanamayyāḥ pṛthivyāḥ / tathāhi vivarti(rta) syādau / kāñcanamayyāṃ pṛthivyāmabhinirvṛttāyāṃ caturatnamaye merau saptasu kāñcanaparvateṣu saptasu sitāsu bāhyamahodadhau, ayameva cakravāte(vṭhe) abhinirvṛtte, kāñcanamayyāḥ pṛthivyāḥ sāro vajramayaḥ samabhyudgataḥ / yo mṛnma (ṇma)yeṣu caturṣu dvīpeṣvaṣṭāsu cāntaradvīpeṣvabhinirvṛtteṣu jambūdvīpasya nābhiḥ saṃvṛttaḥ sa ca vajramayatvādvodhāsanatvācca vajrāsanamityucyate / sa bodhimaṇḍaḥ / taṃ gatāḥ prāptāḥ / samante bhavaḥ sāmantaḥ / veṣṭanaparisāmantaḥ pariveṣṭaḥ / abhyantaraṃ madhyam / bodhāya vṛkṣo bodhivṛkṣaḥ / tanmūle niṣadha bodheradhigamāt / tasya mūlaṃ mūlābhiniveśaparicchinnaḥ pradeśaḥ / tadgataḥ / vāśabdāḥ parasparāpekṣayā vikalpārthāḥ / viheṭhayitumiti vihiṃsitum / vyāpādayitumiti nihaṃtum / āveśayitumiti bhūtapiśācādipraveśanāt / bhayādipratipakṣatvāt / abhayamavairamanuttrāsaṃ mahāmaitrīnāmekamapramāṇam / prabhāvayantīti niṣpādayanti prakāśayantīti sasainyasya mārasya vighnatopi kramaṇāt / caityabhūta iti / cāyṛ pūjāyām / cāyyate devatā asminniti caityam / kṛtyalyuṭo bahulamityadhikaraṇe ṇyat / āya edbhāvaśca stūpa ityarthaḥ / tadbhūtastattādṛśaḥ / nirmālyāderakarṣārhatvāt / apacāyanīyaḥ / yataścaityabhūtastamanye na hiṃsanti / yataḥ śaraṇādistatastatragatā avadhyā bhavanti / tatra sannihitaṃ trāyata iti trāṇam / abhyupagacchato bhayaṃ śṛṇātīti śaraṇam / abhayā līyante asminniti layanam / paramayanaṃ parāyaṇaṃ parā gatiḥ / iti ṣaṣṭhamādhārapūjyatākāritrama //
body.translated_text: 'The venerability of the support' — the support is twofold: one is of [the Prajñāpāramitā] as contained in a book, the other is of it being recited up to being expounded. Its venerability is likewise twofold. The inviolability by others of beings who have gone there. He grasps those two respectively with the pair of outer [and inner aspects] — he says this with the phrase ending 'even at the least.' 'Even at the least' means in the greatest disrespect. 'Will not honor' means beyond merely establishing [it]. 'Opportunity' means opening, occasion. 'Having set aside' means having excluded. 'Previous karma' is the unwholesome karma of a previous birth with fixed ripening, to be experienced in another life or another occasion. Its ripening is an undesired result. 'This' means as stated. With 'just as' and so forth is the example. With 'just so' and so forth is the exemplified. 'Gone to the <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>' — <s>maṇḍa</s> means essence; the essence for the purpose of <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) is <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>; by sitting there, one attains awakening. Whose essence? Of the golden earth. For indeed, at the beginning of the cosmic evolution, when the golden earth has formed, with the four-jeweled <s>Meru</s>, the seven golden mountains, the seven cold [lakes], the outer great ocean, this very <s>cakravāla</s> (world-enclosure) having formed, the diamond essence of the golden earth rose up. When the four earthen continents and eight sub-continents formed, it became the navel of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>; and because it is diamond-made and the seat of awakening, it is called the <s>vajrāsana</s> (diamond throne). That is the <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>. 'Gone to it' means 'having reached it.' '<s>Sāmanta</s>' means existing around; 'encircling around' means surrounding. 'Inner' means the middle. The tree for awakening is the <s>Bodhi</s> tree. By sitting at its root, one attains awakening. 'Its root' is the area delimited by the extent of the roots. 'Gone there.' The particles 'or' serve as alternatives in mutual reference. 'To harm' means to injure. 'To destroy' means to kill. 'To possess' means through the entry of spirits, <s>piśācas</s>, and the like. Because [these four are] antidotes to fear and the like: fearlessness, non-enmity, non-terror — [these three form] one immeasurable, called great loving-kindness. 'They bring about' means they accomplish, they manifest — even overcoming the obstacles of <s>Māra</s> with his army. '<s>Caityabhūta</s>' (become a shrine) — the root <s>cāy</s> means 'to worship'; that in which a deity is worshipped is a <s>caitya</s>. The <s>ṇyat</s> suffix is in the locative sense according to 'the <s>kṛtyalyuṭ</s> [suffixes] are abundant.' Growth and prosperity is the meaning of <s>stūpa</s>. 'Become that' means resembling that. Because of being unworthy of removal of garlands and the like. 'To be honored.' Since he has become a shrine, others do not harm him. Since [he is] a refuge and the like, those who have gone there become inviolable. 'Protection' means that which shields, which is present there. 'Refuge' means that which hears the fear of one who approaches. '<s>Layana</s>' (shelter) means that in which the fearless take rest. 'Supreme goal' means the highest destination. Thus ends the sixth [section], the conduct of the venerability of the support.

body.text: laukiko bhāvanāmārgaḥ / ādau vaktavya ādyatvāt / sa ca trividhaḥ / adhimuktimanaskāraḥ pariṇāmanāmanaskāro 'numodanāmanaskāraśca / tatrādhimuktimanaskāramadhikṛtya śāstram-
body.translated_text: The mundane path of meditation [is next]. It should be stated first because it comes first. And it is threefold: the aspiration-mental-attention, the dedication-mental-attention, and the rejoicing-mental-attention. Regarding the aspiration-mental-attention, the treatise [states] —

body.text:
adhimuktistridhā jñeyā svārthā ca svaparārthikā /
parārthikaiveti
body.translated_text: Aspiration is to be known as threefold: for one's own benefit, for one's own and others' benefit, and for others' benefit alone.

body.text: svasyaiva svaparayoḥ parasyaiva cārthaḥ pradhānamāśayato yasyāṃ sā yathākramaṃ 'svārthā' 'svaparārthā' parārthaiva' ca / tataḥ śāstram-
body.translated_text: That in which one's own benefit, or the benefit of oneself and others, or the benefit of others alone is predominant in intention — that is respectively 'for one's own benefit,' 'for one's own and others' benefit,' and 'for others' benefit alone.' Then the treatise [states] —

body.text: eṣā ca pratyekaṃ trividheṣyate // 2-28 //
body.translated_text: And each of these is considered threefold. // 2-28 //

body.text: mṛdvī madhyādhimātrā ca
body.translated_text: Mild, middling, and intense,

body.text: 'eṣā' iti svārthādiḥ / 'trividhā' mṛdvayādibhedena / tataḥ śāstram-
body.translated_text: 'This' refers to that beginning with 'for one's own benefit.' 'Threefold' by the division into mild and the rest. Then the treatise [states] —

body.text:
mṛdumadhyādi bhedataḥ /
sā punastrividhā
body.translated_text: through the division of mild, middling, and so forth, each is again threefold,

body.text: mṛdvayādīnāṃ pratyekaṃ mṛdvayādibhedāt / tadyathā svārthādimṛdumṛdvī mṛdumadhyāmṛdvadhimātrā / madhyamṛdvī madhyamadhyā madhyādhimātrā / adhimātramṛdvī adhimātramadhyā adhimātrādhimātrā ca / evaṃ svaparārthā / evaṃ parārthā ca / tata śāstram-
body.translated_text: because of the division of each of the mild and so forth into mild and so forth. That is: mild-mild, mild-middling, mild-intense [for one's own benefit]; middling-mild, middling-middling, middling-intense; intense-mild, intense-middling, intense-intense. Similarly for one's own and others' benefit. Similarly for others' benefit. Then the treatise [states] —

body.text: ityevaṃ saptaviṃśatidhā matā // 2-29 //
body.translated_text: Thus it is considered twenty-seven-fold. // 2-29 //

body.text: 'ityevaṃ' trīṇi vārāṇi tribhirbhedāt 'saptaviṃśatidhā' iṣyate /
body.translated_text: 'Thus' — three times [multiplied] by three divisions — 'twenty-seven-fold' is accepted.

body.text: adhimuktiḥ śraddhāchandau saṃpratyayābhilāṣalakṣaṇau kvādhimukti? sūtrasūtrārtharūpāyāṃ bhagavatyāṃ taccaryāyāṃ ca lekhanādikāyāṃ tatpūjāyāṃ ca puṣpādibhirbahuvidhāttābhiḥ / caryāpūjobhdave ca puṇye yathā sūtram / tatra prathamā / evamukte śakra ityādinā yaḥ prajñāpāramitāyai pūjāṃ kariṣyatītyetadantena / likhitveti svayam / pustakagatāṃ vā kṛtveti pareṇa / divyābhiriti viśiṣṭābhiḥ / javānka(?)puṣpādivarjanāt / puṣpāṇi muktakusumāni / mālyāni srajaḥ / gandhā gandhadārūṇi / vilepanāni sa (ta)māla bhavāni / cūrṇā agarucandanādīnām / cīvarāṇi vastrāṇi / pūjābhiriti nivedyādibhiḥ / bahuvidhābhiriti bhakṣyalehyādibhedāt / puṣpādibhiḥ satkuryāditi sambandhaḥ / pūjayedityarthaḥ / gurukuryāditi gauraveṇa / mānayediti
body.translated_text: <s>Adhimukti</s> (aspiration) is faith and desire, characterized by conviction and longing. Where is this aspiration [directed]? Toward the Blessed <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> in the form of the <s>sūtra</s> and its meaning, toward its practice, and toward its worship through writing and the like, and through various offerings of flowers and so forth. And the merit in the arising of practice and worship is according to the <s>sūtra</s>. Therein, the first [section is discussed]. With 'thus spoken, O <s>Śakra</s>' and so forth, up to 'who will make worship to the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.' 'Having written' means by oneself. 'Or having made it into a book' means by another. 'With divine' means with excellent ones — excluding inferior flowers and the like. 'Flowers' means loose blossoms. 'Garlands' means wreaths. 'Incenses' means fragrant woods. 'Unguents' are made from <s>tamāla</s>. 'Powders' are of aloe, sandalwood, and the like. 'Robes' means garments. 'With offerings' means with food-offerings and the like. 'With various' means due to the varieties of eatables, lickables, and the like. The syntactic connection is 'should honor with flowers and the like.' The meaning is 'should worship.' 'Should venerate' means with respect. 'Should esteem' means

body.text: premnā(mṇā) / pūjayediti praṇāmāñjalistutyādibhiḥ / arcayediti dakṣiṇāvartaiḥ / apacāyediti nirmālyādyapanayanaiḥ / śarīrāṇīti dhātūna / stūpeṣviti cetyeṣu pratiṣṭhāpayedavasthāpayet / parigṛṇhīyāt karaṇḍādīn kṛtvā / dhārayedvā karaṇḍādivahanāt / tāṃśceti stūpakaraṇḍādīn / yoyaṃ sarvajñatātmabhāva iti sarvajñataivātmabhāvaḥ / sa nirvartitaḥ / katamasyāṃ pratipadi śikṣamāṇena yāvatsamyaksambuddhena / kā punaḥ sarvajñatetyāha / anuttarāsamyaksambodhiḥ sarvajñateti / abhinirvartitārthaḥ / ka ityāha / asyāpyarthamāha / pratilabdheti / ihaiveti asyāmeva / ātmabhāvaścāsau ātmaprajñapteḥ śarīraṃ ca rūpakāyastathāgato gacchati / kiṃ gacchati tathāgata iti / saṃkhyāṃ gaṇanām / prajñāpāramitā ca upāyakauśalyaṃ ca tābhyāṃ nirjātaḥ san / prabhāvanāntāścatvāro nirdeśāḥ / loke pratītiḥ prabhāvanā / ayamevaiti bhagavatīpūjakaḥ / tatra iti tathāgataśarīrapūjakāt / śeṣaṃ subodham / iti svārthādhimuktiḥ mṛdumṛdvī //
body.translated_text: with affection. 'Should worship' means with prostrations, <s>añjali</s> (joined palms), praises, and the like. 'Should adore' means with circumambulation. 'Should honor' means by removing garland-remnants and the like. 'Relics' means <s>dhātus</s> (bodily remains). 'In <s>stūpas</s>' means one should establish, should deposit them in <s>caityas</s> (shrines). 'Should enclose' means having made caskets and the like. 'Or should hold' means through carrying caskets and the like. 'And those' refers to the <s>stūpas</s>, caskets, and the like. 'The very being of omniscience' — <s>sarvajñatā</s> itself is the essential nature (<s>ātmabhāva</s>). That has been accomplished. On what path of training, up to perfect <s>samyaksaṃbuddha</s>? 'What then is <s>sarvajñatā</s>?' — he says: '<s>Anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening) is <s>sarvajñatā</s>.' The meaning is 'accomplished.' 'Who?' — he states the meaning of this too. 'Obtained.' 'In this very' means in this very [body]. 'And the essential nature' — this is the body, and the physical form-body. The <s>Tathāgata</s> goes. What does the <s>Tathāgata</s> go [to]? The count, the number. <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and <s>upāyakauśalya</s> (skillful means) — born from those two. The four expositions end with 'bringing about.' 'Esteem in the world' means bringing about. 'This very one' refers to the worshipper of the <s>Bhagavatī</s> (the text). 'There' means compared to the worshipper of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body. The rest is easily understood. Thus ends the mild-mild aspiration for one's own benefit.

body.text: evamukte śakra ityādinā hīnaprajñairityetadantena dvītiyā / likhiṣyanti yāvatparyavāpsyantīti svārthaḥ / tata ūrdhva parārthaḥ / tatra pravartayiṣyantītyuddeśaḥ / tribhirnirdeśaḥ / deśayiṣyantītyarthataḥ / upadekṣyantītityavadiṣyanti / uddekṣyantīti granthataḥ / svādhyāsyantīti svādhyāna(ya)ma(mi)tyabhyāsaḥ / mahārthikā mahāphalā / sā kṛtā satī evaṃ bhaviṣyatīti mahāphalaiva bhaviṣyatīti / na jñāsyantīti na śroṣyanti śabdataḥ / na vetsyantīti pustakaṃ na lapsyante / na vedayiṣyantīti / vedanaṃ vedaḥ arthajñānam / tatkarotītiṇic / arthaṃ na jñāsyantītyarthaḥ / uteti prakārāntaram / avetyeti lokottareṇa jñānena satyān jñātvā / prasādaḥ cittagato dharmaḥ / yena cittamatyantamakaluṣīkriyate / udakamiva dakaprasādena maṇinā / śrotasa āpattiḥ saiva phalam / sakṛdāgāmino 'nāgāminaśca phalam / arhato bhāvo 'rhatvaṃ caturthaphalam / ātmānamekaṃ prati bodhiḥ pratyekabodhiḥ / upavṛṃhayitveti lyap kasmānna bhavati? upabṛhaṃnamupabṛṃhaḥ taṃ kṛtvetyeke / tathāpi prāpnoti / curādau saṃgrāmayatipāṭhasya niyamārthatvāt' saṃgrāmayatereva sopasargāt nānyasmāditi / tasmāt prādipratirūpako yanna prādiḥ pradattādivat / avinivartanāya hitā avinivartanīyā / durabhisambheveti durlabhā / vīryaṃ kuśale karmaṇyutsāhaḥ / kutsitakarmaṇi saktaḥ kusīdaḥ / sīdateḥ sapratyayo 'ravindavat / sattvaṃ dhairyaḥ / cittaṃ samādhiḥ / saṃjñā smṛtiḥ / adhimuktiḥ śraddhā / tattvapravicayaḥ prajñā / śraddhādindriyāṇāṃ daurbalyaṃ hīnavīryādipadairucyate / tatra hīnavīryaḥ kusīdairiti viryendriyasya hīnasattvaiḥ / hīnacittairiti samādhīndriyasya / hīnasaṃjñairiti smṛtīndriyasya / hīnādhimuktikairiti
body.translated_text: With 'thus spoken, O <s>Śakra</s>' and so forth, up to 'with inferior wisdom,' is the second [aspiration]. 'Will write' up to 'will obtain' is the self-benefit. After that is the benefit for others. Therein, 'will set in motion' is the general statement. The three are the detailed exposition. 'Will teach' means regarding the meaning. 'Will instruct' means they will explain. 'Will expound' means regarding the text. 'Will study' means study, which is practice/repetition. 'Of great purpose, of great fruit' — being done thus, it will be of great fruit indeed. 'Will not know' means will not hear verbally. 'Will not understand' means will not obtain the book. 'Will not realize' — <s>vedana</s> is <s>veda</s>, knowledge of the meaning; the causative means 'will not know the meaning.' 'Or' indicates another manner. 'Having realized' means having known the truths by supramundane knowledge. '<s>Prasāda</s>' (faith) is a mental quality by which the mind is made utterly unclouded, like water by a water-clearing gem. 'Attainment of the stream' is itself the fruit [of stream-entry]. 'The fruit of the once-returner, non-returner.' 'The state of being an <s>arhat</s>' is the fourth fruit. '<s>Pratyekabodhi</s>' (solitary awakening) is awakening directed toward oneself alone. 'Having nourished' — why is the <s>lyap</s> [suffix used]? Some say '<s>upabṛṃhana</s> is <s>upabṛṃha</s>, having done that.' Even so it is obtained. Because in the <s>curādi</s> class, the reading '<s>saṃgrāmayati</s>' serves as a restriction — 'only from <s>saṃgrāmayati</s> with the prefix, not from another.' Therefore the <s>prādi</s> [prefix rule] is a pseudo-rule, and the <s>prādi</s> does not apply, like in <s>pradatta</s> and the like. '<s>Avinivartanīya</s>' means conducive to non-regression. 'Difficult to attain' means rare. '<s>Vīrya</s>' (vigor) is enthusiasm in wholesome action. One attached to base action is <s>kusīda</s> (lazy). From the root <s>sīd</s>, with suffix, like <s>aravinda</s>. '<s>Sattva</s>' means fortitude. '<s>Citta</s>' means <s>samādhi</s> (concentration). '<s>Saṃjñā</s>' means <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness). '<s>Adhimukti</s>' means <s>śraddhā</s> (faith). '<s>Tattvapravicaya</s>' means <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). The weakness of the faculties of faith and the like is expressed by the words 'inferior vigor' and so forth. Therein, 'of inferior vigor' means 'by those who are lazy' — [referring to] the weakness of the faculty of vigor. 'Of inferior mind' — [weakness] of the faculty of concentration. 'Of inferior cognition' — of the faculty of mindfulness. 'Of inferior aspiration' —

body.text: śraddhendriyasya / hīnaprajñairiti prajñendriyasya / bhagavatyā durabhisambhavatvajñānaṃ sopattikaṃ caryātirekaḥ / puṇyātireka ūhyaḥ / śeṣaṃ pūrvavat / iti svārthādhimuktirmṛdumadhyā //
body.translated_text: of the faculty of faith. 'Of inferior discernment of reality' — of the faculty of wisdom. Thus, the five words 'of inferior vigor' and so forth express the weakness of the five faculties. Thus ends the mild-middling [aspiration] for one's own benefit.

body.text: tasmāttarhītyādinā pratisartavyāntena tṛtīyā / abhīkṣṇaṃ śravaṇādi paripraśnaśca saṃśayacddedārthaḥ / pratisartavyatāyāśca sopattikaṃ jñānamante caryātireka ūhyaḥ / śeṣaṃ pūrvavat / iti svārthādhimuktirmṛdvadhimātrā //
body.translated_text: With 'thus spoken, O <s>Śakra</s>' and so forth, up to the words 'will quickly, speedily, swiftly attain <s>anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi</s>' is the third, the mild-intense [aspiration]. This too is for one's own and others' benefit. Therein, [regarding] 'Even the <s>Tathāgata</s> dwelt in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>' — 'dwelt' means practiced. The attainment of <s>anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi</s> and the turning of the wheel of <s>Dharma</s> too were accomplished through the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> — when this is heard, strong aspiration is produced. Therefore this is the intense. The meaning of 'quickly, speedily, swiftly' is by three divisions of time: 'quickly' means without delay in the [current] life; 'speedily' means in few lives; 'swiftly' means with little difficulty. Thus [ends] the aspiration for one's own benefit.

body.text: tasmāttarhītyādinā dvitīyaprasavatiparyantena caturthī / saptaratnāni tadyathā suvarṇa rūpyaṃ vaiḍūrya musāragalvaṃ / aśmagarbhaḥ lohitikā muktā karketanaṃ ca / tannidānamiti taddhetukam bhagavatyāṃ śraddhadhimokṣaprasādāḥ / cittotpādo 'dhyāśayataḥ / śravaṇādikaṃ arthavivaraṇaṃ manasā anvavekṣā parimīmāṃsā ca / pustakagatāṃ vā kṛtvā saddharmacirasthiti hetornetrya vaikalyāya ca / avasthāpanaṃ caryātirekaḥ puṇyātirekaḥ / yathāpāṭhaṃ śeṣa purvavat / iti svārthadhimaktirmadhyamṛdvī //
body.translated_text: The aspiration for one's own and others' benefit in the mild, middling, and intense [degrees] — these three are [stated] with 'thus spoken, O <s>Śakra</s>' and so forth, up to 'will be of the nature of accomplishing the aims of beings.' The mild is stated by [the passage on] the merit of writing and the like. The middling, by [the passage on] the dharmic gift being superior to the material gift. The intense, by the statement of the great fruit. The rest is easily understood.

body.text: tiṣṭhantu khalvityādinā dvitīya prasavatiparyantena pañcamī / eṣa eva dvitīyo mūrajaphalena mahatā jambuvṛkṣeṇa lakṣitatvāt jambūdvīpaḥ / tato nidānamutpattirasyeti tathoktam / śeṣaṃ subodham / itaḥ prabhṛti yatrānuśaṃsaḥ paṭhyate na caryātirekastatra yadyathoktānuśaṃsa śraddhādikaṃ sa caryātirekaḥ / iti svārthādhimuktirmadhyamadhyā //
body.translated_text: The aspiration for others' benefit too, in its mild, middling, and intense [degrees] — these three are [stated] with 'thus spoken, O <s>Śakra</s>' and so forth up to the end. Among these, [the mild is from] 'that son of good family or daughter of good family who would write' up to 'the great earth.' This is the mild. The middling is from 'moreover, O <s>Śakra</s>' up to 'the immeasurable, incalculable merit.' The intense is from 'moreover, O <s>Śakra</s>' up to the end [of the section].

body.text: tiṣṭhantvityādinā dvitīyaprasavatyantena ṣaṣṭhī / catvāro mahādvīpā āsminniti cāturmahādvīpaḥ / svārthe aṇa / lokadhāraṇāt lokadhātau / śeṣaṃ tathaiva / iti svārthādhimuktirmadhyādhimātrā //
body.translated_text: Therein, in the mild, 'having written' means by one's own hand. 'Or having caused to be written' means through another. 'Having tied' means having bound with thread. 'Having wrapped' means having enclosed in cloth. 'On a high place' — because [the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>] is a deity. 'Would establish' means would place. However, he would not worship. Why? Because he is of inferior aspiration — merely for others' benefit, not for one's own. 'Even so' — even without worship. 'Shall I declare?' — because the merit is abundant. 'Will be established in the irreversible stage' — by hearing [the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>]. [Up to] 'the great earth' is easily understood.

body.text: tiṣṭhantvityādi dvitīyaprasavatiparyantā saptamī / caturdvīpakānāṃ sahasraṃ parimāṇamasyeti sāhasraḥ / sa eva paripurṇatvena cūḍāyogāt cūḍikaḥ / iti svārthādhimuktiradhimātramṛdvī //
body.translated_text: In the middling, 'that gift' is the material gift. 'Would not equal' means would not amount to even a hundredth part. And here, the reason for its being middling is that it goes beyond mere establishment and adds worship, including dharmic [gift]. In the intense, 'of deluded mind' means of confused minds. The rest is easily understood. Thus [ends] the aspiration-mental-attention. //

body.text: tathobhayāntā aṣṭamī / dvīḥsāhasraṃ parimāṇamasyeti dvisāhasraḥ sāhasrasahasramityarthaḥ / sa ca madhyamaḥ sāhasramahāsāhasrayormadhyatvāt / iti svārthadhimuktiradhimātramadhyā //
body.translated_text: Similarly, the eighth [stage of aspiration] has both endpoints. "That whose measure is two-thousand" — thus <s>dvisāhasra</s> (bi-chiliocosm), meaning a thousand of thousands. And it is the middle one, because of being intermediate between <s>sāhasra</s> (chiliocosm) and <s>mahāsāhasra</s> (trichiliocosm). Thus, the aspiration regarding one's own benefit is of the medium-supreme degree.

body.text: tathaivāntau navamyām / triḥsahasraṃ parimāṇamasyeti trisāhasram /
body.translated_text: Similarly, both endpoints [belong to] the ninth [stage]. "That whose measure is three-thousand" — thus <s>trisāhasra</s> (trichiliocosm).

body.text: dvi(tri)sāhasrāṇāṃ sahasramityarthaḥ / sa eva mahāsāhasraḥ / iti svārthādhimuktiradhimātrādhimātrā //
body.translated_text: A thousand of <s>dvisāhasras</s> (or <s>trisāhasras</s>) — this is the meaning. That itself is the <s>mahāsāhasra</s> (great trichiliocosm). Thus, the aspiration regarding one's own benefit is of the supreme-supreme degree.

body.text: tiṣṭhantvādirbhavatiparyantā daśamī / trisāhasra eva lokadhātuḥ / kintu tasmin sarvasattvā manuṣyā bhaveyuḥ / na pūrvaṃ na caramamasminnityapūrvācaramam sahetyarthaḥ / ato jñāyata iha sattvā eva sattvāḥ pūrvatra manuṣyā eveti / parikalpaḥ kalpanā / yāvajjīvaṃ caityapūjā sarvāsu / iha tu kalpaṃ vā kalpāvaśeṣaṃ vā / asyāṃ ca sarvagītavādyaiḥ sarvapuṣpādibhiścaityapūjātirekaḥ / bhagavatīpūjāpuṇyātirekopapattijñānamante / so 'syāṃ caryāpūjātireka / iti parārthadhimuktirmṛdumṛdvī //
body.translated_text: [The passage] beginning with "let them remain" and ending with "it is" is the tenth [stage]. It is the <s>trisāhasra</s> (trichiliocosm) world-realm itself. But in it, all beings would be humans. "Not prior, not final, in this" — meaning "simultaneously together." From this it is known: here "beings" means just beings; in the former [passage], "humans" means just humans. <s>Parikalpa</s> is conceptual construction. Worship of <s>caityas</s> (shrines) for as long as one lives, in all [the former stages]. But here, for a <s>kalpa</s> (aeon) or the remainder of a <s>kalpa</s>. And in this [stage] there is an excess of <s>caitya</s>-worship through all songs and music, all flowers and the like. At the end is the knowledge of the arising of the excess of merit from worship of the <s>Bhagavatī</s> (the Noble Lady, i.e., Prajñāpāramitā). That is the excess of practice-worship in this [stage]. Thus, the aspiration regarding the benefit of others is of the mild-mild degree.

body.text: tiṣṭhantvityādinā prajñāpāramitā mahāsamudrādityetadantenaikādaśī / gaṅgānadīvālikopameṣu trisāhasreṣviti stupasatkāre viśeṣaḥ / śeṣaṃ daśamīvat / bhagavatīcaryāpūjāsu sopapattikamanuśaṃsavistara parijñānamatirekaḥ / idṛśatvena cittātikramād acintyā sadṛśābhāvād atulyam / puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ puṇyakarma / śatatamīmapītyādi / ādāvante ca kalāṃ nopaitīti vacanaṃ madhyepi sambandhārtham / atra ca bhāgaḥ kalā / nopaitīti nārghati / na labhata ityarthaḥ / na kevalaṃ kalāṃ nopaiti tulanārtham / kiṃ tarhi saṃkhyāmapi kalāmapi gaṇanāmapi / apiśabdaiḥ parasparāpekṣayā samuccayaḥ / uktaṃ yathā kalāṃ nopaiti / kathaṃ saṃkhyā? saṃkhyābhirekai [ra] pyatulanāt / pūrvakasya puṇyasya śatamapi sahasramapi yāvatkoṭīśatasahasramapi paścimasya puṇyasya tulanāya na kṣamata iti / gaṇanā gaṇitaṃ pratyutpannādiḥ / tāṃ kathaṃ nopaiti? tadatirekepyatulanāt / pūrvakasya puṇyasya pañcaguṇāpi viṃśatirdaśaguṇamapi sa (śa)taṃ yāvallakṣaguṇāpi koṭī paścimasya puṇyasya tulanāya na kṣamata iti / upamāmapyaupamyapi upaniśāmapi na kṣama [ta] iti pareṇa sambandhaḥ / upamitirūpamā / saiva aupamyam / 'svārthe pyañ / upaniśānamupaniśā / tatrābhinnamupamānamupamā saṃkhyātamupamānamaupamyam / gaṇitamupamānamupaniśā / tadapi trayaṃ tulanāya na kṣamate / tadyathā kalāprasṛtopamenāpi pūrvakeṇa na śakyamuttaraṃ tulayitum / daśaprasṛtopamenāpīti / upaniṣadamapi na kṣamata iti / evamatyantatulanābhāvāt tulanārthayā upaniṣat samīpaniṣadanaṃ pārśvato 'vasthitiḥ, tāmapi nārhatītyarthaḥ / mārṣeti āmantraṇam / āryetyarthaḥ / samudācārā abhiprāyāḥ / samanvāhāraḥ smaraṇam /
body.translated_text: [The passage] beginning with "let them remain" up to and ending with "<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is a great ocean" is the eleventh [stage]. In the worship of <s>stūpas</s> in <s>trisāhasras</s> (trichiliocosms) comparable to the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, there is a distinction. The rest is like the tenth [stage]. The excess is the detailed knowledge with reasons of the benefits of worship of the <s>Bhagavatī</s> through practice-worship. Being inconceivable due to surpassing the mind, because of the nature of such [merit]; unequalled due to the absence of anything similar. <s>Puṇyābhisaṃskāra</s> (meritorious formation) is meritorious action. "Not even a hundredth part" and so on. The statement "does not approach even a fraction" at the beginning and end serves the purpose of connection with the middle as well. And here, a "fraction" (<s>kalā</s>) is a part. "Does not approach" means "is not worthy of." "Does not obtain" — this is the meaning. Not only does it not approach a fraction for the purpose of comparison, but what then? Not even a count (<s>saṃkhyā</s>), not even a fraction (<s>kalā</s>), not even a calculation (<s>gaṇanā</s>). By the words "even," there is a cumulative conjunction in mutual relation. It has been said "it does not approach a fraction." How [does it not approach] a count? Because it is incomparable even by units — a hundred, a thousand, up to a hundred thousand <s>koṭīs</s> of the former merit is not capable of comparison with the latter merit. Calculation (<s>gaṇanā</s>) is arithmetic — multiplication and the like. How does it not approach that? Because it is incomparable even by multiples — five times, twenty times, ten times, a hundred times, up to a <s>lakṣa</s> times, a <s>koṭī</s> of the former merit is not capable of comparison with the latter merit. "Not even a simile (<s>upamā</s>), not even a resemblance (<s>aupamya</s>), not even an analogy (<s>upaniśā</s>) is it capable of" — this connects with the following. <s>Upamiti</s> (comparison) is <s>upamā</s>. That itself is <s>aupamya</s>. "In one's own sense, the <s>ṣyañ</s> [suffix]." <s>Upaniśāna</s> is <s>upaniśā</s>. Among these, an undifferentiated standard of comparison is <s>upamā</s>; a counted standard of comparison is <s>aupamya</s>; a calculated standard of comparison is <s>upaniśā</s>. Even those three are not capable of comparison. That is, even by a standard of comparison of the measure of a fraction (<s>kalā-prasṛta</s>), the former cannot be compared with the latter. "Nor even by a standard of comparison of ten measures" and so on. "It is not capable even of an <s>upaniṣad</s> (proximity)" — thus, because of the absolute impossibility of comparison, the <s>upaniṣad</s> which serves the purpose of comparison — meaning "proximity, standing beside" — it is not worthy even of that — this is the meaning. "<s>Mārṣa</s>" is an address, meaning "<s>Ārya</s>" (Noble One). "Dispositions" (<s>samudācārāḥ</s>) are intentions. "Recollection" (<s>samanvāhāra</s>) is remembering.

body.text:
svādhyāyo mano jāpaḥ / mahāvidyādipada trayaṃ vyākhyātama / ato 'dhikāyā vidyāyā abhāvānniruttarā / atodhikasya dharmasyābhāvādanuttarā / tulyavidyāntarābhāvā dasamā / asamaistathāgataiḥ samatvādasamasamā / prabhāvyanta iti prakāśante / saptabhirbodhyaṅgaiḥ samprayuktāni taṃ niśrayatvāt / taiḥ parigṛhītā adhiṣṭhitāḥ / buddhānāṃ jñānaṃ svayaṃ bhāvāt svayambhū / cittātikramādacintyam / pūrvaśruteneti pūrvaśrutobhdavena / auṣadhītāra iti auṣadhyaśca tārāśca / avabhāsayantītyavabhāsaṃ kurvanti / dharmo nirvāṇaṃ sarvadharmotkṛṣṭatvāt / sa eva samaḥ yānatrayasya dhāraṇatvāt / sa eva sa (śa)maḥ kleśaduḥkhopasamatvāt /
tasmai caryā / kuśalaṃ sucaritaṃ tasya caryā / viṣamo mṛtyuhetuḥ / tasyāparihāro viṣamāparihāraḥ / ayamuddeśaḥ / śeṣo nirdeśaḥ / daṇḍa upavāsanādiḥ / parigṛhītatvaṃ pratyupasthiteti / tatsvabhāvena tathābhāvāt / vyāḍāḥ caṇḍamṛgāḥ / sarīsṛpāḥ sarpāḥ kuṭilaṃ gamanāt / teṣāṃ kāntāraḥ / sthāpayitvetyādi yatpūrvakarmavipākena taṃ bahiṣkṛtya / samanvāhāro manasikaraṇam / pratihatacittā iti sadveṣacitāḥ / vicakṣuḥ vimanāḥ / balakāyo balasamūhaḥ / tasya catvāryaṅgāni gajavājipattirathāḥ / vyūhaḥ sannipātaḥ / bimbisāro magadhādhipaḥ / prasenajit srāvastīpatiḥ / śākyāḥ śākyakulajāḥ kṣatriyāḥ / licchavayo vaiśālakāḥ / pratyu[dā]vṛtto nivṛttaḥ / vihāyasāntarīkṣagatā iti ākāśenākāśaṅgatāḥ / cirasyeti cireṇa / upāvṛtteti punarāyātā / avarakeṇeti alpakena / yathā prajñāpāramitā tathābhāvaṃ tathātvam / prajñāpāramitaiva mahāsamudraḥ / iti svaparārthādhimuktiḥ mṛdumadhyā //
body.translated_text:
"Self-study" (<s>svādhyāya</s>) is mental recitation (<s>manojāpa</s>). The triad of words beginning with <s>mahāvidyā</s> (great science) has been explained. Because there is no science higher than this, it is unsurpassed (<s>niruttarā</s>). Because there is no <s>dharma</s> higher than this, it is supreme (<s>anuttarā</s>). Because there is no equal science, it is the tenth [perfection]. Equal to the <s>Tathāgatas</s> who are unequaled — therefore "<s>asamasamā</s>" (equal to the unequaled). "They shine forth" (<s>prabhāvyante</s>) means they become manifest. "Connected with the seven factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅgas</s>)" means because of depending on them. "Taken up by those" means "supported, sustained." The knowledge of the <s>Buddhas</s> is "self-born" (<s>svayambhū</s>) because of its self-nature. Because of surpassing the mind, it is inconceivable (<s>acintya</s>). "By prior hearing" means by what has arisen from prior hearing. "<s>Auṣadhī-tāra</s>" means herbs and stars. "They illuminate" means they produce radiance. "<s>Dharma</s>" is <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, because it is the most excellent of all <s>dharmas</s>. That itself is "equal" (<s>sama</s>), because it supports the three vehicles. That itself is "peace" (<s>śama</s>), because of the subsiding of defilements and suffering.
The practice directed toward that. "Wholesome" (<s>kuśala</s>) is good conduct; its practice. "Uneven" (<s>viṣama</s>) is the cause of death. Its non-avoidance is "<s>viṣamāparihāra</s>" (non-avoidance of danger). This is the summary. The rest is the detailed exposition. "Punishment" (<s>daṇḍa</s>) is [practices such as] fasting and the like. "Being taken up" (<s>parigṛhītatva</s>) is [expressed as] "having arrived." Because of the nature of that [state], it is so. "Wild beasts" (<s>vyāḍāḥ</s>) are fierce animals. "Creeping creatures" (<s>sarīsṛpāḥ</s>) are serpents, because of their crooked movement. Their wilderness (<s>kāntāra</s>). "Setting aside" and so on — by the ripening of past <s>karma</s>, excluding that [being]. "Recollection" (<s>samanvāhāra</s>) is mental attention. "Those with repelled minds" means those with hostile thoughts. "Without eyes, without mind." "Army-body" (<s>balakāya</s>) is the assembled forces. Its four divisions are elephants, horses, infantry, and chariots. "Formation" (<s>vyūha</s>) is an array. <s>Bimbisāra</s> is the lord of <s>Magadha</s>. <s>Prasenajit</s> is the lord of <s>Śrāvastī</s>. The <s>Śākyas</s> are <s>Kṣatriyas</s> born in the <s>Śākya</s> clan. The <s>Licchavis</s> are those of <s>Vaiśālī</s>. "Turned back" (<s>pratyudāvṛtta</s>) means withdrawn. "Through the sky" — meaning "gone through the atmosphere," that is, "traveling through space." "After a long time" (<s>cirasyā</s>) means "after a long while." "Returned" (<s>upāvṛttā</s>) means "come back again." "By a small [amount]" (<s>avarakeṇa</s>) means "by a little." "The nature of being just as <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is" is its <s>tathatva</s> (suchness). <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> itself is the great ocean. Thus, the aspiration regarding the benefit of others is of the mild-middle degree.

body.text: atha khalvityādinā dvitīya pariṇāyikāntena dvādaśī / ṣaṭpāramitānāyikatvādijñānaṃ sopattikaścaryātirekaḥ puṇyātireka uktaḥ / śeṣaṃ pūrvavat / varṇaḥ stotraṃ guṇā vā / pūrvaṅgameti agreśvarī / nāyiketi saṃgrāhikā / pariṇāyiketi saṃvardhikā / prajñāpāramitā hi svayemeva paramatvāt pāramitā / itarāstayaiva sarvajñatāyāṃ pariṇāmitatvena / śeṣaṃ subodham / iti svaparārthadhimuktirmṛdvadhimātrā /
body.translated_text: Now, [the passage] beginning with "now then" up to and ending with "the second guide" is the twelfth [stage]. Because [<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>] is the guide of the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), the knowledge with reasoning of the excess of practice, the excess of merit, is stated. The rest is as before. "Praise" (<s>varṇa</s>) is eulogy or [enumeration of] qualities. "Forerunner" (<s>pūrvaṅgamā</s>) means the foremost. "Guide" (<s>nāyikā</s>) means the gatherer. "Leader" (<s>pariṇāyikā</s>) means the developer. For <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> itself, being supreme, is a <s>pāramitā</s> (perfection) by its very nature. The others [are perfections] because they are brought to completion in <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience) by that very [Prajñāpāramitā]. The rest is easily understood. Thus, the aspiration regarding the benefit of both self and others is of the mild-supreme degree.

body.text: atha khalvityādinā guṇān vadāmītyetadantena trayodaśī / yopyenāṃ pustakagatāṃ saddharmacirasthitihetoḥ sthāpayitvā pūjayet / tasyāpi sarva ete 'nuśaṃsā iti jñānamatra caryadhikyam / iti svaparārthādhimuktirmadhyamṛdvī /
body.translated_text: Now, [the passage] beginning with "now then" up to and ending with "I shall declare the qualities" is the thirteenth [stage]. "Whoever, having placed it in book form for the sake of the long endurance of the true <s>Dharma</s>, would worship it" — the knowledge here is the excess of practice, that all these benefits accrue even to that person. Thus, the aspiration regarding the benefit of both self and others is of the middle-mild degree.

body.text: evamukta ityādirdvitīyapunaraparāt prāk caturdaśī / ryātireko yathābhūtam / iti svaparārthādhimuktirmadhyamadhyā /
body.translated_text: [The passage] beginning with "thus spoken" up to just before the second "moreover" is the fourteenth [stage]. The excess of practice is as it truly is. Thus, the aspiration regarding the benefit of both self and others is of the middle-middle degree.

body.text: punaraparamityādinā yatra khalu punarityataḥ prāk pañcadaśī / pratyanuyogaḥ praśnaḥ / iti svaparārthādhimuktirmadhyādhimātrā //
body.translated_text: [The passage] beginning with "moreover" up to just before "wherever indeed" is the fifteenth [stage]. "Cross-questioning" (<s>pratyanuyoga</s>) is inquiry. Thus, the aspiration regarding the benefit of both self and others is of the middle-supreme degree.

body.text: yatra khalvityādinā evamukta ityataḥ prāk ṣoḍaśī / sarvadevopasaṃkramaṇaśraddhā tebhyaśca dharmadānacaryātirekaḥ / iti svaparārthādhimuktiradhimātramṛdvī //
body.translated_text: [The passage] beginning with "wherever indeed" up to just before "thus spoken" is the sixteenth [stage]. The coming of all gods and the faith [generated thereby], and the excess of practice in giving the <s>Dharma</s> to them. Thus, the aspiration regarding the benefit of both self and others is of the supreme-mild degree.

body.text: evamukta ityādinā dṛṣṭadhārmikān guṇān parigṛṇhātītyetadantena saptadaśī / devādyāgamanārcanajñānāt praharṣo bhagavatīprabhāvena śraddhādikaṃ caryātirekaḥ / saṃjānīta iti saṃlakṣayati / niṣṭheti niścayaḥ / gantavyeti kartavyā / amānuṣaṃ sattvamiti manuṣyeṣu bhavo mānuṣaḥ / na tathā amānuṣaḥ / aśucyabhāvāt caukṣaḥ / puṣpādiyogāt śuciḥ / apakramaṇamapamaraṇam / klamathaḥ pīḍā / udāro mahān / pratibhotsyata iti budhyateḥ prayogaḥ / gṛddhiḥ abhilāṣaḥ / saṃjñā smṛti / iti svaparārthādhimuktiradhimātramadhyā //
body.translated_text: [The passage] beginning with "thus spoken" up to and ending with "he recounts the qualities visible in this very life" is the seventeenth [stage]. From the knowledge of the coming, worship, and [other activities] of gods and others, there is delight, and through the power of the <s>Bhagavatī</s>, faith and so on is the excess of practice. "Recognizes" (<s>saṃjānīte</s>) means "discerns." "Conclusion" (<s>niṣṭhā</s>) means "certainty." "To be gone to" (<s>gantavyā</s>) means "to be practiced." "A non-human being" — "<s>mānuṣa</s>" means born among humans; not so is "<s>amānuṣa</s>" (non-human). Because of the absence of impurity, [it is] "clean" (<s>caukṣa</s>). Because of contact with flowers and such, [it is] "pure" (<s>śuci</s>). "Departure" (<s>apakramaṇa</s>) is death. "Fatigue" (<s>klamatha</s>) is affliction. "Noble" (<s>udāra</s>) means great. "Will comprehend" (<s>pratibhotsyate</s>) — this is a form from the root <s>budh</s> (to know). "Eagerness" (<s>gṛddhi</s>) is longing. "Cognition" (<s>saṃjñā</s>) is mindfulness. Thus, the aspiration regarding the benefit of both self and others is of the supreme-middle degree.

body.text: punaraparamityādinā āparivartasamāpteraṣṭādaśī / caryātireko yathāsūtram / iti svaparārthādhimuktiradhimātrādhimātrā //
body.translated_text: [The passage] beginning with "moreover" up to the end of the chapter is the eighteenth [stage]. The excess of practice is as stated in the <s>sūtra</s>. Thus, the aspiration regarding the benefit of both self and others is of the supreme-supreme degree.

body.text: aprameyetyādi / atra stūpaścaityam / pāramitā prajñāpāramitā / dhāraṇaṃ dvividham / pustakagatāṃ kṛtvā yadasyāḥ saddharmacirasthitaye bahiḥsthāpanam / yaccodgrahaṇadhāraṇādibhiradhyātmameva sthāpanam //
body.translated_text: "Immeasurable" and so on. Here, a <s>stūpa</s> is a <s>caitya</s> (shrine). "<s>Pāramitā</s>" means <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. "Holding" (<s>dhāraṇa</s>) is twofold: the external preservation for the sake of the long endurance of the true <s>Dharma</s>, having placed it in book form; and the internal preservation through reception, retention, and so on.

body.text: aprameyaguṇadhāraṇaṃ yasyāḥ sā tathoktā / tathoktā ca sā parāmitā ca sā ca stūpaśceti dvandvaḥ / tayoḥ satkāraḥ puṣpādibhiḥ pūjā / tadabhidhāyī parivarto 'prameyaguṇadhāraṇastūpasatkāraparivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: That which holds immeasurable qualities — it is so called. And it is both a <s>pāramitā</s> (perfection) and a <s>stūpa</s> — thus a <s>dvandva</s> (copulative compound). Worship of them both with flowers and the like. The chapter expressing that is the "Chapter on the Worship of the Stūpa that Holds Immeasurable Qualities."

body.text: āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ sāratamānāmni pañjikāyāṃ ratnākaraśāntiviracitāyāṃ tṛtīyaḥ parivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: End of the third chapter in the commentary called <s>Sāratama</s>, composed by <s>Ratnākaraśānti</s>, on the Noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

body.text: 4. guṇaparikīrtanaparivarto nāma caturthaḥ /
body.translated_text: 4. The fourth chapter, called the Chapter on the Proclamation of Qualities.

body.text: adhimuktayo 'dhikṛtāḥ / tatra nava svārthā navaiva ca svaparārthā uktāḥ / asmiṃstu parivarte navaiva parārthā vaktavyāḥ / tatrādau tathāgataśarīreṣvityetadantena ūnaviṃśatitamī / prajñāpāramitaiva dharmakāyatvādatyantapūjyā / tathā rūpakāyaḥ satyakāyatvādityetasminnarthe yau śraddhāprasādau sāmarthyagamyaśca mātrātirekaḥ sa iha caryātirekaḥ / tathāgatānāṃ śarīrāṇi dhātavaḥ / karaṇe ṣaṣṭhī / taiḥ paripūrṇaḥ / kiṃ vyāptimātreṇa? netyāha / cūḍikābaddha iti / dīyeta iti upanyasyeta / ekatareṇa pravāryamāṇa iti / anayorekaṃ gṛhāṇeti nimantryamānaḥ / citrīkāro gauravātiśayaḥ / gurutarā hi bhagavatī tebhyaḥ / etaddhi śarīramiti / yā prajñāpāramitā / bhūtārthastathyārthaḥ / tadyogāt bhūtārthikam / sīdatīti sat / anityaḥ / saccāsau kāyaśceti satkāyo rūpakāyaḥ / dharmakāyapariniṣpattita iti / atrāryamārgo dharmaḥ / sa ca prakarṣa gataḥ prajñāpāramitaiva / nānityaḥ pravāhanityatvāt / bhūtakoṭiprabhāvita iti / bhūtāni tattvāni teṣāṃ koṭiragram / tato 'dhikasya tattvasyābhāvāt / tasyāmeva prabhāvito vyahṛtastādātmyāt / katamaḥ kāya ityāha / yadutetyādi / tathatāmātraparamārthaṃ taddarśanī prajñāpāramitā na tato bhidyata iti bhāvaḥ / tatkiṃ tathāgatadhātuṣvagauravameva? netyāha / na khalvityādi subodham / iti parārthādhimuktirmṛdumṛdvī //
body.translated_text: The aspirations have been treated. Among them, nine [pertain to] one's own benefit, and nine likewise to the benefit of both self and others, as stated. But in this chapter, nine [pertaining to] the benefit of others alone are to be stated. There, first, [the passage] ending with "in the bodies of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>" is the nineteenth [stage]. <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> itself, being the <s>Dharmakāya</s> (truth-body), is supremely worthy of worship. Likewise the <s>Rūpakāya</s> (form-body), being the body of truth — in this matter, the faith and devotion [that arise], and the excess of measure that is understood through [its] power, that is the excess of practice here. The "bodies" (<s>śarīrāṇi</s>) of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> are relics (<s>dhātavaḥ</s>). The sixth case-ending is used in the instrumental sense. "Filled with those." Is it merely by pervasion? No, he says "bound into a pinnacle" (<s>cūḍikābaddha</s>). "Would be offered" means "would be presented." "Being urged by one of the two" — being invited [with the words] "take one of these two." "Special regard" (<s>citrīkāra</s>) is an excess of reverence. For the <s>Bhagavatī</s> is more venerable than those [relics]. "For this very body" — which is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. "True meaning" (<s>bhūtārtha</s>) is actual meaning. Because of connection with that, it is "pertaining to true meaning" (<s>bhūtārthika</s>). "That which exists" (<s>sīdati</s>) — [the prefix] <s>sat</s> [indicates] "impermanent." And it is both existing and a body — thus the <s>satkāya</s> (existing body) is the <s>Rūpakāya</s> (form-body). "From the completion of the <s>Dharmakāya</s>" — here, the noble path is the <s>dharma</s>. And that, in its highest form, is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> itself. "Not impermanent," because of continuity-permanence. "Manifested from the summit of reality" (<s>bhūtakoṭiprabhāvita</s>) — "realities" (<s>bhūtāni</s>) are truths (<s>tattvāni</s>); their "summit" (<s>koṭi</s>) is the apex, because there is no truth higher than that. "Manifested in that very [summit]" means "expressed [there]," because of identity [with it]. "Which body?" — to this he says, "namely" and so on. The ultimate reality of the mere <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) — <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, which reveals it, does not differ from it — this is the import. "Then is there indeed disrespect toward the <s>Tathāgata</s> relics?" No, he says, "certainly not" and so on — easily understood. Thus, the aspiration regarding the benefit of others is of the mild-mild degree.

body.text: api tvityādinā tiṣṭhatu khalvityataḥ prāgviṃśatitamī / apituśabdo viśeṣārthaḥ / yadyapi teṣu me gauravaṃ tathāpītyarthaḥ / punaḥśabdastu pūrvamapi viśeṣayoktatvāt / nirjātānīti viśeṣaṇatvepi hetutvaṃ gamyate nirjātatvādityarthaḥ / tadyathāpītyādinā dṛṣṭāntaḥ devasabhādhikaraṇatvāt devasabhā mahatī śālā yasyāṃ śakrastrayastriṃśebhyo dharma deśayati / ata eva sā sudharmetyucyate / [a] sya ca sudarśanasya devanagarasya dakṣiṇapaścimadigbhāga iti / īṣo (śo) mahāpuruṣaḥ / tasyākhyā pratibhāso rūciḥ / mahatī śākhā asyeti maheśākhyaḥ / mahānmanā ityarthaḥ / sa ceha jñānātmā samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ / tasya hetupratyayabhūto hetusvabhāvo pratyayasvabhāvo ca / ata evāha / tathāgatasyetyādi / tatra sarvajñajñānaṃ śakravat / tathāgatadhātavo nāsya hetupratyayabhūtāḥ /
body.translated_text: By 'Moreover' and so forth, up to just before 'Let it stand indeed' — this is the twentieth [section]. The word '<s>api tu</s>' (moreover) has the sense of a distinction: 'Even though I have reverence for those, still' — this is the meaning. The word '<s>punaḥ</s>' (again) [functions here] because a distinction was already stated earlier. '<s>Nirjātāni</s>' (produced) — though [functioning as] a qualifier, the causal sense is understood: 'because they are produced' — this is the meaning. By 'Just as' and so forth, an illustration [is given]: because it is the venue of the divine assembly. The divine assembly (<s>devasabhā</s>) is the great hall in which <s>Śakra</s> teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to the thirty-three [gods]. For this reason it is called '<s>Sudharmā</s>.' And it is in the south-western direction of this <s>Sudarśana</s> divine city. '<s>Īśa</s>' means the great being. His designation, his manifestation, is his splendor. 'Having great branches' (<s>Maheśākhya</s>) means 'having a great mind' — this is the meaning. And he is here the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> (Perfectly Awakened One), whose nature is knowledge. His cause and condition — [he has] the nature of a cause and the nature of a condition. Therefore he says: 'Of the <s>Tathāgata</s>' and so forth. Therein, the knowledge of the omniscient is like <s>Śakra</s>. The <s>Tathāgata</s> elements are not its causes and conditions.

body.text: śakrasya tadāsanavat / pūrvatra kāyasyādhārabhūto rūpakāya evoktaḥ / iha tu maheśākhyasya jñānakāyasyāsanasthānīyaḥ / ityasminnarthe yau śraddhāprasādau sa caryātirekaḥ / iti parārthādhimuktirmṛdumadhyā //
body.translated_text: Like <s>Śakra's</s> seat. In the earlier [passage], the <s>rūpakāya</s> (form body) was stated as the support of the body. But here, [the elements] stand in the position of a seat for the <s>jñānakāya</s> (knowledge body) called '<s>Maheśākhya</s>.' In this meaning, the faith and devotion constitute the special conduct. Thus, [this is] the aspiration for the benefit of others — soft-medium [degree].

body.text: tiṣṭhatvityādinā tathāgataśarīreṣvityetadantena ekaviṃśatitamī / ihoktabhagavatīmāhātmye yau śraddhāprasādau sa eva caryātirekaḥ / iti parārthādhimuktirmṛdvavadhimātrā //
body.translated_text: By 'Let it stand' and so forth, ending with 'in the bodies of the <s>Tathāgata</s>' — this is the twenty-first [section]. The faith and devotion regarding the greatness of the <s>Bhagavatī</s> (<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>) stated here is itself the special conduct. Thus, [this is] the aspiration for the benefit of others — only of the soft-lowest [degree].

body.text: api tvādi tathāgataśarīrāntāt dvāviṃśatitamī / tathāgato hi sarvalokā (ke) bhyudgatatvāt pūjyataraḥ pūjyatamaḥ sa ca sarvajñajñānam / tato yadi dhātavastadādhāratvāt pūjyāstadā tajjananī tatopi pūjyatamā kā kathā dhātūnāmityasminnarthe śraddhādikaṃ caryātirekaḥ / iti parārthādhimuktirmadhyamṛdvī //
body.translated_text: 'Moreover' and so on through 'bodies of the <s>Tathāgata</s>' — this is the twenty-second [section]. For the <s>Tathāgata</s>, being exalted above all worlds, is most supremely venerable — and he is the omniscient knowledge. Therefore, if the <s>dhātus</s> (relics) are venerable because they are its support, then the mother [<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>] who gave birth to it is even more supremely venerable — what then need be said of the relics? The faith and so on regarding this meaning constitute the special conduct. Thus, [this is] the aspiration for the benefit of others — medium-soft [degree].

body.text: api tvityādinā bhājanabhūtānyabhūvannityetadantena trayoviṃśatitamī / prajñāpāramitāyāḥ sarvajñajñānasya ca guṇā ihoktamaṇiratnānusāreṇa veditavyāḥ / yathā coddhṛtepi tasmiṃ maṇiratnakaraṇḍakaḥ spṛhaṇīyo bhavati / evaṃ buddhastanmātro guṇaiḥ parinirvṛtepi bhagavati dhātavaḥ pūjyā bhavantītyasminnarthe śraddhādikaṃ caryātirekaḥ / iti parārthādhimuktirmadhyamadhyā //
body.translated_text: By 'Moreover' and so forth, ending with 'became vessels' — this is the twenty-third [section]. The virtues of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and of the omniscient knowledge should be understood here in accordance with the precious gem-jewel [analogy]. The faith and so on regarding this constitute the special conduct.

body.text: yathā ca bhagavā(va)nityādinā tathāgataśarīreṣvityetadantena caturviśatitamī / yathā prajñāpāramitānirjātatvāddeśanādharmaḥ parairapi nirdeśyamānaḥ pūjyo bhavati / rājapuruṣaśca rājānubhāvādakutobhayaḥ sarvatra pūjyaḥ / evaṃ prajñāpāramitānirjātatvāttadanubhāvācca dhātavaḥ pūjyā ityasminnarthe puṇyātireke ca śraddhādikaṃ caryātirekaḥ / iti parārthādhimuktirmadhyādhimātrā //
body.translated_text: By 'Just as, O <s>Bhagavān</s>' and so forth, ending with 'in the bodies of the <s>Tathāgata</s>' — this is the twenty-fourth [section]. Just as, because it is produced from <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the teaching-dharma, when expounded even by others, is venerable

body.text: api tvityādinā pūjā kṛtā bhavatītyetadantena pañcaviṃśatitamī / bhagavatīpūjayā traiyadhvikatathāgatāḥ pūjitā bhavantītyasminnarthe śraddhādikaṃ caryātirekaḥ / iti parārthādhimuktiradhimātramṛdvī //
body.translated_text: By 'Moreover' and so forth, ending with 'worship would be performed' — this is the twenty-fifth [section]. By worshipping the <s>Bhagavatī</s> (<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>), the <s>Tathāgatas</s> of the three times are worshipped — the faith and so on regarding this meaning constitute the special conduct.

body.text: punaraparamityādinā dvitīyaṃ paśyatiparyantena ṣaḍviṃśatitamī / traiyadhvikatathāgatānāṃ dharmatayā darśayitrī bhagavatyevetyasminnarthe śraddhādikaṃ caryātirekaḥ / dharmatā dharmakāyaḥ sa ca prajñāpāramitaiveti bhāvaḥ / aparisamāpte eva śakravākye bhagavānāha evametadityādi / ahamapyabhisaṃbuddha iti yāvat / āgamyeti prāpya hetuṃkṛtya / iyatāpi bhagavatyāḥ samyaksaṃbodhikāraṇatvamuktaṃ na tu dharmakāyatvam / tadupasūcanāya punaḥ śakra
body.translated_text: By 'Furthermore' and so forth, ending with the second 'sees' — this is the twenty-sixth [section]. The <s>Bhagavatī</s> alone is the revealer of the <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature) of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> of the three times — the faith and so on regarding this meaning constitute the special conduct.

body.text: āha / mahāpāramitetyādi / samyakprajānātīti niṣprapañcena jñānena vettītyarthaḥ / saṃpaśyatīti sarvākāraṃ paśyatītyarthaḥ / sphuṭīkarttu bhagavānāha / evametadityādi / iti parārthādhimuktiradhimātramadhyā //
body.translated_text: He says: '<s>Mahāpāramitā</s>' and so forth. '<s>Samyak prajānāti</s>' (rightly discerns) means 'knows through knowledge free from conceptual elaboration' — this is the meaning. '<s>Saṃpaśyati</s>' (fully sees) means 'sees in all aspects' — this is the meaning. To make it explicit, the <s>Bhagavān</s> says

body.text: atha khalu śakra ityādinā āparivartasamāpteḥ saptaviṃśatitamī / sarva mahāyānaṃ pāramitābhiḥ saṃgṛhītam / tāsu bhagavatī pradhānaṃ pūrvaṅgamatvāt saṃgrāhakatvāccetyasminnarthe śraddhādikaṃ caryātirekaḥ / upāyakauśalyena parigṛhītānāmityuddeśaḥ / prajñāpāramitayā sarvākārajñatāyāṃ pariṇāmitānāmiti nirdeśaḥ / tatra prakṛtipāramitānāṃ dṛṣṭāntā nānāpuṣpādikā vṛkṣāḥ / ekarasā tu chāyā teṣāmupāyakauśalyaparigṛhītānāṃ dṛṣṭāntaḥ / iti parārthādhimuktiradhimātrādhimātrā //
body.translated_text: From 'Then indeed, <s>Śakra</s>' and so forth through the completion of the chapter — this is the twenty-seventh [section]. The entire <s>Mahāyāna</s> is encompassed by the <s>pāramitās</s>. Among those, the <s>Bhagavatī</s> (<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>) is principal, because it leads the way and because it encompasses [them all].

body.text: prakṛtatvātprajñāpāramitāyāḥ ye guṇāsteṣāṃ parikīrtanaḥ parivartastathoktaḥ /
body.translated_text: Because <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is the principal topic, the chapter is accordingly called 'the proclamation of its virtues.'

body.text: āryāṣṭasāhastrikāyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ sāratamānāmni pañjikāyāṃ ratnākāraśāntiviracitāyāṃ caturthaḥ parivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: In the commentary named <s>Sāratamā</s> on the noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s>, composed by <s>Ratnākaraśānti</s> — [this is] the fourth chapter.

body.text: 5. puṇyaparyāyaparivarto nāma pañcamaḥ /
body.translated_text: Chapter 5: The chapter called '<s>Puṇyaparyāya</s>' (Discourse on Merit) — the fifth.

body.text: uktaṃ 'kāritramadhimuktiśca' / 'stutistobhitaśaṃsitāḥ' vaktavyāḥ 'stutaṃ' sutiḥ / 'stobhitaṃ' stotraḥ / subdhātorbhāve ktaḥ / śaṃsanaṃ śaṃsaḥ / so 'syāstīti śaṃsī / tabhdāvaḥ 'śaṃsitā' praśaṃsetyarthaḥ / ataḥ śāstram-
body.translated_text: It has been stated: 'Accomplishment and aspiration.' 'Praise, laudation, and commendation' are to be explained. '<s>Stuta</s>' (praised) is praise. '<s>Stobhita</s>' (lauded) is laudation — the <s>kta</s> suffix after the root '<s>stubh</s>' [in the sense of] being. '<s>Śaṃsana</s>' (commending) is <s>śaṃsa</s>; that is

children.text: stutiḥ stobhaḥ praśaṃsā ca prajñāpāramitāṃ prati /
children.translated_text: 'Praise, laudation, and commendation regarding the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> —
through three sets of nine, the degrees of aspiration are [enumerated].' // 2-20 //

body.text: prajñāpāramitāyā yo 'dhimokṣaḥ pūrvamuktaḥ svārthobhayārthaparārthabhedena trayodhimuktinavakā ityarthaḥ / tasya guṇobhdāvanaṃ 'mātrāṇāṃ' prabhedānāṃ 'tribhirnavakaiḥ' yathākramam / 'stutiḥ stobhaḥ praśaṃsā ca' 'iṣyata' ityekavacanaṃ stutyādibhiḥ pratyekamabhisambandhāt / tatra guṇobhdāvanasya mṛdumadhyādhimātrabhedāḥ
