body.translated_text: The aspiration toward <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> previously stated — by the division into self-benefit, mutual benefit, and others' benefit, there are three groups of nine aspirations — this is the meaning. The exaltation of their virtues: 'of the degrees' means 'of the subdivisions'

body.text: stutistobhapraśaṃsāḥ / tāsāmapi mṛdumṛdvādayo 'dhimātrādhimātraparyantāḥ prabhedāstrayo navakā ityarthaḥ / tāsāṃ dvau hetū bodhisattvasya parārthakaraṇaśaktiḥ parārthapradhānatā ca /
body.translated_text: — praise, laudation, and commendation. Of these too, from soft-soft to supreme-supreme, the subdivisions are three groups of nine — this is the meaning. Their two causes are the <s>bodhisattva's</s> capacity for benefiting others

body.text: tatrādau punaraparamityataḥ prāk prathamā / asyāṃ parārthakaraṇaśaktistriṣu vastuṣvadhimokṣo dṛḍhataraḥ / kartavyopadeśe bhagavatīguṇe svayaṃ ca tasyāḥ kartavyatayādau śakra āha / ya ityādinā adhimuñcedityetadantena / yo bhagavan kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vādhimuñcediti sambandhaḥ / kimadhimuñcedityāha / imāmityādi sarvam / imāṃ prajñāpāramitāmadhyāśayataḥ śṛṇuyādudgṛṇhīyāt / yāvannetryavaikalyeneti / kathamityāha / bodhāya bodhaye cittamutpādya / kīdṛśaḥ prasannacitto 'syāmeva / katham? adhimucya / imāmaviparītatvenātyantamavadhārya / tacca śraddhayeti darśayitumāha / abhiśraddadhadavakalpayan / imāmeva / hetau śatṛpratyayaḥ / asyāmeva śraddhayetyarthaḥ / āse(śe)rate kuśalā dharmā asminnityāśayaḥ / jalāśayavat / sa punaḥ śraddhācchandau / adhikaḥ prakaṣṭa āśayo adhyāśayaḥ / tena śṛṇuyād granthato 'rthataśca / udgṛṇhīyād āvartayet / dhārayediti hṛdaye sthāpayet / vācayet pāṭhayet / paryavāpnuyāditi sarvathā avagaccheta / iyatā svārtho uktaḥ /
body.translated_text: Therein, first — from 'Furthermore' through to before [the next section] — this is the first [sub-section]. In this, the aspiration regarding three things — the capacity for benefiting others — is most firm. Regarding the instruction of what is to be done, the virtues of the <s>Bhagavatī</s>, and the [practitioner] himself

body.text: pravartayediti pareṣu sañcārayet / ayamuddeśaḥ / paro nirdeśaḥ / deśayedgranthato bhāṣaṇāt / upadiśed arthataḥ / uddiśedityavavadet / iyato parārthaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Should propagate' means 'should cause others to engage.' This is the outline. The rest is the detailed exposition. 'Should teach' — by [reciting] the text. 'Should instruct' — regarding the meaning. 'Should point out' — should explain. To this extent [is stated] the benefit of others.

body.text: svādhyāyediti sutarāmabhyaset / punaḥ punaḥ svārthakaraṇāt / parebhyaśca samprakāśayediti santataṃ prakāśayedgranthataḥ / vistareṇeti bahubhyaḥ prakāśanāt / vivṛṇuyāditi vistareṇeti vartate / manasānvavekṣeteti cittenānubudhya saṃyojya paśyet / sa(śa)mathotpādanāt / parimīmāṃsāmiti vicārāṇāṃ vipaśyanotpādanāt / iyatā caryoktā /
body.translated_text: 'Should study' means 'should practice even more.' Because of the repeated self-benefit. 'And should illuminate for others' means 'should continuously make known the text.' 'In detail' means 'should illuminate for many.'

body.text: asyā abhāve pakṣāntaramāha / pustaketyādinā / ata eva antaśaḥśabdaḥ / pustakagatāmiti / imāmeva dhārayediti / avinaśvarī kuryāt / sthāpayediti svagṛhādau / tisṛbhirāśaṃsābhiḥ / santa āryāḥ / teṣāṃ dharmamārga iti saddharmaḥ / tasya cirasthitiḥ / taddhetoḥ tadartham / iyaṃ hi sādhāraṇaḥ / saddharma iti prathameyamāśaṃsā sarvāryānadhikṛtya / buddhāśca lokaguravasteṣāṃ ca kṛtajñairasmābhirbhavitavyam / teṣāmiyaṃ netrī bodheḥ prāpikā prajñā / taistrikalpāsaṃkhyeyā pariśrameṇotpādya samyaganāgatajanatārthāya svavaṃśe 'vasthāpitā /
body.translated_text: In the absence of this [practice], an alternative is stated: 'A book' and so forth. Hence the word '<s>antaśaḥ</s>' (at least). 'In the form of a book' — 'should retain this very one' means should make it imperishable. 'Should establish' means in one's own home

body.text: yāvadasmānupagatā / tato mā buddhanetrī samucchedobhūd ityapīmāṃ sthāpayet / iti dvitīyeyamāśaṃsā buddhānadhikṛtya / bodhisattvānāṃ cānugrahopasaṃhāraḥ karaṇīyaḥ / sa ca kṛto bhaviṣyati / anayā sthāyitayā netryavaikalyena / ityapīmāṃ sthāpayediti tṛtīyeyamāśaṃsā bodhisattvānadhikṛtya / iti śabdaḥ pūrvatrāpi sambadhyate mā bhūditi / iyatā dvividhaḥ kartavyopadeśa uktaḥ /
body.translated_text: — 'as long as it has come to us.' Therefore, 'lest the guide to <s>Buddhahood</s> be cut off' — for this reason too one should establish it. Thus this is the second aspiration, with reference to the <s>Buddhas</s>. And for the welfare of <s>bodhisattvas</s>

body.text: imaṃ nirdeśamiti kartavyopadeśam / evaṃ mahārthiketyādi / mahān arthakāryamasyā iti mahārthikā / ayamuddeśaḥ / paro nirdeśaḥ / mahānuśaṃsā yathoktaraiṇu(nu)śaṃsaḥ / mahāphalā strotaāpannatvena, sakṛdāgāmitvena, anāgāmitvena, arhattvena, pratyekabodhyā, samyaksambodhyā ca / mahāvipākā sarvābhiścaryāvibhūtibhiḥ / bahumahāguṇasamanvāgatetyupasaṃhāraḥ / iyatā bhagavatīguṇa uktaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'This exposition' means the instruction of what is to be done. 'Of such great purpose' and so forth: 'that which has a great purpose or goal is <s>mahārthikā</s> (of great purpose).' This is the outline. The rest is the detailed exposition. 'Of great benefit' — by the benefits stated above

body.text: aparityajanīyā parigrahādanutsargācca / rakṣitavyā agnimūṣikādibhyaḥ / gopāyitavyā caurādibhyaḥ / yasmāt paramadurlabhā / iyatā svayaṃ kartavyamuktam /
body.translated_text: Not to be abandoned — because of acceptance and because of non-relinquishment. To be guarded — from fire, mice, and the like. To be protected — from thieves and the like. Because it is supremely rare. To this extent, what is to be done by oneself has been stated.

body.text: itīti / etadvastutrayamadhimuñcet / evamevetyavadhārayet / asatyāṃ ca pravṛttau nādhimokṣo dṛḍhaḥ syāt / tata iyatā parārthakaraṇaśaktiruktā / tasyāṃ satyāṃ yaḥ parārtha svalpamapi na karoti svalpaṃ vā karoti so 'lpapuṇyaḥ / itarastasmāt bahutarapuṇyaḥ / tasyaitā stutistotrapraśaṃsāḥ / ataḥ svayameva cetyādinā dvitīyaprasavatiparyantena stutiḥ prathamā //
body.translated_text: 'Thus' — one should have aspiration toward these three things. 'Just so' — one should be certain. And without [proper] engagement, the aspiration would not be firm. Therefore, to this extent the capacity for benefiting others has been stated. In that

body.text: svayameva ceti cakāro ya ityasyānukarṣaṇārthaḥ / na tu parāṃ(raiḥ) pūjāḥ(jāṃ) kārayatītyevakārārthaḥ / saṃpūjyeti sarvapūjāḥ kṛtvā / arthanamarthaḥ / pūjāyāmicchā tadyogādarthikāya / atiśayena tadyogācchandikāya / yācamānāyeti pūjayituṃ bhagavatīṃ prārthayamānāya / dadyādityabhyupagacchet / upanāmayet sannipātayet / niryātayet grāhayet / parityajed avipratisārāt / antaśaḥ iti yāvadityarthaḥ / pustakagatāmapi kṛtveti svayaṃ likhitvā tena vā likhitvā tanmūlyena vā svamūlyena vā lekhayitvā parityāgo dānaṃ tasmai buddhiricchā asyeti tadbuddhiḥ / saṃprakāśayediti guṇataḥ svarūpataśca / dadyāt pūjanāya / saṃvibhajediti spharatāmadhikānāṃ vā dānāt / vistāro vaipulyam / tena caratīti vaistārikī / pratyātmamityātmanaiva / śeṣaṃ subodham / iti mṛdumṛdvī stutiḥ /
body.translated_text: 'By oneself alone' — the particle 'ca' serves to carry forward the word 'ya' (who). It does not mean that he causes others to perform worship — that is the meaning of the particle 'eva.' '<s>Saṃpūjya</s>' (having fully worshipped) means having performed all forms of worship. '<s>Arthana</s>' means request. Desire for worship — by connection with that, 'to one who desires' (<s>arthikāya</s>). By its excess, 'to one who is eager' (<s>chandikāya</s>). 'To one who is requesting' means to one who is beseeching the <s>Bhagavatī</s> (Prajñāpāramitā) in order to worship her. 'Should give' means should agree to. 'Should present' means should bring together. 'Should hand over' means should cause to receive. 'Should relinquish' — without regret. 'At the very least' means 'up to that extent.' 'Even making it into a book' means having written it oneself, or having had it written by him, or having had it written at his cost or at one's own cost — relinquishment is the gift; the intention directed toward that person, the wish, is '<s>tadbuddhi</s>' (that intention). 'Should illuminate' means both in terms of qualities and in terms of essential nature. 'Should give' for the purpose of worship. 'Should distribute' — from the gift to those who are more extensive or superior. 'Extension' is vastness (<s>vaipulya</s>). One who practices by means of that is '<s>vaistārikī</s>' (one who extends). '<s>Pratyātmam</s>' means by oneself alone. The rest is easily understood. Thus this is the mildest of the mild (<s>mṛdumṛdvī</s>) eulogy.

body.text: punaraparādiḥ prāk punaraparāt dvitīyā / tat iti prathamastutāt / iti mṛdumadhyā stutiḥ //
body.translated_text: The passage beginning with '<s>punar apara</s>' (furthermore) up to the second '<s>punar apara</s>' is the second [eulogy]. '<s>Tat</s>' (that) refers to what was praised in the first eulogy. Thus this is the mild-middle (<s>mṛdumadhyā</s>) eulogy.

body.text: punaraparādi tiṣṭhantuśabdāt prāk tṛtīyā / samādāpayediti samyak grāhayet / pratiṣṭhāyet anatikramāt / abhiśraddadhaditi bhagavatīguṇān / anyathā na samyak dātā syāt / abhiśraddadhata iti / anyathā na sa dānapātraṃ syāt / evamuttareṣvapi veditavyam / kilāsitā kusīdaḥ / akilāsitā vīryam / tayā sampādayed yathoktaṃ kāryam / udyukto 'bhiyuktaḥ sannamuṃ bodhisattvaṃ bhagavatīṃ grāhayet / bodhisādhanatvena pratipādayedvācā / tathaiva sandarśayed yuktibhiḥ / tataḥ samādāpayed vācanārcanādiṣu pravṛtteḥ / pravṛttaṃ samuttejayed utsāhayet / vīryakausīdyayorguṇadoṣākhyānāt / ārabdhavīrya stutibhiḥ saṃpraharṣayet / viparyasto lokastato nedaṃ śakyamiti cedāha / vācetyādi / trividho lokaḥ śrāddho vimukha udāsīnaśca / tatra śrāddhaṃ vācaiva neṣyati / sa hi saṃbhāvitasya vācaiva gacchati / vimukhaṃ vineśyati / kudṛṣṭīnāṃ yuktibhirbādhanāt udāsīnamanuneṣyati / anurañjayiṣyati bhagavatyā tadguṇākhyānāt / evaṃ pātrīkṛto ya arthamasyā asmai saṃprakāśayiṣyati / evaṃ ceti prakāśite vārthe 'syacittaṃ śodhayiṣyati / kuddaṣṭīnāṃ bādhanāt / tathāpi saṃśayinaṃ nirvicikitsaṃ kariṣyati yuktyantaraiḥ / śikṣasvatisṛbhiḥ śikṣābhiḥ / atra hītyādinā ta evāha / śikṣamāṇaḥ cintayā / caraṇa(na) samarthena (śamathena) vyāyacchamāno vipaśyamānayā / sattvadhātuḥ sattvarāśiḥ / ātyantikatvād anuttare / upadhayaḥ skandhāḥ sāsravāḥ sāsravānāsravā vā / teṣāṃ saṃkṣayaḥ samastakṣayaḥ / tannimittam / abhivineśyasi sarvāvaraṇakṣayāt / bhūtakoṭiprabhāvanatā tanmātraśeṣatā / parityāgabuddhyeti sarvākārayā tyāgabuddhayā / tata iti dvītīyāyāṃ stutāt daśakuśalapratiṣṭhāpakācca / iti mṛddhadhimātrā stutiḥ //
body.translated_text: The passage beginning with '<s>punar apara</s>' up to the word '<s>tiṣṭhantu</s>' (let them stand) is the third. 'Should cause to undertake' (<s>samādāpayet</s>) means should cause to properly receive. 'Should establish' — because of non-transgression. 'Having faith' (<s>abhiśraddadhat</s>) — in the qualities of the <s>Bhagavatī</s>; otherwise one would not be a proper giver. 'Of one having faith' — otherwise he would not be a worthy recipient of the gift. The same should be understood in the subsequent cases as well. '<s>Kilāsitā</s>' means laziness. '<s>Akilāsitā</s>' means vigor (<s>vīrya</s>). By means of that, one should accomplish the task as stated. 'Diligent' means one who is engaged — such a person should cause another <s>bodhisattva</s> to take up the <s>Bhagavatī</s>. 'Should instruct' means should teach through speech that it is a means to awakening. Similarly, 'should show' means through reasoning. Then 'should cause to undertake' — through engaging in recitation, worship, and so forth. 'Should encourage' one who has engaged — should inspire zeal — through explaining the virtues and faults of vigor and laziness. 'Should gladden' one who has aroused vigor — through praises. If one objects that the world is confused and therefore this is impossible, he says 'by speech' and so forth. The world is of three kinds: faithful, averse, and indifferent. Among these, the faithful one will be led by speech alone, for such a person goes by the word of one who is esteemed. The averse one will be disciplined — because those of wrong views are refuted by reasoning. The indifferent one will be won over — will be delighted — through describing the qualities of the <s>Bhagavatī</s>. One thus made into a worthy vessel — to him one will illuminate the meaning of this. And thus, when the meaning has been illuminated, one will purify his mind — through refuting wrong views. Even so, one who has doubts will be freed from uncertainty through additional reasoning. 'You should train' — with the three trainings. With 'for here' and so forth, he states those very [trainings]. 'Training' through reflection. 'Exerting' through <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding). 'Examining' through <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight). '<s>Sattvadhātu</s>' means the mass of sentient beings. 'Unsurpassed' — because of its ultimacy. '<s>Upadhis</s>' (substrata) are the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) — either defiled, or both defiled and undefiled. Their 'complete destruction' means the destruction of all. That is the cause. 'Will discipline' — through the destruction of all obscurations. 'Approaching the ultimate reality' (<s>bhūtakoṭiprabhāvanatā</s>) means having only that as remainder. 'With the intention of relinquishment' — with the intention of abandoning in every way. 'Therefore' refers to what was praised in the second eulogy, and also from establishing [beings] in the ten wholesome actions. Thus this is the mild-intense (<s>mṛdvadhimātrā</s>) eulogy.

body.text: ita ūrdhva pañcānāṃ stutīnāṃ tiṣṭhantvādiḥ pratiṣṭhāpayedantaḥ pūrvo bhāgaḥ / tata ūrdhva tatkiṃ manyasa ityādi punaparāt prāk paścimo bhāgaḥ / āsu ca sūtrokte puṇyātirekaiḥ śraddhādikaṃ sāmarthyagamyaśca mātrātirekaścaryātirekaḥ / etena paryāyeṇeti prakāreṇa vastutrayādhimokṣe sthitvetyarthaḥ / iti yathākramaṃ madhyamṛddhī madhyamadhyā madhyādhimātrā adhimātramṛdvī adhimātramadhyā ca stutiḥ //
body.translated_text: From here onward, for the five eulogies, the earlier portion [extends] from '<s>tiṣṭhantu</s>' and so forth to '<s>pratiṣṭhāpayet</s>' (should establish). From there onward, the later portion [extends] from '<s>tat kiṃ manyase</s>' (what do you think?) to before '<s>punar apara</s>.' In these [eulogies], through the surpassing merits stated in the <s>sūtra</s>, faith and so forth, and the surpassing of degree that is understood through capability, constitute the surpassing of practice. 'By this method' (<s>etena paryāyeṇa</s>) means by this manner — having been established in the conviction regarding the three objects. Thus, in order, these are the middle-mild, middle-middle, middle-intense, intense-mild, and intense-middle eulogies.

body.text: punaraparādi punaraparātprāk pañca tiṣṭhantukā navamī / ekasyā eva navamyāḥ krameṇābhidhānāt / tathāpyaṣṭamīto mahadantaramiti cet / nāyaṃ doṣaḥ / ekalokadhātukāto gaṃgāvālukopamāt lokadhātuvat / sūtroktapuṇyātirekaiḥ śraddhādikaṃ caryātirekaḥ / ūnapāṭhāḥ pūrvāparaiḥ pūraṇiyāḥ /
body.translated_text: The passage beginning with '<s>punar apara</s>' up to before the [next] '<s>punar apara</s>' — five [eulogies] beginning with '<s>tiṣṭhantu</s>' — constitutes the ninth. Because the single ninth [eulogy] is expounded progressively. If one objects that there is a great gap from the eighth, this is no fault — just as from a single world-system to world-systems equal in number to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>. Through the surpassing merits stated in the <s>sūtra</s>, faith and so forth constitute the surpassing of practice. Incomplete readings should be filled in from the preceding and following [passages].

body.text: caturṣu dhyāneṣviti / atra sūtram- 'viviktaṃ kāmairviviktaṃ pāpakaraikuśalairdharmaiḥ savitarkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ prītisukhaṃ prathamaṃ dhyānamupasampadya viharati / sa vitarkavicāraṇāṃ vyupaśamādadhyātmaṃ saṃprasādāccetasa ekotībhāvādavitarkamavicāraṃ samādhijaṃ prītisukhaṃ dvitīyaṃ dhyānamupasampadya viharati / sa prīte virāgādupekṣako viharati smṛtimān saṃprajānan sukhaṃ ca kāyena pratisaṃvedayate / yattadāryā ācakṣate upekṣakaḥ smṛtimān sukhavihārīti niṣprītikaṃ tṛtīyaṃ dhyānamupasampadya viharati / sa sukhasya ca prahāṇāt duḥkhasya ca pūrvameva prahāṇāt saumanasyadaurmanasyayorastaṅgamādaduḥkhāsukhamupekṣāsmṛtipariśuddhaṃ caturthaṃ dhyānamupasampadya viharati" iti //
body.translated_text: 'In the four <s>dhyānas</s> (meditative absorptions)' — here the <s>sūtra</s> states: 'Secluded from sensual desires, secluded from unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>, accompanied by <s>vitarka</s> (applied thought) and <s>vicāra</s> (sustained thought), born of seclusion, endowed with <s>prīti</s> (rapture) and <s>sukha</s> (happiness), one enters and abides in the first <s>dhyāna</s>. Through the subsiding of <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s>, with inner clarity, with unification of mind, without <s>vitarka</s>, without <s>vicāra</s>, born of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), endowed with <s>prīti</s> and <s>sukha</s>, one enters and abides in the second <s>dhyāna</s>. Through dispassion toward <s>prīti</s>, one abides with equanimity, mindful and clearly comprehending, experiencing <s>sukha</s> with the body — that which the noble ones declare: "One who is equanimous, mindful, and abides in happiness" — one enters and abides in the third <s>dhyāna</s>, which is without <s>prīti</s>. Through the abandoning of <s>sukha</s> and <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering), through the prior disappearance of mental pleasure and displeasure, one enters and abides in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, which is neither painful nor pleasant, purified by equanimity and mindfulness.'

body.text: viviktaṃ kāmairiti / kleśakāmasyāsaṃprayogāt / vastukāmānāmanālambanāt / viviktaṃ pāpakairakuśalairdhamairiti / kleśakāmahetukaiḥ kāmavāṅmanoduścaritaiḥ / savitarka savicāramiti / kāmapratipakṣābhyāṃ vitakavicārābhyāṃ saṃprayogāt / vivekajamiti / kāmavivekājjātam / prītisukhamiti / īpsitārthasiddhitaḥ kāyacittapraśrabdhitaśca prītisukhasahagatam / prathamaṃ dhyānamupasaṃpadyeti samāpadya / viharatīti pratyanubhavati / sa iti / sa eva yogī / vitarkavicāreṣu cittakṣobhakaratvadoṣadarśanāttebhyaścittaṃ vyāvartya samādadhānaḥ / vitarkavicārāṇāṃ vyupaśamāditi samādhibalena / cetasa ekotībhāvāditi vitarkavicārāṇāṃ nirantaramapravṛtteḥ / avitarkamavicāramiti teṣāṃ sarveṇa sarva prahāṇāt / prītervirāgāditi / audārikāttasyāḥ / upekṣaka iti / vitarkavicāraprītināmupekṣaṇāt / smṛtimān saṃprajānanniti / prīteranakavakāśadānāya prajñābahulīkārāt / sukhamiti / veditasukhaṃ praśrabdhisukhaṃ ca / kāyeneti / rūpakāyena manaḥkāyena ca / āryā iti / śrāvakā buddhāśca / yāvatsukhavihārīti / eṣa evāsau dhyāyīti śeṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Secluded from sensual desires' — because of non-association with <s>kleśakāma</s> (afflictive desire), and because material objects of desire are not taken as objects [of the mind]. 'Secluded from unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>' — from the three misdeeds of body, speech, and mind that are caused by afflictive desire. 'Accompanied by <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s>' — because of association with <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s>, which are antidotes to sensual desire. 'Born of seclusion' means born from the seclusion from sensual desires. 'Endowed with <s>prīti</s> and <s>sukha</s>' — accompanied by <s>prīti</s> and <s>sukha</s> arising from the attainment of the desired goal and from the tranquility of body and mind. 'Enters the first <s>dhyāna</s>' means having attained it. 'Abides' means directly experiences it. 'He' means that very <s>yogī</s>. Having seen the fault that <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s> cause mental disturbance, and having turned the mind away from them, one concentrates. 'Through the subsiding of <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s>' — through the power of <s>samādhi</s>. 'With unification of mind' — because of the uninterrupted non-arising of <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s>. 'Without <s>vitarka</s>, without <s>vicāra</s>' — because of their complete and total abandonment. 'Through dispassion toward <s>prīti</s>' — toward its coarser [aspect]. 'Equanimous' — because of equanimity toward <s>vitarka</s>, <s>vicāra</s>, and <s>prīti</s>. 'Mindful and clearly comprehending' — because of cultivating <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) abundantly, in order to give no opportunity for <s>prīti</s> [to arise again]. '<s>Sukha</s>' means both felt happiness and the happiness of tranquility. 'With the body' means with the physical body and the mental body. 'The noble ones' means <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers) and <s>Buddhas</s>. Up to 'abides in happiness' — the remainder is: 'this is that very meditator.'

body.text: tatra sukhasya prahāṇaṃ caturthena dhyānena / duḥkhasya prathamena / ata evāha / pūrvameveti / saumanasyasya tṛtīyena / daurmanasyasya dvitīyena / pūrvamevetyanuvṛtteḥ / upekṣaivātra vedanā / tata āha / aduḥkhāsukhamiti / tayorihātyantaṃ viśuddhilābhāt //
body.translated_text: In that context, the abandoning of <s>sukha</s> (happiness) is by means of the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>. The abandoning of <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering) is by means of the first. Therefore he says 'previously.' The abandoning of mental pleasure (<s>saumanasya</s>) is by means of the third. The abandoning of mental displeasure (<s>daurmanasya</s>) is by means of the second. Because 'previously' carries over [to these as well]. Equanimity here is the [neutral] feeling (<s>vedanā</s>). Therefore he says 'neither painful nor pleasant.' Because in this [fourth <s>dhyāna</s>], there is the attainment of the ultimate purity of both [equanimity and mindfulness].

body.text: tatra prathamasya dhyānasya pañcāṅgāni / vitarkavicārau pratipakṣāṅgaḥ(ṅgam) / prītisukhe anuśaṃsāṅgaḥ(ṅgam) / citaikāgratā tadubhayasanniśrayāṅgaḥ(ṅgam) // dvitīyasya catvāryaṅgāni / adhyātmaṃ saṃprasādaḥ pratipakṣāṅgam / śeṣe aṅgepūrvavat // tṛtīyasya pañcāṅgāni / upekṣāsmṛtiḥ saṃprajanyaṃ ca pratipakṣāṅgam /
body.translated_text: In that regard, the first <s>dhyāna</s> has five limbs. <s>Vitarka</s> (applied thought) and <s>vicāra</s> (sustained thought) are the antidote limb. <s>Prīti</s> (rapture) and <s>sukha</s> (happiness) are the benefit limb. One-pointedness of mind (<s>cittaikāgratā</s>) is the support limb for both. The second [<s>dhyāna</s>] has four limbs. Inner clarity (<s>adhyātmaṃ saṃprasādaḥ</s>) is the antidote limb. The remaining limbs are as before. The third [<s>dhyāna</s>] has five limbs. Equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>), mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>), and clear comprehension (<s>saṃprajanya</s>) are the antidote limb.

body.text: sakhamanuśaṃsāṅgam / niśrayāṅgaḥ(ṅgaṃ) pūrvavat // caturthasya catvāryaṅgāni / upekṣāpariśuddhiḥ pratipakṣāṅgaḥ(ṅgam) / aduḥkhāsukhā vedanā anuśaṃsāṅgaḥ(ṅgam) / niśrayāṅgaḥ(ṅgaṃ) pūrvavat //
body.translated_text: <s>Sukha</s> (happiness) is the benefit limb. The support limb is as before. The fourth [<s>dhyāna</s>] has four limbs. Purification of equanimity (<s>upekṣāpariśuddhi</s>) is the antidote limb. The feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant (<s>aduḥkhāsukhā vedanā</s>) is the benefit limb. The support limb is as before.

body.text: eteṣu caturṣu dhyāneṣu pratiṣṭhāpayet / śeṣaṃ pūrvavat / ityadhimātrādhimātrā stutiḥ //
body.translated_text: One should establish [beings] in these four <s>dhyānas</s>. The rest is as before. Thus this is the most intense of the intense (<s>adhimātrādhimātrā</s>) eulogy.

body.text: punaraparādiḥ prabhavanatāntaḥ prathamaḥ stobhaḥ / ūnapūraṇaṃ pūrvavat / caturṣu dhyāneṣu caturṣvapramāṇeṣu caturṣvārūpyasamāpattiṣu pañcasvabhijñāsu yāvatsamastāsu dhyānāpramāṇārūpyasamāpatyabhijñāsu pratiṣṭhāpayediti /
body.translated_text: The passage beginning with '<s>punar apara</s>' up to '<s>prabhāvanatā</s>' (approaching) is the first exhortation (<s>stobha</s>). The filling in of incomplete [readings] is as before. One should establish [beings] in the four <s>dhyānas</s>, the four <s>apramāṇas</s> (immeasurables), the four formless attainments (<s>ārūpyasamāpattis</s>), and the five <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges) — up to: in all the <s>dhyānas</s>, <s>apramāṇas</s>, formless attainments, and <s>abhijñās</s> one should establish [beings].

body.text: uktāni dhyānāni / maitryādayaḥ kāmāvacarāḥ sattvālambanāścatvāro brahmavihārāḥ / apramāṇasattvālambanāścatvāryapramāṇāni / maitrī karūṇā muditā upekṣā ca / aho vata sarvasattvāḥ sukhena yujyeran duḥkhena viyujyeran sukhena mā viyujyeran saṃkleśānmuñcerannityebhirākāraiḥ sukhasaṃyogāśayo duḥkhaviyogāśayaḥ sukhāviyogāśayo 'saṃkleśāśayaśca / adhimukticaryābhūmau catastropi sattvālambanāḥ / pramuditāsu saptasu tathatālambanāḥ / acalādiṣvanālambanāḥ /
body.translated_text: The <s>dhyānas</s> have been stated. The four <s>brahmavihāras</s> (divine abidings), beginning with <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), belong to the desire realm (<s>kāmāvacara</s>) and have sentient beings as their object. The four <s>apramāṇas</s> (immeasurables) have immeasurable sentient beings as their object: <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), <s>muditā</s> (sympathetic joy), and <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity). 'Oh, may all sentient beings be united with happiness, separated from suffering, never parted from happiness, and released from defilements!' — through these aspects, the intention of union with happiness, the intention of separation from suffering, the intention of non-separation from happiness, and the intention of freedom from defilement [are cultivated]. On the stage of the practice of conviction (<s>adhimukticaryābhūmi</s>), all four have sentient beings as their object. On the [first] seven [stages] beginning with <s>Pramuditā</s> (Joyful), they have <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) as their object. On [the stages] beginning with <s>Acalā</s> (Immovable) and above, they are without object.

body.text: apramāṇeṣu sūtram- "maitrīsahagatena cittena vipulena mahadgatenādvayenāpramāṇenāvaireṇāsampannenānāvaraṇenāvyābādhena sarvatrānugatena subhāvitena dharmadhātuparame loke ākāśadhātuparyavasāne sarvāvantaṃ lokamekaṃ diśaṃ spharitvopasaṃpadya viharati / yāvaddaśadiśaḥ spharitvopasaṃpadya viharati / evaṃ karuṇāsahagatena / evaṃ muditāsahagatena / evamupekṣasahagatena" iti //
body.translated_text: Regarding the <s>apramāṇas</s>, the <s>sūtra</s> states: 'With a mind accompanied by <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), vast, great, non-dual, immeasurable, without enmity, without affliction, without obstruction, without harm, pervading everywhere, well-cultivated, supreme in the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality), in the world extending to the limit of the <s>ākāśadhātu</s> (realm of space), having pervaded one direction of the entire world, one enters and abides. Up to: having pervaded the ten directions, one enters and abides. Likewise with a mind accompanied by <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion). Likewise with a mind accompanied by <s>muditā</s> (sympathetic joy). Likewise with a mind accompanied by <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity).'

body.text: tatra maitrīsahagatena citteneti guṇino nirdeśaḥ / śeṣeṇa guṇānām / vipulenetyāśayato mahattvam / mahadgateneti vardhanataḥ / apramāṇenetyālambanataḥ / advayeneti ekātmakena nirvikalpatvāt / avaireṇeti vipakṣaprahāṇāt / tatra maitryādīnāṃ vipakṣo yathākramaṃ / vyāpādo vihiṃsā aratiḥ, anunayapratighau ca / asaṃpanneneti styānamiddhopaśamāt / anāvaraṇenetyauddhatyakaukṛtyopaśamāt / avyābādhenetyebhireva tribhiścetaso akāluṣyāt / sarvatrānugateneti mitrodāsīnaśatruṣu triṣvapi pravṛttatvāt / subhāviteneti triṣvapi samapravṛttatvāt / uktena prakāreṇa spharitveti vyāpya / lokamiti sattvalokam / sarvāvantamiti devanāgayakṣādibhedaiḥ sarvairyuktam / ekaṃ diśamiti ekadiggatam / kvetyāha / loka iti bhājanaloke dharmadhātuparama iti / dharmadhātuvadanante
body.translated_text: There, 'with a mind accompanied by <s>maitrī</s>' is a description of the possessor of the qualities. The rest describes the qualities themselves. 'Vast' refers to greatness in terms of intention. 'Great' refers to [greatness] in terms of expansion. 'Immeasurable' refers to [greatness] in terms of object. 'Non-dual' means of a single nature, because it is non-conceptual. 'Without enmity' — because of the abandonment of the opposing [factors]. In this regard, the opposing factors of <s>maitrī</s> and the others, in order, are: <s>vyāpāda</s> (malice), <s>vihiṃsā</s> (harmfulness), <s>arati</s> (discontent), and <s>anunaya</s> (attachment) together with <s>pratigha</s> (aversion). 'Without affliction' — because of the subsiding of <s>styāna</s> (torpor) and <s>middha</s> (drowsiness). 'Without obstruction' — because of the subsiding of <s>auddhatya</s> (restlessness) and <s>kaukṛtya</s> (regret). 'Without harm' — because the mind is untroubled by precisely these three. 'Pervading everywhere' — because it operates toward all three: friends, neutral persons, and enemies. 'Well-cultivated' — because it operates equally toward all three. 'Having pervaded' in the manner described means having permeated. 'The world' means the world of sentient beings. 'The entire' means endowed with all [kinds of beings] such as <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, and so forth. 'One direction' means situated in one direction. Where? He says 'in the world' — in the world as a vessel. 'Supreme in the <s>dharmadhātu</s>' means

body.text: ākāśadhātoriva paryavasānamasyeti tathokte / upasaṃpadya viharatīti cittaṃ samādhāya viharatyāryavihāreṇa / daśadiśa iti daśadiggatān / śeṣaṃ subodham //
body.translated_text: in the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, which is infinite like [the <s>dharmadhātu</s> itself] — 'whose extent is like the <s>ākāśadhātu</s> (realm of space)' is said in that sense. 'Enters and abides' means having concentrated the mind, one abides with the noble abiding (<s>āryavihāra</s>). 'The ten directions' means those situated in the ten directions. The rest is easily understood.

body.text: ārūpyasamāpattayaścatvāra ārūpyāḥ / teṣu sūtram "sarvaśo rūpasaṃjñānāṃ samatikramātpratighasaṃjñānāmastaṅgamāt nānātvasaṃjñānāmamanasikārāt anantamākāśamiti ākāśānantyāyatanaṃ upasampadya viharati / sa sarvaśa ākāśānantyāyatanasaṃjñāsamatikramādanantaṃ vijñānamiti vijñānānantyāyatanamupasaṃpadya viharati / sa sarvaśa vijñānānantyāyatanasaṃjñāsamtikramāt nāsti kiñcidityākiñcanyāyatanamupasaṃpadya viharati / sa sarvaśa ākiñcanyāyatanasaṃjñāsamatikramāt naivasaṃjñā nāsaṃjñāyatanamupasampadya viharati" iti //
body.translated_text: The <s>ārūpyasamāpattis</s> (formless attainments) are the four formless states. Regarding these, the <s>sūtra</s> states: "By completely transcending perceptions of form, by the disappearance of perceptions of resistance, by non-attention to perceptions of diversity, [thinking] 'Space is infinite,' one enters and abides in the <s>ākāśānantyāyatana</s> (sphere of infinite space). By completely transcending the perception of the <s>ākāśānantyāyatana</s>, [thinking] 'Consciousness is infinite,' one enters and abides in the <s>vijñānānantyāyatana</s> (sphere of infinite consciousness). By completely transcending the perception of the <s>vijñānānantyāyatana</s>, [thinking] 'There is nothing,' one enters and abides in the <s>ākiñcanyāyatana</s> (sphere of nothingness). By completely transcending the perception of the <s>ākiñcanyāyatana</s>, one enters and abides in the <s>naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana</s> (sphere of neither perception nor non-perception)."

body.text: rūpasaṃjñā nīlapītādisaṃjñāḥ / tāsu viraktasya sarvatrākāśasaṃjñā bhāvanāt / tāsāmatikramāt apratibhāsāt / pratighasaṃjñānāmiti bhittiprākārādyāvaraṇasaṃjñānām / nānātvasaṃjñānāmiti prāsādodyānagirisariccandrasūryādisaṃjñānām / anantamākāśamityevamākāśānantyāyatanamālamvanamasyeti tathoktam / kathamākāśānantyāyatanasamatikramaḥ? sa yena jñānenākāśānantyāyatanamadhimuktavāṃstadevānantamadhimucya sarvatrākāśasaṃjñāvyāvartanāt / vijñānānantyāyatanasamatikramāditi / sa tasmāduccalito na kiñcidālambanaṃ paśyati nārthaṃ na vijñānam / so 'kiñcanatāmevālambanīkṛtya samāpadyate / ākiñcanyāyatanasamatikramāditi / sa ākiñcanyasaṃjñāyāmapi viraktastāmapi vyāvartayati / kiñcanasaṃjñā tu prāgeva nivṛttā / tato naiva saṃjñā / sūkṣmā tu saṃjñā pravartata eva tato nāsaṃjñā / naiva saṃjñā nāsaṃjñā yasminnāyatane samādhāne tattathoktam /
body.translated_text: <s>Rūpasaṃjñā</s> (perceptions of form) are perceptions of blue, yellow, and so on. For one who has become dispassionate toward these, it is because of cultivating the perception of space everywhere. 'By transcending them' means by their non-appearance. 'Of perceptions of resistance' means of perceptions of obstruction such as walls, ramparts, and the like. 'Of perceptions of diversity' means of perceptions of palaces, gardens, mountains, rivers, the moon, the sun, and so forth. 'Space is infinite' — thus it is said that the <s>ākāśānantyāyatana</s> (sphere of infinite space) is its object. How is the transcendence of the <s>ākāśānantyāyatana</s> accomplished? By that very cognition through which one was resolved upon the <s>ākāśānantyāyatana</s>, one resolves upon that as infinite, thereby turning away from the perception of space everywhere. 'By transcendence of the <s>vijñānānantyāyatana</s>' — having risen from that, one sees no object whatsoever, neither an external referent nor consciousness. One attains by making nothingness itself the object. 'By transcendence of the <s>ākiñcanyāyatana</s>' — having become dispassionate even toward the perception of nothingness, one turns away from even that. The perception of 'something' has already ceased before this. Therefore it is not perception. But a subtle perception does indeed continue, therefore it is not non-perception. That meditative state in which there is neither perception nor non-perception — it is accordingly so called.

body.text: pañcābhijñāḥ / ṛddhividhijñānam / divyaśrotram / paracittajñānam / pūrvenivāsānusmṛtijñānam / divyacakṣuśceti / atra sūtram- "so 'nekavidhamṛddhividhaṃ pratyanubhavati / pṛthivīmapi kampayati / eko bhūtvā bahudhā bhavati / bahudhāpi bhūtvā eko bhavati / āvirbhātraṃ tirobhāvamapi pratyanubhavati / tiraḥ kuḍyaṃ tiraḥ prākāraṃ tiraḥparvatamapyasakto gacchati / ākāśamapi krāmati / pṛthivyāmapi unmajjananimajjanaṃ karoti / udakepi pṛthivyāmiva gacchati / dhūmāyatyapi prajvalatyapi" iti vistāraḥ // "sa divyena śrotradhātunā atikrāntamānuṣyakena śabdān śṛṇoti divyān mānuṣakāṃśca / sa parasattvānāmapi parapudgalānāṃ cetasaiva cittaṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / evaṃ [sarāgaṃ] vigatarāgaṃ sadoṣaṃ vītadoṣaṃ samohaṃ vītamohaṃ cittamiti yathābhūtaṃ
body.translated_text: The five <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges) are: <s>ṛddhividhijñāna</s> (knowledge of magical powers), <s>divyaśrotra</s> (divine ear), <s>paracittajñāna</s> (knowledge of others' minds), <s>pūrvenivāsānusmṛtijñāna</s> (knowledge of recollecting former lives), and <s>divyacakṣus</s> (divine eye). Here the <s>sūtra</s> states: "One experiences manifold magical powers. One causes the earth to tremble. Having been one, one becomes many; having been many, one becomes one. One experiences appearing and disappearing. One passes unobstructed through walls, through ramparts, through mountains. One traverses through space. One dives in and out of the earth. One walks on water as if on earth. One emits smoke and blazes forth" — and so on in detail. "With the divine ear-element, surpassing the human, one hears sounds both divine and human. With the mind alone, one truly knows the minds of other beings and other persons. Thus one truly knows

body.text: prajānāti yāvadanuttaraṃ cittamiti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / sa ekāṃ jātimanu smarati / dve tiśro (sro) yāvajjātikoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇyapyanusmarati / ekaṃ divasaṃ dve trīṇi yāvatkalpakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇyapyanusmarati / amutrāha māsamevaṃ nāmā evaṃ gotra evaṃ jātirevamāhāra evaṃ cirasthitika evamāyuṣyaparyantaḥ / sohaṃ tataścyutaḥ sannamutropapanno yāvattataścyuta ihopapanna iti yāvat sākāraṃ soddeśaṃ sanimittamanekavidhaṃ pūrvenivāsamanusmarati // sa divyena cakṣuṣā viśuddhenātikrāntamānuṣyakena sattvān paśyati / cyavamānānupapannānapi suvarṇān durvarṇān hīnān praṇītān sugatau durgatau yathākarmopagān sattvān prajānāti / amī bhavantaḥ sattvāḥ kāyasucaritena vāksucaritena manaḥsucaritena samanvāgatā āryāṇāmanapavādakāḥ samyagdṛṣṭayaḥ / tena kāyavāṅmanaḥsucaritahetunā kāyasya bhedāt sugatau svargaloke deveṣūpapadyante / ime punarbhavantaḥ sattvāḥ kāyaduścaritena vāgduścaritena manoduścaritena samanvāgatā āryāṇāmapavādakā mithyādṛṣṭayaśca mithyādṛṣṭikarmasamādānahetoḥ kāyasya bhedātparaṃmaraṇādapāyadurgativinipātaṃ narakeṣūpapadyante / iuti hi divyena cakṣuṣā atikrāntamānuṣyakena daśadiśi loke sarvalokadhātuṣu dharmadhātuparame ākāśadhātuparyavasāne ṣaṅgatikānāṃ satvānāṃ cyutopapādaṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti" iti //
body.translated_text: the mind as it really is — whether with passion or free from passion, with hatred or free from hatred, with delusion or free from delusion — up to knowing the unsurpassed mind as it really is. One recollects one birth, two, three, up to hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>niyutas</s> of births. One recollects one day, two, three, up to hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>niyutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s>. 'There I was, of such a name, such a <s>gotra</s> (clan), such a birth, such food, of such longevity, with such a lifespan.' 'Having passed away from there, I was reborn here' — up to — 'Having passed away from there, I was reborn here' — thus one recollects manifold former abodes with their aspects, designations, and signs. With the divine eye, purified and surpassing the human, one sees beings dying and being reborn — those of good complexion and bad complexion, inferior and superior, in good destinies and bad destinies — and knows beings as they have gone according to their <s>karma</s>. 'These beings, endowed with good conduct of body, speech, and mind, not revilers of the <s>āryas</s> (noble ones), possessing right view — by the cause of their good conduct of body, speech, and mind, at the breaking up of the body, are reborn in a good destiny, in the heavenly world among the <s>devas</s>. But these beings, endowed with bad conduct of body, speech, and mind, revilers of the <s>āryas</s>, possessing wrong view — by the cause of wrong-view-based action, at the breaking up of the body, after death, are reborn in a bad destiny, in a lower realm, in perdition, in the hells.' Thus with the divine eye, surpassing the human, in the ten directions of the world, in all world-systems, bounded by the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of dharma) and extending to the limits of the <s>ākāśadhātu</s> (realm of space), one truly knows the passing away and rebirth of beings in the six destinies."

body.text: etāsu dhyānāpramāṇārūpyasamāpattyabhijñāsu vyastasamastāsu pratiṣṭhāpayediti sambandhaḥ / śeṣaṃ subodhamiti prathamaḥ stobhaḥ //
body.translated_text: The connection is that one should establish [beings] in these <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations), <s>apramāṇas</s> (immeasurables), <s>ārūpyasamāpattis</s> (formless attainments), and <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), both separately and together. The rest is easily understood. This is the first <s>stobha</s> (section of praise).

body.text: ita ūrdhaṃ tiṣṭhatvādayaḥ pratiṣṭhāpayedantāḥ pratyekaṃ pareṇa tatkiṃ manyasa ityādinā prabhāvanatāntena sahitā yathākramaṃ dvitīyatṛtīyacaturtha pañcamaṣaṣṭhaḥ stobhaḥ /
body.translated_text: From here onward, [the passages] beginning with 'abides' and ending with 'should establish,' each combined with the subsequent [passage] beginning with 'What do you think?' up to [the passage ending with] 'extolling,' constitute in order the second, third, fourth, fifth, and sixth <s>stobhas</s> (sections of praise).

body.text: iti mṛdumadhyo mṛdvadhimātraḥ madhyamṛdu madhyamadhyo madhyādhimātraśca stobhaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus [these are] the <s>stobhas</s> of mild-middle, mild-superior, medium-mild, medium-middle, and medium-superior [degrees].

body.text: punaraparādi punaraparāt prāk saptamaḥ / bhagavatyoḥ parebhyo dānaṃ pūrvakeṣvapyasti / iha tu svayaṃ ca vācanaṃ parebhyaśca likhitvā dānaṃ caryātireka ityadhimātramṛdustobhaḥ //
body.translated_text: The [passage] beginning with '<s>punaraparam</s>' (furthermore), before the [next] '<s>punaraparam</s>,' is the seventh. In the two [versions of the] <s>Bhagavatī</s>, giving to others is [found] in the earlier ones as well. But here, the recitation by oneself and the giving [of copies] after writing them out for others constitutes a surpassing of practice — this is the superior-mild <s>stobha</s>.

body.text: punaraparādi punaraparāt prāgaṣṭamaḥ / arthamasyā vivṛṇuyāditi yatpūrvamuktaṃ tatpāramitādīnāmaudārikaṃ rūpaṃ pratihatānāṃ prasādakaramabhipretya / iha tu koṭitrayānupālambhādikaṃ paramārthamabhipretyāha / arthakuśalādityādi / tatrārthakuśalasya vācanaṃ tamevārthaṃ manasikṛtya vācanāt / sārthāmiti tenaivārthena
body.translated_text: The [passage] beginning with '<s>punaraparam</s>,' before the [next] '<s>punaraparam</s>,' is the eighth. What was previously stated — 'one should explain its meaning' — was said with reference to the gross form of the <s>pāramitās</s> and so forth, aimed at generating faith in those who are hindered. But here, with reference to the ultimate meaning — non-apprehension of the three points and so forth — he says 'skilled in meaning' and so on. Therein, the recitation by one skilled in meaning is recitation having reflected upon that very meaning. '<s>Sārthām</s>' (meaningful) means accompanied by that very meaning.

body.text:
sahitām / savyañjanāmiti tasyaivārthasya vācakā vyañjanā / upadiśet tasyārthasya sūtreṇa saṃsyandanāt / paridīnīpayed yuktibhiḥ / ayamaṣṭame caryātirekaḥ / ayaṃ ityaṣṭame vartamānaḥ / tata iti saptame vṛttāt / iyamapyupadeṣṭavyeti kākvā śiraḥkāyena vā praśnaḥ / naivopadeṣṭavyā parisphuṭāditi bhāvaḥ / abudhyamānasyeti jaḍadhiyaḥ / tasya yuktyāgamābhyāṃ samyaggrāhitasya paravācā calanāt / kaḥ punarenaṃ cālayiṣyatīti / etadāha tatkasya hetoriti / atrottaram / utpatsyate hityādi / bhagavatīdeśakenaiva yā tasyā viparītārthavarṇanā sā tasyāḥ prativarṇikā / tayaiva jaḍasya śraddhālorvañcanāt / utpattau ṇvuc paryāyārharṇotpattiṣu ṇvujiti vacanāt / tatreti tathā sati / mā praṇaṃkṣīditi saṃbodhimārgāt praṇaṣṭo bhraṣṭo mā bhūdityarthaḥ / ṇasa (śa) adarśane radhādiḥ / puṣādiśca / tasmā [ta].......ayaṃ prayogaḥ / tathāpyaṅvṛddhī na bhavataḥ / parasmaipadeṣu tayorvidhānāt / saṃjñāpūrvakasya ca vidheranityatvāt / yathā cāsyāḥ prativarṇikā bhavati yathā ca na bhavati tadubhayaṃ mahatyorbhagavatyorvistareṇoktaṃ- "yo rūpaṃ vedanāṃ yāvatsarvākārajñatāmanityaduḥkhanātmaśūnyāśubhākārairnimittayogena upalambhayogena bhāvayati sa prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāvayati / sa prathamāṃ bodhisattvabhūmiṃ yāvaddaśamīṃ yāvadanuttarāṃ samyaksambodhimadhigamiṣyatīti / ya evamupadekṣyati sa prativarṇikāmupadekṣyati // kathaṃ nopadekṣyati? rūpaṃ svabhāvena śūnyam / yaśca rūpasya svabhāvaḥ so 'bhāvaḥ / yaścābhāvaḥ sā prajñāpāramitā / tasyāṃ rūpameva nāsti kuto nityamanityaṃ vā bhaviṣyatītyevamādi / ya evamupadekṣyati nāsau prativarṇikāmupadekṣyati" iti // ata ihāpi kathaṃ bhagavannityādinā prativarṇikāparijñānāya śakrasya praśnaḥ / bhaviṣyanti kauśiketyādinā bhagavata uttaram / rūpīṇī pañcendriyāṇi kāyasaṃgṛhītatvāt paramāṇusañcayatvādvā kāyāḥ / te abhāvitā anabhyastasaṃvaratvādyeṣāṃ te tathoktāḥ / asaṃvṛtendriyatvāt abhāvitaśilāḥ / tato 'bhāvitacittā anabhyastasamādhayaḥ / tato abhāvitaprajñāḥ samāhitacittasyaiva
yathābhūtaprajñānāt / tato duṣprajñā viparītadṛṣṭayaḥ / tata eḍamūkāḥ sūktīnāmaśravaṇāt / ......prajñāparihīṇāḥ samyagdṛṣṭibhaṅgāt rūpānityatetyupalakṣaṇam / duḥkhatādayopi draṣṭavyāḥ / nityaṃ na bhavatītyanityatā mahāyāne / tadvyavacchedārtha vināśagrahaṇam / vināśalakṣaṇā anityatetyarthaḥ / na hi satāṃ vināśo nāpyanupa(tpa)nnānām / tasmādvināśadarśī tānvastudharmānupalabheta / sattā(tā)mutpādavināśau ca / tadevaṃ
body.translated_text: '<s>Savyañjanām</s>' (with the letter) — the expressions that convey that very meaning are the <s>vyañjanas</s> (syllables/expressions). 'One should instruct' — because of the concordance of that meaning with the <s>sūtra</s>. 'One should make it clear' — through reasoning. This is the surpassing of practice in the eighth [section]. 'This' refers to what is present in the eighth. 'From that' refers to what occurred in the seventh. 'This too should be taught' — the question is posed by <s>Śakra</s> either through the tone of voice or through gestures of the head and body. 'It should not at all be taught, since it is already fully manifest' — this is the purport. 'Of one who does not understand' means of one who is dull-witted. Because such a person, even when properly made to grasp [the teaching] through reasoning and scripture, is swayed by the words of others. 'Who then will sway him?' — this he states with 'For what reason?' and so on. The answer to this is: 'There will arise' and so on. The <s>prativarṇikā</s> (counterfeit/perversion) of the <s>Bhagavatī</s> is the description of a meaning contrary to it by the very one who teaches it; through that very [counterfeit], the dull-witted person's faith is deceived. In '<s>utpatti</s>' (arising), the suffix <s>ṇvuc</s> [is used] according to the rule '<s>ṇvuc</s> in the senses of alternation, desert, and arising.' 'In that case' means when it is so. 'May he not be lost' means may he not be lost or fallen from the path to <s>saṃbodhi</s> (awakening). [The root] <s>ṇaśa</s> [means] 'disappearance,' belonging to the <s>radh-ādi</s> class and also the <s>puṣ-ādi</s> class. Therefore... this is the derivation. Even so, <s>aṅ</s>-augment and <s>vṛddhi</s> do not occur, because they are prescribed for <s>parasmaipada</s> forms, and because rules preceded by technical designations are not invariable. How the <s>prativarṇikā</s> of this [Prajnaparamita] occurs and how it does not occur — both are stated in detail in the two great <s>Bhagavatīs</s>: 'One who cultivates form, feeling, up to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscient knowledge) through the mode of signs, through the mode of apprehension, with the aspects of impermanence, suffering, non-self, emptiness, and impurity — cultivates the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. He will attain the first <s>bodhisattva-bhūmi</s> up to the tenth, up to unsurpassed perfect awakening — one who teaches thus teaches the <s>prativarṇikā</s>.' 'How does one not teach it? Form is empty by its own nature. The own-nature of form is non-existence. And that non-existence is the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. In it, form itself does not exist — how then could it be permanent or impermanent?' and so forth. 'One who teaches thus does not teach the <s>prativarṇikā</s>.' Therefore here too, <s>Śakra's</s> question beginning with 'How, <s>Bhagavan</s>?' is for the purpose of understanding the <s>prativarṇikā</s>. The <s>Bhagavān's</s> answer begins with 'There will be, <s>Kauśika</s>.' '<s>Rūpīṇī</s>' — the five sense faculties are 'bodies' because they are included in the body or because they are aggregations of atoms. They are 'uncultivated' because their restraint has not been practiced — those whose [faculties are] thus are so called. Because their faculties are unrestrained, they are 'uncultivated in moral conduct.' From that, they are 'uncultivated in mind,' their <s>samādhi</s> not having been practiced. From that, they are 'uncultivated in wisdom,' because only one whose mind is concentrated knows things as they really are. From that, they are 'of poor wisdom,' having perverted views. From that, they are 'dumb and mute,' because they have not heard well-spoken words. ...Devoid of wisdom, because their right view is broken. 'Form is impermanent' is illustrative; suffering and so on should also be understood. 'Impermanence' in the sense that 'it does not become permanent' belongs to the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. To distinguish from that, the word 'destruction' is used. 'Impermanence characterized by destruction' is the meaning. For there is no destruction of what exists, nor of what has not arisen. Therefore one who sees destruction would apprehend those as real entities. Both existence and arising-and-destruction [are implied]. Thus

body.text: nityatādicaturviparyāsapratipakṣeṇa hinayānasaṃgṛhītāyāḥ samyagdṛṣṭeḥ prajñāpāramitātvena yā deśanā sā tasyāḥ prativarṇiketyuktaṃ bhavati /
body.translated_text: the teaching that the right view comprised within the <s>Hīnayāna</s>, [applied] as a counteragent to the four <s>viparyāsas</s> (perversions) of permanence and so forth, constitutes the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> — that is said to be the <s>prativarṇikā</s> (counterfeit) of it.

body.text: athaiṣāṃ rūpādīnāmanityatāduḥkhādibhāvanā bodhisattvena bhāvayitavyā na cetyata āha / na khalu punarityādi / draṣṭavyeti bhāvayitavyetyarthaḥ / yadi bhāvayetko doṣaḥ syādata āha / sa cedityādi / prativarṇikāyāmiti hīnayāna ityarthaḥ / evamasyāṃ bhagavatyāṃ samāsataḥ prativarṇikāṃ darśayitvā tasyā caryā pratiṣiddhā / yathā tu prativarṇikā na bhavati tatprathamata eva sūcitaṃ arthakuśalo vācayedityādinā / yaḥ punaḥ śūnyatāniḥsvabhāvatādipadeṣu māhāyānikammanyānāṃ viparyāsastatpratipakṣeṇa dharmakāyakāritraprakaraṇe 'viparyāsakāritraṃ mahatyorbhagavatyoruktam / asyāmapi bhagavatyā madhye 'viparyāsaḥ prāptinirvāṇe sarvākārajñatāniryāṇe 'ṣṭavidhe ca gāmbhīrye parisphuṭamuktaḥ / tasmāttata evāvadhāraṇīyaḥ // ityadhimātramadhyastobhaḥ //
body.translated_text: Now, if [one asks] whether the <s>bodhisattva</s> should or should not cultivate the contemplation of impermanence, suffering, and so on regarding these forms and the rest, he says 'Not at all' and so on. 'Should be seen' means 'should be cultivated.' If one were to cultivate [it], what fault would there be? To this he says 'If' and so on. 'In the <s>prativarṇikā</s>' means 'in the <s>Hīnayāna</s>.' Thus, having shown the <s>prativarṇikā</s> of this <s>Bhagavatī</s> in brief, the practice of that [counterfeit] is prohibited. But how the <s>prativarṇikā</s> does not occur was already indicated at the very beginning with 'One skilled in meaning should recite' and so on. Furthermore, regarding the perversion among those who consider themselves <s>Māhāyānikas</s> concerning terms like emptiness and essencelessness, and its counteragent — the chapter on the conduct of non-perversion in the section on the activities of the <s>dharmakāya</s> is stated in the two great <s>Bhagavatīs</s>. In this <s>Bhagavatī</s> as well, non-perversion is clearly stated in the middle — in [the sections on] attainment, <s>nirvāṇa</s>, the path to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscient knowledge), and the eightfold profundity. Therefore, it should be ascertained from those very [passages]. This is the superior-middle <s>stobha</s>.

body.text: punaraparādiḥ punaraparātprāk pañcatiṣṭhaturnavamaḥ / strotaāpattiphala evaṃ prabhāvyata iti tāvatsattveṣu niṣpādyate / ityadhimātrastobhaḥ /
body.translated_text: The [passage] beginning with '<s>punaraparam</s>,' before the [next] '<s>punaraparam</s>,' with five 'abides,' is the ninth. That [the teaching] is thus efficacious is [shown by the fact that] it is accomplished in beings insofar as the fruit of stream-entry [is attained]. This is the superior <s>stobha</s>.

body.text: punaraparādiḥ punaraparāt prāk pañcatiṣṭhatuḥ prathamā / sakṛdāgāminaḥ phalam / iti mṛdumṛdvī praśaṃsā //
body.translated_text: The [passage] beginning with '<s>punaraparam</s>,' before the [next] '<s>punaraparam</s>,' with five 'abides,' is the first [sub-section]. The fruit of the once-returner. This is the mild-mild praise.

body.text: punaraparādiḥ punaraparāt prāk pañcatiṣṭhatudvitīyā / anāgāminaḥ phalama / iti mṛdumadhyā praśaṃsā //
body.translated_text: The [passage] beginning with '<s>punaraparam</s>,' before the [next] '<s>punaraparam</s>,' with five 'abides,' is the second [sub-section]. The fruit of the non-returner. This is the mild-middle praise.

body.text: punaraparādiḥ punaraparāt prāk pañcatiṣṭhatustṛtīyā / arhatvamarhato bhāvaḥ / iti mṛddhadhimātrā praśaṃsā //
body.translated_text: The [passage] beginning with '<s>punaraparam</s>,' before the [next] '<s>punaraparam</s>,' with five 'abides,' is the third [sub-section]. <s>Arhatva</s> (arhatship) is the state of being an <s>arhat</s>. This is the mild-superior praise.

body.text: punaraparādistiṣṭhatoḥ prāk caturthī / svayamabhisaṃbodhābduddhaḥ, ekamātmānaṃ pratibuddhaḥ pratyekabuddhaḥ / itimadhyamṛdvī praśaṃsā //
body.translated_text: From 'Moreover' up to the [phrase] 'let it stand,' the fourth [level of praise]. 'Self-awakened through awakening' is a <s>Buddha</s>; one who has awakened only oneself is a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>. Thus the moderate-mild praise.

body.text: tiṣṭhatvādipañcakena pañcamī / iti madhyamadhyā praśaṃsā //
body.translated_text: By the fivefold [passage] beginning with 'let it stand,' the fifth [level of praise]. Thus the moderate-moderate praise.

body.text: punaraparādistiṣṭhatoḥ prāk ṣaṣṭhī / kaścideveti prathamaḥ / yaśceti dvitīyaḥ / yo veti tṛtīyaḥ / upanāmayediti dadyāt / kenāśayanetyāha / atraivetyādi / vṛddhyādikaṃ gataḥ prāptaḥ / ayamiti tṛtīyaḥ / tasmāditi prathamād dvitīyācca / iti madhyādhimātrā praśaṃsā //
body.translated_text: From 'Moreover' up to the [phrase] 'let it stand,' the sixth [level of praise]. 'Someone indeed' is the first [example]. 'And whoever' is the second. 'Or whoever' is the third. 'Would present' means 'would give.' 'With what intention?' — thus it is said. Beginning with 'in this very' and so on. 'Having attained increase and the rest' means 'having obtained.' 'This one' is the third [example]. 'Therefore' [follows] from the first and second. Thus the moderate-intense praise.

body.text: tiṣṭhatvādipañcamena saptamī / ityadhimātramṛddhī praśaṃsā //
body.translated_text: By the fivefold [passage] beginning with 'let it stand,' the seventh [level of praise]. Thus the intense-mild praise.

body.text: punaraparādistiṣṭhato prāgaṣṭamī / saṃkhyāpi bhagavannityādi / tatra saṃkhyā pūrvakātpuṇyāduttaraṃ puṇyaṃ śataguṇaṃ sahasraguṇaṃ ityādi / gaṇanā daśaguṇitaśataguṇamityādi / upamā gaṅgānadīvālukāguṇamityādi / aupamyaṃ daśagaṅgānadīvālukāguṇamityādi / upaniśā daśaguṇitaśatagaṅgānadīvālukāguṇamityādi / parimāṇasyātyantamasambhavāttadartha yā upaniṣat samīpe niṣadanam / sāpi na sukarā kartum / ityadhimātramadhyā praśaṃsā //
body.translated_text: From 'Moreover' up to the [phrase] 'let it stand,' the eighth [level of praise]. Beginning with 'Even the calculation, O <s>Bhagavān</s>' and so on. There, 'calculation' [means]: from the previous merit, the subsequent merit is a hundredfold, a thousandfold, and so on. 'Enumeration' is ten-multiplied-hundredfold and so on. 'Comparison' is the sands-of-the-<s>Gaṅgā</s>-river-fold and so on. 'Analogy' is ten-<s>Gaṅgā</s>-river-sands-fold and so on. '<s>Upaniṣā</s>' is ten-multiplied-hundred-<s>Gaṅgā</s>-river-sands-fold and so on. Because of the absolute impossibility of measure, that which serves the purpose of measure is an <s>upaniṣad</s> (proximate sitting, i.e. approach). And even that is not easy to accomplish. Thus the intense-moderate praise.

body.text: tiṣṭhatvādipañcakena navamī / yathāyathetyādinā kauśikaḥ puṇyātirekopapattimāha / sādhu sādhvityādinā taṃ subhūtiḥ sopapattikaṃ protsāhayati / ityadhimātrādhimātrā praśaṃsā //
body.translated_text: By the fivefold [passage] beginning with 'let it stand,' the ninth [level of praise]. By the passage beginning with 'In whatever way' and so on, <s>Kauśika</s> states the proof of the surplus of merit. By the passage beginning with 'Well done, well done!' and so on, <s>Subhūti</s> encourages him with supporting proof. Thus the intense-intense praise.

body.text: puṇyasya paryāyā bhedāstad dyotakaḥ parivartastatparivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: The synonyms of merit are its varieties; that which illuminates them is the chapter (<s>parivarta</s>); hence that chapter.

body.text: āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ sāratamānāmni pañjikāyāṃ ratnākaraśāntiviracitāyāṃ pañcamaḥ parivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: In the <s>Pañjikā</s> commentary named <s>Sāratama</s>, composed by <s>Ratnākaraśānti</s>, on the noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s> — this is the Fifth Chapter.

body.text: 6. anumodanāparimāṇamanāparivarto nāma ṣaṣṭhaḥ /
body.translated_text: 6. The sixth [chapter] is named 'The Chapter on the Immeasurable Mind of Rejoicing.'

body.text: uktāḥ stutistobhapraśaṃsāḥ / pariṇāmanāmanaskāro vaktavyaḥ / tamadhikṛtya śāstram-
body.translated_text: The praises of laudation and eulogy have been stated. The mental act of dedication (<s>pariṇāmanā</s>) is now to be explained. With regard to that, the treatise [states] —

body.text: viśeṣapariṇāmastu tasya kāritramuttamam //
body.translated_text: The special dedication, however, is its supreme function.

body.text: nopalambhākṛtiścāsāvaviparyāsalakṣaṇaḥ // 2-21 //
body.translated_text: It has the form of non-apprehension and is characterized by non-error. [2-21]

children.translated_text: It is secluded, within the domain of the recollection of the nature of the flood of <s>Buddha</s>-merit,
Endowed with skillful means and signless, and approved by the <s>Buddhas</s>. [2-22]
Not engaged in the three realms, the dedication is further threefold:
Mild, moderate, and intense — having the nature of the arising of great merit. [2-23]

body.text: sarvasattvānāṃ dānaśīlabhāvanāmayāt puṇyaugho viśiṣyate prakṛṣyate 'neneti 'viśeṣaḥ' / sa punarasyāḥ sarvasattvānāmagratāyai samyaksaṃbodhikaraṇatā /
body.translated_text: The flood of merit arising from the generosity, morality, and meditation of all beings is surpassed, excelled by this — hence 'special' (<s>viśeṣa</s>). And that [special quality] is its function of bringing all beings to the foremost [position] for the sake of perfect awakening.

body.text: "sarvasattvasādhāraṇaṃ kṛtvā anuttarāyai samyaksaṃbodhaye pariṇāmayati taccānupalambhayogena" iti mahatyoḥ pāṭhāt / tena viśeṣeṇa 'pariṇāmaḥ' //
body.translated_text: From the reading in the great [text]: 'Having made it common to all beings, one dedicates it toward unsurpassed perfect awakening, and that by the method of non-apprehension.' By that special [quality], it is 'dedication' (<s>pariṇāma</s>).

body.text: tamāha / atha khalu maitreya ityādinā / bodhisattvasyeti / utpāditabodhisacittasya / yathoktaviśeṣaviśiṣṭatvānmahāsattvaḥ, pariṇāmanā vyavasāyo 'syeti mahāsattvasya / anumodanāsahagataṃ kuśalaṃ anumodanā / sā cānupalambhapariṇāmasyādau vistareṇa vakṣyate / tasyāḥ pariṇāmanā / tayā sahagatam / idameva ityasya pareṇa puṇyakriyāvastuśabdena sambandhaḥ / tata iti sarvasattvānāṃ dānādimayāt puṇyāt sakāśāt / agramākhyāyate yāvad asamasamamākhyāyate / tasmādagrādi / agrādiphalahetutvāt / tadapi kutaḥ? yathākramaṃ pramuditādyekādaśabhūmisaṃgṛhītasvaparārthasaṃpattihetutvāt / paryāyatvepi sarveṣāmupādānasāmarthyāt / asamābuddhāsteṣāṃ sādhāraṇo viśeṣo 'samasamaḥ / samantaprabhāsāyāṃ bhūmau / kathaṃ dharmameghāyāmasamaḥ? asamasādharmyāt / "daśabhūmīśvarastu bodhisattvo buddha eva draṣṭavyo na tu samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ" iti vacanāt / tadevamagrādipadebhyaḥ pūrveṇa granthena viśeṣapariṇāma uktaḥ / agrādipadaistasyaiva 'kāritramuttamaṃ' iti viśeṣapariṇāmaḥ sakāritraḥ //
body.translated_text: This he states beginning with 'Now then, <s>Maitreya</s>' and so on. 'Of a <s>Bodhisattva</s>' means of one who has generated the mind of awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>). Because of being distinguished by the special [quality] as described, he is a <s>Mahāsattva</s> (great being); since dedication is his resolve, [he is called] a <s>Mahāsattva</s>. The wholesome [merit] accompanied by rejoicing is the rejoicing (<s>anumodanā</s>).

body.text: evamukta ityādinā anupalambhapariṇāmamāha / daśadiśo 'sminniti daśadiśi loke, ākāśaparimāṇe bhājanaloke / sarvata iti tāsu sarvāsu dikṣu / sarvatragatayeti vyāpitayā ghanatayetyarthaḥ / aprameyādiṣu vīpsā digbhiḥ pratyekamabhisambandhārtham / anantāparyanteṣvityanantānanteṣu / tadiyamarthato dviruktirna śabdataḥ / tatra digdeśyānāmaparicchedāt aprameyāḥ / saṃkhyāyā aparicchedāt asaṃkhyeyāḥ / digvaipulyenāparicchedāt aparimāṇāḥ / pratyekaṃ cintayitumaśakyatvāt acintyāḥ / tāsveva cintāsvantagamanāt anantāḥ / evaṃ sākalyena pratidiśamananteṣu trisāhasreṣu pratidiśaṃ ya ekaikastrisāhasraḥ / tasmin aprameyāprameyāṇāṃ yāvat anantāparyantānāṃ tathāgatānāmiti sambandhaḥ / ihāpyekaikena trisāhasreṇa sambandhārtha vīpsā / nanvekasmiṃstrisāhasre eka eva tathāgato nāprameyādiriti cedāha / atīte 'dhvani iti / ekadā traikastathāgato na sarvadā / atītaḥ punaradhvā anāditvāt aprameyaḥ tata ekasminnapi lokadhātāvatīte 'dhvani aprameyāstathāgatāḥ kāladairdhyeṇāparicchedāt / tāvantaśca te saṃkhyayā aparicchedāt asaṃkhyeyāḥ / manasā tiryaksaṃniveśya vaipulyenāparicchedāt aparimāṇāḥ / ekaikacintayā acintyāḥ / ekaikacintāyāmantāgamanāt anantāḥ / īdṛśānāṃ tathāgatānāṃ parinirvṛtānāmiti na tu tiṣṭhatām / arayaḥ kleśāstān hatavanta iti arhatām / aviparītasarvadharmajñānāt samyaksambuddhānām / anena padadvayena prahāṇajñānasampadāvukte /
body.translated_text: Beginning with 'Having thus spoken' and so on, he explains the dedication through non-apprehension. 'In the ten directions here' means in the world of the ten directions, in the container world that is equal in extent to space. 'Everywhere' means in all those directions. 'Gone everywhere' means through pervasiveness, meaning through density. Regarding 'immeasurable' and the rest —

body.text: bhavapathatvāddharme asmimāṇo(no) [vartmaniḥ] / vṛteranipratyayaḥ / saraṇidharaṇivat / muḍāgamaśca / vartmanistṛṣṇā bhavapadavītvāt / yathoktaṃ- "asmimānaḥ pitā ukto mātā tṛṣṇeti cocyate" iti / tayorūnmūlanāt chinnavartmanāṃ chinnavartmanīnāṃ ca / prapañco dvayakalpanā, bhavaḥ saṃsāraḥ / tayornetryau nāyike yathākramaṃ dharmadṛṣṭiḥ pudgaladṛṣṭiśca / tayoḥ parikṣayāt chinnaprapañcabhavanetrīkānāṃ paryāttabāṣpāṇāmiti / punarbhavābhāve na punarbandhano na śoko nāśru / tataḥ parikṣīṇabāṣpāṇām / kaṇṭakasādharmyāt kaṇṭakāḥ kudṛṣṭayaḥ / teṣāṃ kṣodanāt marditakaṇṭakāḥ / śeṣaṃ nidāna eva vyākhyātam / prathamacittotpādo yaḥ pṛthivīsamaḥ / tamupādāya tata ārabhya / etasminnantara ityetāvatyavakāśe / śīlādiskandhaḥ śīlādirāśiḥ / bodhisattvānāmapi balādayaḥ santi / na tu te pāraṅgatāḥ / tatastadvyavacchedāya pāramitāgrahaṇam / anāśravo mārgaḥ parijñaḥ / sarvajñajñānaṃ samyaksambodhiḥ / pūrvaṃ buddhaguṇādibhiḥ saṃprayuktāni / ye cetyādinā buddhaguṇādinapyāha / samyaksambodhireva sukhamupaśamasukhatvāt / sarvadharmeṣu aiśvarya vaśitā / ṛddherabhisaṃskāra kriyā / anāvaraṇaṃ śuddhatvāt / asaṅgamanapekṣatvāt / apratihataṃ sarvasmin sarvākārajñeyapravṛtteḥ / anupama tasyānumānāya viśeṣadṛṣṭāntabhāvāt / parito 'vacchedaḥ parimāna(ṇam) / aśeṣaviśeṣāntarāyāt rūpagrāhi pratyakṣam / tasya tasmin pareṣāmabhāvādaparimeyam / tathāgatānāṃ yathābhūtajñānasamyagjñānam / tadeva balaṃ sarvābhibhūtatvāt / yadbuddhajñānabalamiti / buddhajñānasya balaṃ śaktirniravadhisarvākāraviśvārthakriyāyai / balānāṃ yadbuddhaiḥ jñānadarśanaṃ prāptisākṣātkaraṇam / caturvaiśāradyena suparipūrṇo 'dhigamaḥ svadharmāṇāṃ yaśca dharmādhigama iti sambandhaḥ / sa katham? sarvadharmāṇāṃ paramārthasya samyagjñānasyābhinirhāreṇa niṣpādanena / triparivarta dvādaśākāraṃ lokottaraṃ jñānaṃ dharmaḥ / sa eva cakraṃ devamanuṣyeṣu caṃkramaṇāt / tasya pravartanaṃ daśasu dikṣu / ayamuddeśaḥ / asya nirdeśo navabhiraṅgaiḥ / tasyaiva dharmasya dyotanī vāg dharmoktā / tasyāḥ pragrahaṇaṃ manasā vyavasthāpanam / saiva vāg dharmabherī / tasyāḥ saṃpratāḍanaṃ vineyajayaśrāvaṇam / saiva vā dharmaśaṅkhaḥ / tasya pūraṇaṃ vineyaireva jñānam / tasya dharmaśaṅkhasya pravyāharaṇam / tamevālambya tadarthākāreṇa manasi kurvatāṃ cintābhāvanayoḥ pariniṣpattiḥ / bhāvānābalādutpannaṃ tadeva lokottaraṃ jñānaṃ dharmakhaṅgaḥ / tena praharaṇaṃ kleśānāṃ vidhvaṃsanam / tasyaiva bhūyasi jane pravṛttiḥ dharmavṛṣṭiḥ / tasyāḥ pravarṣaṇam / sa eva yajño nirargaḍatvāt / tasya yajanam / tasya dharmasya dānena sarvasattvānāṃ santapaṇaṃ saṃpravāraṇaṃ ca pariveṣanaṃ(ṇam) / vinītāḥ smṛtyupasthānaiḥ
body.translated_text: Because it is the path of existence, there is the pride of 'I am' (<s>asmimāna</s>) in [this] <s>dharma</s> [, which is called] the path (<s>vartman</s>). The suffix is from the root '<s>vṛt</s>' (to turn), without the '<s>ni</s>' prefix, like '<s>saraṇi</s>' and '<s>dharaṇi</s>.' And there is the augment '<s>muṭ</s>.' The craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) that is the track (<s>vartman</s>) [arises] because of being the path of existence. As it is said: 'The pride of "I am" is called the father, and craving is called the mother.' And of those two —

body.text:
satyeṣvavatāraṇāt / śikṣitāḥ samyakprahāṇarddhipādaiḥ / adhimuktā indriyabalairekāntaniścayāt / niyatā avinivṛtteḥ / buddhānāṃ pariṣadāmiti
vyadhikaraṇe ṣaṣṭhi / parinirvā[pa]yatāmiti okhai śoṣaṇe / buddhānāmasyeti kṣetrīkṛtya mānaso bhāvanaṃ rañjanam / tasmai hitā manobhāvanīyāḥ prasādakarā ityarthaḥ / niravaśeṣamabhisaṃkṣipya anavaśeṣamanumodeteti sambandhaḥ / aikadhyamityaikarāśyena / abhisaṃkṣipyetyasya vivaraṇaṃ piṇḍayitveti tulayitveti / samāhiteneti manasā nirūpya / anumodeteti prītyālambanaṃ kuryāt / anumodanayeti prītyotpādanayā / agrayeti prakṛṣṭayā / kathaṃ tarhi ekādaśapadāni? ekādaśavidhepyālambane tasyāḥ prakarṣāt / tat kutaḥ? madhye daśasu ca dikṣu ye tathāgatāḥ teṣāṃ saparicchadena yāni kuśalamūlāni tadālambanatvāttasyāḥ / kathaṃ pariuṇāmayatītyata āha / bodherāhārakaṃ ākarṣakaṃ bhavatviti /
body.translated_text: Because of introduction to the truths. 'Trained' — by means of the right exertions and the bases of supernatural power. 'Convinced' — by means of the faculties and powers, because of definitive certainty. 'Determined' — because of non-regression. 'Of the assemblies of the <s>Buddhas</s>' — a <s>ṣaṣṭhī</s> (genitive) case in a different subject [relation]. 'Causing to attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>' — the verbal root '<s>okhai</s>' [is used] in the sense of drying up.

body.text: tadevamukta ityādinā vistareṇa sthavirasubhūtiryathānumodya yathā bodhisattvaḥ pariṇāmayati taduktavān / yathā tu tatrānupalambhayogaḥ kartavyastadupadarśanāyāryamaitreyaṃ tatretyādinā pṛcchati / yairvastubhiriti daśadik tathāgatādibhiḥ / yerālambanairiti tadīyaiḥ kuśalamūlaiḥ / yerākāreriti śīlasamādhiskandhādibhiḥ / taccittamityanumodanācittam / api tviti kintu / upalabhyeranniti śaktau liṅga / upalabdhuṃ śakyata iti praśnaḥ / nimittīkarotīti vikalpayati / anyathā anumodanāpariṇāmanayorayogāt //
body.translated_text: Thus, with 'thus spoken' and so forth, the elder <s>Subhūti</s>, having rejoiced in detail, stated how the <s>bodhisattva</s> dedicates. And to demonstrate how the method of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambhayoga</s>) should be applied therein, he asks <s>Āryamaitreya</s> with 'therein' and so forth. 'By whatever objects' means by the <s>Tathāgatas</s> and others in the ten directions. 'By whatever supports' means by their wholesome roots. 'By whatever aspects' means by the aggregates of morality, concentration, and the like. 'That mind' means the mind of rejoicing. 'But' means however. 'Could be apprehended' — the optative [suffix] indicates capacity. 'Can be apprehended' — this is the question. 'Conceptualizes' means discriminates. Otherwise, the rejoicing and dedication would be impossible.

body.text: āryamaitreya āha / na tānītyādi sthavira āha / evantarhi viparyāsāḥ syuriti / asata eva nimittodgrahāt grahaṇāt santīraṇācca yathokramaṃ saṃjñāyāścittasya dṛṣṭeśca viparyāsaḥ / eṣāṃ sādhanārtha rāgo dṛṣṭāntaḥ athāpīti paramatamāśaṅkate / yādṛśo yakṣastādṛśo baliriti bhāvaḥ / cittamiti pariṇāmanācittam / sarvadharmā ityuddeśaḥ / sarvadhātava iti nirdeśaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Āryamaitreya</s> said: 'Not those' and so forth. The elder said: 'Then there would be distortions' — from grasping the sign of the non-existent itself, from apprehending it, and from examining it, there are respectively distortions of perception, of mind, and of view. For the purpose of establishing these, desire/passion is the example. 'But even so' — he anticipates the other's position. 'As is the <s>yakṣa</s> (spirit), so is the offering' — this is the meaning. 'Mind' means the mind of dedication. 'All <s>dharmas</s>' is the general statement. 'All elements' is the detailed exposition.

body.text: yadi cetyādinā doṣamāha / katamairvastvādibhiriti / anumodanācittasambandhibhiḥ / cittamiti pariṇāmanācittam / tasyāpi niḥsvabhāavatvāt / kveti kasyām / pariṇāmanaiva na syāditi bhāvaḥ //
body.translated_text: With 'but if' and so forth, he states the fault. 'By which objects and so forth' means those connected with the mind of rejoicing. 'Mind' means the mind of dedication. Because that too is without self-nature. 'Where' means in which [dedication]. 'There would be no dedication at all' — this is the meaning.

body.text: ata evāryamaitreya āha / nedamityādi / yadapi hi syād bhavet / kva? anumodanāpariṇāmanādau / mātragrahaṇamanuṣṭhānavyavacchedārtham / śraddhā saṃpratyayaḥ / prema prītiḥ / prasādo manasaḥ kāluṣyavigamaḥ / gauravaṃ bhaktiḥ /
body.translated_text: Therefore <s>Āryamaitreya</s> said: 'Not this' and so forth. 'Whatever indeed would exist' means would be. Where? In the rejoicing-dedication and so forth. The word 'mere' serves the purpose of excluding [actual] practice. '<s>Śraddhā</s>' (faith) is conviction. '<s>Prema</s>' (love) is affection. '<s>Prasāda</s>' (serene clarity) is the removal of turbidity of the mind. '<s>Gaurava</s>' (reverence) is devotion.

body.text: upastabdhaḥ sthirīkṛtaḥ / avalayaścittasyāva[na]tiḥ / saṃlayaḥ sannatiḥ / viṣādaḥ khedaḥ / vi[ṣā]dāpattiḥ khedapravāhaḥ / trāsodyama uttrāsaḥ / samagrastrāsaḥ saṃtrāsaḥ / tatpravāhaḥ saṃtrāsāpattiḥ / evaṃ ceti / avalayādyabhāve / yenetyādi / yadityanumodakaṃ cittam / kṣīṇamityuddeśaḥ / niruddhaṃ vinaṣṭatvāt / vigatamasthitatvāt / vipariṇataṃ taditi na kiñcinniḥsvabhāvatvāt /
body.translated_text: '<s>Upastabdha</s>' means made firm. '<s>Avalaya</s>' is the inclination of the mind. '<s>Saṃlaya</s>' is submission. '<s>Viṣāda</s>' is dejection. '<s>Viṣādāpatti</s>' is a continuous flow of dejection. '<s>Trāsodyama</s>' is alarm. 'Complete alarm' is '<s>saṃtrāsa</s>' (terror). Its continuous flow is '<s>saṃtrāsāpatti</s>' (the onset of terror). 'Thus' — in the absence of inclination and the rest. 'By which' and so forth. 'That which' means the mind of the one who rejoices. 'Destroyed' is the general statement. 'Ceased' — because of having perished. 'Gone' — because of not persisting. 'Transformed' — 'that is nothing' — because of being without self-nature.

body.text: samavadhānaṃ tulyakālatā / cittaṃ niruddhaṃ cittadharmatā śāśvatī cedāha / na cetyādi / tasyā asaṃskṛtatvena pariṇāmāyogāt / sugṛhītavacanaṃ durguhītasya supariṇāmitatvāyogāt / ārabhyetyadhikṛtya / kathamityāha / adhiṣṭhānaṃ praśnādhikaraṇaṃ kṛtveti / tatkatham? iha maitreyeti vacanāt / āmantrayate smeti brūte sma / iha maitreyetyata ārabhya kathaṃ saṃjñādiviparyāso na bhavatīti yāvat / evaṃ āryamaitreya uttaramāha / sa cedityādi / yena cittena yatpariṇāmayatīti yaccittaṃ pariṇāmayati / tasminnityubhyasmin / evamiti sugṛhītatvāt / pariṇāmitamiti supariṇāmitam / sphuṭīkarttumāha / yathetyādi / evamityādinopasaṃhāraḥ / kadā tarhi viparyāsaḥ syādityata āha / athetyādi / iyatā viparyāsaprasaṃge codyaṃ parihṛya prakṛtānupalambhakhyāpanāyāha / sa cedityādi / evaṃ sañjānīta ityuddeśaḥ / evaṃ samanvāharatīti nirdeśaḥ / aviparyāsena manasikarotītyarthaḥ / tadityādi / tat cittamevaṃ samanvāhriyamāṇamiti sambandhaḥ / kṣoṇamityādibhiḥ paryāyairmanasi karoti / na tacchakyamiti / asattvācchaśaviṣāṇavat / sava dharmateti niḥsvabhāvataiva / dharmeṣviti buddhadharmeṣu / sa ce dityādinopasaṃhāraḥ / evamityanupalambhena / sarvatra śūnyataikarasena manasikāreṇetyarthaḥ / itīdamāryamaitreyo 'tītān buddhānadhikṛtyoktavān / anāgatānadhikṛtyāha punaraparamityādi / pratyutpannānadhikṛtyāha punaraparamityādibhiḥ / anupalambhapariṇāmo dvitīyaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Simultaneous occurrence' is cotemporality. 'The mind has ceased' — if the nature of mind were eternal, he says: 'Not' and so forth. Because that [nature], being unconditioned, is incompatible with transformation. 'Well-grasped speech' — because what is poorly grasped is incompatible with being well-dedicated. 'Beginning with' means on the basis of. 'How?' — he says: 'The basis' means having made the question the subject. How then? Because of the statement 'here, O <s>Maitreya</s>.' 'He addresses' means 'he speaks.' 'Beginning from \"here, O <s>Maitreya</s>\"' — up to 'how is there no distortion of perception and so forth?' — this is the meaning. Thus <s>Āryamaitreya</s> gives the answer: 'If he' and so forth. 'By which mind he dedicates' means 'whatever mind dedicates.' 'In that' means in both. 'Thus' means because it is well-grasped. 'Dedicated' means well-dedicated. To make it clear, he says 'just as' and so forth. 'Thus' and so forth is the conclusion. 'When then would there be distortion?' — to this he says 'but if' and so forth. 'To this extent' — when there is the occasion for distortion. Having resolved the objection, to reveal the non-apprehension of the main subject, he says 'if he' and so forth. 'Thus perceives' is the general statement. 'Thus reflects upon' is the detailed exposition. The meaning is 'attends correctly.' 'That' and so forth. 'That mind, being thus reflected upon' — this is the connection. 'Attends to' — with the synonyms 'destroyed' and so forth. 'That cannot' — because of non-existence, like a hare's horn. 'With the very nature of <s>dharmas</s>' means with the very naturelessness. 'Among <s>dharmas</s>' means among the <s>Buddha</s>-qualities. 'If he' and so forth is the conclusion. 'Thus' means through non-apprehension. The meaning is 'with mental attention that is of one taste with emptiness throughout.' This was stated by <s>Āryamaitreya</s> with reference to past <s>Buddhas</s>. With reference to future [<s>Buddhas</s>], he says 'furthermore' and so forth. With reference to present [<s>Buddhas</s>], he says 'furthermore' and so forth. Thus [this is] the non-apprehension-dedication, the second.

body.text: punaraparamityādi / atra saṃkṣepeṇa tryaiyadhvikabuddhādīnāṃ puṇyānumodanā / agrāditvaṃ purvavat / atrāviparyāsaṃ darśayitumāha / tasya kathamityādi / evaṃ samanvāharatīti samanvāhāraḥ samyagmanasikāraḥ / te dharmā iti ye pariṇāmayitavyāḥ / sa ca dharmo 'kṣaya iti / anuttarā samyaksambodhiḥ suviśuddhadharmatālakṣaṇā / evaṃ pariṇāmitaṃ bhavatītyaviparyāsāditi bhāvaḥ / na dharmo dharma pariṇāmayatīti niḥsvabhāvatvāt sarvadharmāṇām / ityapīti / evamapi pūrvavat / ata evāha / evaṃ bhadantetyādi / sa cedityādinā prakārāntaramāha / ayamityādinopasaṃhāraḥ / ityaviparyāsapariṇāmastṛtīyaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore' and so forth. Here, in brief, is the rejoicing in the merit of <s>Buddhas</s> and others of the three times. 'Foremost' and so forth is as before. Here, to show the absence of distortion, he says 'how is that' and so forth. 'Thus reflects upon' — reflection is correct mental attention. 'Those <s>dharmas</s>' means those that are to be dedicated. 'And that <s>dharma</s> is inexhaustible' — <s>anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening), characterized by perfectly pure <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature of reality). 'Thus dedicated, it becomes' — because of the absence of distortion — this is the meaning. 'A <s>dharma</s> does not dedicate a <s>dharma</s>' — because of the naturelessness of all <s>dharmas</s>. 'Even this' — as before. Therefore he says 'thus, O venerable one' and so forth. 'If he' and so forth — he states another manner. 'This' and so forth is the conclusion. Thus [this is] the non-distortion-dedication, the third.

body.text: sa cedityādi / puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ puṇyakarma / saṃjñānamabhiniveśaḥ / kathaṃ tarhi pariṇāmayatītyāha / sa cedityādi / viviktaḥ śāntaśca yathākramaṃ svaparaiḥ svaparalakṣaṇaiśca śūnyatvāt / punaḥ sa cedityādinaitadāha / viviktaśāntatvajñānepi yadi tabhdāvābhiniveśaḥ syāt tadā na samyakpariṇāmayati / evamityādinopasaṃhāraḥ / prajñāpāramiteti vacanam / tayaiva samyakpariṇāmanāditi viviktapariṇāmaścaturthaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'If he' and so forth. '<s>Puṇyābhisaṃskāra</s>' is meritorious action. '<s>Saṃjñāna</s>' is grasping/attachment. 'How then does he dedicate?' — to this he says 'if he' and so forth. 'Detached' and 'peaceful' respectively because of being empty of self and of the characteristics of self and others. Again, 'if he' and so forth — he states this: even when knowing the detached and peaceful nature, if there is grasping at that [knowledge], then one does not dedicate correctly. 'Thus' and so forth is the conclusion. 'The word <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>' — because correct dedication is through that alone. Thus [this is] the detached-dedication, the fourth.

body.text: yadapītyādinā smaraṇam / yādṛśa evetyādinā nirūpaṇam / yādṛśa eva sa pariṇāma ityanuttarā samyaksaṃbodhirdharmadhatusvabhāvā tādṛśameva taditi labhyate nityābhisambandhāt / dharmadhātusvabhāvameva tadityarthaḥ / tādṛśameva tatkuśalamūlamiti yadanumodanāsahagatam / yenāpīti pariṇāmanācittena / tadapīti tadapyubhayam / tajjātikamiti saiva jātiḥ sāmānyaṃ yasya / tallakṣaṇamiti tadeva sāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ yasya / tannikāyamiti tadrāsi(śi)kam / tatsvabhāvamiti tatprakṛtikam / sa cedevaṃ saṃjānīta iti / yadyanenāpi tādṛśatvādinā tattvenābhiniviśate tadā na samyakpariṇāmayati /
body.translated_text: 'Whatever also' and so forth is the recollection. 'Of just such a nature' and so forth is the examination. 'Of just such a nature is that dedication' — that is, <s>anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi</s>, whose essential nature is the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of phenomena) — 'just such is that' is obtained, because of the perpetual connection. The meaning is: it is of the very nature of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>. 'Just such is that wholesome root' — that which is accompanied by rejoicing. 'By which also' — by the mind of dedication. 'That too' — that too, both [wholesome root and mind]. 'Of that class' means having that very universal characteristic as its class. 'Of that mark' means having that very universal characteristic as its mark. 'Of that group' means belonging to that same category. 'Of that nature' means being of that very essential nature. 'If he thus perceives' — if, through even such [attributes as] being 'of such a nature' and so forth, he grasps the reality, then he does not dedicate correctly.

body.text: yaccātītamityādinā aparaṃ tattvavikalpamāha / asaṃprāptamanutpannam / sthitirnāstīti prakṛtyaiva naśvaratvāt / tasmāt trayamapi nopalabhyate tato 'sat / tato naiva nimittamakāraṇatvāt / nākāraṇaṃ viṣayaḥ / sa cedityādi / evamiti kṣīṇatvādinā tattvena / nimittīkarotītyupalabhate / tadā na samanvāharati na samyagmanasikaroti / tadā na samyak pariṇāmayati /
body.translated_text: With 'whatever is past' and so forth, he states another examination of reality. 'Unattained' means unarisen. 'There is no persistence' — because of being perishable by its very nature. Therefore the three [times] also are not apprehended; hence they are non-existent. Therefore they are not even a cause, because of not being a basis. 'What is not a basis is not an object.' 'If he' and so forth. 'Thus' means through [the notion of] being destroyed and so forth, i.e., through reality. 'Conceptualizes' means apprehends. Then he does not reflect correctly, does not attend correctly. Then he does not dedicate correctly.

body.text: yadā tarhyanavabodhādasmaraṇādvā na nimittīkaroti tadā samyakpariṇāmaḥ syāditi cedāha / athetyādi / evamapīti / evamanimittīkaraṇepi na pariṇāmayati / pariṇāmanāmātrasyāpyabhāvāditi bhāvaḥ / kadā tarhi samyakpariṇāmitaṃ bhavatyata āha / athetyādi / ya(a)thaśabdo yadyarthaḥ / taditi tādṛśatvādikam / animittaṃ saviṣayatvañca / nimittamiti samyagjñānālambanam / samanvāharatīti samyagmanasikaroti / na ca nimittīkarotīti na sañjānāti nābhiniviśate / evamatretyādinopasaṃhāraḥ / evaṃ bauddhapuṇyaughasya yaḥ svabhāvo dharmatā tayā anusmaraṇam / anumodyādīnāmiti bauddhapuṇyaughasvabhāvānusmṛtipariṇāmaḥ pañcamaḥ //
