body.translated_text: If one objects that correct dedication would occur when, due to non-understanding or non-remembering, one does not conceptualize, he says 'but if' and so forth. 'Even thus' — even in such non-conceptualization, one does not [correctly] dedicate. Because even the mere act of dedication would be absent — this is the meaning. 'When then is it well-dedicated?' — to this he says 'but if' and so forth. The word 'just as' has the meaning of 'if.' 'That' means being 'of such nature' and the rest. 'Signless' together with 'having an object.' 'Sign' means the object of correct knowledge. 'Reflects upon' means attends correctly. 'And does not conceptualize' means does not perceive, does not grasp. 'In this matter, thus' and so forth is the conclusion. Thus, the recollection through the true nature (<s>dharmatā</s>) which is the essential nature of the flood of <s>Buddha</s>-merit. The dedication through the recollection of the essential nature of the flood of <s>Buddha</s>-merit is the fifth.

body.text: idaṃ tadityādi / ivamiti yadenadubha[yaṃ] tattvasya manasikāro na ca nimittīkaraṇam / tacchabdaḥ prasiddhau / upāyakauśalaṃ yatprasiddhamidaṃ tat / ya ityādinā anuśaṃsamāha / athāsmin upāyakauśale ka upāya ityata
body.translated_text: 'This is that' and so forth. 'Thus' means this [twofold approach]: mental attention toward reality and non-conceptualization. The word 'that' is in the sense of the well-known. '<s>Upāyakauśalya</s>' (skillful means) — what is well-known is this. With 'whoever' and so forth, he states the benefit. 'Now, in this skillful means, what is the method?' — to this

body.text: āha / atra cetyādi / iyameveti / sūtrātmikaiva / aśrutavateti imāmasyāṃ veti śeṣaḥ / prajñāpāramitāyā yā pariṇāmanā saiva puṇyakriyā / seyaṃ praveṣṭumavagāhituṃ na hi śakyeti sambandhaḥ / tatreti tathā sati / sa maivaṃ vocaditi syādvacanīya / kosāvityāha / ya ityādi / iti sopāyapariṇāmaḥ ṣaṣṭhaḥ //
body.translated_text: he says 'and herein' and so forth. 'This very one' — the one in the form of the <s>sūtra</s> itself. 'Of one who has not heard' — the supplement is 'of this, in this.' The dedication of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is itself the meritorious action. 'This cannot be entered, cannot be penetrated' — this is the syntactic connection. 'In that case' — that being so. 'He should not speak thus' — this should be the [proper] statement. 'Who is that one?' — he says 'whoever' and so forth. Thus [this is] the dedication-with-skillful-means, the sixth.

body.text: tatkasyetyādi / idaṃ taditi yaduktaṃ tatkuta ityarthaḥ / ātmabhāvāḥ kāyāḥ / saṃskāraḥ kuśalamūlāni / ataśca te śāntā viviktāḥ niḥsvabhāvā ityarthaḥ / ataśca virahitā upalabdhyā nopalabhyanta ityarthaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Then whose' and so forth. 'This is that' — what was stated, from whence? — this is the meaning. 'Essential natures' are bodies. '<s>Saṃskāra</s>' means wholesome roots. And therefore they are peaceful, detached, without self-nature — this is the meaning. And therefore, 'devoid of' — they are not apprehended through apprehension — this is the meaning.

body.text: api tviti / yadyapi nopalabhyante tathāpi yathābhūtamaviparītaṃ niruddhatvādikam / nimittīkṛtyetyudgrahataḥ / vikalpya cetyabhiniveśataḥ / ayathābhūte vikalpapratibhāse yathābhūtaniruddhādisaṃjñī / upalambhaṃ ātmīyaṃ anupalambhe samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmayet / tataḥ kimityāha / tasyetyādi / parinirvāṇamapīti / apiśabdo 'tiśayārthaḥ / tasyātyantaṃ nimittīkaraṇādyayogāt / saviṣaḥ saśalyaśca tāddharmyāt / ityanimittapariṇāmaḥ saptamaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'But however' — although they are not apprehended, still, what is in accordance with reality, without distortion — 'destroyed' and so forth. 'Having conceptualized' — from the point of view of grasping. 'And having discriminated' — from the point of view of attachment. [That is:] with the perception of 'destroyed' and so forth that accords with reality, [applied to] the unreal appearance of conceptualization — one should dedicate one's own apprehension toward non-apprehension, toward <s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (perfect awakening). 'Then what?' — he says 'of that' and so forth. 'Even <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final cessation)' — the word 'even' is in the sense of extreme. Because for that [person], due to the complete impossibility of conceptualization and the rest. 'Poisonous' and 'thorny' — because of the conformity [with the analogy]. Thus [this is] the signless-dedication, the seventh.

body.text: tadyathāpītyādi / praṇītaṃ varṇādiprakarṣāt / kiṃ cāpīti yadyapītyarthaḥ / api tviti tathāpītyarthaḥ / khalu punariti vākyālaṃkāro manyeteti varṇādilābhāt / svādanaṃ svādaḥ paribhogaḥ / pariṇāme ceti avasāne ca / vipākaphalam / durgahīteneti mithyāśrutena / durupa [la]kṣiteneti durvitarkitena / duḥsvādhyāteneti durabhyāsena / subhāṣitam / iti karaṇasamāptyarthaḥ / evaṃ sa iti yoyamuktaḥ / saviṣatvāditi / anarthakaraṇaśaktiratra viṣam / tasmād ityupasaṃhāraḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Just as, for example' and so forth. 'Excellent' — because of the superiority of color and the like. 'Even though' means although. 'But still' means nevertheless. The sentence-ornament '<s>khalu punar</s>' (indeed, moreover) — 'one would think' — because of obtaining color and the like. 'Tasting' is '<s>svāda</s>' (flavor), enjoyment. 'And in transformation' means and at the end. 'The fruit of ripening.' 'By one who has poorly grasped' means by one who has wrongly heard. 'By one who has poorly examined' means by one who has wrongly reasoned. 'By one who has poorly studied' means by one who has wrongly practiced. 'Well-spoken.' 'Thus' has the meaning of the completion of the illustration. 'Thus he' means the one just described. 'Because of being poisonous' and so forth. The capacity to cause harm is here the 'poison.' 'Therefore' is the conclusion.

body.text: kathamityādinā praśnāḥ / ihetyādikamuttaram / abhyākhyānaṃ nindā / abhūtavāditayā khyāpanāt / parigrahītavyādipadeṣu parigraheṇānumodanā lakṣyate / nāntarīyakatvāt / buddhajñānena jñā(jā)nanti buddhacakṣuṣā paśyantīti sambandhaḥ / evaṃ cāsyetyupasaṃhāraḥ / nirviṣatvādikaṃ sarva kuta ityāha adhyāśayenetyādi / iti buddhānujñātapariṇāmo 'ṣṭamaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'How' and so forth are the questions. 'Here' and so forth is the answer. '<s>Abhyākhyāna</s>' (false accusation) is slander. Because of proclaiming through false speech. In the words 'should be accepted' and so forth, acceptance implies rejoicing, because of their inseparability. 'They know with <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, they see with <s>Buddha</s>-vision' — this is the syntactic connection. 'And thus of this one' — this is the conclusion. 'All [qualities such as] being non-poisonous' — whence are they? — he says 'through [pure] intention' and so forth. Thus [this is] the <s>Buddha</s>-authorized dedication, the eighth.

body.text: punaraparamityādi / śīlādīti tathāgataḥ śīlādiskandhaḥ / aparyāpannamanantarbhūtaṃ / tryadhvatraidhātukāparyāpannatvāditi / adhvatraye dhātutraye cānantargatatvādityarthaḥ / dharmadhātumātratvāt teṣāṃ śīlādīnāmiti bhāvaḥ / pariṇāmopīti pariṇāmanāpi / yatrāpi dharma iti samyaksambodhau / avinaṣṭa ityaduṣṭa / aparyāpannaḥ / buddhānujñātapariṇāmayordharmadhātupariṇāmatvena samatāṃ
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore' and so forth. 'Morality and so on' — the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s aggregate of morality and so forth. 'Not included' means not comprised [in conditioned phenomena]. Because of not being included in the three times or the three realms — this is the meaning. Because those [aggregates] of morality and the rest are merely of the nature of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of phenomena) — this is the meaning. 'Even the dedication' means even the act of dedicating. 'In which <s>dharma</s>' means toward <s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (perfect awakening). 'Uncorrupted' means undefiled. 'Not included.' The sameness of the <s>Buddha</s>-authorized dedication and the <s>dharmadhātu</s>-dedication in being dedications [rooted in] the <s>dharmadhātu</s>

body.text: darśayitumāha / tatretyādi / atra dvitīyādiśabdātpareṇa vārtho gamyate / yoyaṃ dharmadhātupariṇāmanayā pariṇāmaḥ / ayaṃ samyakpariṇāma iti sambandhaḥ / katamayetyāha / anayetyanantaroktayā / aparyāpannapariṇāmanayetyarthaḥ / yathā buddhā bhagavanta ityādikayā buddhānujñātapariṇāmanayevetyarthaḥ / evaṃ cetyupasaṃhāraḥ / itya paryāpannapariṇāmo navamaḥ /
body.translated_text: He states [the verse beginning with] 'tatra' etc. to demonstrate [this]. Here, from the word 'second etc.' the meaning is understood through what follows. This transformation that is by way of the transformation of <s>dharmadhātu</s> (the realm of phenomena) — this is the correct transformation: such is the connection. To [the question] 'which one?' he says: 'by this' means by the one just stated. The meaning is: by the transformation that is <s>aparyāpanna</s> (unrestricted). 'Just as the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavats</s>' etc. — the meaning is: by the transformation approved by the <s>Buddhas</s>, as indicated by that [passage]. 'Thus' is the conclusion. This is the ninth [transformation], the <s>aparyāpanna-pariṇāma</s> (unrestricted transformation).

body.text: atha khalvityādi / yo hyayamiti yohyaparyāpannākhyaḥ / asyāmevetyādinā pariṇāmayatītyetatparyantena buddhānujñātapariṇāmasya nirdeśaḥ / atretyanayordharmadhatupariṇāmanayoḥ / agrāditvaṃ pramu[di]tādyekādaśabhūmigataprakarṣahetutvāt / śeṣaṃ subodham / yāvatpañcānāmabhijñānāṃ lābhino bhaveyuriti / ihokte mahāpuṇyodaye yacchaddhādikaṃ sa pūrvakādviśeṣaheturiti mṛdurmahāpuṇyodayapariṇāmo daśamaḥ //
body.translated_text: [He explains] 'atha khalu' etc. 'yo hyayam' means the one called <s>aparyāpanna</s> (unrestricted). From 'asyām eva' etc. up to 'pariṇāmayati' is the exposition of the transformation approved by the <s>Buddhas</s>. 'Here' [refers to] these two: the transformation of <s>dharmadhātu</s> (the realm of phenomena). The quality of being foremost is because it is the cause of excellence pertaining to the eleven <s>bhūmis</s> (stages) beginning with <s>Pramuditā</s> (the Joyful). The rest is easy to understand, up to 'may they become possessors of the five <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges).' In the great arising of merit spoken of here, the faith and so forth is a distinguishing cause superior to the previous one — thus the tenth [transformation] is the mild great-merit-arising transformation.

body.text: tiṣṭhatvityādi subodhaṃ yāvatpratyekabuddhā bhaveyuriti / ihoktapuṇyātireke śraddhādikaṃ pūrvakādviśeṣaheturiti madhyo mahāpuṇyodayapariṇāma ekādaśaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Let it be' etc. is easy to understand, up to 'may they become <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones).' When faith and so forth, in the surplus of merit spoken of here, is a distinguishing cause superior to the previous one — thus the eleventh is the middling great-merit-arising transformation.

body.text: tiṣṭhatvityādi / ye subhūta ityādinā dadyurityetadantenoddeśaḥ / etena paryāyeṇetyādinā dadyurityetadantena nirdeśaḥ / eteneti vakṣyamāṇena / glānaṃ glāniḥ / tatpratyayāni taddhetukāni bhaiṣajyāni / pariṣkārāḥ pariśrāvaṇādayaḥ / sukhahetavaḥ sukhāḥ / teṣāṃ upadhānaiḥ ḍhokanaiḥ / sukhasparśaḥ sukhānubhavaḥ / tena ye vihārāḥ caṃkramādayaḥ / tān sarvasattvānekakaṃ parikalpyeti / upastheyatvena pṛthagavasthāpya / tāṃśca sarvabodhisattvāniti / ekaikaṃ parikalpyeti vartate / upasthāpakatvena pṛthagavasthāpya / ekaṃko bodhisattva iti / upatiṣṭhaditi sambandhaḥ / kimupatiṣṭhet? prakṛtatvāttāneva sarvasattvān / ekaṃkasteṣāṃ sarvabodhisattvānāmiti nirdhāraṇe ṣaṣṭhī / teṣāṃ madhye ekaikaḥ dānaṃ dadyāditi / tebhya eva sarvasattvebhyaḥ / tāvaccirarātrasañcitamiti / tāvatā dīrghakālena sañcitam / tathā mahāvistarasamudānītamiti / tāvanmahāvistareṇotpāditam / tiṣṭhatu khalu punarityādi / pūrvatra gaṃgānadībālukopamalokadhātuvīryāḥ sarvabodhisattvā upasthāpakāḥ pratyekaṃ gaṃgānadībālukopamalokadhātuvīryānāṃ sattvānām / tatra yāvanta upastheyāḥ sattvā iha tāvanta upasthāpakā bodhisattvāḥ pratyekaṃ gaṅgānadīvālukopamā lokadhātuvīryānāṃ sattvānāmiti viśeṣaḥ / tānsarvasattvān
body.translated_text: 'Let it be' etc. From '<s>ye Subhūti</s>' etc. up to 'may give' is the outline. From 'by this method' etc. up to 'may give' is the exposition. 'By this' means by the one to be stated. <s>Glāna</s> means illness. 'Pertaining to that' means medicines caused by that. <s>Pariṣkāras</s> (accessories) are strainers and the like. 'Causes of comfort' means comfortable. 'With their provisions' means with cushions. 'Comfortable touch' means the experience of comfort. 'By that, whatever dwelling places' means promenades and the like. 'Having individually designated all those beings' means having separately established them as those to be served. 'And all those <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' — 'having individually designated' is to be supplied — having separately established them as those who serve. 'Each <s>Bodhisattva</s>' — 'would serve' is the syntactic connection. What would he serve? Because it is the topic at hand, those very beings. 'Each of those, of all the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' — the genitive is used in the partitive sense. Among them, each one would give <s>dāna</s> (gifts) — to those very beings. 'Accumulated over such a long time' means accumulated over that long period. Likewise 'brought together with great abundance' means produced with that great abundance. 'Let it be, moreover' etc. Previously, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> equal in number to the sand-grains of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river world-realms were the servers, each for beings of world-realms equal to the sand-grains of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river. There, as many as were the beings to be served, here that many <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are the servers, each for beings of world-realms equal to the sand-grains of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river — this is the distinction. All those beings

body.text: ekaikaṃ parikalpitāṃśca sarvabodhisattvāniti pūrvavat / śeṣaṃ subodham / ityadhimātro mahāpuṇyodayapariṇāmo dvādaśaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'having individually designated, and all the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' — as before. The rest is easy to understand. Thus the twelfth is the intense great-merit-arising transformation.

body.text: samāptaśca pariṇāmanāmanaskāraḥ //
body.translated_text: The <s>pariṇāmanā-manaskāra</s> (mental engagement of dedication) is completed.

body.text: anumodanāmanaskāro vaktavyaḥ / tamadhikṛtya śāstram-
body.translated_text: The <s>anumodanā-manaskāra</s> (mental engagement of rejoicing) is to be explained. With regard to that, the treatise [states]:

children.translated_text: Rejoicing in roots of virtue through <s>upāya</s> (skillful means) and <s>anupalambha</s> (non-apprehension),
The cultivation of the mental engagement of rejoicing is prescribed here. // 2-24 //

body.text: etadāha / atha khalvāyuṣmānityādinā / niravaśeṣyeti niravaśeṣīkṛtya / agratvādīni caturdaśoktāḥ / kiyatā agratā bhavatīti praśnaḥ / iyatā bhavatītyuttaram / kotrābhiprāyaḥ? agratvameva daśadigmadhyatryadhvakuśalālambanatvāccaturdaśavidhaṃ bhavatīti / yatra tarhi trayodaśapadāni tatrāpi daśadiktryadhvabhedāt trayodaśavidham / tatra kathaṃ madhyamalokadhātoḥ saṃgrahaḥ? tanmadhye sūkṣmamavadhiṃ kṛtvā diśāṃ grahaṇāt / lokadhātvekadeśeṣvapi lokadhātuvyapadeśāt / tadyathā aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānāmatyayāt prasūteti / yadā hi triṃśadrātrā māsāstadāṣṭau / yadā māsaikadeśopi māsastadā nava / na gṛṇhīte grāhyatvenāpratibhāsāt / na manyate vastutvenāpratibhāsāt / nopalabhate svarūpato apratibhāsāt / na kalpayati sāmānyalakṣaṇena / na vikalpayati viśeṣalakṣaṇaiḥ / na paśyati dṛṣṭyā anabhiniveśāt / na samanupaśyati santatamanabhiniveśāt / kalpanā abhūtaparikalpaḥ / tathā viṭhapitāḥ saṃdarśitāḥ / ajātā nirbījatvāt / anirjātā aniṣpatteḥ / anāgatikā anāgatādadhvanaḥpūrvalokādvā / agatikā atītādhvani paraloke vā / evaṃ yāvat nāpi nirudhyata iti / niḥsvabhāvatvātparikalpatatvādveti hetuḥ / evamiti parikalpitena svabhāvena / itthaṃ bhūtān etān dharmāniti paratantrarūpān kuśalān / dharmateti bālabuddhigocaraiḥ svabhāvaiḥ śūnyatā / anumodanādhikārepi tathā anumodya tathaiva pariṇāmayatīti vacanamavaśyapariṇāmanīyatvāt / śeṣaṃ vyākhyatameva yāvat na kṣamata iti / ityanupalambhānumodanā prathamā //
body.translated_text: This he states [beginning with] 'atha khalv āyuṣmān' etc. 'Without remainder' means having made exhaustive. The fourteen qualities beginning with 'foremost' are stated. The question is 'to what extent is there foremost quality?' The answer is 'to this extent.' What is the intention? That the foremost quality itself becomes fourteen-fold because it takes as its object the virtuous [deeds] of the ten directions, the middle [realm], and the three times. Where then there are thirteen terms, there too it is thirteen-fold due to the distinction of the ten directions and the three times. How then is the middle world-realm included? By making a subtle boundary within it and grasping the directions. Because even parts of world-realms are designated as world-realms. Just as [it is said]: 'after the passage of eight or nine months, she gives birth' — for when months are thirty nights, there are eight; when even a part of a month counts as a month, there are nine. 'Does not grasp' — because it does not appear as something to be grasped. 'Does not conceive' — because it does not appear as a real entity. 'Does not apprehend' — because it does not appear in its own nature. 'Does not conceptualize' — by general characteristics. 'Does not discriminate' — by particular characteristics. 'Does not see' — because of non-attachment through view. 'Does not regard' — because of continuous non-attachment. <s>Kalpanā</s> (conceptual construction) is <s>abhūtaparikalpa</s> (false imagination). 'Thus displayed' means shown. 'Unborn' because of being without seed. 'Not arisen' because of non-production. 'Without coming' — from the future time, or from the prior world. 'Without going' — in the past time, or in the other world. Thus up to 'nor does it cease.' The reason is: because of being without own-nature and because of being imagined. 'Thus' means by the imagined own-nature. 'These <s>dharmas</s> being of such nature' means the virtuous ones that are of <s>paratantra</s> (dependent) nature. '<s>Dharmatā</s>' means emptiness of the own-natures that are the objects of the understanding of the immature. Even in the context of rejoicing, one similarly rejoices and similarly dedicates — this statement is because dedication is necessarily required. The rest has already been explained, up to 'is not able.' Thus the first is the rejoicing through <s>anupalambha</s> (non-apprehension).

body.text: punaraparamityādi / vimuktirnirvāṇam / tacca dharmadhātoḥ sarvāvaraṇaviśuddhitā paramārthatastathaiva sarvaṃ dānādītyarthaḥ / saṅgastṛṣṇā / tadabhāvād
body.translated_text: Again, 'punar aparam' etc. <s>Vimukti</s> (liberation) is <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. And that is the complete purification from all obstructions of <s>dharmadhātu</s> (the realm of phenomena); in the ultimate sense, everything — giving and so forth — is just so, this is the meaning. <s>Saṅga</s> (attachment) is <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving). Due to its absence

body.text: asaktānāṃ tṛṣṇāhetukasya janmano 'bhāvād abaddhānām / tato amuktānām / apariṇāmanāyoge tasyāpyanupalambhāt / sa kathamityāha / asaṃkrāntito avināśata iti / tathāhyavasthāntarasaṃkrāntiḥ pariṇāmaḥ pūrvavināśāparotpattī vā / na ca dharmadhātoravasthā / na ca saṃkramo nāpi vināśa iti /
body.translated_text: of those who are unattached — because of the absence of birth caused by craving — they are unbound. Therefore they are unreleased. Regarding the impossibility of dedication, because even that is non-apprehended — to [the question] 'how then?' he says: 'without transference, without destruction.' For indeed, transformation is either transference to another state, or the destruction of the prior and the arising of the subsequent. But there is no [change of] state of <s>dharmadhātu</s> (the realm of phenomena), nor transference, nor destruction.

body.text: samādāyoti gācarataḥ (?) sāvadhikamādāya / ākruṣṭaḥ śaptaḥ / abhihatastāḍitaḥ / paribhāṣito bhūtābhūtadoṣasthānaiḥ / samān iti sannityarthaḥ / styānaṃ ca middhaṃ ca tenābhibhūtā iti sambandhaḥ / tatra styānaṃ cittasyākarmaṇyatā staimityam / staimityalakṣaṇā yā cittasyākarmaṇyatā svālambanapratītaye tat khalu styānam / middhamasvatantravṛttiścetaso 'bhisaṃkṣepaḥ / cetaso 'bhisaṃkṣepaścakṣurādīndriyadvāreṇāpravṛtiḥ / sa cedasvādhīnā / cetaso vṛttistanmiddham / śeṣaṃ subodhamāparivartasamāpteḥ / upāyo vimuktisādṛśyam / teneyaṃ dharmadhātoranumodanānupalambhenetyupāyānumodanā dvitīyā //
body.translated_text: '<s>Samādāya</s>' means taking up from conduct (?), taking up with surplus. '<s>Ākruṣṭa</s>' means reviled. '<s>Abhihata</s>' means struck. '<s>Paribhāṣita</s>' means reproached with true and untrue faults. 'Equal' means peaceful, this is the meaning. <s>Styāna</s> (sluggishness) and <s>middha</s> (torpor) — 'overcome by them' is the syntactic connection. Among these, <s>styāna</s> is the unfitness for work of the mind, rigidity. That unfitness for work of the mind which has the characteristic of rigidity, for the cognition of its own object — that indeed is <s>styāna</s>. <s>Middha</s> (torpor) is the contraction of mind with involuntary functioning. The contraction of mind is non-engagement through the doors of the eye and other sense faculties. And that which is involuntary — that functioning of mind is <s>middha</s>. The rest is easy to understand up to the completion of the chapter. <s>Upāya</s> (skillful means) is similarity to liberation. By that, this rejoicing in <s>dharmadhātu</s> through non-apprehension is the second rejoicing through skillful means.

body.text: anumodanā ca pariṇāmanā ca tasyāḥ / tayorabhidhāyakaḥ parivarto anumodanāpariṇāmanāparivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: Rejoicing and dedication — of that [chapter]. The chapter that expounds both of them is the <s>anumodanā-pariṇāmanā-parivarta</s> (chapter on rejoicing and dedication).

body.text: āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ sāratamānāmni pañjikāyāṃ ratnākāraśāntiviracitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhaḥ parivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: The sixth chapter in the <s>Sāratamā</s> (Most Essential) commentary composed by <s>Ratnākaraśānti</s> on the noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom in Eight Thousand Lines).

body.text: 7. nirayaparivarto nāma saptamaḥ
body.translated_text: 7. The seventh chapter, named the <s>niraya-parivarta</s> (chapter on bringing forth).

body.text: laukiko bhāvanāmārgastrayo manaskārāḥ / taduktaḥ / lokottarastu bhāvanāmārgo 'nirhāraḥ śuddhiratyantaṃ' iti pūrvamuddiṣṭaḥ / tatra nirhāramadhikṛtya śāstram-
body.translated_text: The mundane path of cultivation has three mental engagements. That has been stated. But the supramundane path of cultivation — '<s>nirhāra</s> (bringing forth), purification, and the ultimate' — has been outlined previously. With regard to <s>nirhāra</s> (bringing forth), the treatise [states]:

children.translated_text: The own-nature and the excellence of that [path], the non-conditioning of everything,
The dedication of <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) through non-apprehension, and the great purposefulness. // 2-25 //

body.text: pañcāṅgāni nirhārasya / 'tasya' iti bhāvanāmārgasya prajñāpāramitāviśeṣasya 'svabhāvaḥ' sarvajñajñānapariniṣpādakatvādidharmacakrapravartakatvaparyantaḥ / 'śreṣṭhatā' ṣaṭ pāramitāsu / abhinirhāraḥ sarvadharmāṇāṃ 'anabhisaṃskāraḥ' / anupalambhena sarvadharmānarpayatīti 'arpaṇā' / sarvadharmānupalambhenaiva bodheḥ prāpaṇāt 'mahārthatā' iti / ata āha / atha khalvityādi / asya hi bhāvanāmārgasya svabhāvaḥ prajñāpāramitā / kīdṛśītyāha / sarvajñajñānasya
body.translated_text: There are five limbs of <s>nirhāra</s> (bringing forth). 'Of that' means of the path of cultivation, the special <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom). 'Own-nature' extends from the accomplishment of <s>sarvajña-jñāna</s> (omniscient knowledge) up to the turning of the <s>dharmacakra</s> (wheel of the teaching). 'Excellence' is in the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections). The bringing forth is the '<s>anabhisaṃskāra</s>' (non-conditioning) of all <s>dharmas</s>. 'Dedication' means that one dedicates all <s>dharmas</s> through non-apprehension. Because <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) is attained through the very non-apprehension of all <s>dharmas</s>, there is 'great purposefulness.' Therefore he says 'atha khalu' etc. For the own-nature of this path of cultivation is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. To [the question] 'of what kind?' he says: the accomplishment of <s>sarvajña-jñāna</s> (omniscient knowledge)

body.text: pariniṣpattiḥ yataḥ sā tathoktā / sarvajñatvamiti sarvāvaraṇavāsanānusandhiprahīṇaṃ jñānam / prahāṇasampatsahitā jñānasampadityarthaḥ / tadapi sarvajñatvameva / atropapattiravabhāsakaroti / sarvāvaraṇatamaḥprahāṇamavabhāsaḥ / tatkareti prahāṇasampat / sarvadharmaparamārthapratibhāso vā avabhāsaḥ / tatkareti jñānasampat / ataścaināṃ namaskaromi sāṃpratam / namaskaraṇīyeti / āyatyāṃ pratikṣaṇam / ekena padena dve sampadāvukte / idānīṃ padadvayena prahāṇamāha / anupalipteti sarvāvaraṇamalakṣayāt / sarvalokanirupalepeti triadhātukamalakṣayāt / idānīṃ padatrayeṇa jñānamāha / sarvadharmaparamārthapratibhāsa ālokaḥ / tatkarā / atra dvau hetū padadvayenāha / timiramajñānam / tadviparyayo vitimiraṃ jñānamityarthaḥ / sarva samagraṃ traidhātuka traidhātukaparamārthaḥ / tasminvitimiram / tatkarā / ityālambanavyāptiḥ / kleśāśca dṛṣṭayaśca tā evāndhakārāḥ / sarve ca te te ca teṣāṃ apanetrīti sarvavipakṣakṣayaḥ / iyatā sarveṇa svārthasampattiruktā / parārthasampattimadhikṛtyāha / āśrayaṇīyetyādi / āśrayaṇīyā sarvapadaprepsubhiḥ / agrāṇi padāni strota āpattiḥ sakṛdāgāmitvaṃ yāvatpratyekabodhiḥ / tatkarā / teṣāmupāyaḥ saptatriṃśad bodhipakṣyāḥ / teṣāṃ kṣamakarī vighnaharaṇāt / yāvanna lokottarajñānaṃ tāvad andhāḥ / teṣāṃ tadutpādanād ālokakarī / sarvabhayopadravaiḥ prahīṇa āloko lokottara eva bhāvanāmārgaḥ / tatkarā / iyatā hīnayānikānāmartha uktaḥ /
body.translated_text: is its perfection, and because of that it is so called. <s>Sarvajñatva</s> (omniscience) is knowledge in which the traces and connections of all obstructions have been abandoned. The meaning is: the perfection of knowledge together with the perfection of abandonment — that too is <s>sarvajñatva</s> (omniscience) itself. Here the proof illuminates. The abandonment of the darkness of all obstructions is the illumination. 'That which makes it' is the perfection of abandonment. Or, the manifestation of the ultimate nature of all <s>dharmas</s> is the illumination. 'That which makes it' is the perfection of knowledge. Therefore 'I pay homage to it now.' Because it is worthy of homage. In the future, at every moment. By one phrase, two perfections are stated. Now by two phrases he states abandonment. 'Unstained' — because of the destruction of the defilements of all obstructions. 'Free from the impurities of all worlds' — because of the destruction of the defilements of the three realms. Now by three phrases he states knowledge. The illumination of the ultimate nature of all <s>dharmas</s> is the light. That which makes it [so]. Here two reasons are stated by two phrases. <s>Timira</s> (darkness) is ignorance. The opposite of that, <s>vitimira</s> (free from darkness), means knowledge. 'All' means the complete three realms; the ultimate nature of the three realms — in that, free from darkness. That which makes it [so]. Thus is the scope of the object [of knowledge]. <s>Kleśas</s> (afflictions) and <s>dṛṣṭis</s> (views) — they themselves are the darkness. 'And all of them, and of them, the remover' — this means the destruction of all adversaries. To this extent, the accomplishment of one's own purpose is stated. With regard to the accomplishment of others' purpose, he says '<s>āśrayaṇīyā</s>' (worthy of reliance) etc. Worthy of reliance by all who seek the [various] stages. The foremost stages are stream-entry, once-returning, up to solitary awakening. That which makes [them possible]. The means for those are the thirty-seven <s>bodhipakṣya</s> (factors of awakening). That which creates forbearance for them, by removing obstacles. As long as there is no supramundane knowledge, so long they are blind. By producing that [knowledge] for them, it creates light. The light from which all fears and calamities have been removed is the supramundane path of cultivation itself. That which makes it [so]. To this extent, the purpose for those of the lesser vehicles is stated.

body.text: bodhisattvārthamadhikṛtyāha / pañcacakṣurityādi / te hi parārthapradhānāḥ / tasya saiva sādhanamālambanabhedena pañcacakṣuḥparivārā / abhedena saiva cakṣu sarvadharmaparamārthadarśanāt / vyāpino darśanasya trayo vibandhāḥ / mohatamaritamirāṇi / tatra moho ajñānam / tamondhakāram / timiraṃ cakṣurogaḥ / teṣāṃ vikaraṇī vidhvaṃsanī / saṃkṣepato vitimirakaraṇī timirasāmānyāt / kimutpādayatītyata āha / sarvadharmāṇāmakaraṇīti / sarvadharmāḥ skandhadhātvāyatanāni / teṣāṃ trayaḥ svabhāvāḥ / kalpitaḥ paratantraḥ pariniṣpannaśca / tatra kalpitaṃ na karoti tasya yathālakṣaṇamasattvāt / paratantro abhūtaparikalpaḥ / tatra karoti tatpratipakṣatvāt / pariniṣpanno dharmadhātuḥ / tamapi na karotyanādinidhanatvāt / samyagjñānaṃ karotīti cet? na / anādinidhanacittasantānabhrāntinivṛtyaiva samyagjñānasiddhe / kiṃ tarhi karotītyata āha / utpathetyādi / utpatho dharmāṇāṃ parikalpanā tena prayātānām / mārge dharmanairātmyajñāne avatāraṇī / kasya mārge? sarvajñatāyāḥ / iyatā sarvajñajñānapariniṣpattiriti yaduktaṃ tatparārthepi darśitam / yaduktaṃ sarvajñatvamiti tatparārthepyāha / sarvajñataivetyādinā / yadā hi vāsanānusandhiprahīṇatā tasyāstadāsau sarvajñatetyarthaḥ / sā tarhi prajñāpāramitā utpādikā
body.translated_text: With regard to the benefit of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, he says "five eyes" and so on. For they are primarily devoted to the benefit of others. The very means of accomplishing that, differentiated by its objects, is the retinue of the five eyes. Without differentiation, that itself is the eye, because it sees the ultimate reality of all <s>dharmas</s>. There are three obstructions to pervasive vision: delusion (<s>moha</s>), darkness (<s>tamas</s>), and impairment (<s>timira</s>). Among these, delusion is ignorance. Darkness is obscurity. Impairment is a disease of the eye. The "remover" (<s>vikaraṇī</s>) of these is their destroyer. In brief, "the one that removes impairment" (<s>vitimirakaraṇī</s>), because impairment is the general [term]. "What does it produce?" — to this he says: "the non-producer of all <s>dharmas</s>." "All <s>dharmas</s>" are the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases). These have three natures (<s>svabhāvas</s>): the imagined (<s>kalpita</s>), the other-dependent (<s>paratantra</s>), and the perfected (<s>pariniṣpanna</s>). Among these, it does not produce the imagined, because that does not exist according to its own characteristic. The other-dependent is false construction (<s>abhūtaparikalpa</s>); it does act upon that, because it is its antidote. The perfected is the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of phenomena); it does not produce that either, because it is without beginning or end. If [one objects:] "It produces right knowledge" — no, because right knowledge is established simply through the cessation of error in the beginningless and endless mind-continuum. "What then does it do?" — to this he says, "the wrong path" and so on. "The wrong path" (<s>utpatha</s>) is the conceptual construction of <s>dharmas</s>; for those who have gone by that [path], it is "the one that leads onto the [right] path" — [the path being] the knowledge of the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s>. "Onto the path of what?" Of <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience). Thus, what was stated [earlier] — "the completion of omniscient knowledge" — that has been shown also for the benefit of others. What was stated as "omniscience" — that too he states for the benefit of others, beginning with "omniscience itself" and so on. For when the continuity of latent impressions (<s>vāsanānusandhi</s>) of that [<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>] is exhausted, then that is <s>sarvajñatā</s> — this is the meaning. "Then is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> a producer"

body.text: nirodhikā utpannā niruddhā ca / netyāha / anutpādiketyādi / anutpādikā sarvadharmāṇāmiti vaiyavadānikānām / anirodhikā sarvadharmāṇāmiti sāṃkleśikānām / anutpannāniruddheti svayam / paramārthato yathāpratibhāsaṃ ceti bhāvaḥ / paramārtho hyeṣāṃ dharmadhātuḥ / tenaiṣāmanādinidhanatvādvālapratibhāsinā rūpeṇātyanta- / samatvānnaiṣāmutpādanirodhau / ata evāha / svalakṣaṇaśūnyatāyāmupādāyeti pratītyasamutpannaṃ punareṣāṃ tṛtīyaṃ svabhāvamupādāyāha / mātetyādi / mātā jananī / kutaḥ? sarvabuddhadharmā eva ratnāni teṣāṃ dātrītvāt / tānyeva hi samagrāṇi hetvavasthāni bodhisatvānāṃ śarīram tata iyaṃ taddānātteṣāṃ jananī / buddhagrahaṇābduddhajananītvamarthādgamyate / na punastāvatā buddhānāmatiśayo gamyate / ato viśiṣṭairguṇaiḥ punastadāha daśabaletyādinā /
body.translated_text: "a destroyer, arisen, and ceased?" No, he says: "non-producing" and so on. "Non-producing of all <s>dharmas</s>" means of those pertaining to purification (<s>vaiyavadānika</s>). "Non-destroying of all <s>dharmas</s>" means of those pertaining to defilement (<s>sāṃkleśika</s>). "Unarisen, unceased" — [this applies] to itself. Ultimately, and according to appearance — this is the import. For the ultimate reality of these is the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of phenomena). Therefore, because they are without beginning or end, and because of their absolute equality in the form of hair-like appearances, there is no arising or ceasing of these. Hence he says: "with reference to emptiness of own-characteristic" — and taking their third nature, the dependently arisen (<s>pratītyasamutpanna</s>), he says: "mother" and so on. "Mother" (<s>mātā</s>) is the one who gives birth. "From what?" Because the very <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> are jewels, and she is their bestower. For these very [<s>dharmas</s>], when complete, in their causal state, are the body of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>; therefore, through bestowing those, she is their mother. From the word "<s>Buddha</s>," the quality of being the mother of <s>Buddhas</s> is understood by implication. But the supremacy of the <s>Buddhas</s> is not thereby understood. Therefore, to state it through distinguished qualities, he says again, beginning with "the ten powers" and so on.

body.text: daśa tathāgatabalāni / tatkarā / katamāni daśa? "sthānāsthānajñānabalam / karmavipākajñānabalam / nānādhātujñānabalam / nānādhimuktijñānabalam / indriyaparāparajñānabalam / sarvatragāminīpratipajjñānabalam / dhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattisaṃkleśavyavadānavyutthānajñānabalam / pūrvenivāsānusmṛtijñānabalam / cyutopapādajñānabalam / āśravakṣayajñānabalaṃ ca" iti / lakṣaṇameṣāṃ yathoktaṃ mahatyo rbhagavatyoḥ / tatra sambhavāsambhavau sthānāsthāne / tadyathā duścaritānāmaniṣṭo vipāka [:] sthānamiṣṭo 'sthānamiti / karma ca vipākaśca / nānādhātuḥ puṇyāpuṇyādijanako 'dhyāśayaḥ / nānādhimuktistadyathā rāgadveṣādau sthitānāṃ dveṣarāgādau ruciḥ / indriyāṇi śraddhāvīryasmṛtisamādhiprajñāḥ / teṣāṃ parāparatvaṃ vimātratā / ayaṃ mṛdvindriyo 'yaṃ madhyendriya ityādi / sarvatragāminīpratipat / rāgasya pratipakṣa iyaṃ pratipat / iyaṃ dveṣasyetyādi / caturṇā dhyānānāṃ aṣṭānāṃ vimokṣāṇāṃ trayāṇāṃ samādhīnāṃ savitarkasavicārādīnāṃ catasṛṇāmārūpyasamāpattīnāṃ navānāṃ cānupūrvavihārasamāpattīnām saṃkleśādikam / tatra saṃkleśa āsvādanādinā / vyavadānamanupalambhādinā / vyutthānaṃ siṃhavijṛmbhitena vā avaskandakena vā / pūrve nivāsaḥ pūrvajanma / tasminnanusmṛtiḥ smaraṇam / cyu[tyu]papādau sattvānāṃ maraṇotpattī / āśravāḥ kleśāsteṣāṃ yaḥ kṣayo yena ca mārgeṇa kṣayastadubhayamāśravakṣayaḥ / sattvānām / eṣāṃ sthānāsthānādīnāṃ sarvathā sarvadā samyagjñānaṃ tadiha sthānāsthānādijñānam / tadeva balamitarairaghṛṣyatvāt, teṣāṃ vābhibhavanāt /
body.translated_text: The ten powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. She produces those. What are the ten? "The power of knowledge of what is possible and impossible (<s>sthānāsthānajñānabala</s>). The power of knowledge of the ripening of <s>karma</s> (<s>karmavipākajñānabala</s>). The power of knowledge of the diverse elements (<s>nānādhātujñānabala</s>). The power of knowledge of diverse aspirations (<s>nānādhimuktijñānabala</s>). The power of knowledge of the higher and lower faculties (<s>indriyaparāparajñānabala</s>). The power of knowledge of the paths leading everywhere (<s>sarvatragāminīpratipajjñānabala</s>). The power of knowledge of the defilements, purifications, and emergences from <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations), <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations), <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations), and <s>samāpattis</s> (attainments) (<s>dhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattisaṃkleśavyavadānavyutthānajñānabala</s>). The power of knowledge of the recollection of former abodes (<s>pūrvenivāsānusmṛtijñānabala</s>). The power of knowledge of death and rebirth (<s>cyutopapādajñānabala</s>). And the power of knowledge of the destruction of the defilements (<s>āśravakṣayajñānabala</s>)." Their characteristics are as stated in both great <s>Bhagavatīs</s>. Among these, "possible and impossible" are "place and non-place" (<s>sthānāsthāna</s>). For example: "the unpleasant ripening of misconduct is the place; pleasant [ripening] is the non-place" — and so on. "<s>Karma</s> and <s>vipāka</s>" — action and ripening. "Diverse elements" (<s>nānādhātu</s>) is the disposition (<s>adhyāśaya</s>) that produces merit, demerit, and so on. "Diverse aspirations" (<s>nānādhimukti</s>) — for example, those established in passion have an inclination toward aversion and so on. The "faculties" (<s>indriya</s>) are faith, vigor, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom. Their "higher and lower" status is unevenness — this one has weak faculties, this one has middling faculties, and so on. "The path leading everywhere" (<s>sarvatragāminīpratipat</s>) — this practice is the antidote to passion, this one to aversion, and so on. Regarding the four <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations), the eight <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations), the three <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations) — with and without <s>vitarka</s> (initial thought) and <s>vicāra</s> (sustained thought) and so on — the four formless <s>samāpattis</s> (attainments), and the nine successive dwelling attainments: their defilements and the rest. Among these, defilement is through savoring and the like. Purification is through non-apprehension and the like. Emergence is through the lion's sport or through the leaping [method]. "Former abode" (<s>pūrvanivāsa</s>) is a former birth. "Recollection" (<s>anusmṛti</s>) thereof is remembering. "Death and rebirth" (<s>cyutopapāda</s>) are the dying and arising of beings. "Defilements" (<s>āśravas</s>) are <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions); their "destruction" is that by which they are destroyed and the path by which they are destroyed — both [together] constitute the destruction of the defilements. Of beings. The perfect knowledge of these — [the place and non-place] and so on — at all times and in all ways: that is here the knowledge of place and non-place, and so on. That itself is a "power" (<s>bala</s>), because it is unshakable by others, or because of its overcoming of them.

body.text: anavamardanīyetyabhibhavitumaśakyā / kuta ityāha / caturvaiśāradyakarītvāditi / siṃhavadatyantaniḥśaṃko yuktavādī viśāradaḥ / tasya bhāvo vaiśāradyam /
body.translated_text: "Indomitable" (<s>anavamardanīya</s>) means unable to be overwhelmed. "From what?" he says: "because of producing the four fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradyas</s>)." One who speaks with reason, utterly without hesitation like a lion, is "fearless" (<s>viśārada</s>). The state of that is <s>vaiśāradya</s> (fearlessness).

body.text: catvāri vaiśāradyāni / abhisaṃbodhivaiśāradyam / āśravakṣayavaiśāradyam / āntarāyikadha[rma]vaiśāradyam / nairyāṇikadharmavaiśāradyaṃ ca / abhisambodhistathāgatasya jñānasampat / āśravakṣayaḥ prahāṇasampat / tadubhayaṃ svārthaḥ / āntarāyikā dharmā nirvāṇasya vibandhakāḥ nairyāṇikā dharmā nirvāṇasya prāpakāḥ / etadubhayaṃ parārthaḥ / parebhyastadākhyānāt / teṣu vaiśāradyam / tatpratijñāpratiṣṭhāpaneṣvityarthaḥ / tatkarā / anāthāḥ sattvā anādau duḥkhasāgare bhramatāmeṣāmadyāpi trāturabhāvāt / teṣāṃ nāthastrātā bhagavān buddhaḥ / tatkarā / iyatā sarvajñajñānapariniṣpattireṣeti samarthitaḥ / eṣaiva sarvajñatvamiti samarthayitumāha / saṃsāretyādi / saṃsāraḥ sāśravāḥ skandhāḥ / tasya pratipakṣā hantrī / dharmadhātureva tasya hanteti cedāha / akūṭasthatāmupādāyeti / dharmadhāturhi kūṭastho anādinidhanaikarūpatvāt / sa cetpratipakṣaḥ syāt tadā ādita eva saṃsāro na syāt / prajñāpāramitā punarādimatī, uttarottaragāminī ceti saiva tasya pratipakṣaḥ / anena prahāṇasampaduktā / jñānasampadamāha sarvetyādinā / sarvadharmāṇāṃ svabhāvaḥ paramārthaḥ / tasya vidarśanī tatpratibhāsatvāt / svasya pareṣāñca parārthamadhikṛtyāha / paripūrṇetyādi / paripūrṇamekenāpyanūnatvāt / triparivartadvādaśākāraṃ ca yaddharmacakram / dharmaḥ śāsanam / tadeva cakraṃ vineyasantāneṣu caṃkramaṇāt / tasya pravartano pravartayitrī / buddhānāṃ tathaiva tasya pravartanāt /
body.translated_text: The four <s>vaiśāradyas</s> (fearlessnesses) are: the fearlessness of perfect awakening (<s>abhisaṃbodhivaiśāradya</s>), the fearlessness regarding the destruction of defilements (<s>āśravakṣayavaiśāradya</s>), the fearlessness regarding obstructive <s>dharmas</s> (<s>āntarāyikadharmavaiśāradya</s>), and the fearlessness regarding the <s>dharmas</s> leading to deliverance (<s>nairyāṇikadharmavaiśāradya</s>). The perfect awakening of the <s>Tathāgata</s> is the accomplishment of knowledge (<s>jñānasampat</s>). The destruction of defilements is the accomplishment of abandonment (<s>prahāṇasampat</s>). Both of these constitute one's own benefit (<s>svārtha</s>). The obstructive <s>dharmas</s> are obstacles to <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. The <s>dharmas</s> leading to deliverance are those that bring about <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. Both of these constitute the benefit of others (<s>parārtha</s>), because of proclaiming them to others. The fearlessness regarding these means being assured in establishing the assertions concerning them — this is the meaning. She produces those. "Protectorless" (<s>anātha</s>) — the beings, wandering in the beginningless ocean of suffering without a protector even to this day. Their protector, their savior, is the Blessed <s>Buddha</s>. She produces that [state]. Thus, "the completion of omniscient knowledge is this" — this has been established. That this very [<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>] is omniscience — to establish this he says, beginning with "of <s>saṃsāra</s>" and so on. "<s>Saṃsāra</s>" is the tainted <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates). [She is] their antidote, their destroyer. If [one objects:] "The <s>dharmadhātu</s> itself is its destroyer" — to this he says: "with reference to its unchanging nature." For the <s>dharmadhātu</s> is unchanging (<s>kūṭastha</s>), because of its single nature without beginning or end. If that were the antidote, then <s>saṃsāra</s> would not have existed from the very beginning. But <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> has a beginning and is progressively advancing — therefore she herself is its antidote. By this, the accomplishment of abandonment has been stated. The accomplishment of knowledge he states beginning with "of all" and so on. The "own-nature" (<s>svabhāva</s>) of all <s>dharmas</s> is their ultimate reality (<s>paramārtha</s>). [She is] its revealer, because it appears in her. With regard to the benefit of both oneself and others, he says, beginning with "complete" and so on. "Complete" (<s>paripūrṇa</s>) — because not lacking even one. And the wheel of <s>Dharma</s> has three turnings and twelve aspects. "<s>Dharma</s>" is the teaching. That itself is the "wheel" because of its rolling through the mind-streams of those to be trained. [She is] its "turner" (<s>pravartana</s>), the one who sets it in motion. Because for the <s>Buddhas</s> she likewise sets it in motion.

body.text: tatra dharmacakraṃ satyacatuṣṭayam / tasya trayaḥ parivartāḥ / idaṃ duḥkham / ayaṃ duḥkhasamudayaḥ / ayaṃ duḥkhanirodhaḥ / iyaṃ duḥkhanirodhagāminī pratipaditi / satyacatuṣṭayasya svabhāvaparicchedaḥ prathamaḥ parivartaḥ / tasyaiva yathākramaṃ parijñeyapraheyasākṣātkartavyabhāvayitavyatvaparicchedo dvitīyaḥ parivartaḥ / tasyaivātmanā parijñātaprahīna(ṇa)sākṣātkṛtabhāvitatvaparicchedastṛtīyaḥ / tasmāt triparivartaṃ tat / duḥkhasatyasya duḥkhasvabhāvaḥ parijñeyatvaṃ parijñātatvaṃ ceti traya ākārāḥ / samudayasatyasya tatsvabhāvaḥ praheyatvaṃ prahīṇatvaṃ cetiṃ traya ākārāḥ / nirodhasatyasya tat svabhāvaḥ sākṣātkartavyatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtatvaṃ ceti traya ākārāḥ / mārgasatyasya tat svabhāvo bhāvayitavyatvaṃ bhāvitatvaṃ ceti traya ākārāḥ / tasmāt dvādaśākāraṃ tat /
body.translated_text: There, the wheel of <s>Dharma</s> is the four truths (<s>satyacatuṣṭaya</s>). Its three turnings are: "This is suffering. This is the origin of suffering. This is the cessation of suffering. This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering" — the determination of the own-nature of the four truths is the first turning. The determination of [their respective characters as] to be fully known, to be abandoned, to be directly realized, and to be cultivated, in that same order, is the second turning. The determination that they have been fully known, abandoned, directly realized, and cultivated by oneself is the third. Therefore it has three turnings. The truth of suffering has three aspects: its nature as suffering, its to-be-fully-known character, and its having-been-fully-known character. The truth of origination has three aspects: its nature, its to-be-abandoned character, and its having-been-abandoned character. The truth of cessation has three aspects: its nature, its to-be-directly-realized character, and its having-been-directly-realized character. The truth of the path has three aspects: its nature, its to-be-cultivated character, and its having-been-cultivated character. Therefore it has twelve aspects.

body.text: nanu pratītyasamutpannenāpi svabhāveneyaṃ [na] nirodhikā śāṃ(sāṃ)kleśikānāṃ vināśahetūnāmakiñcitkaratvāt / nāpyutpādikā vaiyavadānikānāṃ mithyājñānanivṛttau cittamātrādeva samyagjñānotpatteḥ / naitadasti / bandhyakṣaṇotpādanasyaiva santānanirodhatvāt / agninā śītanirodhavat / prajñāpāramitayaiva mithyājñānanirodhe
body.translated_text: But surely, even by its dependently arisen nature, this [<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>] is not a destroyer of those pertaining to defilement, because of the inefficacy of the causes of destruction. Nor is it a producer of those pertaining to purification, because right knowledge arises from mind alone upon the cessation of wrong knowledge. This is not so — because the very production of a moment that counteracts barrenness [of the continuum] is the cessation of the [mental] continuum, just as fire causes the cessation of cold. When through <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> alone there is the cessation of wrong knowledge,

body.text: sati bhagavataḥ prāgabhūtasya samyagjñānasya taddhetukatvāt / nirodhasya cāvastuno hetutvāyogāt / cittasyaiva ca niruddhavipakṣasya samyagjñānatvāt / anyathā hi sarvabhrāntinivṛttikālepi vyāpi samyagjñānaṃ na syāditi bhāvanāmārgasya svabhāvaḥ //
body.translated_text: the right knowledge of the <s>Bhagavat</s> (Blessed One), which previously was unmanifest, arises because of having that [cessation] as its cause. And because cessation, being non-substantial, cannot be a cause. And because the mind itself, when its opponent has ceased, is right knowledge. For otherwise, even at the time of the cessation of all error, pervasive right knowledge would not exist — this is the nature of the path of meditation (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>).

body.text: kathamityādinā sarvajñatānuprāptaya ityetadantena śreṣṭhatā / sthātavyamiti vartitavyam / pūjābhiḥ manasikartavyā guṇānusmaraṇaiḥ / namaskartavyā kāyavākcittaiḥ / nidānaṃ prastāvaḥ pṛcchāyāḥ / hetustu bhagavatyāḥ śreṣṭhatā / prajñāpāramitāyā yatkauśalyaparigṛhītasya bodhisattvasyānumodanāsahagataṃ puṇyamaupalambhikānāṃ pañca pāramitāmayāt puṇyādviśiṣyata itīdaṃ nidānamanantaroktatvāt / yata iyaṃ tāsāṃ pariṇāyikā tataḥ śreṣṭheti hetuḥ / apariṇāyakamiti pariṇāyakarahitam / abhavyamayogyam / jātyandhabhūtaṃ jātyandhasadṛśam / śeṣaṃ subodham / iti śreṣṭhatā //
body.translated_text: With "how" and so on, up to "for the attainment of <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience)," [is stated] the supremacy. "One should abide" means one should conduct oneself. "With acts of worship" — one should attend to [<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>] through the recollection of [her] qualities. "One should pay homage" — through body, speech, and mind. The "occasion" (<s>nidāna</s>) is the pretext for the question. But the "reason" (<s>hetu</s>) is the supremacy of the <s>Bhagavatī</s>. The merit accompanied by the rejoicing of a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who is endowed with the skillful means of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> surpasses the merit consisting of the five <s>pāramitās</s> based on apprehension (<s>aupalambhika</s>) — this is the occasion, because it has been stated just before. Because this [<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>] is their guide, therefore [she is] supreme — this is the reason. "Without a guide" (<s>apariṇāyaka</s>) means devoid of a guide. "Incapable" (<s>abhavya</s>) means unfit. "As if born blind" (<s>jātyandhabhūta</s>) means resembling one born blind. The rest is easily understood. Thus [is stated] the supremacy.

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmānityādinā abhinirhāro dvitīyāt evamuktāt prāk / prajñāpāramiteti bhāvanāmārgaḥ / yaḥ pañcānāṃ skandhānāṃ yāvatsarvadharmāṇāmanabhisaṃskāro 'nupalambhaḥ so 'sya abhinirhāraḥ pariniṣpādanam / avayavārthaḥ subodhaḥ / ityabhinirhāraḥ //
body.translated_text: Now, with "O <s>Āyuṣman</s>" and so on, up to just before the second "thus spoken," [is stated] the accomplishment (<s>abhinirhāra</s>). "<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>" here means the path of meditation (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>). That which is the non-fabrication (<s>anabhisaṃskāra</s>) of the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) — indeed of all <s>dharmas</s> — [and their] non-apprehension (<s>anupalambha</s>): that is its accomplishment (<s>abhinirhāra</s>), its completion (<s>pariniṣpādana</s>). The meaning of the individual parts is easily understood. Thus [is stated] the accomplishment.

body.text: evamukta ityādi yāvata saṃkhyāṃ gacchatīti / katamaṃ dharmamityanāśravaḥ / na kaściddharmamiti / dharmāṇāmarpaṇāyāścānupalambhādityarpaṇā //
body.translated_text: "Thus spoken" and so on, up to "it enters into calculation." "What <s>dharma</s>" — [this refers to] the undefiled (<s>anāśrava</s>). "No <s>dharma</s> at all" — because of the non-apprehension of <s>dharmas</s> and of dedication (<s>arpaṇā</s>) — that is dedication.

body.text: atha khalu śakra ityādi śāriputravacanāt prāk / yadi na kañciddharmamarpayati na tarhi sarvajñatāmapīti matvā śakra āha / kimiyamityādi / arpayatyeva kenacitparyāyeṇa / yathā tu nārpayati tadbhagavānāha na yathetyādi / upalambho bālagrāheṇa rūpeṇa / nāma saṃjñā / saṃskāraḥ kalpanā / yathā tvarpayati tatpṛcchati / kathaṃ tarhītyādinā / uttaraṃ yathetyādinā / yathā nārpayatīti dharmāṇāmarpaṇāyāścāvikalpanāt / tatheti / avikalpanayā / na kañcidityādi / dharmāṇāmutpādādīnāṃ cāvikalpanāditi bhāvaḥ / anutpādāyānirodhāyeti notpādāya na nirodhāyetyarthaḥ / asamarthasamāsattvāt / ataśca anupasthitetyakiñcitkaratvāt / evamapīti sarvajñatārpakatvenāpi / dūrīkariṣyatītyasaṃmukhībhāvāt / riktīkariṣyatīti saṃmukhībhūtasya jñānasya tallakṣaṇābhāvāt / tucchīkariṣyatīti tat phalābhāvāt / na kariṣyatīti notpādayiṣyati / astyeṣa paryāya iti yathā tvayoktaḥ / tatkasya hetoriti taddūrīkaraṇādikaṃ kutaḥ? paridīpitāyāmiti nirdiṣṭāyām / na rūpaṃ yāvanna buddhatvamiti na kiñciddharma
body.translated_text: Beginning with 'Now then, <s>Śakra</s>' and so on, up to before <s>Śāriputra's</s> statement. Thinking 'If he does not transfer any <s>dharma</s>, then he does not transfer even <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience),' <s>Śakra</s> says beginning with 'Is this' and so on. He does indeed transfer, by some method. But the manner in which he does not transfer — the <s>Bhagavān</s> states beginning with 'Not as' and so on. 'Apprehension' (<s>upalambha</s>) is by grasping form with the childish grasp. 'Name' is designation (<s>saṃjñā</s>). '<s>Saṃskāra</s>' (formation) is conceptual construction (<s>kalpanā</s>). The manner in which he does transfer — he asks beginning with 'How then' and so on. The answer [follows] beginning with 'As' and so on. 'As he does not transfer' — because of the non-conceptualization of both the <s>dharmas</s> and the act of transfer. 'Thus' — through non-conceptualization. Beginning with 'Not any' and so on — the meaning is: because of the non-conceptualization of arising and the rest of the <s>dharmas</s>. 'For non-arising, for non-cessation' means 'not for the sake of arising, not for the sake of cessation' — because this is an incompetent compound. And therefore, 'not established' — because of being inefficacious. 'Even so' — even though it transfers <s>sarvajñatā</s>. 'Will distance' — because of non-confrontation. 'Will empty' — because when knowledge has been confronted, it lacks those characteristics. 'Will make hollow' — because of the absence of its fruit. 'Will not produce' — will not generate. 'There is this method' means 'as stated by you.' 'For what reason?' means 'whence that distancing and the rest?' 'When it has been illuminated' means 'when it has been set forth.' 'Not form, up to not <s>Buddhahood</s>' means 'not any <s>dharma</s> whatsoever'

body.text: ityarthaḥ / tasmāt kañciddharma paśyan dūrīkariṣyatīti / yāvanna kariṣyatīmām / katamena paryāyeṇeti / kiṃ mahārthatayeti bhāvaḥ //
body.translated_text: — this is the meaning. 'Therefore, seeing some <s>dharma</s>, one will distance' — up to 'will not produce' this [<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>]. 'By which method?' means — the sense is: 'Is it because of its great significance?'

body.text: subhūtirāha netyādi / niḥsvabhāveṣu sarvadharmeṣu dvayābhāvāditi bhāvaḥ / asaṃkṣiptā vikṣipteti / advayatvāt / evamapīti mahārthatayāpi / kimpunaḥ śabdādatiśayārthaḥ / evamityuktvā / tadevāha / evamahamityādinā / niḥṣyanda iti tatpṛṣṭhabhāvī niścayaḥ / yaḥ sattvopalambha iti sambandhaḥ / sattvaḥ pudgaladravyaṃ tadvad asvabhāvajātikāsvabhāvalakṣaṇam / jātirutpattiḥ / tābhyāṃ rahitā / asyaiva nirdeśaḥ sattvāsvabhāvatayetyādinā / pariśeṣādgamyate sattvājātikatayā ajātikateti / viviktatā śūnyatā / acintyatā cittānālambanatā / abhisaṃbodhanaṃ sākṣātkriyā / tadabhāvād anabhisaṃbodhanatā / yathābha / sadbhuto arthaḥ / tasyānabhisaṃbodhanamagrahaṇaṃ sattvaḥ / tadvatprajñāpāramitā / yathā sattvasya balasamudāgamanaṃ balaniṣpādanaṃ na kiñcit tathā tathāgatasya prajñāpāramitayeti mahārthatā //
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> says 'No' and so on. The sense is: because in all <s>dharmas</s> that are without intrinsic nature, there is no duality. 'Neither contracted nor dispersed' — because of non-duality. 'Even so' — even because of great significance. The word '<s>kimpunaḥ</s>' (how much more) conveys the sense of something surpassing. Having said 'thus,' he states that very [point] beginning with 'Thus I' and so on. '<s>Niḥṣyanda</s>' (outflow) is the certainty that follows from it. 'That which is the apprehension of a being' — this is the connection. A 'being' (<s>sattva</s>) is the substantial self of a person; like that [being], it is characterized by the absence of intrinsic nature and of birth. 'Birth' (<s>jāti</s>) is arising (<s>utpatti</s>). Devoid of both of these. The explication of this very [point begins] with 'through the non-intrinsic-nature of beings' and so on. By elimination it is understood: 'through the non-birth of beings, non-born.' 'Seclusion' (<s>viviktatā</s>) is emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>). 'Inconceivability' (<s>acintyatā</s>) is the mind's having no object to grasp. '<s>Abhisaṃbodhana</s>' is direct realization. Because of its absence, there is non-realization (<s>anabhisaṃbodhana</s>). As it is said. The 'real meaning' (<s>sadbhūta artha</s>). Its non-realization, its non-grasping, is a 'being' (<s>sattva</s>). <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is likewise. Just as the accomplishment of the powers of a being — the production of the powers — amounts to nothing, so too does the <s>Tathāgata's</s> [accomplishment] through <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> — this is the great significance.

body.text: abhinirhārasya pañcāṅgānyuktāni / ṣaṣṭhasaptamepi staḥ / adhimokṣahetuḥ pratipakṣahetuśca / te 'dhikṛtya śāstram-
body.translated_text: Five limbs of the bringing-forth (<s>abhinirhāra</s>) have been stated. The sixth and seventh also exist: the cause of conviction (<s>adhimokṣa</s>) and the cause of the antidote (<s>pratipakṣa</s>). Regarding those, the treatise [states] —

children.translated_text: Service of the <s>Buddhas</s>, and whatever skill in means such as generosity and the rest —
These are the causes of conviction herein. [And there are] the causes of decline of the <s>Dharma</s>. [2-26]
<s>Māra's</s> influence, non-conviction regarding the profound <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature of reality),
Adherence to the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) and the rest, and association with evil companions. [2-27]

body.text: atrādhimuktihetavastraya uktāḥ pādatrayeṇa / dharmavyasanaṃ pratikṣepaḥ / tasya catvāro hetava itaraiḥ pañcabhiḥ pādaiḥ / 'anadhimuktatā' anadhimuktiḥ / tatrādhimokṣo 'sminneva bhāvanāmārge 'dhimuktiḥ / tamāha / atha khalvityādinā na dhandhayiṣyatītyetadantena / adhimokṣayiṣyatīti niścite vastunyevameva nānyathetyavadhāraṇamadhimokṣaḥ / taṃ kariṣyatītyarthaḥ / tatkarotīti curādau pāṭhāṇṇic / tasyādhimokṣasya lakṣaṇaṃ tribhiḥ padairgatyantarapratiṣedhāyāha / tatra kāṃkṣā bādhā / abādhyabādhanasya kāṃkṣāmātratvāt / vicikitsā saṃśaya eva / dhandhāyanamapratipattiriti trīṇi gatyantarāṇi / dhandho 'pratipattau / dhandho bhaviṣyatīti dhandhāyiṣyati / lohitāderākṛtigaṇatvāt kyaṣ / ityadhimokṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: Here, three causes of conviction are stated by three quarters [of the verse]. 'Decline of the <s>Dharma</s>' (<s>dharmavyasana</s>) is rejection. Its four causes [are stated] by the remaining five quarters. '<s>Anadhimuktatā</s>' is non-conviction. Therein, 'conviction' is, on this very path of cultivation, the firm adherence (<s>adhimukti</s>). This he states beginning with 'Now then' and so on, up to the end of 'will not hesitate.' 'Will cause conviction' (<s>adhimokṣayiṣyati</s>) means: regarding a certain matter, the determination 'it is just so, not otherwise' is conviction (<s>adhimokṣa</s>); he will produce that — this is the meaning. That he will produce it — the root '<s>kṛ</s>' is read in the <s>curādi</s> (tenth) class, hence the <s>ṇic</s> suffix. The characteristic of that conviction he states in three terms, for the exclusion of alternative outcomes. There, '<s>kāṅkṣā</s>' (doubt) is obstruction. Because the obstruction of that which cannot be obstructed amounts to mere doubt. '<s>Vicikitsā</s>' (uncertainty) is just deliberation. '<s>Dhandhāyana</s>' (hesitation) is non-engagement — these are three alternative outcomes. '<s>Dhandha</s>' [means] non-engagement. 'He will hesitate' means '<s>dhandhāyiṣyati</s>.' Because of the <s>kyaṣ</s> suffix, since it belongs to the <s>lohitādi ākṛtigaṇa</s>. Thus [the section on] conviction.

body.text: adhimokṣasya trayo hetavaḥ / tatra dvau pṛcchati / kutaścyutvehopannaḥ kiyacciracaritāvī ceti / sa iti yo 'dhimoktā / adhimukto 'dhimuktikāritreṇa
body.translated_text: There are three causes of conviction. Of those, he asks about two: 'From where did he pass away and take rebirth here?' and 'For how long has he practiced?' 'He' refers to the one who has conviction. 'One of conviction' is characterized by the conduct of conviction.

body.text: lakṣyate / atastadāha / ya ityādinā / arthata ityaṣṭābhirabhisamayaiḥ / arthanayata iti yathāsvaṃ teṣāmeva vastubhiḥ / dharmata ityebhireva nāmapadavyañjanaiḥ / dharmanayata iti samāsavyāsādibhiḥ / anugamiṣyaṃtyanusaraṇāt / anubhotsyate tathā jñānāt / anubodhayiṣyati tathaiva parān /
body.translated_text: Hence that is stated beginning with 'Whoever' and so on. 'By meaning' means through the eight <s>abhisamayas</s> (realizations). 'By the method of meaning' means through the respective objects of those very [realizations]. 'By <s>dharma</s>' means through those very names, words, and syllables. 'By the method of <s>dharma</s>' means through compound-analysis, expansion, and the like. 'Will follow' — because of following along. 'Will realize' — because of knowledge in that manner. 'Will cause others to realize' — in that very manner, to others.

body.text: tatkasya hetoriti kuto liṅgāt / yaḥ kaścidityādinā liṅgamāha / me dṛṣṭa iti mayā dṛṣṭaḥ / sambandhavivakṣāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhī / tadyathā subhāṣitasya śikṣate, nāgnistṛpyati kāṣṭhānāmiti / avadadhāti sāvadhānaṃ karoti / satkṛtyeti bhaktito rucito vā / nopacchinatti vicchedākaraṇāt /
body.translated_text: 'For what reason?' means 'from what sign?' Beginning with 'Whoever' and so on, he states the sign. 'Seen by me' means 'seen by me' — the genitive case is used when the relation [of agent] is intended, as in '<s>subhāṣitasya śikṣate</s>' (he trains in good speech) and '<s>nāgnis tṛpyati kāṣṭhānām</s>' (fire is not satisfied of wood). 'Attends to' means 'makes attentive.' '<s>Satkṛtya</s>' means 'with devotion' or 'with interest.' 'Does not cut off' — because of not causing discontinuity.

body.text: ciretyādinopasaṃhāraḥ / ciracaritāḥ pāramitā avituṃ śīlamasyeti ciracaritāvī / bahavo buddhāḥ paryupāsitā yena sa tathoktaḥ / iti buddhasevādānādicaryā //
body.translated_text: Beginning with 'for a long time' and so on is the conclusion. 'One who has long-practiced <s>pāramitās</s>, whose habit is to guard [them]' is '<s>ciracaritāvī</s>.' 'One by whom many <s>Buddhas</s> have been attended upon' is so called. Thus, the practice of service to the <s>Buddhas</s>, generosity, and the rest.

body.text: tṛtīyo 'dhimokṣaheturupāyakauśalyam / tadāha / atha khalvityādinā sthaviraḥ subhūtirityataḥ prāk / śakyā punariti kāṃkṣā praśnaḥ / śrotuṃ śabdataḥ / upalakṣayitumarthataḥ / samanvāhartuṃ kālāntare smartum / upapādayituṃ cintākāle / upadhārayituṃ bhāvanākāle cetasi sthirīkaraṇāt / iyamiti pratibhāsamānā / ihāmutra veti pratibhāsamānā dhārā / aneneti pratibhāsamānena / ākāreṇeti lakṣaṇena / tadyathā gauḥ sāsnādimatvena / liṅgeneti kṛtrimeṇa cinhena / tadyathā gaurghaṇṭādinā / nimitteneti svābhāvikena cinhena / tadyathā gauḥśuklatvādinā / nirdeṣṭuṃ parasmaiḥ / śrotuṃ parasmāt /
body.translated_text: The third cause of conviction is skill in means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>). That he states beginning with 'Now then' and so on, up to before 'The Elder <s>Subhūti</s>.' 'Is it possible?' is a question [expressing] doubt. 'To hear' — by its words. 'To recognize' — by its meaning. 'To bear in mind' — to remember at a later time. 'To verify' — during the time of investigation (<s>cintā</s>). 'To retain' — during the time of meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>), because of making firm in the mind. 'This' — [that which is] appearing. 'Here or there' — the stream that is appearing. 'By this' — by this appearing. 'By its form' means by its characteristic — as for instance, a cow by its dewlap and the like. 'By its sign' means by an artificial mark — as for instance, a cow by a bell and the like. 'By its mark' means by a natural mark — as for instance, a cow by whiteness and the like. 'To point out' — to another. 'To hear' — from another.

body.text: bhagavānāha / uttaraṃ no hītyādi / skandhādiśa iti skandhādibhiḥ / rūpaskandha iti vā yāvaddharmāyatanamiti vetyarthaḥ / kuta ityāha / sarvadharmaistaireva viviktatvādasyāḥ / tadapi kutaḥ? niḥsvabhāvatvātteṣām / parikalpitena dharmasvabhāveneti bhāvaḥ / na cānyatreti / na cānyā tatparamārthatvāditi bhāvaḥ / ata eva tadityādinā praśnaḥ / skandhetyādinottaram / vijñaptirūpaṃ skandhādikameva / śūnyaṃ parikalpitena skandhādisvabhāvena / sā tasya tena śūnyatā vijñaptimātratā prajñāpāramitā / tasmādadvayametaddvaṃvīkāram / nanu śūnyatāyā idaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ na prajñāpāramitāyā ityata āha / śūnyatvādityādi / nopalabhyate skandhādi yathālakṣaṇam / yonupalambhaḥ sarvadharmāṇāmiti tadviviktaprakāśamātropalambhalakṣaṇaḥ / na tūpalambhanivṛttimātram / "nābhāvaḥ kasyacitpratipattiḥ pratipattiheturvā" iti vacanāt / yo 'nupalambhaḥ sā prajñāpāramitā prakṛṣṭajñānatvāt pāragatvācca / tathāpi nāsau prajñāpāramitā / syādyadi skandhādiśūnyatāmanubhūya
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> says the answer beginning with 'No indeed' and so on. 'By the <s>skandhas</s> and the rest' means 'by the <s>skandhas</s> and so forth' — meaning 'by form-aggregate' or 'up to <s>dharma-āyatana</s>.' Whence? He says: because of this [<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>'s] being secluded from all those very <s>dharmas</s>. And whence that? Because of the lack of intrinsic nature of those [<s>dharmas</s>] — the sense is: because of their having an imagined <s>dharma</s>-nature. 'Nor is it other' — nor is it something different, because it is their ultimate reality — this is the sense. For that very reason, the question [follows] beginning with 'that' and so on. The answer [follows] beginning with '<s>skandha</s>' and so on. The representational form (<s>vijñaptirūpa</s>) is just the <s>skandhas</s> and the rest. It is 'empty' — of the imagined nature of <s>skandhas</s> and the rest. That emptiness of it by that [imagined nature] is the mere-representation (<s>vijñaptimātratā</s>), which is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Therefore this is a non-dual <s>dvandva</s> (copulative compound). 'But surely this is the definition of emptiness, not of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>' — to this he says beginning with 'because of being empty' and so on. 'Is not apprehended' — the <s>skandhas</s> and the rest, as characterized. 'That which is the non-apprehension of all <s>dharmas</s>' — that has the characteristic of the apprehension of the mere manifestation of their seclusion, not the mere cessation of apprehension — because of the statement: 'The non-existence of something is not cognition, nor a cause of cognition.' 'That which is non-apprehension — that is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>' — because of being supreme knowledge and because of having gone beyond. Even so, it is not that <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> — it would be if, having experienced the emptiness of the <s>skandhas</s> and the rest,

body.text: skandhādyavasīyeta / rajatādyavasāye śuktidarśanavat / etaddarśayitumāha / yadetyādi / yadā tu yathānubhūtaniścayaṃ janayati na skandhā na dhāturnāyatanamiti tadā prajñāpāramitaiva / tannisyandatvāt skandhādyabhāvaniścayasya / śuktiniścaye śuktidarśanavat / prāmāṇyāt / tadyevaṃ yadyathāsti yathā ca nāsti yathā ca prajñāpāramitā syānna syādvā tasya sarvasya samyagbodha upāyakauśalaṃ tṛtīyo 'dhimokṣahetuḥ /
body.translated_text: one were to determine the <s>skandhas</s> and the rest [as real] — like seeing the nacre [as silver] after the determination of silver. To show this he says beginning with 'that which' and so on. But when it generates certainty in accordance with what has been experienced — 'not <s>skandhas</s>, not <s>dhātus</s>, not <s>āyatanas</s>' — then it is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> itself, because the certainty of the non-existence of <s>skandhas</s> and the rest is its outflow — like seeing the nacre upon the determination [that it is] nacre. Because of [its] validity. Thus, the complete understanding of all that — as it exists, as it does not exist, and whether <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> would or would not be — that is the skill in means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>), the third cause of conviction.

body.text: dharmavyasanaṃ vaktavyam / sa ca saddharmapratikṣayaḥ / kutaḥ? dharmavyasanahetutvāt / dharmasya vyasanaṃ vipat / dīrghadurgativāsena tasya śravaṇādyabhāvaḥ / durgaticiravāsahetutvāddharmavyasanahetutvam / tasmāddharmavyasanam / tadeva dharmavyasanasaṃvartanīyaṃ karma / tatsaṃvartate 'smāditi kṛtvā / tadeva prastauti sthavira ityādinā / prajñāpāramitā / eṣa eva bhāvanāmārgaḥ / tasyāṃ yogāpattiḥ samādhānaprāptiḥ /
body.translated_text: The decline of the <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmavyasana</s>) is to be explained. And that is the decline of the true <s>Dharma</s> (<s>saddharma</s>). From what cause? Because of being a cause of the decline of the <s>Dharma</s>. 'Decline of the <s>Dharma</s>' (<s>dharmasya vyasanam</s>) is calamity. Through long residence in the evil destinies, there is the absence of hearing [the <s>Dharma</s>] and the like. Because of being the cause of long residence in evil destinies, it is the cause of the decline of the <s>Dharma</s>. Therefore, [there is] the decline of the <s>Dharma</s>. That very [thing] is the <s>karma</s> conducive to the decline of the <s>Dharma</s> — because it conduces to that. He introduces that very [topic] beginning with 'Elder' and so on. '<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>' — this very path of cultivation. 'Attainment of engagement with it' (<s>yogāpatti</s>) is the attainment of meditative absorption (<s>samādhāna</s>).

body.text: vibhajyeti / kathaṃ vibhajya? keṣāñci[cci]racaritāvinā(tā) bhavati keṣāñcinneti / tatkutaḥ? indriyāṇāṃ śraddhādīnāṃ vimātratayā nānātvena / tāmāha syādityādinā / asyāmagauravatā teṣāmabhūditi sambandhaḥ / buddhānāmantikāditi / antike dūrāntikārthebhya iti pañcamī / tatsannidhāvityarthaḥ / agauravatā aśu(su)śūṣaṇatā aśraddadhānatā ca / bhagavatyāṃ aparyupāsanatā aparipṛcchanatā ca buddheṣu / tata iti śraddhāviyogāt / dharmavyasanasaṃvartanīyaṃ karma saddharmapratikṣepaḥ / kṛtaṃ sakṛtkaraṇāt / sañcitaṃ punaḥ punaḥ karaṇāt / ācitaṃ paripūrṇam / upacitaṃ vipākadanaśaktilābhāt / kāyena sāmagrī śrotumāgamanam / cittena nirvikṣepatā / vācā aprastutānabhidhānam / evaṃ sāmagrimadadānā iti samyagaśṛṇvantaḥ / na jānanti granthataḥ / na paśyanti arthataḥ / na budhyante svabhāvatrayabhedena / tato na vedayante viparītabodhāt / aśraddadhānā ityādi tūktam / tasyopasaṃhāra evaṃ ta ityādinā / pratyākhyānaṃ manasā parityāgaḥ / pratikṣepo vācā / pratikrośanaṃ nindā / upahatyeti dūṣayitvā / dagdheti kuśalamūladāhāt / chando vaśībhāvaḥ / viparyayādvicchandaḥ śithilaḥ / ato vicchandayiṣyantīti śithilīkaraṇāt / vivecayiṣyantīti manasā tyājanāt / vivartayiṣyantīti punaragrahaṇāt / iyatā pratyākhyānamuktam //
body.translated_text: 'Distinguishing' means — how distinguishing? 'For some, the long-practiced state exists; for others, it does not' — and whence [this difference]? Because of the inequality, that is, the diversity, of the faculties such as faith and the rest. This he states beginning with 'It may be' and so on. 'There was a lack of respect toward this [<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>] on their part' — this is the connection. 'From the presence of the <s>Buddhas</s>' — the fifth case [ablative] from words meaning 'near' and 'far,' that is, [meaning] 'in their proximity.' 'Lack of respect' is lack of receptive listening and lack of faith. 'Lack of attendance upon and lack of questioning' regarding the <s>Bhagavatī</s> in the presence of the <s>Buddhas</s>. 'From that' — because of separation from faith. 'The <s>karma</s> conducive to the decline of the <s>Dharma</s>' is the rejection of the true <s>Dharma</s>. '<s>Kṛta</s>' (done) — from doing it once. '<s>Sañcita</s>' (accumulated) — from doing it repeatedly. '<s>Ācita</s>' (heaped up) — fully completed. '<s>Upacita</s>' (intensified) — from having obtained the capacity to give forth its ripened result. 'By body' — the assemblage [required] is coming to hear. 'By mind' — non-distraction. 'By speech' — not uttering irrelevant [words]. 'Those who did not provide the assemblage thus' — that is, those who did not hear properly. 'They do not know' — by the text. 'They do not see' — by the meaning. 'They do not understand' — by the threefold division of natures. 'Therefore they do not experience' — because of erroneous understanding. 'Lacking faith' and so on — that has already been stated. The conclusion of that [section] begins with 'Thus those' and so on. 'Rejection' (<s>pratyākhyāna</s>) is abandonment by the mind. '<s>Pratikṣepa</s>' (repudiation) is [rejection] by speech. '<s>Pratikrośana</s>' (reviling) is censure. 'Having ruined' (<s>upahatya</s>) — having corrupted. 'Burnt' — because of the burning of wholesome roots. 'Desire' (<s>chanda</s>) is mastery. By its opposite, '<s>vicchanda</s>' is laxity. Therefore 'they will cause laxity' — because of making lax. 'They will cause to separate' — because of mental abandonment. 'They will cause to turn away' — because of not taking up [the <s>Dharma</s>] again. To this extent, rejection has been stated.

body.text: pratikṣepamāha nātretyādinā / pratikroṣaṇamāha naitadityādinā / apakrāntāḥ parimuktāḥ paribāhyā ityeko 'rthaḥ / sarva yathā bhavanti tathā sarveṇa aṅgena / sarva yathā bhavati tathā sarvaḥ prakāraḥ / karmābhisaṃskāraḥ karma kriyā / upasthāpiteneti kṛtena / samutthāpitenetyupacitena / saṃvartanī
body.translated_text: He states repudiation beginning with 'Not here' and so on. He states reviling beginning with 'This is not' and so on. 'Departed,' 'released,' and 'excluded' are one meaning. 'All as they are' means 'by every limb, accordingly.' 'All as it is' means 'every manner, accordingly.' '<s>Karmābhisaṃskāra</s>' (karmic formation) — <s>karma</s> is action (<s>kriyā</s>). 'Established' means 'produced.' 'Generated' means 'intensified.'

body.text: pralayaḥ / āavīcitalādā ca brahmalokādyasyāmagninā kṣīyate sā tejaḥsaṃvartanī / kṣepsyante antarābhavaśarīreṇa / upapatsyante upapattibhavaśarīreṇa / samānā santaḥ / bahu vata duḥkhaṃ ca tadvedanīyaṃ yasmāttathoktam /
body.translated_text: '<s>Saṃvartanī</s>' is dissolution (<s>pralaya</s>). That by which, from the base of <s>Avīci</s> [hell] upward and from the <s>Brahmaloka</s> downward, [the world] is consumed by fire — that is the '<s>tejaḥsaṃvartanī</s>' (dissolution by heat). 'They will be cast' — by the body of the intermediate state (<s>antarābhava</s>). 'They will be born' — by the body of the rebirth state (<s>upapattibhava</s>). '<s>Samānā santaḥ</s>' means 'being [of such nature].' 'Much suffering indeed, and that which is to be experienced' — because it is so stated.

body.text: prativarṇikādipadatrayaṃ samānārtham / 'lābhasatkāraṃ tebhya eva / yadartha te dṛśyeraṇ (dūṣyeran) / tatkasya hetoriti / tatteṣāmadarśanādikaṃ kuta ityarthaḥ / kasambakaṃ pūtipūrṇam / tadatyaktamanyānyapi parṇāni nāśayati / jātirjātam / kasambakavajjātameṣāmiti kasambakajātāḥ / kṛṣṇā tṛṇaviśeṣaḥ / prākṛtabhāṣayā kaṇḍā / sāpi kṣetrādanapanītā kṣetraṃ nāśayati / nirjātirniṣpattiḥ / kṛṣṇāvannirjātireṣāmiti kṛṣṇānirjātikāḥ / kṛṣṇo hi kṛṣṇasarpaḥ saviṣaḥ saṃśrṛ(sṛ)ṣṭān daṣṭo saviṣīkaroti / anayeneti tebhyaḥ śrutaśraddhādināmārgeṇa / vyasanaṃ nirayādiduḥkham / āgāḍhamābādhamiti mahatīṃ pīḍām / nigacchet spṛśediti prāpnuyādityarthaḥ / ālokaḥ prakṛtasya karmaṇo vipākajñānam / śuklāṃśaḥ kuśalabhāgaḥ / tadyogāt śuklāṃśikaḥ / samavadhānaṃ yogaḥ / śeṣaṃ subodham / iti dharmavyasanam //
body.translated_text: The three terms beginning with '<s>prativarṇikā</s>' and so on are synonymous. 'Gain and honor from those very ones.' 'For what purpose they would be seen (corrupted)' — 'what is the reason?' — that is, 'whence comes their not being seen, and so on?' — this is the meaning. '<s>Kasambakaṃ</s>' means rotten and full [of decay]. When that is not removed, it destroys other leaves as well. '<s>Jātiḥ</s>' means born. 'Born like <s>kasambakas</s>' — hence '<s>kasambaka-jātāḥ</s>' (those born as kasambakas). '<s>Kṛṣṇā</s>' is a particular type of grass. In the vernacular language, [it is called] '<s>kaṇḍā</s>.' That too, when not removed from the field, destroys the field. '<s>Nirjātiḥ</s>' means 'production.' 'Having the production of <s>kṛṣṇā</s>' — hence '<s>kṛṣṇānirjātikāḥ</s>.' For '<s>kṛṣṇa</s>' [here means] a black serpent, which is venomous; when it comes into contact with those bitten, it makes them venomous. '<s>Anayena</s>' means 'by the wrong path of learning, faith, and so on from those [teachers].' '<s>Vyasanam</s>' is the suffering of the hells and so on. '<s>Āgāḍham ābādham</s>' means great affliction. '<s>Nigacchet spṛśet</s>' means 'would reach' — that is, 'would attain' — this is the meaning. '<s>Ālokaḥ</s>' is the knowledge of the fruition of the action in question. '<s>Śuklāṃśaḥ</s>' means the portion of wholesome [karma]. Through connection with that, one is '<s>śuklāṃśikaḥ</s>' (one having a wholesome portion). '<s>Samavadhānaṃ</s>' is connection. The rest is easily understood. Thus [concludes the section on] the deterioration of <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: evamukta ityādi / atra mārādhiṣṭhita ityādinā mārādhiṣṭhānamuktam / gambhīreṣu dharmeṣvanadhimuktisteṣu śraddhāprasādābhāvenoktā //
body.translated_text: 'Thus spoken' and so forth. Here, by '<s>Māra</s>-influenced' and so on, the influence of <s>Māra</s> is stated. Non-aspiration toward the profound <s>dharmas</s> is stated as the absence of faith and confidence in them.

body.text: punaraparamityādinā caturo hetūnāha / ātmotkarṣī parapaṃsako doṣāntaraprekṣītyeko rāśiḥ / ata evāha / ebhirapi caturbhirityādi / tadatra dharmavyasanahetavaḥ ṣaḍuktāḥ / śāstre tu saṃkṣepataścatvāraḥ / śeṣāṇāṃ skandhādyabhiniveśe 'ntarbhāvāt / ātmotkarṣaṇādināṃ skandhādyabhiniveśe /
body.translated_text: By 'Moreover' and so on, he states four causes. 'Self-exalting, disparaging others, looking for faults in others' — this is one group. Therefore he says: 'By these four also' and so on. Here, six causes of the deterioration of <s>Dharma</s> have been stated. But in the treatise, there are only four in brief — because the remaining ones are subsumed under grasping at <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) and so on. Self-exalting and the rest [are subsumed] under grasping at <s>skandhas</s> and so on.

body.text: nirhāraparivarto 'yaṃ saptāṅgasya nirhārasya dyotanāt / tathāpi nirayagranthasya bahutvānnirayaparivarta ityucyate //
body.translated_text: This is the '<s>Nirhāra-parivarta</s>' (Chapter on Carrying Forth), because it illuminates the seven-limbed carrying forth. Nevertheless, because of the abundance of material on the hells, it is called the '<s>Niraya-parivarta</s>' (Chapter on the Hells).

body.text: āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ sāratamānāmni pañjikāyāṃ ratnākaraśāntiviracitāyāṃ saptamaḥ parivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: In the <s>Pañjikā</s> commentary named <s>Sāratamā</s>, composed by <s>Ratnākaraśānti</s>, on the noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s> — this is the seventh chapter.

body.text: 8. viśuddhiparivarto nāmāṣṭamaḥ /
body.translated_text: 8. The eighth [chapter] is named the '<s>Viśuddhi-parivarta</s>' (Chapter on Purification).

body.text: lokottarasya bhāvanāmārgasya nirhāraḥ saptamaparivartenoktaḥ / śuddhiraṣṭamasyādau vaktavyā / tasyāḥ śuddherduradhimocatāṃ tāvadāha / atha khalvityādinā / anarthikeneti mandacchandena / upastabdho vismitaḥ / aśuśrūṣaṇā-aparipacchakajātīyeneti kalyāṇamitreṣu subhūteḥ praśnaḥ / kiyadagambhīretyādi / kiyatā gambhīrā yato duradhimocetyarthaḥ / bhagavata uttaraṃ rūpaṃ subhūta ityādinā / rūpādayo rūpādīnāṃ ca pūrvāparamadhyāntā abaddhā amuktāḥ svabhāvenādhvatrayeṇa ca niḥsvabhāvatvādityarthaḥ / paramaduradhimoceti paramagambhīratvāditi bhāvaḥ / prākpravṛtto hi bandhaḥ prāgaśuddhiḥ paścāttannivṛttilakṣaṇo mokṣaḥ śuddhiriti prasiddham / iha tu bandhamokṣayoratyantābhāvaḥ śuddhiriti paramagambhīraṃ viśuddhilakṣaṇaṃ śāstre-
body.translated_text: The carrying forth of the supramundane <s>bhāvanā-mārga</s> (path of cultivation) was stated in the seventh chapter. The purification [pertaining to] the eighth [chapter] is to be stated at its beginning. To express the difficulty of aspiring to that purification, he says 'Now then' and so forth. '<s>Anarthikena</s>' means 'by one of feeble aspiration.' '<s>Upastabdhaḥ</s>' means 'astonished.' 'Of the kind that lacks attentiveness and receptivity' — this is <s>Subhūti's</s> question regarding <s>kalyāṇamitras</s> (spiritual friends).
