'How profound' and so on: 'how much profundity is there that it is difficult to aspire to?' — this is the meaning. The <s>Bhagavān's</s> reply [begins with] '<s>Rūpaṃ Subhūte</s>' and so on. Form and so on — the prior, subsequent, and middle aspects of form and so on are unbound and unreleased, by their own nature and by the three times, because they are without self-nature — this is the meaning. '[It is] extremely difficult to aspire to' — because it is supremely profound — this is the import. For it is well known that bondage that arose previously is prior impurity, and the cessation of that afterward, which has the character of release, is purification. But here, the complete absence of both bondage and release is purification — thus the characteristic of purification is supremely profound. In the treatise —

children.translated_text: 'And the purification of the fruit is nothing but the purification of form and so on; of these two,
because the non-severedness is undifferentiated' — thus purification is declared. // [2-26] //

body.text: 'phalaśuddhiḥ' sādhyā / sā ca 'rūpādiśuddhireva' / yasmāt 'tayoḥ' 'abhinnācchinnatā' 'iti śuddhirudīritā' / śuddherlakṣaṇamuktaṃ sutre / katamasyāḥ śuddheḥ? yasyāduradhimocatvamuktam / tatkasya hetorityādi / tadasyā duradhimocatvaṃ kuta ityarthaḥ / uttaraṃ yetyādinā / yata idaṃ tasyā lakṣaṇamiti bhāvaḥ / advayaṃ tādātmyāt / advaidhīkāramavyabhicārāt / anayoreva nirdeśo abhinnamacchinnamiti / yetyanuvādaḥ seti vidhiḥ / anūdyamānaśca dharmo vidhīyamāne niyata iti khyāpitaḥ / ataḥ sāmānyādhikaraṇādabhinnamubhayam / anyonyaniyamādanyonyāvyabhicāraḥ / tasmādacchinnamubhayam / tadevaṃ yaiva skandhānāmekaśo viśuddhiḥ saiva phalaviśuddhiḥ / yaiva phalaviśuddhiḥ saivetarā / anyonyāvyabhicārāt / anyonyaliṅgatā / sa cāvyabhicārastādātmyāt / ata āha / phalaviśuddhita ityādi punaraparamityataḥ prāk iti viśuddhilakṣaṇam /
body.translated_text: 'The purification of the fruit' is what is to be accomplished. And that is 'nothing but the purification of form and so on.' Because 'of these two' the 'non-severedness' is 'undifferentiated' — 'thus purification is declared.' The characteristic of purification has been stated in the <s>sūtra</s>. Of which purification? That whose difficulty of aspiring to has been stated. 'What is the reason?' and so forth: 'whence comes the difficulty of aspiring to it?' — this is the meaning. The answer is 'Because that which' and so on: 'because this is its characteristic' — this is the import. 'Non-dual' — because of identity. 'Non-bifurcated' — because of non-deviation. The exposition of just these two is 'undifferentiated' and 'unsevered.' 'That which' is the corroborative [clause]; 'that' is the injunctive. And the <s>dharma</s> being corroborated is determined in the one being enjoined — thus it is declared. Therefore, from the co-referentiality, both are undifferentiated. From their mutual determination, their mutual non-deviation [is established]. Therefore both are unsevered. Thus indeed, whichever is the purification of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) individually, that itself is the purification of the fruit. Whichever is the purification of the fruit, that itself is the other. Because of mutual non-deviation, there is mutual logical indication. And that non-deviation is because of identity. Therefore he says: 'From the purification of the fruit' and so forth, [continuing] up to just before 'Moreover' — this is the characteristic of purification.

body.text: viśuddhibhedāśvatvāro mahatyorbhagavatyoruktāḥ sarvasaṃgrahārtham / asyāṃ tu noktā bodhisattvamārgādhikārāt / mārgasya viśuddhirucyate / sa ca bhūmau bhūmau navavidho mṛdumṛdvādibhedādadhimātrādhimātrādibhedāt / navavidhasyaiva doṣasya pratipakṣeṇa
body.translated_text: The divisions of purification — four are stated in the two great [texts, i.e., the <s>Mahāprajñāpāramitā</s> and the <s>Bhagavatī</s>] for the purpose of comprehensive inclusion. But in this [text] they are not stated, because the topic here is the <s>bodhisattva</s> path. The purification of the path is what is spoken of. And that is ninefold on each <s>bhūmi</s> (stage), due to the division into mild-mild and so on, [or equivalently] due to the division into intense-intense and so on. [This is] because each of the nine types of fault has its counterpart antidote.

body.text: bhūmayastu śuddhestāścaiva nava / kāmadhāturaṣṭau ca rūpārūpyāḥ / ataḥ śāstram-
body.translated_text: And the stages of purification are precisely nine — [corresponding to] the desire realm, the eight [levels of] form and formless [realms].

children.translated_text: 'The path beginning with mild-mild is the purification on the nine stages,
as the antidote to faults beginning with the most intense-intense.' // 2-30 //

body.text: ato navavidhaṃ mārgamāha / punaraparamityādinā atyantānupapattirityataḥ prāk / sarvajñateti sarvākārajñatā / tasyā viśuddhirdvividhā / yā skandhānāmekaśo viśuddhiḥ pāramitānāṃ ca sā sarvākārajñatāviśuddhiḥ / yā ca tasyāḥ sā teṣāmityekā sarvākārajñatāviśuddhiḥ / adhyātmaśūnyatādīnāṃ skandhādīnāṃ ca yāvadāveṇikabuddhadharmāṇamekaśo yā viśuddhiryā ca prajñāpāramitāyā yā ca sarvākārajñatāyāḥ sarvametadabhinnamacchinnamiti dvitīyā sarvākārajñatāviśuddhiḥ / tadasyāṃ na paṭhyate upalakṣaṇatvāttadgrāhyam / iti mṛdumṛdumārgo mṛdumadhyaśca //
body.translated_text: Therefore he states the ninefold path, beginning with 'Moreover' and so on, up to just before 'absolute impossibility.' '<s>Sarvajñatā</s>' means <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience in all aspects). Its purification is twofold: that which is the purification of the <s>skandhas</s> individually and of the <s>pāramitās</s> — that is the purification of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>; and that which is the purification of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> [itself] is [the purification] of those — this is the first [type of] <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>-purification. The purification individually of <s>adhyātma-śūnyatā</s> (internal emptiness) and the rest, of <s>skandhas</s> and the rest, up to the unique <s>Buddha</s>-qualities, and the purification of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, and the purification of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> — all of this is undifferentiated and unsevered — this is the second [type of] <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>-purification. In that [text], this is not explicitly read, but since it is implied, it should be understood. Thus [these are] the mild-mild path and the mild-moderate [path].

body.text: atha khalvityādi / itaḥ prabhṛti prajñāpāramiteti prajñāpāramitāviśuddhirityarthaḥ / sā gambhīrā duravagāhā sarvadharmāṇāṃ viśuddhatvādatyantaśūnyatvāditi mṛdvadhimārgaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Now then' and so on. From this point onward, '<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>' means 'the purification of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>' — this is the meaning. That is profound and unfathomable, because all <s>dharmas</s> are purified, because they are ultimately empty — this is the mild-intense path.

body.text: sāvabhāsakarī tamopahā viśuddhatvātsarvadharmāṇāmiti madhyamṛdumārgaḥ //
body.translated_text: It is self-luminous and dispels darkness, because all <s>dharmas</s> are purified — this is the moderate-mild path.

body.text: sā āloko darśanaṃ viśuddhatvāditi madhyamadhyo mārgaḥ //
body.translated_text: It is light and vision, because [all dharmas] are purified — this is the moderate-moderate path.

body.text: sā apratisandhirasaṃkrāntirbhavāntare viśuddhatvāditi madhyādhimātro mārgaḥ //
body.translated_text: It is without reconnection and without transmigration to another existence, because [all dharmas] are purified — this is the moderate-intense path.

body.text: sā asaṃkleśo viśuddhitvāt prakṛtyasaṃkliṣṭatvātsarvadharmāṇāmityadhimātramṛdumārgaḥ //
body.translated_text: It is non-defilement, because [all dharmas] are purified, because all <s>dharmas</s> are by nature undefiled — this is the intense-mild path.

body.text: sā aprāptiranabhisamayo viśuddhatvāt sarvadharmāṇāmaprāpteranabhisamayāccetyadhimātramadhyo mārgaḥ //
body.translated_text: It is non-attainment and non-realization, because all <s>dharmas</s> are purified, because of the non-attainment and non-realization [of all dharmas] — this is the intense-moderate path.

body.text: sā anabhinirvṛttirviśuddhatvāt anabhinirvṛttatvāt sarvadharmāṇāmityadhimātrādhimātro mārgaḥ //
body.translated_text: It is non-production, because [all dharmas] are purified, because all <s>dharmas</s> are unproduced — this is the intense-intense path.

body.text: āha / atyantānupapattirityādikamāmārgajñatāparisamāpteḥ / ataḥ śāstram-
body.translated_text: He says: 'Absolute impossibility' and so forth, [continuing] up to the completion of [the section on] <s>mārgajñatā</s> (knowledge of the path). Therefore the treatise [states] —

children.translated_text: 'Being the antidote to the three realms, and the equality of the measurer and the measured,

children.text: mārgaḥ sa ceṣyate tasya codyasya parihārataḥ // 2-31 //
children.translated_text: that is accepted as the path — by the resolution of objections against it.' // 2-31 //

body.text: tasyāṃ 'tridhātupratipakṣatvaṃ' yadāha / atyantānupapattiḥ prajñāpāramitā / kāmadhātvādiṣu viśuddhatvāt / kāmadhātvādiṣvabhāvānupapatteḥ iti tridhātupratipakṣatvam /
body.translated_text: Therein, 'being the antidote to the three realms' — as he says: 'Absolute impossibility is <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>' — because [all dharmas] are purified in the desire realm and the rest; because of the impossibility of [inherent] existence in the desire realm and the rest — this is the antidote-nature with respect to the three realms.

body.text: atra ca 'samatā mānameyayoḥ' / yadāha / āhetyādi / na jāna tīti na gṛṇhāti / na saṃjānīta iti na vikalpayati / sphuṭīkartu praśnaḥ kiṃ punarityādi / uttaraṃ rūpamityādi / viśuddhatyādityatyantasamatvāt / tadevaṃ yathā syājjñeyaṃ grāhyaṃ na bhavati tathaiṣāpi tasya grāhikā na bhavatīti jñeyamānasamatā /
body.translated_text: And here, 'the equality of the measurer and the measured' — as he says 'He says' and so forth. 'Does not know' means 'does not grasp.' 'Does not cognize' means 'does not conceptualize.' To make it explicit, the question [is] 'What then?' and so on. The answer [is] 'Form' and so on — 'because [all dharmas] are purified,' because of their absolute equality. Thus, just as the knowable, being graspable, does not exist [as such], so too this [<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>] does not exist as its grasper — this is the equality of the knowable and the knower.

body.text: yoyaṃ viśuddhilakṣaṇo bhāvanāmārga ukto na sa yuktaḥ / yato 'sminnaṣṭau doṣā ityata āha / 'mārgaḥ sa ceṣyate tasya codyasya parihārataḥ / ' cakāro 'vadhāraṇe / bhinnakramaśca / codyasyeti jātāvekavacanam / bhāvanāmārga eva sa iṣyate tadīyacodyānāmita ūrdhvaṃ parihārādityarthaḥ / atra ca siddhānta eva kākvā kuta etaditi hetusāpekṣāścodyasūcanādyāni / siddhāntahetavaḥ parihārāḥ / tatra dve codye śāriputrasya ṣaṭ subhūteḥ /
body.translated_text: This <s>bhāvanā-mārga</s> (path of cultivation) described as having the characteristic of purification is not correct, because eight faults apply to it — therefore he says: 'That is accepted as the path, by the resolution of objections against it.' The particle '<s>ca</s>' is for emphasis. And the order is rearranged. '<s>Codyasya</s>' (of the objection) — the singular is used in a generic sense. That <s>bhāvanā-mārga</s> itself is accepted, [established] by the resolution of objections raised against it henceforth — this is the meaning. And herein, the thesis itself [serves as] a rhetorical question through [the expression] 'How can this be?' [indicating] expectation of the reason. The hints of objections and so on are theses. The reasons for the theses are the resolutions. Therein, two objections belong to <s>Śāriputra</s>, and six to <s>Subhūti</s>.

body.text: nāpakāraṃ karoti na copakāramiti siddhāntaḥ / sa kutaḥ? yadi hyakiṃcitkarī kathaṃ sā mārga iti codyam / viśuddhitvāditi parihāraḥ / sarvajñatā hi dharmadhātuviśuddhiḥ sa ca viśuddhaḥ prakṛtiśuddhaḥ / tataḥ sā asyākiñcitkarī / kevalamāgantukāvaraṇakṣayaṃ [prati] vyāpriyate / na gṛṇhāti na tyajatīti siddhāntaḥ / sa kutaḥ? yadi hyasau gṛṇhāti vikalpaḥ syāt / atha na gṝṇhāti prajñaiva na syāditi codyam / viśuddhatvādi parihāraḥ / yathā hi yata evāsau dharmān dharmalakṣaṇairna paśyatyata eva dharmatayā paśyati / ata eva viśuddhaḥ / viśuddhatvāt na gṛṇhāti na ca tyajatīti / skandhaviśuddhitaḥ phalaviśuddhiḥ sarvajñatāviśuddhiścoktā / sā ca teṣāṃ viśuddhirātmaviśuddhyā / yathā hyātmano viśuddhiratyantamasattā tathā teṣāmapīti siddhāntaḥ / sa kutaḥ? yadi hi skandhaphalasarvajñatānāmatyantamasattā tadaitā(te)na kiñciditi codyam / atyantaviśuddhitvāditi parihāraḥ / atyantamasanta eva dharmāḥ svalakṣaṇaiḥ / ata eva tacchūnyatālakṣaṇayā dharmatayā santītyarthaḥ / ātmaviśuddhito na prāptirnābhisamaya iti siddhāntaḥ / codyaṃ purvavat / atyantaviśuddhatvāditi parihāraḥ / yata eva dharmalakṣaṇairdharmā atyantamasantaḥ tata eva dharmatayā santaḥ / sā ca prakṛtyaiva śuddhā tacchuddhireva ca sarvajñateti na tasyāḥ prāptirnābhisamaya ityarthaḥ / ātmāparyantatayā rūpavedanā dīnāmaparyantateti siddhāntaḥ / sa kutaḥ / dṛśyate
body.translated_text: 'It neither harms nor helps' — this is the thesis. Whence [is this known]? If indeed it does nothing, how is it a path? — this is the objection. 'Because of purification' — this is the resolution. For <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience) is the purification of <s>dharmadhātu</s> (the realm of dharmas), and that is purified, [meaning] naturally pure. Therefore, this [<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>] does nothing to it. It merely operates toward the destruction of adventitious obscurations. 'It does not grasp, nor does it abandon' — this is the thesis. Whence? If indeed it grasps, there would be conceptual construction. But if it does not grasp, it would not be <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) at all — this is the objection. 'Because of purification' and so on — this is the resolution. For just as, precisely because it does not see <s>dharmas</s> by their [individual] characteristics, it sees [them] by their <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature) — precisely for that reason it is purified. Because of purification, it neither grasps nor abandons. The purification of the fruit from the purification of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), and the purification of <s>sarvajñatā</s>, have been stated. And the purification of those [skandhas and sarvajñatā] is through the purification of the self. For just as the purification of the self is absolute non-existence, so too of those — this is the thesis. Whence? If indeed there is absolute non-existence of the <s>skandhas</s>, the fruit, and <s>sarvajñatā</s>, then [there would be] nothing at all by this — this is the objection. 'Because of absolute purification' — this is the resolution. <s>Dharmas</s> are absolutely non-existent by their own characteristics alone. Precisely for that reason, they exist by their <s>dharmatā</s>, which has the characteristic of the emptiness of those — this is the meaning. 'From the purification of the self, there is neither attainment nor realization' — this is the thesis. The objection is as before. 'Because of absolute purification' — this is the resolution. Precisely because <s>dharmas</s> are absolutely non-existent by their [individual] characteristics, they exist by their <s>dharmatā</s>. And that is by its very nature pure. That very purification is <s>sarvajñatā</s> — therefore there is neither attainment of it nor realization — this is the meaning. 'By the boundlessness of the self, form, feeling, and so on are boundless' — this is the thesis. Whence [is this known]?

body.text: hi skandhādīnāṃ paryantastatkathamaparyantā iti codyam / atyantaviśuddhatvāditi parihāraḥ / yathā hyātmano 'tyantamasattā tathā rūpādīnāmapi svalakṣaṇaiḥ / tato 'satāṃ teṣāṃ kaḥ paryantaḥ? dharmatayā santīti cet .............paryantaḥ / sarvadharmasāmānyalakṣaṇatvāt rūpādikasya / na, bhedasyāparamārthatvāt / tasmādyaiva rūpādiviśuddhiḥ saiva phalaviśuddhiḥ sarvajñatāviśuddhiḥ prajñāpāramitāviśuddhiścetyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: For the boundedness of the <s>skandhas</s> and so on is observed — so how are they boundless? — this is the objection. 'Because of absolute purification' — this is the resolution. Just as there is absolute non-existence of the self, so too of form and so on by their own characteristics. Therefore, of those that are non-existent, what bound can there be? If [one argues] 'they exist by their <s>dharmatā</s>' — [even then there is no] bound, because the <s>dharmatā</s> of form and so on has the general characteristic of all <s>dharmas</s>. No, because differentiation is not ultimately real. Therefore, whichever is the purification of form and so on, that itself is the purification of the fruit, the purification of <s>sarvajñatā</s>, and the purification of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> — this is the meaning.

body.text: ya evamatyantāsattayā sarvadharmāṇāṃ avabodhaḥ sa prajñāpāramiteti siddhāntaḥ / sa kutaḥ?....................bodho na tarhi sātyantaviśuddhiriti codyam / atyantaviśuddhitvāditi parihāraḥ /
body.translated_text: That comprehension which [arises] through the absolute non-existence of all <s>dharmas</s> — that is <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> — this is the thesis. Whence [is this known]? ... The comprehension [would] not [make] it absolutely purified — this is the objection. 'Because of absolute purification' — this is the resolution.

body.text: evaṃ samāptā aṣṭāvatyantabhāvanāmārgamārgajñatādhikārāḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus the eight [objections and resolutions concerning] the supramundane <s>bhāvanā-mārga</s> (path of cultivation) pertaining to the topic of <s>mārgajñatā</s> (knowledge of the path) are completed.

body.text: prathamaparivartena sarvākārajñatoktā / ito 'rdhasaptamaiḥ parivartairmārjñatā / aṣṭamanavamayoḥ parivartayorardhābhyāṃ sarvajñatā vaktavyā / tasya aṣṭau vastūni / yathoktaṃ prāk
body.translated_text: By the first chapter, <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience in all aspects) was stated. By six and a half chapters from here onward, <s>mārgajñatā</s> (knowledge of the path) [was stated]. By the two halves of the eighth and ninth chapters, <s>sarvajñatā</s> (knowledge of all) is to be stated. Its topics are eight, as stated previously:

children.text: prajñayā na bhave sthānaṃ kṛpayā na śame sthitiḥ /
children.translated_text: By <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) there is no abiding in <s>bhava</s> (existence); by <s>kṛpā</s> (compassion) there is no remaining in <s>śama</s> (quiescence);
Without <s>upāya</s> (skillful means) there is remoteness; with <s>upāya</s> there is nearness. // 1-10 //
The adversary and its antidote, the practice, and the equality thereof —
The path of vision of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and others — thus it is accepted as <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience). // 1-11 //

body.text: iti / atra śāstram-
body.translated_text: Thus. Herein the treatise [states] —

children.text: nāpare na pare tīre nāntarāle tayoḥ sthitā /
children.translated_text: Neither on this shore, nor on the far shore, nor standing in between them,
<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is understood through the equality of the paths. // 3-1 //

body.text: 'prajñāpāramitā' iti sarvajñatā / 'nāpare tīre ' iti saṃsāre / 'na pare tīre ' iti nirvāṇe / nāpi tayorantarāle sthitā' / trayaṃ nopalabhyata ityarthaḥ / kuta ityāha / 'adhvānāṃ samatāyogād' iti / dharmatayāpyadhvasamatvāt / dharmāṇāṃ ca yathālakṣaṇamanupalambhat / etadāha / āyuṣmān ityādinā / seti samādhānaṃ pūrvamuktatvāt / iyamiti sarvajñatākhyena viśeṣeṇa vaktavyatvāt / ata evāha / viprakṛteti / viśeṣeṇa prakṛtatvāt vartamānatvādvā / athavā kuto na sthitā? yato viprakṛtā trayānupalambhena bādhitā / bhagavān hetumāha / atyantaviśuddhatvāditi / svairlakṣaṇairasatāṃ dharmāṇāṃ dharmatālakṣaṇena nityaviśuddhatvādityarthaḥ / śrāvakāstu
body.translated_text: '<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>' means <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience). 'Not on this shore' means in <s>saṃsāra</s>. 'Not on the far shore' means in <s>nirvāṇa</s>. 'Nor standing in between them' — the three are not apprehended — this is the meaning. Why? He says: 'Through the equality of the paths.' Because of the equality of the paths even by <s>dharmatā</s> (the nature of dharmas). And because of the non-apprehension of <s>dharmas</s> according to their [individual] characteristics. This he states beginning with 'Venerable' and so on. 'She' — the resolution has been stated previously. 'This' — because it is to be spoken of with the specific designation of <s>sarvajñatā</s>. Therefore he says '<s>viprakṛtā</s>' — because it is specifically elaborated, or because it is present [now]. Alternatively, why does she not abide? Because she is '<s>viprakṛtā</s>' — negated by the non-apprehension of the three. The <s>Bhagavān</s> states the reason: 'Because of absolute purity.' Because <s>dharmas</s>, whose own characteristics are non-existent, are eternally pure by the characteristic of <s>dharmatā</s> — this is the meaning. But the <s>Śrāvakas</s>,

body.text: svaduḥkhakṣayamātraiṣiṇaḥ saṃsāraṃ parikalpya tenātyantamudvignā nirvāṇaṃ parikalpya tasminnatīvotkaṇṭhitā laghu ladhveva parinirvānti / naivaṃ bodhisatvāḥ, sarvasattvārthaṃ niruttarabodhikāmā iti saṃsāranirvāṇāpratiṣṭhatā //
body.translated_text: who desire merely the cessation of their own suffering, having conceptualized <s>saṃsāra</s>, are utterly distressed by it, and having conceptualized <s>nirvāṇa</s>, are exceedingly eager for it, and quickly attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are not like this, for they desire unsurpassed awakening for the benefit of all beings — hence [they have] non-abiding in either <s>saṃsāra</s> or <s>nirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: śāstram-
body.translated_text: The treatise [states] —

body.text: anupāyena dūraṃ sā sanimittopalambhataḥ /
body.translated_text: Without <s>upāya</s> (skillful means) she is far away, because of apprehension with signs;

body.text: 'sanimittaṃ upalambho 'nupāyaḥ' / tena sā dūrībhavati / tadāha / āyuṣmānityādi / evamapīti nāmatopi nimittatopi / riñciṣyati tyakṣyati nāmataḥ / dūrīkariṣyati nimittataḥ / iti dūrībhāvaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Apprehension with signs is non-skillful means.' By that she becomes distant. This he states beginning with 'Venerable' and so on. 'Even so' means even by name or by sign. '<s>Riñciṣyati</s>' — will abandon by name. '<s>Dūrīkariṣyati</s>' — will make distant by sign. Thus [is explained] the becoming distant.

body.text: upāyakauśalenāsyāḥ samyagāsannatoditā // 3-2 //
body.translated_text: Through <s>upāyakauśalya</s> (skillful means) her proper nearness is declared. // 3-2 //

body.text: niḥsaṅgā vṛttiḥ samyagupāyakauśalam / tenāsannībhavati / tadāha / evamukta ityādinā / saṅgaḥ saktirabhūtaparikalpaḥ / sā nāmato syānnimittatopi / tayorapi bhūte 'rthe 'bhāvāt / ākhyātā ṣoḍaśabhirdṛṣṭimārgalakṣaṇaiḥ / sunirdiṣṭā dvādaśabhiḥ prayogaiḥ / supariniṣṭhitā saṃsāranirvāṇayorapratiṣṭhānāt / supariśuddhā saṅgakoṭīnāṃ vivarjanāt / yatra hīti vākyālaṅkāre / nāmetyāścarye / imepi saṅgā iti saṅgāpi vakṣyamāṇāḥ / ataḥ saṅgavarjanamupāyakauśalamityā sannībhāvatā /
body.translated_text: Non-attached conduct is proper <s>upāyakauśalya</s> (skillful means). By that she becomes near. This he states beginning with 'Thus spoken' and so on. '<s>Saṅga</s>' (attachment) is clinging, which is false conceptualization. That would be by name or by sign. [There is no attachment to] either, because of the non-existence of a real object. 'Explained' — by sixteen characteristics of the path of vision. 'Well-elucidated' — by twelve practices. 'Well-established' — because of non-abiding in either <s>saṃsāra</s> or <s>nirvāṇa</s>. 'Well-purified' — because of the abandonment of the points of attachment. 'Where indeed' — a literary ornament. 'Name' — [an exclamation of] wonder. 'Even these attachments' — the attachments to be discussed. Therefore, the abandonment of attachment is <s>upāyakauśalya</s> — thus the nearness.

body.text: te punaḥ saṅgāḥ sāmānyenoktāḥ / viśeṣato vaktavyāḥ / ataḥ śāstram-
body.translated_text: Those attachments have been stated in general. They are to be explained in detail. Therefore the treatise [states] —

children.translated_text: In the emptiness of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) such as <s>rūpa</s> (form), in <s>dharmas</s> belonging to the three times,
In giving and so on, and in the wings of awakening — the notion regarding the practice is the adversary. // 3-3 //

body.text: rūpādīnāṃ sarvadharmāṇāṃ skandho rāśiḥ / tasya śūnyatāyāṃ traiyadhvike paradharmesu pāramitā bodhipakṣyaviṣayāyāṃ ca caryāyāṃ yā 'saṃjñā' nāmato nimittato vā sā 'vipakṣatā' / svārthe tal devatāvat / sa vipakṣaḥ sa saṅga ityarthaḥ /
body.translated_text: The aggregate, that is, the collection, of all <s>dharmas</s> beginning with <s>rūpa</s> (form). In the emptiness of that, in the <s>dharmas</s> of others pertaining to the three times, in the practice that pertains to the <s>pāramitās</s> and the wings of awakening — whatever 'notion' there is, whether by name or by sign, that is 'the adversary.' The suffix '<s>tal</s>' is in the sense of the abstract. That adversary, that attachment — this is the meaning.

body.text: etadāha / atha khalvityādinā / asyāṃ bhagavatyāṃ 'caryāsaṃjñā' na paṭhyate / sā paṭhitānāmupalakṣaṇatvānnocyate / dānapāramitāṃ yāvatprajñāpāramitāṃ smṛtyupasthānāni yāvadāryāṣṭaṅgamārga carāmīti sañjānīte saṅga iti / asyāmadhikasaṅgamāha / iyantamityādinā / ye saṅgāsta uktāḥ / yathā te saṅgāstannoktam / tataḥ śakrasya praśno 'tha khalvityādinā / paryāyeṇeti prakāreṇa / idaṃ tu prathamaṃ bodhicittamiti / eṣa vikalpaḥ prathamaḥ saṅgaḥ / bodhau pariṇāmayāmīti /
body.translated_text: This he states beginning with 'Now then' and so on. In this holy [text], the 'notion regarding the practice' is not read [explicitly]. It is not stated because it serves as an indicator of those that are read. 'I practice the <s>dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of giving) up to <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom), the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness) up to the noble eightfold path' — such a notion is attachment. Regarding the additional attachment in this [text], he says beginning with 'This much' and so on. Those attachments that have been stated — how those are attachments has not been stated. Then comes <s>Śakra's</s> question beginning with 'Now then' and so on. '<s>Paryāyeṇa</s>' means 'by way of.' 'But this is the first thought of awakening' — this discrimination is the first attachment. 'I dedicate to awakening' —

body.text: evaṃ vikalpya pariṇāmanā dvitīyaḥ / kathamimau saṅgau? tasya cittasyātītatvenāsattvāt / bodheścānāgatatvena / cittaprakṛtiḥ sadāstīti cedāha / na cetyādi / na śakyā iti nityasya pariṇāmāyogāt / tasmādubhau vikalpau / abhūtakalpanāt / śeṣāstu yathā saṅgāstathā purvamevoktam /
body.translated_text: Having thus discriminated, the dedication is the second [attachment]. How are these two attachments? Because that mind, being past, is non-existent. And because <s>bodhi</s> (awakening), being future, [is non-existent]. If one says 'the nature of mind always exists,' he says 'No' and so on. 'It cannot be' — because of the impossibility of transforming what is permanent. Therefore both are discriminations — because they are false conceptualizations. The rest — how they are attachments — has been stated previously.

body.text: saṅgāḥ teṣāṃ varjanamarvāguktaṃ bhavati / ataḥ śāstram-
body.translated_text: The attachments and their abandonment have been stated earlier. Therefore the treatise [states] —

body.text:
dānādiṣvanahaṅkāraḥ pareṣāṃ tanniyojanam /
saṅgaḥ koṭī niṣedho 'yaṃ
body.translated_text: Non-ego-making regarding giving and so on, and the directing of others therein — attachment at its point, this is the prohibition.

body.text: 'dānādiṣvanahaṃkāraḥ' sāmarthyāt / pūrvamuktaḥ / 'pareṣāṃ tanniyojanaṃ' āha tasmāttarhītyādinā / tasmāditi svayaṃ saṅgavivarjanāt kāraṇāt / tarhīti pareṣāṃ sandarśanādikāle / sandarśayateti pūrvamaśrutavataḥ rocayatā / samādāpayateti / anuṣṭhānāya samyag grāhayatā / samprahaṣayateti mantharān protsāhayatā / sampraharṣayateti / ārabdhavīryān sādhukāraiḥ / bhutānugamaḥ saṅgatyāgāt / evaṃ samādāya teṣvaparāddhaṃ (?) darśayitumāha / evamityādi / na kṣiṇotīti buddheṣvaparāddhaṃ na karoti / svayambhūtānugame 'nuśaṃsamāha / imāścetyādinā / tadevaṃ yanna 'dānādiṣvanahaṅkāro ' yanna'pareṣāṃ tatra niyojanaṃ', eṣa dvividhaḥ saṅgakoṭīnāṃ sthūlānāṃ niṣedhaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Non-ego-making regarding giving and so on' — by implication, has been stated previously. 'The directing of others therein' — he says beginning with 'Therefore then' and so on. 'Therefore' — because of the cause of one's own abandonment of attachment. 'Then' — at the time of showing and so on to others. 'Shows' means making those who have not previously heard appreciate it. 'Causes to undertake' means making them properly grasp it for practice. 'Encourages' means urging the sluggish. 'Inspires' means cheering on those who have begun their effort with words of praise. 'Conformity with reality' — from the abandonment of attachment. Having thus undertaken, he says beginning with 'Thus' and so on to show the transgression regarding those. 'Does not diminish' means does not commit a transgression against the <s>Buddhas</s>. Regarding the benefit of one's own conformity with reality, he says beginning with 'And these' and so on. Thus, that which is not 'non-ego-making regarding giving and so on' and not 'the directing of others therein' — this is the twofold prohibition of the gross points of attachment.

body.text: śāstram /
body.translated_text: The treatise [states] —

body.text: sūkṣmaḥ saṅgo jīnādiṣu // 3-4 //
body.translated_text: The subtle attachment is toward the <s>Jinas</s> (Conquerors) and so on. // 3-4 //

body.text: buddhādau yaḥ saṅgaḥ sa sūkṣmaḥ / tamāha atha khalu bhagavānityādinā / na sā śakyā pariṇāmayitumiti tryadhvaprasaṅgāt / na nimittīkartuṃ nārambaṇīkartumiti / apūrvatvenākāraṇatvāt / durbodhatvācca / yato na sā dṛṣṭaśrutamatavijñāta cakṣuṣā śrotreṇa ghrāṇajivhākāyairmanasā vāpratītatvāt yathā kramam / gambhīrā prajñāpāramitā viviktatvāt / prakṛtigambhīrā prakṛtiviviktatvāt / ataśca namaskaraṇiyā / sarvadharmā api prakṛtiviviktāḥ / yā teṣāṃ prakṛtiviviktatā sā prajñāpāramitā / yato 'kṛtāste bhagavatābhisambuddhāḥ / yataste prakṛtyaiva na kiñcit / yā caiṣāṃ prakṛtiḥ sābhāvaḥ / yaścābhāvaḥ saiṣāṃ prakṛtiḥ / ekalakṣaṇatvāt yadutālakṣaṇatvāt / evamaśeṣāḥ saṅgakoṭayo vivirjitā bhavanti / acintyā cintātītatvāt / nahi sā rūpaṃ na vedanā yāvanna buddhadharmāḥ / śeṣaṃ subodham /
body.translated_text: The attachment toward the <s>Buddhas</s> and so on — that is subtle. This he states beginning with 'Now then, the <s>Bhagavān</s>' and so on. 'She cannot be dedicated' — because of the consequence regarding the three times. 'She cannot be made a sign, nor made an object' — because of the absence of a cause for what is unprecedented, and because of being difficult to comprehend. Since she is not experienced through the seen, heard, thought, or cognized — through the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind respectively. <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is 'profound' because of being isolated. 'Profound by nature' because of being isolated by nature. And therefore she is to be honored. All <s>dharmas</s> too are isolated by nature. That natural isolation of them is <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>. Because 'they are uncreated, [yet] fully awakened to by the <s>Bhagavān</s>.' Because by their very nature they are nothing whatsoever. And that which is their nature — that is their non-existence. And that which is their non-existence — that is their nature. Because of having a single characteristic, namely, being without characteristics. Thus all the points of attachment are completely abandoned. [She is] 'inconceivable' because she transcends thought. For she is not <s>rūpa</s> (form), not <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), and so on up to not the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>. The rest is easily understood.

body.text: nāpi sā dṛṣṭaśrutamatavijñātetyādinā yaduktaṃ / atra śāstram
body.translated_text: With regard to what was stated beginning with 'Nor is she the seen, heard, thought, or cognized' and so on — herein the treatise [states] —

children.translated_text: The profundity of that, by its very nature, because of the isolation of the course of <s>dharmas</s>;
The knowledge that has a single nature among <s>dharmas</s> is the abandonment of attachment. // 3-5 //
By the negation of the seen and so on, the difficulty of comprehending her is declared;
Because of not being cognized through <s>rūpa</s> (form) and so on, her inconceivability is accepted. // 3-6 //

body.text: 'vivekād' iti viviktatvāt / 'dharmapaddhatiḥ' dharmarāśiḥ / dharmāṇāṃ jñānamiti sambandhaḥ / ekā teṣāṃ prakṛtiḥ khyātiryasmiṃstathoktam / tanna vipakṣapratipakṣau vaktavyau / saṅgāsaṅgau kasmāduktau? ataḥ śāstram-
body.translated_text: 'Isolation' means being isolated. 'The course of <s>dharmas</s>' is the collection of <s>dharmas</s>. 'Knowledge of <s>dharmas</s>' — this is the connection. 'That in which there is a single nature, that is, manifestation, of those — that is so called.' Then the adversary and the antidote need not be stated. Why then are attachment and non-attachment stated? Therefore the treatise [states] —

children.text: evaṃ kṛtvā yathokto vai jñeyaḥ sarvajñatānaye /
children.translated_text: Having done thus, as stated, one should know in the method of <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience) —
This is the complete division of the adversary and the antidote. // 3-7 //

body.text: 'evaṃ kṛtvā' iti saṅgāsaṅgavyapadeśaṃ kṛtvā / 'yathoktaṃ' iti / yathokto vibhāgaḥ 'sarvajñatānaye ' / sarvo 'yaṃ 'vipakṣapratipakṣayoḥ' veditavyaḥ / tathā hi / saṅga upalambho vikalpaḥ / asaṅgo 'nupalambhaḥ prajñāpāramitā / tasmātsaṅgo vipakṣo 'saṅgaḥ pratipakṣaḥ iti vipakṣapratipakṣau //
body.translated_text: 'Having done thus' means having made the designation of attachment and non-attachment. 'As stated' — the division as stated 'in the method of <s>sarvajñatā</s>' — all this is to be understood as pertaining to 'the adversary and the antidote.' For indeed, attachment is apprehension, conceptualization. Non-attachment is non-apprehension, <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>. Therefore attachment is the adversary, and non-attachment is the antidote — thus [are explained] the adversary and the antidote.

body.text: prayogastatsamatā ca vaktavyā / ataḥ śāstram-
body.translated_text: The practice and its equality are to be stated. Therefore the treatise [states] —

children.translated_text: Regarding <s>rūpa</s> (form) and so on, their impermanence and so on, their non-fulfillment and fulfillment,
And regarding their non-attachment — the practice with respect to the conduct is through negation. // 3-8 //

children.text: avikāro na kartā ca prayogo duṣkarastridhā /
children.translated_text: Non-modification and non-agency — the practice is difficult in three ways;
Because of attaining the fruit as befitting, it is fruitful and as desired. // 3-9 //

body.text: aparapratyayo yaśca saptadhā khyātivedakaḥ /
body.translated_text: And that which is independent of others, sevenfold, making known the manifestation —

body.text: 'tadanityādau' iti / rūpāderanityatvanityatvādau / iṭ radhādibhya iti iñcāparipuriḥ / pariprapūreḥ bhāva iti pariprapūraḥ asaṅgaḥ / vivakṣāvaśāt tacchabdena saṅgo gṛhyate / samāhāradvandvaḥ / saṅgāsaṅgatvayorityarthaḥ / ekaśeṣastu na bhavatyana(?)bhidhānāt / 'rūpādau' rūpāderanityatvanityatvādau / rūpāderaparipūrṇatvaparipūrṇatvayoḥ / rūpādeḥ saṅgāsaṅgayośca / yā 'caryā' caraṇaṃ tatpratiṣedhena prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caraṇaṃ 'prayogo ' rūpādyādiṣu / amī ca catvāraḥ / uttare cāṣṭau / 'avikāro 'kartā' / [uddeśa] duṣkaraḥ kāritraduṣkaro 'bandhyo 'parapratyayaḥ saptadhākhyātivedakaśceti dvādaśavidhaḥ prayogaḥ / atastaṃ pṛcchati / āha / tena hītyādinā kathaṃ caritavyamiti / kathaṃ prayogaḥ kartavyaḥ? atra rūpādayaḥ sarvadharmāḥ / skandhāstūpalakṣaṇam / rūpe yāvadvijñāne na caratīti rūpādīnna sañjānīta ityarthaḥ / tadā carati prajñāpāramitāyāmiti rūpādiprayogaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Their impermanence and so on' means regarding the impermanence and non-impermanence and so on of <s>rūpa</s> (form) and so on. The augment '<s>iṭ</s>' is from [the rule] '<s>radhādibhya</s>' and so on, and '<s>iñ</s>' is [for] non-fulfillment — '<s>pariprapūra</s>' is the abstract noun of '<s>pariprapūri</s>' — [which means] non-attachment. By the intention of the speaker, the word '<s>tad</s>' refers to attachment. [This is] a collective compound. The meaning is: of both attachment and non-attachment. But a single-remainder [compound] is not possible because of non-denotation. 'Regarding <s>rūpa</s> and so on' — regarding the impermanence and non-impermanence and so on of <s>rūpa</s> and so on; regarding the non-fulfillment and fulfillment of <s>rūpa</s> and so on; and regarding the attachment and non-attachment of <s>rūpa</s> and so on. That 'practice,' the conduct — its negation in <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is the 'practice' regarding <s>rūpa</s> and so on. And these are four. And the subsequent eight: 'non-modification,' 'non-agency,' [and from the] outline: 'difficult' — difficult in execution, 'fruitful,' 'independent of others,' 'sevenfold,' 'making known the manifestation' — thus the practice is twelvefold. Therefore he asks about it. He says beginning with 'Therefore then' and so on — 'How should one practice?' — how should the practice be carried out? Herein, '<s>rūpa</s> and so on' refers to all <s>dharmas</s>. The <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) are merely an indication. 'Does not practice with respect to <s>rūpa</s>, up to <s>vijñāna</s>' means does not conceptualize <s>rūpa</s> and so on — this is the meaning. 'Then one practices <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>' — thus is the practice regarding <s>rūpa</s> and so on.

body.text: sa cedrūpamanityaṃ yāvadvijñānamanityamiti na carati / tathā nityamiti sukhamiti śūnyamityaśūnyamiti ātmeti anātmeti śubhamiti aśubhamiti na carati tadā carati prajñapāramitāyāmiti rūpādyanityatvādiprayogaḥ //
body.translated_text: If one does not practice [thinking] '<s>rūpa</s> is impermanent,' up to '<s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) is impermanent,' and likewise does not practice [thinking] 'permanent,' 'pleasant,' 'empty,' 'non-empty,' 'self,' 'non-self,' 'pure,' 'impure' — then one practices <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> — thus is the practice regarding the impermanence and so on of <s>rūpa</s> and so on.

body.text: sa cedrūpaṃ yāvadvijñānaṃ aparipūrṇa paripūrṇa vā / tadeva rūpāderaparipūrṇatvaṃ paripūrṇatvaṃ tadeva rūpādi iti na carati / tadā caratyasyāmityaparipuriparipūriprayogaḥ //
body.translated_text: If one does not practice [thinking] '<s>rūpa</s> up to <s>vijñāna</s> is unfulfilled or fulfilled,' [thinking] 'that very non-fulfillment of <s>rūpa</s> and so on is the fulfillment, and that very [fulfillment] is <s>rūpa</s> and so on' — then one practices in this [<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>] — thus is the practice of non-fulfillment and fulfillment.

body.text: evamukta ityādinā caturthaṃ prastauti / bhagavāṃstamāha / rūpaṃ sasaṅgamityādinā caritavyāntena / atraiva evaṃ carannityādinānuśaṃsamāha / asaktetyādi / sarvasaṅgābhāvādasaktā / tato na baddhā kleśaistraidhātuke / tato na muktā kleśaiḥ / na samatikrāntā traidhātukam / evaṃ hītyādinopasaṃhāraḥ / iti rūpādisaṅgāsaṅgaprayogaḥ //
body.translated_text: Beginning with 'Thus spoken' and so on, he introduces the fourth [type]. The <s>Bhagavān</s> tells him beginning with '<s>Rūpa</s> with attachment' and so on, up to 'how one should practice.' Herein itself, beginning with 'Practicing thus' and so on, he states the benefit. Beginning with 'Unattached' and so on — because of the absence of all attachment, one is unattached; therefore not bound by afflictions in the three realms; therefore not freed from afflictions; [and therefore] not transcending the three realms. Beginning with 'For thus' and so on is the conclusion. Thus is the practice regarding attachment and non-attachment of <s>rūpa</s> and so on.

body.text: subhūtirāhetyādinā parihāṇirbhavedityedantena pañcamaḥ / hānivṛddhayorabhāvādavikāratā / ākāśavat / varṇo guṇaḥ / ityavikāraprayogaḥ //
body.translated_text: Beginning with '<s>Subhūti</s> said' and so on, up to 'there would be decline' — [this is] the fifth [type]. Because of the non-existence of decrease and increase, there is non-modification — like space. '<s>Varṇa</s>' (color) [here means] quality. Thus is the practice of non-modification.

body.text: tadyathāpītyādinā sthaviraśabdāt prāk ṣaṣṭhaḥ / saṃkliśyate śabdasyārthaḥ pratihanyata(?) iti / dvitīyasyānunīyata iti / deśanayā hānivṛddhayorakaraṇādakartṛprayogaḥ //
body.translated_text: Beginning with 'Just as' and so on, up to before the word '<s>Sthavira</s>' (Elder) — [this is] the sixth [type]. The meaning of the word '<s>saṃkliśyate</s>' (is defiled) is 'is harmed.' Of the second, '<s>anunīyate</s>' (is appeased). Because of not causing decrease or increase through teaching — [this is] the practice of non-agency.

body.text: sthavira ityādinābhisamboddhakāmāntena saptamaḥ / trividhāṃ duṣkaratāṃ vaktuṃ bhagavatī bhāvanāduṣkaratāmanuṣaṅgādāha / tasyāmeva sthitānāmuddeśāderduṣkaratvāt / caranniti śamathena / na saṃsīdati layena / notplavate auddhatyena / na pratyudāvartate nivartate / ākāśabhāvanā / ekalakṣaṇatāpratibhāsāt / ayaṃ sannāha iti yaḥ sarvasattvārthāya samyaksambodhau / ākāśeneti / ākāśanibhena yogena tadatyāgāt / tato duṣkaratā sattvānāmanupalambhādanantācca / viśvārthamuddiśya bodheḥ / sa coddeśaḥ sannāha ityuddeśaduṣkaratāprayogaḥ //
body.translated_text: By [the passage beginning with] '<s>sthavira</s>' (elder) and ending with 'wishing to awaken' — the seventh [section]. In order to state the threefold difficulty, the <s>Bhagavatī</s> states the difficulty of meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) by way of connection. Because for those established in that [meditation], instruction and the like are difficult. 'Walking' — by <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding). 'Does not sink' — by [avoidance of] <s>laya</s> (torpor). 'Does not float up' — by [avoidance of] <s>auddhatya</s> (agitation). 'Does not turn back' — does not revert. [This is] the meditation on space. Because of the appearance as having a single characteristic. 'This is the armor' — that which [is directed] toward perfect awakening for the sake of all beings. 'By space' — by a yoga resembling space, because of not abandoning that. Hence the difficulty [arises] from the non-apprehension of beings and from [their] infinity. 'Aiming at universal welfare' — [directed toward] awakening. And that aim is the 'armor' — thus the application of the difficulty of the aim (<s>uddeśaduṣkaratā</s>).

body.text: ākāśamityādinā sannahyata ityetadantenāṣṭamaḥ / uccairgatirvibandhapātanaṃ(?) parimocanam / uccairnayanamutkṣepaḥ / etāvānsattvārthāya prayogaḥ / sa ca duṣkaraḥ / ākāśavatsattvarāśeranantatvādarūpitvādadravyatrvācceti prayogaduṣkaratāprayogaḥ //
body.translated_text: By [the passage from] 'space' and so on, ending with 'dons the armor' — the eighth [section]. 'High going' is the removal of obstruction (?); liberation. 'Raising high' is elevation. This much is the practice for the sake of beings. And that is difficult. Because the mass of beings is like space — infinite, formless, and insubstantial — thus the application of the difficulty of practice (<s>prayogaduṣkaratā</s>).

body.text: atha khalvityādinātha khalvityataḥ prāṅnavamaḥ / prayogasya phalaṃ kāritram / sāṃkleśikadharmaprahāṇaṃ vaiyavadānikadharmotpādanaṃ ca / tadubhayaṃ duṣkaraṃ bhagavatyā tayorakaraṇāditi kāritraduṣkaratāprayogaḥ //
body.translated_text: By [the passage beginning with] 'now then' and ending with [the next] 'now then' — the ninth [section]. The fruit of practice is <s>kāritra</s> (conduct). The abandonment of defiling <s>dharmas</s> (<s>sāṃkleśikadharma</s>) and the production of purifying <s>dharmas</s> (<s>vaiyavadānikadharma</s>). Both of those are difficult, because the <s>Bhagavatī</s> does not perform either — thus the application of the difficulty of conduct (<s>kāritraduṣkaratā</s>).

body.text: atha khalvityādinātha khalvityataḥ prāgdaśamaḥ / ya evaṃ yogamāpatsyata iti hetvavasthāyām / kva sa iti phalāvasthāyām / ākāśa iti ākāśaṃ tārāpatham / iha tu tatsādharmyādanuttarā bodhiḥ / abhyavakāśaṃ bhūmerūpariṣṭhādacchannamarūpiṣṭhānam / iha tu tatsādharmyāddhīnabodhiḥ / tadubhayaṃ phalam / tasya yathābhavyaṃ prāpteravandhyaprayogaḥ //
body.translated_text: By [the passage beginning with] 'now then' and ending with [the next] 'now then' — the tenth [section]. 'One who will thus attain the yoga' — this is in the stage of the cause (<s>hetvavasthā</s>). 'Where is he?' — this is in the stage of the fruit (<s>phalāvasthā</s>). 'Space' means the path of the stars. But here, by analogy with that, [it means] <s>anuttarā bodhi</s> (unsurpassed awakening). 'Open ground' (<s>abhyavakāśa</s>) — an uncovered place above the earth. But here, by analogy with that, [it means] <s>hīnabodhi</s> (lesser awakening). Both of those are the fruit. Because of the attainment of that [fruit] in accordance with [the practitioner's] nature — the practice is not fruitless.

body.text: atha khalvityādinā avatāramityetadantamekādaśaḥ / śakrastasya bodhisattvasya rakṣāvaraṇaguptiṃ kartukāmaḥ / rakṣāvaraṇābhyāṃ sahitā guptistathoktā / taṃ subhūtirāha / kimenaṃ prāpsyasīti / sa āha neti / tataḥ kimityāha evamityādi / evamiti / sarvadharmānupalambhena / śeṣaṃ sugamam / evamanvayavyatirekābhyāṃ prajñāpāramitādhīnaiva tasya rakṣā na parādhīnetyaparapratyayaprayogaḥ //
body.translated_text: By [the passage beginning with] 'now then' and ending with '<s>avatāra</s>' (opportunity) — the eleventh [section]. <s>Śakra</s>, wishing to perform the protection, guarding, and safekeeping of that <s>bodhisattva</s>. Safekeeping accompanied by protection and guarding is thus termed. <s>Subhūti</s> says to him: 'Will you attain this?' He says: 'No.' 'Then what?' — he says 'thus' and so forth. 'Thus' means through the non-apprehension of all <s>dharmas</s>. The rest is easily understood. Thus, through both positive concomitance and negative concomitance [it is shown that] his protection depends solely on <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, not on anything else — this is the application of [the principle of] non-dependence on others.

body.text: api cetyādinā parijānātītyetadantena dvādaśaḥ / mahatyorbhagavatyoḥ saptadhā khyātiḥ paṭhyate / "māyāmarīcisvapnapratiśrutkāpratibhāsapratibimbagandharvanagaropamāḥ sarvadharmāḥ" iti / yā ca saptadhā khyātiḥ sā sarvāpyanvākhyātiḥ / dvayaśūnyena sthitānāṃ sarvadhārmāṇāṃ paratantrasvabhāvānāṃ dvayena khyātiḥ / sā ekenāpi dṛṣṭāntena śakyā darśayitum / yathā hi śabde 'sati pratiśabdo 'samprakhyāti / tathā sati dvayaśūnye svabhāve dharmā asatā dvayarūpeṇa prakhyāntīti / tasmādasyāṃ bhagavatyāṃ pratiśrutkopamataiva paṭhyate / ata enāṃ prati śāstrapāṭho 'nyathā kartavyaḥ / 'yo 'paro khyātivedakaḥ' iti / dvividhā prajñāpāramitā lokottarā śuddhā laukikī ca / yathoktaṃ drumavikalpapraveśāyāṃ dhāraṇyāma avikalpadhātupratiṣṭhito bodhisattvo jñeyanirviśiṣṭena jñānena ākāśasamatalānsarvadharmān paśyati / tatpṛṣṭhalabdhena māyāmarīcisvapnapratibhāsapratiśrutkāpratibimbodakacandranirmitasamānsarvadharmānpaśyati" iti / ato lokottaramadhikṛtyāha / ākāśasyetyādi /
body.translated_text: By [the passage from] 'moreover' and ending with 'fully knows' — the twelfth [section]. In the two great [texts of the <s>Bhagavatī</s>], sevenfold appearance (<s>khyāti</s>) is taught: 'All <s>dharmas</s> are like illusion (<s>māyā</s>), a mirage (<s>marīci</s>), a dream (<s>svapna</s>), an echo (<s>pratiśrutkā</s>), a reflection (<s>pratibhāsa</s>), a mirror-image (<s>pratibimba</s>), and a city of <s>gandharvas</s> (celestial musicians).' And this sevenfold appearance is entirely 'counter-appearance' (<s>anvākhyāti</s>). Of all <s>dharmas</s> that exist as empty of duality — having the <s>paratantra-svabhāva</s> (dependent nature) — the appearance by means of duality [constitutes this]. That can be shown even by a single example: just as when there is no [original] sound, an echo does not appear — so too, when the nature empty of duality exists, <s>dharmas</s> appear by means of non-existent dual form. Therefore, in this <s>Bhagavatī</s>, only the simile of the echo is taught. Hence the textual reading of the <s>śāstra</s> regarding this must be understood differently: 'the other one who knows appearance.' <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is twofold: supramundane-pure and mundane. As stated in the <s>Drumavikalprapraveśa-dhāraṇī</s>: 'A <s>bodhisattva</s> established in the realm of non-conceptualization sees all <s>dharmas</s> as equal to the surface of space, through a knowledge undifferentiated from what is to be known. Through the subsequently-obtained [knowledge], he sees all <s>dharmas</s> as like illusion, mirage, dream, reflection, echo, mirror-image, moon-in-water, and magical creation.' Therefore, regarding the supramundane, he says 'of space' and so on.

body.text: śuddhalaukikīmadhikṛtyāha / tatkimityādi / parijānātīti / tataḥ kiṃ tasya rakṣaṇīyaṃ pratibhāsānāmalīkatvāditi bhāvaḥ / ityanyathākhyātivedakaprayogaḥ //
body.translated_text: Regarding the pure mundane [prajñāpāramitā], he says 'what then?' and so on. 'Fully knows' — then what is there to be protected by it, since the appearances are unreal? — this is the import. Thus the application of knowing otherwise-appearance.

body.text: uktāḥ prayogāḥ / prayogasamatā vaktavyā / tāmadhikṛtya śāstram-
body.translated_text: The applications have been stated. The equality of application (<s>prayogasamatā</s>) is to be stated. Regarding that, the <s>śāstra</s> [says]:

body.text: caturdhāmananā tasya rūpādau samatā matā // 3-10 //
body.translated_text: 'The fourfold non-thinking regarding form etc. is considered the equality [of application].' (3-10)

body.text: rūpādyadhiṣṭhānaṃ caturvidhamamananaṃ prayogasamatetyarthaḥ / yathoktaṃ mahatyoḥ / "rūpaṃ na manyate / rūpeṇa na manyate / rūpaṃ mameti na manyate / rūpepi na manyate / evaṃ vedanādiṣu" iti / imāṃ tu bhagavatīṃ prati śāstrapāṭho 'nyathā kartavyaḥ-
body.translated_text: The fourfold non-thinking (<s>amananā</s>) with form etc. as its basis is the equality of application — this is the meaning. As stated in the two great [texts]: 'One does not think form. One does not think by means of form. One does not think "form is mine." One does not think in form. Likewise regarding feeling and the rest.' But regarding this <s>Bhagavatī</s>, the textual reading of the <s>śāstra</s> must be understood differently:

body.text: aṣṭadhāmananaṃ tasya rūpādau samatā mata /
body.translated_text: 'The eightfold non-thinking regarding form etc. is considered the equality [of application].'

body.text: caturdhā grāhakasya caturdhā ca grāhyasyākalpanaṃ prayogasamatetyarthaḥ / tadāha ataścetyādinā atha khalvityataḥ prāk / ataśceti yataḥ pratiśrutkopamāḥ sarvadharmāḥ / ataśca tāniti sarvadharmān na manyate bhāvābhiniveśena / na samanupaśyati dṛṣṭyā / na jānāti grahaṇena / na sañjānīte kalpanayā / iti caturvidhaṃ grāhakakalpanam / tathaiva grāhyavikalpanamāha te cetyādinā / na vedyanta iti sattvena na manyante / na saṃdṛśyanta iti na dṛśyante / na saṃvidyanta iti na gṛhyante / nopalabhyanta iti na vikalpyante / ityevamaṣṭadhā grāhyagrāhakayorakalpanena viharatīti sarvadharmeṣu carati / tataḥ kiṃ syādityāha sa cedityādi subodham / iti prayogasamatā /
body.translated_text: The fourfold [non-thinking] of the grasper and the fourfold [non-thinking] of the grasped — the non-conceptualizing [of both] is the equality of application — this is the meaning. He states that, from 'therefore' and so on up to [the next] 'now then.' 'Therefore' — because all <s>dharmas</s> are like an echo. 'And therefore those' — all <s>dharmas</s> — 'does not think' — with attachment to [their] existence. 'Does not perceive' — with [ordinary] view. 'Does not know' — with grasping. 'Does not cognize' — with conceptualization. Thus the fourfold conceptualization of the grasper. Likewise he states the conceptualization of the grasped, from 'they' and so on: 'Are not felt' — not thought of by [their] being. 'Are not seen' — not perceived. 'Are not found' — not grasped. 'Are not apprehended' — not conceptualized. Thus, through the eightfold non-conceptualization of both grasped and grasper, 'one abides' — one moves among all <s>dharmas</s>. 'What then would result?' — to this he says 'if' and so on — easily understood. Thus the equality of application.

body.text: prayogasamatānusaṅgāddeśanāsamatāyāmapyasyāṃ deśanāyāmabhisampratyayārthamāha / atha khalvityādinā āparivartasamāpteḥ / lokadhātāviti.......... /
body.translated_text: By way of connection with the equality of application, regarding the equality of teaching (<s>deśanāsamatā</s>) also in this teaching, for the purpose of conviction, he says 'now then' and so on up to the completion of the chapter. 'In the world-realm'............

body.text: viśuddhiparivarto nāmāṣṭamaḥ parivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: The eighth chapter, named the 'Purification Chapter' (<s>Viśuddhiparivarta</s>).

body.text: 9. stutiparivarto nāma navamaḥ /
body.translated_text: 9. The ninth [chapter], named the 'Praise Chapter' (<s>Stutiparivarta</s>).

children.translated_text: Aspects, together with applications, qualities, faults together with characteristics,
the liberation-portion and penetration-portion, the trainee, the irreversible assembly. (1-12)

body.text: samatā
body.translated_text: Equality,

children.translated_text: And the purification of the field of existence and cessation, the unsurpassed,
the awakening to all aspects — this is [the chapter] with skill in means. (1-13)

body.text: ākārāḥ, prayogāḥ, guṇāḥ, doṣāḥ, lakṣaṇāni, mokṣabhāgīyaṃ, nirvedhabhāgīya, avaivartikasaṃghaḥ, saṃsāranirvāṇasamatā, buddhakṣetrapariśuddhiḥ, upāyakauśalaṃ cetyekādaśavastūni sarvākārābhisambodhaḥ / yathoddeśaṃ nirdeśāt prathamata ākārāṇāṃ nirdeśaḥ /
body.translated_text: Aspects, applications, qualities, faults, characteristics, the liberation-portion, the penetration-portion, the irreversible <s>saṅgha</s> (assembly), the equality of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) and <s>nirvāṇa</s> (cessation), the purification of the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field), and <s>upāyakauśala</s> (skill in means) — these eleven topics constitute the 'awakening to all aspects' (<s>sarvākārābhisambodha</s>). According to the order of enumeration, by way of detailed exposition, the aspects are explained first.

children.translated_text: The definition of 'aspects' is: the modes of knowing things.

children.text: sarvajñatānāṃ traividhyāt trividhā eva te matāḥ // 4-1 //
children.translated_text: Because of the threefold [division] of <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omnisciences), they too are considered threefold. (4-1)

body.text: 'vastu' ālambanaṃ catuḥsatyādi / tasya 'jñānam' / tasya 'prakārāḥ' / yaiḥ prakāraistatparikṣepaḥ teṣāṃ 'ākārā' iti lakṣaṇatvāt / 'sarvajñatānāṃ' iti jātau vahuvacanam / sarvajñatāyā ityarthaḥ / kathaṃ tasyāstraividhyam? sarvajñatā mārgajñatā sarvākārajñatā ceti / tatrādau sarvajñatākārāḥ saptaviṃśatiḥ / śāstram-
body.translated_text: 'Thing' (<s>vastu</s>) is the object (<s>ālambana</s>) — the four truths and so on. Its 'knowledge.' Its 'modes' — by which modes that [knowledge] is encompassed — their being 'aspects' is their definition. 'Of the <s>sarvajñatās</s>' — the plural is in the generic sense; the meaning is 'of <s>sarvajñatā</s>.' How is it threefold? <s>Sarvajñatā</s> (knowledge of all), <s>mārgajñatā</s> (knowledge of paths), and <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects). Therein, first, the aspects of <s>sarvajñatā</s> are twenty-seven. The <s>śāstra</s> [says]:

children.translated_text: Beginning from the 'non-existent aspect' up to the 'immovable form,'

children.text: catvāraḥ prati satyaṃ te mārge pañcadaśa smṛtāḥ // 4-2 //
children.translated_text: four for each truth, and fifteen in the path — thus they are declared. (4-2)

body.text: asatpāramiteyamiti asadākārāmārabhya yāvadacalapāramiteyamityacalākārāḥ / teṣu catvāraścatvāro duḥkhasamudayanirodhasatyeṣu pariviṣṭāḥ / pañcadaśa mārgasatye / asadākārapāramitā / asatpāramitā / evamuttarā api sarvāḥ / tatra duḥkhe catvāraḥasatsamatāvivikta-anavamṛdya /
body.translated_text: 'This is the non-existent <s>pāramitā</s> (perfection)' — beginning from the non-existent aspect up to 'this is the immovable <s>pāramitā</s>' — the immovable aspects. Among those, four for each of the truths of suffering, origination, and cessation are assigned. Fifteen [are assigned] to the truth of the path. 'The <s>pāramitā</s> of the non-existent aspect' — 'the <s>pāramitā</s> of non-existence.' Similarly all the subsequent ones also. Therein, four for suffering: non-existence, equality, isolation, non-crushability.

body.text: ākāśasamatāmiti / ākāśavadrūpāderasattām / yathā hyākāśasya rūpidravyābhāvo lakṣaṇaṃ tathā rūpādīnāṃ svalakṣaṇābhāvaḥ / sarvadharmānupalabdhisamatāmiti / sarvadharmānupalabdhireva sukhaduḥkhayoḥ samatā / atyantaśūnyatāmiti / pudgalena svabhāvena ca śūnyatāmityarthaḥ / bādhakaṃ duḥkhaṃ bādhyatvādavamṛdya ātmā / anavamṛdyānātmā / tadākāratvāt anavamṛdyapāramitā / sarvadharmāṇāṃ bādhyabādhakānāmanupalabdhitāṃ nirūpalambhatāṃ [upādāya] /
body.translated_text: 'The equality of space' — the non-existence of form etc. like space. For just as the defining characteristic of space is the absence of material substance, so too the absence of own-characteristics of form etc. 'The equality of the non-apprehension of all <s>dharmas</s>' — the non-apprehension of all <s>dharmas</s> is itself the equality of pleasure and pain. 'Absolute emptiness' — emptiness of person and own-nature — this is the meaning. Suffering that afflicts is 'crushable' (<s>avamṛdya</s>) because of being afflicted — the self. 'Non-crushable' (<s>anavamṛdya</s>) is non-self. Because of having that as its aspect, [it is called] the <s>pāramitā</s> of non-crushability. 'Regarding the non-apprehension-ness of all <s>dharmas</s>, of the afflicted and the afflictor.'

body.text: samudaye catvāraḥ / tathā hi- padaṃ hetuḥ prāktanāḥ skandhāḥ / svabhāva ātmano bhāvaḥ / kāyakarma / vacanaṃ vākkarma / nāma manaskarma kleśāśca / eṣāmabhāvo yathākramaṃ.....asvabhāvaḥ / ......tadākāratvāttatpāramitā / anāmāśaroratāmiti / nāma arūpiṇaḥ skandhāḥ / śarīraṃ rūpaskandhaḥ / tayorabhāvo 'nāmaśarīratā / gatyāgatī kāyakarma / tadabhāvo 'nāgatiragatiśca / vācāṃ heturvikalpaḥ / tadabhāvo 'vikalpatā /
body.translated_text: Four for origination. Thus: '<s>pada</s>' (basis) is the cause — the former aggregates. '<s>Svabhāva</s>' (own-nature) is the being of the self. Bodily action. 'Speech' is verbal action. 'Name' is mental action, and the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). The non-existence of these, respectively..... non-own-nature. Because of having that as its aspect, that <s>pāramitā</s>. 'Non-name-and-body-ness' — 'name' is the formless aggregates; 'body' is the form-aggregate. The non-existence of both is non-name-and-body-ness. Going and coming is bodily action; its non-existence is non-going and non-coming. The cause of speech is conceptualization; its non-existence is non-conceptualization.

body.text: nirodhe catvāraḥ / tathā hyasau gamanaṃ vā syāt grāhyaṃ vā kṣayo vā utpattirvā / eṣāmabhāvo yathākramaṃ agamanaṃ, asaṃhāryaṃ, akṣayaḥ, anupapattiḥ / tadākāratvāttatpāramitā / sarvadharmāṇāmagamanatā gatyabhāvaḥ / sarvadharmāṇāmagrāhyatā / na hi dharmo dharmaṃ gṛṇhātīti / kṣaya eva dharmaḥ / tena yogaḥ / tadabhāvādakṣayadharmayogatā / abhinirvṛttirutpattiḥ / tadabhāvādanirvṛttitā /
body.translated_text: Four for cessation. Thus, that [cessation] would be either going, or graspable, or destruction, or arising. The non-existence of these, respectively: non-going, non-removable, non-destruction, non-arising. Because of having that as its aspect, that <s>pāramitā</s>. 'The non-going-ness of all <s>dharmas</s>' — the absence of movement. 'The non-graspability of all <s>dharmas</s>' — for indeed, one <s>dharma</s> does not grasp another <s>dharma</s>. '<s>Dharma</s> is indeed destruction' — that is its connection. Because of the absence of that, 'the state of having the yoga of non-destruction-dharma.' '<s>Abhinirvṛtti</s>' is arising; because of its absence, 'non-production-ness.'

body.text: mārge pañcadaśa- akāraka-ajānaka-apaśyaka-asaṃkrānti-avinaya-svapna-pratiśrutka-pratibhāsa-marīci-māyā-asaṃkleśa-avyavadāna-anupalepa-aprapañca amananā-acalā / akārakādyākāratvāttatpāramitā / akārako mārgastena kārakānupalabdheḥ / ajānakāpaśyako mārgastena jānakapaśyakānupalabdheḥ / asaṃkrāntirmārgastena cyutyupapattyorayogadarśanāt / avinayo mārgastena tryadhvasamāyā dharmaprakṛteravinayāt / svapnāditulyatvāt svapno mārgaḥ vinaiva draṣṭāramandhaḥkārāt (?) / pratiśrutko mārgaḥ / asati śabde śabdopalambhāt / pratibhāsaḥ pratibimbaṃ sa mārgaḥ / asatyarthe 'rthadarśanāt / marīcirmārgaḥ / tajjalaskandhavadasato lokadhātoḥ pratibhāsāt / māyā mārgo nimittāpratibhāsāt / anutpādavijñāpanatāmiti / yataḥ pañcabhirapyebhiranutpādo mārga ādīpyate / pratibhāsahetumantareṇa tathā tathā pratibhāsāt / asaṃkleśo mārgastena rāgādyanupalabdheḥ / avyavadānaṃ mārgastena kliṣṭasattvānupalabdheḥ / anupalepo mārgaḥ / ākāśavannirupalepasya dharmadhātostena darśanāt / aprapañco mārgaḥ prapañcapratipakṣatvāt / amananā mārgaḥ / sarvamananāsamuddhātitvāt / acalo mārgaḥ / dharmadhātuśarīratvena śāśvatatvāt / iti sarvajñatākārāḥ //
body.translated_text: Fifteen for the path: non-agent, non-knower, non-seer, non-transference, non-training, dream, echo, reflection, mirage, illusion, non-defilement, non-purification, non-staining, non-proliferation, non-thinking, immovable. Because of having the non-agent aspect and so on, that <s>pāramitā</s>. The path is a non-agent, because of the non-apprehension of an agent therein. The path is a non-knower and non-seer, because of the non-apprehension of a knower and seer therein. The path is non-transference, because of seeing the impossibility of death and rebirth therein. The path is non-training, because of the non-training of the <s>dharma</s>-nature that is the same in the three times therein. The path is a dream, because [it operates] without a seer, from darkness (?). The path is an echo, because of the apprehension of sound when there is no [original] sound. The path is a reflection (<s>pratibhāsa</s>), because of the seeing of an object when there is no [real] object. The path is a mirage, because of the appearance of a non-existent world-realm like a body of water from that [mirage]. The path is illusion, because of the non-appearance of the [actual] cause. 'The nature of manifesting non-arising' — because by all five of these [examples], non-arising is illuminated as the path, due to the appearance in such-and-such ways without a cause of appearance. The path is non-defilement, because of the non-apprehension of desire etc. therein. The path is non-purification, because of the non-apprehension of defiled beings therein. The path is non-staining, because of seeing the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (reality-realm) as free from staining like space. The path is non-proliferation, because of being the antidote to proliferation. The path is non-thinking, because of the complete transcendence of all thinking. The path is immovable, because of being eternal through having the <s>dharmadhātu</s> as its body. Thus the aspects of <s>sarvajñatā</s>.

body.text: atha mārgajñatākārāḥ ṣaṭtriṃśat /
body.translated_text: Now, the aspects of <s>mārgajñatā</s> (path-knowledge) — thirty-six.

children.text: hetau mārga ca duḥkhe ca nirodhe ca yathākramam /
children.translated_text: In the cause, in the path, in suffering, and in cessation, respectively,

children.text: aṣṭau te sapta pañceti ṣoḍaśeti ca kīrtitāḥ // 4-3 //
children.translated_text: they are declared as eight, seven, five, and sixteen. (4-3)

body.text: hetuḥ samudayaḥ / ataḥ samudayamārgau prathamata uktau phalopāyatvāt / duḥkhanirodhau paścāduktau phalatvāt teṣvākārā yathākramam / 'aṣṭau sapta pañca ṣoḍaśeti ca kīrtītāḥ' sūtre tatra samudaye 'ṣṭau-virāga-asamutthāna-śāntanirdoṣa-niṣkleśa-niḥsattva / kathaṃ tadaṣṭau? yato nirdoṣe tritayaḥ-arāga-adveṣa-amoha / prāktanā hi pañcaskandhāḥ samudayaḥ / rajyante 'sminniti rāgaḥ / parikalpitaḥ svabhāvo dharmāṇām / vigato rāgo 'smāditi virāgaḥ samudayaḥ / sarvadharmāṇāmavitathatāmiti / vitathena kalpitena svabhāvena śūnyatām / samutthānaṃ kleśaheturvikalpaḥ / tasyāsminnabhāvādasamutthānaḥ samudayaḥ / sarvadharmāṇāṃ nirvikalpatāmiti / agrāhakatvāt / śāntaḥ samudayaḥ / nirodha ityarthaḥ / tatkutaḥ? sarveṣāṃ
body.translated_text: The cause is the origin (<s>samudaya</s>). Hence, the origin and the path are stated first, because they are the means to the fruit. Suffering and cessation are stated afterward, because they are the fruit. The aspects in those, in order: 'eight, seven, five, and sixteen are proclaimed' in the <s>sūtra</s>. Therein, in the origin, eight: <s>virāga</s> (dispassion), <s>asamutthāna</s> (non-arising), <s>śānta</s> (peaceful), <s>nirdoṣa</s> (faultless), <s>niṣkleśa</s> (affliction-free), <s>niḥsattva</s> (being-free). How are those eight? Because in 'faultless' there is a triad: <s>arāga</s> (without passion), <s>adveṣa</s> (without aversion), <s>amoha</s> (without delusion). For the five prior aggregates are the origin. '<s>Rāga</s>' (passion) — because one is attached to it; it is the imagined nature of <s>dharmas</s>. '<s>Virāga</s>' — because passion is absent from it — this is the origin. 'The non-falsity of all <s>dharmas</s>' means their emptiness of the false, imagined nature. '<s>Samutthāna</s>' (arising) is conceptual discrimination, the cause of afflictions. Because of its absence therein, the origin is '<s>asamutthāna</s>' (non-arising). 'The non-conceptual nature of all <s>dharmas</s>' — because of being non-grasping. The origin is 'peaceful.' The meaning is cessation. From what? Of all

body.text: dharmanimittānāṃ dharmapratibhāsānāṃ paramārthapratibhāse 'nupalabdheḥ / ata eva arāgapāramitā adoṣapāramitā amohapāramitā ca / guṇapāramitāmiti rāgadoṣamohakṣayapāramitām / sarvakleśābhāvānniṣkleśaḥ samudayaḥ / parikalpāsattāmiti grāhakāsattām / api ca sarvatra kliṣṭaḥ syād duḥkhī ca (?) / tadabhāvānniḥsattvaḥ samudayaḥ / bhūtakoṭitāmiti dharmapudgalaśūnyatām /
body.translated_text: <s>dharma</s>-signs, <s>dharma</s>-appearances — because of non-apprehension in the appearance of ultimate reality. Therefore indeed, the perfection of non-passion, the perfection of non-fault, and the perfection of non-delusion. 'The perfection of qualities' means the perfection of the exhaustion of passion, fault, and delusion. Because of the absence of all afflictions, the origin is '<s>niṣkleśa</s>' (affliction-free). 'The non-existence of imagined constructs' means the non-existence of the grasper. Moreover, everywhere one would be afflicted and suffering. Because of the absence of that, the origin is '<s>niḥsattva</s>' (being-free). 'The reality-limit nature' means the emptiness of <s>dharmas</s> and persons.

body.text: mārge sapteti- apramāṇa-antadvayānanugama-asambhinna-aparamṛṣṭa-avikalpa-aprameya-asaṅga / apramāṇo mārgaḥ / sarvadharmāṇāṃ samutthānasyāsamutthānatāmalokatvamupādāya / antadvayānanugamo mārgaḥ / sarvadharmeṣvanabhiniveśatāmiti / yathāpratibhāsaṃ bhāvasya tacchūnyatayā vā bhāvasyānanugamaḥ / asambhinno mārgaḥ / asambhedanatāmiti bhedānupalabdhim / aparāmṛṣṭo mārgastena hīnayānāspṛhaṇāt / avikalpo mārgaḥ / vikalpasamatāmiti vikalpānāmanupalabdhim / aprameyo mārgaḥ / apramāṇadharmatāmupādāyeti / apramāṇadharmatālambanatvāt / asaṅgo mārgaḥ / sarvadharmeṣvasaṅgatāmiti nirupalambhatām /
body.translated_text: In the path, seven: <s>apramāṇa</s> (immeasurable), <s>antadvayānanugama</s> (non-following of the two extremes), <s>asambhinna</s> (undivided), <s>aparamṛṣṭa</s> (untouched), <s>avikalpa</s> (non-conceptual), <s>aprameya</s> (unfathomable), <s>asaṅga</s> (unattached). The path is immeasurable — on account of the non-arising nature of the arising of all <s>dharmas</s>, [and] on account of being without light [i.e., beyond illumination]. The path is non-following of the two extremes — 'the non-grasping nature regarding all <s>dharmas</s>' — the non-following of either the entity as it appears or the emptiness of that entity. The path is undivided — 'the non-divisible nature' means the non-apprehension of division. The path is untouched — because of not aspiring to the lesser vehicle through that. The path is non-conceptual — 'the equality of conceptualizations' means the non-apprehension of conceptualizations. The path is unfathomable — 'on account of the nature of immeasurable <s>dharmas</s>' — because of having immeasurable <s>dharma</s>-nature as its object. The path is unattached — 'the non-attached nature regarding all <s>dharmas</s>' means non-apprehension.

body.text: duḥkhe pañca- anitya-duḥkha śūnya-anātma-lakṣaṇa / sāsravāḥ pañcaskandhā duḥkham / tadatrānityaṃ bhavatyeveti (?) / sarvadharmāṇāmasaṃskṛtatāmiti yathāpratibhāsamanutpannatām / duḥkhaṃ duḥkhaṃ sukhavilakṣaṇatvādākāśavat / śūnyaṃ duḥkhaṃ sarvadharmānupalabdheḥ / anātmā duḥkhaṃ yathāpratibhāsaṃ sarvadharmeṣvabhiniveśāyogāt / trīṇi saṃskṛtalakṣaṇāni / jātirjarānityatā ca / tadabhāvādalakṣaṇaṃ duḥkham / anabhinivṛttitāmiti yathāpratibhāsaṃ yathā paramārthaṃ cāsaṃskṛtatām //
body.translated_text: In suffering, five: <s>anitya</s> (impermanent), <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering), <s>śūnya</s> (empty), <s>anātma</s> (non-self), <s>alakṣaṇa</s> (without characteristics). The five defiled aggregates are suffering. And therein, impermanence certainly obtains. 'The unconditioned nature of all <s>dharmas</s>' means the non-arisen nature as they appear. Suffering is suffering — because of being different from pleasure, like space. Suffering is empty — because of the non-apprehension of all <s>dharmas</s>. Suffering is non-self — because of the impossibility of grasping at all <s>dharmas</s> as they appear. The three conditioned characteristics are: arising, decay, and impermanence. Because of their absence, suffering is without characteristics. 'The non-regression nature' means the unconditioned nature both as [things] appear and as [they are in] ultimate reality.

body.text: nirodhe ṣoḍaśa / tathā hi nirodhaḥ śūnyataiva viśuddhā / na ca śūnyatā bhidyate bhedakānāmanupalabdheḥ / tasmādākāśavadanantāparyanto nirodhaḥ / anukrameṇa vistāreṇa vā paricchedādyathākramaṃ tataḥ ṣoḍaśa śūnyatāḥ santyekarasāḥ / ata āha / sarvaśūnyatāpāramiteyamanantāparyantatāmupādāyeti / adhyātmaśūnyatāpāramiteyaṃ bahirdhāśūnyatāpāramiteyaṃ yāvadabhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatāpāramitetyādi / ataśca nirodhasatye ṣoḍaśākārāḥ / iti mārgajñatākārāḥ /
body.translated_text: In cessation, sixteen. For cessation is just emptiness, purified. And emptiness is not divided, because of the non-apprehension of dividers. Therefore, like space, cessation is infinite and boundless. By enumeration or by extension, through delimitation, there are accordingly sixteen emptinesses, being of one taste. Hence he says: 'This is the perfection of all emptinesses, on account of the infinite and boundless nature.' 'This is the perfection of internal emptiness, this is the perfection of external emptiness,' up to 'this is the perfection of the emptiness of the non-existence of self-nature,' and so on. And thus, in the truth of cessation there are sixteen aspects. These are the aspects of <s>mārgajñatā</s> (knowledge of the paths).

body.text: sarvākārajñatākārāḥ daśottaraṃ śatam / yataḥ śāstram-
body.translated_text: The aspects of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience in all aspects) are one hundred and ten. Because the treatise [states] —

children.translated_text: Beginning with the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness), ending with the aspects of <s>buddhahood</s>,
of disciples, <s>bodhisattvas</s>, and <s>Buddhas</s>, respectively, // 4-4 //
thirty-seven, thirty-four, thirty-nine — these are declared;
according to the threefold division of omniscience, in conformity with the truth of the path. // 4-5 //

body.text: tānadhikṛtya smṛtyupasthānādītyādikaṃ āparivartasamāpteḥ / smṛtyupasthānādibodhipakṣyadharmapāramiteyamiti / smṛtyupasthānādayaḥ saptavargā anekaśo vibhaktāḥ saptatriṃśabdodhipakṣyā dharmā bhavanti / pratyekaṃ teṣāmanupalambhāttadākārāḥ pāramitāḥ............ [stutiparivarto nāma navamaḥ //]
body.translated_text: Regarding those, 'beginning with the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s>' and so forth, up to the completion of the chapter. 'This is the perfection of the <s>bodhipakṣya dharmas</s> (factors of awakening) beginning with the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s>' — the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> and the other seven groups, divided in many ways, constitute the thirty-seven <s>bodhipakṣya dharmas</s>. Through the non-apprehension of each of them individually, there are the aspects [as] perfections............ [The chapter on praise is the ninth.]

body.text: 10. dhāraṇaguṇaparikīrtanaparivarto nāma daśamaḥ /
body.translated_text: 10. The tenth chapter is named the '<s>Dhāraṇīguṇaparikīrtana-parivarta</s>' (Chapter on the Proclamation of the Qualities of <s>Dhāraṇī</s>).

body.text: ......bodhirdharmacakrapravartanaparyantā nāhetutvāditi phalaratnapradātāprayogaḥ //
body.translated_text: ......Awakening, extending up to the turning of the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>, is not without cause — hence [this is] the practice of the giver of the fruit-jewel.

body.text: śuddharāśirityādi pragāścaryāt / teṣāmeva phalānāmākāśavadviśuddhidarśanāditi śuddhakaḥ prayogaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'The pure heap' and so on — from the preceding [discussion of] wonder. The seeing of the purification of those very fruits as being like space — this is the practice of the purifier.

body.text: āścaryamityādi / atha khalvāyuṣmānityataḥ prāk / likhyeteti likhituṃ śakyate / likhitarvyaiveti tāvataiva kālena likhitavyā bhavet / dṛḍhasamādānasya vighnābhāvāditi bhāvaḥ / tatkasya hetoriti kuta idamāsaṃ (śaṃ)kitamityarthaḥ / evaṃ hītyādinottaram / dharmateyamiti bhāvaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Wonder' and so on. 'O <s>Āyuṣman</s>' and so forth — [the section] before that. 'Can be written' means 'is able to be written.' 'Should be written in just that [time]' means 'it could be written in just that much time.' Because there is no obstruction for one of firm resolve — this is the meaning. 'For what reason' means 'whence is this apprehended?' — this is the meaning. 'Because it is thus' and so forth is the answer. '<s>Dharmatā</s> (the nature of reality) is such' — this is the meaning.

body.text: kiñcāpīti yadyapi / na prasahiṣyata iti na prabhaviṣyati / acchidrasamādānasyatyakhaṇḍasamādānasya ityavadheraṇa(na)tikramāt sāvadhiḥ prayogaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Even though' means although. 'Will not prevail' means will not be able to. 'Of one whose resolve is unbroken' means of one whose resolve is intact — because of not transgressing the limit. [This is] the practice with a definite limit.

body.text: uktāḥ prayogāḥ / guṇā vaktavyāḥ / tānadhikṛtya śāstram-
body.translated_text: The practices have been stated. The qualities are to be stated. Regarding those, the treatise [states] —

body.text: mārāṇāṃ śaktihānyādiścaturdaśavidho guṇaḥ /
body.translated_text: The loss of power of the <s>Māras</s> and the rest — the qualities are of fourteen kinds.

body.text: guṇāḥ prayogānuśaṃsāḥ māraśaktivyāghātādayaścaturdaśa / tatrādau atha khalvityādi na hi śāriputretyataḥ prāk / buddhānāṃ ānubhāveneti / tena māraśaktivyāghātāditi bhāvaḥ / prasatteḥ(?)adarśanāt pṛcchati / tatkasya hetoriti / samanvāhariṣyantīti smariṣyanti / parigrahīṣyantītyānukūlye cāvasthānāditi māraśaktivyāghātaguṇaḥ //
body.translated_text: The qualities are the benefits of the practice. The loss of power of the <s>Māras</s> and the rest are fourteen. Therein, first, 'Now then' and so forth, up to before 'Not indeed, O <s>Śāriputra</s>.' 'By the empowerment of the <s>Buddhas</s>' — thereby, 'the loss of the <s>Māras</s>' power' — this is the meaning. Because of not seeing [the <s>Māras</s>' power] prevailing, he asks: 'For what reason.' 'They will recollect' means they will remember. 'They will accept' — because of remaining favorably disposed — this is the quality of the loss of the <s>Māras</s>' power.

body.text: na hi śāriputretyādi / evamukta ityataḥ prāk / iti buddhasamanvāhārajñānaguṇaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Not indeed, O <s>Śāriputra</s>' and so forth, up to before 'Thus spoken.' This is the quality of the <s>Buddha</s>'s recollective knowledge.

body.text: evamukta ityādi buddhacakṣuṣeti yāvat / anubhāvaḥ prabhāvaḥ / adhiṣṭhānamadhikaśaktyādhānam / parigrahaḥ svīkāraḥ / kutasteṣāṃ buddhādhiṣṭhānaṃ buddhaparigraho vetyata āha jñātāsta ityādi / jñātāḥ samanvāhṛtāḥ / adhiṣṭhitāḥ svīkṛtāḥ / dṛṣṭā māṃsacakṣuṣā / vyavalokitā buddhacakṣuṣā / iti buddhāvalokitatvaguṇaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Thus spoken' and so forth, up to 'with <s>Buddha</s>-vision.' '<s>Anubhāva</s>' (influence) is power. '<s>Adhiṣṭhāna</s>' (empowerment) is the bestowal of superior power. '<s>Parigraha</s>' (acceptance) is taking under one's care. 'Whence do they have the <s>Buddha</s>'s empowerment and the <s>Buddha</s>'s acceptance?' — to this he says 'they are known' and so forth. 'Known' means recollected. 'Empowered' means accepted. 'Seen' — with the fleshly eye. 'Beheld' — with the <s>Buddha</s>-eye. This is the quality of being beheld by the <s>Buddhas</s>.

body.text: ye te bodhisattvā ityādi yepītyataḥ prāk / tathatvāyeti samyaksambodhyāsannībhāvaguṇaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Those <s>bodhisattvas</s>' and so forth, up to before 'even those.' 'For the sake of suchness' — this is the quality of approaching <s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (perfect awakening).

body.text: yepītyādi / ime khalviyataḥ prāk / mahārthika āyatyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmibhiḥ / mahānuśaṃso bodhisattvasampattibhiḥ / mahāphalaḥ paścādanuttarāyā bodhyāḥ / mahādipākaḥ caramabhavabhāvinībhiḥ kulagotralakṣaṇādisampattibhiḥ / pariśramaḥ klamathaḥ / pariṣpa(spa)ndo vyāpāraḥ / iti mahārthatādiguṇaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Even those' and so forth, up to before 'these indeed.' 'Of great purpose' — in the future, through the <s>bodhisattva</s> stages. 'Of great benefit' — through the perfections of the <s>bodhisattva</s>. 'Of great fruit' — afterward, through unsurpassed awakening. 'Of great ripening' — through the perfections of family, lineage, marks, and the like that pertain to the final existence. '<s>Pariśrama</s>' (exertion) is fatigue. '<s>Parispanda</s>' (activity) is effort. This is the quality of great purpose and the rest.

body.text: ime khalvityādi na santrāsamāpadyanta iti yāvat / sūtrāntā iti prajñāpāramitāprabhṛtayaḥ / atyayeneti parinirvāṇena / vartanyāmiti pūrvadeśe / nanu madhyadeśe ṣoḍaśeṣu mahānagareṣu bhagavatā dharmo deśitaḥ / tasya kathaṃ tato 'nyatra pracāra ityata āha / navamaṇḍa ityādi / navamaṇḍo 'bhinavaḥ sāraḥ / sa prāpto vineyairasyeti tathokte dharmavinaye / dharmaścāsau deśanādharmatvādvinayaśca kleśavinayāditi dharmavinayaḥ / bhagavati parinirvṛte saddharmasya loke 'vasthānaṃ pañcavarṣasahasrāṇi tato 'ntardhānakālaḥ / tatsamaye sannidhāne / tataḥ kimityāha / samanvāhṛtā ityādi / uttarasyāṃ diśīti digantarāṇāṃ vyavacchedaḥ / uttare digbhāga iti / tasyā api bhāgāntarāṇāṃ vistāreṇa caratīti vaistārikī / uttarāpatha iti vacanaṃ dakṣiṇāpathādervyavacchedāya /
body.translated_text: 'These indeed' and so forth, up to 'they will not be terrified.' '<s>Sūtrāntas</s>' means the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and the like. 'By passing away' means by <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. 'In the outlying regions' means in the frontier lands. 'But surely the <s>Bhagavān</s> taught the <s>Dharma</s> in the sixteen great cities of the central region — how then is its circulation elsewhere?' — to this he says 'fresh essence' and so forth. 'Fresh essence' (<s>navamaṇḍa</s>) means new pith. 'That has been obtained by the disciples' — in the <s>Dharma</s>-<s>Vinaya</s> so called.
