'<s>Dharma</s>' because it is a teaching-<s>dharma</s>; '<s>Vinaya</s>' because it disciplines the afflictions — hence '<s>Dharma</s>-<s>Vinaya</s>.' When the <s>Bhagavān</s> has passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, the duration of the true <s>Dharma</s> in the world is five thousand years; after that is the time of disappearance. At that time, in its proximity. 'Then what?' — he says 'they will be recollected' and so forth. 'In the northern direction' — this excludes the other directions. 'In the northern quarter' — and of that, it excludes the other parts. 'Extensive in its spread' means '<s>vaistārikī</s>' (widely circulating). The term 'in the northern regions' is to distinguish from the southern regions and the like.

body.text: bahava ityalpakapakṣyasya subahava iti bahutvaprakarṣāya / kiñcāpīti yadyapi / śeṣaṃ subodham / atra caturbhiḥ kāraṇaiḥ śāsanāpacaya uktaḥ / bhagavato 'tyayena / navamaṇḍaprāptatvena / antardhānakālasannipātena / pravartakālyatvena ca / tathāpi śāsanaṃ tānabalaṃbya pravartiṣyata iti śāsanāvalambatvaguṇaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Many' — the word '<s>subahava</s>' (very many) is to express the abundance on the side of the few. 'Even though' means although. The rest is easily understood. Here, four causes of the decline of the teaching are stated. By the passing of the <s>Bhagavān</s>. By the [teaching] having obtained fresh essence. By the coincidence with the time of disappearance. And by [its presence] in the frontier regions. Even so, the teaching will continue relying on them — this is the quality of being the support of the teaching.

body.text: cirayānetyādi yāvatsambodhimārabhyeti / praśnaḥ pṛcchā / tatkaraṇāt paripṛṣṭāḥ parijñātapṛcchāḥ paripṛcchāḥ / tathā karaṇāt paripṛcchitāḥ /
body.translated_text: 'For a long time' and so forth, up to 'beginning with <s>saṃbodhi</s>.' '<s>Praśna</s>' is a question. '<s>Paripṛṣṭāḥ</s>' means those whose questions have been fully answered, through having done that [questioning]. Similarly, '<s>paripṛcchitāḥ</s>' means those who have been fully questioned.

body.text: parihatapraśnāḥ kṛtāḥ paripuripraśnokṛtāḥ / śīleṣviti bahuvacanamādyarthaṃ śīlādiṣvityarthaḥ / śeṣaṃ subodham / iti śukladharmaparipūraṇaguṇaḥ //
body.translated_text: '<s>Parihatapraśnāḥ kṛtāḥ</s>' means those whose questions have been completely resolved. 'In the precepts' — the plural is in the sense of 'and so forth,' meaning 'in the precepts and the rest.' The rest is easily understood. This is the quality of the fulfillment of wholesome <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: tatkasyetyādi samyaksambodhimārabhyeti yāvat / jātivyativṛttānāmapīti tāṃ taduttarāṃ ca jātimatikrāntānāmapi samudācārāḥ prayogāḥ / abhinandanamabhilāṣaḥ śeṣaṃ sugamam / iti kathāpuruṣatāguṇaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Then whose' and so forth, up to 'beginning with <s>saṃbodhi</s>.' 'Even of those who have passed beyond birth' means even of those who have transcended that birth and the ones beyond it — their activities are practices. '<s>Abhinandana</s>' (delight) is aspiration. The rest is easy to understand. This is the quality of being a person of story [i.e., one whose story is told].

body.text: teṣu cetyādi yāvatsamyaksambodhāviti / chandato mantrato veti / abhiprāyeṇa vyavacāreṇa vā / śeṣaṃ subodham / iti abhedyatāguṇaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'And in those' and so forth, up to 'in <s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s>.' 'By intention or by deliberation' — by aspiration or by conduct. The rest is easily understood. This is the quality of indestructibility.

body.text: tāṃ cetyādinā samyaksambodhāvityetadantena bahujanakuśalamūlotpādanaguṇaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'That' and so forth, up to the end marked by 'in <s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s>' — this is the quality of generating the wholesome roots of many beings.

body.text: tatkasyetyādi evaṃ cetyataḥ prāk prasthāpayiṣyāma iti prasthānamātreṇa / samprabhāvayiṣyāma iti bhāvanāprakarṣasaṃpādanāt / pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyāma iti sthirīkariṣyāmaḥ / śeṣaṃ subodham / iti pratijñātaparārthasaṃpādanaguṇaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Then whose' and so forth, up to before 'thus.' 'We shall set forth' means merely by setting [them] forth. 'We shall fully bring about' means by accomplishing the excellence of cultivation. 'We shall establish' means we shall make firm. The rest is easily understood. This is the quality of accomplishing the pledged benefit of others.

body.text: evaṃ cetyādi bhaviṣyantīti yāvat / evaṃ ceti yathokte parārthasaṃpādane sati / udārādhimuktikā bhaviṣyantīti / yathoktaṃ mahatyostadeva saṃkṣipya brūmaḥ / "te khalu udārādhimuktikā bhaviṣyanti / rūpaśabdagandharasasparśadharmeṣu ta udārāṇi dānāni datvā udārāṇi kuśalamūlānyabhisaṃskṛtya udāraṃ vipākaṃ parigṛhya sattvānāmarthāya vipākādvipākaṃ parigṛhīṣyanti" iti udāraphalaparigrahaguṇaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Thus' and so forth, up to 'they will be.' 'Thus' means when there is the accomplishment of the benefit of others as described. 'They will be of noble aspiration.' The stated [passage] from the two great [texts], we summarize thus: 'They will indeed be of noble aspiration. Having given noble gifts in the domains of form, sound, smell, taste, touch, and <s>dharmas</s>, having produced noble wholesome roots, having accepted a noble ripening, they will accept ripening after ripening for the benefit of beings.' This is the quality of accepting a noble fruit.

body.text: yadityādi evamukta ityataḥ prāk / yaditi yasmādudārādhimuktikatvāt / adhyālambitavyānīti saṃkramitavyāni / śeṣaṃ subodham / iti vaistarikaparārthasaṃpādanaguṇaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'That which' and so forth, up to before 'thus spoken.' 'That which' means because of the noble aspiration. 'Should be transferred to' means should be redirected. The rest is easily understood. This is the quality of accomplishing the benefit of others extensively.

body.text: evamukta ityādyāparivartasamāpteḥ / pāramitānāṃ kṛtaśa iti tadartham / tāsāṃ pariśuddhaye / arthāyeti hitāya / anveṣiṣyante prajñāpāramitā kvaiṣā labhyatāmiti / paryeṣiṣyanta itastato gatvā gaveṣiṣyante / iha lapsyata iti śrutvā / abhivadanī (ntī) ti samyagvadanti / upagamiṣyanti sannidhānataḥ / upapatsyante prayatne sati lābhāt / upanaṃsyante ayatnenaiva lābhāt / śeṣaṃ subodham / iti ṣaṭpāramitāniyatalābhaguṇaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Thus spoken' and so forth, up to the completion of the chapter. 'Of the <s>pāramitās</s>, in parts' means for that purpose — for the purification of those [<s>pāramitās</s>]. 'For the purpose of' means for the benefit. 'They will seek the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>' — '[asking] where can this be obtained?' 'They will search' — going hither and thither, they will search. 'Here it will be obtained' — having heard this. 'Speaking correctly' means speaking well. 'They will approach' — from its proximity. 'They will obtain' — when effort is present, from acquisition. 'They will receive' — even without effort, from acquisition. The rest is easily understood. This is the quality of the certain attainment of the six <s>pāramitās</s>.

body.text: ityukto guṇaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus the qualities have been stated.

body.text: yathokteṣu prayogeṣu cetasaḥ sthāpanaṃ dhāraṇam / tasya guṇā anuśaṃsāścaturdaśa / teṣāṃ parikīrtanaścāsau parivartaśca /
body.translated_text: The fixing of the mind upon the practices as stated is retention (<s>dhāraṇa</s>). Its qualities and benefits are fourteen. The chapter that proclaims them is that chapter.

body.text: āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ sāratamānāmni pañjikāyāṃ ratnākaraśāntiviracitāyāṃ daśamaḥ parivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: End of the tenth chapter in the <s>Pañjikā</s> commentary named <s>Sāratama</s>, composed by <s>Ratnākaraśānti</s>, on the Noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

body.text: 11. mārakarmaparivarto nāmaikādaśamaḥ /
body.translated_text: 11. The eleventh [chapter] is named the "<s>Mārakarma-parivarta</s>" (Chapter on the Deeds of <s>Māra</s>).

body.text: doṣāḥ prayogāntarāyakarāḥ / te vaktavyāḥ / tamadhikṛtya śāstram-
body.translated_text: The faults are those that create obstacles to practice. They are to be stated. With regard to them, the treatise [states] —

body.text: doṣāśca ṣaḍviboddhavyāścaturbhirdaśakaiḥ saha // 4-12 //
body.translated_text: The faults are to be understood as forty-six, together with four groups of ten. // 4-12 //

body.text: doṣāḥ ṣaṭcatvāriṃśadityarthaḥ / ata āha / atha khalvityādi / keciditi praśnaḥ / kāṅkṣākimarthagateḥ / athavā cicchabdo na paṭhitavyaḥ / bahūnīti sāmānyenokte viśeṣajijñāsayā praśnaḥ / kiyadrūpāṇoti / teṣāmityādyuttaram / vakṣyamāṇāni ṣaṭcatvāriṃśaditi bhāvaḥ / bhāṣamāṇādipadāni sarvacaryāṇāmupalakṣaṇāni / cireṇa pratibhānamutpatsyata iti cireṇa pāramitānāṃ pūraṇam / tataścireṇaiva bodhiḥ syāt / iti cirapratibhānadoṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: "Faults, forty-six" — this is the meaning. Therefore he says, "Now then" and so on. "Some" is the question. From the word <s>kāṅkṣā</s> (doubt), the meaning is questioning. Or alternatively, the word <s>cit</s> should not be read. When "many" has been stated in general, the question arises from the desire to know the specifics: "Of what kind?" "Of those" and so on is the answer. The sense is that forty-six will be stated. The words beginning with "speaking" and so on are indicative of all [types of] practice. "Insight will arise after a long time" means the perfections will be fulfilled after a long time. And from that, awakening would occur only after a long time. Thus, the fault of delayed insight.

body.text: tadapi cetyādi / vikṣepsyata iti / uddhataṃ bhaviṣyati / anupāyakuśalasya kṣiprataraṃ tadutpattau mānotpatteḥ / tato 'nyān bodhisattvānavamanyamānasya nīcakuleṣūtpattyā cireṇaiva bodhiḥ syādityāśupratibhānadoṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: "Even that" and so on. "Will be distracted" means the mind will become agitated. For one who lacks skill in means, when that [insight] arises too quickly, pride arises. Then, despising other <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, through rebirth in low families, awakening would come only after a long time — thus, the fault of hasty insight.

body.text: jṛmbhamāṇā iti sadarpakāyaprasārāḥ / hasanta iti aṭṭahāsān kurvantaḥ / uccavagghayanta iti darpāduttiṣṭhantaḥ / iti kāyakarmavaiguṇyam //
body.translated_text: "Yawning" (<s>jṛmbhamāṇā</s>) means proudly stretching their bodies. "Laughing" (<s>hasantaḥ</s>) means making loud laughter. "Jumping up" (<s>uccavagghayantaḥ</s>) means rising up out of pride. Thus, the fault of bodily misconduct.

body.text: vikṣiptacittā ityasamāhitā / anyonyavijñānasamaṅgina iti paraiḥ smarayitavyāḥ / svayaṃ tu smṛtiṃ na pratilapsyante / bhinneṣvapīryāpatheṣūddeśavismaraṇādveti cittavaiguṇyadoṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: "With distracted minds" (<s>vikṣiptacittā</s>) means unconcentrated. "Possessing mutual consciousness" (<s>anyonyavijñānasamaṅginaḥ</s>) means they must be reminded by others. But they themselves will not regain mindfulness. Even when the modes of deportment are disrupted, because of forgetting the topic being recited — thus, the fault of mental deficiency.

body.text: parasparamityādi / uccagghamānā iti parasparamuccagghayantaḥ / vikṣiptacakṣuṣa itastataḥ / visāmagrīti yāvatāmāgamane pustakamākṛṣyate tāvatāmasamagratetyayogavihitasvādhyāyāditā doṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: "Mutually" and so on. "Laughing at each other" (<s>uccagghamānā</s>) means mocking one another. "With distracted eyes" — [looking] here and there. "Disassemblage" (<s>visāmagrī</s>) means that while [some] are coming, the manuscript is withdrawn, and those [who came] are not assembled — thus, the fault of improperly arranged self-study and the like.

body.text: na vayamityādi punaraparamityataḥ prāk / cittotpādaistathā tatheti pūrvoktam / na nirjāyante na niṣpadyante / iti vaimukhyanimittagrāhitā doṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: "We do not" and so on, up to before "moreover." "With the generations of the mind, thus and thus" — as previously stated. "They are not born, they are not accomplished" — thus, the fault of grasping at signs of aversion.

body.text: punaraparamityādi tadyathāpītyataḥ prāk / vivarjya cetasā / utsṛjya kāyavāgbhyām / niryāṇaṃ śikṣāparyantagamanam / iti hetubhraṃśadoṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: "Moreover" and so on, up to before "just as." "Having abandoned mentally" (<s>vivarjya cetasā</s>). "Having cast off by body and speech" (<s>utsṛjya kāyavāgbhyām</s>). "Deliverance" (<s>niryāṇa</s>) is reaching the end of training. Thus, the fault of falling away from the cause.

body.text: tadyathāpītyādi tadyathāpītyataḥ prāk / piṇḍamāhāraḥ / chorayitvā tyaktvā / kavaḍaṃ grāsam / patraḥ palyasampatsamūhaḥ / palāśopamapratipanna iti palāśopameṣu sūtrānteṣvabhiyuktāḥ / damayiṣyāmaḥ pañcendriyadamanāt / śamayiṣyāmaḥ cetaso damanāt / parinirvāpayiṣyāmaḥ punarbhavakṣayāt / kuśalamūlānāmabhisaṃskāro niṣpādanāni tadarthāḥ prayogavyāpārāḥ / na ca tairmantavyamiti / teṣāmātmanaścānupalambhāditi praṇītāsvādabhraṃśadoṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: "Just as" and so on, up to before the next "just as." "<s>Piṇḍāhāra</s>" is alms-food. "Having discarded" (<s>chorayitvā</s>) means having thrown away. "A morsel" (<s>kavaḍa</s>) is a mouthful. "<s>Patra</s>" is the assemblage of leaves and the like. "Proficient in the <s>Palāśopama</s>" (<s>palāśopamapratipanna</s>) means devoted to the <s>sūtras</s> [known as] the <s>Palāśopama</s> (Similes of Leaves). "We shall tame" (<s>damayiṣyāmaḥ</s>) — because of taming the five faculties. "We shall calm" (<s>śamayiṣyāmaḥ</s>) — because of taming the mind. "We shall cause to attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>" (<s>parinirvāpayiṣyāmaḥ</s>) — because of the exhaustion of further existence. "The fabrication of wholesome roots" (<s>kuśalamūlānām abhisaṃskāra</s>) is their accomplishment; "for that purpose" are the practical efforts. "And they should not be thought of" — because of the non-apprehension of those [roots] and of oneself. Thus, the fault of falling away from the taste of the sublime.

body.text: tadyathāpītyādi tadyathāpītyataḥ prāk / prakāśamiti sālokam / upanidhyāyediti paśyet / varṇasaṃsthāna iti varṇākārau / ityuttamayānabhraṃśadoṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: "Just as" and so on, up to before the next "just as." "Luminous" (<s>prakāśa</s>) means endowed with light. "Would perceive" (<s>upanidhyāyet</s>) means would see. "Color and shape" (<s>varṇasaṃsthāna</s>) means hue and form. Thus, the fault of falling away from the supreme vehicle.

body.text: tadyathāpītyādi tadyathāpītyataḥ prāk / kevalamātmadamaśamathameveti / saṃvarṇata iti vartate / ityapītyādi / pratisaṃlayanaṃ samādhiḥ / tadapi ityevam / ātmadamaśamathārthameva saṃvarṇyate / ita ūrdhvaṃ itītyādi sugamam / iti dṛṣṭa evetyādi / dṛṣṭe dharme prāpte janmani / anupādāyeti na kiñcitparigahya / nityakālamityābodheḥ / satataṃ caitat pratijanmabhāvāt / samitaṃ ca pratyahaṃ bhāvāditi satatasamitam / śeṣaṃ subodham / ityuddeśabhraṃśadoṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: "Just as" and so on, up to before the next "just as." "Only self-control and tranquility" (<s>kevalām ātmadamaśamatham eva</s>) — and so on. "Praises" (<s>saṃvarṇate</s>) is to be supplied. "Even that" and so on. "Meditative absorption" (<s>pratisaṃlayana</s>) is <s>samādhi</s> (concentration). "That too" — in the same way. "Is praised only for the sake of self-control and tranquility." "From here onward" and so on — easily understood. "In this very" and so on. "In the visible <s>dharma</s>" (<s>dṛṣṭe dharme</s>) means in the present life. "Without grasping" (<s>anupādāya</s>) means without appropriating anything. "For all time" (<s>nityakāla</s>) means until awakening. "And constantly" — because of [occurring] in every birth. "And continuously" (<s>samita</s>) — because of [occurring] every day — thus "constantly and continuously" (<s>satatasamita</s>). The rest is easily understood. Thus, the fault of falling away from the summary.

body.text: iti prathamaṃ daśakam //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the first group of ten.

body.text: tadyathāpītyādi tadyathāpityataḥ prāk / palagaṇḍaḥ sūtradhāraḥ / merupṛṣṭhe sudarśanaṃ nāma śakrasya sauvarṇa nagaram / tanmadhye śakrasya vaijayanto nāma prāsādaḥ / pratipārśvaṃ yojanaśatadvayaṃ sārdham / ekatvena yojanasahasram / sūryācandramasostu merorarddhādvahirākāśagāmisphāṭikaṃ vartulaṃ vimānam / yathākramamekapañcaśatpañcāśacca yojanāni madhyasūtreṇa / tanmadhye yastayoḥ prāsādo bahubhūmestadiha tayorvimānaṃ vaktavyam / tacca vaijayantādatīvālpapramāṇam / nirmāṇaṃ viśeṣavatī kriyā / upanayanti prāpayantītyupā[ya]saṃmohadoṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: "Just as" and so on, up to before the next "just as." A "<s>palagaṇḍa</s>" is a carpenter. On the summit of <s>Meru</s> is the golden city of <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) named <s>Sudarśana</s>. In its center is <s>Śakra</s>'s palace named <s>Vaijayanta</s>. On each side, two hundred and fifty <s>yojanas</s>; in total, one thousand <s>yojanas</s>. But the chariots of <s>Sūrya</s> (the Sun) and <s>Candra</s> (the Moon) are crystal, circular mansions traveling through the sky from below the halfway point of <s>Meru</s>. In sequence, [their diameters are] fifty-one and fifty <s>yojanas</s> respectively along the central axis. The multi-storied palace of those two [luminaries] within [their chariots] — that is what is meant here by their "mansion." And that is extremely small in comparison to the <s>Vaijayanta</s> [palace]. "Emanation" (<s>nirmāṇa</s>) is a distinguished creation. "They bring near" (<s>upanayanti</s>) means they cause to attain — thus, the fault of delusion about means.

body.text: tadyathāpītyādi / bhagavānāha / tadyathāpītyataḥ prāk / loke cakrasya pravartanāt cakravartī / tatpunaścakramapauruṣamākāśagāmi sahasrāraṃ sanābhikaṃ sanemikaṃ āyasaṃ tāmraṃ raupyaṃ sauvarṇa vā yathāyogam / varṇo jāmbunadanibhaḥ / saṃsthānaṃ dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇopetam / tejaḥ sarvamabhibhūḥ prabhāvaḥ prabhāmaṇḍalaśca / ṛddhiḥ sampattiḥ / viśeṣataḥ saptaratnāni- cakraratnaṃ hastiratnaṃ
body.translated_text: "Just as" and so on. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Up to before the next "just as." A "<s>Cakravartin</s>" (universal monarch) is one who sets in motion the wheel (<s>cakra</s>) in the world. And that wheel is non-human, sky-going, thousand-spoked, with hub and rim, made of iron, copper, silver, or gold respectively. His complexion resembles <s>Jāmbūnada</s> (gold). His form is endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great being. His brilliance overwhelms all; his power includes a halo of radiance. His fortune (<s>ṛddhi</s>) is his prosperity. In particular, [he possesses] the seven jewels: the wheel-jewel, the elephant-jewel,

body.text: aśvaratnaṃ pariṇāyakaratnaṃ gṛhapatiratnaṃ maṇiratnaṃ ceti / dhandhayati mohayatyaparisphuṭatvādalpatvācceti dhandhakaḥ / yasmāddhetorbodhisattvaḥ samudeti sa bodhisattvasamudāgamaḥ / avāpya lābhamātreṇa / samāsādya śravaṇādibhiḥ / vivarjya tyaktvā / vivartya parāṅmukhībhūya / iti cakravartisādharmyānnirmāṇakāyabhraṃśadoṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: the horse-jewel, the minister-jewel, the householder-jewel, and the gem-jewel. "<s>Dhandhaka</s>" means one who confuses and deludes, because of indistinctness and insignificance. That cause from which the <s>Bodhisattva</s> arises is the "<s>bodhisattvasamudāgama</s>" (arising of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>). "Having obtained" (<s>avāpya</s>) — merely by obtaining. "Having encountered" (<s>samāsādya</s>) — through hearing and the like. "Having abandoned" (<s>vivarjya</s>) — having cast off. "Having turned away" (<s>vivartya</s>) — having turned one's back. Thus, by analogy with the <s>Cakravartin</s>, the fault of falling away from the <s>Nirmāṇakāya</s> (emanation body).

body.text: bhagavānāha / tadyathāpītyādi tadyathāpītyataḥ prāk / rasāḥ ṣaṭ / dravyabhedāt parasparasāṃkaryācca śataṃ bhavati / tataḥ śatarasaṃ bhojanam / ṣaṣṭikāḥ ṣaṣṭirātreṇa pacyante teṣāmodānaḥ ṣaṣṭikodanaḥ / śakandhvādiṣu darśanātpararūpam / utsṛjya cetasā / vivarjya kāyena / iti śatarasabhojasādharmyāt sambhogakāyabhraṃśadoṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said. "Just as" and so on, up to before the next "just as." There are six flavors (<s>rasas</s>). Through differentiation of substances and mutual intermixture, they become a hundred. From that, food of a hundred flavors. "<s>Ṣaṣṭika</s>" [rice] ripens in sixty nights; the boiled rice made from it is "<s>ṣaṣṭikodana</s>." From seeing [such food] among the <s>Śakandhus</s> and others, its form is inferred. "Having cast off mentally" (<s>utsṛjya cetasā</s>). "Having abandoned bodily" (<s>vivarjya kāyena</s>). Thus, by analogy with the food of a hundred flavors, the fault of falling away from the <s>Saṃbhogakāya</s> (enjoyment body).

body.text: tadyathāpītyādi prāk punaraparaśabdāt / gambhīraṃ paramārthaśekharatvāt / prabhāsvaraṃ paramanirmalālokatvāt / ityanardhyamaṇiratnasya dharmāddharmakāyabhraṃśadoṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: "Just as" and so on, up to before the next "moreover." "Profound" (<s>gambhīra</s>) — because of being the crest-jewel of ultimate reality. "Luminous" (<s>prabhāsvara</s>) — because of being supremely pure light. Thus, by the analogy of the priceless gem-jewel, the fault of falling away from the <s>Dharmakāya</s> (truth-body), from that <s>dharma</s>.

body.text: ita ūrdhvaṃ gadyadvayena bhagavatyāṃ pañca viparyāsāḥ pratiśe(ṣe)dhyāḥ (?) / punaraparamityādyevamukte ityataḥ prāk / bahūni pratibhānānīti rūpādīnāṃ sarvākārajñatāparyantānāṃ pratibhānāni / bhagavatyāmasaṃvidyamānatvāccittavikṣepakarāṇīti tattabhdāvapratibhānadoṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: From here onward, by two prose [passages], five errors regarding the <s>Bhagavatī</s> (the Noble Lady, i.e., <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>) are to be refuted (?). "Moreover" and so on, up to before "thus spoken." "Many insights" (<s>bahūni pratibhānāni</s>) means insights about form and the rest, up to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience in all aspects). Because they do not exist in the <s>Bhagavatī</s>, they cause distraction of the mind — thus, the fault of insight regarding the existence of those [dharmas in her].

body.text: evamukta ityādi punaraparāt prāk / ye kecit prajñāpāramitā likhiteti, asatīti, akṣarāṇīti, anakṣareti vā manyante sarvaṃ tanmārakarma / tathā hi na sā likhitā apagandhādivirahāt / nāsatī paramārthasattvāt / nākṣarāṇi sarvadharmāṇāmanakṣaratvāt / nānakṣarā tanniṣyandatvādeṣāmakṣarāṇām / ebhireva ca tasyāḥ sūcanāt / etānyeva ca tenārthenālambya tasyā adhigamāt / tadevaṃ likhanābhiniveśo 'sattvābhiniveśo 'kṣarābhiniveśo 'nakṣarābhiniveśaśceti catvāro doṣāḥ //
body.translated_text: "Thus spoken" and so on, up to before the next "moreover." Whoever thinks that <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is written, or that it is non-existent, or that it consists of syllables, or that it is without syllables — all of that is the deed of <s>Māra</s>. For she is not written, because of the absence of scent and the like. She is not non-existent, because she exists ultimately. She does not consist of syllables, because all <s>dharmas</s> are without syllables. She is not without syllables, because these [syllables] are her outflow. And also because she is indicated by these very [syllables]. And also because, relying on precisely that meaning, these [syllables] lead to her realization. Thus, clinging to writing, clinging to non-existence, clinging to syllables, and clinging to non-syllables — these are four faults.

body.text: punaraparamityādi / deśo mālavādiḥ / śatena sahasreṇa vā saṃkhyātagṛho 'nāḍhyānāṃ nivāso grāmaḥ / sahasreṇa lakṣeṇa vā saṃkhyātagṛha āḍhyānāṃ nivāso nagaram / nagarameva ca vastubhūyiṣṭhaṃ nigamaḥ / maṇḍalaṃ kāśyādi janapadaḥ / tatsamūho rāṣṭram / rājādhyuṣitaṃ nagaraṃ rājadhānī / ākhyānaṃ gadyakāvyam / gulmo ghahāḥ(ṭṭaḥ?) / viśikhā rathyā / śivikā yāpyayānam / jīvitārthāḥ pariṣkārāḥ jīvitapariṣkārāḥ / itihāsaḥ purāvṛttam / śeṣaṃ subodham / iti gantavyādinānārthamanasikāravikṣepadoṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: "Moreover" and so on. "Region" (<s>deśa</s>) means <s>Mālavā</s> and the like. A dwelling of the non-wealthy, consisting of houses counted by the hundred or thousand, is a village (<s>grāma</s>). A dwelling of the wealthy, consisting of houses counted by the thousand or <s>lakṣa</s>, is a city (<s>nagara</s>). A city that is predominantly commercial is a town (<s>nigama</s>). A circle (<s>maṇḍala</s>) [such as] <s>Kāśī</s> and the like is a district (<s>janapada</s>). An assemblage of those is a kingdom (<s>rāṣṭra</s>). A city inhabited by the king is a capital (<s>rājadhānī</s>). "Narrative" (<s>ākhyāna</s>) is prose poetry. "<s>Gulma</s>" is a thicket (or a guardhouse?). "<s>Viśikhā</s>" is a street. "<s>Śivikā</s>" is a palanquin. "Necessities of life" (<s>jīvitārthāḥ pariṣkārāḥ</s>) are the provisions for livelihood. "<s>Itihāsa</s>" is ancient history. The rest is easily understood. Thus, the fault of distraction through mental attention to various purposes such as destination and the like.

body.text: iti dvitīyaṃ daśakam //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the second group of ten.

body.text: punaraparamityādinā draṣṭavyarājādimanasikāravikṣepadoṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: Beginning with "moreover" and so on — the fault of distraction through mental attention to kings and others who are to be visited.

body.text: punaraparamityādinā prāptavyāgnyādimanasikāravikṣepadoṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: Beginning with "moreover" and so on — the fault of distraction through mental attention to fire and other [elements] that are to be obtained.

body.text: punaraparamityādi prāk punaraparāt / antarāyā vighātāḥ / lābhaścīvarādiprāptiḥ / satkāra ādaraḥ / śloko yaśaḥ / tairāsvāda uddharṣaḥ / cittotpīḍā cīvarādivighātaiḥ / ityutpīḍāsvādadauṣau //
body.translated_text: "Moreover" and so on, up to before the next "moreover." "Obstacles" (<s>antarāyāḥ</s>) are hindrances. "Gain" (<s>lābha</s>) is the acquisition of robes and the like. "Honor" (<s>satkāra</s>) is respect. "Fame" (<s>śloka</s>) is renown. "Savoring" (<s>āsvāda</s>) through those is elation. "Mental oppression" (<s>cittotpīḍā</s>) is through hindrances to robes and the like. Thus, the two faults of oppression and savoring.

body.text: punaraparamityādi prāk punaraparāt / kiñcāpīti yadyapi / upāyakauśalyamiti yena hīnabodhau na patediti / upāyakauśalyarahitasya gambhīrasūtrānte atanmārgaṇadoṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: "Moreover" and so on, up to before the next "moreover." "Even though" (<s>kiñcāpi</s>) means "although." "Skill in means" (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>) is that by which one does not fall into the lesser awakening. For one lacking skill in means, the fault of not seeking that [skill] in the profound <s>sūtras</s>.

body.text: iti ūrdhvaṃ vaidhuryāṇi bāhulyena vaktavyāni / tāni dharmabhāṇakena saha dhārmaśravaṇikānāṃ visāmagrī / dharmasya bhāna(ṇa)ko vaktā guruḥ / dharmaśravaṇaṃ prayojanameṣāmiti dhārmaśravaṇikaḥ śiṣyaḥ / samagrabhāvaḥ sāmagrī / viparyāsāt visāmagrī / tatrādau punaraparavākyadvayam / kilāsaṃ kausīdyam / bahukṛtyatā gṛhiṇām / sapi kausīdyamiti cchandakilāsavaidhuryam /
body.translated_text: From here onward, the discordances (<s>vaidhurya</s>) are to be stated at length. They are the disharmony between the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher and the <s>Dharma</s>-listeners. The "<s>Dharma</s>-preacher" (<s>dharmabhāṇaka</s>) is the speaker, the teacher. Those whose purpose is hearing the <s>Dharma</s> are the "<s>Dharma</s>-listeners" (<s>dhārmaśravaṇika</s>), the students. Their state of being assembled is "assemblage" (<s>sāmagrī</s>). Its opposite is "disassemblage" (<s>visāmagrī</s>). There, first, two sentences beginning with "moreover." "Sluggishness" (<s>kilāsa</s>) is laziness. "Being occupied with many tasks" (<s>bahukṛtyatā</s>) belongs to householders. That too is laziness — thus, the discordance of desire and sluggishness.

body.text: tataḥ punaraparavākyadvayam / antaśa ityadhikameva likhitukāmaḥ / gatimān śabdajñānāt / matimān arthajñānāt / smṛtimān ubhayordhāraṇāt / kṣepsyata iti karme karttariprayogaḥ / gamiṣyatītyarthaḥ / udaghaṭitajñaḥ sāmānyokte viśeṣajñānāt / vipañcitajñaḥ kiñcidapyuktau viśeṣaparijñānāt / anabhijñaḥ padaparamaḥ / sa hi yaducyate tadeva jānāti nādhikam //
body.translated_text: Then, two sentences beginning with "moreover." "At least" (<s>antaśa</s>) — he wishes to write even more. "Possessed of [understanding the] course" (<s>gatimān</s>) — because of knowledge from the words. "Possessed of intelligence" (<s>matimān</s>) — because of knowledge of the meaning. "Possessed of mindfulness" (<s>smṛtimān</s>) — because of retaining both. "Will be thrown" (<s>kṣepsyate</s>) — the passive form is used in an active sense; meaning "will go away." "One who understands from hints" (<s>udaghaṭitajña</s>) — because of knowing the specifics when only the general is stated. "One who understands from elaboration" (<s>vipañcitajña</s>) — because of fully understanding the specifics when even a little is stated. "One who does not understand" (<s>anabhijña</s>) — one who is limited to the words. For such a one knows only what is stated, nothing more.

body.text: imāni catvāri vaidhuryāṇi / cchandadeśāntaragamanavaidhuryam / udghāṭitajñatetaratāvaidhuryam / abhijñatetaratāvaidhuryam //
body.translated_text: These are four discordances: the discordance of desire and going to another region. The discordance of being one who understands from hints and [the teacher being] otherwise. The discordance of being one who understands and [the teacher being] otherwise.

body.text: tṛtīyaṃ daśakam //
body.translated_text: End of the third group of ten.

body.text: punaraparamityādi āmiṣaṃ dravyam / tadgurukabahumānādasyeti āmiṣagurukaḥ / evaṃ lobhādigurukaḥ / yāvatā svayaṃ vartate tāvadicchatīti alpecchaḥ / santuṣṭo adhikāniṣṭeḥ / pravivikto gṛhasthairasaṃstutatvāt / iyatā pravrajitasya dānāśaktiruktā / arthavā na dātukāma iti santamapyartha gṛhīmātsaryāt / ityāmiṣārthitādānānārthitāvaidhuryam //
body.translated_text: "Moreover" and so on. "Material things" (<s>āmiṣa</s>) are possessions. One who greatly esteems those is "<s>āmiṣaguruka</s>" (one who values material things). Similarly, "<s>lobhādigurukaḥ</s>" (one who values greed and the like). "One who is content with whatever one has" is "<s>alpeccha</s>" (of few desires). "<s>Santuṣṭa</s>" (contented) means without desire for more. "<s>Pravivikta</s>" (secluded) means not mingling with householders. By this much, the inability of the renunciant to give has been stated. "One who possesses wealth but does not wish to give" — because of the stinginess of a householder who possesses wealth. Thus, the discordance of the one who seeks material things and the giving, and of the one who does not seek.

body.text: punaraparamityādi punaraparāt prāk / śrāddho bhaviṣyati / tataḥ śrotukāmaḥ śabdataḥ / avabodhu(ddha)kāmo 'rthataḥ / artha dātukāmaḥ parityaktukāma iti nirakṣepadānāt / dharmabhāṇakastu na vakṣyati / aśrāddhatvāt, dhanairaṇa(na)rthikatvāt,
body.translated_text: "Moreover" and so on, up to before the next "moreover." "He will be faithful" (<s>śrāddha</s>). Therefore, "desirous of hearing" — with respect to the words. "Desirous of understanding" — with respect to the meaning. "Desirous of giving wealth, desirous of renouncing" — because of unreserved giving. But the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher will not speak — because of lack of faith, because of not desiring wealth,

body.text: dharmamātsaryādvā / imāni trīṇi vaidhuryāṇi / śrāddhetaratāvaidhurya dānārthitāgrahaṇānarthitāvaidhurya śrotukāmatādharmamātsaryavaidhurya ca //
body.translated_text: or because of stinginess regarding the <s>Dharma</s>. These are three discordances: the discordance of the faithful one and the other; the discordance of the one seeking a gift and the non-acceptance, and the one not seeking; and the discordance of the one desirous of hearing and the stinginess regarding the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: punaraparamityādi / tāni sūtrāṇīti yāni śrotukāmaḥ / dharmāntarāyo dharmavyasanam / tadasyāsti pūrvajanmasaddharmapratikṣepāditi dharmāntarāyikaḥ / tattayā tabhdāvena na sambhaviṣyanti na bhaviṣyanti / nāvatariṣyanti nānyata āgamiṣyanti / aprāptadharmabhāṇina ityaprāptadharmabhāṇakasya / prativāṇī pratyākhyānam / iti sūtrāntarā[ya]sambhavatadarthitāvaidhuryam //
body.translated_text: Beginning with 'Moreover' and so on. 'Those <s>sūtras</s>' means those which one wishes to hear. '<s>Dharmāntarāya</s>' (obstruction to the <s>Dharma</s>) is the decline of the <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmavyasana</s>). 'He has that because of the rejection of the true <s>Dharma</s> in a previous birth' — hence he is '<s>dharmāntarāyika</s>' (one with obstruction to the <s>Dharma</s>). 'By that, by that state, they will not come to be, will not arise, will not descend, will not come from elsewhere.' 'Of one who has not attained a preacher of the <s>Dharma</s>' — '<s>prativāṇī</s>' is rejection. Thus the obstacle of non-occurrence and non-attainment of <s>sūtras</s>.

body.text: punaraparamityādi / na śrotukāmo bhaviṣyatīti dharmāntaravyagratayā / ata idaṃ cchandakilāsavaidhuryādanyacchandavaidhuryam //
body.translated_text: Beginning with 'Moreover' and so on. 'He will not be desirous of hearing' — because of being preoccupied with other <s>dharmas</s>. Therefore this is the obstacle of different desire, distinct from the obstacle of desire and sluggishness.

body.text: tataḥ punaraparavākyadvayena middhagurukacchandikatāvaidhuryam //
body.translated_text: Then, by two 'Moreover' sentences, the obstacle of torpor, heaviness, and desire for comfort.

body.text: punaraparavākyena durgatiduḥkhabhayābhdavavaimukhyadoṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: By one 'Moreover' sentence, the fault of aversion due to fear of the suffering of evil destinies.

body.text: punaraparavākyena sugatisukhānāmapi duḥkhatvābhdavavaimukhyadoṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: By one 'Moreover' sentence, the fault of aversion due to [realizing] that even the pleasures of happy destinies are suffering.

body.text: tataḥ punaraparavākyena ekākitā parṣadgurukatāvaidhuryam / anubandhukāmatā anavakāśadānavaidhuryam / durbhikṣādidiggamanāgamanavaidhuryaṃ ca / tatraikākitāparṣadgurukatāvaidhuryāntaṃ caturthaṃ daśakam //
body.translated_text: Then, by one 'Moreover' sentence: the obstacle of solitude and esteeming assemblies; the desire for companionship and the obstacle of not giving opportunity; and the obstacle of traveling and returning in regions [due to] famine and the like. Among those, up to the end of the obstacle of solitude and esteeming assemblies is the fourth group of ten.

body.text: ekena punaraparavākyena sabhayadiggamanāgamanavaidhurye //
body.translated_text: By one 'Moreover' sentence, the obstacles of traveling and returning in regions with dangers.

body.text: punaraparamityādi kulāvalokanabahukṛtyatayā dhārmaśravaṇikānāṃ pratyākhyānadoṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: Beginning with 'Moreover' and so on: the fault of rejecting listeners of the <s>Dharma</s> because of being preoccupied with visiting families.

body.text: iti hītyādinā mārakarmaṇāṃ bāhulyaṃ buddhāvivarjanīyatāṃ mārasya ca teṣvabhiyogakāraṇamāha / punaraparamityādi / śramaṇaveśāgatena māreṇa saṃśayaprakṣepadoṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: By the passage beginning with 'For thus' and so on, he explains the multiplicity of <s>Māra's</s> deeds, the impossibility of avoiding the <s>Buddhas</s> [on <s>Māra's</s> part], and <s>Māra's</s> reason for making effort against them. Beginning with 'Moreover' and so on: the fault of casting doubt by <s>Māra</s> who has come in the guise of a <s>śramaṇa</s> (ascetic).

body.text: punaraparamityādi / nirmitabhikṣusaṅghena svayaṃ buddhaveṣeṇa māreṇa gambhīradharmacāriṇāṃ hīnabodhivyākaraṇadoṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: Beginning with 'Moreover' and so on: the fault of predicting inferior awakening for practitioners of the profound <s>Dharma</s>, by <s>Māra</s> in the guise of a <s>Buddha</s> with a magically created assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s>.

body.text: evaṃ subhūta ityādinā āparivartāntāccaturo 'rthānāha / māramarmaṇāṃ bāhulyaṃ tatkāraṇaṃ tebhyaśca vinā tāmalpabuddhitvādikam / yathā ca mārasya teṣvabhiyogastathā sarvabuddhānāṃ bodhisattvaparigraheṣviti ṣaṭcatvāriṃśadantarāyāḥ //
body.translated_text: Beginning with 'Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>' and so on, up to the end of the chapter, he states four matters: the multiplicity of <s>Māra's</s> vulnerable points, their cause, and apart from those, the [practitioners'] feeble intelligence and the like; and just as <s>Māra</s> makes effort against those [practitioners], so too all <s>Buddhas</s> [make effort] in embracing <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. Thus the forty-six obstacles.

body.text: mārakarmāṇyate evāntarāyāḥ / taddyotakaḥ parivartastatparivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Māra's</s> deeds — these indeed are the obstacles. The chapter that illuminates them is that chapter.

body.text: āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ sāratamānāmni pañcikāyāṃ ratnākaraśāntiviracitāyāmekādaśaḥ parivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: In the <s>Pañjikā</s> commentary named <s>Sāratama</s>, composed by <s>Ratnākaraśānti</s>, on the noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s> — this is the Eleventh Chapter.

body.text: 12. lokasaṃdarśanaparivarto nāma dvādaśaḥ /
body.translated_text: 12. The twelfth [chapter] is named '<s>Lokasaṃdarśana</s>' (Showing of the World).

body.text: uktā doṣāḥ / lakṣaṇaṃ vaktavyam / tadadhikṛtya śāstram-
body.translated_text: The faults have been stated. The characteristics (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) are to be explained. Regarding those, the treatise [states] —

children.text: lakṣyate yena tajjñeyaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ trividhaṃ ca tata /
children.translated_text: That by which [something] is characterized — that should be known as the characteristic; and it is threefold.

children.text: jñānaṃ viśeṣaḥ kāritraṃ svabhāvo yaśca lakṣyate // 4-13 //
children.translated_text: Knowledge, distinction, function, and the nature that is characterized. [4-13]

body.text: 'yena lakṣyate ' tallakṣaṇamiti jñeyam / karaṇe lyuṭ / tacca vividhaṃ 'jñānaṃ viśeṣaḥ kāritraṃ' ceti / yaśca lakṣyate tadapi lakṣaṇam / karmaṇi lyuṭ / sa ca 'svabhāva' eveti caturvidhaṃ lakṣaṇam / tatrādau jñānaṃ vaktavyam / tatra sarvajñatākāreṇa tāvat /
body.translated_text: 'That by which it is characterized' — that is to be known as the 'characteristic.' The suffix <s>lyuṭ</s> is in the instrumental sense. And that is threefold: 'knowledge, distinction, and function.' And 'that which is characterized' — that too is a 'characteristic' — the suffix <s>lyuṭ</s> is in the objective sense. And that is 'the intrinsic nature' alone — thus the characteristic is fourfold. Among those, first, knowledge is to be explained. Therein, by the aspect of <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience),

children.translated_text: In the production of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, in the world that has the nature of being perishable,
In the mental conduct of beings, in its contraction and outward activity; [4-14]
And in the indestructible aspect, in [the states] beginning with attachment — extensively —
In the great extent, in the immeasurable, and in consciousness that is non-demonstrable; [4-15]
And in the knowledge of the invisible mind — that is designated as 'unshelling' and the like.
Then, by the aspect of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), the knowledge of those [dharmas] is stated next. [4-16]
In <s>tathatā</s>, in the awakening of the sage, in the proclamation thereof — this is
The collection of the characteristic of knowledge, under the heading of <s>sarvajñatā</s>. [4-17]

body.text: jñānagrahaṇaṃ saptamyantaiḥ sahaḥ saṃbadhyate / 'tathāgatasya nirvṛttau' iti bhagavatyāḥ sakāśāttathāgatasya niṣpattau jñānam tadāha / atha khalvityādinā atha khalvityataḥ prāk / tatrādau dṛṣṭāntaḥ / evamevetyataḥ prāk / māturglānāyā iti mātari glānāyām / sparśavihāra iti sparśapracāraḥ / amanaāpa iti amanojñaḥ duḥkhahetutvāt / sudhṛtā dhārayeyuriti supuṣṭāṃ puṣṭīyuḥ / tathā puṣṭīyuḥ yathā supuṣṭā syāt / gopāyanaṃ rakṣaṇam / kelāyanaṃ sodhanaṃ vyādhiharaṇāt kelāśabdaḥ / kaṇḍvādiduḥkho vā sparśa iti / viṣayendriyavijñānasannipātajaścaita[si]kaḥ sparśaḥ / sa ca duḥkhaheturduḥkha / cakṣuṣa iti pañcamī / āpāto 'manuṣyāṇām / utpāto vidyudādiḥ / mamakāreṇa mamā [ye]yuḥ / samanvāharantītyetat kuta ityāha / yepi te likhantīti tāmeva / tathāgatasyeti śākyamuneḥ /
body.translated_text: The word 'knowledge' is to be connected with the [words in the] seventh case (locative). 'In the production of the <s>Tathāgata</s>' — knowledge of the production of the <s>Tathāgata</s> from the <s>Bhagavatī</s> (<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>). This he states from 'Now then' and so on, up to before [the next] 'Now then.' Therein, first the example. Up to before 'Just so.' 'When the mother is ailing' — when there is illness in the mother,

body.text: yepīti na kevalaṃ śākyamuniḥ / tiṣṭhantīti santi / dhriyanta iti avatiṣṭhante / yāpayantīti yāvadāyuravatiṣṭhante / autsukyamāpadyante / kathamityāha / kimitītyādi / kidṛśī mātetyata āha / janayitrīti / asyāḥ sarvajñatāyāḥ / darśayitrīti prāpikā / evamiti janakatvenaiva / iti tathāgatasya nirvṛttau jñānaṃ prathamam //
body.translated_text: 'Even those' — not only <s>Śākyamuni</s>. 'They abide' means 'they exist.' 'They are sustained' means 'they remain.' 'They continue' means 'they remain for the extent of their lifespan.' They become anxious. How? He says beginning with 'How?' and so on. 'What kind of mother?' — to this he says 'the progenitress.' Of this <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience). 'The shower' means the one who leads to it.

body.text: lokasya sandarśayitrītyuktam / ataḥ pṛcchatyatha khalvityādinā / evamukta ityādi uttaram / loka ityākhyātā iti lujo vināśe / lujyante pralujyante kṣaṇikatvāt santānanirodhācceti lokāḥ / kartturyuc / nairukto varṇavyatyayaḥ / kathaṃ loka iti darśitā iti / yadi luñjanta iti lokāḥ / tadāsyāḥ ko 'tiśaya iti bhāvaḥ / viśvādarśitamiti(?)lujatvādanyat(?) / yato 'tiśayaḥ syādityarthaḥ / na lujyanta ityādi / nanu tathāpi vyāhatame[ta]t na lujyante na pralujyante tasmālloka iti? nāsti vyāghātaḥ / yasyāyamatra sambandhaḥ / loka iti pañcaskandhāḥ / te bhagavatyā prajñāpāra[mi]tayā na lujyante na pralujyanta iti darśitāḥ / tatkasya hetorityādinā praśnaḥ / śūnyatetyādinottaram / yathā śūnyatā evamanimittādaya ityāha na cetyādinā / kathamiti pṛṣṭam / ata evaṃ ityādinopasaṃhāraḥ / iti lokajñānaṃ dvitīyam //
body.translated_text: It has been said 'the shower to the world.' Therefore he asks beginning with 'Now then' and so on. Beginning with 'Thus spoken' and so on is the answer. '<s>Loka</s>' (world) means 'that which is named [from the root] <s>luj</s> in the sense of perishing.' 'The worlds perish and disintegrate' — because of momentariness and because of the cessation of the continuum — hence they are '<s>lokāḥ</s>.' The suffix <s>yuc</s> is in the agent sense. The etymological [analysis] involves transposition of letters. 'How is the world shown?' —

body.text: sattvānāṃ cittacaryāsvityanenāprameyāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ cittacaritajñānaṃ nirdiṣṭam / tacca na vināśatvāprameyatājñānena / tataḥ punaraparamityādinā sattvāprameyatājñānamuktvā yopītyādinā taccittacaritajñānamāha / tatra kathaṃ sattvānāmaprameyatājñānam? yatasteṣāṃ niḥsvabhāvatayā na pramāṇaṃ na saṃkhyā / kathaṃ taccittacaritānāṃ jñānam? sattvāsattayā teṣāmapyasattvāt / lokasya sandarśayitrīti sattvānāmapi lokatvāt / ityaprameyasattvacittacaritajñānaṃ tṛtīyam //
body.translated_text: 'In the mental conduct of beings' — by this, the knowledge of the mental conduct of immeasurable beings is indicated. And that [is known] not without the knowledge of the immeasurability of destruction. Therefore, beginning with 'Moreover' and so on, having stated the knowledge of the immeasurability of beings, he states the knowledge of their mental conduct beginning with 'Even those' and so on. There, how is there knowledge of the immeasurability of beings?

body.text: 'tatsaṃkṣepe bahirgatau' iti / bahirgatirvikṣepaḥ / tasya cittasya saṃkṣepasahitā bahirgatistatsaṃkṣepabahirgatiḥ / ataścittasya saṃkṣepavikṣepajñānaṃ punaraparagadyadvayenāha / sa saṃkṣepaṃ kṣayataḥ kṣayaṃ cākṣayato yathābhūtaṃ prajānātīti / saṃkṣepo hi cittasya prakṛtau sthānam / taccāsya kṣaya eva / sa cākṣayaścittaprakṛterakṣayatvāt / tasmātsa tathāgataḥ saṃkṣepaṃ kṣayataḥ kṣayaṃ cākṣayato yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / dharmatāta ityādi / lyablope pañcamī / cittadharmatāmapekṣya tāni vikṣiptāni bahirmukhatvāt prajānāti / svalakṣaṇāpekṣayā kīdṛśānītyāha / akṣīṇānītyādi /
body.translated_text: 'In its contraction and outward activity' — 'outward activity' (<s>bahirgati</s>) is distraction. The contraction of that mind together with [its] outward activity is 'its contraction-and-outward-activity.' Hence the knowledge of the mind's contraction and distraction — he states this by two 'Moreover' prose passages. 'He knows as it truly is the contraction as decrease and the decrease as non-decrease.' 'Contraction'

body.text: na kṣīṇāni nāpyaṃśataḥ kṣīṇāni tato na saṃkṣiptāni / avikṣiptānīti nāpi vikṣiptāni / kuta ityāha / alakṣaṇāni hīti / yasmātsvalakṣaṇaiḥ śūnyānītyarthaḥ / iti cittasaṃkṣepavikṣepajñānaṃ caturtham //
body.translated_text: — [they are] not decreased, nor even partially decreased, therefore not contracted. 'Nor distracted' — and not distracted either. Why? He says: 'Because they are without characteristics' — because they are empty of their own characteristics — this is the meaning. Thus, the knowledge of the mind's contraction and distraction is the fourth.

body.text: 'akṣayākāratāyāṃ ca' iti kṣayapāṭho mahatyau prati / imāṃ tu prati 'ameyākṣayatāyāṃ ca' iti pāṭhaḥ / asyāṃ hi paṭhyate aprameyākṣayāni cittānīti / tadāha / punaraparamityādinā / kathaṃ ceti praśnaḥ / uttaraṃ tasyetyādinā / adhiṣṭhitamiti na kadācinna sthitamanādinidhanamityarthaḥ / dharmatayeti bhāvaḥ / ata eva saṃskṛtalakṣaṇābhāvād anirodhamanutpādamasthitam / anāśrayaṃ ṣaṇṇāmapīndriyāṇāṃ tasminnavyāpārāt / pramāṇābhāvād aprameyam / kṣayābhāvād akṣayam / yeneti yenādhiṣṭhitatvādinā / ākāśetyādi / yathā ākāśasyāprameyatākṣatayā tathā cittasya / evamityādinopasaṃhāraḥ / iti aprameyākṣayatājñānaṃ pañcamam //
body.translated_text: 'And in the indestructible aspect' — the reading '<s>kṣaya</s>' (decrease) is for the larger [text]. But for this [text] the reading is '<s>ameyākṣayatāyāṃ ca</s>' (and in the immeasurable indestructibility). For in this [text] it reads: 'the minds are immeasurable and indestructible.' This he states beginning with 'Moreover' and so on. 'And how?' is the question. The answer begins with 'Of that' and so on. '<s>Adhiṣṭhita</s>' (sustained) means 'never not',

body.text: aprameyākṣayatāyāṃ ceti cakāro 'nuktasamuccayārthaḥ / tena saṃkliṣṭāsaṃkliṣṭajñānaṃ līnapragṛhītajñānaṃ sāśravānāśravajñānaṃ ca parigṛhyate / tatrādyaṃ punaraparagadyadvayenāha / asaṃkleśasaṃkliṣṭānīti saṃkliṣṭiḥ saṃkleśaḥ kleśopakleśairmalinīkaraṇam / na saṃkleśo 'saṃkleśaḥ / tena saṃkliṣṭāni / yato 'saṃketāni / kit nivāse / cittadharmatā(ta)yā na samyaksthānaṃ teṣāmāgantukatvāt / prakṛtītyādi / cittadharmatā hi prakṛtyaiva prabhāsvarā nirmalā nityamasaṃkliṣṭeti saṃkliṣṭāsaṃkliṣṭacittajñānaṃ ṣaṣṭham //
body.translated_text: 'And in the immeasurable indestructibility' — the word '<s>ca</s>' (and) has the sense of gathering what is unmentioned. By this, the knowledge of the defiled and undefiled, the knowledge of the slack and uplifted, and the knowledge of the with-outflows and without-outflows are included. Among those, the first is stated by two 'Moreover' prose passages. '<s>Asaṃkleśasaṃkliṣṭāni</s>' (defiled without defilement) — '<s>saṃkliṣṭi</s>' is defilement (<s>saṃkleśa</s>), [which is] the contamination by afflictions and secondary afflictions.

body.text: dvitīyaṃ punaraparagadyadvayenāha / anālayalīnānīti / anālayo 'layanam / alayanenaiva līnāni / cittaṃ hi līnaṃ na cittaprakṛtiḥ / na hi cittaprakṛtirna mahyaṃ na meti vā / agrāhyāṇi tāni cittāni na pragrahītavyānīti / agrahaṇaṃ pragrahaḥ / praśabdasya pratiṣedhārthatvāt / prasthānavat pravāsavacceti bhāvaḥ / iti līnapragṛhītacittajñānaṃ saptamam //
body.translated_text: The second is stated by two 'Moreover' prose passages. '<s>Anālayalīnāni</s>' (slack without clinging) — '<s>anālaya</s>' is non-clinging; through non-clinging itself they are slack. For the mind is slack, not the nature of the mind. For the nature of the mind is not 'mine' or 'not mine.' 'Ungraspable' — those minds are not to be uplifted. '<s>Agrahaṇa</s>' is <s>pragraha</s> (uplift); the prefix '<s>pra</s>-'

body.text: punaraparagadyadvayena tṛtīyamāha / asvabhāvānītyādi / ātmanyeva bhāvaḥ svabhāvaḥ / tadabhāvādasvabhāvāni / visaratyebhiścittamityāsravā asaṃkalpāḥ / tadyogātsāsravāṇi / kutaḥ? yato 'satsaṃkalpāni / asatāṃ kāmarūpārūpyabhavānāṃ kalpanāt / abhāvagatikānītyādi / abhāvaḥ śūnyatā / sā gatireṣāmiti tathoktāni / tasmād anābhogāni kāmarūpārūpyabhaveṣu visaraṇāt / tato 'nāsravāṇītyarthaḥ / iti sāsravānāsravacittajñānamaṣṭamam //
body.translated_text: By two 'Moreover' prose passages, the third is stated. Beginning with '<s>asvabhāvāni</s>' (without intrinsic nature) and so on. '<s>Svabhāva</s>' (intrinsic nature) is existence in itself; because of its absence, [they are] without intrinsic nature. '<s>Āsravas</s>' (outflows) are [those through which] the mind flows outward — [they are] unwholesome resolves (<s>asatsaṃkalpāḥ</s>); because of connection with those, [the minds are] with outflows. Why? Because they are 'of unwholesome resolve' — because of imagining [the pleasures of] the realms of desire, form, and formless. 'Without existence as its destination'

body.text: 'sarāgādau' iti / sarāgavītarāgajñānaṃ sadoṣavītadoṣajñānaṃ samohavītamohajñānaṃ ca / tatrādau punaraparagadyadvayenāha / yā cittasya sarāgatetyādi / cittasya sarāgatā na cittaprakṛteḥ / tasmādvinaiva rāgaṃ sarāgāṇītyarthaḥ / yaścittasya vigama ityādi / vigamaḥ śūnyatā / na sā sarāgateti saiva vītarāgatetyarthaḥ / iti sarāgavītarāgacittajñānaṃ navamam //
body.translated_text: 'Beginning with attachment' (<s>sarāgādau</s>) — the knowledge of [minds] with and without attachment, the knowledge of [minds] with and without aversion, and the knowledge of [minds] with and without delusion. Among those, the first is stated by two 'Moreover' prose passages. Beginning with 'That which is the attachment of the mind' and so on. The attachment of the mind is not [the attachment] of the nature of the mind. Therefore, the meaning is: they are with attachment even without attachment. 'And that which is the disappearance of the mind' and so on —

body.text: punaraparagadyadvayena dvitīyam / tatsubodham / iti sadoṣavītadoṣacittajñānaṃ daśamam //
body.translated_text: By two further prose [passages], the second [type is stated]. That is easily understood. Thus the knowledge of mind with faults and free from faults is the tenth.

body.text: tataḥ punaraparagadyadvayena tṝtīyam / iti samohavītamohacittajñānamekādaśam //
body.translated_text: Then, by two further prose [passages], the third [type is stated]. Thus the knowledge of mind with delusion and free from delusion is the eleventh.

body.text: "pravistṛte mahadgate 'pramāṇe ca" iti śāstram / pravistṛtaṃ vipulamanantaṃ kāmadhātvālambanaṃ brahmavihārādi / mahadgataṃ rūpadhātvālambanam / kāmādrūpasya prakṛṣṭatvādārūpyadhātvālambanam / tridhātvālambanamanālambanaṃ cāpramāṇam / atastrīṇi jñānāni mahatyoḥ / vipulacittajñānaṃ mahadgatacittajñānamapramāṇacittajñānaṃ ca / imāṃ tu bhagavatīṃ prati 'apramāṇe ca' iti cakāro 'nuktasamuccayārthaścādyayorabhisambadhyate / vipule 'vipule ca / mahadgate 'mahadgate ca / apramāṇe ceti / tasmādasyāṃ trīṇī jñānāni / avipulavipulajñānam, amahadgatamahadgatajñānam, apramāṇajñānaṃ ceti / tatrādyaṃ punaraparagadyadvayenāha / asamutthānetyādi samutthānaṃ vistāraḥ / tadyogapratiṣedhād asamutthānayogāni / atiprasārapratiṣedhād asamutthānaparyāpannāni dharmatayā / tasmād avipulāni / na hīyanta ityādi / na hīyante nāpacīyante tasmānnāvipulāni / na vivardhante tasmānna vipulāni na vigacchantīti na viśeṣaṃ gacchanti / tasmānna vipulāni nāvipulāni / avigamatvādeveti nirvikāratvādeva cittānāmiti cittadharmatāyāḥ iti vipulāvipulacittajñānaṃ dvādaśaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Extensive, exalted, and immeasurable' — thus says the treatise. '<s>Pravistṛtam</s>' (extensive) means vast and infinite — [referring to] that which takes the desire realm as its object, such as the <s>brahmavihāras</s> (divine abidings) and so on. '<s>Mahadgatam</s>' (exalted) — [refers to] that which takes the form realm as its object. Because the form realm is superior to the desire realm, [what takes] the formless realm as its object [is also included]. '<s>Apramāṇam</s>' (immeasurable) — that which takes the three realms as its object and also that which is without object. Therefore there are three knowledges in the two great [texts]: the knowledge of the extensive mind, the knowledge of the exalted mind, and the knowledge of the immeasurable mind. But with regard to this <s>Bhagavatī</s> [text], in '<s>apramāṇe ca</s>' (and immeasurable), the particle '<s>ca</s>' has the sense of an unexpressed conjunction and connects with the first two [as well]: 'and extensive,' 'and exalted,' 'and immeasurable.' Therefore in this [text] there are three knowledges: the knowledge of the non-extensive-extensive, the knowledge of the non-exalted-exalted, and the knowledge of the immeasurable. Therein, the first is stated by two further prose [passages]. '<s>Asamutthāna</s>' and so forth — '<s>samutthāna</s>' means expansion. Because of the negation of its connection, they are 'of non-arising connection.' Because of the negation of excessive extension, they are 'comprised within non-arising,' by their <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature). Therefore they are non-extensive. 'They do not decrease' and so forth — they do not decrease, they do not diminish, therefore they are not non-extensive. They do not increase, therefore they are not extensive. 'They do not depart' means they do not undergo differentiation. Therefore they are neither extensive nor non-extensive. 'Because of non-departure itself' means because of the very changelessness of minds — that is, of the <s>dharmatā</s> of mind. Thus the knowledge of the extensive-non-extensive mind is the twelfth.

body.text: punaraparagadyadvayena dvitīyamāha / anāgatikānītyādi / dūrādantike gatirāgatiḥ / antikāddūragatirgatiḥ / parito gatiḥ paryāpanna
body.translated_text: By two further prose [passages], the second [type] is stated. '<s>Anāgatikāni</s>' and so forth — movement from far to near is '<s>āgati</s>' (coming). Movement from near to far is '<s>gati</s>' (going). Movement all around is '<s>paryāpanna</s>' (being encompassed),

body.text: lokasandarśanaparivarto nāma dvādaśaḥ //
body.translated_text: The chapter named '<s>Lokasandarśana-parivarta</s>' (Showing the World) is the twelfth.

body.text: acintyaparivarto nāma trayodaśaḥ //
body.translated_text: The chapter named '<s>Acintya-parivarta</s>' (The Inconceivable) is the thirteenth.

body.text: This chapter is missing in original text
body.translated_text: This chapter is missing in the original text.

body.text: aupamyaparivarto nāma caturdaśaḥ //
body.translated_text: The chapter named '<s>Aupamya-parivarta</s>' (Analogy) is the fourteenth.

body.text: This chapter is missing in original text
body.translated_text: This chapter is missing in the original text.

body.text: 15. devaparivarto nāma pañcadaśaḥ
body.translated_text: 15. The chapter named '<s>Deva-parivarta</s>' (The Gods) is the fifteenth.

body.text: ...........tyāha / yānyenamityādi / kāni punarasya kalyāṇamitrāṇītyata āha tānyevetyādi / tānyasmai kathamarthamupadekṣyantītyata āha evaṃ cetyādi / evamanenākāreṇa / ehi tvamityādinā kārṣīrityetadantena / yogamiti prayogamabhiyogaṃ vā / mā parāmṛkṣa iti tabhdāvena mā grahīḥ / aparāmṛṣṭeti sarvadharmairavikalpitā / parijayo 'bhyāsaḥ / evaṃ hītyādinā upasaṃhāraḥ / samyaksambodhī samyakpariṇāmanamanāsvādaḥ / ityanāsvādanāviśeṣeṇa mārge caturthaḥ kṣaṇaḥ //
body.translated_text: He says [beginning with] 'those which' and so forth. 'What then are his <s>kalyāṇamitras</s> (spiritual friends)?' — to this he says 'those very' and so forth. 'How will those instruct him in the meaning?' — to this he says 'Thus' and so forth. 'In this manner' — 'Come, you' and so forth up to 'you should do.' '<s>Yoga</s>' means practice or application. 'Do not grasp' means 'do not seize with attachment.' '<s>Aparāmṛṣṭā</s>' means 'unconceptualized with respect to all <s>dharmas</s>.' '<s>Parijaya</s>' means familiarization. 'For thus' and so forth is the conclusion. '<s>Samyaksambodhi</s>' (perfect awakening), perfect dedication — non-relishing. Thus, by the distinction of non-relishing, [this is] the fourth moment in the path.

body.text: ukto viśeṣaḥ ṣoḍaśavidhaḥ / kāritraṃ daśavidhaṃ vaktavyam / tatra śāstram-
body.translated_text: The sixteen-fold distinction has been stated. The tenfold conduct (<s>kāritra</s>) is to be explained. Therein, the treatise [states] —

children.text: hitaṃ sukhaṃ ca trāṇaṃ ca śaraṇaṃ layanaṃ nṛṇām /
children.translated_text: 'Benefit, happiness, protection, refuge, shelter for beings,
final resort, island, and that called 'guide.' // 4-27 //
'Without deliberate effort, having the nature of direct realization of the fruit by the three vehicles,
the last is the conduct of [reaching the] destination — this is the characteristic of conduct.' // 4-28 //

body.text: etadāha subhūtirityādinā / tacca duṣkaretyādinā subhūtiḥ prastauti / evametadityādinā bhagavānācaṣṭe / ye lokahitāya samprasthitā iti bodhimabhisambudhya pañcabhyo gatibhyaḥ sattvān parimocya teṣāmabhaye nirvāṇe pratiṣṭhāpanāditi hitakāritram //
body.translated_text: This is stated by [the passage beginning with] '<s>Subhūti</s> said' and so on. And that [conduct] being difficult — by 'It is difficult' and so on, <s>Subhūti</s> introduces [it]. By 'It is so' and so on, the <s>Bhagavān</s> explains. 'Those who have set forth for the benefit of the world' — having fully awakened to <s>bodhi</s>, liberating beings from the five <s>gatis</s> (destinies) and establishing them in the fearless <s>nirvāṇa</s> — this is the conduct of benefit.

body.text: lokasukhāya lokānukampāyai samprasthitā iti bodhimabhisambudhya sattvān duḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsebhyaḥ parimocya teṣāṃ sukhe nirvāṇe pratiṣṭhāpanamiti sukhakāritram //
body.translated_text: 'Having set forth for the happiness of the world, out of compassion for the world' — having fully awakened to <s>bodhi</s>, liberating beings from suffering, grief, and distress, and establishing them in the <s>nirvāṇa</s> of happiness — this is the conduct of happiness.

body.text: lokasya trāṇaṃ bhaviṣyāma ityādinā trāṇādikāritrāṇāmuddeśaḥ / ityevaṃrūpaṃ vīryamārabhanta iti sambandhaḥ / yathoddeśamaṣṭābhiḥ kathañcavākyairnirdeśaḥ / tata iti tebhyo duḥkhebhyaḥ / enamiti lokam / vyāyacchanta iti saṃrakṣanti / vīryamiti prayogam / trāṇaṃ bhavanti trāṇakaraṇāditi trāṇakāritram //
body.translated_text: By 'We shall become the protection of the world' and so forth, the outline of the conducts of protection and so on [is given]. 'They undertake vigor of this kind' — this is the connection. In accordance with the outline, the detailed exposition is by eight 'however' sentences. '<s>Tataḥ</s>' means 'from those sufferings.' '<s>Enam</s>' means 'the world.' '<s>Vyāyacchante</s>' means 'they guard.' '<s>Vīryam</s>' means 'exertion.' 'They become protection, because of the act of protecting' — this is the conduct of protection.
Thus beginning with [that passage]........... ..........

body.text: [avidyā]ṇḍajamasminniti kṛtvā / sa eva paṭalaṃ dṛṣṭirodhakatvāt / avidyaivāṇḍakośapaṭalaṃ tena paryavanaddhā avaguṇṭhitāḥ / tamo mohaḥ / tenābhibhūtā andhīkṛtāḥ / avabhāsayantaḥ ālokaṃ kurvantaḥ / vidhunvanti apanayanti / evamālokakaraṇādālokā bhavantītyālokakāritram //
body.translated_text: '<s>Aṇḍaja</s>' (egg-born) [is applied] in this [context] — 'because of this' is the reasoning. That itself is the membrane (<s>paṭala</s>), because it obstructs vision. Ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) itself is the egg-shell membrane; by that they are enveloped, covered. '<s>Tamas</s>' is delusion; by that they are overwhelmed, made blind. '<s>Avabhāsayantaḥ</s>' means 'producing light.' '<s>Vidhunvanti</s>' means 'they remove.' Thus, because of producing light, they become lights — this is the conduct of illumination.

body.text: anutpādaścānirodhaśceti samāhāradvandvaḥ / prakṛtiḥ sarvadharmāṇāṃ dharmatā / tayā teṣāmanutpādānirodhāya dharmadeśanāt pariṇāyakāḥ parito netāraḥ paramārthabodhakā iti pariṇāyakakāritram //
body.translated_text: 'Non-arising and non-ceasing' — this is a collective compound (<s>samāhāra-dvandva</s>). '<s>Prakṛti</s>' is the <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature) of all <s>dharmas</s>. By that, for the sake of [teaching] the non-arising and non-ceasing of those [dharmas], because of teaching the <s>Dharma</s>, [they are] '<s>pariṇāyakas</s>' (guides) — leaders all around, instructors in the ultimate truth — this is the conduct of guiding.

children.translated_text: 'Without deliberate effort, having the nature of direct realization of the fruit by the three vehicles,
the last is the conduct of [reaching the] destination' — [this is the characteristic of conduct.] //

body.text: iti tribhiryānairanābhogataḥ phalasākṣātkriyātmakaṃ gatikāritramityarthaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus, by the three vehicles, without deliberate effort, having the nature of direct realization of the fruit — this is the conduct of [reaching the] destination — this is the meaning.

body.text: grāmasya (?) hi gatiḥ prāptireva / yadābhogena gamanena yānatrayaphalasyāpi gatiḥ prāptireva sā tu nirābhogā / na hi pumān kāyena cetasā vā gantvā tatprāpnoti kintvābhogata eva / tathā hyākāśagatikāḥ sarvadharmāḥ / na hyākāśasya gatirāgatirvā / svabhāva evāsya gatiḥ / tasmādākāśagatikā ityākāśasamāḥ / kuta ityāha / yathā hītyādi / akṛtamanutpāditatvāt / avikṛtamavasthāntarānutpādanāt / anabhisaṃskṛtaṃ hetupratyayaiḥ sambhūya tasyākaraṇāt / sthitamutpadya vṛtteḥ / saṃsthitaṃ samantataḥ sthiteḥ / vyavasthitaṃ kvacideva sthiteḥ / eṣāṃ viparyāsādāsthitamasaṃsthitamavyavasthitam / ākāśakalpatvādavikalpā nirābhogāḥ / dharmatāmātratvāddharmāṇāmiti bhāvaḥ /
body.translated_text: For the '<s>gati</s>' (destination) of the village is nothing but arrival. That which, through deliberate effort and movement, is the arrival — the attainment of the fruit of the three vehicles — that too is arrival, but it is without deliberate effort. For a person does not arrive at it by going with body or mind, but rather spontaneously. For thus, all <s>dharmas</s> have space as their destination. For space has neither going nor coming. Its very own nature is its destination. Therefore 'having space as their destination' means 'equal to space.' How so? — he says 'Just as' and so forth. '<s>Akṛtam</s>' — because of being unproduced. '<s>Avikṛtam</s>' — because of not producing another state. '<s>Anabhisaṃskṛtam</s>' — because of not being produced by the convergence of causes and conditions. '<s>Sthitam</s>' — because of continuing after arising. '<s>Saṃsthitam</s>' — because of being established on all sides. '<s>Vyavasthitam</s>' — because of being established in a specific [location]. The opposites of these are <s>asthita</s> (non-abiding), <s>asaṃsthita</s> (non-established), and <s>avyavasthita</s> (non-determined). Because of being like space, they are unconceptualized and without deliberate effort — because <s>dharmas</s> are nothing but <s>dharmatā</s> — this is the import.

body.text: yathā vākāśagatikā evaṃ śūnyatādigatikāḥ / tadevamagatigatikāḥ sarvadharmā iti........gatikāritram //
body.translated_text: Just as they have space as their destination, so too they have emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) and the rest as their destination. Thus, all <s>dharmas</s> have non-going as their destination — this is ........ the conduct of destination.

body.text: uktaṃ daśavidhaṃ kāritram /
body.translated_text: The tenfold conduct has been stated.
.......... the treatise [states] —

children.translated_text: 'Of afflictions, signs, and marks, of the adverse and the antidote,
detachment, and the nature of difficult-solitary — the outline is [based on] non-apprehension.' // 4-29 //
'And the prohibited attachment, and that called the object-cognition,
the non-opposing doubt — that has the nature of non-basis, non-destination, and non-birth.' // 4-30 //
'And the non-apprehension of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) — the own-nature is sixteen-fold.

children.text: lakṣmīva lakṣa(kṣya)te ceti caturthaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ matam // 4-31 //
children.translated_text: Like <s>Lakṣmī</s>, it is perceived — thus the fourth characteristic is held.' // 4-31 //

body.text: yaḥ svabhāvaścaturthaṃ lakṣaṇamiṣṭaṃ sa ṣoḍaśavidhaḥ / sarvakarmasādhanaṃ lakṣaṇam / lakṣyata iti kṛtvā / ata evāha 'lakṣyate ceti' / lakṣaṇāntaramapyāha 'lakṣmīva' iti / lakṣmayogāllakṣmī lakṣaṇayogāllakṣaṇamityarthaḥ / kathaṃ 'ṣoḍaśātmakaḥ'? ityata āha'kleśaliṅge 'tyādi / ato 'sya prastāvanā subhūtirāhetyādinā bhagavānāhetyataḥ prāk / caritāḥ ṣaṭpāramitā rakṣantīti caritāvinaḥ / katame ta ityāha / ya imāmityādi / kiṃsvabhāvā ityanena padena svabhāvapraśnaḥ / uttaraṃ bhagavānāhetyādinā / vinayo 'panayaḥ / tamarhantīti vainayikāḥ / tairviviktaḥ svabhāva eṣāmiti tathoktāḥ / iyatā catvāraḥ svabhāvā uktāḥ / kleśavivekaḥ / kleśaliṅgavivekaḥ / kleśanimittavivekaḥ / vipakṣapratipakṣavivekaśca / tatra kleśo rāgādiḥ / kleśaliṅgaṃ kleśakṛtaṃ kāyādidauṣṭhulyam / kleśanimittamayoniśo manasikārādi / vivakṣapratipakṣau rāgārāgau dveṣādveṣo mohāmohau ca / subhūtirāhetyādinā subhūtirāhetyataḥ prāk / etadāha / eṣa eva svabhāvo gatiḥ yāmabhisambudhya deśayiṣyantaḥ sattvānāṃ gatirbhaviṣyantīti //
body.translated_text: That which is the own-nature — the fourth characteristic that is accepted — is sixteen-fold. The characteristic is that which accomplishes all actions — because 'it is perceived' (<s>lakṣyate</s>). Therefore he says 'it is perceived.' He also states another characteristic: 'Like <s>Lakṣmī</s>' — through the connection with <s>lakṣma</s> (mark), [it is called] <s>Lakṣmī</s>; through the connection with characteristic, [it is called] '<s>lakṣaṇa</s>' — this is the meaning. How is it 'sixteen-fold'? — to this he says '<s>kleśaliṅga</s>' and so on. Therefore its introduction [begins with] '<s>Subhūti</s> said' and so on, up to just before '<s>Bhagavān</s> said.' 'Having practiced the six <s>pāramitās</s>, they protect' — hence '<s>caritāvinaḥ</s>' (those whose conduct [is such]). 'Who are they?' — to this he says 'Those who this' and so on. 'Of what nature?' — by this word, the question about own-nature [is asked]. The answer [begins with] '<s>Bhagavān</s> said' and so on. '<s>Vinaya</s>' means removal. 'Those who are worthy of that' are <s>vainayikas</s> (those to be trained). 'Detached from those' is the own-nature of these — thus they are so called. To this extent, four own-natures have been stated: detachment from afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>); detachment from signs of affliction (<s>kleśaliṅga</s>); detachment from marks of affliction (<s>kleśanimitta</s>); and detachment from the adverse and its antidote (<s>vipakṣa-pratipakṣa</s>). Therein, '<s>kleśa</s>' means passion (<s>rāga</s>) and the rest. '<s>Kleśaliṅga</s>' means the unsuitability of body and so on caused by affliction. '<s>Kleśanimitta</s>' means improper attention (<s>ayoniśo manasikāra</s>) and the rest. '<s>Vipakṣa-pratipakṣa</s>' means passion and non-passion, hatred and non-hatred, delusion and non-delusion. [This runs from] '<s>Subhūti</s> said' and so on, up to just before [the next] '<s>Subhūti</s> said.' He states this: this very own-nature is the '<s>gati</s>' (destination) — having fully awakened to which, they will teach, and will become the destination [i.e., refuge] of beings.

body.text: subhūtirāhetyādi buddhabhūmirveti yāvat / atra na rūpādisambaddha iti na rūpādisvabhāvāyai(ya) svabodhaye / na rūpāderarthāyeti na rūpādisvabhāvānāṃ sattvānāmarthāya / evaṃ na bhūmitraya svabhāvānāṃ (?) / svabodhaye / nāpi / nāpi bodhitrayasvabhāvānāṃ sattvānāmarthāya / tadityādinā praśnaḥ / uttaraṃ sarvetyādi / na pratikāṃkṣitavyānīti na labhyatvena draṣṭavyāni / atra trīṇi na draṣṭavyānītyekameva sthānaṃ draṣṭavyamiti bhāvaḥ / iti duṣkarasvabhāvaḥ //
body.translated_text: '<s>Subhūti</s> said' and so on, up to 'the <s>Buddha</s>-stage.' Here, 'not connected with form and so on' means not for the sake of the own-nature of form and so on — for one's own awakening. 'Not for the purpose of form and so on' means not for the sake of beings [characterized by] the own-natures of form and so on. Similarly, not [for the sake of] the own-natures of the three stages — for one's own awakening. Nor for the sake of beings [characterized by] the own-natures of the three awakenings. By '<s>Tat</s>' and so on, the question [is asked]. The answer [begins with] 'All' and so on. 'Not to be expected' means 'not to be seen as obtainable.' Here, 'three things are not to be seen' — [implies that] only one ground is to be seen — this is the import. Thus [this is] the own-nature of difficulty.

body.text: duṣkarasahita ekānto 'duṣkaraikāntaḥ' / evamukta ityādi yenāyamityataḥ prāk / abhimato 'rtho 'rthavaśaḥ / taṃ ca svayameva bhagavānāha / asthānaṃ hītyādinā buddhabhūmirvetyekāntaḥ / ityaikāntikasvabhāvaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Difficulty combined with solitariness' is '<s>duṣkaraikānta</s>' (the difficult-solitary). 'Thus spoken' and so on, up to just before 'by which this.' '<s>Arthavaśa</s>' means the intended meaning. And the <s>Bhagavān</s> himself states that: by 'It is impossible' and so on, up to 'the <s>Buddha</s>-stage' — [this is] the solitariness. Thus [this is] the own-nature of solitariness.

body.text: yenāyaṃ sarvasattvānāṃ kṛtaśaḥ sannāhaḥ sannaddha ityuddeśasvabhāvaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'By which this [armor] is donned systematically for all beings' — this is the own-nature of the outline.

body.text: subhūtirāhetyādi kaccidityataḥ prāk / gambhīreti pratijñā / catvāro hetavaḥ pare bhāvanānupalabdheḥ / adhvatrayepi bhāvakānupalabdheḥ / bhāvyasya prajñāpāramitāvastuno 'nupalabdheḥ / tadālambanānāṃ cānupalabdheriti / asiddhatvaparihārāya tatkasyetyādinā praśnaḥ / na hītyādinottaram / pariniṣpanno vastubhūtaḥ / ataścākāśabhāvanaiṣā sarvadharmabhāvanā ca dharmatāmātradarśanāddharmāṇāṃ cānupalabdheḥ / ata evāsaṅgabhāvanaiṣānantabhāvanā ca sarvadharmeṣvanupalabdheravyāghātāddharmāṇāṃ
body.translated_text: '<s>Subhūti</s> said' and so on, up to just before 'Is it the case that.' 'Profound' — this is the thesis. The four reasons are subsequent [to it]: because of the non-apprehension of cultivation; because of the non-apprehension of the cultivator even in the three times; because of the non-apprehension of the object to be cultivated, [namely] the thing that is <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>; and because of the non-apprehension of its objects. To ward off the charge of non-establishment, the question [begins with] 'Of what then?' and so on. The answer [begins with] 'Not indeed' and so on. '<s>Pariniṣpanna</s>' means 'existing as a real thing.' And therefore this is a cultivation [that is like] the cultivation of space, and a cultivation of all <s>dharmas</s> — because of seeing only <s>dharmatā</s> of <s>dharmas</s>, and because of the non-apprehension of <s>dharmas</s>. Therefore also this is a cultivation without attachment, and an infinite cultivation — because of non-apprehension in all <s>dharmas</s>, because of non-obstruction, and because of the infinity of <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: cānantyāt / asato bhāvanāsadbhāvanā grāhyānupalambhāt / aparigrahabhāvanā grāhakānupalambhāt / upaparīkṣitavyo veditavyaḥ / ityanupalambhakasvabhāvaḥ //
body.translated_text: And because of infinity — the cultivation of the non-existent is the cultivation of the existent, because of the non-apprehension of the graspable. The cultivation of non-grasping [is] because of the non-apprehension of the grasper. '<s>Upaparīkṣitavya</s>' means 'to be understood.' Thus [this is] the own-nature of non-apprehension.

body.text: kaccidityādinā subhūtirāhetyataḥ prāk / anabhiniveśasvabhāvaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Is it the case that' and so on, up to just before '<s>Subhūti</s> said.' [This is] the own-nature of non-attachment.

body.text: subhūtirāha / yo bhagavannityādi atha khalu śakra ityataḥ prāk / vyavacāritetyālambitā / nimnaprāgbhāvapravaṇaśabdā ādhārārthāḥ / taiḥ saha bahuvrīhiḥ / santatiścittasantānaḥ / ākāśanimnayeti ākāśopamatvāt sarvajñatāyāḥ / iyaṃ sā vyavacāraṇeti prajñāpāramitāyā iti śeṣaḥ / tadityākāśopamatvaṃ tasyāḥ kutaḥ? uttaram / aprameyā hītyādinā / deśataḥ kālataśca pramātumaśaktyatvādaprameyā / tathaiva pramāṇavirahād apramāṇā / na tadrūpaṃ yāvannāpi kvacitpradeśe sthitamiti / sarveṣāmeṣāṃ deśakālavyāpitvena pramāṇāviṣayatvādaprameyasya tādrūpyāyogāt / api tvityādi / taditi vartate / kenaciditi / kenacidrūpādinā svabhāvena / rūpādīnāṃ pramāṇāvattvāditi bhāvaḥ / tatkasyeti praśnaḥ / uttaraṃ rūpameva hītyādi / rūpādiśabdairatra rūpādidharmatocyate / tasmādavirodhaḥ / na ca rūpādibhedepi dharmatāyā bhedo rūpādīnāmalīkatvenābhedakatvāttadānīmastaṅgamāccetyālambanasvabhāvaḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> says 'That which, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is permanent' and so forth, up to before 'Now then, <s>Śakra</s>.' '<s>Vyavacāritā</s>' means 'apprehended.' The words <s>nimna</s> (inclined downward), <s>prāgbhāva</s> (directed forward), and <s>pravaṇa</s> (tending toward) have the sense of a support; with these there is a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound. '<s>Santati</s>' means the mental continuum (<s>cittasantāna</s>). '<s>Ākāśanimnā</s>' (inclined toward space) — because <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience) is like space. 'This is that discernment' — the word '<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>' is to be supplied. 'That' — whence comes the space-like nature of that [<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>]? The answer is given by 'immeasurable indeed' and so forth. It is immeasurable because it cannot be measured in terms of place or time. Similarly, it is without measure (<s>apramāṇā</s>) because of the absence of any standard of measurement. Its form is not established anywhere, even in any location whatsoever. Because all these — place, time, and pervasiveness — are beyond the scope of measurement, it is impossible for the immeasurable to have such a form. 'But moreover' and so forth — 'that' is continued [from before]. 'By anything' means by any intrinsic nature such as form and the rest. The sense is: because form and the rest are subject to measurement. 'Then of what?' — this is the question. The answer is 'form itself indeed' and so forth. The words 'form and the rest' here refer to the <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature) of form and the rest. Therefore there is no contradiction. And even though there is differentiation among form and the rest, there is no differentiation in <s>dharmatā</s>, because form and the rest, being unreal, are incapable of producing differentiation — at that time there is cessation. // This is the nature of the object of apprehension. //

body.text: atha khalu śakra ityādyāparivartasamāpteḥ / gambhīrā duradhimocatvāt / duravagāhā cintāmayyā prajñayā durdṛśā laukikabhāvanāmayyā / duranubodhā lokottarāyā / cikīrṣitasyākaraṇamalpotsukatā / avanatamāvarjitam / yatra na kaścidityādinā traiyadhvikakriyāniṣedhaḥ / ākāśetyādinā karmaniṣedhaḥ / ātmetyādinā kartṛniṣedhaḥ / sarvadharmāṇāṃ labhyānāmanāgamanatayā heyānāmagamanatayā ca gambhīraḥ / vipratyanīko viparītaḥ / yato 'nugrahāyāvikalpanāyaiṣa dharma udgrahe ca lokaścarati / lokaviparītā pratītirvipratyayaḥ / iti vipratyayasvabhāvaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Now then, <s>Śakra</s>' and so forth, up to the end of the chapter. 'Profound' — because it is difficult to comprehend. 'Hard to fathom' — difficult to see through wisdom born of reflection (<s>cintāmayī prajñā</s>). 'Hard to realize' — through mundane meditative wisdom (<s>laukikabhāvanāmayī</s>). 'Hard to fully understand' — through supramundane [wisdom]. 'Low enthusiasm' is the failure to accomplish what one intends. '<s>Avanatam</s>' means 'inclined,' that is, '<s>āvarjitam</s>' (turned toward). By 'where no one' and so forth, there is the negation of activity across the three times. By 'space' and so forth, the negation of action. By 'self' and so forth, the negation of the agent. Because all <s>dharmas</s> that can be obtained do not come into being, and because those to be abandoned do not arrive — [therefore it is] profound. '<s>Vipratyanīka</s>' means contrary, opposite. Because this <s>dharma</s> is taught for the sake of benefit, non-conceptualization, and apprehension, while the world conducts [itself otherwise]. The worldly understanding that is contrary is '<s>vipratyaya</s>' (mistrust). // This is the nature of mistrust. //

body.text: devaiḥ śakrādibhirupalakṣitaḥ parivarto devaparivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: The chapter characterized by <s>devas</s> such as <s>Śakra</s> and others is the '<s>Deva-parivarta</s>' (Chapter on the Gods). //

body.text: āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ sāratamānāmni pañjikāyāṃ ratnākaraśāntiviracitāyāṃ pañcadaśaḥ parivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: In the <s>Pañjikā</s> commentary named <s>Sāratama</s>, composed by <s>Ratnākaraśānti</s>, on the noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s> — this is the fifteenth chapter. //

body.text: 16. tathatāparivarto nāma ṣoḍaśaḥ /
body.translated_text: 16. The sixteenth [chapter] is named the '<s>Tathatā-parivarta</s>' (Chapter on Suchness).

body.text: atha khalvityādi / nāyaṃ kvacitpratihanyata iti sarvatrāsya bādhakābhāvāt / ataśca apratihatalakṣaṇo 'pratihatasvabhāvaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Now then' and so forth. 'It is not obstructed anywhere' — because there is no obstruction to it anywhere. And therefore, 'having the characteristic of being unobstructed' means having the nature of being unimpeded.

body.text: ākāśasamatayeti / yata ākāśasamaṃ tatastadvadevāpratigham / kutaḥ samatetyata āha / sarvapadānāṃ sarvavastūnāṃ anupalabdhitaḥ / apratimo nirupamaḥ advitīyatvāditi sadṛśābhāvāt / pratibodhakaṃ lakṣaṇamasyeti pratilakṣaṇaḥ / tadabhāvād apratilakṣaṇaḥ / niṣpratyarthikatvāditi virodharahitatvāt / ityapratihatasvabhāvaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'By the equality with space' — because it is equal to space, therefore it is just so, unobstructed. 'Why is it equal?' — to this he says: 'because of the non-apprehension of all <s>padas</s> (entities), of all things.' '<s>Apratima</s>' means without comparison, because of being without a second, that is, because of the absence of anything similar. '<s>Pratilakṣaṇa</s>' means 'having a characteristic that enables recognition'; because of its absence, it is '<s>apratilakṣaṇa</s>' (without distinguishing marks). Because of being without an adversary — that is, because of being free from opposition. // This is the nature of being unobstructed. //

body.text: padaṃ pratiṣṭhā sugatidurgatinirvāṇāni / tadabhāvād apadaḥ / anabhinirvṛttatvāditi / na khalvanabhinirvṛttasya kvacitpratiṣṭhā / kuto 'nabhinirvṛttaḥ? yato 'nutpāda utpādarahitaḥ / kuto 'nutpādaḥ? sarvotpattīnāmanutpattitvāt / na hi satāmutpattirutpattilakṣaṇāyogāt / nāpyasatām / asattvādeva kharaviṣāṇavat / durgatipathaḥ sugatipatho nirvāṇapathaśceti panthānaḥ / tadabhāvād apathaḥ / ata evāha / sarvapathānupalabdhitvāt / ityapadasvabhāvaḥ //
body.translated_text: '<s>Pada</s>' means a resting place — the good destinies, bad destinies, and <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Because of their absence, it is '<s>apada</s>' (without foundation). 'Because of being unaccomplished' — indeed, that which is unaccomplished has no resting place anywhere. Why is it unaccomplished? Because '<s>anutpāda</s>' means devoid of arising. Why is there non-arising? Because all arisings are themselves non-arising. For there is no arising of what already exists, since the characteristic of arising is inapplicable [to what already is]. Nor of what does not exist — precisely because of its non-existence, like the horns of a rabbit. The path of bad destinies, the path of good destinies, and the path of <s>nirvāṇa</s> — these are the paths. Because of their absence, it is '<s>apatha</s>' (pathless).
