Therefore he says: 'because of the non-apprehension of all paths.' // This is the nature of being without foundation. //

body.text: atha khalvityādi / anujāta iti / anupūrvo janiḥ sakarmakaḥ / karmāsya janakaḥ / kartā janyaḥ / anuḥ sādṛśye / tasmādiha kartari ktaḥ / karmaṇi ṣaṣṭhi / sambandhavivakṣayā bhagavato 'nujātaḥ subhūtiḥ / tatkasyetyādi tattasyānujātatvaṃ? uttaraṃ tathā hītyādinā / bhagavata eṣa putraḥ sadṛśaśca śūnyatāvāditvāditi bhāvaḥ / atha khalvityādi / ajātatvādityanujātatve hetumāha / ajātatvena pitāputrayoḥ sādṛśyāditi bhāvaḥ / yadyajātaḥ tau kathaṃ pitāputrau? saṃvṛtyeti bhāvaḥ / anupā(jā)ta ityādinā hetvantaramāha / anupā(jā)to 'nugatastathāgatasya tathatām / tatopyanujātastathāgatasya / anugamya jāto 'nujāta iti bhāvaḥ / asiddho heturiti cedāha / yathetyādi / anāgatetyanutpannā / agatetyavinaṣṭā / kiṃ punaḥ prāpte 'rhattve 'nupā(jā)taḥ kiṃ vā pūrvamevetyata āha / ādita ityādi / atathateti / tathatāśabdānābhidheyatvāt / evaṃ hītyādinopasaṃhāraḥ / gatyagatī(?) gatiḥ / tatpratiṣedhādagatisvabhāvaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Now then' and so forth. '<s>Anujāta</s>' — '<s>jani</s>' (birth) preceded by '<s>anu</s>' takes an object. The object here is the progenitor. The agent is the one born. '<s>Anu</s>' is in the sense of resemblance. Therefore here the <s>kta</s> suffix is in the agent [sense]. The sixth case [genitive] is for the object. Through the desire to express a relationship — '<s>Subhūti</s> is born after <s>Bhagavān</s>.' 'Then of whom?' and so forth — whose born-after nature is that? The answer is by 'for thus' and so forth. The sense is: he is the son of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and is similar [to him] because both teach <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness). 'Now then' and so forth. 'Because of being unborn' and so on — he states the reason for being '<s>anujāta</s>.' The sense is: because of the similarity of father and son in being unborn. If they are unborn, how are they father and son? The sense is: conventionally (<s>saṃvṛtyā</s>). By '<s>anupājāta</s>' and so forth, he states another reason. '<s>Anupājāta</s>' means he has followed (<s>anugata</s>) the <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Therefore too he is '<s>anujāta</s>' of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. The sense is: having followed, he is born — hence '<s>anujāta</s>.' If the reason is unestablished, he says 'just as' and so forth. '<s>Anāgata</s>' means unarisen. '<s>Agata</s>' means unperished. 'Furthermore, is he born-after upon attaining <s>arhathood</s>, or already before?' — to this he says 'from the very beginning' and so forth. '<s>Atathatā</s>' — because it is not expressible by the word <s>tathatā</s>. By 'for thus' and so forth, there is the conclusion. '<s>Gatyagatī</s>' (?) is motion. By its negation — // this is the nature of being without motion. //

body.text: anujātatve hetvantaramāha tathāgatasyetyādinā / tathatā hi dharmāṇāṃ sthitiḥ / anatikramaṇīyatvāttathāvasthitā / hetvantaramāha / yathetyādinā / pūrvasvabhāvānuvṛtteḥ avikārā / svabhāvāntarānutpatteḥ nirvikārā / vikalpasvabhāvābhāvād avikalpā / vikalpāviṣayatvāt nirvikalpā / hetvantaramāha / yathācetyādinā / na kvacitpratihanyata iti sarvagatatvāt / tatkasya hetoriti / tadapratihatatvaṃ kutaḥ? tathā hi yasya yā tathatā tatraiva sāsti tato 'nyatra pratihanyata eva / vastvabhāvāt / uttaraṃ yā cetyādinā evaṃ hītyataḥ prāk / ekaivaiṣeti pratijñā / tatkimekajātīyatvādekā? netyāha / advayeti / dvayaṃ bhedastadabhāvādadvayetyeko
body.translated_text: He states another reason for being <s>anujāta</s> with '<s>Tathāgata</s>'s' and so forth. For <s>tathatā</s> is the abiding nature (<s>sthiti</s>) of <s>dharmas</s>. It abides as such because it cannot be transgressed. He states another reason with 'just as' and so forth. It is '<s>avikārā</s>' (unchanging) because of the continuity of its prior nature. It is '<s>nirvikārā</s>' (free from transformation) because no other nature arises. It is '<s>avikalpā</s>' (non-conceptual) because of the absence of a conceptual nature. It is '<s>nirvikalpā</s>' (beyond conceptualization) because it is beyond the domain of conceptualization. He states another reason with 'and just as' and so forth. 'It is not obstructed anywhere' — because of being present everywhere. 'For what reason?' — whence comes that unobstructed nature? For indeed, the <s>tathatā</s> of whatever [thing] exists only there [in that thing]; elsewhere it would indeed be obstructed — because of the non-existence of the entity [elsewhere]. The answer is by 'and that which' and so forth, up to before 'for thus.' 'This is one alone' — this is the proposition. 'Is it one because of being of one kind?' No, he says '<s>advaya</s>' (non-dual). Duality is differentiation; because of its absence, '<s>advaya</s>' — this is the meaning of the word 'one.'

body.text: śabdasyārthaḥ / ekamapi sambandhibhedābhdidyate / tadyathā pūrvākāśamaparākāśamiti / tadvadrūpatathatā vedanātathatā saṃjñātathatetyeṣa bhedo bhavatīti cedāha / advaidhīkāreti / ataśca advayatathatā / nityaṃ tathaiveti tathatā / advayā ca svayamabhedāttathatā ca paratopyabhedādityadvayatathatā / hetumāha / na kvacidityādinā / tatkhalu tasya bhavati yadyadādhāraṃ taddhetukaṃ vā / tadyathā kūpodakaṃ yavāṅkura iti / tathatā tu na kvacit nāpi kutaścit / tasmātkeṣucidapratibaddhatvānna sā kasyacit / yataḥ sā na kasyacittataḥ sādvayādvaidhīkārādvayatathatā / tato na kvacitpratihanyate / tasmādanujātaḥ subhūtistathāgatasyeti siddham /
body.translated_text: Even what is one is spoken of [as if different] due to the difference of its relata — just as 'eastern space' and 'western space.' 'Similarly, might there be differentiation such as the <s>tathatā</s> of form, the <s>tathatā</s> of feeling, the <s>tathatā</s> of perception?' — if so, he says '<s>advaidhīkāra</s>' (non-bifurcation). And therefore it is '<s>advaya-tathatā</s>' (non-dual suchness). 'Eternally just so' — therefore <s>tathatā</s>. It is non-dual (<s>advayā</s>) because of its own non-differentiation, and it is suchness (<s>tathatā</s>) because of non-differentiation from the other's perspective too — hence '<s>advaya-tathatā</s>.' He states the reason with 'not anywhere' and so forth. Indeed, that which has a support belongs to what has that as its cause — just as well-water [depends on the well] and a barley sprout [on the seed]. But <s>tathatā</s> is not anywhere nor from anything. Therefore, because of not being bound to any [particular things], it does not belong to anyone. Because it does not belong to anyone, therefore it is '<s>advaya-advaidhīkāra-advaya-tathatā</s>' (non-dual, non-bifurcated, non-dual suchness). Therefore it is not obstructed anywhere. Hence it is established that <s>Subhūti</s> is <s>anujāta</s> (born after) the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

body.text: hetvantaramāha / evaṃ hītyādinā / evaṃ hīti evamapi / tadevāha / akṛtatathatayeti / akṛtā cāsau nityatvāttathatā ca / na sā kadācinna tathateti nityaṃ tathaiva bhāvāt / tataḥ sādvayeti kālabhedenāsyābhedāt / tathāgatamiti karmaṇi dvitīyā /
body.translated_text: He states another reason with 'for thus' and so forth. 'For thus' means 'also in this way.' He states that very thing: 'by uncreated suchness' — it is uncreated because it is permanent, and it is suchness. It is never not suchness — because it is eternally just so in nature. Therefore it is non-dual (<s>advaya</s>) — because of its non-differentiation through temporal distinctions. '<s>Tathāgatam</s>' — the second case [accusative] is in the object sense.

body.text: hetvantaramāha yathetyādinā / sarvatreti sarvalokadhātuṣu / sarvadharmaṣviti sarvavastuṣu / avikalpā teṣāmavikalpanāt / nirvikalpā tathaiva sarvavikalpānāṃ prahāṇām / evameva ceti sarvatrāvikalpanirvikalpatayā / aluptamityacchinnam / evaṃ hītyādinopasaṃhāraḥ //
body.translated_text: He states another reason with 'just as' and so forth. 'Everywhere' means in all world-realms. 'In all <s>dharmas</s>' means in all things. It is '<s>avikalpā</s>' (non-conceptual) because of the non-conceptualization of those [things]. It is '<s>nirvikalpā</s>' (beyond conceptualization) similarly because of the abandonment of all conceptualizations. 'And just so' — because of being non-conceptual and beyond conceptualization everywhere. '<s>Aluptam</s>' means unbroken, uninterrupted. By 'for thus' and so forth, there is the conclusion. //

body.text: hetvantaramāha yathetyādinā nānyatreti nānyā bhedakatvānupalabdheḥ / dvitīyābhāvādananyā cāsau tathatā ceti ananyatathatā / tasyā anugamaḥ / tenopagatastathatāṃ saṃvṛtyā / paramārthamāha / na cetyādinā / atretyasminnupagame / na kaścitsubhūtiranyo vā / na kvaciditi tathāgate 'nyasmin vānugatimupagataḥ / dharmapubhdalanairātmyadarśanāditi bhāvaḥ / evaṃ hītyādinopasaṃhāraḥ /
body.translated_text: He states another reason with 'just as' and so forth. '<s>Nānyatra</s>' means 'not other' — because of the non-apprehension of anything that differentiates. Because of the absence of a second, it is non-other (<s>ananyā</s>), and it is suchness — hence '<s>ananya-tathatā</s>' (non-other suchness). Its following (<s>anugama</s>) — by that, one has approached suchness conventionally. He states the ultimate meaning with 'and not' and so forth. 'Here' means in this approach. No one — neither <s>Subhūti</s> nor anyone else — 'not anywhere' means [not] in the <s>Tathāgata</s> or in any other — has approached or attained the following. The sense is: because of seeing the selflessness of both <s>dharmas</s> and persons (<s>pudgala</s>). By 'for thus' and so forth, there is the conclusion.

body.text: hetvantaramāha yathetyādinā / evaṃ hītyādinopasaṃhāraḥ / ityajātasvabhāvaḥ //
body.translated_text: He states another reason with 'just as' and so forth. By 'for thus' and so forth, there is the conclusion. // This is the nature of being unborn. //

body.text: tathāgatatathatayāpītyādi iyaṃ setyataḥ prāk / atra sarvatathāprabhedānāmabhedaṃ darśayan bhedaṃ pratiṣedhatīti sarvāsāṃ rūpāditathatānāmanupalambhāttathatānupalalambhaḥ ṣoḍaśaḥ svabhāvaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'By the <s>tathatā</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s> too' and so forth, up to before 'this is that.' Here, by showing the non-differentiation of all the varieties of suchness, he negates differentiation. Because of the non-apprehension of all such <s>tathatās</s> — the <s>tathatā</s> of form and so forth — the non-apprehension of <s>tathatā</s> is the sixteenth essential nature. //

body.text: asyāstathatāyā māhātmyamāha / iyaṃ setyādinā / gamirjñānārthaḥ tathatāgatānena tasmāttathāgata iti bhāvaḥ /
body.translated_text: He states the greatness of this <s>tathatā</s> with 'this is that' and so forth. '<s>Gami</s>' has the meaning of knowledge; through <s>tathatā</s>, one has come (<s>āgata</s>) to that — therefore '<s>Tathāgata</s>' (thus-come). This is the meaning.

body.text: asyāṃ deśyamānāyāṃ yadabhdutamabhūttadāha / asyāmityādinā / ṣaḍavikāramaṣṭādaśamahānimittaṃ yathā bhavati tathā akampata yāvat saṃprāgarjat / atra trayo dhātavaścalanārthāḥ / trayaḥ śabdārthāḥ / mṛdumadhyādhimātrakriyābhedādaṣṭādaśamahānimittāni
body.translated_text: When this [<s>tathatā</s>] was being taught, what was wondrous — that he states with 'in this' and so forth. The six transformations and eighteen great signs occur as follows: the earth quaked and so on, up to thundered. Here, three [relate to] the meaning of movement, and three to the meaning of sound. Due to the distinction of mild, medium, and intense activity, there are eighteen great signs.

body.text: bhavanti / tatra calanamaṅgataḥ / kampanaṃ sākalyena / sākalyenātyantaṃ kampanaṃ kṣobhaḥ / vedhaḥ śabdaḥ / raṇitaṃ daṇḍāhatakāṃsīvat / garjanaṃ navamahāmeghavat / ṣaḍvikārāstadyathā- "pṛthivyāḥ pūrvā digunnamati paścimāvanamati / paścimā digunnamati pūrvāvanamati / uttarāvanamati uttarā digunnamati / dakṣiṇāvanamati / madhye unnamati / ante 'vanamati / ante unnamati madhye 'vanamati" iti / kiṃvadityāha / tathāgatasya cetyādi / evaṃ hīti / tathāgatābhisambodhāvivasubhūtestathatānirdeśe mahānimittaprādurbhāvasamatayā /
body.translated_text: Among those, '<s>calana</s>' (trembling) is partial movement. '<s>Kampana</s>' (shaking) is movement in its entirety. Intense shaking throughout is '<s>kṣobha</s>' (quaking). '<s>Vedha</s>' is sound. '<s>Raṇita</s>' (resounding) is like a bell struck with a stick. '<s>Garjana</s>' (thundering) is like a new great cloud. The six transformations are as follows: 'The eastern side of the earth rises while the western side sinks; the western side rises while the eastern sinks; the northern side sinks while the northern side rises; the southern side sinks; the middle rises while the periphery sinks; the periphery rises while the middle sinks.' 'Like what?' — he says: 'And of the <s>Tathāgata</s>' and so forth. 'For thus' — by the equality of the manifestation of the great signs at the teaching of <s>tathatā</s> by <s>Subhūte</s>, just as at the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>abhisaṃbodhi</s> (perfect awakening).

body.text: prakārāntaramapyāha / punaraparamityādinā jāyerannityetatparyantena / na saṃvidyanta iti pratijñā / nopalabhyanta iti hetuḥ / yairiti svadharmaiḥ / anujāyeteti kartari liṅ / ye ceti tāthāgatā dharmāḥ / anujāyeranniti karmaṇi liṅ / evaṃ hītyupasaṃhāraḥ / tathatā kathaṃ caryā? tanmātre 'vasthānāt / asmin khalu punarityādi sugamam /
body.translated_text: He also states another mode with 'moreover' and so forth, up to the end of 'would be born.' 'They are not found' — this is the proposition. 'They are not apprehended' — this is the reason. 'By which' means by their own <s>dharmas</s> (characteristics). '<s>Anujāyeta</s>' — the optative is in the agent sense. 'And those which' are those <s>dharmas</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. '<s>Anujāyeran</s>' — the optative is in the object sense. By 'for thus' there is the conclusion. How is <s>tathatā</s> to be practiced? By abiding in just that alone. 'In this indeed moreover' and so forth — easily understood.

body.text: kiñcāpīti yadyapi trayastriṃśata ityapādāne tasiḥ / jātyā pakṣiṇaḥ mahākāyatvācchakuneḥ / antarā cittasyeti dyāvāpṛthivyormadhyasaṃjñinaḥ / evaṃ bhavatīti eṣa vitarko bhavati / śeṣaṃ subodhaṃ virahito bhavatīti yāvat ! iha jñānaviśeṣakāritrasvabhāvalakṣaṇe ukte /
body.translated_text: 'Although' (<s>kiñcāpi</s>) means 'even though.' '<s>Trayastriṃśataḥ</s>' — the <s>tasi</s> suffix is in the ablative sense. 'By nature a bird' — because of the great size of the bird (<s>śakuni</s>). '<s>Antarā cittasya</s>' (midway, of the mind) refers to one dwelling in the space between heaven and earth. 'Thus it is' means this doubt arises. The rest is easily understood — up to 'he becomes free from.' Here, the characteristics of the nature of special knowledge and its function have been stated.

body.text: bodhisattvānāṃ mokṣabhāgīyaṃ vaktavyam / tacca tadvirahiṇāṃ bodhisattvānāmarhattvaprāptikāraṇanirdeśena sūcitaṃ vyaktikartuṃ śāriputra āha / yathāhaṃ bhagavannityādi / prajñāpāramitā bhāvayitavyeti sarvadharmaparamārthajñānāya / caryamāṇasya ca dānapāramitāderanimittīkaraṇārtham / upāyakuśalenetyupāye kuśalena / tatropāyaḥ sarvākārajñatācittasya nityamatyāgaḥ / sarvapuṇyānāṃ ca bodhau samyakpariṇāmanā / samyakpariṇāmanānumodane ca tatparivartokte ataḥ śāstroktalakṣaṇamuktaṃ bhavati /
body.translated_text: The liberation-portion (<s>mokṣabhāgīya</s>) of <s>bodhisattvas</s> must be stated. And that, for <s>bodhisattvas</s> who lack it, is indicated through the teaching of the cause for attaining <s>arhatship</s>. To make this explicit, <s>Śāriputra</s> says 'As I, O <s>Bhagavān</s>' and so forth. '<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be cultivated' — for the sake of the ultimate knowledge of all <s>dharmas</s>. And for the purpose of making the practice of <s>dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of generosity) and the rest signless. 'With skillful means' (<s>upāyakuśalena</s>) means one who is skilled in means. Therein, the means is the constant non-abandonment of the mind directed toward <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects). And the proper dedication of all merit toward <s>bodhi</s> (awakening). Proper dedication and rejoicing — these are stated in that chapter. Therefore, the characteristic stated in the treatise has been declared.

children.translated_text: Skill in the accomplishment of signless giving and the rest —
In [the context of] this complete understanding of all aspects, this is considered the liberation-portion (<s>mokṣabhāgīya</s>). // 4-32 //

body.text: tesya pañcaprabhedā mahatyorbhagavatyoḥ / tathā ca śāstram-
body.translated_text: Its fivefold division is [found] in the two great [texts] of the <s>Bhagavatī</s>. And thus the treatise [states] —

children.translated_text: Faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) has the <s>Buddha</s> and so forth as its object; vigor (<s>vīrya</s>) has giving and the like as its domain;
mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>) is the accomplishment of intention; <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) is freedom from conceptualization. // 4-33 //

body.text: dharmeṣu sarvairākāraiḥ jñānaṃ prajñeti pañcadhā /
body.translated_text: Knowledge of all phenomena in all their aspects is <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) — thus [the five faculties are explained] in fivefold manner.

body.text: etadeva bhagavānāha / evamukta ityādinā / atha śāstram-
body.translated_text: This very [point] the <s>Bhagavān</s> states, with 'Thus spoken' and so forth. Now the treatise:

body.text: tīkṣṇaiḥ subodhā sambodhirdurbodhā mṛdubhirmatā // 4-34 //
body.translated_text: With sharp [faculties], <s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (perfect awakening) is easily awakened; with dull [faculties], it is considered difficult to awaken. // 4-34 //

body.text: etadeva atha khalvityādinā prastuvanti / kṛcchreṇa sambhavo 'syā iti durabhisambhavā / etaddevairaviśeṣeṇoktam / atha khalvityādinā bhagavān pudgalaviśeṣeṇāha / duṣprajñairityādi / duṣpra jñādipadaiḥ sūcito viśeṣo mṛdūni mokṣabhāgīyāni / tīkṣṇaistu mokṣabhāgīyaiḥ svabhisambhavā samyaksambodhiḥ / atastāni darśayitukāmaḥ subhūtirāha / yabhdagavānityādi / evamukta ityādinā bhagavata uttaram / sarvadharmāṇāmasattayā bodheḥ svabhisambhavatvamuktaṃ subhūtinā tadayuktam / yato yadyetāvata svabhisambhavā syāttadā sarvasattvānāmādita eva tathā syāt / tasmātpratipattitaḥ prāptiḥ / sā ca na teṣāmasti yeṣāṃ mṛdūni mokṣabhāgīyāni / ato 'sambhavatvādaprāpterdurabhisambhaveti brūmaḥ / nanvabhijñāste śrutacintādibalena samyaksambodhau tatteṣāṃ kuto 'prāptirityata āha / asadbhūtatvādadurabhisambhaveti / te hi bālagrāhyamevārtha bodhiṃ manyante / sa cāsadbhūtatvādalīkatvānna prāpyata iti bhāvaḥ / tathā hi / vikalpaṃ vā bodhi manyeran / vikalpanirmitaṃ vārtham / pakṣadvayamapyayuktam / avikalpatvādvikalpāviṭhapitatvācca bodheḥ / etaddarśayitumāha / avikalpatvādityādi /
body.translated_text: This very [point] they introduce with 'Now then' and so forth. 'Because its arising is difficult' means 'hard to fully awaken to.' This is stated by the gods without distinction. With 'Now then' and so forth, the <s>Bhagavān</s> states [the matter] with reference to specific persons. 'Those of poor wisdom' and so forth — the distinction indicated by the words 'poor wisdom' and the like refers to dull faculties conducive to liberation (<s>mokṣabhāgīya</s>). But with sharp faculties conducive to liberation, <s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s> is easily fully awakened to. Therefore, wishing to show those [faculties], <s>Subhūti</s> says 'O <s>Bhagavān</s>' and so forth. With 'Thus spoken' and so forth is the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s reply. By the non-existence of all <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Subhūti</s> has stated that awakening is easily attainable — but that is not correct. Because if it were easily attainable merely by that [non-existence], then for all beings it would be so from the very beginning. Therefore, attainment is through practice. And that [practice] does not exist for those whose faculties conducive to liberation are dull. Therefore, we say it is 'hard to fully awaken to' because of the impossibility [of practice] and the non-attainment. Now, if they recognize [the truth] through the power of hearing, reflection, and the like regarding <s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s>, then how can there be non-attainment for them? — to this he says: 'Because of its non-real nature, it is not hard to fully awaken to.' For they consider as awakening only what is grasped by the childish. And that, because of its non-real nature — its falsity — is not attained: this is the purport. Moreover, they might consider awakening to be conceptualization; or they might consider the object to be produced by conceptualization. Both positions are untenable — because awakening is non-conceptual and not established by conceptualization. To show this, he says 'Because of non-conceptuality' and so forth.

body.text: atha khalvityādinā sthaviraśāriputrasyottaram / sa hi manyate śūnyatvātsvabhisambhavetyayaṃ viruddho heturiti / evaṃ ceti / ākāśasamatayā ca / ākāśasamā hīti hetuḥ / yattatvaṃ yeṣāṃ tenaiva teṣāmabhisambodhāditi bhāvaḥ / evaṃ viruddhatvamuktvā anumāne bādhāṃ vivakṣuḥ prasaṅgaṃ karoti yadi cetyādinā / na tveveti naiva / yasmādityādinā viparyayamāha / athavā parasya hetau dūṣite svapakṣasādhanamevedam / evamukta ityādinā vistareṇa subhūtiḥ prasaṅgaṃ vighaṭayati / vivartituḥ samboddhuḥ samboddhavyasya ca vikalpane / katamaḥ sa dharmo yo vivartata ityuktvā avivartanameva sādhayitumāha yastasyāmevetyādi / sarvadharmāsthānayogeneti / sarvadharmaṣvasthānameva yogo nyāyaḥ / tena dharmatāyāṃ sthitaḥ / dharmataiva śuddhā bodhiḥ / sā ca prakṛtyaiva śuddheti bhāvaḥ / evamukta ityādi śāriputrasya vacanam / dharmanayajātiḥ dharmāṇāṃ tattvaprakāraḥ / ye cetyādinā viśeṣamāha / ca śabdastuśabdasyārthe / atha khalvityādinā pūrṇaḥ subhūtiṃ smārayati / śeṣaṃ subodhamāsiddhāntasthāpanāgraṃthāt anuttarayā bodhyāniryāsyatyayaṃ bodhisattvo mahāsattva ityasmāt / ata iyatā vistareṇa
body.translated_text: With 'Now then' and so forth is the reply of the Elder <s>Śāriputra</s>. For he holds that 'because of emptiness, it is easily fully awakened to' — this is a contradictory reason. 'And thus' — and by equality with space. 'For they are equal to space' is the reason. The meaning is: because they are fully awakened to by that very nature which is theirs. Having stated the contradiction thus, wishing to express the defeat (<s>bādhā</s>) in the inference, he constructs a <s>prasaṅga</s> (reductio) with 'If' and so forth. 'But not at all' means 'certainly not.' With 'Because' and so forth, he states the converse. Or, when the opponent's reason has been refuted, this is simply the establishment of one's own position. With 'Thus spoken' and so forth, <s>Subhūti</s> dissolves the <s>prasaṅga</s> in detail. Regarding the conceptualization of the one who turns [toward awakening], the one who fully awakens, and that which is to be fully awakened to — having said 'Which is that <s>dharma</s> that turns?', he proceeds to establish non-turning itself with 'That which in that very' and so forth. 'By the method of the non-abiding of all <s>dharmas</s>' means: the very non-abiding in all <s>dharmas</s> is the proper method; by that, [one is] established in <s>dharmatā</s> (the true nature of phenomena). <s>Dharmatā</s> itself is pure awakening. And that is pure by its very nature — this is the purport. With 'Thus spoken' and so forth are the words of <s>Śāriputra</s>. '<s>Dharmanayanajāti</s>' means the mode of the true nature of <s>dharmas</s>. With 'Those who' and so forth, he states the distinction. The word 'ca' has the meaning of 'tu' (but). With 'Now then' and so forth, <s>Pūrṇa</s> reminds <s>Subhūti</s>. The rest is easily understood up to the passage establishing the doctrine, from 'This <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> will emerge through unsurpassed awakening.' Therefore, with this extent of elaboration,

body.text: samanvitam / tīkṣṇairmokṣabhāgīyaiḥ svabhisambhavā samyaksambodhiriti / uktāni mokṣabhāgīyāni //
body.translated_text: endowed [with the above]. With sharp faculties conducive to liberation, <s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s> is easily fully awakened to — the faculties conducive to liberation have been stated.

body.text: mokṣasya bhāgo bhajanaṃ prāptiḥ tasmai hitāni mokṣabhāgīyāni tadapyuktāni / nirvedhabhāgīyāni vaktavyāni / nirvedhaḥ prativedho darśanamārgaḥ / tasya bhāgaḥ prāptiḥ / tasmai hitāni nirvedhabhāgīyāni / tāni catvāri / ūṣmamūrdhākṣāntiragradharmāśceti / tatrādyamadhikṛtya śāstram-
body.translated_text: Liberation's portion — the attainment of <s>mokṣa</s> — [those qualities] that are beneficial for that are called <s>mokṣabhāgīya</s> (conducive to liberation); those too have been stated. The <s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s> (faculties conducive to penetration) are to be stated. <s>Nirvedha</s> means penetration — the path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>). Its portion is attainment. Those beneficial for that are <s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>. They are four: <s>ūṣman</s> (heat), <s>mūrdhan</s> (summit), <s>kṣānti</s> (forbearance), and <s>agradharma</s> (supreme dharma). Regarding the first of these, the treatise:

children.translated_text: The object of the <s>ūṣman</s> (heat) [stage] is here declared to be all sentient beings;
the aspect is equal-mindedness and the like — stated as tenfold with respect to those very [beings]. // 4-35 //

body.text: ata āha / atha khalvityādi yāvadahaṃ nātha iti / sthātavyamiti spṛhaṇataḥ / śikṣitavyamabhyāsataḥ / samaṃ sthātavyamityādinā daśacittānyuktani / samacittaṃ maitracittaṃ niḥśāṭhyacittaṃ nihatamānacittaṃ mātāpitrādicittaṃ putraduhitādicittaṃ ceti / nāthaḥ sānāthyaṃ kartum / ūṣmagatam //
body.translated_text: Therefore he says 'Now then' and so forth, up to 'I, O Lord.' 'One should abide' — with aspiration. 'One should train' — with practice. With 'One should abide equally' and so forth, the ten [types of] mind are stated: equal mind, loving mind (<s>maitra</s>), mind free from deceit, mind with pride destroyed, mind like [that toward] mother and father, mind like [that toward] son and daughter, and so forth. 'Lord' means one who provides protection. [This constitutes] the <s>ūṣmagata</s> (heat stage).

children.translated_text: For one who has himself turned away from evil and is established in giving and the like,
the exhorting of others to those [virtues], and speaking in praise [of them] — [this constitutes] conformity. // 4-36 //

body.text: mūrdhagaṃ
body.translated_text: [This is] the <s>mūrdhagata</s> (summit stage).

body.text: etadāha svayaṃ cetyādinā / pāpāni daśakuśalāni / pāpebhyo nivṛttau viratau / parijayo 'bhyāsaḥ / avidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārāḥ saṃskārapratyayaṃ vijñānamityādiranulomaḥ pratītyasamutpādaḥ / avidyānirodhāt saṃskāranirodha ityādiḥ pratilomaḥ / anyeṣāmiti pareṣāṃ samādāpakaḥ samyaggrāhakaḥ / varṇavādī guṇavādī samanujño 'nukūla iti mūrdhagatam //
body.translated_text: This he states with 'Oneself' and so forth. 'Evils' are the ten unwholesome [actions]. 'Turned away from evils' means abstention, refraining. '<s>Paricaya</s>' means practice. 'Formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>) conditioned by ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>); consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) conditioned by formations' — and so forth is the forward [order of] dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>). 'From the cessation of ignorance, the cessation of formations' — and so forth is the reverse [order]. 'Of others' means one who properly causes others to take up [these practices]; one who speaks of virtues, one who approves, one who conforms — [this is] the <s>mūrdhagata</s> (summit stage).

children.translated_text: Knowledge of truth for oneself and others is considered <s>kṣānti</s> (forbearance);
likewise the <s>agradharmas</s> (supreme dharmas) should be known through the ripening of beings and the like. // 4-37 //

body.text: svayaṃ sa satyānāṃ jñānaṃ pareṣāṃ ca tasmin samādāpanaṃ 'varṇavādānukūlatā' iti ca kṣāntigatam / svayaṃ ca sattvānāṃ paripācanabuddhakṣetrapariśodhanādi pareṣāṃ ca tatsamādāpanaṃ varṇavādānukūla[te]ti cāgradharmagatam / etadubhayamāha / evaṃ satyeṣvityādinā / satyeṣviti duḥkhādisatyaviṣayeṣu yathākramaṃ parijñānaprahāṇasākṣātkriyābhāvanāsu strotaāpattyādipañcaphalajñānasākṣātkriyāyāṃ yāvadbodhisattvanyāmāvakrāntau / tathā sattvaparimācanādau ca sthitvā
body.translated_text: For oneself, knowledge of the truths, and for others, causing them to take up that [knowledge], and 'speaking in praise and conformity' — this constitutes the <s>kṣāntigata</s> (forbearance stage). For oneself, the ripening of beings, the purification of buddha-fields, and the like, and for others, causing them to take up those, and speaking in praise and conformity — this constitutes the <s>agradharmaqata</s> (supreme dharma stage). He states both of these with 'Thus regarding the truths' and so forth. 'Regarding the truths' means regarding the objects of the truths of suffering and the like — in order: full knowledge, abandonment, direct realization, and cultivation; in the direct realization of the five fruits beginning with stream-entry (<s>srotaāpatti</s>), up to the entry into the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-certainty (<s>nyāma</s>). And having abided in the ripening of beings and the like,

body.text: anyeṣāmapi tatra samādāpane tadvarṇavādinā tatsamanujñena bhavitavyamiti kṣāntigatāgradharmagate //
body.translated_text: one should also cause others to take up those [practices], speaking in praise of them and approving — [this is] the <s>kṣāntigata</s> and <s>agradharmaqata</s> [stages].

body.text: tasyaivamityādinā nirvedhabhāgīyānāṃ phalamāha / anāvaraṇaṃ rūpaṃ vedanā saṃjñā yāvat saddharmasthitiranāvaraṇā bhaviṣyatīti //
body.translated_text: With 'For him, thus' and so forth, he states the fruit of the <s>nirvedhabhāgīyas</s> (faculties conducive to penetration). 'Unobstructed' — form, feeling, perception, up to 'the abiding of the true <s>Dharma</s> will be unobstructed.'

body.text: tathatāpradhānaḥ parivartastathatāparivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: The chapter predominantly about <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) is the <s>Tathatā-parivarta</s> (Chapter on Suchness).

body.text: āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ sāratarā(mā)nāmni pañjikāyāṃ ratnākaraśāntiviracitāyāṃ ṣoḍaśaḥ parivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: In the commentary (<s>pañjikā</s>) called <s>Sāratamā</s>, composed by <s>Ratnākaraśānti</s>, on the noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s> — [this is] the sixteenth chapter.

body.text: 17. avinirvatanīyākāraliṅganimittaparivarto nāma saptadaśaḥ /
body.translated_text: 17. The seventeenth [chapter] is called the Chapter on the Marks, Signs, and Characteristics of Non-retrogression (<s>avinirvatanīyākāraliṅganimitta-parivarta</s>).

body.text: 'mokṣanirvedhabhāgīye śaikṣo 'vaivartiko gaṇaḥ / ' iti pūrvamuddiṣṭam / tatra dve ukte / tṛtīyo vaktavyaḥ / ataḥ śāstram-
body.translated_text: 'The <s>mokṣa</s>- and <s>nirvedha-bhāgīya</s> [faculties], the learner (<s>śaikṣa</s>), the non-retrogressing assembly' — this was previously indicated. Of these, two have been stated. The third is to be stated. Therefore the treatise:

children.translated_text: Those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who abide in the paths of seeing (<s>darśana</s>) and cultivation (<s>abhyāsa</s>),
having taken up the factors of penetration — that is the non-retrogressing assembly (<s>avaivartikagaṇa</s>) here. // 4-38 //

body.text: 'atra' iti mahāyāne / 'avaivartikagaṇaḥ' / tallakṣaṇam / vivartāya prabhavati vaivartikaḥ / na tathetyavaivarktiko 'vinivartanīyaḥ / athāsya nirvedhabhāgīyeṣu sthitasya kati liṅgānītyata āha /
body.translated_text: 'Here' means in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. 'Non-retrogressing assembly' — its definition: one who is capable of turning [back] is <s>vaivartika</s> (retrogressing); one who is not so is <s>avaivartika</s> — non-retrogressing (<s>avinivartanīya</s>). Now, how many marks does one established in the <s>nirvedhabhāgīyas</s> have? Therefore he says:

children.translated_text: The marks of non-retrogression for one established in the factors of penetration
are stated as twenty, beginning with turning away from form and the like. // 4-39 //

body.text: avaivartikatvaparijñānamityarthaḥ / atha katame rūpādinivṛttyādayaḥ?
body.translated_text: The meaning is: the ascertainment of non-retrogression. Now, what are 'turning away from form and the like'?

children.translated_text: Turning away from form and the like, the destruction of doubt and [bad] destinies,
for oneself, when established in wholesome [states]; and the exhorting of others to those [states]. // 4-40 //
And giving and the like based on others; non-craving even for profound objects;
loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>); non-association with body and the like; and the fivefold obscuration (<s>āvaraṇa</s>) — // 4-41 //
the abandonment of all latent tendencies (<s>anuśaya</s>); mindfulness and clear comprehension; purity
regarding robes and the like, and the non-arising of worms in the body. // 4-42 //
Non-crookedness of mind; acceptance of <s>dhūta</s> (ascetic) [practices]; absence of envy and the like;
proceeding in conformity with <s>dharmatā</s> (the true nature); desiring hell for the sake of [all] beings. // 4-43 //
Not being led astray by others; [recognizing] <s>Māra</s> who teaches another path
as <s>Māra</s>; and conduct approved by the <s>Buddhas</s>. // 4-44 //
One who is established in the <s>ūṣman</s> (heat), <s>mūrdhan</s> (summit), <s>kṣānti</s> (forbearance), and <s>agradharma</s> (supreme dharma) [stages],
with these twenty marks, does not turn back from awakening (<s>saṃbodhi</s>). // 4-45 //

body.text: ata āha / atha khalvityādi / ākriyante vyajyanta ebhiriti ākārāḥ / liṅgyante gamyanta ebhiriti liṅgāni / nimīyante nirūpyanta ebhiriti nimittāni / ekārthatvepi trayāṇāmupādāna(naṃ) sattvāntaraśaṅkāyā vyavacchedārtham / paryāyaskandhaṃ (vacanaṃ) athavā aparaḥ paryāyaḥ / kathamityādi / ata eva vāśabdaḥ / kathaṃ ve ti kena prakāreṇa jānīyāma iti sambandhaḥ /
body.translated_text: Therefore he says 'Now then' and so forth. '<s>Ākāras</s>' (aspects) are those by which [things] are made manifest. '<s>Liṅgas</s>' (marks) are those by which [things] are known. '<s>Nimittas</s>' (signs) are those by which [things] are ascertained. Although the three are synonymous, [all three are] employed for the purpose of excluding the doubts of other beings — or as a statement using synonyms. Or [it is] another synonym. 'How' and so forth — the word 'or' is used for this very [purpose]. 'How?' means 'by what manner would we know?' — this is the connection.

body.text: atibahūni liṅgāni tatrādyaṃ tāvadāha yā cetyādinā / caturdhā bhūmiḥ / pṛthagjanaśrāvakapratyekabuddhabuddhasambandhāt / iyaṃ caturvidhāpi tathatābhūmirityucyate / kuta ityāha / sarvāśca ityādi / caśabdo hetau / yasmātsarvā etāstathatayādvayāḥ / rūpādīnāṃ sarvadharmāṇāṃ yathālakṣaṇamasattvāt tathataivaitāḥ / tathatā caikaiva na dve na bahavyaḥ / tasmāttathatayādvayā abhinnāḥ advaidhīkārādacchinnāḥ vikalpasvabhāvavirahāt avikalpāḥ / vikalpāgocaratvāt nirvikralpāḥ / itīti / evaṃ lakṣaṇā yā tathatā tāṃ tathatāṃ dharmatāmavatarati / kathamavataratītyāha tathatāyāmityādi / sthitastanmātradarśanāt / na kalpayati samyak na vikalpayati vitatham / evamavataratītyevaṃ satyavatarati / ..........tyāha / evamavatīrṇa ityādi / uktena krameṇāvatīrṇaḥ san / yatheti yayā mātrayā śrutvāpīti śravaṇānantaramapi / tatopi vātikramyeti tata uttarakālamapi / na kāṅkṣatīti na bādhate / naivamitīti sambandhaḥ / vividhā matiḥ vimatiḥ / tanna karoti evaṃ vā na veti / ata evāha na vicikitsatoti / na dhandhāyatītyapratipatteḥ pratiṣedhaḥ / kiṃ tarhi karotītyāha / api tvityādi / tathataiva sarvaṃ na santi rūpādaya ityadhimuñcati śraddhayā / avagāhate prajñayā / etadeva jñānaṃ mukhyaṃ liṅgam / asya paricchedamāha / na cetyādinā /
body.translated_text: There are very many marks; therefore he states the first with 'That which' and so forth. The ground (<s>bhūmi</s>) is fourfold — in connection with ordinary persons, <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>Buddhas</s>. This fourfold [ground] is also called the <s>tathatā-bhūmi</s> (ground of suchness). Why? He says with 'And all' and so forth. The word 'ca' is in the sense of a reason: because all these are non-dual through <s>tathatā</s> (suchness). Because of the non-existence according to their [own] characteristics of all <s>dharmas</s> such as form and the like, these are nothing but <s>tathatā</s>. And <s>tathatā</s> is only one — not two, not many. Therefore, 'non-dual through <s>tathatā</s>' means undivided; 'undifferentiated' means uncut; 'non-conceptual' means free from the nature of conceptualization; 'beyond conceptualization' means not within the range of conceptualization. Thus — the <s>tathatā</s> that has such characteristics, that <s>tathatā</s>, that <s>dharmatā</s> — one 'enters' into it. How does one enter? He says with 'In <s>tathatā</s>' and so forth. Established [in it] from seeing only that [suchness]. One does not construct [anything] correctly, nor does one misconceive [anything] falsely. Thus one enters — and having entered in this way... he says with 'Having thus entered' and so forth. Having entered in the stated manner. 'In whatever degree' — even after hearing. 'Even passing beyond that' — even in the time afterward. 'Does not crave' means [suchness] does not obstruct [him]. 'Not thus' is the connection — <s>vimati</s> is varied opinion: 'It is thus or not thus' — that he does not produce. Therefore he says 'Does not doubt.' 'Does not hesitate' — this is the negation of non-comprehension. What then does he do? He says with 'But rather' and so forth. He resolves with faith that '<s>tathatā</s> alone is everything — forms and the like do not exist.' He penetrates with wisdom. This very knowledge is the primary mark. He states its delimitation with 'Not' and so forth.

body.text: paricchedāpekṣayā bahuvacanaṃ ebhirliṅgairiti / tathataiva sarvamiti jñānāt 'rūpādibhyo nivṛttiḥ' nirvedhāṅgeṣvavaivartikaliṅgaṃ prathamam //
body.translated_text: The plural 'by these marks' is in consideration of the delimitation. From the knowledge that '<s>tathatā</s> alone is everything,' 'turning away from form and the like' is the first mark of non-retrogression in the [stages of] factors conducive to penetration.

body.text: punaraparamityādi / anyeṣāmiti / ito dharmādvāhyānām / śramaṇānāmiti pravrajitānām / mukhamullokayati praṇataḥ paśyati / kimitītyāha / ime ityādi / jānanti laukikena jñānena / paśyanti lokottareṇa / dātavyamiti bhaktito deyam / vyapāśrayata iti sevate śaraṇaṃ vā gacchati / satyeṣu ratneṣu ca vimatirvicikitsā / tasyāḥ kṣaye sati sarvametanna karotīti 'vikitsākṣayo ' dvitīyaṃ teṣu talliṅgam //
body.translated_text: With 'Furthermore' and so forth. 'Of others' means those outside this <s>Dharma</s>. 'Of <s>śramaṇas</s>' means of renunciants. 'Looks at the face' means sees with deference. Why? He says with 'These' and so forth. 'They know' — with worldly knowledge. 'They see' — with supramundane [knowledge]. 'Should be given to' means should be offered out of devotion. 'Takes refuge in' means serves or goes for refuge. Doubt (<s>vimati</s>) regarding the truths and the [Three] Jewels — upon its destruction, one does not do all this. Thus 'the destruction of doubt' is the second mark among those [marks of non-retrogression].

body.text: sa khalvityādi / apāyā narakapretatiryañcaḥ / svībhāvaḥ strītvam / sa cāvaśiṣṭānāmakṣaṇānāmupalakṣaṇamiti 'akṣaṇakṣayaḥ' tṛtīyaṃ teṣu talliṅgam //
body.translated_text: Beginning with 'That one indeed' and so on. '<s>Apāyas</s>' (evil destinies) are the hells, hungry ghosts, and animals. '<s>Svībhāva</s>' (one's own nature) is being female. And that is an indication of the remaining inopportune states — thus 'the exhaustion of inopportune states' (<s>akṣaṇakṣaya</s>) is the third sign among those.

body.text: punaraparamityādi / daśasu kuśaleṣu svayaṃ sthitvā 'pareṣāṃ' teṣu 'samādāpanaṃ' dṛḍhīkaraṇaṃ ceti caturthaṃ teṣu talliṅgam //
body.translated_text: Beginning with 'Moreover' and so on. Having oneself abided in the ten wholesome [courses of action], 'the establishment of others' (<s>samādāpana</s>) in them, and their confirmation — this is the fourth sign among those.

body.text: punaraparamityādi / yaṃ yaṃ dharmamiti sūtrageyādikam / dadāti ca parasmai hitāya sukhāya caṣa bhavatviti teṣāmeva hitasukhāya / iti anenākāreṇa sādhāraṇaṃ karoti / yathā ca dharmadānaṃ tathānyadapi dānaśīlādikamiti 'parādhāraṃ dānādi' pañcamaṃ teṣu talliṅgam //
body.translated_text: Beginning with 'Moreover' and so on. 'Whatever <s>dharma</s>' means the <s>sūtra</s>, <s>geya</s>, and the like. 'He gives for the benefit and happiness of others' — 'may it be so for them' means for the benefit and happiness of those very [beings]. 'Thus by this manner he makes it common.' And just as the gift of <s>Dharma</s>, so too other [practices such as] generosity, morality, and the rest — thus 'sustaining others through generosity and the like' (<s>parādhāra dānādi</s>) is the fifth sign among those.

body.text: punaraparamityādinā na dhandhāyatītyetadantena 'gambhīre 'rthepyakāṅkṣaṇaṃ' ṣaṣṭhaṃ teṣveva talliṅgam //
body.translated_text: By the passage beginning with 'Moreover' and so on, up to the end of 'does not hesitate' — 'non-doubt regarding the profound meaning' (<s>gambhīre 'rthepy akāṅkṣaṇa</s>) is the sixth sign among those very [signs].

body.text: 'maitraṃ kāyādi' iti kāyādi karma / tadāha hitavacanaścetyādinā / upalakṣaṇatvāditi 'maitraṃ kāyādi' saptamaṃ teṣu talliṅgam //
body.translated_text: 'Friendly bodily [action] and the rest' — bodily and other actions. This he states beginning with 'speaking beneficial words' and so on. Because it is an indication [of other things as well] — thus 'friendly bodily [action] and the rest' is the seventh sign among those.

body.text: 'asaṃvāsaḥ pañcadhāvaraṇena vā' iti / pañca nivaraṇāni / kāmacchando vyāpādastyānamiddhamauddhatyakaukṛtyaṃ vicikitsā ceti / ebhirasaṃvāso 'samanvāgamaḥ / tamāha / alpastyānamiddhaśca bhavatītyupalakṣaṇatvāt / iti pañcabhirnivaraṇaisaṃvāso 'ṣṭamaṃ teṣu talliṅgam //
body.translated_text: 'Non-association with the fivefold obstruction' — the five hindrances are: sensual desire (<s>kāmacchanda</s>), malice (<s>vyāpāda</s>), torpor and drowsiness (<s>styānamiddha</s>), restlessness and remorse (<s>auddhatyakaukṛtya</s>), and doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>). Non-association with these is non-possession. This he states: 'He has little torpor and drowsiness' — because it is an indication [of the others]. Thus non-association with the five hindrances is the eighth sign among those.

body.text: sarva yathā bhavati tathānuśayasya dveṣānubandhasya hānaṃ 'sarvānuśayahāanam' / tadāha niranuśayaśca bhavatīti / navamaṃ teṣu talliṅgam //
body.translated_text: 'Every manner of the elimination of the <s>anuśaya</s> (latent tendency) connected with hatred' is 'the elimination of all <s>anuśayas</s>.' This he states: 'And he is free from <s>anuśayas</s>.' [This is] the ninth sign among those.

body.text: 'smṛtisaṃprajñatā' itismṛtisahitaṃ saṃprajanyam / tadāha sobhikrāmanvetyādinā / abhikramo gamanam / apratikrama āgamanam / bhrāntaṃ vikṣiptam / na vilambitamiti vilambe vikṣepāt / sahaseti asamīkṣya bhūmim / upalakṣaṇaṃ caitaccaṃkramasthānaniṣadyāśayaneṣu vikṣepasyeti smṛtisaṃprajanyaṃ daśamaṃ teṣu talliṅgam //
body.translated_text: 'Mindfulness and clear comprehension' (<s>smṛtisaṃprajñatā</s>) is clear comprehension accompanied by mindfulness. This he states beginning with 'He walks with awareness' and so on. '<s>Abhikrama</s>' is going forward. '<s>Apratikrama</s>' is coming back. '<s>Bhrānta</s>' is distracted. 'Not delayed' — because delay involves distraction. '<s>Sahasa</s>' means without examining the ground. And this is an indication [extending to] distraction in walking, standing, sitting, and lying down — thus mindfulness and clear comprehension is the tenth sign among those.

body.text: tasya khalvityādi yānītyataḥ prāk / yūkāyogād yūkilaḥ / picchāditvādilac / caukṣaḥ śuciḥ / ābādhaḥ pīḍā / ādīnava upadrava iti 'śucicīvarāditā' ekādaśaṃ teṣu talliṅgam //
body.translated_text: Beginning with 'Of that one indeed' and so on, up to before 'which.' '<s>Yūkā</s>' (lice) — because of the connection with lice, '<s>yūkila</s>' (lousy). The suffix '<s>lac</s>' is because of belonging to the <s>picchādi</s> group. '<s>Caukṣa</s>' means clean. '<s>Ābādha</s>' is affliction. '<s>Ādīnava</s>' is harm — thus 'cleanliness of robes and the like' is the eleventh sign among those.

body.text: yānītyādi subhūtirāhetyataḥ prāk / sambhavanti jāyante kāyasya bhakṣaṇāya / abhyudgatānīti prativiśiṣṭāni / iti 'śarīre kri(kṛ)mīṇāmasamubhdavo ' dvādaśaṃ teṣu talliṅgam //
body.translated_text: Beginning with 'Which' and so on, up to before '<s>Subhūti</s> said.' 'They arise, they are born, for the consumption of the body.' '<s>Abhyudgatāni</s>' means especially distinguished. Thus 'the non-arising of worms in the body' is the twelfth sign among those.

body.text: subhūtirāhetyādi punaraparāt prāk / cittālpakṛtyatā alpatvādavikṣepācca / cittasya kauṭilyaṃ kuṭilatā / yattu svadoṣapracchādanopāyastacchāṭhyam yatparavañcanāya sa vaṅkaḥ / paravañcanārthamabhūtasvaguṇasaṃdarśanaṃ māyā / ebhirvirahādyathākramaṃ cittākauṭilyaṃ cittāśāṭhyatā cittāvaṅkatā cittāmāyāvitā ca / śeṣaṃ subodham / iti 'cittakauṭilyaṃ' trayodaśaṃ teṣu talliṅgam //
body.translated_text: Beginning with '<s>Subhūti</s> said' and so on, up to before the [next] 'Moreover.' 'The mind's doing of small deeds' (<s>cittālpakṛtyatā</s>) is because of smallness and because of non-distraction. '<s>Kauṭilya</s>' (crookedness) of the mind is its state of being crooked. That which is a means of concealing one's own faults — that is '<s>śāṭhya</s>' (deceitfulness). That which is for the purpose of deceiving others — that is '<s>vaṅka</s>' (guile). The display of false qualities in oneself for the purpose of deceiving others is '<s>māyā</s>' (deception). Through the absence of these, respectively: non-crookedness of mind, non-deceitfulness of mind, non-guile of mind, and non-deceptiveness of mind. The rest is easily understood. Thus 'crookedness of mind' [i.e., its absence] is the thirteenth sign among those.

body.text: punaraparamityādi / atra lābhādigurūkatāpratiṣedhena dhutagrahotpyupalabhyate / iti 'dhutaguṇasamādanaṃ' caturdaśaṃ teṣu talliṅgam //
body.translated_text: Beginning with 'Moreover' and so on. Here, by the prohibition of esteeming gain and the rest, the adoption of ascetic practices (<s>dhutaguṇa</s>) is also understood. Thus 'the adoption of ascetic qualities' is the fourteenth sign among those.

body.text: nerṣyāmātmasaryabahulo bhavatīti mātsaryagrahaṇena ṣaṭpāramitāvipakṣā upalakṣyante / iti 'amatsarāditā' pañcadaśaṃ teṣu talliṅgam //
body.translated_text: 'He is not envious, not predominantly miserly' — by the mention of miserliness, the adversaries of the six <s>pāramitās</s> are indicated. Thus 'non-miserliness and the like' is the fifteenth sign among those.

body.text: na ca gambhīreṣvityādi punaraparāt prāk / saṃsyandanaṃ saṃyojanam / dharmatayā yuktaṃ sarvamavagacchatīti 'dharmatāyuktagāmitvaṃ' ṣoḍaśaṃ teṣu talliṅgam //
body.translated_text: Beginning with 'And in the profound' and so on, up to before the [next] 'Moreover.' '<s>Saṃsyandana</s>' is conjunction (<s>saṃyojana</s>). He understands everything as connected with <s>dharmatā</s> (the true nature) — thus 'proceeding in accordance with <s>dharmatā</s>' is the sixteenth sign among those.

body.text: punaraparamityādi dhārayitavyāntaram / pratideśayetyeayamatyayato deśaya / pratiniḥsajeti pratiniyamenātyantikatvena parityaja / evamiti bodhicittatyāge sati / evamapīti / īdṛśepi māyeṇoktai / śeṣaṃ subodham / iti lokānāmartho 'smāditi 'lokārthaṃ narakaiṣaṇā' narakasvīkāraḥ / saptadaśaṃ teṣu talliṅgam //
body.translated_text: Beginning with 'Moreover' and so on, up to the next 'should retain.' '<s>Pratideśaya</s>' means 'confess from the transgression.' '<s>Pratiniḥsaja</s>' means 'definitively and completely abandon.' 'Thus' means when there is the abandonment of <s>bodhicitta</s>. 'Even so' — even when such [things] are said by <s>Māra</s>. The rest is easily understood. Thus, 'for the benefit of the world' — because the benefit of the world comes from this — the 'seeking of hell' (<s>narakaiṣaṇā</s>), that is, the acceptance of hell [for the sake of others], is the seventeenth sign among those.

body.text: punaraparādi dhārayitavyāntam / yacchrutaṃ prajñāpāramitādi tatpratideśaya pratyācakṣva / yad gṛhītaṃ badhicittapāramitācaryādi tatparityaja / abhūtavicitravādī kaviḥ / tasya karma kāvyam / avinivartanīyasya dhātuḥ prakṛtiḥ / apratyudāvartanīyadharmeti pareṇa sambadhyate / śeṣaṃ subodham / iti 'parairaneyatā' 'ṣṭādaśaṃ teṣu talliṅgam //
body.translated_text: Beginning with 'Moreover' and so on, up to the [next] 'should retain.' 'Whatever has been heard — the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and the like — confess it, renounce it. Whatever has been adopted — the <s>bodhicitta</s>, the <s>pāramitā</s>-practice, and the like — abandon it.' 'One who speaks untrue and fanciful things' is a poet. His work is poetry (<s>kāvya</s>). 'The nature of the irreversible' is its natural disposition (<s>prakṛti</s>). 'Of irreversible nature' (<s>apratyudāvartanīyadharma</s>) connects with the following [clause]. The rest is easily understood. Thus 'not being led astray by others' is the eighteenth sign among those.

body.text: punaraparādi dhārayitavyāntam / saṃsāre cāriketyādinā bodhisattvamārgaṃ dūṣayati / ihaiva tvamityādinā śrāvakādimārgaṃ grāhayati / abhinirvṛtta iti kṣīṇāyuḥ / vāśabdo vikalpe / ihaivetyādikaṃ vā vakṣyati /
body.translated_text: Beginning with 'Moreover' and so on, up to the [next] 'should retain.' Beginning with 'wandering in <s>saṃsāra</s>' and so on, he disparages the <s>Bodhisattva</s> path. Beginning with 'right here you should' and so on, he causes [the practitioner] to adopt the <s>Śrāvaka</s> and other paths. '<s>Abhinirvṛtta</s>' means one whose lifespan is exhausted. The word '<s>vā</s>' indicates an alternative. He will either say 'right here' and so on,

body.text: aho vatetyādikaṃ vā / cittaṃ na kupyati na calatīti mārabhāṣitasya hīnamārgasya mārabhāṣitatvena jñānāt / ata idaṃ mārasyānyamārgopadeśino 'māra ityavabodhaḥ' ūnaviṃśatitamaṃ teṣu talliṅgam //
body.translated_text: or 'Aho!' and so on. 'The mind does not become angry, does not waver' — because of knowing that the inferior path spoken by <s>Māra</s> is spoken by <s>Māra</s>. Therefore this — 'the recognition of <s>Māra</s> who teaches another path as <s>Māra</s>' — is the nineteenth sign among those.

body.text: sā cedityādi dhārayitavyāntam / viveko mahāyānatyāgaḥ / tadarthāni vacanāni vivekapadāni / tāni parato mārāditaḥ śrutvā cittaṃ na parihīyate iti sambandhaḥ / na calatītyarthaḥ / kuta ityāha / dharmatāyā iti dharma eva dharmatā mahāyānacaryā tataḥ / na pratyudāvartata iti na vimukhībhavati / nānyathābhāva iti na viparyayaḥ / na hīnayāne bahumāna ityarthaḥ / tānīti vivekapadāni / caśabdo hetau / yasmānmārakarmāṇi jānāti / asthānamiti pareṇa sambadhyate / tatheti yathā buddhānuvarṇitam / śeṣaṃ subodham / iti 'caryābuddhānumoditā' viṃśatitama teṣu talliṅgam //
body.translated_text: Beginning with 'If that' and so on, up to the [next] 'should retain.' '<s>Viveka</s>' (separation) is the abandonment of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. The words serving that purpose are '<s>vivekapadas</s>' (words of separation). Having heard those from another — from <s>Māra</s> and the like — 'the mind does not deteriorate' — this is the connection. The meaning is: 'it does not waver.' Whence? He says: 'From <s>dharmatā</s>' — <s>dharma</s> itself is <s>dharmatā</s>, which is the <s>Mahāyāna</s> practice; from that. 'Does not turn away' means 'does not become averse.' 'No change of state' means 'no reversal' — the meaning is: no esteem for the lesser vehicle. 'Those' refers to the words of separation. The word '<s>ca</s>' is in the causal sense — because he recognizes <s>Māra's</s> deeds. '<s>Asthāna</s>' (impossible) connects with the following. '<s>Tathā</s>' (thus) means as praised by the <s>Buddhas</s>. The rest is easily understood. Thus 'practice approved by the <s>Buddhas</s>' is the twentieth sign among those.

children.translated_text: Established in the <s>ūṣman</s> (heat), <s>mūrdhan</s> (summit), <s>kṣānti</s> (patience), and <s>agradharma</s> (supreme dharma) [stages],
By these twenty signs, one enters <s>saṃbodhi</s> (awakening) and does not turn back.

body.text: ayamupasaṃhāraḥ / ūṣmādiṣu nirvedhabhāgīyeṣu sthite ya ebhirviśatyā liṅgairlakṣitaḥ sa sambodherna nivartate / so 'vinivartanīya ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: This is the conclusion. One who is established in the <s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s> (penetrative) [stages] beginning with heat and so on, and who is characterized by these twenty signs — he does not turn back from <s>saṃbodhi</s>. He is '<s>avinivartanīya</s>' (irreversible) — this is the meaning.

body.text: darśanamārge sthitamadhikṛtya śāstram-
body.translated_text: Regarding one who is established on the path of seeing, the treatise [states] —

children.text: kṣāntijñānakṣaṇāḥ ṣaṭ ca pañca pañca ca dṛkpathe /
children.translated_text: Six moments of patient acceptance and knowledge, and five and five, on the path of seeing —
Should be known as the characteristics of irreversibility for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. [4-46]

body.text: darśanamārge sthitasya bodhisattvasyāvaivartikaṃ liṅgaṃ veditavyam / kiṃ tat? 'kṣāntijñānalakṣaṇāḥ' kṣāntikṣaṇāḥ jñānakṣaṇāśca / 'ṣaṭ ca pañca pañca ca' iti ṣoḍaśetyarthaḥ / katame ṣoḍaśa?
body.translated_text: The irreversible sign of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> established on the path of seeing should be understood. What is it? '<s>Kṣāntijñānakṣaṇāḥ</s>' — the moments of patient acceptance and the moments of knowledge. 'Six and five and five' means sixteen — this is the meaning. Which sixteen?

children.translated_text: The turning away from the perception of form and the rest; firmness of mind regarding the two inferior
Vehicles, and the turning away [from them]; the diminishment of the limbs of <s>dhyāna</s> and the rest; [4-47]
Lightness of body and mind; the [practice] conducive to non-indulgence in sensual pleasures;
Perpetual <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate conduct); and the purification of livelihood; [4-48]
In the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) and the rest, in the obstacles, in the accumulation [of merit] together with the faculties and the rest,
In the battle, in miserliness and the rest — 'no' in [both] practice and engagement; [4-49]
And the prohibition regarding the mode of dwelling; the non-attainment of even an atom of <s>dharma</s>;
Certainty in one's own stage; and establishment in the three stages; [4-50]
The giving up of life for the sake of the <s>Dharma</s> — these are the sixteen moments,
The signs of irreversibility for the wise one established on the path of seeing. [4-51]

body.text: tatrādyamāha / punaraparamityādinā dhārayitavyāntena / abhisaṃskarotīti utpādayatītyarthaḥ / tamapi dharmamiti rūpādikaṃ nopalabhata ityādi / atra upalambha evābhisaṃskāraḥ / sa evotpādanam / anutpādajñāne kṣāntirasyeti bahuvrīhiḥ / iti 'rūpādisaṃjñāvyāvṛttiḥ' duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāntiḥ / sā dṛṅmārge prathamaṃ talliṅgam //
body.translated_text: Among those, the first is stated by the passage beginning with 'Moreover' and so on, up to the [next] 'should retain.' '<s>Abhisaṃskaroti</s>' means 'he produces' — this is the meaning. 'That <s>dharma</s> too' means form and the rest — 'he does not apprehend' and so on. Here, apprehension itself is the formation (<s>abhisaṃskāra</s>). That itself is the production. 'One in whom there is patient acceptance in the knowledge of non-arising' — this is a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound. Thus 'the turning away from the perception of form and the rest' is the <s>dharmajñānakṣānti</s> (patient acceptance of knowledge of the truth) regarding suffering — the first sign on the path of seeing.

body.text: punaraparamityādi dhārayitavyāntam / vicchankyisyatīti vigatacchandaṃ kariṣyati / ājñāsyati lokottareṇa jñānena / vihanyase kliṣyase / vivecanatā bodhicittatyājanam / tatreti samyaksambodhau / dṛḍhacittena iti samyaksambodhau 'cittadārḍhyaya' duḥkhe dharmajñānam / tad dṛṅmārge dvitīyaṃ talliṅgam //
body.translated_text: Beginning with 'Moreover' and so on, up to the [next] 'should retain.' '<s>Vicchankyiṣyati</s>' means 'he will cause to become disheartened.' '<s>Ājñāsyati</s>' means 'he will know through supramundane knowledge.' '<s>Vihanyase</s>' means 'you are afflicted.' '<s>Vivecanatā</s>' is the abandonment of <s>bodhicitta</s>. 'Therein' means in <s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (perfect awakening). 'With a firm mind' — 'firmness of mind' regarding <s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s> is the <s>dharmajñāna</s> (knowledge of the truth) regarding suffering — the second sign on the path of seeing.

body.text: punaraparādi bhavatyantam / iti 'hīnayānavinivṛttiḥ' duḥkhe 'nvayajñānakṣānti / sā dṛṅmārge tṛtīyaṃ liṅgam //
body.translated_text: Beginning with 'Moreover' and so on, up to the end of 'he is.' Thus 'the turning away from the lesser vehicle' is the <s>anvayajñānakṣānti</s> (patient acceptance of subsequent knowledge) regarding suffering — the third sign on the path of seeing.

body.text: sa ākāṅkṣannityādi veditavyāntam / iti 'dhyānādīnāmaṅgaparikṣayaḥ' kāmotpattivibandhe daurbalyaṃ duḥkhe 'nvayajñānam / tad dṛṅmārge caturthaṃ talliṅgam //
body.translated_text: Beginning with 'If he desires' and so on, up to the end of 'should be understood.' Thus 'the diminishment of the limbs of <s>dhyāna</s> and the rest' — the weakness of the impediment to the arising of desire — is the <s>anvayajñāna</s> (subsequent knowledge) regarding suffering — the fourth sign on the path of seeing.

body.text: punaraparādi sa cedityataḥ prāk / atra na nāmaguruka ityādikaṃ 'cetolaghutvam' / so 'bhikrāmanvetyādikaṃ 'kāyalaghutvam' / tadubhayaṃ samudaye dharmajñānakṣāntiḥ / sā dṛṅmārge pañcamaṃ talliṅgam //
body.translated_text: Beginning with 'Moreover' and so on, up to before 'if that.' Here, 'he is not burdened by name' and the like is 'lightness of mind' (<s>cetolaghutvam</s>). 'He walks with awareness' and the like is 'lightness of body' (<s>kāyalaghutvam</s>). Both of these constitute the <s>dharmajñānakṣānti</s> (patient acceptance of knowledge of the truth) regarding the origin [of suffering] — the fifth sign on the path of seeing.

body.text: sa cedityādi prāganarthikāt / yathoktaiva saṃjñābhyupāyaḥ tena nirvṛttā 'kāmasevābhyupāyikī' / sā samudaye dharmajñānam / tad dṛṅmārge ṣaṣṭhaṃ tallīṅgam //
body.translated_text: Beginning with 'If that' and so on, up to before '<s>anarthika</s>' (useless). The perception as described above is the means; the [practice] accomplished through it is 'conducive to non-indulgence in sensual pleasures.' That is the <s>dharmajñāna</s> (knowledge of the truth) regarding the origin — the sixth sign on the path of seeing.

body.text: anarthikā eva cetyādi dhārayitavyāntam / atyarthaṃ saumanasyajananāt priyarūpaiḥ / atyarthaṃ sukhajananāt sātarūpaiḥ / praśaṃsāyāṃ rūpap vā / anarthikā eveti nityamanarthikāḥ / na samaviṣameṇeti na yuktāyuktena / kathamityāha / dharmeṇaivetyādi / apamardanaṃ pīḍā / pañcabhirmokṣabhāgīyaiścaturbhirnirvedhabhāgīyaiḥ saptabhiśca darśanakṣaṇairyogāt satpuruṣairityādini ṣoḍaśapadāni / iti 'sadaiva brahmacāritvaṃ samudaye 'nvayajñānakṣāntiḥ / sā dṛṅmārge saptamaṃ talliṅgam //
body.translated_text: Beginning with 'Useless indeed' and so on, up to the [next] 'should retain.' 'Exceedingly producing delight' — by pleasant forms. 'Exceedingly producing happiness' — by agreeable forms. Or in the [sense of] praise. 'Useless indeed' means always useless. 'Not by right or wrong' means not by appropriate or inappropriate [means]. How? He says beginning with 'By the <s>Dharma</s> alone' and so on. '<s>Apamardana</s>' (oppression) is affliction. The sixteen terms beginning with 'by the five pertaining to liberation, by the four pertaining to penetration, and by the seven moments of seeing' are through the connection [with practice]. 'By good persons' and the remaining sixteen terms. Thus 'perpetual <s>brahmacarya</s>' (celibate conduct) is the <s>anvayajñānakṣānti</s> (patient acceptance of subsequent knowledge) regarding the origin — the seventh sign on the path of seeing.

body.text: punaraparādi dhārayitavyāntam / mantrajātirmantrāviśeṣaḥ grahadevatāyāḥ / auṣadhiḥ pā(pha)lapākāntā / strīdevatāyā mantro vidyā /
body.translated_text: Beginning with 'Moreover' and so on, up to the [next] 'should retain.' '<s>Mantrajāti</s>' (type of spell) is a particular spell of a deity who seizes. '<s>Auṣadhi</s>' (herb) is [a plant] up to the ripening of fruit. The spell of a female deity is '<s>vidyā</s>.'

body.text: bhaiṣajyamauṣadham / ādiśabdena yantramantrādiparigrahaḥ / vigrahaḥ kāyena kalaho vivādastu vācā / iti 'ājīvapariśuddhiḥ' samudaye 'nvayajñānam / dṛṅmārge 'ṣṭamaṃ tāliṅgam //
body.translated_text: '<s>Bhaiṣajya</s>' (medicine) is a remedy. By the word 'and so on,' <s>yantras</s> (magical diagrams), spells, and the like are included. '<s>Vigraha</s>' (strife) is quarrel by body; but '<s>vivāda</s>' (dispute) is by speech. Thus 'the purification of livelihood' is the <s>anvayajñāna</s> (subsequent knowledge) regarding the origin — the eighth sign on the path of seeing.

body.text: navamāt prabhṛti pañcakṣaṇānadhikṛtya śāstram-
body.translated_text: Beginning with the ninth, regarding the five moments, the treatise [states] —

children.translated_text: 'In the <s>skandhas</s> and the rest, in the obstacles, in the accumulation together with the faculties and the rest,
In the battle, in miserliness and the rest — "no" in [both] practice and engagement;

body.text: vihāre pratiṣedhaśca'
body.translated_text: And the prohibition regarding the mode of dwelling' —

body.text: iti / 'yogaḥ' sābhiniveśā vṛttiḥ / 'anuyogo ' nirabhiniveśā vṛttiḥ / tābhyāṃ vihārastayorvihārastadvānsamādhiḥ / tasya 'pratiṣedhaḥ' / 'neti' iti naño sambandhādityarthaḥ / sa punarvihāraḥ 'skandhādau' prathamaḥ / 'antarāyeṣu' dvitīyaḥ / 'sambhāre ' tṛtīyaḥ / 'sendriyādike samare ' caturthaḥ / 'matsarādau' pañcamaḥ / tatra caturaṃ tāvadāha punaraparamityādinā na ca te kalahetyataḥ prāk / na te skandhāyatanetyādi / yogāścānuyogaśca yogānuyogaṃ tadanuiyuktāstena saha yuktāḥ / sahārthe 'nuśabdaḥ / na viharantīti sambandhaḥ / atropapattirmahatyobhaṃgavatyoruktā- "tathā hi sa śūnyatāyāṃ sthito na kasyaciddharmasya hīnatvaṃ vā utkṛṣṭatvaṃ vā samanupaśyati" iti / enāmasyāṃ vākyadvayenāha / saṃkleśapakṣo niḥsāratvena saṅgaṇikārāmatāviṣayatvāt saṅgaṇikārāmatā / saivāsattvena kathāmātratvāt kathā / śeṣaṃ pūrvavat / utkṛṣṭatvādrājasaṃkleśanirodhaḥ / sa eva kathā asākṣātkṛtatvena kathāmātratvāt kathā / etāveva kathe dve / yathāyogamuttaratrāpīti skandhādiyogānuyogavihāraviraho nirodhe dharmajñānakṣāntiḥ / sā dṛṅmārge navamaṃ talliṅgam //
body.translated_text: Thus. '<s>Yoga</s>' (engagement) is activity with grasping. '<s>Anuyoga</s>' (pursuit) is activity without grasping. The abiding through those two is the abiding of those two — that <s>samādhi</s> (concentration). Its 'negation.' 'Not' — from the connection of the negation particle — this is the meaning. And that abiding is: first, 'in the aggregates and so forth'; second, 'in obstacles'; third, 'in the accumulation [of merit]'; fourth, 'in the battle beginning with the faculties and the like'; fifth, 'in stinginess and the rest.' Therein, for the fourth, he first says with 'furthermore' and so forth, up to before 'and they do not quarrel.' 'Not in the aggregates, sense-bases' and so forth. '<s>Yogānuyoga</s>' — <s>yoga</s> and <s>anuyoga</s> — those engaged therein are those yoked with it; the word '<s>anu</s>' is in the sense of 'together with.' 'They do not abide' — this is the syntactic connection. The justification for this is stated in the two great [texts]: 'For thus, one who abides in emptiness does not perceive any <s>dharma</s> as inferior or as superior.' He states this in two sentences. The defilement-side, because of being without essence, has the domain of delight in company — hence '<s>saṅgaṇikārāmatā</s>' (delight in company). That itself, because of being without a being, is mere talk — hence 'talk.' The rest is as before. Because of superiority, [there is] the cessation of the defilement of <s>rajas</s> (passion). That itself is 'talk,' because of not being directly realized — hence being mere talk. These are the two talks. [Applied] correspondingly also further on — thus the freedom from the abiding in the engagement and pursuit of talk about the aggregates and the like is the <s>dharmajñānakṣānti</s> (patient acceptance of the knowledge of dharmas) regarding cessation. That, on the path of seeing, is the ninth sign thereof.

body.text: pañca nivaraṇāni caurāḥ kuśaladravyaharatvāt / śeṣaṃ pūrvavat / iti nirodhe dharmajñānam / tad dṛṅmārge daśamaṃ talliṅgam //
body.translated_text: The five <s>nīvaraṇas</s> (hindrances) are thieves, because they steal wholesome goods. The rest is as before. Thus [this is] the <s>dharmajñāna</s> (knowledge of dharmas) regarding cessation. That, on the path of seeing, is the tenth sign thereof.

body.text: kuśaladharmasambhāraḥ senā / śeṣaṃ pūrvavat / iti nirodhe 'nvayajñānakṣāntiḥ / sā dṛṅmārge ekādaśaṃ talliṅgam //
body.translated_text: The accumulation of wholesome <s>dharmas</s> is the army. The rest is as before. Thus [this is] the <s>anvayajñānakṣānti</s> (patient acceptance of subsequent knowledge) regarding cessation. That, on the path of seeing, is the eleventh sign thereof.

body.text: tayā senayā vipakṣāṇāṃ bādhanaṃ yuddham / śeṣaṃ pūrvavat / yuddhe sati nirodhaḥ prāpyate / nirodho nirvāṇaṃ vimuktiḥ / kaścāsau? dehapratiṣṭhābogapratibhāsānāṃ vijñaptīnāṃ parāvṛttiḥ / tasmāddehādīnāmavikalpanāt na grāmanagaranigamajanapadarāṣṭrarājadhānīkathāyogānuyogamanuyuktā viharanti / tatra cakṣurādi pañcakaṃ
body.translated_text: The battle is the subduing of opponents by that army. The rest is as before. When there is battle, cessation is attained. Cessation is <s>nirvāṇa</s>, liberation. And what is that? The transformation (<s>parāvṛtti</s>) of the representations (<s>vijñaptis</s>) of body, support, enjoyment, and appearance. Therefore, through the non-conceptualization of body and the rest, they do not abide engaged and pursuing talk about villages, cities, towns, settlements, kingdoms, and capitals. Therein, the five [sense faculties] beginning with the eye

body.text: dehaḥ / sa hi grāma indriyagrāmatvāt / dehānāmādhāratvāt pratiṣṭhā nagaram / niyatendriyagamyatvāt nigamo bhogaḥ pañcaviṣayāḥ / janapadādayaḥ pratiṣṭhāviśeṣāḥ / ātmātmīyavikalpakṣaye sati mokṣaḥ / tata ātmavikalpānadhikṛtyāha / nātmakathetyādi / ātmīyavikalpānadhikṛtyāha / nāmātyetyādi / ita urdhvarūpāḥ kathāste yathāyogamātmīyavikalpā bhogavikalpāḥ pratiṣṭhāvikalpā vā veditavyāḥ / yadi tathā tathā na viharanti kathaṃ tarhi viharantītyāha / api nvityādi / prajñāpāramitaiva katha pratyavekṣā / śeṣaṃ purvavat / sarvatra dharmatayā samatāyogānuyogamanuyuktā eva viharantītyarthaḥ / sarvajñatāpratisaṃyuktairiti bodhicittapratisaṃyuktaiḥ / yuddhendriyādikathāyogānuyogavihāraviraho nirodhe 'nvayajñānam / tad dṛṅmārge dvādaśaṃ talliṅgam //
body.translated_text: are the 'body.' For it is a 'village' (<s>grāma</s>) because of being a village of faculties. 'City' (<s>nagara</s>) is the support, because of being the basis of bodies. 'Town' (<s>nigama</s>) is enjoyment — the five sense-objects — because of being accessible to specific faculties. 'Settlement' (<s>janapada</s>) and the rest are particular supports. When the conceptualization of self and what belongs to self is exhausted, there is liberation. Therefore, regarding the conceptualization of the self, he says 'not talk of the self' and so on. Regarding the conceptualization of what belongs to self, he says 'not of the name' and so on. From this point onward, the talks that are form-based should be understood, correspondingly, as conceptualizations of what belongs to self, conceptualizations of enjoyment, or conceptualizations of support. If they do not abide thus and thus, how then do they abide? — he says 'but rather' and so forth. <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> itself is the talk, the examination. The rest is as before. The meaning is: they abide engaged and pursuing the equality of all <s>dharmas</s> through their <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature). 'Connected with <s>sarvajñatā</s>' means connected with <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening). The freedom from the abiding in the engagement and pursuit of talk about battle, faculties, and the like is the <s>anvayajñāna</s> (subsequent knowledge) regarding cessation. That, on the path of seeing, is the twelfth sign thereof.

body.text: 'matsarādau ca' iti śāstram / yadāha mahatyoḥ / "sa dānapāramitāyāṃ caranna mātsaryakathāyogamanuyukto viharati yāvat prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caranna dauṣṭhulyakathāyogamanuyukto viharati" iti / tadasyāmāha / na ca te kalahabhaṇḍanavigrahavivādakathāyogānuyogamanuyuktā viharantīti / vipakṣatvātkalahā mātsaryādayaḥ / pratipakṣatvātkalahā mātsaryādayaḥ / pratipakṣatvābhdaṇḍanādayaḥ / yadobhayeṣāṃ cetasi cārastulyabalatā ca tadā vigrahaḥ / yadā tu pratipakṣairvipakṣā durbalīkriyante tadā vivādaḥ / tāveva vigrahavivādau kathā vikalpatvāt / tasyāṃ yogānuyogamanuyuktā na viharanti / abhedaḥ samatājñānam / bhedo nānātvavikalpaḥ / mitrakāmāścetyādi dhārayitavyāntaṃ sugamam / iti mārge dharmajñānakṣāntiḥ / sā dṛṅmārge trayodaśaṃ talliṅgam //
body.translated_text: 'And in stinginess and the rest' — thus [says] the treatise. As the two great [texts] say: 'Practicing the <s>dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of generosity), he does not abide engaged in talk of stinginess, up to: practicing the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom), he does not abide engaged in talk of mental heaviness.' He states that in this [text]: 'And they do not abide engaged and pursuing talk of quarrel, contention, dispute, and argument.' Because they are the opposing side, quarrels are stinginess and the like. Because they are the counteracting side, contentions and the like. When the mental activity and equal strength of both [sides obtain], that is dispute. But when the opponents are weakened by the counteracting [forces], that is argument. Those very disputes and arguments are 'talk,' because they are conceptualizations. They do not abide engaged and pursuing that. 'Non-differentiation' is the knowledge of equality. 'Differentiation' is the conceptualization of multiplicity. 'Desiring friends' and so forth, up to 'should be retained' — easily understood. Thus [this is] the <s>dharmajñānakṣānti</s> (patient acceptance of the knowledge of dharmas) regarding the path. That, on the path of seeing, is the thirteenth sign thereof.

body.text: punaraparādi sa cedityataḥ prāk / anetaitadāha /
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore' and so forth, up to before 'if he.' He states this by that:

body.text: 'dharmasyāṇoralabdhatā / niścitatvaṃ svabhūmau ca' iti / so 'ṇumapi dharma na samanupaśyati yo vivarte, bhavān vā vivartena / tathāpi svasyāmavinivartanīyabhūmau niḥsaṃśayo bhavati / vicikitsā saṃśayaḥ / saṃsīdanaṃ mandotsāhatā / ānantaryacitteneti / anantaryapaścāttāpena / prativinodanaṃ sarvathātyāgaḥ / viṣkambhaṇaṃ mandākaraṇam / avinivartanīyacittamātmano 'vinivartanīyatvaniścayaḥ / asaṃhāryamapratyāneyam / ityavaivartikabhūmau 'sthiraniścayatva' mārge dharmajñānam / tad dṛṅmārge caturdaśaṃ talliṅgam //
body.translated_text: 'The non-apprehension of even an atom of <s>dharma</s>, and certainty in one's own stage.' He does not perceive even an atom of <s>dharma</s> that turns back, or turning back. Even so, he becomes free from doubt regarding his own stage of irreversibility. '<s>Vicikitsā</s>' (uncertainty) is doubt. '<s>Saṃsīdana</s>' (sinking) is feeble enthusiasm. 'With a mind of immediate succession' means with the remorse immediately following. '<s>Prativinodana</s>' (dispelling) is complete abandonment. '<s>Viṣkambhaṇa</s>' (suppression) is weakening. 'The irreversible mind' is the certainty of one's own irreversibility. '<s>Asaṃhārya</s>' means not to be turned back. Thus, 'firm certainty on the irreversible stage' — [this is] the <s>dharmajñāna</s> (knowledge of dharmas) regarding the path. That, on the path of seeing, is the fourteenth sign thereof.

body.text: 'bhūmitritayasaṃsthitiḥ / ' mārakarma tathāgatabhāṣitasyānyathātvaṃ bhāvinī cātmanaḥ samyaksambodhiriti trīṇi sthānāni 'bhūmitritayam' / tasmin 'saṃsthitiḥ'
body.translated_text: 'Establishment in the threefold ground.' <s>Māra</s>'s activity, the alteration of what was spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, and one's own future <s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (perfect awakening) — these three positions are the 'threefold ground.' 'Establishment' therein

body.text: ātyantiko niścayaḥ / tāmāha / sa cetkhalvityādinā dhārayitavyāntena / ihaivetyasminneva janmani / nāyaṃ tathāgata ityasmātpūrva iti śabdaḥ paro draṣṭavyaḥ / tathā tannānyathetyukte 'rthādgamyate bhaviṣyatyeva me 'nuttarā samyaksambodhiriti / buddhādhiṣṭhānaṃ buddhanirmāṇam / addheti tattvata ityarthaḥ / iti bhūmitrayasaṃsthitimārge 'nvayajñānakṣāntiḥ / sā dṛṅmārge pañcadaśaṃ talliṅgam //
body.translated_text: is absolute certainty. He states that with 'if indeed' and so forth, up to 'should be retained.' 'In this very [life]' means in this very birth. 'Not this <s>Tathāgata</s>' — the word 'prior' before this should be understood as 'subsequent.' Similarly, when 'that is not otherwise' is stated, it is understood from the context that 'my unsurpassed <s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s> will certainly come to be.' '<s>Buddhādhiṣṭhāna</s>' (empowerment of the <s>Buddha</s>) is a manifestation of the <s>Buddha</s>. '<s>Addha</s>' means 'in truth' — this is the meaning. Thus, the establishment in the threefold ground — [this is] the <s>anvayajñānakṣānti</s> (patient acceptance of subsequent knowledge) regarding the path. That, on the path of seeing, is the fifteenth sign thereof.

body.text: punaraparamityādi āparivartāntāt / ātmanaḥ parityāgo vikrayādi / jīvitasya parityāgo maraṇam / buddhairbhagavabhdirdeśito dharmaḥ sarvadharmāḥ śūnyā iti / tameva mohapuruṣāḥ pratikṣipanti / tasya svayaṃ paraiśca parigrahāya jīvitamapi tyajati / sa hi buddheṣu yatpremagauravaṃ taddharme karoti / dharmakāyāstathāgatā iti jñānāt / ātmanaśca bhāvibuddhatvadarśanāt / śrāvakasyāpītyupalakṣaṇam / bodhisattvasyāpi devāderapi / śeṣaṃ subodhamiti / 'dharmārthaṃ jīvitatyāgaḥ' mārge 'nvayajñānam / tad dṛṅmārge ṣoḍaśaṃ talliṅgam //
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore' and so forth, up to the end of the chapter. The giving up of oneself is selling and the like. The giving up of life is dying. The <s>Dharma</s> taught by the blessed <s>Buddhas</s> is 'all <s>dharmas</s> are empty.' Deluded persons reject that very [teaching]. For the sake of its acceptance by oneself and by others, he gives up even his life. For the love and reverence that he has for the <s>Buddhas</s>, he applies to the <s>Dharma</s> — because of knowing that the <s>Tathāgatas</s> are <s>dharmakāya</s> (dharma-body). And because of seeing one's own future <s>buddhahood</s>. 'Even of a <s>śrāvaka</s>' (disciple) is illustrative — even of a <s>bodhisattva</s>, even of a <s>deva</s> and the like. The rest is easily understood. Thus, 'the giving up of life for the sake of the <s>Dharma</s>' — [this is] the <s>anvayajñāna</s> (subsequent knowledge) regarding the path. That, on the path of seeing, is the sixteenth sign thereof.

body.text: 'ityamī ṣoḍaśa kṣaṇāḥ / avaivartikaliṅgāni dṛṅmārgasthasya dhīmataḥ' // ityupasaṃhāraḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Thus these sixteen moments. The signs of irreversibility of the wise one who abides on the path of seeing.' // This is the conclusion. //

body.text: avinivartanīyasya yānyākāraliṅganimittāni taddyotakaḥ parivartastatparivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: The aspects, signs, and marks of the irreversible [<s>bodhisattva</s>] — the chapter that illuminates those is that chapter.

body.text: āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ sāratamānāmni pañjikāyāṃ ratnākaraśāntiviracitāyāṃ saptadaśaḥ parivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: In the <s>Pañjikā</s> commentary named <s>Sāratama</s>, composed by <s>Ratnākaraśānti</s>, on the noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s> — this is the seventeenth chapter.

body.text: 18. śūnyatāparivarto nāmāṣṭādaśaḥ /
body.translated_text: 18. The eighteenth [chapter] is named the '<s>Śūnyatā-parivarta</s>' (Chapter on Emptiness).

body.text: nirvedhāṅgadṛṅmārgayoravaivartikaliṅgāni saṃkhyayā viśeṣataścoktani / bhāvanāmārgastu gambhīraḥ / tato tānyubhayathāpi vaktumaśakyāni / ataḥ śāstram-
body.translated_text: The signs of irreversibility on the <s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s> (penetrative) and the path of seeing have been stated in terms of number and distinction. But the <s>bhāvanā-mārga</s> (path of cultivation) is profound. Therefore, those [signs] cannot be stated in either way. Hence the treatise [states] —

body.text: gambhīro bhāvanāmārgaḥ
body.translated_text: The path of cultivation is profound.

body.text: etadāha / atha khalvityādinā pratyekabuddhairityetadantena / āścaryaṃ bhagavannityekaṃ codyam / kimāścaryamityata āha / mahāguṇetyādi /
body.translated_text: He states this: with 'now then' and so forth, up to the end of 'by <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>.' 'It is wondrous, O <s>Bhagavān</s>' — this is one objection. 'What is wondrous?' — to this he says 'of great qualities' and so forth.

body.text: mahān guṇasambhāraḥ paramagambhīratayā kalpāsaṃkhyeyadvayanirantaraprayatnalabhyatayā ca / ata eva viśeṣato jñātumaśakyatvādapramāṇāḥ saṃkhyātumaśakyatvādaparimitāḥ / bodhisattvo mahāsattva iti bhāvanāmārgastho 'vaivartikaḥ / avinivartanīyeneti bhāvanāmārgasthena / saṃkhyātikramād anantam / paramodāratvād aparyantam / asaṃhārya samyagagrādyaṃ samyagjñātumaśakyaṃ śrāvakapratyekabuddhairapīti bhāvanāmārgasya gāmbhīryam //
body.translated_text: 'Great accumulation of qualities' — because of its supreme profundity and because it is obtainable [only] through uninterrupted effort over two incalculable <s>kalpas</s> (eons). For that very reason, because they cannot be known specifically, they are immeasurable; because they cannot be counted, they are unlimited. '<s>Bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>' means the irreversible one abiding on the path of cultivation. 'By the irreversible one' means by one abiding on the path of cultivation. Because of exceeding number, [it is] infinite. Because of being supremely noble, [it is] boundless. '<s>Asaṃhārya</s>' — 'foremost' and the rest that are correct — impossible to be correctly known even by <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples) and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary realizers) — this is the profundity of the path of cultivation.

body.text: subhūtirāhetyādi pratibalaḥ śakto nirdeṣṭum / kintu sattvā(rvā)rtho na syāditi bhāvaḥ / tataḥ kimityāha / ata evetyādi / evakāro bhinnakramaḥ / sthānānītyataḥ pareṇa draṣṭavyaḥ / sarvāṇi gambhīrāṇīti vīpsārthaḥ / sthānānīti bhāvanāmārgālambanāni / prajñāpāramitāyāṃ pratisaṃyuktāni tadādhāraṇītyarthaḥ / sūcayitavyānīti sūcyantāmityarthaḥ / iti subhūteradhyeṣaṇā //
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> says and so forth. '<s>Pratibala</s>' means capable of explaining. But the benefit of beings would not be [served] — this is the meaning. 'Then what?' — he says 'for this very reason' and so forth. The particle '<s>eva</s>' is in rearranged order; it should be read after '<s>sthānāni</s>' (topics). 'All are profound' — the word indicates distributive meaning. '<s>Sthānāni</s>' (topics) means the objects of the path of cultivation. 'Connected with <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>' means having that as their basis — this is the meaning. 'Should be indicated' means 'let them be indicated.' This is <s>Subhūti</s>'s request.

body.text: evamukta ityādi / ārabhyeti / ādau nirdiśya / nigamayitukāma iti bhāvanārge yojayitukāmaḥ / iti bhagavato 'bhyupagamaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Thus spoken' and so forth. 'Beginning with' means having first taught. 'Wishing to conclude' means wishing to apply to the path of cultivation. This is the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s assent.

body.text: atha śāstram-
body.translated_text: Now the treatise [states] —
