children.translated_text: The profundity is emptiness and the like.
Freedom from the extremes of superimposition and deprecation — that is profundity. // 4-52 //

body.text: 'gambhīro bhāvanāmārgaḥ' ityuktam / tasya 'gāmbhīryaṃ' gambhīrabhāvaḥ / yataḥ sa gambhīro bhavati tacca śūnyatānimittādikam / mārgasya gambhīryamālambanagāmbhīryāditi bhāvaḥ / taccālambanaṃ 'śūnyatādi' / śūnyatāderapi kā gāmbhīryatā? yāsya samāropāntenāpavādāntena cārahitatā / bhagavānabhyupagataṃ sūcayitumāha / gambhīramitītyādi / sarvadharmāṇāṃ yathāpratibhāsabhāvo yathātattvaṃ ca bhāvaḥ śūnyatā / saivānimittaṃtadvedane nimittanirodhāt / saivāpraṇihitaṃ tadvidāṃ traidhātuke 'praṇidhānāt / saivānabhisaṃskārasteṣāṃ punarbhavāya karmākaraṇāt / saivānutpādasteṣāṃ tena karmaṇānutpādāt / saivājātisteṣāṃ prakṛtyajātatājñānāt / saivābhāvo 'dravyatvāt / saiva virāgaśuddhiḥ kleśānuśayasamudghātāt / saiva nirodhasteṣāṃ punarbhavavi(ni)rodhāt / saiva nirvāṇaṃ teṣāṃ vāsanāsamudghātāt / saiva vigamasteṣāṃ sāśravaskandhoparamāt // iti śūnyatādikam //
body.translated_text: 'The path of cultivation is profound' — this was stated. Its 'profundity' is the state of being profound. That because of which it is profound — that is emptiness, signlessness, and the like. The profundity of the path is due to the profundity of its object — this is the meaning. And that object is 'emptiness and the like.' And what is the profundity even of emptiness and the like? It is its freedom from the extreme of superimposition and from the extreme of deprecation. The <s>Bhagavān</s>, [wishing to] indicate what he has assented to, says 'profound indeed' and so forth. The existence of all <s>dharmas</s> as they appear and their existence as they truly are — [that] is emptiness. That itself is signlessness — because of the cessation of signs for those who know it. That itself is wishlessness — because those [who know it] do not form aspirations in the three realms. That itself is non-formation — because of their not performing <s>karma</s> for future existence. That itself is non-arising — because of their non-arising through that <s>karma</s>. That itself is non-birth — because of the knowledge that they are unborn by nature. That itself is non-existence — because of being non-substantial. That itself is the purity of dispassion — because of the eradication of the latent tendencies of afflictions. That itself is cessation — because of the cessation of their future existence. That itself is <s>nirvāṇa</s> — because of the eradication of their latent impressions. That itself is departure — because of the cessation of the aggregates with outflows. Thus [this is] emptiness and the like.

body.text: subhūtirāheti kākvā pṛcchatītyarthaḥ / dharmāṇāmiti śūnyatādinām / sarvadharmāṇāmiti skandhadhātvādīnām / bālagrāhyā rūpādayaste kathaṃ gambhīrāḥ? ataḥ svayameva pṛcchati kathaṃ cetyādi / uttaraṃ yathā tathatetyādi /
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> says — he asks with wonder — this is the meaning. 'Of <s>dharmas</s>' means of emptiness and the like. 'Of all <s>dharmas</s>' means of the aggregates, elements, and the rest. 'Those such as form and the rest, which are grasped by the childish — how are they profound?' Therefore he himself asks 'how then' and so forth. The answer is 'just as suchness' and so forth.

body.text: kasya tathateti cedāha tatretyādi / sphuṭīkartumāha yathetyādi / yatreti yasyāṃ rūpāditathatāyāṃ vedyamānāyāṃ kalpitaṃ rūpādi na prakhyāti iyaṃ rūpādīnāṃ gambhīratā / paramārthasatā rūpeṇa teṣāṃ prakhyānāt / samyagdeśanayā toṣitaḥ subhūtirāha / āścaryamityādi / sūkṣmeṇeti nipuna(ṇa)vedyena / nirvāṇaṃ ca sūcitam / bhāvanāmārgasthasyāvaivartikasya sarveṣāṃ parikalpitānāmaprakhyānāt / rūpādibhyaśca nivāritaḥ / teṣāṃ paramārthasya prakhyānāt / tatra nirvāṇena rūpādisamāropāntamutkatā / iti śūnyatādigambhīratā //
body.translated_text: 'Whose suchness?' — to this he says 'therein' and so forth. To make it explicit, he says 'just as' and so forth. 'Therein' means: when the suchness of form and the rest is being cognized, the imagined form and the rest do not appear — this is the profundity of form and the rest. Because they appear as form through being real in the ultimate sense. <s>Subhūti</s>, gratified by the correct teaching, says 'it is wondrous' and so forth. 'By the subtle' means by what is known through subtlety. 'And <s>nirvāṇa</s> has been indicated' — because for the irreversible one abiding on the path of cultivation, all imagined [constructs] do not appear. 'And [he is] turned away from form and the rest' — because those appear as their ultimate reality. Therein, through <s>nirvāṇa</s>, freedom from the extreme of superimposition regarding form and the rest [is shown]. Thus [this is] the profundity of emptiness and the like.

body.text: atha śāstram-
body.translated_text: Now the treatise [states] —

children.translated_text: Reflection, weighing, and contemplation — continuously — are the path of meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>),

children.text: nirve āṅgeṣu dṛṅmārge bhāvanāmārga eva ca // 4-53 //
children.translated_text: upon the factors conducive to penetration (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>), the path of seeing (<s>dṛṅmārga</s>), and the path of meditation (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>) itself. // 4-53 //

body.text: 'abhīkṣṇaṃ' iti prabandhena / ataḥ prābandhikāni 'cintātulananidhyānāni' svabhāvo bhāvanāmārgasya alambanaṃ śūnyatādi / śūnyatāderādhāro nirvedhabhāgīyadṛṅmārgabhāvanāmārgāḥ(rgaḥ) kathaṃ bhāvanāmārgasyā(ścā)syaiva viṣaya iti cedāha-
body.translated_text: "Continuously" (<s>abhīkṣṇam</s>) means in an unbroken series. Therefore, "reflection, weighing, and contemplation" are sequential; the own-nature of the path of meditation; the object is emptiness and the like. The support of emptiness and the like is the factors conducive to penetration, the path of seeing, and the path of meditation. If [one objects:] "How can the path of meditation be its own object?" — to this he says:

body.text: prābandhikatvādiṣṭo 'sau
body.translated_text: "Because of its sequential character, it is so taught."

body.text: 'prābandhiko ' hi bhāvanāmārgaḥ / tataḥ prākṛto viṣayaḥ paścāttamo viṣayīti nāsti virodhaḥ / atra sūtraṃ bhagavānāhetyādi / imānīti yathoktāni śūnyatādīni / prajñāpāramitāpratisaṃyuktānīti / vikalpapāramittaiva prajñā prajñāpāramitā darśanamārgo bhāvanāmārgaśca / nirvedhabhāgīyāni tu tādarthyātprajñāpāramitā / tasyāṃ trividhāyāṃ pratisaṃyuktāni sambaddhāni tadādhārāṇītyarthaḥ / ya imānio cintayiṣyati tulayiṣyati upanidhāsyatīti sambandhaḥ / kathamityata āha / evaṃ mayetyādi / sthātavyamiti cintayaikāntaniścayāt / śikṣitavyamiti tulanena śamathotpādanāt / pratipattavyamityupanidhyānena vipaśyanotpādanāt / ājñaptaṃ granthaśravaṇāt / ākhyātamarthajñāpanāt / upadiṣṭaṃ rahasyakīrtanāt catasro yuktayaḥ / apekṣāyuktiḥ sarvahetūnapekṣya kāryotpatteḥ / kāryakāraṇayuktiḥ tebhyaḥ pratyekaṃ kāryaviśeṣotpatteḥ / upapattiḥ sādhanayuktiḥ / yena pramāṇena yo 'rthaḥ sidhyati / dharmatāyuktiḥ svabhāvaniyamodharmāṇām / agni eva dahatyāpa eva kledayantītyādi / ābhiḥ samādhyālambanasya rahasi paryaṅkamāruhya satkṛtya sātatyena nirūpaṇaṃ cintā / tatraiva navākāreṇa śamathena cetasaḥ samīkaraṇaṃ tulanam / dharmānvicinoti pravicinoti parivitarkayati parimīmāṃsāmāpadyata iti caturākārā vipaśyanā upanidhyānam // tatra yathāvabhdāvikatājñānaṃ vicayaḥ /
body.translated_text: For the path of meditation is sequential. Therefore, the earlier [stage] is the object, and the later one is the subject — thus there is no contradiction. Here the <s>sūtra</s> [begins with] "the <s>Bhagavān</s> said" and so on. "These" refers to the emptiness and the rest as stated. "Connected with <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>" — the wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) that is the perfection of non-conceptualization is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>: the path of seeing and the path of meditation. But the factors conducive to penetration are <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> because of being directed toward that purpose. "Connected with" the threefold [<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>] means linked, having that as their support — this is the meaning. "Whoever will reflect upon these, will weigh, will contemplate" — this is the connection. "How?" — to this he says: "Thus by me" and so on. "One should abide" — through reflection, because of definitive certainty. "One should train" — through weighing, because of producing <s>śamatha</s> (calm). "One should practice" — through contemplation, because of producing <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight). "Instructed" (<s>ājñapta</s>) — through hearing the text. "Declared" (<s>ākhyāta</s>) — through making the meaning known. "Taught" (<s>upadiṣṭa</s>) — through proclaiming the esoteric [meaning]. The four types of reasoning (<s>yuktis</s>): the reasoning of dependence (<s>apekṣāyukti</s>) — because effects arise in dependence upon all causes. The reasoning of cause and effect (<s>kāryakāraṇayukti</s>) — because from each [cause] a specific effect arises. The reasoning of proof (<s>upapatti/sādhanayukti</s>) — the <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition) by which a given meaning is established. The reasoning of <s>dharmatā</s> (natural law) — the natural determination of <s>dharmas</s>: "fire alone burns, water alone moistens" and so on. By means of these, the examination of the object of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), in solitude, having ascended to the cross-legged posture, with devotion and continuity, is "reflection" (<s>cintā</s>). In that very [state], the equalization of the mind by <s>śamatha</s> in the ninefold manner is "weighing" (<s>tulana</s>). "He investigates <s>dharmas</s>, thoroughly investigates, reflects upon, and subjects to thorough examination" — this fourfold <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) is "contemplation" (<s>upanidhyāna</s>). Among these, the knowledge of things as they truly are is investigation (<s>vicaya</s>).

body.text: pañcaiva skandhā ityādi yathāvabhdāvikatājñānaṃ pravicayaḥ / sarva ete śūnyā ityādi nirvikalpena manasā prajñāsahagatena nimittīkaraṇaṃ parivitarkaḥ / santīraṇaṃ parimīmāṃsā / iti bhāvanāmārgasya svabhāvaḥ //
body.translated_text: "There are just five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates)" and so on — the knowledge of things as they truly are is thorough investigation (<s>pravicaya</s>). "All these are empty" and so on — the making-an-object [of this] with a non-conceptual mind accompanied by wisdom is reflection (<s>parivitarka</s>). Thorough examination is ascertainment (<s>parimīmāṃsā</s>). Thus [is stated] the own-nature of the path of meditation.

body.text: navadhā ca prakārataḥ /
body.translated_text: And ninefold by [its] varieties.

body.text: sa bhāvanāmārgaḥ prakārabhedena navadhā bhavati / cakārādvipakṣo navadhā / kathamityāha-
body.translated_text: That path of meditation, through the division of varieties, becomes ninefold. And by the word "and" (<s>ca</s>), the opposing [faults] are also ninefold. How? He says:

body.text: mṛdumadhyādhimātrāṇāṃ punarmṛdvādibhedataḥ // 4-54 //
body.translated_text: Through the further division of mild, middling, and intense into mild and so on. // 4-54 //

body.text: mṛdumṛduḥ / mṛdumadhyaḥ / mṛdvadhimātraḥ / madhyamṛduḥ / madhyamadhyaḥ / madhyadhimātraḥ / adhimātramṛduḥ / adhimātramadhyaḥ / adhimātrādhimātraśceti / vipakṣāṇāmapyeta eva nava prakārāḥ / tatraite mārgasya prakārā anulomamutpadyante / taiḥ pratilomaṃ vipakṣaprakārāḥ kṣīyante / adhimātrādhimātro 'dhimātramadhyo yāvanmṛdumṛduḥ / sa ca vipakṣo bhāvanāheyaḥ kleśavikalpā yathāyogām / audāriko hi malaścelātpurva niṣpīḍyate paścāsūkṣmaḥ / tadvaccittādapi /
body.translated_text: Mild-mild, mild-middling, mild-intense, middling-mild, middling-middling, middling-intense, intense-mild, intense-middling, and intense-intense. The opposing [faults] too have these same nine varieties. Among these, the varieties of the path arise in progressive order. By those, the varieties of the opposing [faults] are diminished in reverse order: intense-intense, intense-middling, down to mild-mild. And that opposing [factor] — the defilements and conceptualizations that are to be abandoned by meditation — [is diminished] accordingly. For the coarser dirt is squeezed out of a garment first, the subtler afterward. Likewise also from the mind.

body.text: tatrādyaḥ tathetyādinā / dvitīya evamityādinā / tataḥ yathā punaraparādibhīḥ prasavatyantaiḥ tataḥ dvāvekena punaraparādinā subhūtirāhetyataḥ prāk / tathetyādi / tatheti yathoktena krameṇa sampādayamānaḥ śamathena / upanidhyāyana vipaśyanayā / upaparīkṣamāṇa ubhābhyām / prayujyamānaḥ śamathavīryeṇa / ghaṭamāno vipaśyanāvīryeṇa / vyāyacchamāna ubhayavīryeṇa / svayameva bhagavān pṛcchati kiyatkarma karotīti / uttaraṃ svayamevāha tadyathāpītyādinā / prasādā prabhavantīti prāsādikā guṇāḥ / matvarthīyo 'c / paraparigṛhīteti parakīyā na vaśayen na śaknuyāt / saṃsārādityāgāmino janmaprabandhāt / chorayatīti tyajati / vipṛṣṭhīkaroti / āgāmino 'nāgamanāt / vyantīkarotītyaparāntataḥ pūrvāntanayanāt / yathājñaptamityādi pūrvavat / yathoddiṣṭaṃ yathā nirdiṣṭamityuddeśanāt / tiṣṭhati cintayā saṃśayacchedāt / śikṣate śamathena / pratipadyate vipaśyanayā / upanidhyāyatītyubhābhyām / evaṃ yogaṃ bhāvanāmāpadyate / iyatā ekaṃ karmoktam /
body.translated_text: There, the first [is stated] beginning with "thus" and so on. The second [beginning with] "in this way" and so on. Then, by [passages beginning with] "moreover" and so on, ending with "it generates"; then two [stages are stated] by one "moreover" passage, up to just before "<s>Subhūti</s> said." "Thus" and so on — "thus" means while accomplishing in the manner stated, through <s>śamatha</s> (calm). "Contemplating" — through <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight). "Examining" — through both. "Applying oneself" — through the effort of <s>śamatha</s>. "Striving" — through the effort of <s>vipaśyanā</s>. "Exerting" — through the effort of both. The <s>Bhagavān</s> himself asks, "How much action does he perform?" He himself gives the answer beginning with "just as" and so on. "Graces arise" (<s>prasādāḥ prabhavanti</s>) — meaning "praiseworthy qualities" (<s>prāsādikā guṇāḥ</s>). The suffix is in the sense of <s>matvartha</s>. "Appropriated by another" (<s>paraparigṛhītā</s>) means "belonging to another" — he cannot control, he cannot bring [them] under his power. "From <s>saṃsāra</s>" means from the continuity of births that are yet to come (<s>āgāmina</s>). "He cuts off" (<s>chorayati</s>) means he abandons, he turns his back on. "Of the future" — because of the non-coming of what is to come. "He brings to an end" (<s>vyantīkaroti</s>) — because of bringing the future into conformity with the past. "As instructed" and so on — as before. "As indicated, as explained" — because of indication. "He abides" — through reflection, because of cutting through doubt. "He trains" — through <s>śamatha</s>. "He practices" — through <s>vipaśyanā</s>. "He contemplates" — through both. "Thus he enters into the practice of meditation." By this much, one action has been stated.

body.text: dvitīyamāha tāṃścetyādinā samyaksambodherityetadantena / iti bhāvanāmārgo mṛdumṛduḥ //
body.translated_text: He states the second beginning with "and those" and so on, ending with "for perfect awakening" (<s>samyaksambodhi</s>). Thus, the mild-mild path of meditation.

body.text: evamityādi evamityanantaroktavat / tāvatkarmeti bahutarakalpavyantīkaraṇam / samyaksambodhivinivartakadoṣavivarjanaṃ ca / adhikamāha
body.translated_text: "In this way" and so on — "in this way" means as just stated. "That much action" (<s>tāvat karma</s>) means the bringing to an end of many more <s>kalpas</s> (aeons). And the avoidance of faults that would cause turning back from perfect awakening. In addition he says

body.text: yathetyādinā prāk punaraparāt / tata iti dāyakāt / ayameva viśiṣyate bahutarapuṇyatayā prakṛṣyate / ityata āha / yoyamityādi / iti bhāvanāmārgo mṛdumadhyaḥ //
body.translated_text: beginning with "that which" and so on, up to before the next "moreover." "From that" means from the donor. "This very one is distinguished" — he excels through greater merit. Therefore he says: "whoever this" and so on. Thus, the mild-middling path of meditation.

body.text: punarityādi / dadyādarpaṇataḥ / pratiṣṭhāpayedavipratisārataḥ / iti bhāvanāmārgo mṛddhadhimātraḥ //
body.translated_text: "Moreover" and so on. "He would give" — because of offering. "He would establish" — because of absence of regret. Thus, the mild-intense path of meditation.

body.text: punarityādi / manasikāro vihāraḥ / iti bhāvanāmārgo madhyamṛduḥ //
body.translated_text: "Moreover" and so on. "Mental attention" (<s>manasikāra</s>) is the mode of abiding (<s>vihāra</s>). Thus, the middling-mild path of meditation.

body.text: punarityādinā bhāvanāmārgo madhyamadhyaḥ //
body.translated_text: By "moreover" and so on — the middling-middling path of meditation.

body.text: punarityādi / vyutthāya dharma deśayet tacca bodhau pariṇāmayediti bhāvanāmārgo madhyādhimātraḥ //
body.translated_text: "Moreover" and so on. "Having emerged [from meditation], one should teach the <s>Dharma</s>, and that [merit] should be dedicated toward awakening" — thus, the middling-intense path of meditation.

body.text: punaraparetyādi / tacca dharmadānaṃ / prajñāpāramitoktena pariṇāmena pariṇāmayediti bhāvanāmārgo 'dhimātramṛduḥ //
body.translated_text: "Moreover" and so on. And that is the gift of <s>Dharma</s>. "One should dedicate with the dedication taught in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>" — thus, the intense-mild path of meditation.

body.text: punarityādi / taddharmadānaṃ prajñāpāramitoktapariṇāmena pariṇamayya punaḥ pratisaṃlayane yogamāpadyate / iti bhāvanāmārgo 'dhimātramadhyaḥ //
body.translated_text: "Moreover" and so on. Having dedicated that gift of <s>Dharma</s> with the dedication taught in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, one again enters into the practice of meditative absorption (<s>pratisaṃlayana</s>). Thus, the intense-middling path of meditation.

body.text: yaḥ punastat pratisaṃlayanamavirahitaṃ karoti prajñāpāramitayā sa tasya bhāvanāmārgo 'dhimātrādhimātraḥ //
body.translated_text: Whoever, moreover, makes that meditative absorption inseparable from <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> — that is the intense-intense path of meditation.

body.text: subhūtirāhetyādi / iha bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavatīti bāhulyenoktam / ataḥ subhūteścodyam / abhisaṃskāro vikalpaḥ / tadvatpuṇyābhisaṃskāropi / tasmādvahutaraṃ puṇyamiti bahutaro vikalpa uktaḥ syāditi / uttaraṃ bhagavānāha sopītyādinā prasavatyantena / idānīmiti bhāvanāmārgakāle / yathālakṣaṇamasattvācchūnyaḥ / ajñātārthe kapratyayaḥ / bālairajñātaḥ śūnyaka ityeva / evameva ākhyāti prakhyātīti ākhyaḥ / anākhye ākhyā bhavati ākhyāyate lohitāderākṛtigaṇatvāt kyaṣ / prakhyātītyarthaḥ / evamuttareṣvapi draṣṭavyam / asvāmikatvād riktaḥ / agrāhyatvāt tucchaḥ / grāhakābhāvatvād asaraḥ / evamiti śūnyatādibhiḥ / śeṣaṃ subodham / iti bahutaraṃpuṇyaṃprasavacodyaparihārau //
body.translated_text: "<s>Subhūti</s> said" and so on. "Here, one generates more merit" — this has been said with emphasis. Therefore <s>Subhūti</s> raises the objection. "Fabrication" (<s>abhisaṃskāra</s>) is conceptualization. Likewise, "meritorious fabrication" (<s>puṇyābhisaṃskāra</s>) [is also conceptualization]. Therefore, "one generates more merit" amounts to saying "one generates more conceptualization" — thus [the objection]. The answer is given by the <s>Bhagavān</s> beginning with "that too" and so on, ending with "it generates." "Now" (<s>idānīm</s>) means at the time of the path of meditation. "Empty" — because of not existing according to its [imagined] characteristic. The <s>ka</s>-suffix is in the sense of "unknown" (<s>ajñāta</s>). "Unknown by the childish" — meaning "empty" indeed. "In this way" (<s>evam</s>) — it "speaks forth" (<s>ākhyāti</s>), it "shines forth" (<s>prakhyāti</s>); hence "<s>ākhya</s>." "In the inexpressible" (<s>anākhye</s>), "it speaks" (<s>ākhyā bhavati</s>) — it "is spoken of" (<s>ākhyāyate</s>); the <s>kyaṣ</s> suffix [is used] because of belonging to the <s>lohitādi ākṛtigaṇa</s>. The meaning is: "it becomes manifest." The same should be understood in the subsequent [cases] as well. "Ownerless" (<s>asvāmikatva</s>) — hence "empty" (<s>rikta</s>). "Ungraspable" (<s>agrāhyatva</s>) — hence "vain" (<s>tuccha</s>). "Absence of a grasper" (<s>grāhakābhāva</s>) — hence "without essence" (<s>asāra</s>). "Thus" (<s>evam</s>) means by emptiness and the like. The rest is easily understood. Thus, the objection regarding the generation of greater merit and its resolution.

body.text: subhūtirāhetyādi / utkarṣopi viśeṣaḥ / chedopi nānākaraṇam / tayorvyavacchedārthamubhayorupādānam / pramāṇānītyaudāryaparicchedāḥ / saṃkhyayāpīti gaṇanayāpi na kṣapayituṃ kṣayaṃ netum / syābhdagavannityādi sugamam / adhikaṃ vacanaṃ adhivacanaṃ mukhyaṃ vācakamityarthaḥ / akṣayā apīti
body.translated_text: "<s>Subhūti</s> said" and so on. "Superiority" (<s>utkarṣa</s>) is also distinction (<s>viśeṣa</s>). "Division" (<s>cheda</s>) is also differentiation (<s>nānākaraṇa</s>). In order to distinguish between the two, both are mentioned. "Measures" (<s>pramāṇāni</s>) are the delimitations of extent. "Not even by enumeration" (<s>saṃkhyayā api</s>) — not even by calculation can it be exhausted, brought to an end. "O <s>Bhagavān</s>" and so on — easily understood. "<s>Adhivacana</s>" (designation) means the primary designator — this is the meaning. "Inexhaustible too" —

body.text: ākāśavat / aprameyātāpītyākāśasyeva / akṣayāprameyaśūnyatānimittādīnāṃ abhilāpāḥ śabdāḥ / nanu śabdā api vicatrāḥ kathamekārthe vyavacchedyabhedyaleśāditi bhāvaḥ / ata evāha deśanābhinirhāra eṣa iti / deśyate 'nayeti deśanā karuṇā tasyābhinirhāro niḥṣyandaḥ sa cāsau nirdeśaśca / atra śāstram-
body.translated_text: like space. "Immeasurable too" — like space itself. The "expressions" (<s>abhilāpāḥ</s>) of the inexhaustible, immeasurable emptiness, signlessness, and the rest are words (<s>śabdāḥ</s>). "But are not the words too diverse? How [can there be] distinction and division in one meaning?" — this is the import. Therefore he says: "This is the accomplishment of teaching" (<s>deśanābhinirhāra</s>). "Teaching" (<s>deśanā</s>) is compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), that by which one teaches. Its "accomplishment" (<s>abhinirhāra</s>) is its outflow (<s>niḥṣyanda</s>); and that is also exposition (<s>nirdeśa</s>). Here the treatise [states]:

children.translated_text: "The expositions of the innumerable and so on are not tenable ultimately;
they are the outflow of compassion, accepted conventionally by the sage." // 4-55 //

body.text: 'na kṣamā' iti na yuktāḥ / ityasaṃkhyeyādinirdeśe codyaparihārāḥ //
body.translated_text: "Not tenable" (<s>na kṣamāḥ</s>) means not logically justified. Thus, the objection and resolution regarding the exposition of the innumerable and so on.

body.text: subhūtihāha / āścaryamityādyapi tu khalvityataḥ prāk / avāggocaratvād anabhilāpyāḥ / pāramitārthasyeti śūnyatālakṣaṇasya / atra śāstram-
body.translated_text: "<s>Subhūti</s> said" — "How wonderful!" and so on, up to before "but indeed." Because of being beyond the reach of speech, [they are] inexpressible (<s>anabhilāpya</s>). "Of the meaning of the <s>pāramitā</s>" means of the characteristic of emptiness. Here the treatise [states]:

children.translated_text: "Decrease and increase are not logically possible for a thing that is beyond words;
by what is there decrease in what is called "meditation," and by what has [anything] arisen?" // 4-56 //

body.text: ityanabhilāpyasya hānivṛddhyabhāvaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus, the absence of decrease and increase for the inexpressible.

body.text: kathaṃ tarhi bodhirityata āha / api tu khalvityādyāparivartasamāpteḥ / sa dānaṃ dadattānmanasikārāṃstāṃścittotpāniti yairdānaṃ dadāti / tāni ca kuśalamūlānīti yāni taiscittotpādaiḥ saṃprayuktāni / yathā bodhisthā pariṇāmayatīti / anyathā na sā pariṇāmanā bodhaye syāt / evamuttarāsvapi draṣṭavyam //
body.translated_text: "How then is awakening?" — to this he says: "But indeed" and so on, up to the end of the chapter. "He gives the gift" — by those mental attentions and those mind-generations by which he gives the gift. "And those wholesome roots" — those that are conjoined with those mind-generations. "Just as awakening is, so he dedicates" — otherwise that dedication would not be for the sake of awakening. The same should be understood in the subsequent [cases] as well.

body.text: yathānuttarā samyaksambodhirityuktam / ataḥ pṛcchati / atha khalvityādinā / bhagavānāha tathataiṣā subhūte 'nuttarā samyaksambodhirityādi / abhīkṣṇamiti punaḥ punaḥ / bahulamiti prabandhane / evaṃ khalvityādinopasaṃhāraḥ / atra śāstram-
body.translated_text: "As <s>anuttarā samyaksambodhi</s> (unsurpassed perfect awakening)" — this has been said. Therefore he asks, beginning with "Now then" and so on. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "<s>Tathatā</s> (suchness), O <s>Subhūti</s>, is <s>anuttarā samyaksambodhi</s>" and so on. "Continuously" (<s>abhīkṣṇam</s>) means again and again. "Abundantly" (<s>bahulam</s>) means in an unbroken series. "Thus indeed" and so on is the conclusion. Here the treatise [states]:

body.text: yathā bodhistathaivāsāviṣṭasyāthaisya sādhakaḥ /
body.translated_text: "Just as awakening is, so is this [path]; and this is the accomplisher of that [awakening].

body.text: tathatālakṣaṇā bodhiḥ sopi tallakṣaṇo mataḥ // 4-57 //
body.translated_text: Awakening has the characteristic of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), and that [path] too is considered to have that [same] characteristic." // 4-57 //

body.text: 'asau' iti 'sopi' iti bhāvanāmārgaḥ //
body.translated_text: "This" (<s>asau</s>) and "that too" (<s>sa api</s>) refer to the path of meditation (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>).

body.text: śūnyatāpradhānaḥ parivartaḥ śūnyatāparivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: The chapter in which emptiness is predominant is the "Chapter on Emptiness" (<s>Śūnyatā-parivarta</s>).

body.text: āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ sāratamānāmni pañjikāyāṃ ratnākaraśāntiviracitāyāmaṣṭādaśaḥ parivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: End of the eighteenth chapter in the <s>Pañjikā</s> commentary named <s>Sāratama</s>, composed by <s>Ratnākaraśānti</s>, on the Noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

body.text: 19. gaṅgadevābhaginīparivarto nāmekonaviṃśatitamaḥ /
body.translated_text: 19. The nineteenth [chapter] is named the "<s>Gaṅgadevābhaginī-parivarta</s>" (Chapter on the Sister of the River-Goddess <s>Gaṅgā</s>).

body.text: atha khalvityādi prāgevamuktāt / na pūrveṇa cittena bodhirna ca paścimena tayorasamavadhānāditi codyam //
body.translated_text: "Now then" and so on, up to before "thus spoken." "Awakening is not [attained] by the prior mind, nor by the subsequent one, because of their non-conjunction" — this is the objection.

body.text: evamukta ityādi prāgevamuktāt / iyatā dīpadṛṣṭāntena parihāraḥ / atra śāstram-
body.translated_text: "Thus spoken" and so on, up to before "thus spoken." By this much, the resolution is through the lamp-analogy. Here the treatise [states]:

body.text: pūrveṇa bodhirno yuktā manasā paścimena vā /
body.translated_text: "Awakening is not logically possible by the prior mind, nor by the subsequent one"

body.text: iti codyam /
body.translated_text: — this is the objection.

body.text: dīpadṛṣṭāntayogena
body.translated_text: "By the application of the lamp-analogy,"

body.text: bodhiriti vartate / anena parihāraḥ //
body.translated_text: "awakening" — this continues. By this is the resolution.

body.text: atha śāstram-
body.translated_text: Then the treatise [states]:

body.text: gambhīrā dharmatāṣṭadhā // 4-58 //
body.translated_text: "The profundity of <s>dharmatā</s> (the nature of reality) is eightfold." // 4-58 //

body.text: yā bodhiriti vartate / kevalāyā bodhestathataiva lakṣaṇamuktamaṣṭādaśe / saparicchadāyāstu bodherlakṣaṇamaṣṭavidhaṃ gāmbhīryam / tatkathamaṣṭadhā?
body.translated_text: "Which is awakening" — this continues. The characteristic of awakening alone, [taken] by itself, has been stated as <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) in the eighteenth [chapter]. But the characteristic of awakening together with its accompaniments is the eightfold profundity (<s>gāmbhīrya</s>). How is it eightfold?

children.text: utpāde ca nirodhe ca tathatāyāṃ gabhīratā /
children.translated_text: "Profundity in arising and in cessation, and in <s>tathatā</s> (suchness),
in the knowable and in knowledge, in practice, in non-duality, and in skill in means." // 4-59 //

body.text: 'advayaṃ ca upāyakauśalyaṃ ca; iti samāhāradvandvaḥ / ata evamukta ityādinā prāgevamuktādgāmbhīrya subhūtiḥ prastauti / anyatra tebhya iti vinā tebhyaḥ / evamukte bhagavānityādinā parijayaṃ karotītyetadantenāṣṭavidhaṃ gāmbhīryamāha / yaccittamiti bhrāntamabhūtaparikalpātmakam / niruddhamiti santānakṣayāt kṣīṇam / no hīti naivetyarthaḥ / bhrāntikāraṇasya dvayābhiniveśasya kṣayāditi bhāvaḥ / ityutpādagāmbhīryam //
body.translated_text: 'Non-duality and skillful means' — this is a collective compound (<s>samāhāra-dvandva</s>). Therefore, by 'Thus spoken' and so on, preceding the [passage on] profundity already stated, <s>Subhūti</s> introduces [it]. '<s>Anyatra tebhyaḥ</s>' means 'apart from those.' By '<s>Bhagavān</s>, when thus spoken' and so on, ending with 'familiarizes' — he states the eightfold profundity. 'That which is mind' — [means] the erroneous, having the nature of false imagination (<s>abhūtaparikalpa</s>). 'Ceased' — destroyed through the exhaustion of the continuum. '<s>No hi</s>' means 'not at all' — this is the meaning. Because of the destruction of the grasping at duality, which is the cause of error — this is the import. Thus [this is] the profundity of arising.

body.text: yaccittamutpannamiti abhrāntam / bhrāntikṣayāccittādhīnatvācca cittotpatteriti bhāvaḥ / nirodhadharmi bhagavanniti pratikṣaṇamiti bhāvaḥ / nirotsyata iti santānanirodheneti bhāvaḥ / no hīdamiti svarasata utpatteḥ praṇidhānādibhiśca saviśeṣamakṣayīkṛtatvāditi bhāvaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'That which is mind that has arisen' — [means] the non-erroneous. Because of the cessation of error and because the arising of mind is dependent on mind — this is the import. '<s>Bhagavān</s>, it is of the nature of cessation' — [means] moment by moment — this is the import. 'It will cease' — through the cessation of the continuum — this is the import. '<s>No hi</s>' (not indeed) — because it arises naturally, and because through aspiration (<s>praṇidhāna</s>) and the rest it has been rendered especially inexhaustible — this is the import.

body.text: yaccittamanutpannarmityutpādagāmbhīrye yaduktam yanna nirodhadharmītyanantarameva yaduktaṃ yannirodhadharmītyasmiṃsteṣāṃ punaruktatā syāt / yaccittamiti yaccittasantānaḥ / anutpādānirodhadharmītyanādinidhanam yo dharma iti nirvāṇākhyaḥ / nirodhoniruddham / tatsvabhāvo 'syeti svabhāvaniruddhaḥ / dharmateti śūnyatā / iti nirodhagāmbhīryam /
body.translated_text: 'That which is mind that is unarisen' — [now,] in the profundity of arising, what was stated as 'it is not of the nature of cessation,' and immediately after what was stated as 'it is of the nature of cessation' — in [this passage], there would be repetition of those. 'That which is mind' means 'that which is the continuum of mind.' 'Of the nature of non-arising and non-ceasing' — that which is beginningless and endless, the <s>dharma</s> called <s>nirvāṇa</s>. '<s>Nirodha</s>' means that which has ceased. 'Having that as its own nature' — hence 'ceased by own nature.' '<s>Dharmatā</s>' means <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness). Thus [this is] the profundity of cessation.

body.text: tathaiva sthāsyatīti yāvadākāśam / mā kuṭasthā bhūditi tathatāvat / no hīdamiti pravāhanityatvāditi bhāvaḥ / gambhīrā tathateti samyagjñānādapi sūkṣmatvāditayatāgāmbhīryam //
body.translated_text: 'It will remain just so' — extending as far as space. 'Lest it become immutable' — [extending] as far as <s>tathatā</s> (suchness). '<s>No hi</s>' — because of the permanence of the stream — this is the import. 'Profound is <s>tathatā</s>' — because of subtlety even compared to correct knowledge, [this is] the profundity of <s>tathatā</s>.

body.text: tathatāyāṃ cittamiti tadveditvāttasyā ādheyam / no hīdamiti jñānābhdede vedyatvāyogāt / cittaṃ tathatetyekalakṣaṇāditi bhāvaḥ / anyattathatāyā ilikṣaṇabhedādeva / no hīdamiti lakṣaṇabhedepi tādātmyāt / tadevamagrāhyatvepi vedyā tathateti jñeyagāmbhīryam //
body.translated_text: 'Mind in <s>tathatā</s>' — because mind knows that [tathatā], it is its content. '<s>No hi</s>' — because in the non-difference of knowledge, [tathatā] cannot be an object of cognition. 'Mind is <s>tathatā</s>' — because of the single characteristic — this is the import. 'It is other than <s>tathatā</s>' — precisely because of the difference in characteristics. '<s>No hi</s>' — because even though the characteristics differ, there is identity. Thus, although it is ungraspable, <s>tathatā</s> is knowable — [this is] the profundity of the knowable.

body.text: samanupaśyasi tvamiti cittarūpam / no hītyagrāhyatvāt / tadeva grāhyamapi cittaṃ vettīti jñānagāmbhīryam //
body.translated_text: 'Do you see?' — [refers to] the form of mind. '<s>No hi</s>' — because of its ungraspability. That very mind, though graspable, knows — [this is] the profundity of knowledge.

body.text: gambhīre caratīti prajñāpāramitārthe / samudācārā ālambananimittāni / pravartante na bhavanti / na samudācaranti na prakhyāntīti caryāgāmbhīryam //
body.translated_text: 'Practices in the profound' — in the meaning of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>. '<s>Samudācāras</s>' are the objects and signs [that serve as supports]. 'They operate, they do not exist.' 'They do not present themselves, they do not manifest' — [this is] the profundity of practice.

body.text: nimitte caratīti dvayanimitte 'dvayanimitte vā / no hīti na dvayanimitte nādvayanimitte / nimittamiti dvayādvayanimittam / avibhāvitamaprahīṇam / no hīti nāprahīṇam / prahīṇamevetyarthaḥ / ityadvayagāmbhīryam //
body.translated_text: 'Practices in signs' — in the sign of duality or the sign of non-duality. '<s>No hi</s>' — neither in the sign of duality nor in the sign of non-duality. 'Sign' means the sign of duality and non-duality. '<s>Avibhāvitam</s>' (not discerned), '<s>aprahīṇam</s>' (not abandoned). '<s>No hi</s>' — it is not not-abandoned; it is indeed abandoned — this is the meaning. Thus [this is] the profundity of non-duality.

body.text: api nviti kinnu / nimittaṃ vibhāvitaṃ bhavatītyapratipūrṇeṣu sarvabuddhadharmeṣu iti bhāvaḥ / subhūtiruttaramāha / na sa bhagavannityadinā / ihaiveti / asminneva janmani / kuta ityāha / sa cedityādi / śrāvako bhavaediti na samyaksambuddhaḥ / etattadityādinopasaṃhāraḥ / yallakṣaṇaṃ yannimittamiti yaddharmanimittaṃ yacca dharmatānimittaṃ tatsarvaṃ jānāti / parijayamabhyāsamātraṃ karoti / ityupāyakauśalagāmbhīryam //
body.translated_text: '<s>Api nu</s>' means 'is it the case that?' 'The sign has been discerned' — [this implies] 'while all <s>Buddha</s>-qualities are not yet fulfilled' — this is the import. <s>Subhūti</s> gives the answer: 'Not so, <s>Bhagavān</s>' and so on. '<s>Ihaiva</s>' means 'in this very birth.' 'How so?' — he says '<s>Sa cet</s>' and so on. 'He would become a <s>Śrāvaka</s>' — and not a <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> (Perfectly Awakened One). By 'This very' and so on, the conclusion [is given]. 'That which is the characteristic, that which is the sign' — means 'that which is the sign of <s>dharmas</s> and that which is the sign of <s>dharmatā</s>' — he knows all of that. 'He familiarizes' — [means] mere practice. Thus [this is] the profundity of skillful means.

body.text: tatrāṣṭamaṃ gāmbhīryaṃ viprakṛṣṭam / bodhe śeṣāṇi sannikṛṣṭānītyuktavidhaṃ gāmbhīryam / uktaśca 'śaikṣau'vaivartiko gaṇaḥ' //
body.translated_text: Therein, the eighth profundity is remote — in [relation to] awakening. The remaining [seven] are proximate — thus the profundity has been stated in the manner described. And it has been stated: 'The learner and the irreversible assembly.'

body.text: 'samatā bhavaśāntyoḥ' vaktavyā / ataḥ śāstram-
body.translated_text: 'The equality of existence and quiescence' is to be stated. Therefore the treatise [states] —

body.text: svapnopamatvāddharmāṇāṃ bhavaśāntyorakalpanā /
body.translated_text: 'Because all <s>dharmas</s> are dream-like, there is no conceptualization of existence and quiescence.'

body.text: eṣa saṃsāra etannirvāṇamiti bhedakalpanā / saṃsāranirvāṇayoḥ samatājñānaṃ bhāvanāmārge / svapnopamānsarvadharmān paśyatastayorbhedakānupalambhāt / nanvabhūtaparikalpaḥ saṃsāraḥ sa ca bhrāntimātraṃ bhrāntikṣayastu nirvāṇam / kadā tayoḥ samatājñānam? bhāvanāmārge saṃmukhībhūte sarvadharmanairātmyasaṃvedanāditi cet / darśanamārgepyetadastīti bhāvanāmārgasya ko 'tiśayaḥ? tasmāttato vyutthitasya samatājñānaṃ grāhyam / taccāyuktam / vyutthitasya hi jñānaṃ bhrāntaṃ svapnopamatvāt svapnaḥ / bhāvanāmārgastu samyagjñānaṃ divasopamatvāddivasaḥ / tatra kadā yuktaṃ syāt? yadi daivasikādabhyāsātiśayāt, svapneti prajñāpāramitā vivardheta / ataḥ sūtre 'tha khalvityādinā vivardhata ityetadantena praśnaḥ / subhūtirāhetyādinā bhāvitavyontenottaram / avikalpa iti / vikalpo viśeṣaḥ / avikalpo nirviśeṣaḥ / prajñāpāramitābhyāsata iti bhāvanāmārgābhyāsataḥ / iti saṃsāranirvāṇasamatā //
body.translated_text: 'This is <s>saṃsāra</s>, this is <s>nirvāṇa</s>' — such conceptualization of difference [is negated]. The knowledge of the equality of <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s> is [found] in the <s>bhāvanā-mārga</s> (path of cultivation) — for one who sees all <s>dharmas</s> as dream-like, because there is no apprehension of a distinction between those two. Objection: False imagination (<s>abhūtaparikalpa</s>) is <s>saṃsāra</s>, and that is merely error; the cessation of error is <s>nirvāṇa</s>. When [then does] the knowledge of equality of those two [arise]? If one says: 'On the <s>bhāvanā-mārga</s>, when it becomes directly present, through the realization of the selflessness of all <s>dharmas</s>' — [the reply is:] this exists on the <s>darśana-mārga</s> (path of seeing) too, so what is the superiority of the <s>bhāvanā-mārga</s>? Therefore the knowledge of equality should be understood as belonging to one who has emerged from [samādhi]. But that is incorrect. For the knowledge of one who has emerged is erroneous, being dream-like — it is a dream. But the <s>bhāvanā-mārga</s> is correct knowledge, being day-like — it is daytime. When then would [the equality] be appropriate? If through the superiority of practice in the daytime, the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, which is the 'dream,' would increase. Therefore in the <s>sūtra</s>, by 'Now then' and so on, ending with 'increases' — the question [is posed]. <s>Subhūti</s> gives the answer with 'should cultivate' and so on. '<s>Avikalpa</s>' — '<s>vikalpa</s>' means distinction; '<s>avikalpa</s>' means without distinction. 'Through the practice of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>' means through the practice of the <s>bhāvanā-mārga</s>. Thus [this is] the equality of <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: śāriputra āhetyādi / iha svapnaśabdena svapna evocyate / kṣayasaṃjñeti kṣayo nirvāṇaṃ tasya saṃjñā udgrahaḥ / bhutārthakalpanaṃ kalpaḥ / vitathakalpanaṃ vikalpaḥ / evameveti / ākāśavattathāgatavadvā / cittaṃ cetanā buddhirvikalpaḥ ityeko 'rthaḥ / viviktānīti niḥsvabhāvāni / viplutā hi buddhiravidyamānameva nimittīkṛtyārambaṇī karoti / cetanāpītyādi sugamam / kāyasākṣīti kāya āśrayaḥ / tatparāvṛttyā kāyena sākṣātkārī kāyasākṣī enamarthamityetaccodyaṃ visarjayiṣyatīti parihariṣyati / ajito maitreya iti paryāyau / yo dharmo visarjayediti maitreyaḥ / visarjayitavya iti praśnaḥ / yena dharmeṇeti vācā / yasya dharmasyeti śāriputrasya / utpitsuḥ trāsa uttrāsaḥ / saṃbhūtastrāsaḥ santrāsaḥ / tasya pravāhaḥ santrāsāpattiḥ / balādhānaṃ bhāvanā balavāsanā / atra śāstram-
body.translated_text: '<s>Śāriputra</s> said' and so on. Here, by the word 'dream,' a dream itself is meant. '<s>Kṣayasaṃjñā</s>' — '<s>kṣaya</s>' is <s>nirvāṇa</s>; its '<s>saṃjñā</s>' is apprehension. '<s>Kalpa</s>' is conceptualization of the real. '<s>Vikalpa</s>' is conceptualization of the unreal. '<s>Evameva</s>' means 'likewise' — like space, or like the <s>Tathāgata</s>. 'Mind, volition, cognition, conceptualization' — these are synonymous. '<s>Viviktāni</s>' means devoid of own-nature. For deluded cognition, taking as real what does not exist, makes it an object. 'Volition too' and so on — this is easily understood. '<s>Kāyasākṣī</s>' — '<s>kāya</s>' means the basis (<s>āśraya</s>). By the transformation of that [basis], one who directly realizes through the body is a '<s>kāyasākṣī</s>' (bodily witness). 'This matter' — this objection he will resolve, i.e., he will answer. <s>Ajita</s> and <s>Maitreya</s> are synonyms. 'The <s>dharma</s> that would resolve' — [refers to] <s>Maitreya</s>. 'Should be resolved' — this is the question. 'By which <s>dharma</s>' — by speech. 'Of which <s>dharma</s>' — of <s>Śāriputra's</s> [question]. '<s>Utpitsu</s>' (ready to spring up) — the fright is '<s>uttrāsa</s>.' The fright that has arisen is '<s>santrāsa</s>.' Its continuation is '<s>santrāsāpatti</s>' (falling into fright). '<s>Balādhāna</s>' is cultivation, the impression of strength. Herein the treatise [states] —

body.text: karmābhāvādicodyānāṃ parihārā yathoditāḥ // 4-60 //
body.translated_text: 'The resolutions of objections beginning with the non-existence of action, as stated.' // 4-60 //

body.text: iti saṃsāranirvāṇasamatāyāṃ codyaparihārāḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus [conclude] the objections and resolutions regarding the equality of <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: 'kṛtiśuddhiranuttarā' vaktavyā / ataḥ śāstram-
body.translated_text: 'The unsurpassed purification of action' is to be stated. Therefore the treatise [states] —

children.translated_text: 'Whatever purification of the world of beings [exists], through the offering of that purification,
likewise [comes] the purification of the container-world, the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field).' // 4-61 //

body.text: ekadā yatraika eva buddho jāyate tadbuddhakṣetram / tasya śuddhatā pariśuddhiḥ / sā kuto bhavati? 'sattvalokasya' dṛśyate 'yāśuddhiḥ' vyāḍakāntārāditā / tasyāḥ svabuddhakṣetrapariśuddhādupasaṃhārāt / mama buddhakṣetre sarvathaivaṃ mā bhūditi / eṣā vistareṇa mahatyoruktā / iha tu saṃkṣepataḥ / punaraparamityādinā atha khalu tatretyataḥ prāk / uttrāsādiniṣedha ukto vaktavyaśca tadapekṣayā punaraparaśabdāḥ / durgatā bhūmiḥ kāntāram / vyāḍaiḥ kāntāraṃ vyāḍakāntāram pānīyavarjitakāntāraṃ pānīyakāntāram / yadicecchabdo yadyarthe / divyopabhogetyādi / samabuddhakṣetrasattvā iti vartate / rudhirādyāhāravyudāsāya caitaduktam / sarvasvaparityāga eva kuśalam / yadeteṣāṃ loka iti bhājanaloke sukhasamaṅgilaḥ / sukhaṃ samarpitamāhitameṣāmiti sukhasamarpitāḥ / sarvata iti sarvatra / vyādhikāntāraṃ rogopasargaḥ / iyatīti cittakṣaṇaparimāṇā / apūrveti bhāvinī / yadutākoṭīriti nahi niraṃśasya kṣaṇasya koṭirasti / yā setyarthā(tyapūrvā) bhut / apūrvā koṭīryatrābhisaṃbhotsye / iti buddhakṣetrapariśuddhiḥ //
body.translated_text: That in which at one time a single <s>Buddha</s> is born — that is a <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field). Its purification is its complete purity. Whence does that arise? 'Whatever impurity of the world of beings is seen' — such as wilderness infested with wild beasts and the like — through the bringing-together from the purification of one's own buddha-field: 'May such things never exist at all in my buddha-field.' This is stated in detail in the two great [texts]. Here, [it is stated] in brief. From 'Moreover' up to just before 'Now then, there.' The prohibition of fright and the rest, which was stated and is still to be stated — in reference to that, the words '<s>punarapara</s>' [occur]. A desolate region (<s>durgatā bhūmi</s>) is a wasteland. A wasteland with wild beasts is a '<s>vyāḍakāntāra</s>'; a wasteland without water is a '<s>pānīyakāntāra</s>.' '<s>Yadiccha</s>' — the word '<s>iccha</s>' is in the sense of 'if.' 'With divine enjoyments' and so forth — it is understood that the beings of the buddha-field are equal [in this respect]. This is stated to exclude food consisting of blood and the like. The relinquishment of everything is itself the wholesome. 'Their world' means in the container-world, [they are] endowed with happiness. 'Happiness is conferred, bestowed upon them' — hence '<s>sukhasamarpitāḥ</s>.' '<s>Sarvataḥ</s>' means 'everywhere.' '<s>Vyādhikāntāra</s>' means affliction by disease. '<s>Iyatī</s>' means 'measured by a mind-moment.' '<s>Apūrvā</s>' means 'future.' '<s>Yadutākoṭīḥ</s>' — for indeed there is no limit to a partless moment. 'That which' — [means] that unprecedented [limit]. 'The unprecedented limit at which I shall fully awaken.' Thus [this is] the purification of the buddha-field.

body.text: atha khalvityādyāparivartāntāt / anena yattasyāṃ deśanāyāṃ saṃvṛttaṃ tadāha / asaktāni alagnāni / antarikṣe vihāyasīti kevala evākāśe / pariniṣpattiriva pariniṣpattirvaśībhāvaḥ / pramāṇabaddhaḥ pramāṇaniyataḥ / asātakāntārāṇi duṣkāntārāṇi / śeṣaṃ subodham //
body.translated_text: 'Now then' and so on, up to the end of the chapter. By this, he states what occurred in that teaching. '<s>Asaktāni</s>' means unattached. '<s>Antarikṣe vihāyasi</s>' means in empty space alone. '<s>Pariniṣpatti</s>' means mastery, like [the word] <s>pariniṣpatti</s>. '<s>Pramāṇabaddha</s>' means delimited by measure. '<s>Asātakāntārāṇi</s>' means unpleasant wastelands. The rest is easily understood.

body.text: gaṅgadevābhaginyā lakṣitaḥ parivartastatparivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: The chapter is marked by <s>Gaṅgādevā</s>, the sister — hence that chapter [is so named].

body.text: āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ sāratamānāmni pañjikāyāṃ ratnākaraśāntiviracitāyāmekonaviṃśatitamaḥ parivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: In the <s>Pañjikā</s> commentary named <s>Sāratamā</s>, composed by <s>Ratnākaraśānti</s>, on the noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s> — this is the nineteenth chapter.

body.text: 20. upāyakauśalyamīmāṃsāparivarto nāma viṃśatitamaḥ /
body.translated_text: 20. The chapter named '<s>Upāyakauśalya-mīmāṃsā-parivarta</s>' (Investigation of Skillful Means) is the twentieth.

body.text: kṣetrapariśuddhiruktā / upāyakauśalaṃ vaktavyam / ataḥ śāstram-
body.translated_text: The purification of the buddha-field has been stated. Skillful means (<s>upāyakauśala</s>) is to be explained. Therefore the treatise [states] —

children.translated_text: 'Its domain and its practice, the overcoming of enemies,
non-abiding, [proceeding] in accordance with the target, and having an uncommon characteristic,' // 4-62 //
'unattached and non-apprehending, acting through signs and aspiration,
its indication, and the immeasurable — [thus] skillful means is tenfold.' // 4-63 //

body.text: asya hyupāyakauśalasya 'viṣayaḥ' sūtre prathamaṃ vaktavyaḥ / tataḥ'prayogaḥ' prathamābhyāsaḥ / tato daśa prabhedāḥ sā (śā)travātikramādayaḥ / 'nimittapraṇidhikṛtau' tābhyāmiti tathoktau nimittakṛtaḥ praṇidhikṛtaśca /
body.translated_text: For the 'domain' of this skillful means is to be stated first in the <s>sūtra</s>. Then the 'practice' — the initial familiarization. Then the ten divisions beginning with 'overcoming of enemies' and so on. 'Acting through signs and aspiration' — by these two [there are] the one acting through signs and the one acting through aspiration — thus they are so stated.

body.text: atha khalvityādi / atrādau bhūtakoṭimityetadantena viṣaya uktaḥ / śūnyatāsamādhinaivānimittāpraṇihitayorbodhipakṣādīnāṃ copalakṣaṇāt / śūnyatāyāmiti śūnyatāsamādhau / santatiḥ pravāhaḥ / kathaṃ pratyavekṣamāṇa ityāha rūpaṃ śunyamitīti / tāmiti śūnyatām / dharmatāmiti dharmaprakṛtim / dharmatayeti dharmasāratayā / bhūtakoṭiriti śūnyataiva kaivalyaṃ gatā bhūtakoṭiḥ / ityupāyakauśalasya viṣayaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Now then' and so on. Here, first, by [the passage] ending with '<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>' (the limit of reality), the domain is stated — because <s>śūnyatā-samādhi</s> (concentration on emptiness) implies <s>ānimitta</s> (signlessness) and <s>apraṇihita</s> (wishlessness), as well as the <s>bodhipakṣas</s> (factors of awakening) and the rest. 'In <s>śūnyatā</s>' means in the <s>śūnyatā-samādhi</s>. '<s>Santati</s>' means continuum. 'How does one examine?' — to this he says '<s>Rūpaṃ śūnyam</s>' (form is empty) and so on. '<s>Tām</s>' means that <s>śūnyatā</s>. '<s>Dharmatā</s>' means the essential nature of <s>dharmas</s>. '<s>Dharmatayā</s>' means by the essence of <s>dharmas</s>. '<s>Bhūtakoṭi</s>' — <s>śūnyatā</s> itself, having attained isolation, is <s>bhūtakoṭi</s> (the limit of reality). Thus [this is] the domain of skillful means.

body.text: evamukta ityādi tadyathāpītyataḥ prāk / asamāhita eveti sākṣātkartavyatayānadhyavasita eva / atrāntarā iti yāvadbuddhadharmā asya na paripakvāḥ / evamityuktena krameṇa / ārūḍha upārjitāḥ / śeṣa subodham / ityupāyakauśalasya prayogaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Thus spoken' and so on, up to just before '<s>tadyathāpi</s>.' '<s>Asamāhita eva</s>' means one who has not yet applied oneself to direct realization. '<s>Atrāntarā</s>' means 'while the <s>Buddha</s>-qualities are not yet matured for him.' '<s>Evam</s>' means in the manner described. '<s>Ārūḍha</s>' means accumulated. The rest is easily understood. Thus [this is] the practice of skillful means.

body.text: tadyathāpītyādi tadyathāpītyataḥ prāk / śūro nirbhīḥ / vīryamutsāhaḥ / pratiṣṭhānaṃ sthairyam / pratibhānamabhyūhaḥ / pratipattiranuṣṭhānam / yasminkālādau yadyuktaṃ tajjñānāt kālādijñaḥ / gatiḥ kāyavākcittakarmaṇyatā / tāṃ gataḥ prāptaḥ / praharaṇāvaraṇaṃ kavacādi / smṛtiḥ smaraṇam / matirabhyūhaḥ / gatirjñānam / dhṛtirdhāraṇam / nītirnītijñānam / viśāradaḥ paṇḍitaḥ iti śatrava eva 'śātravā' antarāyāḥ / teṣāmatikramaścaturbhirapramāṇairiti prathamamupāyakauśalam //
body.translated_text: '<s>Tadyathāpi</s>' and so on, up to just before the next '<s>tadyathāpi</s>.' '<s>Śūra</s>' means fearless. '<s>Vīrya</s>' means enthusiasm. '<s>Pratiṣṭhāna</s>' means steadfastness. '<s>Pratibhāna</s>' means discernment. '<s>Pratipatti</s>' means practice. One who knows what is appropriate at what time and so on — through the knowledge of time and so on, he is '<s>kālādijña</s>' (one who knows time, etc.). '<s>Gati</s>' means the fitness of body, speech, and mind for action. 'Having attained that' means having reached [it]. '<s>Praharaṇāvaraṇa</s>' means armor and the like. '<s>Smṛti</s>' means mindfulness. '<s>Mati</s>' means discernment. '<s>Gati</s>' means knowledge. '<s>Dhṛti</s>' means retention. '<s>Nīti</s>' means knowledge of conduct. '<s>Viśārada</s>' means learned. Thus the enemies themselves are the '<s>śātravāḥ</s>' — the obstacles. Their overcoming through the four immeasurables is the first [type of] skillful means.

body.text: tadyathāpītyādi tadyathāpītyataḥ prāk / caratīti gacchati / na ca bhūmau patatīti pātapratiṣedhaḥ sthitiḥ / na ca kañcinniśrityeti pratiṣṭhāpratiṣedhaḥ / niśrityetyāspadīkṛtya / viharatīti tiṣṭhati / na ca tatrāpīti viharaṇepi niśritaḥ / patatyaparipūrṇairiti / atra na patatīti na pratitiṣṭhatītyarthaḥ / pratiṣṭhāvirahādapratiṣṭha upāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: '<s>Tadyathāpi</s>' and so on, up to just before the next '<s>tadyathāpi</s>.' 'Practices' means moves. 'And does not fall to the ground' — the negation of falling is stability. 'And without relying on anything' — the negation of a support. '<s>Niśritya</s>' means 'having made into a basis.' 'Abides' means dwells. 'Not even there' — even in [that] abiding, [one is] unsupported. 'Falls with incomplete [qualities]' — here, 'does not fall' means 'does not become established' — this is the meaning. Because of the absence of a support, [this is] the non-abiding skillful means.

body.text: tadyathāpītyādi prāgevamuktāta / vārayediti / ākāśa eva sthāpayet / patanaṃ na dadyāditi patituṃ na dadyāt / uddharva kṣiptasya sa(śa)rasyeva śarāntaraiściramapātāya ya āvedhastadvadābuddhadharmaparipākama(kaṃ) sākṣātkaraṇāya cittasya cittāntarairya āvedhaḥ / tadanatikrameṇa vṛttiryathāvedhamupāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: "As follows" and so on — as previously stated. "Should prevent" means one should place [it] in space itself. "Should not let fall" means one should not allow it to fall. Just as an arrow shot upward is kept from falling for a long time by successive arrows, so too the penetration (<s>āvedha</s>) of the mind by successive mental states to prevent falling — for the sake of directly realizing the maturation of <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>s — that is the method (<s>upāya</s>) of practice in accordance with penetration, without transgressing that [sequence].

body.text: evamukta ityādi prāk punaraparāt / carati śamathena / viharati vipaśyanayā / samādhisamāpattirubhābhyām / mameti mayā / abhinirharatīti niṣpādayati / samādhiścāsau vimokṣaśca muktidvāratvāt / cittotpādaścittābhinirhāraḥ / anenāyaṃ duṣkarakārakaḥ / eṣa ca sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhairasādhāraṇatvādasādhāraṇa upāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: "Thus spoken" and so on — up to "moreover." "Practices" means through <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding). "Dwells" means through <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight). "Attainment of <s>samādhi</s>" means through both. "By me" means by myself. "Brings forth" means accomplishes. It is both <s>samādhi</s> and <s>vimokṣa</s> (liberation), because it is the gateway to liberation. The generation of mind is the bringing forth of mind (<s>cittābhinirhāra</s>). By this, he is one who does what is difficult. And this is the uncommon method (<s>asādhāraṇa upāya</s>) because it is not shared with all <s>Śrāvaka</s>s and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>s.

body.text: punaraparādi prāk punaraparāt / sattva ātmā puruṣaḥ / indriyāṇi pañca śraddhādīni / balānyapi pañcaiva / bodhyaṅgāni sapta / mārgo 'ṣṭāṅgaḥ / sattvadṛṣṭiḥ saktiḥ / tatprahāṇāya sattvānāmabhisambuddhaḥ / sattvān deśayiṣyāmīti sañcintya śūnyatādisamāpattirasaktiḥ / tadyogādasakta upāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: "Moreover" and so on — up to "moreover." <s>Sattva</s> means self, person. The faculties (<s>indriya</s>s) are the five beginning with faith (<s>śraddhā</s>). The powers (<s>bala</s>s) are also five. The factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>s) are seven. The path (<s>mārga</s>) is eightfold. The view of a self (<s>sattvadṛṣṭi</s>) is attachment (<s>sakti</s>). For the abandonment of that, one is awakened for the sake of beings. Having thought "I shall teach beings," the attainment of emptiness and other [meditations] is non-attachment (<s>asakti</s>). Through the practice of that, the method is non-attached (<s>asakta upāya</s>).

body.text: punaraparādi prākpunaraparāt / dharmasaṃjñā skandhadhātvādisaṃjñā / sa upalambhaḥ / tatprahāṇāyetyādi pūrvavat / evaṃ śūnyatādisamāpattiranupalambhaḥ / tadyogādanupalambha upāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: "Moreover" and so on — up to "moreover." The perception of <s>dharma</s>s (<s>dharmasaṃjñā</s>) is the perception of aggregates, elements, and so forth. That is apprehension (<s>upalambha</s>). "For the abandonment of that" and so on is as before. Thus the attainment of emptiness and so forth is non-apprehension (<s>anupalambha</s>). Through the practice of that, the method is non-apprehension (<s>anupalambha upāya</s>).

body.text: punaraparādi punaraparātprāk / strī pumān rūpaṃ śabda iti nimittasaṃjñā / tatprahāṇāyetyādi pūrvavat / evamanimittasamāpattirānimittam / tadyogādānimitta upāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: "Moreover" and so on — up to "moreover." Woman, man, form, sound — this is the perception of signs (<s>nimittasaṃjñā</s>). "For the abandonment of that" and so on is as before. Thus the attainment of the signless (<s>animittasamāpatti</s>) is the signless (<s>ānimitta</s>). Through the practice of that, the method is signless (<s>ānimitta upāya</s>).

body.text: punaraparādi yo hītyataḥ prāk / devaḥ śakraścakravarttī syāmityādirbhavabhogābhilāṣaḥ praṇihitam / tasya mūlaṃ viparyāsāḥ / tasmāccaturviparyāsaprahāṇāyetyādi pūrvavat / evamapraṇihitasamādhirapraṇihitam tadyogādapraṇihita upāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: "Moreover" and so on — up to "whoever indeed." The wish for existence and enjoyment, such as "May I become <s>Śakra</s>, a god, a <s>Cakravartin</s>," is the directed (<s>praṇihita</s>). Its root is the [four] distortions (<s>viparyāsa</s>s). Therefore, "for the abandonment of the four distortions" and so on is as before. Thus the undirected <s>samādhi</s> (<s>apraṇihitasamādhi</s>) is the undirected (<s>apraṇihita</s>). Through the practice of that, the method is undirected (<s>apraṇihita upāya</s>).

body.text: yo hi kaścidityādi naitat sthānaṃ vidyata iti yāvat / anupalambhādīnāmupāyā vimokṣamukhatrayaṃ viṣaya uktaḥ / sāṃpratameṣāmanabhisaṃskārādikamadhikaṃ viṣayamamoghatāṃ ca bravīti / anabhisaṃskāre patediti hīnabodhau / traidhātukeneti saṃsāreṇa //
body.translated_text: "Whoever indeed" and so on — up to "this situation does not exist." The three doors of liberation (<s>vimokṣamukhatraya</s>) — non-apprehension and the rest — have been stated as the domain of the methods. Now he speaks of the additional domain of these — non-fabrication (<s>anabhisaṃskāra</s>) and so forth — and their infallibility. "Would fall into non-fabrication" means into the inferior awakening. "By the triple realm" means by <s>saṃsāra</s>.

body.text: evaṃ hītyādi subhūtirāhetyataḥ prāk / samyaksambodhikāmena bodhisattvena vijño bodhisattvaḥ praṣṭavyaḥ / samyaksambodhaye kiṃ bhāvayeyaṃ kathaṃ ca bhāvayeyamiti / sa cedācakṣīta śūnyatādikameva bhāvaya tacca parijayaṃ mātuḥ sākṣātkārṣīḥ / tatropāyaḥ sarvasattvāparityāgacittādiriti / etattasyākhyāturavaivartikatve liṅgam / tasmāttasya liṅgamasminniti talliṅga upāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: "Thus indeed" and so on — up to "<s>Subhūti</s> said." A <s>Bodhisattva</s> who desires perfect awakening (<s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s>) should ask a wise <s>Bodhisattva</s>: "What should I cultivate for perfect awakening, and how should I cultivate it?" If he were to explain: "Cultivate emptiness and the rest, and through familiarization with that, you will directly realize the Mother [<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>]." Therein the method is the mind of not abandoning all beings, and so forth. This is the sign (<s>liṅga</s>) of the one who explains being irreversible (<s>avaivartika</s>). Therefore, the method that has that as its sign is the sign-method (<s>talliṅga upāya</s>).

body.text: subhūtirāhetyādi sacetpunarityataḥ prāk / bahavo bodhāya caranti teṣvalpakāste ya evaṃ visarjayanti / vyākṛtāste 'vaivarttikatve 'saṃhāryāḥ
body.translated_text: "<s>Subhūti</s> said" and so on — up to "if moreover." Many practice for awakening; among them, those who thus send forth [beings] are few. They are predicted as irreversible (<s>avaivartika</s>), not to be swayed

body.text: sadevamānuṣāsureṇa lokena / yataste 'lpakā ato 'lpapramāṇā ityapramāṇa upāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: by the world with its gods, humans, and <s>Asura</s>s. Because they are few, hence of small measure — this is the immeasurable method (<s>apramāṇa upāya</s>).

body.text: tadevaṃ navamasya paścārddhāt prabhṛti viṃśatitamasya pūrvārddhaṃ yāvadekādaśaparivartāḥ sarvākārābhisaṃbodhiḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus, from the latter half of the ninth [chapter] up to the first half of the twentieth, [there are] eleven chapters [constituting] the realization in all aspects (<s>sarvākārābhisaṃbodhi</s>).

body.text: ita ūddharvaṃ mūrddhābhisamayo vaktavyaḥ / tasyoddeśaḥ pūrvamuktaḥ ślokadvayena ṣaḍakṣarādhikena-
body.translated_text: From here onward, the peak realization (<s>mūrdhābhisamaya</s>) is to be explained. Its summary has been stated previously in two verses plus six syllables:

children.translated_text: Verse 123:
The sign (<s>liṅga</s>) of that, its increase (<s>vivṛddhi</s>), its maturation (<s>nirūḍhi</s>), and the stability of mind (<s>cittasaṃsthiti</s>),
and the fourfold antidote (<s>pratipakṣa</s>) to the fourfold conceptualization (<s>vikalpa</s>). [Verse 1-14]
Verse 124:

children.text: pratyekaṃ darśanākhye ca bhāvanākhye ca vartmani /
children.translated_text: In each of the paths called seeing (<s>darśana</s>) and cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>),
the uninterrupted <s>samādhi</s> (<s>ānantaryasamādhi</s>) together with the wrong understandings (<s>vipratipatti</s>s). [Verse 1-15]

body.translated_text: Verse 125:

body.text: mūrdhābhisamayaḥ
body.translated_text: The peak realization (<s>mūrdhābhisamaya</s>).

body.text: tasyāṣṭau vastūni / 'liṅgavivṛddhiḥ nirūḍhiścittasaṃsthitiḥ' / dṛṅmārge vipakṣapratipakṣāḥ bhāvanāmārge vipakṣapratipakṣā ānantaryasamādhivipratipattayaśceti /
body.translated_text: Its eight topics are: sign (<s>liṅga</s>), increase (<s>vivṛddhi</s>), maturation (<s>nirūḍhi</s>), and stability of mind (<s>cittasaṃsthiti</s>); on the path of seeing, the adverse factors and their antidotes; on the path of cultivation, the adverse factors and their antidotes; the uninterrupted <s>samādhi</s> (<s>ānantaryasamādhi</s>); and the wrong understandings (<s>vipratipatti</s>s).

body.text: tatra liṅgamadhikṛtya śāstram-
body.translated_text: Regarding the sign (<s>liṅga</s>), the treatise [states]:

children.translated_text: Verse 126:
Even within a dream, seeing all <s>dharma</s>s as dreamlike, and so forth —
the sign of the <s>yoga</s> that has reached its peak (<s>mūrdhaprāpta</s>) is considered to be twelvefold. [Verse 5-1]

body.text: 'mūrdhaprāptasya' iti prakarṣaprāptasya / 'yogasya' iti trisarvajñatāprayogasya / sa cetpunarityādi veditavyā / svapnāntaragatopi svapnopamān sarvadharmān paśyati na ca sākṣātkarotīti prathamaṃ liṅgam //
body.translated_text: "Of one who has reached the peak" means of one who has reached excellence. "Of the <s>yoga</s>" means of the practice directed toward the three omnisciences (<s>trisarvajñatā</s>). "If moreover" and so on should be understood [from the sūtra]. Even while within a dream, one sees all <s>dharma</s>s as dreamlike but does not directly realize [them] — this is the first sign.

body.text: punaraparādi veditavyāntam / svapnāntaragatopi śrāvakabhūmau pratyekabuddhabhūmau traidhātuke ca spṛhāṃ na karotīti dvitīyam //
body.translated_text: "Moreover" and so on, up to "should be understood." Even while within a dream, one does not crave for the stage of <s>Śrāvaka</s>s, the stage of <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>s, or the triple realm — this is the second [sign].

body.text: punaraparādi veditavyāntam / svapnāntaragato mahatyāṃ pariṣadyubhayasaṅghaparivṛtaṃ tathāgatamātmānaṃ paśyatīti tṛtīyam //
body.translated_text: "Moreover" and so on, up to "should be understood." While within a dream, one sees oneself in a great assembly, surrounded by both communities (<s>saṅgha</s>s), as a <s>Tathāgata</s> — this is the third [sign].

body.text: punaraparādi veditavyāntaram / svapnāntaragato vaihāyasamabhyudgamya sattvebhyo dharma deśayati vyāmagataṃ cātmānaṃ saṃjānīte / bhikṣūṃśca nirmitīta ye lokadhātvantareṣu buddhakṛtyaṃ kurvantīti caturtham //
body.translated_text: "Moreover" and so on, up to "should be understood." While within a dream, having risen into the sky, one teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to beings and perceives oneself as being a <s>vyāma</s> [in stature]; and [one sees] monks who are emanated (<s>nirmita</s>) performing the activities of a <s>Buddha</s> in other world-systems — this is the fourth [sign].

body.text: punaraparādi veditavyāntam / svapnāntaragatopyātmanaḥ pareṣāṃ vā vadhabandhanaśiraśchedādīn dṛṣṭvā nottrasyati / vibuddhasya caivaṃ bhavati svapnopamaṃ sarva traidhātukaṃ mayā cābhisaṃbudhyaivaṃ dharmo deśayitavya iti pañcamam //
body.translated_text: "Moreover" and so on, up to "should be understood." Even while within a dream, having seen the killing, binding, beheading, and so forth of oneself or others, one is not frightened. And upon awakening, one thinks: "The entire triple realm is dreamlike, and having attained awakening, I should teach the <s>Dharma</s> in this way" — this is the fifth [sign].

body.text: punaraparādi veditavyāntam / svapnāntaragatasya nairayikādīn sattvān dṛṣṭvā evaṃ bhavati / tathā kariṣyāmi yathā me 'bhisambuddhasya buddhakṣetre trayo 'pāyāḥ sarvathā na bhaviṣyantīti ṣaṣṭham //
body.translated_text: "Moreover" and so on, up to "should be understood." While within a dream, having seen beings in hell-realms and so forth, one thinks: "I shall act in such a way that when I am awakened, in my <s>Buddha</s>-field the three lower realms (<s>apāya</s>s) will in no way exist" — this is the sixth [sign].

body.text: punaraparādi punaraparāt prāk / svapnāntaragato yadi grāmadāhādau vartamāne prativibuddha evaṃ samanvāharet / yathā mayā svapne 'vaivartikaliṅgānyātmani dṛṣṭāni tena satyenāyaṃ grāmadāhādiḥ śāmyatviti / sa cecchāmyati tatsaptamaṃ liṅgam //
body.translated_text: "Moreover" and so on — up to "moreover." While within a dream, if when a village fire and such are occurring, one who has awakened recollects thus: "Just as I have seen in my dream the signs of irreversibility (<s>avaivartikaliṅga</s>) in myself, by that truth may this village fire and so forth be pacified" — and if it is pacified, that is the seventh sign.

body.text: punaraparādi āparivartasamāpteḥ / yadi kaścitsattvo 'manuṣyeṇa gṛhīto 'dhiṣṭhitaḥ āviṣṭo vā antaḥpraveśāt / tatra bodhisattvaḥ satyādhiṣṭhānaṃ kuryāt / yadyahaṃ vyākṛtaḥ pūrvabuddhairanuttarāyāṃ bodhau yadi ca me pariśuddho 'dhyāśayastāmabhisamboddhaṃ yathā ca nāsti buddhānāṃ kiñcidajñātam / anena satyenāyamamanuṣyo 'pakrāmatviti sa cettasmāt satyādhiṣṭhānāt apakrāmati tadaṣṭamaṃ liṅgam //
body.translated_text: "Moreover" and so on — up to the end of the chapter. If some being is seized by a non-human spirit, possessed or entered from within, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> should make a truth-declaration (<s>satyādhiṣṭhāna</s>): "If I have been predicted by former <s>Buddha</s>s for unsurpassed awakening (<s>anuttarā bodhi</s>), and if my intention (<s>adhyāśaya</s>) is pure to attain that awakening, and since there is nothing unknown to the <s>Buddha</s>s — by this truth, may this non-human spirit depart." If it departs due to that truth-declaration, that is the eighth sign.

body.text: upāyakauśalyānāṃ mīmāṃsā parijñānaṃ tadarthaḥ parivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: The investigation and complete understanding of skillful means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>) — that is the purpose of this chapter.

body.text: āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ sāratamānāmni pañjikāyāṃ ratnākaraśāntiviracitāyāṃ viṃśatitamaḥ parivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: This is the twentieth chapter in the commentary (<s>pañjikā</s>) named <s>Sāratamā</s> on the noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s>, composed by <s>Ratnākaraśānti</s>.

body.text: 21. mārakarmaparivarto nāmaikaviṃśatitamaḥ /
body.translated_text: Chapter 21: The chapter on the deeds of <s>Māra</s> (<s>mārakarma-parivarta</s>), the twenty-first.

body.text: tatra khalvityādi / ayamekaviṃśatitamaḥ parivarto mārakarmaṇām / kasteṣāṃ prastāvaḥ? navayānasaṃprasthitasya bodhisattvasya satyādhiṣṭhānaphalasampādanādinā mithyāmānotpādanāya bahudhā mārāḥ / parākramata ityayameṣāṃ prastāvaḥ /
body.translated_text: "Therein indeed" and so on. This twenty-first chapter concerns the deeds of <s>Māra</s>. What is their occasion? For a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has newly set out on the vehicle, <s>Māra</s>s exert themselves in many ways to produce false pride, through the accomplishment of the fruits of truth-declarations and so forth. "They exert themselves" — this is their occasion.

body.text: tatretyanantarokte satyādhiṣṭhāne / autsukyamiti prāptāvasarasya karmaṇaḥ karaṇārtha mutsāhaḥ / balamutsāhaśaktiḥ / tejaḥ prabhāvaśaktiḥ / kathaṃ tejovattaramiti yāvat / tasau matvartha iti bhatvāspadatvaṃ nāstīti bhatvena na bhavitavyam / tadyathā āyuṣmān sarasvān iti / evaṃ tarhi dīptyarthā[d]dravateḥ śatrantāt tarap / tejasā dīptataraṃ tejovattaramiti / autsukyamiti / ātmani bahumānam / āvamaṃsyata ityādi / avamāno 'nādaraḥ / uccagghānamantarhāsaḥ / ullāpanaṃ manasānyatkaraṇam / kutsanaṃ doṣadarśitā / taṃsanaṃ doṣavāditā / sambodhāvitīti / itiśabdo hetau / mānaṃ janayiṣyatītyādi / atra saśabdasya sarvatretyarthaḥ / jananamutpādanam / vadhaṃnaṃ puraḥsarīkaraṇam / stambhanaṃ sthirīkaraṇam / bṛṃhaṇa paripuṣṭiḥ / utpādanamaccairnayanam / mānenetyādi / anyebhyo 'dhikatvena cittasyonnatiḥ sāmānyena mānaḥ sa pūrvamuktaḥ / iha tu tadviśeṣā ucyante / yā tasya hīnādunnatiḥ sa mānaḥ / yādṛśādeva so 'timānaḥ / yo punaḥ prakṛṣṭāt sa mānātimānaḥ / aprāpte 'vaivartikatve prāptaṃ mayeti so 'bhimānaḥ / yā punarabhūtairavaivartikaguṇairguṇavānasmīti sa mithyāmānaḥ / tathā rūpāniti mahābhūtān bodhisattvān dṛṣṭaveti pareṇa sambandhaḥ / śeṣaṃ teṣāmeva viśeṣaṇam / bhajiṣyata ityatra bhajeriṭpratiṣedho bhavati saṃjñāpūrvakasya vidheranityatvāt / tadeva mārabandhanamiti mānam /
body.translated_text: "Therein" refers to the truth-declaration (<s>satyādhiṣṭhāna</s>) just mentioned. "Eagerness" (<s>autsukyam</s>) means enthusiasm for performing an action whose occasion has arrived. "Strength" (<s>bala</s>) means the power of effort. "Splendor" (<s>tejas</s>) means the power of influence. "How is it more splendid?" — [this is] the extent [of the question]. The <s>matvar</s> suffix means there is no basis for becoming, i.e., one should not become [proud]. As in "the venerable <s>Sarasvan</s>." Alternatively, from the root <s>dru</s> meaning "to shine," with the suffix <s>tarap</s> after the stem ending in <s>śatṛ</s>, "more splendid" means "shining more with splendor." "Eagerness" means self-esteem. "Will look down upon" and so on — contempt (<s>avamāna</s>) means disregard; mockery (<s>uccagghāna</s>) means inner laughter; deflection (<s>ullāpana</s>) means mentally directing attention elsewhere; disparagement (<s>kutsana</s>) means showing faults; censuring (<s>taṃsana</s>) means speaking of faults. "For awakening" — the word "<s>iti</s>" indicates the reason. "Will generate pride" and so on — here the word "<s>sa</s>" means "everywhere." Generation means production; increase (<s>vardhana</s>) means making foremost; solidification (<s>stambhana</s>) means making firm; nourishment (<s>bṛṃhaṇa</s>) means full development; raising (<s>utpādana</s>) means elevating high. "Through pride" and so on — the exaltation of mind by [thinking oneself] superior to others is pride (<s>māna</s>) in general, as stated before. But here its specific forms are stated: the exaltation over one who is inferior is pride (<s>māna</s>); over one who is equal is excessive pride (<s>atimāna</s>); over one who is superior is the pride of prides (<s>mānātimāna</s>); thinking "I have attained" when irreversibility has not been attained is conceit (<s>abhimāna</s>); claiming "I possess qualities" through non-existent qualities of irreversibility is false pride (<s>mithyāmāna</s>). Similarly, "having seen forms" means having seen great beings, <s>Bodhisattva</s>s — this connects with what follows. The rest is qualification of those very [Bodhisattvas]. In "will resort to," the prohibition of <s>bhaj</s> with <s>iṭ</s> applies because a rule preceded by a designation is not permanent. That very pride is the bondage of <s>Māra</s>.

body.text: punaraparamityādi / nāmāpadeśaḥ saṃjñākathanam / mṛduko mṛdvindriyaḥ / āraṇyakatvādayo dhutaguṇāḥ / grāmādvahiḥ krośātparamaraṇyam / tatraiva sthānāt āraṇyakaḥ / piṇḍapātasyaiva bhojanāt piṇḍapātikaḥ / pāṃsukūlasyeva prāvaraṇāt pāṃsukūlikaḥ / madhyānhasyopānta eva bhojanāt khalu paścābhdaktikaḥ / ekāsana eva bhuṅkte ekāsanikaḥ / sakṛdāstīrṇe nityaṃ śayanāt yāthāsaṃstarikaḥ / tricīvarādadhikatyāgāt traicīvarikaḥ / śmaśānasamīpa eva sthānāt śmāśānikaḥ / vṛkṣamūla eva sthānāt vṛkṣamūlikaḥ / niṣadyayā rātrinayanān naiṣadyikaḥ / acchanno 'vakāśo 'bhyavakāśaḥ / tatraiva sthānāt ābhyavakāśikaḥ / aurṇakaśānakādereva prāvaraṇāt nāmantikaḥ / alpaiṣaṇāt alpecchaḥ / tāvataiva santoṣāt santuṣṭaḥ / ekākitvāt praviviktaḥ / dṛṣṭe dharme tasminneva janmani bhavo dṛṣṭadhārmikaḥ / tena ādekṣyati vyapadekṣyati / kathamityāha pūrvamapītyādi / yacchabdastasmādarthe / adhiṣṭhānamāviṣkaraṇam / dhutaguṇaiḥ saṃlekhaḥ karṣaṇaṃ dhanulekhanavat / manyāṃ karotīti ṇic / yac manyanā māna ityarthaḥ / śeṣaṃ subodhaṃ dhutaguṇāḥ saṃvidyanta iti yāvat /
body.translated_text: "Moreover" and so on. "Name-designation" (<s>nāmāpadeśa</s>) means the stating of a title. "Gentle" (<s>mṛduka</s>) means one of soft faculties. Being forest-dwelling (<s>āraṇyakatva</s>) and so forth are the ascetic qualities (<s>dhutaguṇa</s>s). A forest (<s>araṇya</s>) is beyond a <s>krośa</s> from a village; one who stays there is a forest-dweller (<s>āraṇyaka</s>). One who eats only alms-food is an alms-eater (<s>piṇḍapātika</s>). One who wears only rag-robes is a rag-robe wearer (<s>pāṃsukūlika</s>). One who eats only just before midday is an afternoon-faster (<s>paścādbhaktika</s>). One who eats at a single sitting is a single-sitter (<s>ekāsanika</s>). One who always sleeps on a mat spread once is a "as-spread" practitioner (<s>yāthāsaṃstarika</s>). One who renounces more than three robes is a three-robe wearer (<s>traicīvarika</s>). One who stays near a charnel ground is a charnel-ground dweller (<s>śmāśānika</s>). One who stays at the root of a tree is a tree-root dweller (<s>vṛkṣamūlika</s>). One who passes the night sitting is a sitter (<s>naiṣadyika</s>). An uncovered open space is <s>abhyavakāśa</s>; one who stays there is an open-air dweller (<s>ābhyavakāśika</s>). One who wears only wool, hemp, and such is called <s>nāmantika</s>. One of little seeking is of few desires (<s>alpeccha</s>). One content with just that much is contented (<s>santuṣṭa</s>). One who is solitary is secluded (<s>pravivikta</s>). <s>Dṛṣṭadhārmika</s> means pertaining to the present life, in this very birth. By that, "he will designate, he will proclaim." How? He says "even before" and so on. The word "<s>yat</s>" has the meaning of "therefore." <s>Adhiṣṭhāna</s> means manifestation. Mortification (<s>saṃlekha</s>) through ascetic qualities means emaciation, like scraping a bow. "Makes [someone] think" — the causative suffix <s>ṇic</s> [is used]; the meaning is: that which is thinking [oneself superior] is pride (<s>māna</s>). The rest is easily understood — the ascetic qualities exist, up to that point.

body.text: tasya khalvityādi / nāmādhiṣṭhāneneti kimatra nāma? avinivartanīyaśabdastadguṇaśabdaśca / stambhābhibhūta iti stambho guruṣvagauravam / katamannāmadheyamityata āha / yadevetyādi / teneti bodhisattvena / anuvartitamityanuvicintitam / asyaiva nirdeśa uttarābhyām / anuvitarkitaṃ kiṃ me nāma bhavediti / anuvicāritamidaṃ me nāma bhavediti / vyākariṣyatītyāyākhyāsyati māraḥ / anuvartitamākāṅikṣatam / sametīti saṃvadati / kiṃ kena saṃvadatītyata āha nāmnā nāmeti / tataḥ kimityāha vyākṛta ityādi / saṃdhāvya saṃsṛtyeti tāsu tāsu durgatiṣūtpadya / yadi ceti cakāraḥ samuccayārthaḥ sūkṣmasūkṣmāṇīti durlakṣyāṇi /
body.translated_text: 'Of that indeed' and so forth. 'By the empowerment of the name' — what here is the 'name'? The word '<s>avinivartanīya</s>' (irreversible) and the word for its qualities. 'Overcome by torpor' — '<s>stambha</s>' (torpor) is disrespect toward elders. 'What is the name?' — to this he says 'whatever' and so forth. 'By him' means by the <s>bodhisattva</s>. '<s>Anuvartita</s>' (followed) means reflected upon. The exposition of just this is by the next two [terms]. '<s>Anuvitarkita</s>' (deliberated upon) means 'what might my name be?' '<s>Anuvicārita</s>' (examined) means 'this is my name.' 'He will predict' means <s>Māra</s> will proclaim. '<s>Anuvartita</s>' means anticipated. 'Agrees' means accords. 'What accords with what?' — to this he says 'the name with the name.' 'Then what?' — he says 'predicted' and so forth. 'Having wandered, having transmigrated' means having been born in those various evil destinies. 'And if' — the particle '<s>ca</s>' is in the sense of conjunction. 'Most subtle' means difficult to perceive.

body.text: araṇyaṃ ca yathoktam / vanaprasthaṃ ca giriguhā ca śmaśānaṃ ca palālapuñjaśceti dvandvaḥ / ādiśabdādvṛkṣamūlādi / āraṇyakānītyaraṇye bhavāni / ata eva prāntāni vijanapadānīti vijanasthānāni / viviktāni śūnyāni / vivikto rahitaḥ grāmasyāntaḥ samīpamekadeśo vā / manasikāraviveka iti manasikārebhyo vivekaḥ / mṛdunā abhiniveśena niśritaḥ / madhyena ālīnaḥ / adhimātreṇa adhyavasitaḥ / tenaivātmotkarṣaṇāt adhyavasāyamāpannaḥ / saṃkīrṇo gṛhipravrajitaiḥ / ākīrṇaḥ pravrajitaireva bodhisattvacaṇḍālaḥ tairasaṃvāsyatvāt / bodhisattvadūṣī svadoṣeṇa teṣāṃ dūṣaṇāt / bodhisattvapratirūpako dehasāmyāt / bodhisattvaprativarṇiko nāmasāmyāt / bodhisattvakāraṇḍavakaḥ haṃseṣviva teṣvakṛṣṇeṣu kṛṣṇatvāt / cauraḥ śramaṇaveṣeṇa dharmagrahaṇāt / cauro bodhisattvānāmasammatatvāt / cauraḥ sadevakasya lokasya mithyādakṣiṇīyatvāt / tajjātīya ityādinā tāvadvaśasya sabhdirasevyatāṃ vistareṇāha / sthāma balam / anāryāḥ pāpāḥ / udvignaṃ bhītam / tatrāpi tāvaditi tādṛśepi / maṃtrāyamāṇenetyādinā maitryādicatuṣṭayaviṣayabhedānāha / evaṃ cetyādinā praṇidhānam / ayamapīti / yasya khalu punarityādikaḥ sarvaḥ / abhijñāyeti / atyutka[ṭaḥ] parākramaḥ puruṣakāraḥ / idamapītyādinā paścimamārakarmopasaṃhāraḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Forest' is as described. 'Hermitage,' 'mountain cave,' 'cremation ground,' and 'heap of straw' — this is a <s>dvandva</s> compound. By the word 'and so forth,' the root of a tree and the like [are included]. '<s>Āraṇyaka</s>' means existing in the forest. For that very reason, 'remote' means in uninhabited places. 'Secluded' means empty. '<s>Vivikta</s>' (solitary) means separated — [a place] within or near a village, or a particular area. 'Seclusion of mental attention' means seclusion from mental attentions. 'Inclined' — through mild grasping. 'Absorbed' — through middling [grasping]. 'Determined' — through intense [grasping]. 'Having attained determination' — because of self-aggrandizement through that very [determination]. '<s>Saṃkīrṇa</s>' (mixed) means [mingling] with householders and renunciants. '<s>Ākīrṇa</s>' (crowded) means with renunciants alone — a '<s>bodhisattva-caṇḍāla</s>' (outcaste among <s>bodhisattvas</s>) because of being unfit to dwell with them. A '<s>bodhisattva-dūṣī</s>' (corrupter of <s>bodhisattvas</s>) because of corrupting them through his own faults. A '<s>bodhisattva-pratirūpaka</s>' (counterfeit <s>bodhisattva</s>) because of bodily resemblance. A '<s>bodhisattva-prativarṇika</s>' (name-imitator of <s>bodhisattvas</s>) because of resemblance in name. A '<s>bodhisattva-kāraṇḍavaka</s>' (crane among <s>bodhisattvas</s>) because of being black among those who are not black, like [cranes] among geese. A 'thief' because of grasping the <s>Dharma</s> in the guise of a <s>śramaṇa</s> (ascetic). A 'thief' because of not being approved by [genuine] <s>bodhisattvas</s>. A 'thief' because of being falsely worthy of offerings from the world together with its gods. With '<s>tajjātīya</s>' (of that kind) and so forth, he states at length the unsuitability of associating with such a person. '<s>Sthāma</s>' (strength) is power. '<s>Anārya</s>' (ignoble) means wicked. '<s>Udvigna</s>' (agitated) means afraid. 'Even in such [a situation]' means even in such a person. With 'counseling' and so forth, he states the distinctions in the objects of the fourfold [practice of] <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) and the rest. With 'thus' and so forth is the aspiration. 'This one also' — all [beginning with] 'whoever indeed.' '<s>Abhijñāya</s>' means knowing. 'Extremely strenuous effort' is <s>puruṣakāra</s> (human endeavor). With 'this too' and so forth is the conclusion of the final deed of <s>Māra</s>.

body.text: mārakarmaṇāmabhidhāyakaḥ parivartastathoktaḥ //
body.translated_text: The chapter that declares the deeds of <s>Māra</s> is so named.

body.text: āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ sāratamānāmni pañjikāyāṃ ratnākaraśāntiviracitāyāmekaviṃśatitamaḥ parivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: In the <s>Pañjikā</s> commentary named <s>Sāratama</s>, composed by <s>Ratnākaraśānti</s>, on the noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s> — this is the twenty-first chapter.

body.text: 22. kalyāṇamitraparivarto nāma dvāviṃśatitamaḥ /
