body.translated_text: 22. The twenty-second [chapter] is named the '<s>Kalyāṇamitra-parivarta</s>' (Chapter on the Spiritual Friend).

body.text: atha khalvityādinā āsu khalu punarityataḥ prāk / prajñāpāramitaiveti prādhānyādavadhāraṇam / yathā ca saikā tayā sahitāḥ ṣaṭ / ata āha / sarvā eva cetyādi / kuta ityāha / ṣaḍevetyādi / tā eva niṣṭhāṃ gatāḥ śāstā yaḥ paramaṃ phalam / tataḥ pūrvānta eva mārgaḥ / āloko lokottaraṃ jñānaṃ pramuditāyāṃ sopi tā eva / ulkā prayatnavāhī mārgo vimalādibhūmiṣu ṣaṭsu sopi tā eva / avabhāso divasālokaḥ / sa cāyatnavāhī mārgo 'calādiṣu bhūmiṣu sopi tā eva / ataśca tā eva trīṇi ratnāni / tasmāttā eva śaraṇaṃ yāvat dīpaḥ / padārthaḥ pūrvavat / tā eva mātā dhāraṇātpoṣaṇācca / tā eva pitā bijādhānāt / jñānāyeti darśanāya / bodhāyeti bhāvanāmārgāya / taktasya hetoriti kutaḥ prajñāpāramitaiva yathoktaguṇā netarā ityarthaḥ / atra hītyādinā parihāraḥ / traiyadhvikabuddhānāṃ ca sarvajñatā tatprasūtaivetyākhyātumāha / yepītyādi / nirjātā niṣpannā / antargatā iti yathāyogamantarbhūtāḥ / buddhajñānādipadāni pūrvameva vyākhyātāni / sarvabhūtānāṃ upakāribhūto bhavatīti sambandhaḥ / kadetyāha yadetyādi / iti kalyāṇamitrasevā navamaṃ liṅgam //
body.translated_text: 'Now then' and so forth, up to before 'in these indeed.' '<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> alone' — the restriction is because of [its] preeminence. And just as it alone [is preeminent], so the six [<s>pāramitās</s>] are [preeminent] together with it. Hence he says 'all indeed' and so forth. 'From what [reason]?' — he says 'the six alone' and so forth. Those very [<s>pāramitās</s>], having reached their culmination, are the teacher who is the supreme fruit. Therefore, the path is only the preliminary [stage]. 'Light' (<s>āloka</s>) is supramundane knowledge on the first [stage], <s>Pramuditā</s> (Joyful) — that too is those very [<s>pāramitās</s>]. 'Torch' (<s>ulkā</s>) is the path requiring effort on the six stages beginning with <s>Vimalā</s> (Stainless) — that too is those very [<s>pāramitās</s>]. 'Illumination' (<s>avabhāsa</s>) is daylight. And that is the effortless path on the stages beginning with <s>Acalā</s> (Immovable) — that too is those very [<s>pāramitās</s>]. And therefore, those very [<s>pāramitās</s>] are the Three Jewels. Therefore, those alone are the refuge, up to 'lamp.' The meaning of the terms is as before. Those very [<s>pāramitās</s>] are the mother — because of bearing and nourishing. Those very [<s>pāramitās</s>] are the father — because of planting the seed. 'For the sake of knowledge' means for seeing. 'For the sake of awakening' means for the path of cultivation. 'For what reason?' means 'whence [does it follow that] <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> alone possesses the qualities stated, and not another?' — this is the meaning. With 'herein indeed' and so forth is the resolution. 'And the <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience) of the <s>Buddhas</s> of the three times is born from that very [<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>]' — to declare this he says 'even those' and so forth. '<s>Nirjāta</s>' means accomplished. '<s>Antargata</s>' means, correspondingly, included within. The terms '<s>Buddha</s>-knowledge' and the rest have already been explained previously. 'One becomes a benefactor of all beings' — this is the syntactic connection. 'When?' — he says 'when' and so forth. Thus, the service of the spiritual friend is the ninth sign [of irreversibility].

body.text: āsu khalvityādi subhūtirāhetyataḥ prāk / yasmāt iyameva praṇāyikā tasmāt aparapraṇeyatā ityādi / tasmādaparapraṇeyatā daśamaṃ liṅgam //
body.translated_text: 'In these indeed' and so forth, up to before '<s>Subhūti</s> said.' Because this very [<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>] is the guide, therefore there is non-susceptibility to being led by others, and so forth. Therefore, non-susceptibility to being led by others is the tenth sign.

body.text: subhūtirāhetyādi / saṃkleśo vyavadānaṃ ca prajñāyata iti yāvat / asaṅgalakṣaṇetyanupalambhalakṣaṇā / sarvadharmasvalakṣaṇānāṃ tasyāmanupalambhāt / tathā rūpādayopi śūnyatvādviviktatvāt / yadityādinā codyaṃ na codyaṃ na hītyarthaḥ / udagraho nimittasya abhiniveśo vastutvena grāhaḥ / tadevamasaṅgalakṣaṇā bhagavatī dharmāśca / tathāpyasti saṃkleśo 'sti vyavadānamityekādaśamaṃ liṅgam //
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said and so forth. 'Defilement and purification are discerned' — up to this point. 'Of the characteristic of non-attachment' means of the characteristic of non-apprehension. Because of the non-apprehension in it of the own-characteristics of all <s>dharmas</s>. Similarly, form and the rest too [are non-attached], because of being empty, because of being secluded. With 'that which' and so forth is the objection — 'not an objection, not [valid]' — this is the meaning. '<s>Udagraha</s>' (grasping) is the grasping of a sign; '<s>abhiniveśa</s>' (attachment) is grasping as a real entity. Thus, the <s>Bhagavatī</s> (<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>) has the characteristic of non-attachment, and so do the <s>dharmas</s>. Even so, there is defilement and there is purification — this is the eleventh sign.

body.text: subhūtirāhetyādi sa cetpunarityataḥ prāk / anavamardanīya ityasaṃhāryaḥ / anenāpīti sarvadharmeṣvavivikteṣvityādinā anavamardanīyatvalābho dvādaśaṃ liṅgam // ityuktāni liṅgāni //
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said and so forth, up to before 'if he again.' '<s>Anavamardanīya</s>' means invincible (<s>asaṃhārya</s>). 'By this also' — through the [statement] 'non-secluded among all <s>dharmas</s>' and so forth — 'the attainment of invincibility' is the twelfth sign. Thus the signs have been stated.

body.text: vivṛddhirvaktavyā / ataḥ śāstram-
body.translated_text: The increase (<s>vivṛddhi</s>) is to be stated. Hence the treatise [states] —

children.translated_text: The number of beings born in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, the worship of the <s>Buddhas</s>, merit, and the like —
having made the comparison in many ways, the increase is sixteenfold. // 5-2 //

body.text: ṣoḍaśaprakārā vivṛddhiruktā sūtre / kiṃ kṛtvā? 'upamāṃ kṛtvā' / kīdṛśīm? jambūdvīpe ye janāḥ sattvāsteṣāmiyattayā sūtroktena māhātmyena manuṣyabhāvacittotpādalakṣaṇena yā buddhapūjā tayā yacchubhaṃ puṇyaṃ tadādiryasyā upamāyāḥ, tām / ādiśabdaṃ (bdāt?) labdhara (?)kāri(?)mahāmaṇiratnādiparigrahaḥ / buddhabhūmirbahubhiḥ prakārairuktā vināpyupamām //
body.translated_text: A sixteenfold increase is stated in the <s>sūtra</s>. Having done what? 'Having made the comparison.' Of what kind? Through the greatness stated in the <s>sūtra</s>, measured by the number of beings in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> — the worship of the <s>Buddhas</s> characterized by the human state and the generation of <s>bodhicitta</s> — that merit, and the like constituting the beginning of the comparison — that [comparison]. By the word 'and so forth' — the possession of the great <s>maṇi</s>-jewels and the rest that are obtained. The <s>Buddha</s>-stage is stated in many ways, even without comparison.

body.text: tatrādyā sa cetpunarityādinā tadyathāpītyataḥ prāk / yāvajjīvamiti yāvadāyuḥ / taddānamiti yadbuddhebhyo sarvasattvebhyaḥ / manasikāraiḥ viharatīti vivṛddhisaṃgṛhītaiḥ / sthāpayitveti tyaktvā / tatteṣāṃ sthāpanaṃ kasya hetoḥ? vadhyagatāniveti vadhyasthānagatānivā(va) / virāgayata ityaprāptavataḥ / itiprajñāpāramitāpratisaṃyuktairmanasikārai rātriṃdivānāṃ nayanāt prathamā vivṛddhiḥ //
body.translated_text: Therein, the first [increase is stated] with 'if he again' and so forth, up to before 'just as, for example.' 'For the duration of life' means for the extent of one's lifespan. 'That gift' means that which [is given] to the <s>Buddhas</s> and to all beings. 'Abides through mental attentions' means through [mental attentions] included in the increase. 'Having set aside' means having excluded. Why is there the setting aside of those? 'As if led to the execution ground' — as if gone to the place of execution. 'He causes dispassion' means [he teaches] those who have not attained [dispassion]. Thus, through leading [beings] day and night by mental attentions connected with <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> — this is the first increase.

body.text: tadyathāpītyādi na ca parihīyata iti yāvat / prajñāpāramiteti tāvadanveṣṭavyeti sambandhaḥ / kīdṛśena? avirahitasarvajñatācittena / avirahitātpūrvaṃ manasikāraśabdaḥ kvacit paṭhyate / sā vānyā veti pustakabhedāt / prajñāpāramitāpratisaṃyuktairmanasikāraiḥ kṣaṇamapyavirahād dvitīyā vivṛddhiḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Just as, for example' and so forth, up to 'and he does not decline.' '<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>' — [the supplement is] 'should be sought' — this is the syntactic connection. With what [attitude]? 'With a mind not separated from <s>sarvajñatā</s>-thought.' Before '<s>avirahita</s>' (not separated), the word '<s>manasikāra</s>' (mental attention) is read in some [manuscripts]. Whether that [reading] or another — because of manuscript variants. Through not being separated even for a moment from mental attentions connected with <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> — this is the second increase.

body.text: subhūtirāhetyādi netatsthānaṃ vidyata iti yāvat anutpattikeṣu dharmeṣu kṣāntipratilambhādvyākaraṇalābha iti tṛtīyā //
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said and so forth, up to 'that situation does not exist.' Through the attainment of prediction by obtaining patient acceptance of the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s> — this is the third [increase].

body.text: subhūtirāhetyādyā parivartāntāt / vyākaraṇe 'bhisambodhe ca nirmānatvāccaturthī //
body.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s> said and so forth, up to the end of the chapter. Because of the manifestation-nature of the prediction and the full awakening — this is the fourth [increase].

body.text: kalyāṇamitrādiḥ parivarto kalyāṇamitraparivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: The chapter beginning with the spiritual friend is the '<s>Kalyāṇamitra-parivarta</s>' (Chapter on the Spiritual Friend).

body.text: āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ sāratamānāmni pañjikāyāṃ ratnākaraśāntiviracitāyāṃ dvāviṃśatitamaḥ parivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: In the <s>Pañjikā</s> commentary named <s>Sāratama</s>, composed by <s>Ratnākaraśānti</s>, on the noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s> — this is the twenty-second chapter.

body.text: 23. śakraparivarto nāma trayoviṃśatitamaḥ /
body.translated_text: 23. The twenty-third [chapter] is named the '<s>Śakra-parivarta</s>' (Chapter of <s>Śakra</s>).

body.text: tena khalu punarityādi evaṃ śikṣamāṇaṃ cetyataḥ prāk / sadevamānuṣāsuraṃ lokaṃ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhayānikānanupāyakuśalāṃśca bodhisattvo 'bhibhavati / teṣāṃ cānabhibhūto bhavatīti pañcamī vivṛddhiḥ //
body.translated_text: 'By him indeed then' and so forth, up to before 'thus training.' The <s>bodhisattva</s> surpasses the world with its gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s>, all the <s>śrāvaka</s> and <s>pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle-followers, and those who lack skill in means. And he is not surpassed by them — this is the fifth increase.

body.text: evaṃ śikṣamāṇaṃ cetyādi āparivartāntāt / catvāro lokapālāḥ śakrastadanye ca devāstamupasaṃkramiṣyantītyādibhiranuśaṃsaiḥ ṣaṣṭhī //
body.translated_text: 'Thus training' and so forth, up to the end of the chapter. Through the benefits such as the four world-guardians, <s>Śakra</s>, and the other gods approaching him — this is the sixth [increase].

body.text: śakreṇoktaḥ parivartaḥ śakraparivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: The chapter spoken by <s>Śakra</s> is the '<s>Śakra-parivarta</s>'.

body.text: āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ sāratamānāmni pañjikāyāṃ ratnākaraśāntiviracitāyāṃ trayoviṃśatitamaḥ parivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: In the <s>Pañjikā</s> commentary named <s>Sāratama</s>, composed by <s>Ratnākaraśānti</s>, on the noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s> — this is the twenty-third chapter.

body.text: 24. abhimānaparivarto nāma catarśititamaḥ /
body.translated_text: 24. The twenty-fourth [chapter] is named the '<s>Abhimāna-parivarta</s>' (Chapter on Conceit).

body.text: atha khalvityādi kathaṃ cānandetyataḥ prāk / ālīno bhavatīti anulagno bhavati / kathamityāha / eṣa ityādi yāvatparipūrayiṣyatīti / na hyevamityādi / yathānyasūtreṣu tathāgatabhāṣitaṃ yujyamānaṃ evamatra nāstītyarthaḥ / gādhaḥ pratiṣṭhā / āsvādo ruciḥ / nāmagotragrahaṇaṃ dhutaguṇakīrtanaṃ ca pūrvavat / utsadā upacitāḥ kāyā rāśayaḥ iti saptamī vivṛddhiḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Now then' and so forth, up to before 'and how does he not delight.' 'He becomes attached' means he becomes fixated. 'How?' — he says 'this' and so forth, up to 'he will fulfill.' 'Not thus indeed' and so forth — 'that which, as spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s> in other <s>sūtras</s>, is apt — in this [sūtra] there is no such [statement]' — this is the meaning. '<s>Gādha</s>' (ground) is a foothold. '<s>Āsvāda</s>' (savoring) is relish. The grasping of name and lineage, and the proclamation of <s>dhūtaguṇas</s> (ascetic qualities) — are as before. '<s>Utsada</s>' means heaped up. '<s>Kāya</s>' means assemblages, groups. This is the seventh increase.

body.text: kathaṃ cetyādyā pavirtāntāt sarvaṃ subodham / ityaṣṭamī vivṛddhiḥ //
body.translated_text: 'And how' and so forth, up to the end of the chapter — all easily understood. This is the eighth increase.

body.text: yoyamavinivartanīyo 'bhimāno bodhisattvasya bavhanarthahetustadupalakṣitaḥ parivarto 'bhimānaparivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: The conceit of irreversibility that belongs to the <s>bodhisattva</s>, which is the cause of many harms — the chapter characterized by that is the '<s>Abhimāna-parivarta</s>' (Chapter on Conceit).

body.text: āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ sāratamānāmni pañjikāyāṃ ratnākaraśāntiviracitāyāṃ caturviśatitamaḥ parivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: In the <s>Pañjikā</s> commentary named <s>Sāratama</s>, composed by <s>Ratnākaraśānti</s>, on the noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s> — this is the twenty-fourth chapter.

body.text: 25. śikṣāparivarto nāma pañcaviṃśatitamaḥ /
body.translated_text: 25. The twenty-fifth [chapter] is named the '<s>Śikṣā-parivarta</s>' (Chapter on Training).

body.text: atha khalvityādi pāraṃ gacchatīti yāvat / kva śikṣamāṇaḥ sarvajñatāyāṃ śikṣata iti praśnaḥ / kṣaye 'nutpāde 'nirodhe 'jātau'bhāve
body.translated_text: 'Now then' and so forth, up to 'goes to the far shore.' 'In what is he training when he trains in <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience)?' — this is the question. 'In exhaustion, in non-arising, in non-cessation, in non-birth, in non-existence,

body.text: viveke virāge ākāśe dharmadhātau nirvāṇe śikṣamāṇa ityuttaram / atropapattiḥ / yā hi tathāgatasya tathatā yayāsau tathāgataḥ na sā kṣīyate 'kṣayatvāt [a?] kṣayasya / na ca sā utpadyate va nirudhyate vā jāyate vā bhavati vā vibhavati vā vivicyate vā rajyate vā ākāśībhavati vā dharmībhavatīti vā nirvāti vā / evaṃ śikṣamāṇaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣata ityanena mārgamāha //
body.translated_text: in seclusion, in dispassion, in space, in the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of dharmas), in <s>nirvāṇa</s> — [when] training [thus]' — this is the answer. Here is the justification: that which is the <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, by which he is the <s>Tathāgata</s> — that does not diminish, because of the indestructibility of the indestructible. Nor does it arise, nor cease, nor be born, nor exist, nor perish, nor become secluded, nor become passionate, nor become space-like, nor become <s>dharma</s>-like, nor attain <s>nirvāṇa</s>. 'Training thus, one trains in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>' — by this he states the path.

body.text: buddhabhūmau śikṣata ityanena phalamāha / amṛtadhāturmokṣadhātuḥ / nāthakāmā iti nāthatvakāmāḥ / abhyudgatatetyutkṛṣṭatā / śakunīn dhnanti śākunikāḥ / niṣādā mṛtapā(? mṛgayavaḥ) / dhīvarāḥ kaivartāḥ / urabhrā meṣāḥ / tān dhnantīti aurabhrikāḥ / andho 'cakṣuḥ / badhiro 'śrotraḥ / kāṇa ekākṣaḥ / kuṇṭho vakrabāhuḥ / kubjo bhagnapṛṣṭhaḥ / kuṇiḥ karavikalaḥ / laḍgaḥ saṃhatajānuḥ / khañjo vikalagatiḥ / jaḍo niṣpratibhaḥ / lolo 'sthirapadaḥ / lallo 'karmaṇyajivhaḥ / kalla uccaiḥ śabdaśrāvī / hīnāṅgo ninditāṅgaḥ / vikalāṅga ūnāṅgaḥ / vikṛtāṅgo manuṣyavisadṛśāṅgaḥ / nigacchatīti niṣpādayati / tāmanuprāpnotīti balādipariśuddhim / jānamiṣyāmaḥ paśyayiṣyāma iti / śatrantātkarotyarthe ṇic / ṭilopaḥ / śeṣaṃ subodhaṃ yāvat pāraṃ gacchanti / iti navamī vivṛddhiḥ //
body.translated_text: 'One trains in the <s>Buddha</s>-stage' — by this he states the fruit. '<s>Amṛtadhātu</s>' (realm of the deathless) is the <s>mokṣadhātu</s> (realm of liberation). '<s>Nāthakāma</s>' means those desiring to be protectors. '<s>Abhyudgatatā</s>' means superiority. '<s>Śākunika</s>' — those who strike birds — are bird-hunters. '<s>Niṣāda</s>' means a hunter (deer-catcher). '<s>Dhīvara</s>' means a fisherman. '<s>Urabhra</s>' means sheep; those who strike them are '<s>aurabhrika</s>' (sheep-butchers). '<s>Andha</s>' (blind) means without eyes. '<s>Badhira</s>' (deaf) means without ears. '<s>Kāṇa</s>' (one-eyed) means having one eye. '<s>Kuṇṭha</s>' (cripple-armed) means having crooked arms. '<s>Kubja</s>' (hunchback) means having a broken back. '<s>Kuṇi</s>' (maimed-hand) means having disabled hands. '<s>Laḍga</s>' (knock-kneed) means having joined knees. '<s>Khañja</s>' (lame) means having defective gait. '<s>Jaḍa</s>' (dull) means without brilliance. '<s>Lola</s>' (unsteady) means of unsteady speech. '<s>Lalla</s>' (stammerer) means having an unfit tongue. '<s>Kalla</s>' (hard-of-hearing) means one who hears [only] loud sounds. '<s>Hīnāṅga</s>' means having despised limbs. '<s>Vikalāṅga</s>' means having deficient limbs. '<s>Vikṛtāṅga</s>' means having limbs unlike those of humans. '<s>Nigacchati</s>' means accomplishes. 'He attains that' means [he attains] the purification of strength and the rest. 'We shall know, we shall see' — the causative suffix <s>ṇic</s> is in the sense of 'to do,' from the root [ending in] <s>śatṛ</s>. <s>Ṭilopa</s> [applies]. The rest is easily understood, up to 'they go to the far shore.' This is the ninth increase.

body.text: tadyathāpītyādi punaraparātprāk / suvarṇajātarūpādayaḥ gobalīvardanyāyena / ūṣarāḥ sakṣāramṛttikāḥ / ujjaṅgalā ucca(?)nirjalāḥ / tṛṇaṃ vīraṇādi / khāṇḍaḥ su(śu)ṣkatarukīlakaḥ / kaṇṭakādhānaḥ kaṇṭakīmadanādirvividhāste yeṣu / śeṣaṃ subodham / iti daśamī //
body.translated_text: 'As for example' and so on, [is to be taken] before 'again another.' Gold, <s>jātarūpa</s>, and the like are [explained] by the principle of 'cow and bull' [i.e., they are synonymous]. '<s>Ūṣara</s>' means [land] with alkaline soil. '<s>Ujjaṅgala</s>' means high(?) and waterless. '<s>Tṛṇa</s>' means <s>vīraṇa</s> grass and the like. '<s>Khāṇḍa</s>' means a dry tree-stump peg. '<s>Kaṇṭakādhāna</s>' means those places in which various thorny plants such as <s>madana</s> and the like [grow]. The rest is easily understood. Thus the tenth [topic]. //

body.text: punaraparādi punaraparātprāk / cakravartirājyaṃ saṃvartate 'smāditi tat saṃvartanīyam / ityekādaśī //
body.translated_text: 'Again another' and so on, [is to be taken] before 'again another.' '<s>Cakravartin</s> sovereignty evolves from this' — therefore it is called '<s>saṃvartanīya</s>' (that which causes evolution). Thus the eleventh [topic]. //

body.text: punaraparādi punaraparātprāk / śakraḥ saṃvartate 'smāditi tatsaṃvartanīyam / iti dvādaśī //
body.translated_text: 'Again another' and so on, [is to be taken] before 'again another.' '<s>Śakra</s> evolves from this' — therefore it is '<s>saṃvartanīya</s>.' Thus the twelfth [topic]. //

body.text: punaraparādi punaraparātprāk / brahmā saṃvartate 'smāditi tatsaṃvartanīyam / iti trayodaśī //
body.translated_text: 'Again another' and so on, [is to be taken] before 'again another.' '<s>Brahmā</s> evolves from this' — therefore it is '<s>saṃvartanīya</s>.' Thus the thirteenth [topic]. //

body.text: punaraparādi jīvitendriyavākyātprāk / kuśalasasyaprarohavirodhino rāgadveṣamohāḥ khilāḥ / vicikitsā satyaratneṣu vimatiḥ / īrṣyā parasampattau vyāroṣaḥ / śeṣāḥ ṣaṭ pāramitāvipakṣāḥ / śeṣaṃ subodham / iti caturdaśī //
body.translated_text: 'Again another' and so on, [is to be taken] before the statement on the life-faculty. '<s>Khila</s>' (waste-land [= mental defilements]) are <s>rāga</s> (passion), <s>dveṣa</s> (hatred), and <s>moha</s> (delusion), which obstruct the sprouting of wholesome crops. '<s>Vicikitsā</s>' (doubt) is uncertainty regarding the [Three] Jewels of truth. '<s>Īrṣyā</s>' (jealousy) is resentment at others' prosperity. The remaining six are the adversaries of the <s>pāramitās</s>. The rest is easily understood. Thus the fourteenth [topic]. //

body.text: tadyathāpītyādi sa cetpunarityataḥ prāk / ajñāna iti prajñāpāramitāvipakṣe / puṇyāgraḥ puṇyairagraḥ / tadeva darśayitumāha tatkimityādi / buddhaviṣayo buddhadharmasākalyam / vaśavartī vṛṣabhiḥ / tabhdāvastattā / vikrīḍitaṃ ṛddhiprātihāryeṇa / siṃhanādanadanamanuśāsanīprātihāryeṇa / buddhānāṃ sampattirubhayāryasaṃghaiścaryam / vyavacārayati parijñānāt / na ca prativahati teṣvanavasthānāt / śeṣaṃ subodham / iti pañcadaśī //
body.translated_text: 'As for example' and so on, [is to be taken] before 'if moreover he.' '<s>Ajñāna</s>' (ignorance) is the adversary of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>. '<s>Puṇyāgra</s>' means foremost in merit. To show that very [point], he says 'what then' and so on. '<s>Buddhaviṣaya</s>' (the domain of the <s>Buddha</s>) is the totality of <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>. '<s>Vaśavartī</s>' (one who has mastery) [is explained] by [the synonym] '<s>vṛṣabhi</s>' (bull). '<s>Tattvā</s>' means <s>tathatā</s> (suchness). '<s>Vikrīḍita</s>' (sport) is through the miracle of supernatural power. 'Lion's roar-teaching' is through the miracle of instruction. 'The accomplishment of the <s>Buddhas</s>' is the wonder of both noble <s>Saṅghas</s>. '<s>Vyavacārayati</s>' (he discerns) is because of full understanding. 'Nor does he persist' is because of non-abiding in them. The rest is easily understood. Thus the fifteenth [topic]. //

body.text: sa cetpunarityādyāparivartāntāt / atha tāmapi na sañjānīte / kathamityāha iyaṃ setyādi vāśabdāntam / evamapītyebhireva tribhirākāraiḥ / sa cedevaṃ caratīti tathaivāsaṃjānannasamanupaśyan / iti ṣoḍaśī vivṛddhiḥ //
body.translated_text: 'If moreover he' and so on, up to the end of the chapter. 'Now he does not even recognize that [<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>].' How? — to this he says 'this is' and so on, up to the word '<s>vā</s>.' 'Even so' — by these very three aspects. 'If he thus practices' — thus, not recognizing, not perceiving. Thus the sixteenth [topic] is 'growth' (<s>vivṛddhi</s>). //

body.text: śikṣāyā vācakaḥ parivartaḥ śikṣāparivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: The chapter that expresses the training is the '<s>Śikṣā-parivarta</s>' (Training Chapter). //

body.text: āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ sāratamānāmni pañjikāyāṃ ratnākaraśāntiviracitāyāṃ pañcaśiṃtitamaḥ parivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: In the <s>Pañjikā</s> commentary named <s>Sāratamā</s>, composed by <s>Ratnākaraśānti</s>, on the noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s> — this is the twenty-fifth chapter. //

body.text: 26. māyopamaparivarto nāma ṣaḍviṃśatitamaḥ /
body.translated_text: 26. The twenty-sixth [chapter] is named the '<s>Māyopama-parivarta</s>' (Chapter on Illusion-likeness).

body.text: uktā vivṛddhiḥ / nirūḍhirvaktavyā / ataḥ śāstram-
body.translated_text: Growth (<s>vivṛddhi</s>) has been stated. Maturity (<s>nirūḍhi</s>) is to be stated. Therefore the <s>śāstra</s> [says]:

children.translated_text: The unsurpassed perfection of the <s>dharmas</s> of the three [types of] omniscience,
without abandoning the purpose of beings —

body.text: tribhiḥ sarvajñatvaiḥ saṃgṛhītā dharmāḥ 'trisarvajñatvadharmāḥ' / tāraṇamocanāśvāsanaparinirvāpaṇāni 'sattvārthāḥ' / ataḥ sūtre 'tha khalvityādi viharantīti yāvat / carannapīti kva caran? vivṛddhau / kiṃ caran? dānādīn / cittaṃ krāmatīti gacchatīti prasīdatītyarthaḥ / cittamutpāditamityaho batāhamenāmadhigaccheyamiti / uhyamānāniti hriyamānān / same yukte nirdoṣe / pārime tīra iti nirvāṇe / samṛdhyantāṃ teṣāmiti cittotpādā iti pareṇa sambandhaḥ / abhīpsitāḥ prītikaratvāt / paricintitāḥ punaḥpunarutpādanāt / parigṛhītā aparityāgayogena / buddhadharmāṇāmiti buddhaḥ sarvajñaḥ / tasya dharmāṇāmityayamuddeśaḥ /
body.translated_text: is called maturity (<s>nirūḍhi</s>). // 5-3 //

body.text: tasya nirdeśastribhiḥ sarvajñatvaiḥ sarvajñabhāvaiḥ yataḥ sa sarvajño bhavati sarvajñatā ca svayambhūṃtvaṃ ca, asaṃhāryatā ca / tatra sarvākārasarvadharmasamyagjñānamiha sarvajñatā / svayameva cittādeva bhavantyasya dharmā iti svayaṃbhūḥ / sarvadharmavaśavartītyarthaḥ / tasya dharmāḥ svayaṃbhūtvena ye saṃgṛhītāḥ / nāsya saṃhāramastīti asaṃhāryaḥ /
body.translated_text: The <s>dharmas</s> encompassed by the three omnisciences are 'the <s>dharmas</s> of the three omnisciences.' The rescuing, liberating, comforting, and bringing to final cessation [of beings] are 'the purposes of beings.' Therefore, in the <s>sūtra</s>, 'now then' and so on, up to 'dwelling.' 'Even while practicing' — practicing where? In growth. Practicing what? Giving and the like. 'The mind proceeds' means 'goes' means 'becomes serene' — this is the meaning. 'The mind has been generated' means 'oh, may I attain this!' 'Being carried away' means being taken. '<s>Sama</s>' means appropriate, faultless. 'On the far shore' means in <s>nirvāṇa</s>. 'May they prosper' — the connection with the following [clause] is through 'their thought-generations.' [They are] 'desired' because of being a cause of joy. 'Reflected upon' because of being generated again and again. 'Embraced' by the method of non-abandonment. 'Of the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>' — the <s>Buddha</s> is the omniscient one. 'Of his <s>dharmas</s>' — this is the heading.

body.text: savāsanasarvāvaraṇanirmukta ityarthaḥ / tasya dharmā ye 'saṃhāryatvena saṃgṛhītāsteṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ paripūraṇāya bhavantviti iyatā paripūriruktā //
body.translated_text: RSt_137

body.text: sattvārthāparityāgamāha / na me bhagavannityādinā / imairiti sautro nirdeśaḥ / ato bhisa ais bhavati / ido 'nādeśaśca na bhavati / imairityuktam / katamairityāha / kimitītyādi / kimitiśabdasya kathaṃ nāmetyarthaḥ iti nirūḍhiḥ //
body.translated_text: ) The meaning is: freed from all obscurations together with their latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>). 'His <s>dharmas</s> that are encompassed by indestructibility' — 'may they all be perfected' — by this much, perfection (<s>paripūri</s>) has been stated. //

body.text: cittasya saṃsthitiḥ / sā vaktavyā / samādhirityarthaḥ / ataḥ śāstram-
body.translated_text: He states the non-abandonment of the purpose of beings. With 'not indeed, O <s>Bhagavān</s>' and so on. 'By these' — this is a <s>sautra</s> (scriptural) exposition. Therefore '<s>bhisa</s>' occurs by '<s>ais</s>.' And '<s>ido</s>' — a secondary form — does not occur. 'By these' has been stated. 'By which [ones]?' — to this he says 'what?' and so on. The meaning of the word '<s>kim</s>' is 'how indeed?' — thus maturity (<s>nirūḍhi</s>). //

children.translated_text: The stability of the mind (<s>cittasaṃsthiti</s>) — that is to be stated. <s>Samādhi</s> (concentration) is the meaning. Therefore the <s>śāstra</s> [says]
[129] Likened to a four-continent [world-system], a thousand, a two-thousand, and a three-thousand [world-system] —

body.text: sūtre puṇyabahutvena samādhirukto na sākṣāt / katham? caturdvipakaśca lokadhātuḥ sāhasraśca dvisāhasrakaśca trisāhasrakaśca tairupamāḥ kṛtvā / katamena granthena? yasteṣāṃ bhagavannityādinā abhinirhṛtāni bhagavantītyetadantena / teṣāmiti sarveṣām / tāniti pratirūpān / dharmatā dharmasamūhaḥ svabhāvo vā / palāgreṇeti palapramāṇena pramāṇaṃ grahītuṃ iyanti palānīti / atha kiṃ kasyātropamānam? puṇyaparimāṇasya jambūdvīpādiparimāṇam / śāstra upacāraḥ kṛtaḥ / nanvanumodanāmātrasyaitatpuṇyaparimāṇaṃ na samādheḥ? anumodanāpuṇyānumodanena puṇyabahutvenetyabhiprāyādadoṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>samādhi</s> is declared through the abundance of merit. // 5-4 //

body.text: anumodanāyāḥ paripūraṇārthaṃ tāmakurvatāṃ ca nindārthamāha / evamityādi / mārādhiṣṭhitā iti māreṇa mahāpāpena nirutsāhīkṛtāḥ / na śṛṇvanti śabdataḥ / na jānantyarthataḥ / na paśyantyādarataḥ / na samanvāharantīti nābhimukhīkurvanti / mārapakṣe bhavāḥ mārapākṣikāḥ / tadvadeva mahataḥ sattvārthasya vighātakaraṇāt / mārabhavanebhyaścyutā iti / mārā eva atyantaṃ tatsādharmyāt / abhinirhṛtā iti niṣpāditāḥ / kairityāha / yairityādi / yeṣāmityādi ca /
body.translated_text: In the <s>sūtra</s>, <s>samādhi</s> is stated through the abundance of merit — not directly. How? By making comparisons (<s>upamāḥ kṛtvā</s>) to a four-continent world-system, a thousand-fold, a two-thousand-fold, and a three-thousand-fold [world-system]. By which passage? By 'O <s>Bhagavān</s>, of those' and so on, up to 'O <s>Bhagavatī</s>, have been accomplished.' 'Of those' means 'of all.' 'Those' means 'the replicas.' '<s>Dharmatā</s>' means the collection of <s>dharmas</s>, or the intrinsic nature. 'By the tip of a blade [of grass]' means by <s>pala</s>-measurements — 'so many <s>palas</s>' is to be taken as the measure. Now what is compared to what here? The extent of merit is compared to the extent of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> and so on. In the <s>śāstra</s>, a figurative expression has been made. Objection: This extent of merit belongs only to the act of rejoicing, not to <s>samādhi</s>? — [Reply:] There is no fault, because the intention is [implied by the phrase] 'through the abundance of merit of the rejoicing-merit.'

body.text: evamukta ityādinā anumoditavyāntena śakrapraśaṃsā /
body.translated_text: For the purpose of completing the rejoicing and for the purpose of censuring those who do not perform it, he says 'thus' and so on. '<s>Mārādhiṣṭhita</s>' means those who have been rendered without enthusiasm by <s>Māra</s> the great evil one. 'They do not hear' — verbally. 'They do not know' — in meaning. 'They do not see' — with respect. 'They do not attend to' means they do not face [it]. 'Those who belong to <s>Māra</s>'s side' — beings belonging to <s>Māra</s>'s faction. Just so, because they obstruct the great purpose of beings. 'Fallen from the abodes of <s>Māra</s>' — they are <s>Māras</s> themselves, due to their extreme similarity [to <s>Māra</s>]. '<s>Abhinirhṛtā</s>' means 'accomplished.' By whom? — he says 'by those' and so on. And 'of those' and so on.

body.text: yarityādinā yairapītyataḥ prāk / mahāyānaprasthitānāṃ anumodanānuśaṃsāḥ /
body.translated_text: With 'thus spoken' and so on, up to 'one should rejoice' — the praise of <s>Śakra</s>.

body.text: yairapītyādinā prathamacittotpādikānāmapi na kevalamanumoditāni svasantāne cāvaropitānyabhinirhṛtāni ca bhavanti / anumodya cāvaśyaṃ pariṇāmanā kartavyā / yathā ca te kartavye tathānumodanāpariṇāmanāparivartādveditavyam / yathoktaṃ mahatyobhagavatyoḥ- 'tāni kuśalamūlāni anumodyānuttarāyāṃ
body.translated_text: With 'which' and so on, [up to] before 'by those also.' The benefits of rejoicing for those set out on the <s>Mahāyāna</s>.

body.text: samyaksambodhau pariṇāmayitavyāni / tathā ca pariṇāmayitavyāni yathā na cittaṃ citte carati na cānyatra cittāt" ityādi / tadevamanumodanāsahagataṃ kuśalamūlamasya samādherālambanaṃ samyaksambodhau pariṇāmanamākāraḥ / cittasaṃsthitiḥ svabhāvaḥ / kva saṃsthitiḥ? na citte grāhakalakṣaṇena na vānyatreti na sarvadharmeṣu / kiṃ tarhi? sarvadharmatathatāyāmadvayāyāmiti cittasaṃsthitiḥ //
body.translated_text: RSt_138

body.text: darśanaheyā vikalpāḥ sapratipakṣā vaktavyāḥ / tānadhikṛtya śāstram-
body.translated_text: ) perfect awakening (<s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). And one should dedicate thus: such that the mind does not move in the mind, nor [does it move] elsewhere from the mind' — and so on. Thus, the root of virtue accompanied by rejoicing is the object (<s>ālambana</s>) of this <s>samādhi</s>; the dedication toward perfect awakening is the aspect (<s>ākāra</s>); the stability of mind (<s>cittasaṃsthiti</s>) is the intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāva</s>). Where is the stability? Not in the mind with the characteristic of a grasper, nor elsewhere — hence not in all <s>dharmas</s>. What then? In the <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) of all <s>dharmas</s>, which is non-dual — thus [is] the stability of mind. //

children.translated_text: The conceptualizations to be abandoned by seeing (<s>darśanaheya</s>), together with their antidotes, are to be stated. Regarding those, the <s>śāstra</s> [says]

children.text: pravattau ca nivṛttau ca pratyekaṃ tau navātmakau /

children.translated_text: [130] In activity and in cessation, each [being] of nine-fold nature,

body.text: dvau tāvadvikalpau 'grāhyau' grāhyasya vikalpanāt / kathaṃ 'vikalpau'? yatastayorātmā na yathāviṣayaṃ vitathaḥ kalpo vikalpa iti kṛtvā / tau punaḥ kasminviṣaye? pravṛttipakṣe ca / 'pratyekaṃ' ityubhayorapi pakṣayoḥ / 'navātmakau' navaprabhedau //
body.translated_text: the two conceptualizations of the graspable (<s>grāhya</s>) should be known as having unreal objects. // 5-5 //

children.translated_text: The conceptualizations of substance (<s>dravya</s>), designation (<s>prajñapti</s>), existent (<s>sat</s>), and being (<s>sattva</s>) are considered as of the grasper (<s>grāhaka</s>);
each is nine-fold, by the division of ordinary persons and noble ones. // 5-6 //

body.text: aparau dvau 'vikalpau grāhakau' grāhakasya vikalpanāt / kathaṃ dvau? yathākramaṃ dravyasataḥ prajñaptisataśca sattvasya vikalpanāt / tatra prathamaṃ pṛthagjanānāṃ dvitīyamāryāṇām / tāvapi 'pratyekaṃ navātmakau' / kathaṃ tau grāhakavikalpau? asata eva grāhakasya kalpanāt / vitatho hi kalpo vikalpaḥ / etadevāha-
body.translated_text: The other two 'conceptualizations [are] of the grasper' — because of the conceptualization of the grasper. How are they two? Because of the conceptualization of being — of that which is existent as substance, and of that which is existent as designation, respectively. Therein, the first [belongs] to ordinary persons, the second to noble ones. Those too are 'each nine-fold.' How are they conceptualizations of the grasper? Because of the conceptualization of a grasper that is [in fact] non-existent. For a false imagination is a <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptualization). This very [point] he states:

children.text: grāhyau cenna tathā sto 'rthau kasya tau grāhakau matau /
children.translated_text: If the graspable [objects] are not thus real, for whom are those [conceptualizations] considered as of the grasper?
Thus, emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) with respect to the nature of a grasper is the characteristic of those two [conceptualizations]. // 5-7 //

body.text: 'grāhakabhāvena' iti grāhakasattvarūpeṇa / 'tayoḥ' iti grāhakavikalpayoḥ //
body.translated_text: 'With respect to the nature of a grasper' — with respect to the reality of a grasping being. 'Of those two' — of the conceptualizations of the grasper. //

body.text: catvāropyamī vikalpā viṣayabhedena pratyekaṃ navavidhāḥ / ata ādyamadhikṛtya śāstram-
body.translated_text: All four of these conceptualizations are each nine-fold according to the difference of object. Therefore, regarding the first, the <s>śāstra</s> [says]:

children.translated_text: This [conceptualization] pertains to intrinsic nature, lineage, practice, realization,
the object and non-error of knowledge, to the antidote and its opposite, // 5-8 //
to oneself, to attainment, to the agent, its characteristic function, and to the fruit —
the conceptualization based on the side of activity is held to be nine-fold. // 5-9 //

body.text: 'kartṛtatkāritrakriyāphale ' iti kartari tatkāritrakriyāphale cetyarthaḥ / svabhāvādinavakaṃ pravṛttipakṣaḥ / bodhisattvopādeyatvāt / tadadhiṣṭhāna eṣa vikalpaḥ / tasmātprathamaḥ / ataḥ prathamaṃ vikalpamadhikṛtya sūtre navavākyāni /
body.translated_text: 'Agent, its characteristic function, and fruit' means: in the agent, in the characteristic function of that, and in the fruit — this is the meaning. The nine-fold [set] beginning with intrinsic nature is the side of activity. Because it is to be taken up by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. This conceptualization is based on that. Therefore [it is] the first. Hence, regarding the first conceptualization, there are nine statements in the <s>sūtra</s>.

body.text: tatrādyamadhikṛtya sūtram / subhutirāha / kathaṃ ca bhagavan māyopamamityādi tadyathāpityataḥ prāk / māyākāranirmitaṃ gajādikaṃ māyā / tadvadanyadapi yat khyāti nehāsti tat māyopamam / ta thā ca cittam / grāhakalakṣaṇatvāt grāhakasya cāsattvāt / na hyasati grāhye grāhakaṃ yuktam / grāhyābhāvaḥ kathamiti cet / yadi jñānenārthaḥ prakāśyeta syādgrāhyatvam / na ca prakāśyeta / aprakāśasya prakāśyavirodhāt / athārthaḥ prakāśātmaiva / kiṃ tasya jñānena? tasmānmāyopamaṃ cittaṃ tadasat kathamabhisaṃbudhyata iti praśnaḥ / uttaraṃ tatkimityādinā / no hīdaṃ no dīdamityasattvāditi bhāvaḥ / anyatretyanyam / taṃ dharmamityātmānam / no hīdamiti tasyātyantamasattvāditi bhāvaḥ /
body.translated_text: Regarding the first of those, the <s>sūtra</s> [says]: <s>Subhūti</s> says — 'How, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is [everything] illusion-like?' and so on, [up to] before 'as for example.' That which is created by the illusion-maker — elephants and the like — is <s>māyā</s> (illusion). Similarly, anything else that appears but does not exist here is illusion-like (<s>māyopama</s>). And so too is the mind. Because of having the characteristic of a grasper, and because of the non-existence of the grasper. For when the graspable is non-existent, a grasper is not appropriate. 'How is the graspable non-existent?' — if the object were illuminated by knowledge, there would be graspability. But [the object] is not illuminated — because of the contradiction between what is non-luminous and what is to be illuminated. Or, if the object is itself of the nature of luminosity, what need has it for knowledge? Therefore the mind is illusion-like; it is non-existent — how then can it attain <s>abhisaṃbodhi</s> (awakening)? — this is the question. The answer is with 'what then' and so on. 'Not this, nor not-this' — because of non-existence — this is the purport. 'Otherwise' means 'another.' 'That <s>dharma</s>' means 'itself.' 'Not indeed this' — because of its utter non-existence — this is the purport. /

body.text: etadeva sphuṭīkartumāha / nāhamityādi / astīti nāstīti vā nirdeśaṃ nopaiti / asato 'vijñātarūpasya vidhipratiṣedhābhyāmasambandhāditi bhāvaḥ / yopi dharma ityādi sugamam / tasmāttarhītyādi / tarhiśabdo 'kṣamāyām / tasmāditi grāhakalakṣaṇatvāt / grāhakatvasya vāyogāt / atyantagrahaṇena caitadāha / yatheyaṃ svena lakṣaṇena grāhakatvena śūnya tathā sarvaiḥ saṃprayogibhiḥ, teṣāmapi grāhakalakṣaṇatvāt / ālambanabhūtaiśca sarvadharmaiḥ, ālambanasya grāhyalakṣaṇatvāt / dharmāṇāṃ ca yathāyogaṃ grāhyagrāhakalakṣaṇatvāt / kathaṃ punargrāhakau na staḥ? abhede grāhyagrāhakatvāyogāt, aṅgulyagravat / bhede jaḍasya paratopi prakāśāyogāt / ajaḍasya svayameva prakāśāt / nāsau bhāvayitavyaḥ / na punaḥpunarbuddhau niveśyaḥ kharaviṣāṇavat / nāpyasāvityādi / kasyaciddharmasyeti samyaksambodhyādeḥ / āvāhaka āhārakaḥ / nirvāhako niṣpādakaḥ / asato 'kiñcitkaratvāt / pratītyasamutpāda eṣa enaṃ prāpya bodhisattvaḥ saṃbudhyata iti cedāha / kathaṃ cetyādi / na hyasat prāpyata iti bhāvaḥ / anuttarāpītyādi / atyantaviviktā prajñāpāramitāvat / kathaṃ bhavatīti naiva bhavati / atyantāsatoḥ sādhyasādhanatvāyogāditi bhāvaḥ /
body.translated_text: To make this very point clear, he says beginning with 'I do not' and so on. It does not admit of designation as either 'it exists' or 'it does not exist' — because a non-existent [thing] of unrecognized form has no connection with either affirmation or negation — this is the meaning. Beginning with 'Whatever <s>dharma</s>' and so on is easily understood. Beginning with 'Therefore, then' and so on — the word '<s>tarhi</s>' expresses impatience. 'Therefore' means because of having the characteristic of a grasper. Or because of the impossibility of being a grasper. And he states this emphatically with the word '<s>atyanta</s>' (utterly): just as this [<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>] is empty of its own characteristic of being a grasper, so too [it is empty] of all its associates, because they too have the characteristic of a grasper; and of all <s>dharmas</s> that are objects, because the object has the characteristic of the grasped; and because <s>dharmas</s> have the characteristic of grasped and grasper as appropriate. But how are the two — grasper [and grasped] — non-existent? Because in non-difference, the relation of grasped and grasper is impossible — like the tip of a finger [with itself]. In difference, because what is insentient cannot illuminate even to another. And because what is sentient illuminates by itself. 'That should not be cultivated' — it should not be repeatedly imposed upon the mind, like the horn of a hare. Beginning with 'Nor is that' and so on — 'of any <s>dharma</s>' means of <s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s> and the rest. '<s>Āvāhaka</s>' is one who brings in. '<s>Nirvāhaka</s>' is one who accomplishes — because a non-existent [thing] is inefficacious. If one says, 'It is through <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) that the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having attained this, awakens,' he replies beginning with 'How, then?' and so on — because a non-existent [thing] cannot be attained — this is the meaning. Beginning with 'Even unsurpassed' and so on — it is utterly secluded, like <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. 'How does it come to be?' means it does not come to be at all — because for two things that are utterly non-existent, the relation of means and end is impossible — this is the meaning.

body.text: evamukta ityādi / yata eva ata eveti / hetvanurūpatvātphalasyetyarthaḥ / sa cedityādinā hetuṃ paripūrayati / yadi hi saṃjānīte tadā vikalpaḥ syāt na prajñāpāramitā / evamityādinopasaṃhāraḥ / nāpyabhisaṃbudhyata ityabhisaṃbodheravikalpanāditi bhāvaḥ / abhisabudhyate cetyādi / parikalpitena hi rūpeṇa trayamidaṃ nāsti tacchūnyena tu vijñaptirūpeṇāstīti bhāvaḥ / tathāpi saṃvṛttireṣāṃ yathā
body.translated_text: Beginning with 'Thus spoken' and so on. 'For the very reason that, therefore' — the meaning is: because the result conforms to the cause. Beginning with 'If that' and so on, he completes the cause. For if he recognizes [it], there would be conceptualization, not <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Beginning with 'thus' and so on is the conclusion. 'Nor does he fully awaken' — because of the non-conceptualization of awakening — this is the meaning. Beginning with 'And he does awaken' and so on — for by the imagined form, these three do not exist; but by the empty representational form (<s>vijñaptirūpa</s>), they do exist — this is the meaning. Even so, the conventional reality of these, just as

body.text: pratibhāsasamatvāt / śūnyatā tu paramārthaḥ / gambhīre 'rthe caratīti yato 'sminnarthe na śakyate 'nyaiścaritum / duṣkarakāraka iti / yataḥ sa bhagavān sākṣātkartuṃ śaktopi na sākṣātkaroti sattvāvekṣayā / bhāṣitasyārthamiti ābhiprāyikamartham / duṣkaramanyeṣāṃ sukaraṃ bodhisattvasyeti bhāvaḥ / kutaḥ sukaram? upāyakuśalatvāt / sa copāyaḥ prajñāpāramitaiva / atastamevāha tathāhītyādinā / ya iti bodhisattvaḥ / ya iti gambhīro 'rthaḥ / yeneti prajñāpāramitākhyena / athāsyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carataḥ sā caryā kiyatā bhavatītyata āha / sa cedityādi / na saṃsīdatīti na bhajyate / ayamuddeśaḥ / asya nirdeśaḥ ṣoḍhā / nāvalīyata iti nāsyāṃ madhyapremā / na saṃlīyata iti nāsyāṃ mṛdupremā / na vipṛṣṭhībhavatīti nāpremā / nottrasyatīti naināṃ tyaktukāmaḥ / na saṃtrasyatīti na tyajati / na saṃtrāsamāpadyata iti na prabandhena tyajati / tadevaṃ ṣaḍvidhabhaṅgapratiṣedhādetadgamyate yosyāmabhimukhībhūtāyāmatyantaṃ prīyate so 'syāṃ caratīti / aparamāha sa cedityādinā / aparamāha / āsannetyādinā / aparamāha dūrīkṛtetyādinā / iha svabhāvādayo navārthāḥ / pravṛttipakṣe bodhisattvairupādeyatvāt / teṣu vikalpaḥ sammoho 'samyagjñānam / tatrādyaḥ svabhāvavikalpaḥ / svabhāvaḥ svābhiprāyaḥ / ahamanuttarāṃ samyaksambodhimadhigaccheyaṃ tanmārgeṇeti / bodhicittamityarthaḥ / tasmin vikalpaḥ / ākāro bodheḥ prajñāpāramitāyāśca śūnyatāyāṃ yadajñānamasamāhitajñānaṃ ca / samāhitajñāne ca tisro manyanā / ahaṃ carāmi āsannā me mahābodhirahaṃ vā dūre hīnabodheḥ syāmiti / asya pratipakṣaḥ kathaṃ bhagavanmāyopamaṃ cittamityata ārabhya tadyathāpītyataḥ prāk / iti svabhāvavikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: — because of the sameness of appearance. But emptiness is the ultimate reality. 'He practices in the profound meaning' — because others cannot practice in this meaning. 'One who does what is difficult' — because that <s>Bhagavān</s>, though capable of directly realizing [it], does not directly realize [it] out of consideration for beings.

body.text: tadyathāpītyādi / āsannā me mahābodhirdūre hīnabodhī yatohaṃ buddhagotra iti sammohaḥ / asya pratipakṣaḥ / ākāśasamatvādgotrasya tadvadavikalpā prajñāpāramiteti gotravikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: Beginning with 'Just as, for example' and so on. '<s>Bodhi</s> is near to me, the inferior <s>bodhi</s> is far, because I am of the <s>Buddha</s>-lineage' — this is the delusion. Its antidote: because the lineage is equal to space, similarly <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is non-conceptual — this is the conceptualization regarding lineage (<s>gotravikalpa</s>).

body.text: tadyathāpītyādi / asti me pratipattisamudāgamaḥ / tata āsannā me mahābodhirdūre hīnabodhī iti saṃmohaḥ / tasya pratipakṣaḥ samudāgamasya māyāpuruṣopamatvādavikalpā prajñāpāramiteti pratipatsamudāgamavikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: Beginning with 'Just as, for example' and so on. 'I have the accomplishment of practice; therefore <s>bodhi</s> is near to me, the inferior <s>bodhi</s> is far' — this is the delusion. Its antidote: because the accomplishment [of practice] is like a man created by illusion, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is non-conceptual — this is the conceptualization regarding the accomplishment of practice (<s>pratipatsamudāgamavikalpa</s>).

body.text: tadyathāpītyādi / pratibhāsaḥ pratibimbaḥ / jñānapratibhāsasya pratibhāsatvenaiva yad jñānaṃ na tvālambanasya ca / seha jñānasyālambanā bhrāntiḥ / sā mama jātā / tata āsannā me mahābodhirdūre hīnabodhī iti saṃmohaḥ / tasya pratipakṣaḥ pratibimbavadavikalpā prajñāpāramiteti ālambanābhrāntivikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: Beginning with 'Just as, for example' and so on. '<s>Pratibhāsa</s>' is reflection. The knowledge that arises from the appearance of knowledge being merely an appearance — that is knowledge, not [knowledge] of the object. Here, the appearance of the object to knowledge is error. 'That has arisen in me; therefore <s>bodhi</s> is near to me, the inferior <s>bodhi</s> is far' —

body.text: tadyathāpītyādi / pratipakṣo hantā vipakṣo hantavya iti saṃmohaḥ / asya pratipakṣo yathā tathāgatasya priyāpriyau na stastadvadavikalpāyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caratopīti pratipakṣavipakṣavikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: Beginning with 'Just as, for example' and so on. 'The antidote is the destroyer, the adversary is what is to be destroyed' — this is the delusion. Its antidote: just as for the <s>Tathāgata</s> there is neither dear nor disagreeable, so too for one who practices the non-conceptual <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> — this is the conceptualization regarding antidote and adversary (<s>pratipakṣavipakṣavikalpa</s>).

body.text: yathaiva hītyādi abhūtakalpanāt kalpaḥ / tasya vigamakalpanādvikalpaḥ / tau prahīṇau yathā tathāgatasya tadvadavikalpāyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caratopi / tatra kalpavigamo vikalpaḥ svādhigamasaṃmohaḥ / tasya pratipakṣaḥ kalpavikalpaprahīṇā prajñāpāramiteti svādhigamavikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: Beginning with 'Just as indeed' and so on. '<s>Kalpa</s>' is from unreal imagination. '<s>Vikalpa</s>' (conceptualization) is from imagining its cessation. Both have been abandoned just as by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, so too for one who practices the non-conceptual <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. There, the cessation of imagination is conceptualization — [it is] the delusion regarding one's own realization (<s>svādhigamasaṃmoha</s>). Its

body.text: tadyathāpītyādi / prajñāpāramitāmahaṃ bhāvayāmi / tata āsannā me mahābodhirdūre hīnabodhī iti kartari sammohaḥ / tasya pratipakṣaḥ / kartustathāgatanirmitopamatattadvadeva kartari nirvikalpā prajñāpāramiteti kartari vikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: Beginning with 'Just as, for example' and so on. 'I cultivate <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>; therefore <s>bodhi</s> is near to me, the inferior <s>bodhi</s> is far' — this is the delusion regarding the agent. Its antidote: because the agent is like one created by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, similarly <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is non-conceptual regarding the agent — this is the conceptualization regarding the agent (<s>kartṛvikalpa</s>).

body.text: tadyathāpītyādi / sa ca tathāgatanirmito yadarthaṃ nirmitastacca kṛtyaṃ karoti / na ca tāṃ kriyāṃ vikalpayati / tadvadbodhisattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāvayati na ca vikalpayatīti pratipakṣaḥ / bodhivikalpanaṃ kriyāphalavikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: Beginning with 'Just as, for example' and so on. And that [being] created by the <s>Tathāgata</s> performs the task for which it was created, yet does not conceptualize that action. Similarly, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> cultivates <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> yet does not conceptualize — this is the antidote. The conceptualization regarding awakening (<s>bodhivikalpa</s>) —

body.text: tadyathāpītyādi [ā parivartā]ntāt / śilpinā yadartha dāruyantramayaḥ pumānkṛtaḥ sa tadartha karoti na vikalpayati / tadvadbodhisattvo bodhaye, na (tāṃ) bodhiṃ prāpsyati na ca tāṃ vikalpayatīti pratipakṣaḥ / bodhivikalpanaṃ kriyāphalavikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: Beginning with 'Just as, for example' and so on [up to the end of the chapter]. The wooden puppet made by the artisan for a purpose performs that purpose yet does not conceptualize. Similarly, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> [strives] for awakening, yet he will not attain that awakening and does not conceptualize it — this is the antidote.

body.text: māyopamacittopalakṣitaḥ parivarto māyopamaparivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: The chapter characterized by the mind being like an illusion is the '<s>Māyopama</s>' (Illusion-like) Chapter.

body.text: āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ sāratamānāmni pañjikāyāṃ ratnākaraśāntiviracitāyāṃ ṣaḍiṃvaśatitamaḥ parivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: In the <s>Pañjikā</s> commentary named <s>Sāratama</s>, composed by <s>Ratnākaraśānti</s>, on the noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s> — this is the Twenty-sixth Chapter.

body.text: 27. sāraparivarto nāma saptaviṃśatitamaḥ /
body.translated_text: 27. The twenty-seventh [chapter] is named the '<s>Sāra</s>' (Essence) Chapter.

body.text: māyopamaparivartasyānte prathamo grāhyavikalpa uktaḥ / itare trayo vikalpā iha sāraparivarte vaktavyāḥ / tatra dvitīyaṃ grāhyavikalpamadhikṛtya śāstram /
body.translated_text: At the end of the <s>Māyopama</s> chapter, the first conceptualization of the grasped has been stated. The other three conceptualizations are to be explained here in the <s>Sāra</s> chapter. Regarding the second conceptualization of the grasped, the treatise [states] —

children.translated_text: Because of falling into existence and quiescence, and in the deficiency of realization,
And in the absence of support, and in the impairment of one who has entered the path; [5-10]
In dependence on another's guidance, in the reversal from the summary teaching,
In partiality, in multiplicity, in the delusions of position and departure; [5-11]
And in following behind — this conceptualization is ninefold,
Based on the side of cessation, and arises in the minds of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and the like. [5-12]

body.text: adhigamanyūnatādau doṣe bodhisattvapraheye[']bhāvānnivṛttipakṣādhiṣṭhāno navavidhaśca śrāvakādīnāṃ manobhavastairaheyatvāt / etānāha atha khalvityādinātha khalu bhagavānityataḥ prāk / tatra śāriputra ekamāha / tataḥ subhūtirekaṃ tato devaputrāstrīn / punaḥ subhūtiścaturaḥ / ihāpi pratipakṣāḥ paṭhyante / tadviparyayeṇa vikalpā gamyante / sāre batāyamiti bataśabdo harṣe / utkṛṣṭaṃ phalaṃ samyaksaṃbodhiḥ / so 'nusāraḥ / tannimittaṃ bodhisattvaścarati / katama ityāha / ya ityādi / prajñāpāramitā cātra ubhayanairātmyajñānamucyate / tasyāṃ carataḥ saṃsāre nātyantamudvego nirvāṇe nātyantamutkaṇṭhā / ubhayoranupalambhatvāt / tatoyamanuttarāṃ samyaksambodhimadhigacchediti pratipakṣaḥ / anyathā tu saṃsāre vā patetpañcabhiḥ pāramitābhiḥ / nirvāṇe vā pudgalanairātmyajñānāt / ata eva ca vinā prajñāpāramitayā bodhisattvo bodhisattvākhyāṃ na labhate / tadyathā samyagabhiṣiktopi cakravartinaḥ putraścakravartiśabdaṃ vinā saptabhī ratnairityadhigamanyūnatāvikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: Because faults such as the deficiency of realization and the like — which are to be abandoned by <s>Bodhisattvas</s> — do not exist [in <s>Śrāvakas</s>], [this conceptualization] is 'based on the side of cessation' and is ninefold; and it arises in the minds of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and the like, because it is not to be abandoned by them. These he states beginning with 'Now then' and so on, up to before 'Now then, the <s>Bhagavān</s>.' There, <s>Śāriputra</s>

body.text: saraṇaṃ sāraḥ / karma dharmaḥ / gamyatā sudharṣaṇatetyarthaḥ / viparyayādasāro durddharṣaṇatā / ataḥ pāramitānāṃ durddharṣaṇatve sa carati yaścarati prajñāpāramitāyām / sā hi tāsāṃ parigrahasamarthā / tadyathā strīṇāṃ sadhūrtake nagaramārge śasrapāṇipuruṣa iti pratipakṣaḥ / anyathā sudharṣaṇāḥ syuriti parigrahābhāvavikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Refuge' (<s>saraṇa</s>) is the 'essence' (<s>sāra</s>). '<s>Karma</s>' is <s>dharma</s>. '<s>Gamyatā</s>' (attainability) means invincibility (<s>sudharṣaṇatā</s>) — this is the meaning. By the opposite, 'essencelessness' (<s>asāra</s>) is vulnerability (<s>durdharṣaṇatā</s>). Therefore, regarding the invincibility of the <s>pāramitās</s>, he who practices <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> practices that. For that [<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>] is capable of supporting them.

body.text: etadabhavaditi namaskartavyā ityādyatha khalvityataḥ prāk / namaskartavyāsta iti kutaḥ? pratipattisākalyādaparādhīnatvāduddeśānivṛtteśca / ata evāhuḥ yairityādi / sarvamabhinirhṛtānīti pratipattitaḥ pañcabhiḥ pāramitābhiḥ / ihetyubhayanairātmyavedinyām / ata eva gambhīrāyāmiti pratipakṣaḥ / tasyāmacaratāṃ pratipattivaikalyaṃ syāt / tataste mārādibhiḥ suyodhanāḥ syuḥ / akṣatakavacā iva yodhāḥ pratiyodhairiti pratipattivaikalyavikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'This occurred' — [they] are to be venerated — and so on, up to before 'Now then.' 'They are to be venerated' — why? Because of the completeness of practice, because of non-dependence on others, and because of non-reversal from the summary teaching. For this very reason they say beginning with 'By those' and so on. 'All have been brought forth' — through practice, completely

body.text: tathetyādi / ye ceti vartate / tatheti prajñāpāramitāpradhānāsu pāramitāsu caranta iti hetau śatṛpratyayaḥ / tathā caraṇādityarthaḥ / tataḥ kimityāha / bhūtakoṭirityādi / yathā hi cakravartī pradhānaṃ mahāprabhāvatvāt, kodrārātīḥ (? koṭṭarājānaḥ)
body.translated_text: Beginning with 'Thus' and so on. 'And those who' is understood. 'Thus' — 'practicing in the <s>pāramitās</s> headed by <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>' — the <s>śatṛ</s> (present participle) suffix is in the causal sense; meaning 'because of practicing thus.' 'What then?' — he says beginning with '<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>' (reality-limit) and so on. For just as a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch) is the chief,

body.text: tadanuvartinastathaiva prajñāpāramitā pradhānaṃ tayā saṃsāranirvāṇayoranupalambhāt / yathā te pāramitābhiḥ saṃsāre na pātyante tathā pudgalanairātmyajñānavaśena bhūtakoṭiṃ na sākṣātkurvanti / yadi tu prajñāpāramitā pradhānaṃ na syāt tadā hīnabodhiṃ bhūtakoṭiṃ sākṣātkuryureveti parapratyayagāmitvavikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: Those who follow him [are likewise]; in the same way, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is the chief — because through it there is non-apprehension of both <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Just as through the <s>pāramitās</s> they are not made to fall into <s>saṃsāra</s>, so too through the knowledge of the selflessness of the person (<s>pudgalanairātmya</s>) they do not directly realize the <s>bhūtakoṭi</s> (reality-limit). If

body.text: anenāpītyādi / aneneti vakṣyamāṇena / tamevāhurya ityādinā na sākṣātkurvantīti / kutaḥ? uddeśaḥ samyaksaṃbodhau litsā / kutastasmādanivṛttiḥ? yato na tāvatprajñāpāramitā tato nivartate tadarthameva tasyāṃ caraṇāt / nāpītarāḥ / tadanupraviṣṭānāṃ tāsāmapyanivṛtteḥ / tadyathā sarvāḥ kunadyo mahānadīmanupraviśya samudrameva gacchanti na nivartata ityuddeśanivṛttikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: "By this too" and so on. "By this" means by what is to be stated. [The passage from] "they bring to that very" up to "they do not directly realize" — from what? The summary (<s>uddeśa</s>) is the aspiration for <s>samyaksambodhi</s> (perfect awakening). From what does the non-regression [follow]? Because <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> does not turn back from that, since it is practiced for that very purpose. Nor do the others [turn back], because even those that have entered into it do not turn back. Just as all small rivers, having entered a great river, go to the ocean alone and do not turn back — thus, the conceptual construction of the non-regression of the summary.

body.text: navāpyete vikalpā mahatyorbhagavatyo svārthasampattimadhikṛtya yojitāḥ / ataḥ prādeśikatvanānātvavikalpau yathā tayoruktau tathā tāvad brūmaḥ / pāramitāpañcakaṃ vāmahastavat / ṣaṣṭhī dakṣiṇahastavat / ubhābhyāṃ sarvakṛtyeṣu vyāpārasiddheriti pratipakṣaḥ / yadi tu dakṣiṇahastaprāyā ṣaṣṭhī na syāttadā prādeśikaḥ syādvyāpāra iti prādeśikavikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: These nine conceptual constructions too have been applied with regard to the accomplishment of one's own benefit in the two great <s>Bhagavatīs</s>. Therefore, we shall first state the conceptual constructions of partiality and diversity as they are stated in those [two texts]. The group of five <s>pāramitās</s> is like the left hand. The sixth is like the right hand. Through both, the accomplishment of activity in all tasks [is achieved] — this is the antidote (<s>pratipakṣa</s>). But if the sixth, which is predominantly like the right hand, were absent, then the activity would be partial — thus, the conceptual construction of partiality.

body.text: yathā hi nānārasāḥ kunadīmahānadyo mahāsamudramanupraviśyaikarasā bhavanti tathā nānārasāḥ pañca pāramitāḥ ṣaṣṭhīmanupraviśyaikarasā bhavantīti pratipakṣaḥ / nānārasāḥ tathaiva tāḥ samyaksambodhāvapīti nānātvavikalpaḥ / asyāṃ tu bhagavatyāṃ parārthasannāhamadhikṛtya dvāvimau vikalpau subhūtirāhetyādinā / atha khalvityādinā tatra sannahyanta ityanena duṣkaratvaṃ darśitamanantānāṃ sattvānāmarthasya kartumaśakyatvāt / tathāpyevameva sannāhaḥ kartavya īdṛśīṃ mahāśayatāmantareṇa svaparārthayoḥ kartumaśakyatvāditi pratipakṣaḥ / sarvasattvānāmarthasya kenacidakaraṇādātmavineyānāmarthāya sannāhaḥ kartavya iti prādeśikatvavikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: Just as rivers of diverse flavors, both small and great, having entered the great ocean, become of one flavor, so too the five <s>pāramitās</s> of diverse flavors, having entered the sixth, become of one flavor — this is the antidote. [But] they remain of diverse flavors just as they are, even in <s>samyaksambodhi</s> (perfect awakening) — this is the conceptual construction of diversity. But in this <s>Bhagavatī</s>, these two conceptual constructions are [presented] with regard to the armor for the benefit of others, beginning with "<s>Subhūti</s> said" and so on. Beginning with "now then" and so on — by "they don the armor for that" the difficulty is shown, because it is impossible to accomplish the benefit of infinite beings. Nevertheless, such an armor must indeed be donned, because without such great-mindedness it is impossible to accomplish either one's own or others' benefit — this is the antidote. Because no one can accomplish the benefit of all beings, the armor should be donned for the benefit of those who are one's own trainees — this is the conceptual construction of partiality.

body.text: nānātvavikalpapratipakṣaḥ samatā / tāmeva vivakṣuḥ paramaduṣkaratvamāha te cetyādinā / vainayikā iti vinayārhāḥ sattvāḥ / tathāpi kasya duṣkaratetyata āha / evaṃ cetyādi / dṛṣṭāntena dṛḍhīkartumāha / ākāśamityādi / tatkasya hetoriti kutaḥ sādharmyādityarthaḥ / ata uttaraṃ ākāśetyādi / anenetyupasaṃhāraḥ / punadrdṛḍhīkartumāha / ākāśenetyādi / ākāśopamaiḥ sattvairityarthaḥ / kuto vivāda ityāha / ayaṃ cetyādi veditavyāntam / caśabdo hetau / vivādaḥ kalahaḥ / sattvānayaṃ vinetukāmaste cāsattvātpariharantīti kalahaḥ / vainayiketyādi / yathā ca vineyā na santi tathā vinayitāpi / tata ubhayāsattayā sutarāṃ paramaduṣkaratā / evamiyaṃ bodhisattvena sarvasattvātmasamatā draṣṭavyā yataḥ śaknuyāt
body.translated_text: The antidote to the conceptual construction of diversity is equality (<s>samatā</s>). Wishing to express precisely that, he states the supreme difficulty beginning with "they" and so on. "<s>Vainayika</s>" means beings who are worthy of being trained. "Even so, for whom is it difficult?" — to this he says: "even thus" and so on. To confirm by analogy, he says: "space" and so on. "For what reason?" means "from what analogy?" — this is the meaning. The answer begins with "space" and so on. "By this" is the conclusion. To further confirm, he says: "by space" and so on — meaning "by beings who are like space." "From what arises dispute?" he says: "and this" and so on, up to "should be understood." The word "and" (<s>ca</s>) is in the causal sense. "Dispute" (<s>vivāda</s>) is conflict. They wish to train beings, but those [beings] are non-entities, so they abandon [the idea] — this is the conflict. "<s>Vainayika</s>" and so on — just as the trainees do not exist, so too the trainer. Therefore, through the non-existence of both, the supreme difficulty [is all the greater]. "Thus, this equality with all beings should be seen by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, whereby he would be able

body.text: svaparārthau kartum / sa punarasyāṃ caran kathaṃ jñeya ityāha / sa cedityādi / na saṃsīdatīti na khidyate sutarāṃ prīyata ityarthaḥ / tatkasya hetoriti / mattasya prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caraṇaṃ kasya hetornaiva kasyacit / dharmanairātmyādarśanāditi bhāvaḥ / ata uttaraṃ sattvaviviktatayetyādi / evamityādinā draṣṭavyāntenopasaṃhāraḥ / viviktatā hi sarvadharmāṇāṃ samateti vistareṇa pratipakṣaḥ / nānā sattvā nānā dharmāstato nāstyekarasā prajñāpāramiteti nānātvavikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: to accomplish both one's own and others' benefit. How then is one who practices in this [equality] to be recognized?" he says: "if he" and so on. "He does not sink" (<s>na saṃsīdati</s>) means he is not distressed; rather, he is supremely delighted — this is the meaning. "For what reason?" — "the reason for one who is intoxicated [by <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>] to practice in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> — for what reason? — for no reason whatsoever. Because of seeing the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s>" — this is the import. The answer begins with "because of the seclusion of beings" and so on. The conclusion is from "thus" and so on up to "should be seen." For the seclusion of all <s>dharmas</s> is equality — this is the antidote in detail. "Beings are diverse, <s>dharmas</s> are diverse, therefore <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is not of one flavor" — this is the conceptual construction of diversity.

body.text: evaṃ devaputrā ityādi / eva bhāṣyamāṇāyāmiti / evamidānīṃ mayā deśyamānāyāṃ sarvadharmaviviktatāyāmiti caryākāle deśyamānāyāṃ bodhisattvo na saṃsīdatīti sambandhaḥ / na saṃsīdatīti sthānaprasthānayorna muhyati / kena gantavyaṃ kva vā sthātavyamiti / tayaiva sarvadharmasamatāsaṃvedinyā prajñāpāramitayorasaṃmohāt / tathāhi / yena bodhistena gantavyaṃ bodhau sthātavyam / te ca gatisthitī tasyā eva svādhī ne hetuphalāvasthe / tato yena sā gacchati yatra vā tiṣṭhati tatpariṇāmitā api pañca pāramitāstenaiva gacchanti tatraiva tiṣṭhanti / tadyathā cakravartinaścakraratnaṃ yena gacchati yatra vā tiṣṭhati sarvo balakāyastenaiva gacchati tatraiva tiṣṭhatīti pratipakṣaḥ / avijñāḥ pañcapāramitāḥ ṣaṣṭhī nirābhāsā / tataḥ sthānaprasthānayoraniścayaḥ sthānaprasthānaṃ(na)sammohavikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: "Thus, O sons of the gods" and so on. "While it is being thus spoken" — meaning "while this seclusion of all <s>dharmas</s> is being taught as it is now being taught by me" — "during the time of practice" — while it is being taught, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not sink — this is the connection. "Does not sink" means he is not confused about where to stand and where to proceed — "by what should one go, and where should one stand?" Because of the non-confusion through that very <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, which is the awareness of the equality of all <s>dharmas</s>. For thus: one should go by that by which [one goes to] awakening, one should stand in awakening. And those movements of going and standing are under the control of that very [<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>] — being the states of cause and effect. Therefore, wherever she goes and wherever she stands, the five <s>pāramitās</s> that have been dedicated go by that very [path] and stand in that very [place]. Just as the wheel-jewel of a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch) — wherever it goes and wherever it stands, the entire army goes by that very [path] and stands in that very [place] — this is the antidote. "Unknowing" — the five <s>pāramitās</s>; the sixth is without appearance. Therefore, there is uncertainty about standing and proceeding — this is the conceptual construction of confusion about standing and proceeding.

body.text: yata ityādi na saṃsīdatīti prasāditametat / yataśca na saṃsīdati tato gamyate carati prajñāpāramitāyāṃ pūrvameveti śeṣaḥ / anyathā kuto na saṃsīdet / tadyathā cakravartinaścakraratnamagrato gacchati paścādbalakāya iti pratipakṣaḥ / udāraviṣayatvātpañcapāramitāḥ prāk pravartante / sūkṣmaviṣayatvāt pṛṣṭhataḥ ṣaṣṭhīti pṛṣṭhato gamanavikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: "Because" and so on — "he does not sink" — this has been established. "And because he does not sink, from that it is known [that] he practices in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> already beforehand" — this is to be supplied. Otherwise, why would he not sink? "Just as the wheel-jewel of the <s>Cakravartin</s> goes in front, and the army follows behind" — this is the antidote. Because of having a gross object, the five <s>pāramitās</s> operate first. Because of having a subtle object, the sixth [operates] behind — this is the conceptual construction of going behind.

body.text: ityukto dvitīyo grāhyavikalpo navavidhaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus has been stated the second [type], the conceptual construction of the object (<s>grāhyavikalpa</s>), which is ninefold.

body.text: prathamaṃ grāhakavikalpamadhikṛtya śāstram-
body.translated_text: With regard to the first conceptual construction of the subject (<s>grāhakavikalpa</s>), the treatise [states]:

children.translated_text: "The first [conceptual construction] of the subject should be known [through] grasping and releasing,
in mental attention, in the adherence of the elements, and of the triad" // 5-13 //
"and in standing, and in clinging, in the designation of <s>dharma</s>-entities,

children.text: śa(sa)ktau ca pratipakṣe ca yathecchaṃ ca gatikṣatau // 5-14 //
children.translated_text: in attachment, in the antidote, and in the harm of going as one pleases." // 5-14 //

body.text: dravyasannātmā 'prathamo grāhakaḥ' / sa cāsti prajñāpāramitāvat / sā hi kiñcidgṛṇhāti kiñcinmuñcatīti grahaṇamokṣaṇavikalpaḥ / sāpi na gṛṇhāti na muñcatīti pratipakṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: The substantially real self is the "first subject" (<s>grāhaka</s>). And it exists, like <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> — for she grasps something and releases something — thus, the conceptual construction of grasping and releasing. "She too neither grasps nor releases" — this is the antidote.

body.text: gṛhyanta eva dharmāsteṣāṃ manasikārāditi manasikāravikalpaḥ / na sa dharmānmanasikarotīti pratipakṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: "<s>Dharmas</s> are indeed grasped; their mental attention [exists]" — thus, the conceptual construction of mental attention. "He does not mentally attend to <s>dharmas</s>" — this is the antidote.

body.text: manasikarotyeva dharmāstraidhātuke śleṣāditi traidhātukaśleṣavikalpaḥ / nāsau traidhātuke śliṣyatīti pratipakṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: "He indeed mentally attends to <s>dharmas</s>; [he does so] because of adherence to the three realms" — thus, the conceptual construction of adherence to the three realms. "He does not adhere to the three realms" — this is the antidote.

body.text: traidhātuke sthitaḥ kathaṃ tatra na śliṣyatīti sthānavikalpaḥ / nāsau kvacittiṣṭhatīti pratipakṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: "If he abides in the three realms, how does he not adhere there?" — thus, the conceptual construction of standing. "He does not stand anywhere" — this is the antidote.

body.text: satyabhiniveśe kathaṃ na tiṣṭhatīti abhiniveśavikalpaḥ / nāsau kiñcidabhiniviśata iti pratipakṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: "If there is clinging to truth, how does he not stand?" — thus, the conceptual construction of clinging. "He does not cling to anything" — this is the antidote.

body.text: asti bodhisattvasya dharmavastūnāṃ prajñaptiḥ / dānapāramitā śīlapāramitā yāvat sarvākārajñateti sarvavastuprajñaptivikalpaḥ / sāpyasya nāstīti pratipakṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: "The <s>Bodhisattva</s> has designations of <s>dharma</s>-entities — <s>dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of giving), <s>śīlapāramitā</s> (perfection of morality), up to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience in all aspects)" — thus, the conceptual construction of the designation of all entities. "He too does not have that" — this is the antidote.

body.text: śa(sa)kta eva samyaksambodhau tāmabhisambudhyate / anyathā vaimukhyāditi śa(sa)ktivikalpaḥ / aśa(sa)ktāḥ sarvadharmā aparigṛhītāḥ / na cāśa(sa)ktaḥ kiñcidabhisambudhyate / sa cedevaṃ carati carati prajñāpāramitāyāmiti pratipakṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: "He who is attached to <s>samyaksambodhi</s> (perfect awakening) awakens to it; otherwise, because of turning away" — thus, the conceptual construction of attachment. "All <s>dharmas</s> are unattached, ungrasped. And one who is unattached does not awaken to anything. If he practices thus, he practices in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>" — this is the antidote.

body.text: dānapāramitāśūnyā śīlapāramitāśūnyetyevamādi pratipakṣavikalpaḥ / sopi bodhisattvasya nāstīti pratipakṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: "<s>Dānapāramitā</s> is empty, <s>śīlapāramitā</s> is empty" and so on — this is the conceptual construction of the antidote. "That too does not exist for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>" — this is the antidote.

body.text: sarvākāraiḥ sarvadharmāṇāmanupalambhe yathecchagamanaṃ tasya kṣatiḥ / sā bodhisattvasyāstīti yathecchagamanavyāghātavikalpaḥ / sopi tasya nāstīti pratipakṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: "When there is non-apprehension of all <s>dharmas</s> in all aspects, going as one pleases causes harm to him" — "that exists for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>" — thus, the conceptual construction of the harm of going as one pleases. "That too does not exist for him" — this is the antidote.

body.text: amī nava prabhedā mahatyorbhagavatyoruktāḥ / asyāṃ tu sāmānyena dravyasadgrāhakavikalpaṃ sapratipakṣamāha / atha khalvityādinā nāpītyataḥ prāk / jānanneveti na hi bhagavataḥ kiñcidajñātamasti / bodhisattvo mahāsattva iti lokaprasiddhito dravyasatpudgalarūpaḥ sa kena kāraṇena na saṃsīdatīti dravyasadgrāhakavikalpaḥ / tasya pratipakṣo 'nupalambhaḥ / tamevāha / viviktatvādityādinā / asattvādityarthaḥ / sa hi svayamasat kutaḥ saṃsīdatīti /
body.translated_text: These nine subdivisions are stated in the two great <s>Bhagavatīs</s>. But in this [text], he states in general terms the conceptual construction of the substantially real subject together with its antidote, beginning with "nor" and so on, up to before "but indeed." "Some <s>dharma</s>" refers to the <s>skandhas</s> and the like, which are the objects of the designation of self. "He does not sink" — because of his own non-existence. Therefore he says: "of what then" and so on. "Some <s>dharma</s>" means the <s>skandhas</s> and the like, or mind. (

body.text: dvitīyaṃ grāhakavikalpamadhikṛtya śāstram-
body.translated_text: With regard to the second conceptual construction of the subject, the treatise [states]:

children.translated_text: "In the non-deliverance as indicated, in the determination of path and non-path,
in cessation and arising, in connection and disconnection with entities," // 4-15 //
"in standing, in the destruction of the lineage, in the absence of aspiration and cause,
and in the apprehension of the opponent — [this is] the other conceptual construction of the subject." // 4-16 //

body.text: ete nava vikalpāḥ pṛthagjanānāṃ prathamasyaiva bhāvānna teṣāṃ dharmāḥ / tairapraheyatvāt / teṣāṃ pratipakṣaḥ ṣaṣṭhī yathā sūtram / yathā sārathiraśvānāṃ sanmārgeṇa yathoddeśaṃ netā tathā ṣaṣṭhī pañcānāmiti pratipakṣaḥ / ṣaṣṭhyabhāvānniyanturabhāvādyathoddeśāniryāṇavikalpaḥ /
body.translated_text: These nine conceptual constructions belong to ordinary beings (<s>pṛthagjanas</s>), because only the first [type] applies to them; these [second type of] <s>dharmas</s> do not [apply] to them, because they are not to be abandoned by those [ordinary beings]. Their antidote is the sixth [<s>pāramitā</s>], as per the <s>sūtra</s>. "Just as a charioteer (<s>sārathi</s>) guides horses along the right road to the indicated destination, so does the sixth [guide] the five" — this is the antidote. "In the absence of the sixth, because there would be no guide, [there is] the conceptual construction of non-deliverance to the indicated destination."

body.text: sarvākārajñatāmārgo bodhisattvānāṃ mārgaḥ / hīnabodhimārgasteṣāmamārgaḥ / tayoravadhāraṇaṃ ṣaṣṭhyaiveti saiva pratipakṣaḥ / tadabhāve mārgāmārgāvadhāraṇavikalpaḥ /
body.translated_text: The path of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience in all aspects) is the path of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. The path to the lesser awakening is their non-path. The determination of both [is accomplished] by the sixth alone — she herself is the antidote. In her absence, [there would be] the conceptual construction of the inability to determine path and non-path.

body.text: naiṣā kasyaciddharmasyotpādikā nirodhikā vā dharmatāṃ pramāṇīkṛtyeti pratipakṣaḥ / utpādikā buddhadharmāṇāṃ nirodhikā tadāvaraṇānāmityutpādanirodhavikalpaḥ /
body.translated_text: "She is neither a producer nor a destroyer of any <s>dharma</s>, taking <s>dharmatā</s> (the nature of reality) as authoritative" — this is the antidote. "She is a producer of <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> and a destroyer of their obstructions" — this is the conceptual construction of arising and cessation.

body.text: sarvadharmā na saṃyuktā na visaṃyukta iti pratipakṣaḥ / saṃyuktā visaṃyuktā veti saṃyogaviyogavikalpaḥ /
body.translated_text: "All <s>dharmas</s> are neither connected nor disconnected" — this is the antidote. "They are either connected or disconnected" — this is the conceptual construction of connection and disconnection.

body.text: rupādau yāvatsarvākārajñatāyāṃ na sthāsyatīti yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ / sarvadharmāṇāṃ kvacidapyasthitatvāditi pratipakṣaḥ / rūpe yāvatsarvākārajñatāyāṃ sthāsyatīti sthānavikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: "One should make the effort not to stand in form and the rest up to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>" — because all <s>dharmas</s> do not stand anywhere — this is the antidote. "One will stand in form up to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>" — this is the conceptual construction of standing.

body.text: yathā hi phalakāmo bījamavaropya samyak savardhya yāvatphalāni paripācya bhakṣayati / evaṃ mahābodhikāmaḥ pāramitāsu śikṣitvā tābhiḥ sattvānanugṛhya saṃsārānmocayatīti pratipakṣaḥ / bodhau cittamutpādya sattvānupekṣata iti gotravipraṇāśavikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: "Just as one who desires fruit, having planted the seed, properly nurtured [the plant], and finally ripened the fruits, eats them — so one who desires great awakening, having trained in the <s>pāramitās</s>, benefits beings through them and liberates them from <s>saṃsāra</s>" — this is the antidote. "Having generated the mind toward awakening, one neglects beings" — this is the conceptual construction of the destruction of the lineage (<s>gotra</s>).

body.text: prārthito 'rthaḥ prārthanā / sarvadharmavaśavartitāmanuprāptukāmena ṣaṣṭhyāṃ śikṣitavyamiti pratipakṣaḥ / tacca śikṣamāṇe sā na syāditi prārthanābhāvavikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: "Aspiration" (<s>prārthanā</s>) is the desired goal. "One who wishes to attain mastery over all <s>dharmas</s> should train in the sixth" — this is the antidote. "And while training [in it], that [mastery] would not arise" — this is the conceptual construction of the absence of aspiration.

body.text: ṣaṣṭhī hetuḥ sarvadharmāṇāṃ samudra iva sarvaratnānāṃ tayā paribhāvitā hi śukladharmā buddhadharmā bhavantīti pratipakṣaḥ / ṣaṣṭhyabhāve heturna syāditi hetvabhāvavikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: "The sixth is the cause of all <s>dharmas</s>, like the ocean [is the repository] of all jewels; for wholesome <s>dharmas</s> that are cultivated by her become <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>" — this is the antidote. "In the absence of the sixth, there would be no cause" — this is the conceptual construction of the absence of a cause.

body.text: prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carantaṃ traiyadhvikā buddhāḥ samanvāharanti / na ca rūpādito yāvanna sarvākārajñatātaḥ / api tu yatra na rūpādi yāvadyatra na sarvākārajñatā tathā samanvāharantīti pratipakṣaḥ / rūpādito yāvatsarvākārajñatātaḥ samanvāharantīti pratyarthikadharmopalambhavikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: "The <s>Buddhas</s> of the three times recollect the one who practices in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> — and not from form and the rest up to not from <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>; rather, where there is no form and the rest up to where there is no <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>, thus they recollect" — this is the antidote. "They recollect from form and the rest up to from <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>" — this is the conceptual construction of the apprehension of the opponent <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: etepi na va prabhedāḥ mahatyorbhagavatyoruktāḥ / asyāṃ tu sāmānyenaiva prajñaptisaṃgrāhakavikalpaṃ sapratipakṣamāha / nāpītyādinā api tu khalvityataḥ prāk / kaściddharma iti ātmaprajñaptiviṣayaḥ skandhādiḥ / na saṃsīdatīti svayamasattvāt / ata evāha / tatkasyetyādi / kaściddharma iti skandhādi cittaṃ vā /
body.translated_text: These nine subdivisions too are stated in the two great <s>Bhagavatīs</s>. But in this [text], he states in general terms the conceptual construction of the subject that grasps designations, together with its antidote, beginning with "nor" and so on, up to before "but indeed." "Some <s>dharma</s>" refers to the <s>skandhas</s> and the like, which are the objects of the designation of self. "He does not sink" — because of his own non-existence. Therefore he says: "of what then" and so on. "Some <s>dharma</s>" means the <s>skandhas</s> and the like, or mind.

body.text: sopītyādi / yena dharmeṇeti cittena yo dharma iti bodhisattvaḥ / evametadityādirabhyupagamaḥ / iyatā pratipakṣa uktaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'That one too' and so on. 'By which <s>dharma</s>' — by the mind. 'Which <s>dharma</s>' — the <s>bodhisattva</s>. 'It is so' and so on is the acknowledgment. To this extent, the antidote has been stated.

body.text: mā bhūd dravyasatsattvaḥ / ahaṃkāraviṣayaḥ skandhādiśvattaṃ vā bodhisattva iti prajñaptisaṃgrāhakavikalpaścaturthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Lest there be a being existing as a real substance — the object of the sense of 'I,' or the <s>bodhisattva</s> as something that exists in the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) and so on — the fourth [type of] conceptualization is the conceptualization that grasps a designation.
