body.text: evaṃ bhagavatā caturvidhāvikalpapratipakṣabhūtā bhagavatī vistareṇa deśitā / bodhisattvastu tasyāṃ caran yathā jñeyastadāha / api tu khalvityādi / bhāṣyamāṇe granthataḥ / deśyamāne arthataḥ / nirdeśyamāne nirviśeṣaṃ kathanāt / upadiśyamāne rahasyakathanāt / na saṃsīdati na mandībhavati / na viṣīdati khedāt / na viṣādamāpadyate santatakhedāt / nāvalīyate cittanamanāt / na saṃlīyate santataṃ tannamanāt / vipṛṣṭhaṃ vaimukhyāt / bhagnapṛṣṭhaṃ punarasāṃmukhyāt / nottrasyati trāsonmukhatvāt / na saṃtrasyati samyak trāsāt / nainamāpadyate sātatyena / tadā veditavyaṃ caratyasyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāmiti / asyāmacarataḥ saṃsīdanādīnāmavaśyaṃbhāvāt /
body.translated_text: Thus the <s>Bhagavatī</s> (<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>), which is the antidote to fourfold conceptualization, has been taught in detail by the <s>Bhagavān</s>. But how a <s>bodhisattva</s> practicing in it should be known — this he states beginning with '<s>Api tu khalu</s>' and so on. '<s>Bhāṣyamāṇe</s>' — [while it is being] spoken, in terms of the text. '<s>Deśyamāne</s>' — [while it is being] taught, in terms of the meaning. '<s>Nirdeśyamāne</s>' — because of exposition without distinction. '<s>Upadiśyamāne</s>' — because of esoteric instruction. '<s>Na saṃsīdati</s>' — does not become dejected, does not become feeble. '<s>Na viṣīdati</s>' — because of weariness. '<s>Na viṣādamāpadyate</s>' — because of continuous weariness. '<s>Nāvalīyate</s>' — because of the bending of the mind. '<s>Na saṃlīyate</s>' — because of the continuous bending of the mind. '<s>Vipṛṣṭham</s>' — because of turning away. '<s>Bhagnapṛṣṭham</s>' — because of not turning back again. '<s>Nottrasyati</s>' — because of being on the verge of fright. '<s>Na saṃtrasyati</s>' — because of complete fright. '<s>Nainamāpadyate</s>' — because of its continuity. Then one should know: 'he practices in this <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>' — for when one does not practice in it, dejection and the rest inevitably occur.

body.text: subhūtirāhetyādinā pāramitāntena subhūterabhyupagamaḥ / evamityādinā / asyāṃ carato 'nuśaṃsātiśayānāha / anugṛṇhanti viśeṣādhānataḥ / samanvāharanti smaraṇataḥ / tepi tasya buddhā bhagavanto dharma deśayantīti sambandhaḥ / kīdṛśā ityāha / bhikṣusaṃghetyādi / kīdṛśasyetyāha / prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carata ityādi / nāma cetyādi / nāma saṃjñā / gotraṃ gārgyādi / balaṃ kāyabalaṃ buddhibalaṃ ca / varṇaḥ pariśiṣṭā guṇāḥ / rūpaṃ varṇasaṃsthāne / etāni parikīrtayamānāḥ prakarṣeṇa prakarṣarūpam / udānamiti guṇaharṣobhdavāṃ gāthāṃ udānayantyudāharanti / kasya guṇā ityāha tasyetyādi / tadyathāpītyādinā dṛṣṭāntamāha / evamevetyādinā dārṣṭāntikam / kiṃ sarveṣāmityādinā praśnaḥ / uttaraṃ no hīdamityādinā / sarvasaṃgāḥ sarve 'bhūtopalambhāḥ / santi bhagavannityādinā punaḥ praśnaḥ / uttaraṃ santītyādinā / ime ta ityādinopasaṃhāraḥ / aparānapyāha yepītyādinā / imepītyādinopasaṃhāraḥ /
body.translated_text: By '<s>Subhūti</s> said' and so on, up to the end of the <s>pāramitā</s> [section] — <s>Subhūti's</s> acknowledgment. By 'Thus' and so on — he states the surpassing benefits of one who practices in this. '<s>Anugṛṇhanti</s>' — through conferring distinction. '<s>Samanvāharanti</s>' — through recollection. 'Those <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> also teach the <s>Dharma</s> to him' — this is the connection. 'Of what kind?' — to this he says '<s>Bhikṣusaṃgha</s>' and so on. 'Of what kind [of person]?' — to this he says 'One who practices in <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>' and so on. '<s>Nāma</s>' and so on: '<s>nāma</s>' is name. '<s>Gotra</s>' is lineage such as <s>Gārgya</s> and so on. '<s>Bala</s>' is bodily strength and intellectual strength. '<s>Varṇa</s>' means the remaining qualities. '<s>Rūpa</s>' means color and shape. 'Proclaiming these' — in an eminent manner, in an eminent form. '<s>Udāna</s>' — they utter, they recite, a verse expressing the joy of [their] qualities. 'Whose qualities?' — to this he says 'Of that one' and so on. By '<s>Tadyathāpi</s>' and so on, he gives the illustration. By '<s>Evameva</s>' and so on, the illustrated [point]. 'Is it of all?' and so on — the question. The answer [begins with] '<s>No hi</s>' and so on. '<s>Sarvasaṃgāḥ</s>' — all false apprehensions. '<s>Santi Bhagavan</s>' and so on — again the question. The answer [begins with] '<s>Santi</s>' and so on. By 'These are' and so on — the conclusion. He also states others, by '<s>Ye pi</s>' and so on. By 'These too' and so on — the conclusion.

body.text: punaraparamityādinā avinivartanīyānāṃ vaśitā tasyāḥ prāptiḥ / tāmavakrāntāḥ praviṣṭāḥ / buddhairnāmādiparikīrtanasyānuśaṃsamāha / yeṣāṃ khalvityādinā punaraparamityādi / kathamadhimokṣyantītyāha / evametadityādi / teṣāṃ ceti na kevalamakṣobhyasya keṣāmityāha / ye cetyādi teṣāṃ ceti / akṣobhya-tabdodhisattvānām / evamityādinā śravaṇānuśaṃsamupasaṃhṛtya tathātvapratipattyādīnāmanuśaṃsotkarṣamāha / evamanuśaṃsātiśayeṣūkteṣu prakṛtāyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyā viśeṣanirdeśa āparivartāntābhdaviṣyati / taṃ
body.translated_text: By 'Moreover' and so on — the mastery of the irreversible ones (<s>avinivartanīya</s>); the attainment of that [mastery]. '<s>Tām avakrāntāḥ</s>' means 'having entered that.' He states the benefit of the <s>Buddhas'</s> proclamation of names and so on, by 'Of whom indeed' and so on, then 'Moreover' and so on. 'How will they become devoted?' — to this he says 'It is so' and so on. 'And of those' — not only of <s>Akṣobhya</s>; 'of whom?' — to this he says 'And those who' and so on. 'And of those' — of the <s>bodhisattvas</s> of <s>Akṣobhya</s> [and others]. By 'Thus' and so on, having concluded the benefit of hearing, he states the supreme benefit of practicing in accordance with suchness and so on. When these supreme benefits have been stated, a special exposition of the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> under discussion will follow up to the end of the chapter. That

body.text: prastotuṃ subhūtirāha yadā bhagavannityādi / tathatāvinirmukta iti / tathatāmātrasyeva prakhyānāt / parikalpitasya nānāvidhasyāpratibhāsanāt / na kaściddharma upalabhyate / tadā koyamityādi sugamam / tathataiva tāvannopalabhyata iti tasyā agrāhyatvāt / yaḥ sthāsyatīti bodhisattvaḥ /
body.translated_text: — to introduce [it], <s>Subhūti</s> says 'When, O <s>Bhagavān</s>' and so on. '<s>Tathatāvinirmukta</s>' — because only <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) alone is manifest; because the manifold conceptually constructed [reality] does not appear. 'No <s>dharma</s> whatsoever is apprehended.' Then 'Who is this?' and so on — this is easily understood. 'Even <s>tathatā</s> itself is not apprehended' — because of its ungraspability. 'He who will stand' — the <s>bodhisattva</s>.

body.text: sajjatīti vihanyata ityarthaḥ / ārabhyeti adhikṛtya / dharmavādīti yuktivādī / dharmasyeti buddhanirvāṇasya / anudharmamanukūlaṃ mārgaḥ / vyākurvan ācakṣāṇaḥ / vyākaromyācakṣe / sarvadharmāṇāṃ viviktaṃ vivekaḥ śūnyatā / tasminvihāraḥ samādhiḥ sarvadharmāṇāṃ anupalambhaḥ / tasminvihāraḥ yaḥ khalu punarityādinā subhūtervihārādvodhisattvavihārasyortṣa darśayati / upapattimāha / tathāgatavihāraṃ hītyādinā / carataḥ samādhiniṣpattaye / viharato niṣpannena samādhinā / śeṣaṃ subodham / durbodhaṃ tu prāgeva vyākhyātam //
body.translated_text: '<s>Sajjati</s>' means 'is obstructed' — this is the meaning. '<s>Ārabhya</s>' means 'with reference to.' '<s>Dharmavādī</s>' means 'one who speaks in accordance with reasoning.' '<s>Dharmasya</s>' means 'of the <s>Buddha's</s> <s>nirvāṇa</s>.' '<s>Anudharma</s>' means 'the conforming path.' '<s>Vyākurvan</s>' means 'declaring.' '<s>Vyākaromi</s>' means 'I declare.' 'The detachment of all <s>dharmas</s>' — the detachment is the emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>). The abiding in that is the <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) — the non-apprehension of all <s>dharmas</s>. The abiding in that — by 'He who indeed' and so on, he shows the superiority of the <s>bodhisattva's</s> abiding over <s>Subhūti's</s> abiding. He gives the justification: 'For the abiding of the <s>Tathāgata</s>' and so on. 'Of one who practices' — for the accomplishment of <s>samādhi</s>. 'Of one who abides' — by the accomplished <s>samādhi</s>. The rest is easily understood. What is difficult to understand has been explained earlier.

body.text: sārādiḥ parivartaḥ sāraparivarttaḥ /
body.translated_text: The chapter that begins with '<s>Sāra</s>' (essence) is the '<s>Sāra-parivarta</s>' (Chapter on the Essence).

body.text: āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ sāratamānāmni pañjikāyāṃ ratnākaraśāntiviracitāyāṃ saptaviṃśatitamaḥ parivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: In the <s>Pañjikā</s> commentary named <s>Sāratamā</s>, composed by <s>Ratnākaraśānti</s>, on the noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s> — this is the twenty-seventh chapter.

body.text: 28. avakīrṇakusumaparivarto nāmāṣṭāviṃśatitamaḥ /
body.translated_text: 28. The chapter named '<s>Avakīrṇakusuma-parivarta</s>' (Chapter on the Scattered Flowers) is the twenty-eighth.

body.text: māyopamasāraparivartābhyāṃ darśanaheyā vikalpā uktāḥ / darśanamārgādeśca prajñāpāramitāvihārasyāvaśyakaṃ bodhiprāpakatvamuktam / tatastasya tathābhāve kāraṇatrayamanena parivartena prathamaṃ vakṣyati paścādvodhilakṣaṇam / ataḥ kāraṇatrayamadhikṛtya śāstram-
body.translated_text: By the chapters on Illusion-Likeness and Essence, the conceptualizations to be abandoned by the path of seeing (<s>darśana-mārga</s>) have been stated. And of the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-abiding [described] from the path of seeing onward, the inevitable attainment of <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) has been stated. Then, given that state of affairs, three causes will be stated first by this chapter, and afterward the characteristic of <s>bodhi</s>. Therefore, with regard to the three causes, the treatise [states] —

children.translated_text: 'Demonstrations to them regarding <s>bodhi</s>, and the entrustment due to its cause,
the proximate cause of its attainment — characterized by an abundance of merit.' // 5-17 //

body.text: tasyā bodheryathoktāt prajñāpāramitāvihārādavaśyaṃ prāptiḥ 'tatprāptiḥ' / tasyā 'anantaro ' 'vinābhāvī 'hetuḥ' jñāpakastrividha uktaḥ sūtre / 'bodhau sandarśanā' vyākaraṇaṃ yad 'anyeṣāṃ' sa prathamo hetuḥ / bhāvināṃ bodhihetorāryānandāya 'parīndanā' dvītīyo hetuḥ / 'puṇyābāhulyalakṣaṇaḥ' tṛtīyaḥ / ataḥ sūtram // atha khalvityādi avakīrṇakusumanāmāno vyākartavyāḥ / tato devaiḥ puṣpamānītaṃ vyākartavyairavakīrṇaṃ tato raśmīnāṃ niścārapraveśau / ānandapṛṣṭena
body.translated_text: The attainment of that <s>bodhi</s> from the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-abiding as described — that is '<s>tatprāpti</s>' (the attainment of that). Its 'proximate' — inseparable — 'cause,' the indicator, is stated as threefold in the <s>sūtra</s>. 'Demonstrations regarding <s>bodhi</s>' — the prediction (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>) — 'of others' — that is the first cause. The 'entrustment' of the <s>bodhi</s>-cause of the future ones to noble <s>Ānanda</s> for the sake of joy — is the second cause. 'Characterized by an abundance of merit' — is the third. Therefore the <s>sūtra</s> [states]: 'Now then' and so on — those named <s>Avakīrṇakusuma</s> (Scattered Flowers) are to receive prediction. Then flowers are brought by the <s>devas</s>, scattered by those who are to receive prediction, and then rays of light issue forth and reenter. Through <s>Ānanda's</s> question,

body.text: bhagavatā teṣāṃ vyākaraṇam / tatteṣāṃ vyākaraṇamanyasminviśiṣṭe lokadhātāvitilakṣyate lokadhātoranirdeśāt / āyuḥsaddharmaśitikālayoścayatatvāt / tadanu tasmāttarhītyādinā upasaṃhāro vihartavyāntaḥ / iti prakṛtena vihāreṇa bodhiprāpteḥ prathamaṃ kāraṇam //
body.translated_text: the <s>Bhagavān</s> gives their prediction. Their prediction in a different, distinguished world-realm is implied, because of the non-specification of [this] world-realm, and because of the increase in lifespan and duration of the true <s>Dharma</s>. After that, by 'Therefore then' and so on, the conclusion, ending with 'should abide.' Thus, through the abiding discussed [above], the first cause of the attainment of <s>bodhi</s> [is established].

body.text: tato ye hītyādinā samyaksambuddhānāmityetadantena prajñāpāramitācāriṇāṃ guṇānāha / tato ye caināmityādinā veditavyāntena yepyenāṃ śrutvā na pratikṣipanti teṣāṃ guṇamāha / atra pratikrośaṇaṃ mānasī nindā / prativahanaṃ manasā tyāgaḥ / pratikopanaṃ tasmai kopaḥ / pratisaṃharaṇaṃ guptau sthāpanam / pratiṣedhanaṃ niḥsāratākhyāpanam / pratikṣepo 'sabhdūtabādhakābhidhānam / tadavyavasāyaḥ saptamaḥ / tataḥ kiñcāpītyādinā caritavatetyetadantena hīnayānāpatane kāraṇadvayamāha / praṇidhānādināvisaṃvāditāṃ kṛtajñatāṃ ceti / tadevaṃ ye hi kecidityādinā vistareṇopodghātaṃ kṛtvā tasmāttarhītyādinā parīndanāmāha / parīndanā samarpaṇā saivānubandhinī anuparīndanā / akṣarasannipātāditi / akṣarasannipāto vyañjanakāyaḥ / tamadhikṛtyeti lyap lope pañcamī / kimarthamityāha / udgrahaṇāyetyādi / kathaṃ parīndanetyata āha / yatheyaṃ nāntarddhīyeteti / yatheyamantarhitā na syāttathā tvayā karaṇīyamityarthaḥ / ata ūrdhvaṃ sa cedityādinā āhāriketyetadantena dvitīyamupodghātaṃ kṛtvā tasmāttarhītyādinā dvitīyā parīndanā / atra punareveti paścāt / nāśayeriti hārayeḥ / śīghramananuśa(sa)raṇāt utsṛje / smartumaśakyatvāt vismareḥ / aparāddhaḥ kṛtāparādhaḥ / ārādhanamārāgaṇaṃ ca toṣaṇam / mātā bījadhā[ra]nā(ṇā)t / jananī bījapṛṣṭeḥ / janayitrī utpādanāt / tata urdhvaṃ udgrahītavyeyamityādinā tādṛśī prajñāpāramitā sadevakasya lokasya śāstetyetadantenopoddhātaṃ kṛtvā tasmāttarhītyādinānuśā nītyetadantena tṛtīyā parīndanā /
body.translated_text: Then by 'For those who' and so on, ending with 'of the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddhas</s>' — he states the virtues of those who practice <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>. Then by 'And those who this' and so on, ending with 'should be known' — he states the virtue of those who, even upon hearing it, do not reject it. Here, '<s>pratikrośaṇa</s>' is mental censure. '<s>Prativahana</s>' is mental rejection. '<s>Pratikopana</s>' is anger toward that [teaching]. '<s>Pratisaṃharaṇa</s>' is placing in concealment. '<s>Pratiṣedhana</s>' is declaring it to be without essence. '<s>Pratikṣepa</s>' is making objections that have no true obstructive force. The non-resolution of that is the seventh [type]. Then by 'Although something' and so on, ending with 'has practiced' — he states two causes for falling into the lesser vehicle: non-deception through aspiration and the like, and gratitude. Thus, by 'For whoever indeed' and so on, having made the introduction in detail, by 'Therefore then' and so on, he states the entrustment (<s>parīndanā</s>). '<s>Parīndanā</s>' is handing over; that itself when continuous is '<s>anuparīndanā</s>' (subsequent entrustment). '<s>Akṣarasannipāta</s>' — the collection of syllables is the body of words (<s>vyañjanakāya</s>). '<s>Tam adhikṛtya</s>' — the fifth case in place of the <s>lyap</s> absolutive. 'For what purpose?' — to this he says '<s>Udgrahaṇāya</s>' (for the sake of taking up) and so on. 'How is the entrustment?' — to this he says 'So that this does not disappear' — 'You should act so that this does not become lost' — this is the meaning. From this point onward, by '<s>Sa cet</s>' and so on, ending with '<s>āhārika</s>' — having made a second introduction — by 'Therefore then' and so on, the second entrustment. Here '<s>punareva</s>' means 'afterward.' '<s>Nāśayeḥ</s>' means 'you would cause to be lost.' 'Because of quickly not following up' — '<s>utsṛje</s>' (you would abandon). 'Because of inability to remember' — '<s>vismareḥ</s>' (you would forget). '<s>Aparāddha</s>' means 'one who has committed an offense.' '<s>Ārādhana</s>' and '<s>ārāgaṇa</s>' mean 'pleasing.' '<s>Mātā</s>' (mother) — because of bearing the seed. '<s>Jananī</s>' (genetrix) — because of the bursting forth of the seed. '<s>Janayitrī</s>' (one who gives birth) — because of production. Then from that point onward, by 'This should be taken up' and so on, ending with 'the teacher of the world including its gods' — having made the introduction — by 'Therefore then' and so on, ending with '<s>anuśāsanī</s>' (instruction) — the third entrustment.

body.text: atra suniruktā supaṭhitā dharmakāyateti prajñāpāramitaiva dharmaḥ kāya eṣāṃ tattaditi vakṣyamāṇena kartavyādinā sambadhyate / tatra kartavyamupasthānādi dātavyaṃ puṣpādi samanvāhartavyaṃ deśanādi / kalyāṇata iti puṇyakāmatayā / sparśavihārata iti tenaiva sukhībhāvāt / guṇavattayeti kalyāṇādinā / bhāṣeye(yami)ti vadeyam / kalpaṃ vā yāvattato vā upari yadi vistara iṣṭaḥ syāt / kintarhi saṃkṣepeṇānanda bhāṣaye(bhāṣe) / yādṛśa ityādi / tato yopi kaścidityādinā samyaksambodhirityetadantenopodghātaṃ kṛtvā caturthī parindanāmāha / tamāttarhītyādinā nāntardhīyetyetadantena /
body.translated_text: Here '<s>suniruktā supaṭhitā dharmakāyatā</s>' (well-expounded, well-recited, being the <s>dharmakāya</s>) — <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> itself is the <s>dharma</s>; 'body' of these — that — this connects with what is to be stated: 'what is to be done' and so on. Therein, 'what is to be done' [includes] attendance and so on; 'what is to be given' [includes] flowers and so on; 'what is to be recollected' [includes] teaching and so on. '<s>Kalyāṇataḥ</s>' means through the desire for merit. '<s>Sparśavihārataḥ</s>' means because of becoming happy through that very [contact]. '<s>Guṇavatā</s>' means through [qualities such as] excellence and so on. '<s>Bhāṣeya</s>' means 'I would speak.' 'For a <s>kalpa</s> (aeon) or beyond that' — if a detailed [exposition] were desired. 'But rather, in brief, <s>Ānanda</s>, I speak.' 'Of such a kind' and so forth. Then by 'Whoever' and so on, ending with '<s>samyaksambodhi</s>' (perfect awakening) — having made the introduction — he states the fourth entrustment: 'Therefore then' and so on, ending with 'does not disappear.'

body.text: caturthakamiti vaktavye dvitīyakamityuktam / u(anu)ktānāmuktasāmānyenaikīkaraṇāt / paridadāmi parindāmi samarpayāmītyeko 'rthaḥ / evaṃ caturākārā parindanā dvitīyaṃ kāraṇam //
body.translated_text: Where 'the fourth' should have been said, 'the second' was said — because of the unification of the unstated with the stated, by their commonality. '<s>Paridadāmi</s>, <s>parindāmi</s>, <s>samarpayāmi</s>' — these are synonymous, meaning 'I entrust.' Thus the fourfold entrustment is the second cause.

body.text: tata eṣā hyānandetyādinopādghātaṃ kṛtvā sa cet tvamityādi naitatsthānaṃ vidyata iti yāvat / atra adhvaparyantaḥ kṣaṇaḥ / viṃśaṃ kṣaṇaśataṃ tatkṣaṇaḥ / tatkṣaṇāḥ ṣaṣṭirlavaḥ / lavāstriṃśanmuhūrtaḥ / nālikā ghaṭikā / iti puṇyabahutvaṃ tṛtīyaṃ kāraṇam //
body.translated_text: Then by 'For this indeed, <s>Ānanda</s>' and so on — having made the introduction — '<s>Sa cet tvam</s>' and so on, up to 'this situation does not exist.' Here, '<s>adhvaparyanta</s>' is a moment (<s>kṣaṇa</s>). Twenty moments make a '<s>tatkṣaṇa</s>.' Sixty <s>tatkṣaṇas</s> make a '<s>lava</s>.' Thirty <s>lavas</s> make a '<s>muhūrta</s>.' A '<s>nālikā</s>' is a <s>ghaṭikā</s> (water-clock unit). Thus the abundance of merit is the third cause.

body.text: tato 'tha khalu bhagavānityādinā akṣobhyasya bhagavataḥ sabuddhakṣetrasya sapariṣadaḥ sandarśanamantardhāyanaṃ ca dṛṣṭāntaḥ / atra sāgaropamatvamativistīrṇatvāt / gambhīratvaṃ dhyānasampadā / akṣobhyatvaṃ prajñāsampadā / dārṣṭāntike yojayitumāha / evamānanda sarvadharmā ityādi / sarvadharmā hītyādinā yuktimāha / na kāryasamarthā iti pratijñāntaram / nirīhakā hītyādinā yuktimāha / evaṃ caranta ityādinānuśaṃsāmāha / mahābodhiśabdāt prāk / asaṅgatāmiti nirupala[mbha]tām / apratihatajñānatāṃ vā / pramāṇaṃ vaipulyaniyamaḥ / kṣayaḥ kālaniyamaḥ / paryantaḥ saṃkhyāniyamaḥ / pramāṇabaddheti pramāṇaparicchinnā / aprameyatvādityanupalambhāt / kṣayo 'pacayaḥ / parikṣayo 'bhāvaḥ / ākāśākṣayatvāditi ākāśavadakṣayatvāt / kuta ityāha sarvadharmānutpādata iti / anutpannā sarvadharmāḥ / atasteṣāmanupalambhalakṣaṇā prajñāpāramitāpyākāśavadakṣayeti / abhinirhartavyeti pratyakṣīkartavyā / rūpādīnāmakṣayatveneti teṣāmanutpādataḥ / evamavidyādīnām / iyaṃ seti yā skandhādīnāmavidyādīnāṃ cākṣayatvena / antadvayamutpattivināśau madhyamutpannasya sthitiḥ / āveṇiko 'nyairasādhāraṇaḥ / na ca kiñciddharmamiti skandhaiḥ saṃgṛhītam / kutaḥ? pratītyotpādadarśanāt / nityamityanādinidhanam / dhruvamiti sthiram / śāśvatamityanidhanam / kārakaṃ vedakaṃ veti / īhaturgṛhītuścābhāvāt / ita uttaro granthaḥ subodhaḥ samyaksambodhariti yāvat / iyatā kṣayānutpādajñānalakṣaṇā bodhirucyate / atra śāstram-
body.translated_text: Then, beginning with 'Now then, the <s>Bhagavān</s>' and so on, the showing and disappearance of <s>Bhagavān Akṣobhya</s> together with his <s>Buddha-kṣetra</s> and assembly is the example. Here, 'ocean-likeness' is because of vast extensiveness. 'Profundity' is because of the accomplishment of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation). '<s>Akṣobhya</s>-ness' (imperturbability) is because of the accomplishment of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). To apply [these] to the meaning [of the analogy], he says beginning with 'Thus, <s>Ānanda</s>, all <s>dharmas</s>' and so on. Beginning with 'For all <s>dharmas</s>' and so on, he states the reasoning. 'They are not efficacious' is an alternative thesis. Beginning with 'For they are without activity' and so on, he states the reasoning. Beginning with 'One who practices thus' and so on, he states the benefit — up to before the word '<s>mahābodhi</s>.' '<s>Asaṅgatā</s>' (non-attachment) means the state of non-apprehension. Or the state of unobstructed knowledge. '<s>Pramāṇa</s>' (measure) is limitation by extent. '<s>Kṣaya</s>' (decrease) is limitation by time. '<s>Paryanta</s>' (boundary) is limitation by number. '<s>Pramāṇabaddha</s>' (bound by measure) means delimited by measure — because of immeasurability, i.e., because of non-apprehension. '<s>Kṣaya</s>' (decrease) is diminution. '<s>Parikṣaya</s>' (complete decrease) is non-existence — because of being indestructible like space. Whence? He says: 'because of the non-arising of all <s>dharmas</s>.' All <s>dharmas</s> are unarisen; therefore <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> too, having the characteristic of their non-apprehension, is indestructible like space. 'Should be brought forth' means should be made manifest. 'Because of the indestructibility of form and the rest' — because of their non-arising. Similarly for ignorance and the rest. 'This is that' — that which consists in the indestructibility of the <s>skandhas</s> and the rest and of ignorance and the like. 'The two extremes' are arising and destruction; 'the middle' is the abiding of what has arisen. '<s>Āveṇika</s>' (distinctive) means not shared by others. 'And he does not [apprehend] any <s>dharma</s>' — that which is comprised by the <s>skandhas</s>. Why? Because of seeing dependent origination. 'Permanent' means without beginning or end. 'Stable' means firm. 'Eternal' means without end. 'An agent or an experiencer' — because of the non-existence of an acting or a grasping [entity]. The text from here onward is easily understood — up to '<s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s>.' To this extent, awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) characterized by the knowledge of cessation and non-arising is spoken of. Here the treatise [states] —

children.translated_text: Awakening is said to be the knowledge of the cessation and non-arising of defilements.
Because of the non-existence of cessation and because of non-arising — for those [two] are the objects of knowledge, respectively. [5-18]

body.text: malāḥ kleśavikalpāḥ / teṣāṃ 'kṣayānutpādayoḥ' ye 'jñāne ' sā bodhiḥ / 'te ' ca jñāne teṣāṃ 'kṣayābhāvādanutpādācca yathākramaṃ' veditavye / kṣayasyātyantamasattayā jñānaṃ kṣayajñānam / anutpādasyo(syānu)tpattikatvena jñānamanutpādajñānamiti bhāvaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Defilements' (<s>malas</s>) are the conceptualizations that are afflictions. The 'knowledge of the cessation and non-arising' of those — that is <s>bodhi</s> (awakening). And 'those' two knowledges of them [defilements] are 'to be understood from the non-existence of cessation and from non-arising, respectively.' Because of the utter non-existence of cessation, the knowledge [thereof] is '<s>kṣayajñāna</s>' (knowledge of cessation). Because of the non-arising character of non-arising, the knowledge [thereof] is '<s>anutpādajñāna</s>' (knowledge of non-arising) — this is the meaning.

body.text: atha bodherlakṣaṇāntarasambhavepi kimarthamidaṃ lakṣaṇamuktam? darśanamārgeṇa kṣīṇānāṃ vikalpānāmakṣayato 'nutpādataśca vyavalokanārtham / tadevāha-
body.translated_text: But even if another characteristic of <s>bodhi</s> is possible, why is this characteristic stated? For the purpose of examining from the [perspective of] non-decrease and non-arising the conceptualizations that have been destroyed by the path of seeing. He states just this —

children.translated_text: When the nature [of dharmas] has not ceased, by the path called 'seeing,'
What kind (<s>jāta</s>) of conceptualization has been destroyed, or what has come to non-arising? [5-19]

body.text: vikalpānāṃ prakṛtistathatā / na kadācittasyāḥ kṣaya utpādo vā / jātireva 'jātaṃ' prakāraḥ / tato na kaścidvikalpaprakāro darśanamārgeṇa kṣīṇa utpādaṃ vā tyājita iti //
body.translated_text: The nature (<s>prakṛti</s>) of the conceptualizations is <s>tathatā</s> (suchness). Never is there destruction or arising of it. '<s>Jāta</s>' itself means 'kind' (<s>prakāra</s>). Therefore, no kind of conceptualization has been destroyed by the path of seeing, nor has it been made to abandon arising.

body.text: anye tvāhuḥ-
body.translated_text: Others, however, say —

children.translated_text: 'The knowledge of cessation is the certainty, regarding the truths, of "fully known" and the like.',
'The [certainty] beginning with "never again a knowable" is held to be the attainment of non-arising.'

body.text: te hi śasyante- santi skandhāḥ santi catvāri satyāni / tatra saṃkṣepataḥ kleśaduḥkhayoḥ kṣayaḥ punaranutpādaśca prāpyate / tatoḥ prāptayorye jñāne te kṣayānutpādajñāne / prādhānyena tathāgatānāṃ tu jñeyāvaraṇamapi kṣīyate teṣāmakliṣṭasyāpyajñānasya kṣayāditi / tannirāsāya śāstram-
body.translated_text: For they maintain: 'There exist <s>skandhas</s>, there exist four truths. Among those, in brief, the cessation and further non-arising of afflictions and suffering are attained. The two knowledges of those attainments are the knowledge of cessation and the knowledge of non-arising. Predominantly

children.text: sattā ca nāma dharmāṇāṃ jñeye cāvaraṇakṣayaḥ /
children.translated_text: That there is existence of <s>dharmas</s>, and that in the knowable there is the destruction of obscurations —
That which is said by others [regarding] the Teacher — at this I am astonished.' [5-20]
Therefore, nothing whatsoever is to be removed, and nothing whatsoever is to be added.
Reality is to be seen as it truly is; one who sees reality is liberated. [5-21]

body.text: 'nāma' śabdo 'marṣe / 'atra vismīyate mayā' iti vipakṣapratipakṣayorayogāditi bhāvaḥ / 'ataḥ' kāraṇāt 'nāpaneyaṃ kiñcit' pudgalasya dharmāṇāṃ ca svayamabhāvāt / 'prakṣeptavyaṃ na kiñcanaṃ' pudgaladharmanairātmyayoranādinidhanatvāt / kiṃ tarhi? tadubhayaṃ 'bhūtaṃ' bhūtatvena 'draṣṭavyam' / yato bhūtaṃ pudgalanairātmyaṃ dṛṣṭvā kleśāvaraṇādvimucyate / bhūtaṃ dharmanairātmyaṃ dṛṣṭvā jñeyāvaraṇād 'vimucyate ' / tasmādabhūtānāṃ pudgaladharmāṇāṃ dṛṣṭirvipakṣaḥ / teṣāṃ nairātmyadarśanaṃ pratipakṣaḥ / ubhayostu nairātmyayorbhūtatvaṃ mahārathaiḥ kṣuṇṇam / tata iha nocyate //
body.translated_text: The word '<s>nāma</s>' expresses indignation. 'At this I am astonished' — because of the impossibility of both the adversary and the antidote — this is the meaning. 'Therefore' — for this reason — 'nothing is to be removed' — because of the intrinsic non-existence of the person and of <s>dharmas</s>. 'Nothing is to be added' —

body.text: tasmāttarhītyādi / kṣayānutpādalakṣaṇā bodhisatasyā avaśyalabhyatā kāraṇatrayaṃ ca prasaṅgādāgatam / prākṛtaṃ tu māyopamasāraparivarte nirdiṣṭaṃ darśanaheyānāṃ vikalpānāṃ prahāṇam / ato yasmāddarśanamārgeṇa darśanaheyānāṃ vikalpānāṃ prahāṇaṃ tasmāddhetoḥ / tarhīti darśanakāle prajñāpāramitāyāṃ darśanamārgātmikāyāṃ caritavyam //
body.translated_text: 'Therefore, then' and so on. The awakening characterized by cessation and non-arising, and the three causes of its inevitable attainment for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, have come up incidentally. But the main [topic] — the abandonment of conceptualizations to be abandoned on the path of seeing, as set forth in the <s>Māyopama</s> and <s>Sāra</s> chapters —

body.text: tatkasya hetoriti / hetumukhena darśanamārgasya lakṣaṇapraśnaḥ / prajñāpāramitāyāmiti / atratye darśanamārge dhyānapāramitetyatra cārtho gamyate / tenānuktasamuccayaḥ / prajñāpāramitā ceti / kuta ityāha / prajñāpāramitāyāṃ hītyādi / bhāvanāparipūriṃ ṣaṭpāramitā gacchantīti sambandhaḥ / sarvā iti pratyekaṃ samagrāḥ satyaḥ / ekaikayā ṣaṇṇāmapi saṃgrahāditi bhāvaḥ / ataśca ṣaḍeva pāramitāṣaṭkā darśanamārgaḥ / saṃkṣiptā ceyaṃ bhagavatī / ato lakṣaṇamātramasyāmuktam / yathā tvekaikayā sarvasaṃgrahastadvistareṇa mahatyorbhagavatyoruktam / atra śāstram-
body.translated_text: 'For what reason?' — this is a question about the characteristic of the path of seeing by way of its cause. 'In <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>' — here the meaning of the path of seeing is understood, and in '<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>' also the meaning is understood. Hence an unmentioned collection. <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>

children.text: ekaikasyaiva dānādau teṣāṃ yaḥ saṃgraho mithaḥ /
children.translated_text: The mutual inclusion of each one [of the <s>pāramitās</s>] such as generosity and the rest,
That, being momentary, is comprised by patient acceptance here on the path of seeing. [5-22]

body.text: ekaikameva ekaikaśaḥ svārtha śas / tasya bhāva ekaikasya / avyayatvāddhi lopaḥ / tena 'ekaikasyaiva dānādau' iti dānādiṣu / 'teṣāṃ' dānādīnāṃ 'mithaḥ' anyonyaṃ 'yaḥ saṅgrahaḥ' / so 'smin mūrdhābhisamaye darśanamārgaḥ / sa ca 'ekakṣaṇīkaḥ' na tu ṣoḍaśakṣaṇāḥ(ṇaḥ) / sa ca kṣāntyā 'saṃgṛhītaḥ' na punaraṣṭābhiḥ kṣāntibhiraṣṭābhirjñānaiḥ / iti mūrdhābhisamaye darśanamārgaḥ //
body.translated_text: '<s>Ekaika</s>' (each one) — '<s>ekaikaśaḥ</s>' [means] severally; the suffix '<s>śas</s>' [means] 'in its own sense.' '<s>Bhāva</s>' of that is [the state of] each one. Because of being an indeclinable, there is elision. Thus 'of each one, in generosity and the rest' means in the [individual] <s>pāramitās</s> such as generosity. 'Of those' — of generosity and the rest — 'mutually' (<s>mithaḥ</s>) — of one another — 'that which is the inclusion' —

body.text: tato bhāvanāmārgaḥ / tamāha / sarvāṇi cetyādinā / upāyau ca kauśalyaṃ ceti upatyakauśalyāni / tatra niśrayatvādupāyau siṃhavijṛmbhitāvaskandhakau samādhī / kauśalyaṃ pratītyasamutpādasyānulomaṃ ca vyavalokanam- "avidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārāḥ saṃskārapratyayaṃ vijñānaṃ yāvajjātipratyayā jarāmaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsāḥ sambhavantītyanulomam / avidyānirodhātsaṃskāranirodhaḥ / saṃskāranirodhādvijñānanirodho yāvajjātinirodhājjarāmaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsā nirudhyante" iti pratilomam /
body.translated_text: Then the path of cultivation (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>). This he states beginning with 'And all' and so on. '<s>Upāya</s> (means) and <s>kauśalya</s> (skill)' — means and skill [separately] are '<s>upāyakauśalyāni</s>.' Therein, because they are the basis, the two means are the <s>siṃhavijṛmbhita</s> (lion's stretch) and <s>avaskandaka</s> (leaping) <s>samādhis</s>. The skill is dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>).

body.text: tatra siṃhavijṛmbhitaḥ samādhiḥ / tadyathā- "prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ samāpadyate / dvitīyaṃ tṛtīyaṃ caturtham / ākāśānantyāyatanaṃ vijñānānantyāyatanaṃ ākiñcanyāyatanaṃ naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanaṃ nirodhasamāpattiṃ ca samāpadyate / nirodhasamāpattervyutthito naivasaṃjñānasaṃjñāyatanaṃ samāpadyate / tata ākiñcanyāyatanaṃ vijñānānantyāyatanaṃ ākāśānantyāyatanaṃ caturthaṃ dhyānaṃ tṛtīyaṃ dvitīyaṃ prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ samāpadyata" iti /
body.translated_text: There, the <s>siṃhavijṛmbhita samādhi</s> (lion's stretch concentration). Namely: 'He attains the first <s>dhyāna</s>, the second, the third, the fourth; the sphere of infinite space, the sphere of infinite consciousness, the sphere of nothingness, the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception;

body.text: avaskandakasamādhiḥ / tadyathā- "prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ samāpadyate dvitīyaṃ tṛtīyaṃ caturtham / ākāśānantyāyatanaṃ vijñānānantyāyatanaṃ ākiñcanyāyatanaṃ naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanaṃ
body.translated_text: The <s>avaskandaka samādhi</s> (leaping concentration). Namely: 'He attains the first <s>dhyāna</s>, the second, the third, the fourth; the sphere of infinite space, the sphere of infinite consciousness, the sphere of nothingness, the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception,

body.text: nirodhasamāpattiṃ ca / tato vyutthāya prathamaṃ dhyānam / tato nirodham / tato dvitiyaṃ dhyānam / tato nirodham / tatastṛtīyaṃ dhyānam / tato nirodham / tataścaturtha dhyānam / tato nirodham / tata ākāśānantyāyatanam / tato nirodham / tato vijñānānantyāyatanam / tato nirodham / tata ākiñcanyāyatanam / tato nirodham / naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanam / tato nirodham / tato 'samāhitacitte patati / tato nirodhaṃ samāpadyate / tato 'samāhite citte tiṣṭhati / tato naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanam / tato 'samāhite / tata ākiñcanyāyatanam / tato 'samāhite / tato vijñānānantyāyatanam / tato 'samāhite / tata ākāśānantyāyatanam / tato 'samāhite / tataścaturthaṃ dhyānam / tato 'samāhite / tatastṛtīyam / tato 'samāhite / tato dvitīyam / tato 'samāhite / tataḥ prathamam / tato 'samāhite citte tiṣṭhati" iti /
body.translated_text: and the attainment of cessation. Then, rising from that, the first <s>dhyāna</s>; then cessation; then the second <s>dhyāna</s>; then cessation; then the third <s>dhyāna</s>; then cessation; then the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>; then

body.text: tatra prathamāyāṃ gatau nava sthānāni / dvitīyāyāṃ saptadaśa / āgamane 'ṣṭādaśa / atra śāstram-
body.translated_text: In the first progression there are nine stages. In the second, seventeen. In the return, eighteen. Here the treatise [states] —

children.translated_text: Having attained the <s>samādhi</s>, then the <s>siṃhavijṛmbhita</s> (lion's stretch) —
He observes dependent origination in forward and reverse order. [5-23]
Having set aside the attainment of the desire [realm] and the non-concentrated consciousness,
The attainments including cessation — having gone and returned, or twofold; [5-24]
By skipping one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight —
The <s>avaskandaka</s> (leaping) attainment proceeds up to cessation, with unequal [progressions]. [5-25]

body.text: siṃhavijṛmbhito yathā sūtrameva / avaskandastu gahanam / tena tasya lakṣaṇamāha / 'avaskandasamāpattiḥ' bhavati / kathamityāha / 'nava samāpattīrdvidhā gatvā' paścād 'āgamya' / ādau kathaṃ gatvetyata āha 'ānirodham' iti / nirodhasamāpattimante kṛtvā / itarā aṣṭau krameṇa prāgityarthaḥ / punaḥ kathaṃ gatvetyata āha 'ekadvitricatuṣpañcaṣaṭsaptāṣṭavyatikramāt' / 'sanirodhāḥ' kṛtvā / kāḥ? itarā aṣṭau 'samāpattīḥ' / kāmāvacaraṃ ca 'asamāhitaṃ' cittaṃ 'avadhīkṛtya' / ante gantavyaṃ kṛtvetyarthaḥ / paścāt kathamāgatyetyata āha 'atulyagā' iti / atulyagā satī / asamāhitādasamāhitaḥ / samāhitācca samāhitamagacchantītyarthaḥ / ihāpi 'kāmāptamavadhīkṛtya vijñānamasamāhitaṃ' iti sambadhyate /
body.translated_text: The <s>siṃhavijṛmbhita</s> is just as [described in] the <s>sūtra</s>. But the <s>avaskandaka</s> is complex. Therefore he states its characteristic: 'The <s>avaskandaka</s> attainment' exists. How? He says: 'having gone through the nine attainments in two ways,' afterward 'having returned.' At first

body.text: teneyasamāhitāccittātprabhṛtyāgacchati / antepyasamāhita eva citte gatvā tiṣṭhati / iti mūrdhābhisamaye bhāvanāmārgaḥ //
body.translated_text: Therefore, starting from this non-concentrated state of mind, he proceeds. At the end too, having gone to the non-concentrated state of mind, he abides. Thus, on the summit-realization (<s>mūrdhābhisamaya</s>), the path of cultivation.

body.text: sarvāṇi copāyakauśalyāni paripūriṃ gacchantītyuktam / kathaṃ ca teṣāṃ bhāvanāparipūribhavet / yadi bhāvanāheyāścatvāro vikalpanavakāḥ kṣīyeran / teṣāṃ ca pratipakṣā eva mahatyorbhagavatyoḥ paṭhyante / te tu sāmarthyādgamyante / vayamapi tameva pāṭhamabhisaṃkṣipya tān vakṣyāmaḥ / tatrādyaṃ vikalpanavakamadhikṛtya śāstram-
body.translated_text: And it has been said that all <s>upāyakauśalyas</s> (skillful means) reach completion. How then would their completion through cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) come about? If the four sets of nine conceptualizations (<s>vikalpa-navaka</s>) to be abandoned through cultivation are eliminated. And their antidotes are indeed read in the two great <s>Bhagavatīs</s> (i.e., the longer and shorter Prajñāpāramitā sūtras). They are understood through implication. We too shall explain them by abbreviating that very reading. Regarding the first set of nine conceptualizations, the treatise states—

children.translated_text: Regarding abbreviation, elaboration, protection by <s>Buddhas</s>,
non-acceptance, the absence of qualities pertaining to the three times, and the threefold path to liberation; [5-26]

body.text: eko grāhyavikalpo 'yaṃ prayogākāragocaraḥ /
body.translated_text: This is one <s>grāhya-vikalpa</s> (conceptualization of the apprehended), having as its domain the aspects of practice.

body.text: 'ekaḥ' iti prathamaḥ / 'prayogākāragocaraḥ' iti prajñāpāramitāprayogaviśeṣaḥ viṣayaḥ / 'vistare ' 'saṃkṣepe ' ceti paṭhitavyam / vṛttānurodhāt tvanyathā paṭhitam / vistare sammoho vistaravikalpaḥ / tasya pratipakṣaḥ / bahuṣu sthāneṣu bodhisattvena śikṣitavyaṃ dānādiṣu yāvadvaleṣu vaiśāradyeṣviti //
body.translated_text: 'One' means the first. 'Having as its domain the aspects of practice' means the specific practice of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is its object. It should be read as 'elaboration' and 'abbreviation.' However, it has been read differently to conform to the meter. Confusion regarding elaboration is the <s>vistara-vikalpa</s> (conceptualization of elaboration). Its antidote is: the <s>Bodhisattva</s> should train in many topics, from <s>dāna</s> (giving) and so forth up to the powers (<s>balas</s>) and confidences (<s>vaiśāradyas</s>).

body.text: saṃkṣepe sammohaḥ saṃkṣepavikalpaḥ / tasya pratipakṣaḥ na ca kvacan śikṣitavyamiti / bahunāmapi teṣāṃ na ca kvacaneti śūnyataikarasatvāt / sambuddhaiḥ'sānāthyena' yaḥ parigrahaḥ / tadabhāve vikalpaḥ kalpanā / tasya pratipakṣaḥ / yaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ śikṣitvā dānapāramitāṃ yāvatsarvākārajñatāmanuprāpsyati / tenaivaṃ jñātavyaṃ- daśadiksarvabuddhaiḥ sānāthyenāhaṃ parigṛhītaḥ svasyāṃ mātari teṣāṃ kṛtajñatayeti //
body.translated_text: Confusion regarding abbreviation is the <s>saṃkṣepa-vikalpa</s> (conceptualization of abbreviation). Its antidote is: 'nor should one train in anything whatsoever.' Even though they are many, 'nor in anything whatsoever' — because of the single flavor of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness). By the <s>Sambuddhas</s>, 'with protection' — that which is acceptance. The conceptualization is the imagining of its absence. Its antidote is: one who, having trained in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, will attain <s>Dānapāramitā</s> up to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience of all aspects). By that, one should know thus: 'I am accepted with protection by all the <s>Buddhas</s> of the ten directions, out of their gratitude toward their own mother.'

body.text: 'guṇābhāvo ' 'nuśaṃsābhāvaḥ / prayogadarśanabhāvānākālabhāvitatvāt 'traikālikaḥ' / tasmiṃstrayo vikalpāstrisraḥ kalpanāḥ / teṣāṃ pratipakṣāḥ / anuśaṃsān vistareṇoktvā yathāha- 'itīme 'nuśaṃsāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carataḥ prajñāpāramitāmabhinirharataḥ prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāvayataḥ /" iti yathākramaṃ prayogadarśanabhāvanāmārgakālikaguṇābhāve trayo vikalpāḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Absence of qualities' means absence of benefits. 'Pertaining to the three times' — because they do not arise in the times of practice, seeing, and cultivation. Therein are three conceptualizations, three imaginings. Their antidotes are: having stated the benefits extensively, as it says — 'These are the benefits for one who practices <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, for one who accomplishes <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, for one who cultivates <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.' Thus, respectively, three conceptualizations regarding the absence of qualities at the times of the path of practice, seeing, and cultivation.

body.text: 'śreyasaḥ pathi' iti nirvāṇamārge / prayogādibhedāt trividhā sammohāstrayo vikalpāḥ / teṣāṃ pratipakṣā yathākramaṃ- "rūpavedanādīnāṃ śāntavaśikatucchāsārakatayā tasyāṃ caritavyam /
body.translated_text: 'On the path to liberation' means on the path to <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Due to the distinction of practice and so forth, there are three kinds of confusion — three conceptualizations. Their antidotes, respectively, are: 'One should practice therein by viewing <s>rūpa</s> (form), <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), and so forth as peaceful, controlled, trivial, and insubstantial.'

body.text: ākāśaśūnyatābhinirhāratayābhinirhartavyā / ākāśaśūnyatā bhāvanayeyaṃ bhāvayitavyā" iti / iti trayaḥ prayogādibodhimārgasaṃmohavikalpāḥ //
body.translated_text: 'It should be accomplished through the accomplishment of space-emptiness (<s>ākāśa-śūnyatā</s>). This space-emptiness should be cultivated through cultivation.' Thus, these are the three conceptualizations of confusion regarding the paths to awakening beginning with practice.

body.text: ityukto navavidhaḥ prathamo grāhyavikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus has been explained the ninefold first <s>grāhya-vikalpa</s> (conceptualization of the apprehended).

body.text: dvitīyaṃ vikalpanavakamadhikṛtya śāstram-
body.translated_text: Regarding the second set of nine conceptualizations, the treatise states—

body.text: dvitīyaścittacaittānāṃ pravṛttiviṣayo mataḥ // 5-27 //
body.translated_text: The second is regarded as having as its domain the activity of <s>citta</s> (mind) and <s>caittas</s> (mental factors). [5-27]

children.translated_text: The non-arising of <s>citta</s> (mind), mental attention toward the seat of enlightenment (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>),
mental attention toward the <s>Hīnayāna</s>, non-attention toward <s>Sambodhi</s> (perfect awakening); [5-28]
Regarding cultivation and non-cultivation, and the very reverse of that,
and what is not in accordance with reality — this should be known as conceptualization on the path of cultivation. [5-29]

body.text: dvitīyo grāhyavikalpaścittacaittānāṃ yā pravṛttistadviṣayaḥ / kiyacciraṃ carannasyāṃ cīrṇo bhavatīti praśnaḥ / uttaram / prathamacittotpādamupādāyeti cittotpādavikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: The second <s>grāhya-vikalpa</s> (conceptualization of the apprehended) has as its domain the activity of <s>citta</s> (mind) and <s>caittas</s> (mental factors). The question is: 'How long must one practice before one's practice therein is completed?' The answer: 'Beginning from the first arising of the thought of awakening (<s>prathamacittotpāda</s>)' — this is the <s>cittotpāda-vikalpa</s> (conceptualization of the arising of mind).

body.text: yāvabdodhimaṇḍala manasikaroti / kathamiyaṃ caritavyābhinirhartavyā bhāvayitavyeti / ābodhimaṇḍā manasikāravikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'As long as one directs attention to the seat of enlightenment (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>)' — 'How should this be practiced, accomplished, cultivated?' — this is the <s>ābodhimaṇḍa-manasikāra-vikalpa</s> (conceptualization of mental attention up to the seat of enlightenment).

body.text: hīnayānamanasikārāṇāṃ cāvakāśaṃ na dadātīti hīnayānayormanasikāravikalpau //
body.translated_text: 'And one does not give opportunity to mental attentions of the <s>Hīnayāna</s>' — these are the two conceptualizations of mental attention toward the <s>Hīnayāna</s>.

body.text: sarvākārajñatā mānasikārāvipraṇāśa eva cāsyāṃ caryā / tathā caritavyaṃ yathā cittacaitasikā na pravartanta iti saṃbodhyamanasikāravikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'The non-loss of mental attention toward <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience of all aspects) is indeed the practice therein. One should practice thus: so that <s>citta</s> (mind) and <s>caitasikas</s> (mental factors) do not operate' — this is the <s>sambodhi-amanasikāra-vikalpa</s> (conceptualization of non-attention toward perfect awakening).

body.text: kiṃ bhāvayan sarvākārajñatāmanuprāpsyati neti bhāvanāvikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Will one attain <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> by cultivating? No' — this is the <s>bhāvanā-vikalpa</s> (conceptualization of cultivation).

body.text: abhāvayaṃstāmanuprāpsyati neti [a]bhāvanāvikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Will one attain it by not cultivating? No' — this is the <s>abhāvanā-vikalpa</s> (conceptualization of non-cultivation).

body.text: neti bhāvayannābhāvayannanuprāpsyati / neti naiva bhāvanānābhāvanāvikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'No — will one attain it by neither cultivating nor not cultivating? No' — this is the conceptualization of neither cultivation nor non-cultivation.

body.text: tatkathaṃ tāmanuprāpsyati yathā tathatā bhūtakoṭīrdharmadhāturityayathātvavikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Then how will one attain it? In the manner that <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), <s>bhūtakoṭi</s> (limit of reality), <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of phenomena)' — this is the <s>ayathātva-vikalpa</s> (conceptualization of what is not in accordance with reality).

body.text: iti dvitīyo grāhyavikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus is the second <s>grāhya-vikalpa</s> (conceptualization of the apprehended).

body.text: tṛtīyaṃ vikalpanavakamadhikṛtya śāstram-
body.translated_text: Regarding the third set of nine conceptualizations, the treatise states—

children.translated_text: The first <s>grāhaka</s> (conceptualization of the apprehender) should be known as having the domain of the designation of beings (<s>sattva-prajñapti</s>),
and as consisting of the power of investigation regarding the non-emptiness of the designation of <s>dharmas</s>. [5-30]

children.text: kṛtena vastuno yānatritaye ca sa kīrtitaḥ /
children.translated_text: It is proclaimed in regard to an entity's having been produced, the three vehicles,
the impurity of offerings (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>), and the disruption of practice. [5-31]

body.text: aprajñapanīyāḥ sattvāḥ anupalambhāditi sattvaprajñaptivikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Beings are not to be designated — because of non-apprehension' — this is the <s>sattva-prajñapti-vikalpa</s> (conceptualization of the designation of beings).

body.text: aprajñapanīyāḥ sarvadharmā iti dharmaprajñaptivikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'All <s>dharmas</s> are not to be designated' — this is the <s>dharma-prajñapti-vikalpa</s> (conceptualization of the designation of dharmas).

body.text: alakṣaṇaśūnyān sarvadharmān paśyatītyaśūnyatvavikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'One sees all <s>dharmas</s> as devoid of characteristics and empty' — this is the <s>aśūnyatva-vikalpa</s> (conceptualization of non-emptiness).

body.text: dharmāśca dharmānupalambhaśca yaścābhyāṃ carati sopi nopalabhyata iti śaktivikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: '<s>Dharmas</s>, the non-apprehension of <s>dharmas</s>, and the one who practices through both — he too is not apprehended' — this is the <s>śakti-vikalpa</s> (conceptualization of power).

body.text: dharmāṇāṃ pravicayaḥ kartavyaḥ / sa cānupalambhayogeneti pravicayātmako vikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'The investigation of <s>dharmas</s> should be carried out. And that through the method of non-apprehension' — this is the <s>pravicayātmaka-vikalpa</s> (conceptualization consisting of investigation).

body.text: na ca vastunaḥ kṛte so 'syāṃ carati / yato 'kṛtāvikṛtānabhisaṃskṛtā sarvadharmā iti vastūddeśavikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'And he does not practice therein for the sake of any entity. Because all <s>dharmas</s> are unmade, unaltered, and uncompounded' — this is the <s>vastūddeśa-vikalpa</s> (conceptualization of the designation of an entity).

body.text: yadyapyakṛtāvikṛtānabhisaṃskṛtāḥ sarvadharmāstathāpi yathā kaścittathāgatanirmito 'bhisaṃbudhya dharmacakraṃ pravartya tribhiryānaiḥ sattvān parimocayati lokavyavahāreṇa na paramārthena tathaiva ca tathāgatopīti yānatrayavikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: Even though all <s>dharmas</s> are unmade, unaltered, and uncompounded, nevertheless, just as a certain emanation of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, having attained perfect awakening and turned the <s>Dharmacakra</s> (wheel of Dharma), liberates beings through the three vehicles — by worldly convention, not in the ultimate sense — so too is it with the <s>Tathāgata</s> himself. This is the <s>yānatraya-vikalpa</s> (conceptualization of the three vehicles).

body.text: yadyapi tathāgato nirmitānna viśiṣyate tathāpi dakṣiṇāpariśuddhiḥ / yathā hi tathāgate pratiṣṭhāpitā dakṣiṇā ānirupadhiśeṣānnirvāṇānna kṣīyate tathāḥ nirmitepi / tathā tathāgatāyākāśe puṣpāṇi kṣipatastathā namo buddhāyeti bruvato manasi kurvato vā saṃjñāṃ ca pramāṇīkṛtya yā hi dharmatā tathāgatasya saiva vinirmitasyāpīti dakṣiṇāpariśuddhivikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: Although the <s>Tathāgata</s> is not distinguished from his emanations, nevertheless the purification of offerings (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>) applies. Just as an offering established in the <s>Tathāgata</s> does not diminish from <s>nirvāṇa</s> without remainder (<s>anupadhiśeṣa-nirvāṇa</s>), so too with the emanation. Likewise, for one who casts flowers into the sky before the <s>Tathāgata</s>, or who says 'Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>,' or who directs mental attention, taking perception as authoritative — for the <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature) of the <s>Tathāgata</s> is the same as that of the emanation. This is the <s>dakṣiṇā-pariśuddhi-vikalpa</s> (conceptualization of the purification of offerings).

body.text: caryā pāramitādiḥ / tasyā vikopanaṃ bhedanam / kutaḥ? dharmatātaḥ / dānapāramitāyā yāvat prajñāpāramitāyā vā / evaṃ yāvatsarvadharmāṇāṃ dharmateti / kathaṃ tarhi bhagavatā dharmā vikopitāḥ? nāmanirmitā hi te dharmā nirdiṣṭā dharmāṇāṃ sūcanāya / kathaṃ paro 'vatarediti / na tu dharmāṇāṃ dharmatā vikopiteti caryāvikopanavikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: Practice means the <s>pāramitās</s> and so forth. Its disruption means its breaking apart. From what cause? From <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature). Of <s>Dānapāramitā</s>, up to <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Similarly, the <s>dharmatā</s> of all <s>dharmas</s>. 'Then how were <s>dharmas</s> disrupted by the <s>Bhagavat</s>?' Those <s>dharmas</s> were taught as mere designations, for the purpose of indicating <s>dharmas</s> — 'How would the other enter [the teaching]?' But the <s>dharmatā</s> of <s>dharmas</s> was not disrupted. This is the <s>caryā-vikopana-vikalpa</s> (conceptualization of the disruption of practice).

body.text: caturthaṃ vikalpanavakamadhikṛtya śāstram
body.translated_text: Regarding the fourth set of nine conceptualizations, the treatise states—

children.translated_text: The other [conceptualization], ninefold, has as its domain the designation of beings and its causes,
is connected with the path of cultivation, and is the opposing factor, by virtue of its obstruction. [5-32]
Regarding the threefold non-occurrence of each of the three omnisciences,
on the path of peace, in conjunction and disjunction with <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) and so forth; [5-33]
And in inequality, in suffering and so forth, in the nature of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions),

children.text: dvayābhāve ca sammohe vikalpaḥ paścimo mataḥ // 5-34 //
children.translated_text: and in the absence of duality — this is regarded as the final conceptualization based on confusion. [5-34]

body.text: yairākārairliṅgairnimittairdharmāḥ sūcyante tāni tathāgatenānubuddhāni / tenocyate tathāgatasya sarvākārajñateti sarvākārajñatāsammohavikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: The aspects, marks, and signs by which <s>dharmas</s> are indicated — those have been awakened to by the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Therefore it is said that the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience of all aspects) — this is the <s>sarvākārajñatā-sammoha-vikalpa</s> (conceptualization of confusion regarding omniscience of all aspects).

body.text: yau ca śrāvakapratyekabuddhamārgau ye ca bodhimārgāste sarve bodhisattvena paripūrayitavyāḥ / taiśca mārgakaraṇīyaṃ kartavyam / na ca bhūtakoṭiḥ sākṣātkartavyāparipūrya praṇidhānamaparimucya sattvānapariśodhya buddhakṣetraṃ tenocyate bodhisattvasya mārgajñateti mārgajñatāsammohavikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: The paths of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and the paths to awakening — all these should be completed by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. And with those paths, what is to be done must be done. But one should not directly realize <s>bhūtakoṭi</s> (the limit of reality) without completing one's vow and without liberating beings and without purifying the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field). Therefore it is said that the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s <s>mārgajñatā</s> (path-omniscience) — this is the <s>mārgajñatā-sammoha-vikalpa</s> (conceptualization of confusion regarding path-omniscience).

body.text: etāvadeva sarvaṃ yadādhyātmikabāhyā dharmāḥ / te ca śrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ sarvajñateti sarvajñatāsammohavikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: All this is just this much — namely, internal and external <s>dharmas</s>. And those constitute the <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience) of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> — this is the <s>sarvajñatā-sammoha-vikalpa</s> (conceptualization of confusion regarding omniscience).

body.text: sarvadharmāṇāṃ pāraṃ nirvāṇaṃ gatā sarvārthā vā gatānayeti prajñāpāramitā / sarvadharmāṇāṃ vā pāraṃ paramo 'rtho 'bhinnaṃ tattvaṃ so 'syāṃ tathāgatairduṣṭaḥ / api cāsyāṃ tathatā bhūtakoṭirdharmadhāturantargatastenocyate prajñāpāramiteti śāntimārgasammohavikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> means: all <s>dharmas</s> have gone to the other shore, <s>nirvāṇa</s>; or, all purposes have gone, have been led, by it. Or, the ultimate meaning of all <s>dharmas</s>, the undivided reality — that has been seen in it by the <s>Tathāgatas</s>. Moreover, <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), <s>bhūtakoṭi</s> (limit of reality), and <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of phenomena) are included within it. Therefore it is called <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. This is the <s>śānti-mārga-sammoha-vikalpa</s> (conceptualization of confusion regarding the path of peace).

body.text: neyaṃ tathatādibhiḥ saṃyuktā na visaṃyuktā / tathāhīyamarūpānidarśanāpratighā, ekalakṣaṇā yadutālakṣaṇātvāditi tathatādisaṃyogaviyogavikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: It is neither conjoined with <s>tathatā</s> and so forth, nor disjoined from them. For thus it is formless, without indication, without resistance, of a single characteristic — namely, because of being without characteristics. This is the <s>tathatādi-saṃyoga-viyoga-vikalpa</s> (conceptualization of conjunction and disjunction with suchness and so forth).

body.text: neyaṃ kaiścidācchettuṃ(?) śakyate / tasmādasādhāraṇīkṛtya samatvasammohavikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: It cannot be cut off by anyone. Therefore, the conceptualization of confusion regarding equality, which treats it as exclusive — this is the <s>samatva-sammoha-vikalpa</s> (conceptualization of confusion regarding equality).

body.text: asyāṃ caratā duḥkhasamudayanirodhamārgādyartheṣu caritavyamiti duḥkhādisammohavikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: While practicing therein, one should practice regarding the objects of suffering, origination, cessation, and the path, and so forth — this is the <s>duḥkhādi-sammoha-vikalpa</s> (conceptualization of confusion regarding suffering and so forth).

body.text: rāgādayo nārtho nānartha iti prakṛtisammohavikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Rāga</s> (desire) and the like are neither beneficial nor harmful — this is the <s>prakṛti-sammoha-vikalpa</s> (conceptualization of confusion regarding the nature [of afflictions]).

body.text: yathā na dvayo nādvayo dharma upalabhyate tathā nadvayaṃ nādvayaṃ dharmamanuprāpnotīti dvayābhāvasammohavikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: Just as no <s>dharma</s> that is dual or non-dual is apprehended, so too one does not attain a <s>dharma</s> that is dual or non-dual — this is the <s>dvayābhāva-sammoha-vikalpa</s> (conceptualization of confusion regarding the absence of duality).

body.text: ityuktāḥ ṣaṭtriṃśabhdāvanāheyāḥ vikalpāḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus have been explained the thirty-six conceptualizations to be abandoned through cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>).

body.text: evaṃ tāvabhdavatu doṣāṇāṃ kṣayo guṇānāṃ punaḥ kathamudaya ityata āha-
body.translated_text: Thus let there be the elimination of faults. But how then does the arising of qualities occur? To this, [the treatise] says—

children.translated_text: When these impurities have been eliminated, like those who have been revived after a long time,
the abundances of qualities, which accomplish the happiness of the world in all its aspects, [arise]. [5-35]
All [qualities], with their complete convergence, attend upon
that great being who is replete with desired fruits, as rivers [flow toward] the great ocean. [5-36]

body.text: prakṛtisiddhā guṇāḥ kevalamākrāntā [a]guṇairāśān cireṇa / doṣakṣayāt praśatā (? prakaṭā?) i(e)va taṃ bodhisattvaṃ bhajante sarvadoṣaprahāṇaśālinam / 'abhisāraḥ' saṃdohaḥ / śeṣaṃ gatārtham //
body.translated_text: The qualities are established by nature; they were merely obscured by faults for a long time. Due to the elimination of faults, they become manifest and attend upon that <s>Bodhisattva</s> who is replete with the abandonment of all faults. '<s>Abhisāra</s>' means 'convergence' (<s>saṃdoha</s>). The rest is self-evident.

body.text: tasyetyādi vivarjayiṣyatīni yāvat / iti bhāvanāmārgasyānuśaṃsaḥ //
body.translated_text: Beginning with 'Of that' and so on, up to 'will abandon.' Thus is the benefit of the path of cultivation (<s>bhāvanā-mārga</s>).

body.text: ānantaryasamādhirvaktavyaḥ / tamadhikṛtya śāstram-
body.translated_text: The <s>ānantarya-samādhi</s> (immediate concentration) is to be explained. Regarding that, the treatise states—

children.translated_text: Having established the people of the three-thousand[-fold world-system] in the attainment of <s>Śrāvaka</s>- and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>-[awakening],
and the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in the <s>niyāma</s> (certainty of attainment), with merit comparable to the wholesome — [5-37]
By the abundance of that merit, the immediate [concentration leading to] the attainment of Buddhahood —
that is the <s>ānantarya-samādhi</s> (immediate concentration), and that is <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience of all aspects). [5-38]

body.text: antarayituṃ śakto 'ntaryaḥ / na tathā anantaryaḥ svārtha'ṇ / ānantaryaḥ samādhiḥ sa uktaḥ sūtre / kathamānantaryaḥ? yathā 'buddhatvāpteranantaraḥ' / avyavahitau hetuḥ kathamuktaḥ? 'puṇyabahutvena' / tadapi kathamuktam? śubhaṃ puṇyaṃ tadevopamā / tāṃ kṛtvā / kathaṃ tacchubham? trisāhasrajanaṃ trisāhasralokadhātavīryā(yā)n sattvān 'pratiṣṭhāpya' / kva? 'śiṣyakhaḍgādhigamasampadi bodhisattvaniyāme ca / ' śiṣyāḥ śrāvakāḥ khaḍgāḥ pratyekabuddhāsteṣām / arthādgamyate bodhisattvasya ca prāṅniyāmāvakrānteradhigamasampattau bodhisattvaniyāme ca / kva punarevamuktaṃ puṇyabahutvam? mahatyorbhagavatyo / asyāṃ kathamuktam? aupalambhikabodhisattvoyāṃ (ttvasya) gaṃgānadīvālukopamakalpakṛtāddānamayātpuṇyādenaṃ samādhimantaśo 'cchaṭāsaṃghātamātramapi samāpadyamānasya bahutarapuṇyatvena / etatkārikāyāṃ kathamuktam? vināpi tena cārthagateścakārasyānuktasamuccayārthatvāt / 'sarvākārajñatā ca tat' iti / tacca buddhatvaṃ sarvākārajñatālakṣaṇam //
body.translated_text: That which is capable of obstructing is an obstacle (<s>antarya</s>). Not so the unobstructed (<s>anantarya</s>) — [meaning] its own purpose. The <s>ānantarya-samādhi</s> (immediate concentration) — that is spoken of in the <s>sūtra</s>. How is it 'immediate' (<s>ānantarya</s>)? As [stated]: 'immediately [preceding] the attainment of Buddhahood.' How is the cause of [being] uninterrupted stated? 'Through the abundance of merit.' How is that also stated? The auspicious (<s>śubha</s>) is merit (<s>puṇya</s>) — that itself is the simile (<s>upamā</s>). Having made that [simile] — how is it auspicious? By 'establishing' beings of the three-thousand-fold world, beings of the power of the three-thousand great world-system — where? 'In the attainment of the disciples and solitary realizers, and in the certainty of the <s>bodhisattva</s>.' The 'disciples' are <s>śrāvakas</s>; the 'solitary ones' (<s>khaḍga</s>) are <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>; of those — the meaning is understood: of the <s>bodhisattva</s> too, prior to entering certainty (<s>niyāma</s>), in the attainment and in the <s>bodhisattva</s>-certainty. Where then is this abundance of merit stated? In the [two] great [pāramitā sūtras], O Blessed Lady. How is it stated there? Because for the <s>bodhisattva</s> who apprehends [things as real], merit [accumulated] through giving over <s>kalpas</s> equal in number to the sands of the Ganges river is surpassed by the greater merit of one who attains even a mere finger-snap of this <s>samādhi</s>. How is this stated in the <s>kārikā</s>? Even without that [explicit statement], because of the implication of meaning, and because the particle 'ca' has the sense of aggregating what is unstated — '<s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience) is also that.' And that Buddhahood is characterized by <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects).

body.text:
ālambanamabhāvosyāḥ (sya) smṛtiścādhipatirmataḥ /
ākāraḥ śāntatā cā [tra]
body.translated_text: The object (<s>ālambana</s>) of this [samādhi] is non-existence (<s>abhāva</s>); mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>) is considered the dominant condition (<s>adhipati</s>); the aspect (<s>ākāra</s>) is quiescence (<s>śāntatā</s>); and here [the aim is]—

body.text: ānantaryasamādheḥ 'ālambanamabhāvaḥ' sarvadharmāṇāṃ smṛtiradhipatipratyayaḥ / 'ākāraḥ śāntatā' sarvadharmākārāstagamaḥ / 'atra' sarvākārajñatāyām-
body.translated_text: The object of the <s>ānantarya-samādhi</s> is 'non-existence' — of all <s>dharmas</s>. Mindfulness is the dominant condition (<s>adhipati-pratyaya</s>). The 'aspect is quiescence' — the subsiding of the aspects of all <s>dharmas</s>. 'Here' — in <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience)—

body.text: jalpājalpipravādinām // 5-39 //
body.translated_text: of those who engage in debate and counter-debate. // 5-39 //

body.text: vādināṃ jalpaiśca jalpaiśca prahṛtya yuddhaṃ vṛttaṃ 'jalpājalpi' / yathā daṇḍādaṇḍi / ataḥ sūtram / sarvopāyakauśalyāni parigrahītukāmenetyādi /
body.translated_text: A battle (<s>yuddha</s>) conducted by disputants striking with arguments and counter-arguments is called '<s>jalpājalpi</s>' — like [the compound] <s>daṇḍādaṇḍi</s> (mutual beating with sticks). Hence the <s>sūtra</s>: 'For one who wishes to comprehend all skillful means' — and so forth.

body.text: upeyata ityupāyaḥ sarvākārajñatā / tasmiṃ kauśalyāni vipratipattīnāmapohanāni / tāni labdhukāmena prajñāpāramitāyāmiti / ānantaryasamādhilakṣaṇāyām / caritavyaṃ prayogato nirhārataśca / nirhṛtya bhāvayitavyā / bhāvitāyāṃ tasyāmanantarameva sarvākārajñatālābhe sarvavipratipattīnāṃ kṣayāditi bhāvaḥ / abhinirharatīti yathālambanaṃ yathādhipati yathākāraṃ ca saṃmukhīkaroti / abhinirhartavyā iti svarasavāhinaḥ kartavyāḥ / atyayeneti / atyayo 'vadhiḥ / abhavyaścetyādinā tathāgatasamanvāhṛtasyānuśaṃsamāha nantvānantaryasamādhisamāpannasya / na hi tasya bhūyo durgatiḥ sugatirvā / anantarameva bodhiprāptaiḥ / śeṣaṃ sugamamāparivartasamāpteḥ /
body.translated_text: That which is approached is the means (<s>upāya</s>) — [namely] <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience). Skill (<s>kauśalya</s>) therein is the removal of wrong views (<s>vipratipatti</s>). By one wishing to obtain those, 'in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>' — that is, in [the Prajñāpāramitā] characterized by the <s>ānantarya-samādhi</s>. One should practice through application (<s>prayoga</s>) and extraction (<s>nirhāra</s>). Having extracted, one should cultivate [it]. When cultivated, immediately after that comes the attainment of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>, since all wrong views are exhausted — that is the import. 'Extracts' (<s>abhinirharati</s>) means brings face-to-face according to [its] object, according to [its] dominant condition, and according to [its] aspect. 'Should be extracted' means should be made to flow spontaneously. 'Atyayena' means 'atyaya' is a limit. With 'he is incapable' and so forth, [the text] states the benefit for one who is looked after by the <s>Tathāgata</s> and who has attained the <s>ānantarya-samādhi</s>. For there is no more lower rebirth or higher rebirth for him — immediately [comes] the attainment of enlightenment. The rest is easy to understand until the end of the chapter.

body.text: vipratipattīradhikṛtya śāstram-
body.translated_text: Regarding wrong views (<s>vipratipatti</s>), the treatise [states]—

children.translated_text: Regarding the arising of the object (<s>ālambana</s>), and regarding the ascertainment of its intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāva</s>),
regarding the knowledge of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience), regarding ultimate reality (<s>paramārtha</s>) together with conventional [truth] (<s>saṃvṛti</s>), // 5-40 //

children.text: prayoge triṣu ratneṣu sopāye samaye muneḥ /
children.translated_text: regarding practice (<s>prayoga</s>), regarding the Three Jewels together with the means (<s>upāya</s>), regarding the dispensation (<s>samaya</s>) of the Sage,
regarding error (<s>viparyāsa</s>), regarding the right path (<s>samārga</s>), and regarding the antidote and its opposite, // 5-41 //
regarding characteristics (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) and regarding meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) — wrong views are considered
[to occur] in relation to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>, sixteenfold, of the disputants. // 5-42 //

body.text: 'ṣoḍhā daśa' ceti ṣaṭdaśa ca ṣoḍaśetyarthaḥ / kutaḥ ṣoḍaśa? yatastāḥ ṣoḍaśasvartheṣu ālambanopapattyādiṣu / kathaṃ tarhi 'sarvākārajñatādhārāḥ' ālambanādistāsāṃ viṣayaḥ? viṣayasambandhāttu sarvākārajñatāyāṃ viṣayatvopacāraḥ / tadyathā rājaputre 'parāddho rājanyaparāddho bhavati / vipratipattayopi prāyeṇa pratipakṣapāṭhādunnetavyāḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Sixteenfold and ten' means sixteen — that is the meaning. Why sixteen? Because those [wrong views occur] in their sixteen respective topics — object, arising, etc. How then [are they] 'based on <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>'? The object etc. is the subject-matter of those [wrong views]; but through the relation to the subject-matter, there is a figurative attribution of being the subject-matter to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> [itself]. Just as one who offends against a prince is [said to be] one who offends against the king. The wrong views too should generally be extracted from the statement of the antidotes.

body.text: tatrādyā vipratipattiḥ / yadi sarvākārajñatāyā abhāva ālambanaṃ sa tarhi katamaḥ? yadi dharmāṇāṃ parikalpitaḥ svabhāvastadevaṃ bhrāntiḥ syādvālavijñānavat / atha paratantraḥ sa kathamabhāvaḥ? atra parihāraḥ / yasya svabhāvo nāsti so 'bhāvaḥ / nāsti sāṃyogikaḥ svabhāvo dharmāṇāṃ svayamabhāvāt / api ca tathatā svabhāvo dharmāṇāṃ sā cābhāva ityālambanopapattau vipratipattiḥ //
body.translated_text: The first wrong view: If the object (<s>ālambana</s>) of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> is non-existence (<s>abhāva</s>), then which [thing] is it [directed at]? If the intrinsic nature of <s>dharmas</s> is imagined (<s>parikalpita</s>), then there would be error, like the cognition of a child. If [it is] dependent (<s>paratantra</s>), how can it be non-existent? The response here: That whose intrinsic nature does not exist — that is 'non-existence.' There is no conjunctive intrinsic nature of <s>dharmas</s>, since they are self-non-existent. Moreover, <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) is the intrinsic nature of <s>dharmas</s>, and that is non-existence — this is the wrong view regarding the arising of the object.

body.text: yadyabhāvāḥ sarvadharmāḥ kenopāyakauśalyenādikarmiko dānādiṣu carati? deyadāyakadānādīnāmabhāvasvabhāvāvadhāraṇameva tasyopāyakauśalyamiti tatsvabhāvāvadhāraṇe vipratipattiḥ //
body.translated_text: If all <s>dharmas</s> are non-existent, by what skillful means does a beginner practice giving (<s>dāna</s>) etc.? The very ascertainment of the non-existence-nature of the gift, the giver, the giving, etc. is his skillful means — this is the wrong view regarding the ascertainment of intrinsic nature.

body.text: dṛṣṭasatyasya tarhi kimupāyakauśalyam? sa āryeṇa cakṣuṣā dharmān vyavalokayan bhāvamapi paratantraṃ svabhāvaṃ nopalabhate / saṃyogikena svabhāvena parikalpitena vā tasyāpyabhāvāt / kiṃ punarabhāvaṃ parikalpitaṃ svabhāvaṃ, tasyātyantamasattvāt / sa dānādau caran deyadāyakadānādīn pratyekamabhāva iti saṃjānīte / bhāvābhāvānupalambhe kathamabhāvaṃ saṃjānīte? saṃvṛtyā na tu paramārthena / iha dānādayaḥ sarve mārgaprakārāḥ sarvākārāḥ / teṣu jñātā(to) bhāvābhāvānupalambhaḥ / tato jñānaṃ koṭiṣvabhāvasaṃjñeti sarvākārajñatājñāne vipratipattiḥ //
body.translated_text: For one who has seen the truth, what then is skillful means? He, examining <s>dharmas</s> with the noble eye, does not apprehend even the dependent (<s>paratantra</s>) nature as existent — because of the non-existence of even that, by [its] conjunctive intrinsic nature or imagined [nature]. What is it then — the imagined intrinsic nature that is non-existent? Because of its utter non-reality. He, practicing giving etc., cognizes each of the gift, giver, giving, etc. as non-existent. If there is no apprehension of either existence or non-existence, how does he cognize [them as] non-existent? Conventionally (<s>saṃvṛtyā</s>), not ultimately. Here, giving etc. are all aspects of the path — all aspects (<s>sarvākāra</s>). Knowledge of those is the non-apprehension of existence and non-existence. Then knowledge at the extremes [takes] the designation of non-existence — this is the wrong view regarding the knowledge of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>.

body.text: yā saṃvṛtiḥ sa eva paramārthaḥ / eta ekaiva tayostathatā / api tu skandheṣu bhāvasaṃjñināṃ tatparihārārthamabhāva iti saṃvṛtyā nirdiśyate 'bhāvasaṃjñināṃ bhāva iti / paramārthato na bhāva upalabhyate nāpyabhāva iti satyadvaye vipratipattiḥ //
body.translated_text: That which is conventional (<s>saṃvṛti</s>) is itself the ultimate (<s>paramārtha</s>). That <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) of those two is one. Moreover, for those who have the notion of existence regarding the aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>), in order to remove that, 'non-existence' is taught conventionally — 'for those with the notion of existence, [there is] existence.' Ultimately, neither existence is apprehended nor non-existence — this is the wrong view regarding the two truths.

body.text: prayogaścaryā / kathaṃ caryā? śūnyāḥ sarvadharmā iti / sarvāsu ca śūnyatāsu dānādau ca sarva trakoṭitrayānupalambheneti prayoge vipratipattiḥ //
body.translated_text: Practice (<s>prayoga</s>) is conduct (<s>caryā</s>). How is the conduct? 'All <s>dharmas</s> are empty' — in all emptinesses and in giving etc., all through the non-apprehension of the three extremes — this is the wrong view regarding practice.

body.text: buddha iti karmaṇi niṣṭhā / tato jñātaḥ sarvo buddhaḥ syāt / atha buddhavāniti buddhaḥ kena kartari ktaḥ? sarvaśca cetano buddhaḥ syāt / atrottaram / bhūtārtha iti buddhaḥ / bhūtā nya(ya)sya dharmā abhisaṃbuddhā iti vā / bhūto asyārthaḥ pratividdha iti vā / abhisaṃbuddhā yathāvat sarvadharmā asyeti vā / caturṣvapi pakṣeṣu bahuvrīhau kṛte nairuktavidhiḥ kartavyaḥ / bhūtārtha ityartho jñeyaḥ / tatsambandhādvodhaḥ / samāsārthaḥ- bhūtamevārtho yasya bodhasya sa buddhaḥ / anyeṣāmavaśyaṃ kvacidbhrānteḥ / bhūtārthaḥ kathaṃ buddhaḥ? bhūtasya bubhdāvo arthasya sattvaṃ iti bhāvaḥ / bhūtā asya dharmā abhisambuddhā iti bhūtāḥ / bhūtairarthaiḥ puruṣasya sambandho jñānakṛta eva / iha tu prakarṣagaterabhisambodhaḥ kṛta iti pradarśanārthamabhisambuddhagrahaṇam / asyeti samāsārthaḥ / samāsastu dvayoreva padayoḥ / tatra bhutaśabdasya bubhdāvo dhramasya dvitīyākṣaralopaḥ / bhūto 'syārthaḥ pratividdha iti / pratividdhaḥ pratyakṣārthaḥ / tripado bahuvrīhiḥ / ddhaśabdātpūrvasya śabdasya curādeśaḥ / abhisambuddhā yathāvatsarvadharmā asyeti / matibuddhipūjārthebhyaśceti vartamāne ktaḥ / ktasya ca vartamāna iti
body.translated_text: '<s>Buddha</s>' — the suffix <s>kta</s> [is used] in the passive sense (<s>karman</s>). Then everything known would be '<s>buddha</s>.' Or if '<s>buddha</s>' means 'one who has knowledge' — [then the suffix] <s>kta</s> is in the agent sense — every sentient being would be '<s>buddha</s>.' The answer here: '<s>Buddha</s>' means [one whose] object is real (<s>bhūtārtha</s>). Or: 'Whose <s>dharmas</s> have been truly awakened to (<s>abhisaṃbuddha</s>).' Or: 'Whose object has been penetrated as real.' Or: 'One by whom all <s>dharmas</s> have been truly awakened to.' In all four interpretations, when a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound is formed, the etymological rule must be applied. '<s>Bhūtārtha</s>' means the object should be understood as knowledge (<s>bodha</s>). Through its relation to that. The meaning of the compound: that awakening whose object is real — that is '<s>buddha</s>.' For others, error somewhere is inevitable. How is '<s>bhūtārtha</s>' [the meaning of] '<s>buddha</s>'? The sense is: the existence of the object that is real, [expressed by] the possessive affix of '<s>bhūta</s>.' 'Whose <s>dharmas</s> have been truly awakened to' — 'bhūta' [is formed thus]. The relation of a person with real objects is created by knowledge alone. Here, however, because of the intensification expressed [by <s>abhi-</s>], the term <s>abhisaṃbuddha</s> is used for demonstration. 'Asya' — the meaning of the compound. But a compound is [formed] of only two words. There, of the word '<s>bhūta</s>' the possessive derivation; of the word '<s>dharma</s>' the deletion of the second syllable. 'Whose object has been penetrated as real' — 'penetrated' means directly perceived. [This is] a three-word <s>bahuvrīhi</s>. From the word '<s>ddha</s>', the preceding word undergoes the <s>cur</s>-substitution. 'By whom all <s>dharmas</s> have been truly awakened to' — the suffix <s>kta</s> [is used] in the present sense according to [the rule] 'after [roots meaning] understanding, devotion, worship, etc.' And [the suffix] <s>kta</s> in the present [tense] — the

body.text: kartari ṣaṣṭhī / atrādyasya padasya buśabdaḥ / atha dvitīyasya takāraḥ / tṛtīyasya dhaśabda iti buddharatne vipratipattiḥ //
body.translated_text: sixth case [genitive] is in the agent sense. Here the first word has the syllable '<s>bu</s>.' Then the second [has] the letter '<s>ta</s>.' The third [has] the syllable '<s>dha</s>' — this is the wrong view regarding the <s>Buddha</s>-jewel.

body.text: atha dharmaratnaṃ katamat? bodhiḥ / sarvadharmotkṛṣṭatvāt / tatra yadi dharmatā dharmātpṛthageva gaṇyate, 'dvayamidaṃ dharmadharmatāsaṃgrahāt' iti vacanāt, tadā tāthāgataṃ jñānaṃ bodhiḥ / iṇajādibhya iti budherbhāva iṇa / atha dharmatāpi dharmādharmaprakṛtitvāt / tadāsyaiva dharmaratnaṃ bhūtakoṭitvāt tattvaśikharatvādityarthaḥ / tadā ca karmaṇi budheriṇa / ubhayathāpi buddhistāthāgate jñāne pravartate prakarṣagateḥ / tatra dharmatāpakṣamadhikṛtyāha / "bodhiḥ śūnyatā tathatā bhūtakoṭirdharmatā dharmadhātuḥ" iti / tatra śūnyatā lakṣaṇataḥ / tathatā nirvikāratvāt / bhūtakoṭistattvaśikharatvāt / dharmatā dharmaprakṛtitvāt / dharmadhāturāryadharmāṇāṃ hetutvāt / punarāha / "nāmadheyamātrametat bodhiriti" iti / itiśabdo bhinnakramaḥ / nāmadheyamātrametaditi yo 'rthaḥ so 'rtho bodhirityarthaḥ / nāmadheyānāmarthaśūnyatā bodhiriti yāvat / punarāha / "abhedārtho bodhyarthaḥ" iti / sarvajñajñānatathatāmātraprakhyānāt / jñānapakṣamadhikṛtyāha / "bodhistathatāvitathatānanyatathatānanyathābhāvo bodheḥ" iti / tatra bodhestathateti bodhasya tathatā / tathaiva bodharūpeṇaiva bhāvo nālīkena rūpeṇa / avitathatetyabhrāntatā / ananyatathateti bodhādanyo 'līkastasya tathatā bodharūpatā / asatā tena rūpeṇa bodhasyaiva prakhyānāt / tadviraho 'nanyatathatā / ananyathībhāva iti / bodhasya prakṛtiḥ svenātmanā prakāśaḥ / tasyānyathībhāvo 'līkenātmanā prakāśaḥ / tadviraho 'nanyathībhāvaḥ / sarvavibhramaviveko jñānasya bodhirityarthaḥ / punarāha / "nāmanimittamātrametadvodhiriti" iti / itiśabdo bhinnakramaḥ / nāmanimittamātrametaditi yo bodhaḥ sā bodhirityarthaḥ / prayoga eṣa bodherbodhiṃ sūcayati / na tvayaṃ bodhiravikalpatvāttasyāḥ / tatra nāmetyarūpiṇaḥ skandhāḥ / teṣāmalīko 'rthasadṛśa ākāro nimittam / punarāha / "buddhānāṃ bodhastasmadvodhiḥ" iti / prakarṣagateriti bhāvaḥ / punarāha "buddhairabhisambuddhā tasmādvodhiḥ" iti / arthaḥ pradhānamasminvacane na śabdaḥ / buddhānāmadhigatastasmādvodhirityarthaḥ / ṣaṣṭhīsamāse kṛte pūrvapadasya bobhāvaḥ / uttarapadasya dhiśabdaḥ śeṣaḥ / umāśabdavanniyoga iti dharmaratne vipratipattiḥ //
body.translated_text: Now what is the <s>Dharma</s>-jewel? <s>Bodhi</s> (enlightenment) — because it is the most excellent of all <s>dharmas</s>. There, if <s>dharmatā</s> (the nature of reality) is counted as entirely separate from <s>dharma</s>, from the statement 'these two [are included in] the collection of <s>dharma</s> and <s>dharmatā</s>,' then the knowledge of the <s>Tathāgata</s> is <s>bodhi</s>. [The suffix] <s>iṇ</s> [is derived] from [the root] <s>budh</s> in the sense of a state, according to '<s>iṇ</s> after [roots like] <s>aj</s> etc.' Or if <s>dharmatā</s> too [is included], since it is the essential nature of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> — then that itself is the <s>Dharma</s>-jewel, because it is the ultimate point of reality (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>), because it is the pinnacle of truth — that is the meaning. Then [the suffix] <s>iṇ</s> from <s>budh</s> is in the passive sense. In both cases, <s>buddhi</s> (understanding) applies to the knowledge of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, due to intensification. Regarding the <s>dharmatā</s> interpretation, [the sūtra] says: '<s>Bodhi</s> is emptiness, suchness, the ultimate point, dharmatā, dharmadhātu.' There: 'emptiness' — by way of characteristic; 'suchness' — because of non-transformation; 'ultimate point' (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>) — because it is the pinnacle of truth; '<s>dharmatā</s>' — because it is the essential nature of <s>dharmas</s>; '<s>dharmadhātu</s>' — because it is the cause of noble <s>dharmas</s>. [The sūtra] further says: 'This is merely a designation — <s>bodhi</s>.' The word '<s>iti</s>' is in inverted order. 'This is merely a designation' — this meaning is what '<s>bodhi</s>' means. That is: the emptiness-of-meaning of designations is <s>bodhi</s>. [The sūtra] further says: 'The meaning of <s>bodhi</s> is the meaning of non-duality' — because only the suchness of omniscient knowledge is proclaimed. Regarding the knowledge interpretation, [the sūtra] says: '<s>Bodhi</s> is the suchness, non-falsity, non-other-suchness, and non-alteration of awakening.' There: 'suchness of awakening' — the suchness of awakening; as awakening itself, existence in the form of awakening alone, not in a false form. 'Non-falsity' — non-erroneousness. 'Non-other-suchness' — the suchness of something other than awakening that is false, [meaning] its awakening-form; since even that unreal [thing] is proclaimed as having the form of awakening; the absence of that [otherness] is 'non-other-suchness.' 'Non-alteration' — the nature of awakening is self-luminosity; its alteration would be luminosity in a false form; the absence of that is 'non-alteration.' The meaning is: <s>bodhi</s> of knowledge is the discrimination from all error. [The sūtra] further says: 'This is merely name and sign — <s>bodhi</s>.' The word '<s>iti</s>' is in inverted order. 'This is merely name and sign' — that understanding is <s>bodhi</s> — that is the meaning. This formulation of <s>bodhi</s> indicates [further] <s>bodhi</s>. But this itself is not <s>bodhi</s>, because of its (<s>bodhi</s>'s) non-conceptual nature. There, 'name' — the formless aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>). Their unreal aspect resembling an object is the 'sign' (<s>nimitta</s>). [The sūtra] further says: 'The awakening of <s>Buddhas</s> — therefore <s>bodhi</s>' — the sense is: due to intensification.
