[The sūtra] further says: 'Truly awakened to by <s>Buddhas</s> — therefore <s>bodhi</s>.' The meaning is primary in this statement, not the word. The meaning is: attained by <s>Buddhas</s> — therefore <s>bodhi</s>. When a genitive compound is formed, the first member undergoes the '<s>bo</s>'-transformation; the remaining part of the latter member is the syllable '<s>dhi</s>'; the connection is like [that of] the word '<s>umā</s>' — this is the wrong view regarding the <s>Dharma</s>-jewel.

body.text: saṃhatatvāt saṃghaḥ / abhedyo 'cchedya ityarthaḥ / kasmādabhedyaḥ / kena vā / samyaksambodherabhedyaḥ / sadevakena samārakena lokena hīnabodherāhārakairdharmairakuśalaiśceti saṃgharatne vipratipattiḥ //
body.translated_text: Because of being united, [it is called] <s>Saṃgha</s>. Meaning: indivisible, unbreakable. Why indivisible? Or by whom [is it indivisible]? Indivisible from <s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (perfect awakening). [Indivisible] by the world with its gods and <s>Māra</s>, by those who seek the inferior awakening, by unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> — this is the wrong view regarding the <s>Saṃgha</s>-jewel.

body.text: 'sopāye samaye muneḥ iti kārikāpāṭhe upāyakauśalamupāya uktaḥ / viṣayeṇa viṣayiṇo nirdeśāt / abhisamayaḥ samayaḥ ityuktaḥ / ayo bodhaḥ / sa(saṃ)śabdaḥ saṃmukhārthaḥ / mithyājñānamajñānameveti bhāvaḥ / muneriti bhāvapradhānam / buddhatvasyetyarthaḥ / upāyakauśalyaṃ bodherabhisamayaṃ ceti samudāyārthaḥ / "avirahitasarvajñatācitto dānādiṣu carati koṭītrayānupalambhena / na ca dānādīnāṃ vipākamātmani spṛhayati / kintu sarvasattvaparimocanāya samyaksambodhau pariṇāmayati" ityādikamupāyakauśalyaṃ vistareṇetyupāyakauśalye vipratipattiḥ //
body.translated_text: 'With skillful means and the realization of the sage' — in the verse reading, <s>upāyakauśalya</s> (skillful means) is stated as '<s>upāya</s>' (means). Because of indicating the possessor through the object. '<s>Abhisamaya</s>' (realization) is stated as '<s>samaya</s>' (occasion). '<s>Aya</s>' means understanding. The prefix '<s>sam</s>' has the meaning of 'face to face.' 'Wrong knowledge is just non-knowledge' — this is the meaning. '<s>Muneḥ</s>' (of the sage) — the expression is primarily in the abstract sense; the meaning is 'of <s>buddhahood</s>.' The collective meaning is 'skillful means and the realization of awakening.' 'Not being separated from the thought of <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience), one practices generosity and the rest through the non-apprehension of the three spheres. And one does not desire the ripening of generosity and the rest for oneself, but rather dedicates it toward <s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (perfect awakening) for the liberation of all beings' — this and the like constitutes <s>upāyakauśalya</s> in detail. Thus [this is] the error regarding skillful means.

body.text: astyabhisamayo niḥprapañcetyatra na bhāvo nābhāva ityabhisamaye vipratipattiḥ //
body.translated_text: 'There is realization, [which is] free from conceptual elaboration' — herein, 'neither existence nor non-existence' — this is the error regarding realization.

body.text: sūtre prapañcaśabdaḥ paṭhyate / śāstre viparyāsaśabdaḥ / ubhayorekārthatvāt / rūpaṃ nityamanityaṃ rūpaṃ sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ rūpamātmānātmetyādayo viparyāsasyātibahavaḥ / saṃkṣepato yāvānvikalpaḥ sa sarvaḥ prapañcaḥ / aprapañcānna prapañcayatīti pratipakṣaḥ / aprapañco dharmadhāturnirvikalpatvāt / tanna prapañcayatīti na vikalpayatīti viparyāse vipratipattiḥ //
body.translated_text: In the <s>sūtra</s>, the word '<s>prapañca</s>' (conceptual elaboration) is read. In the treatise, the word '<s>viparyāsa</s>' (distortion) [is read]. Because both have the same meaning. 'Form is permanent, form is impermanent; form is pleasant, form is suffering; form is self, form is non-self' — such distortions are exceedingly numerous. In brief, whatever conceptual discrimination there is — all of that is <s>prapañca</s> (conceptual elaboration). 'From non-elaboration, he does not elaborate' — this is the antidote. The non-elaboration is the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of dharmas), because of being free from conceptual discrimination. 'He does not elaborate that' means 'he does not conceptually discriminate.' Thus [this is] the error regarding distortion.

body.text: iha bodhisattvena durgatimārgā jñātavyāḥ sahetuphalaistebhyaśca sattvā nivārayitavyāḥ / evaṃ narakinannaragaruḍagandharvādimārgāḥ / evaṃ cāturmahārājikānāṃ trāyastriṃśānāṃ yāvannaivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanānām / evaṃ śrotaāpannamārgo yāvadarhanmārgaḥ pratyekabuddhamārgo bodhisattvamārgo buddhamārgaśca jñātavyaḥ sahetuḥ saphalaḥ / ye ca yasmin pale vyavasthāpanīyāstāṃsteṣu vyavasthāpayati yāvabudddhatve / svayaṃ tu hīnayānabhūmīḥ sarvā (rva?) jñānena cātikramya bodhisattvayānamavakrāmatīti mārge vipratipattiḥ //
body.translated_text: Here, the <s>bodhisattva</s> must know the paths of the evil destinies together with their causes and fruits, and must prevent beings from [falling into] them. Similarly, the paths of hell-beings, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, and the like. Similarly, [the paths] of the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> [gods], the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> [gods], up to the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. Similarly, the path of the stream-enterer up to the path of the <s>arhat</s>, the path of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s>, the path of the <s>bodhisattva</s>, and the path of the <s>Buddha</s> — [all] must be known together with their causes and fruits. And those who are to be established in whichever fruit — he establishes them in those, up to <s>buddhahood</s>. But he himself, having transcended all the stages of the lesser vehicles through [omniscient] knowledge, enters the <s>bodhisattva</s> vehicle. Thus [this is] the error regarding the path.

body.text: iha sarva evāryapudgalāḥ kleśopakleśaiḥ kāmarūpārūpyadhātubhirbodhipakṣaiḥ pāramitādibhistatphalaiśca sarvāryadharmerna saṃyuktvā na visaṃyuktvā arūpiṇo 'nidarśanā ekalakṣaṇā yadutālakṣaṇāḥ / ya evaṃ na jānanti tān prati saṃvṛsyā nirdiśyate bodhipakṣā dharmā bodherāhārakā bodhyāvaraṇānāmapahārakā iti vipakṣapratipakṣayorvipratipattiḥ //
body.translated_text: Here, all noble persons — without being conjoined with or disjoined from afflictions and secondary afflictions, the desire, form, and formless realms, the factors of awakening, the <s>pāramitās</s> and the like, and their fruits, and all noble <s>dharmas</s> — are formless, non-demonstrable, of one characteristic, namely without characteristics. For those who do not know this, it is taught conventionally: 'The factors of awakening (<s>bodhipakṣya dharmas</s>) are the nourishment of awakening and the removers of obscurations to awakening.' Thus [this is] the error regarding the opponents and antidotes.

body.text: vistareṇa bhagavatā dharmāṇāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ deśitaṃ sattvānāmavatāraṇāya saṃvṛtyā paramārthatastena lakṣaṇe śikṣitavyaṃ nālakṣaṇe / yataḥ sthita evaiṣa nityaṃ lakṣaṇadhāturiti lakṣaṇe vipratipattiḥ //
body.translated_text: The characteristic of <s>dharmas</s> has been taught in detail by the <s>Bhagavān</s> conventionally, for the purpose of introducing beings [to the teaching]. One should train in the characteristic by means of ultimate reality — not in the absence of characteristics. Because 'this realm of characteristics is always established.' Thus [this is] the error regarding characteristics.

body.text: yadyalakṣaṇāḥ pāramitādayo dharmāḥ kathamalakṣaṇānāṃ teṣāṃ bhāvanā bhavati? "nāsti subhūte 'bhāvasvabhāveṣu dharmeṣu bhāvasaṃjñinaḥ prajñāpāramitā bhāvanāviparyāsāt / api tu sarvāsāṃ dharmasaṃjñānāṃ bhāvanāvibhāvane prajñāpāramitā / evaṃ yāvannāsti bhāvasaṃjñino dānapāramitā bhāvanā / eṣohamasmai idaṃ dadāmītyevaṃ saṃjñinaḥ / " evaṃ bodhipakṣādiṣu vaktavyam / dṛṣṭasatyāstu dharmāṇāṃ kevalamabhāvasvabhāvatāṃ bhāvayanti na bhāvasaṃjñayā nānyabhāvasaṃjñayā / saṃjñā hi prapañcaḥ prajñāpāramitā tu niḥprapañceti bhāvanāyāṃ vipratipattiḥ /
body.translated_text: If the <s>pāramitās</s> and other <s>dharmas</s> are without characteristics, how can there be cultivation of those without characteristics? 'There is no cultivation of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> for one who perceives existence in <s>dharmas</s> that are without the nature of existence, O <s>Subhūti</s>, because of the distortion of cultivation. Rather, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is the non-manifestation of the cultivation of all perceptions of <s>dharmas</s>. Similarly, there is no cultivation of <s>dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of generosity) for one who perceives existence — for one who perceives "I give this to this person."' The same should be stated for the factors of awakening and the rest. But those who have seen the truths cultivate only the non-existence-nature of <s>dharmas</s> — not through the perception of existence, nor through the perception of another kind of existence. For perception is conceptual elaboration, while <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is free from conceptual elaboration. Thus [this is] the error regarding cultivation.

body.text: avakīrṇakusumanāmāno bodhisattvā iha parivarte bodhau vyākṛtāḥ / atastairupalakṣitaḥ parivartastatparivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: The <s>bodhisattvas</s> named <s>Avakīrṇakusuma</s> (Strewn Flowers) were predicted for awakening in this chapter. Therefore the chapter characterized by them is that chapter.

body.text: āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ sāratamānāmni pañjikāyāṃ ratnākaraśāntiviracitāyāmaṣṭaviṃśatitamaḥ parivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: In the <s>Pañjikā</s> commentary named <s>Sāratama</s>, composed by <s>Ratnākaraśānti</s>, on the noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s> — this is the twenty-eighth chapter.

body.text: 29. anugamaparivarto nāmaikonatriṃśattamaḥ /
body.translated_text: 29. The twenty-ninth [chapter] is named the '<s>Anugama-parivarta</s>' (Chapter on Following).

body.text: anupūrvābhisamaya idānīṃ vaktavyaḥ / tamadhikṛtya śāstram-
body.translated_text: The <s>anupūrvābhisamaya</s> (sequential realization) is now to be stated. Regarding that, the treatise [states] —

children.translated_text: Through generosity, through wisdom, up to [the other pāramitās], through recollections of the <s>Buddha</s> and the rest, and that —
through the non-existence-nature of <s>dharmas</s> — this is accepted as the sequential practice. // 6-1 //

body.text: 'anupūrvikriyā' anupūrvaśikṣā anupūrvapratipadyā pūrvamuddiṣṭā saṃprati nirdeṣṭavyā / sā 'matā' iṣṭā / kathamityāha / dānenetyādi / 'dānena' iti dānapāramitayā / 'prajñayā yāvad' iti prajñāpāramitayā / yāvadgrahaṇācchīlapāramitayā kṣāntipāramitayā vīryapāramitayā dhyānapāramitayā ca / 'buddhādau smṛtibhiśca' iti buddhādiviṣayābhiranusmṛtibhiḥ / cakāro bhinnakramaḥ / 'dharmābhāvasvabhāvena' ceti bhāvapradhāno nirdeśaḥ / dharmāṇāmabhāvasvabhāvatvena cetyarthaḥ / 'iti' evaṃ 'sā matā' /
body.translated_text: '<s>Anupūrvikriyā</s>' (sequential practice) — the sequential training, the sequential course of practice, was previously indicated in summary and is now to be explained in detail. It is 'accepted' — approved. 'How?' — he says 'through generosity' and so forth. 'Through generosity' means through the <s>dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of generosity). 'Through wisdom, up to' means through the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom). By the word 'up to,' through the <s>śīlapāramitā</s> (perfection of morality), <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s> (perfection of patience), <s>vīryapāramitā</s> (perfection of vigor), and <s>dhyānapāramitā</s> (perfection of meditation). 'Through recollections of the <s>Buddha</s> and the rest' means through the recollections (<s>anusmṛtis</s>) having the <s>Buddha</s> and others as their objects. The particle '<s>ca</s>' is in rearranged order. 'Through the non-existence-nature of <s>dharmas</s>' — the expression is primarily in the abstract sense. The meaning is 'through the non-existence-nature of <s>dharmas</s>.' 'Thus' — in this way, 'it is accepted.'

body.text: ataḥ sūtraṃ punaraparamityādi / evamiti vakṣyamāṇena vākyatrayeṇa / prajñāpāramitetyunupūrvakriyā / anugantavyeti veditavyā / kathamityāha / sarvadharmāsaṅgataḥ prajñāpāramitānugantavyā / sarvadharmāsambhedataḥ prajñāpāramitānugantavyā / sarvadharmāsambhavataḥ prajñāpāramitānugantavyeti / tatrādau sarvadharmāḥ
body.translated_text: Hence the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Furthermore' and so forth. 'Thus' — by means of the three sentences to be stated. '<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>' — the sequential practice. 'Is to be followed' means 'is to be understood.' 'How?' — he says: 'Through the non-attachment of all <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is to be followed. Through the non-division of all <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is to be followed. Through the non-origination of all <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is to be followed.' Therein, first, 'all <s>dharmas</s>'

body.text: ṣaṭpāramitāḥ / tāsāmeva bodhimārgatvāt / dharmaśabdasya ceha mārgavācitvāt / sarvadharmāṇāmasaṅgatā niḥsaṅgatā nirvighnatā / bodhisattvairanukramakaraṇīyeṣu prathamacittotpādādiṣu sattvaparimocanānteṣu tayā(thā?)sānugantavyā / tadyathā- "prathamacittotpādamupādāya dānapāramitāyāṃ carannātmanā ca dānaṃ dadāti parāṃśca dānapāramitāyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati dānasya ca varṇa bhāṣate / ye cānye dānapāramitāyāṃ caranti teṣāṃ ca varṇavādī bhavati samanujñaḥ / sa tena dānena mahāntaṃ bhogaskandha pratilabhya dānaṃ dadāti vigatamatsareṇa cittena annaṃ pānaṃ vastraṃ vilepanaṃ śayanamupāśrayamanyadvā pariṣkāropakaraṇaṃ dadāti tadarthinām / sa tena dānena sattvān śīle samādhau prajñāyāṃ vimuktau vimuktijñānadarśane ca pratiṣṭhāpayati / sa taireva śīlādiskandhaiḥ samanvāgataḥ śrāvakādibhūmimatikrāmati bodhisattvāniyāmamavakrāmati buddhakṣetraṃ pariśodhayati sattvān paripācayati sarvākārajñatāmanuprāpnoti dharmacakraṃ pravartayati / sattvāṃstriṣu yāneṣu pratiṣṭhāpya saṃsārātpratimocayati / evaṃ khalu dānenānupūrvakriyā / tāṃ ca sarvānnopalabhate / tathā hyasyāḥ svabhāvo nāsti / yasya ca svabhāvo nāsti so 'bhāva iti dānapāramitayānupūrvakriyā / evaṃ śīlādibhirapi" iti ṣaḍbhiḥ pāramitābhiḥ ṣaḍanupūrvakriyāḥ //
body.translated_text: are the six <s>pāramitās</s>. Because those very [<s>pāramitās</s>] are the path to awakening. And because the word '<s>dharma</s>' here means 'path.' 'The non-attachment of all <s>dharmas</s>' is their non-clinging nature, their unobstructed nature. In the sequential tasks to be performed by <s>bodhisattvas</s> — from the first generation of <s>bodhicitta</s> up to the liberation of beings — it is to be followed through that [non-attachment]. That is: 'Beginning from the first generation of <s>bodhicitta</s>, practicing the <s>dānapāramitā</s>, one gives gifts oneself and establishes others in the <s>dānapāramitā</s>, and praises generosity. And one approves of and praises those who practice the <s>dānapāramitā</s>. Through that generosity, having obtained a great mass of wealth, one gives gifts with a mind free from stinginess — food, drink, clothing, ointments, bedding, shelter, and other requisites and accessories — to those who desire them. Through that generosity, one establishes beings in morality, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation. Endowed with those very aggregates of morality and the rest, one transcends the stages of <s>śrāvakas</s> and others, enters the certainty of the <s>bodhisattva</s>, purifies the <s>buddha-kṣetra</s> (buddha-field), matures beings, attains <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience in all aspects), and turns the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>. Having established beings in the three vehicles, one liberates them from <s>saṃsāra</s>. Thus indeed, through generosity, [there is] the sequential practice. And all of that, one does not apprehend. For its self-nature does not exist. And that whose self-nature does not exist is non-existent' — thus, through the <s>dānapāramitā</s>, [there is] the sequential practice. 'Similarly through morality and the rest' — through the six <s>pāramitās</s>, six sequential practices.

body.text: sarvadharmāsambhedataḥ prajñāpāramitānugantavyeti / sarvadharmāḥ ṣaḍanusmṛtayaḥ / tāḥ kathaṃ dharmāḥ? cittadhāraṇāt / api ca puṇyamapi loke dharma ucyate / tāśca bhāvanāmayaṃ puṇyam / sarvadharmāṇāmasaṃbhedato 'bhinnatā samatā / abhāvasvabhāvatvāt / tayānugantavyeti pūrvavat / tathāhi- "bodhisattvaḥ prathamacittotpādamupādāya sarvākārajñatāpratisaṃyuktairmanasikārairabhāvasvabhāvānsarvadharmānadhimucya ṣaḍanusmṛtīrbhāvayati / tāḥ svayaṃ ca bhāvayati parāṃśca tāsu pratiṣṭhāpayati tāsāṃ ca varṇa bhāṣate / ye cānye tāsu caranti teṣāṃ varṇavādi bhavati samanujñaḥ / sa tāstathā bhāvayannabhāvasvabhāvayogena saptatriṃśataṃ(taḥ) bodhipakṣān yāvatsarvākārajñatāṃ paripurayati / so 'bhāvasvabhāvenaiva sarvadharmānabhisaṃbudhya dharmacakraṃ pravartya yāvatsarvasattvān parimocayati / tatra buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ na rūpādiskandhairna lakṣaṇānuvyañjanairna śīlādiskandhairna daśabalavaiśāradyapratisaṃvibhdirna mahākaruṇayā na mahāmaitryā nāṣṭādaśabhirāveṇikairnāpi pratītyasamutpādato mānasikaroti / tatkutaḥ? abhāvasvabhāvatvātteṣāmityanusmṛtiramanasikāro buddhānusmṛtiḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Through the non-division of all <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is to be followed.' 'All <s>dharmas</s>' are the six <s>anusmṛtis</s> (recollections). 'How are those <s>dharmas</s>?' Because they sustain the mind. Moreover, even merit is called '<s>dharma</s>' in the world. And those [recollections] are merit born of meditation. 'The non-division of all <s>dharmas</s>' is their undifferentiated nature, their equality — because of being of the nature of non-existence. Through that, it is to be followed — as before. That is: 'The <s>bodhisattva</s>, beginning from the first generation of <s>bodhicitta</s>, convinced of all <s>dharmas</s> as being of the nature of non-existence through mental attentions connected with <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>, cultivates the six <s>anusmṛtis</s>. He cultivates them himself and establishes others in them, and praises them. And he approves of and praises those who practice them. Cultivating them thus through the method of non-existence-nature, he fulfills the thirty-seven <s>bodhipakṣya</s> [dharmas], up to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>. Having fully awakened to all <s>dharmas</s> through the very nature of non-existence, having turned the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>, up to liberating all beings. Therein, one does not attend mentally to the blessed <s>Buddha</s> through the form-aggregates and the rest, through the marks and secondary marks, through the aggregates of morality and the rest, through the ten powers and fearlessnesses, through the analytical knowledges, through great compassion, through great loving-kindness, through the eighteen unique [<s>Buddha</s>-qualities], nor even through dependent origination. Why? Because those are of the nature of non-existence' — such recollection that is non-mental-attention is the recollection of the <s>Buddha</s>.

body.text: sa prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caranna kuśalā[ku]śalān dharmān manasikaroti / teṣāmabhāvasvabhāvatvādityamanasikāro dharmānusmṛtiḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, one does not attend mentally to wholesome and unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>. Because those are of the nature of non-existence' — such non-mental-attention is the recollection of the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: yosau bhagavataḥ srāvakasaṃghaścatvāraḥ puruṣayugā aṣṭau mahāpuruṣapudgalāḥ svabhāvastasya nāsti / yasya dharmasya svabhāvo nāsti so 'bhāva ityamanasikāro saṃghānusmṛtiḥ /
body.translated_text: 'That <s>saṃgha</s> of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s disciples — the four pairs of persons, the eight kinds of great persons — its self-nature does not exist. That <s>dharma</s> whose self-nature does not exist is non-existent' — such non-mental-attention is the recollection of the <s>Saṃgha</s>.

body.text: tena prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caratākhaṇḍe 'cchidre 'kalmāṣe 'parāmṛṣṭe bhujiṣye vijñapraśaste samādhisaṃvartanīye śīle sthitvā tacchīlamabhāvasvabhāvato manasikartavyamityamanasikāro śīlānusmṛtiḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, having established oneself in morality that is unbroken, uncut, unspotted, untouched, liberating, praised by the wise, conducive to concentration — one should attend mentally to that morality as being of the nature of non-existence' — such non-mental-attention is the recollection of morality.

body.text: sa prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carannāmiṣaṃ vā aṅgapratyaṅgāni vā tyajan sarvaṃ tadabhāvasvabhāvato manasikarotītyamanasikāro yo(tyā)gānusmṛtiḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, whether giving up material possessions or limbs and secondary limbs — one attends mentally to all of that as being of the nature of non-existence' — such non-mental-attention is the recollection of renunciation.

body.text: ye te devāḥ śrotaāpannāścāturmahārājakāyikeṣu yāvatparanirmitavaśavartiṣu deveṣūpapannāste sarve 'bhāvasvabhāvā ityanusmṛtiramanasikāro devatānusmṛtiḥ /"
body.translated_text: 'Those gods who are stream-enterers, [re]born among the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> gods up to the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods — all of them are of the nature of non-existence' — such recollection that is non-mental-attention is the recollection of the deities.

body.text: iti ṣaḍbhiranusmṛtibhiḥ ṣaḍanupūrvakriyāḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus, through the six <s>anusmṛtis</s> (recollections), six sequential practices.

body.text: sarvadharmāsambhavataḥ prajñāpāramitānugantavyeti / svalakṣaṇadhāraṇāt dharmāḥ / skandhā dhātava āyatanāni bodhipakṣāḥ pāramitā yāvatsarvākārajñateti sarvadharmāḥ / teṣāmasaṃbhavata ityasaṃbhavajñānato 'nupūrvakriyā veditavyā / asaṃbhavo 'bhāvasvabhāvatā / tathā hi- "teṣāṃ nāsti svabhāvaḥ / yasya svabhāvo nāsti so 'svabhāvaḥ / sa prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caran prathamacittotpādamupādāya sarvadharmāṇāmabhāvasvabhāvatāmadhimucya catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni catvāri samyakprahāṇāni yāvatsarvākārajñatāṃ bhāvayati / so 'bhāvasvabhāvān sarvadharmānabhisaṃbudhya dharmacakraṃ pravartayati / tribhiśca yānaiḥ sattvān saṃsārātparimocayati" iti dharmāṇāmabhāvasvabhāvatayā trayodaśyānupūrvakriyāḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Through the non-origination of all <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is to be followed.' '<s>Dharmas</s>' — because of bearing their own characteristics. Aggregates, elements, sense-bases, factors of awakening, <s>pāramitās</s>, up to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> — these are 'all <s>dharmas</s>.' 'Through their non-origination' — the sequential practice is to be understood through the knowledge of non-origination. Non-origination is the nature of non-existence. That is: 'Their self-nature does not exist. That whose self-nature does not exist is without self-nature. Practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, beginning from the first generation of <s>bodhicitta</s>, convinced of the non-existence-nature of all <s>dharmas</s>, one cultivates the four <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness), the four <s>samyakprahāṇas</s> (right exertions), up to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>. Having fully awakened to all <s>dharmas</s> as being of the nature of non-existence, one turns the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>. And through the three vehicles, one liberates beings from <s>saṃsāra</s>.' Thus, through the non-existence-nature of <s>dharmas</s>, thirteen sequential practices.

body.text: ita ūrdhvaṃ codyāni svayamūhyāni parihārāstu vaktavyāḥ / yadyabhāvasvabhāvāḥ pāramitā bhāvyante tadā tabhdāvanā niṣphalā turagaviṣāṇabhāvanāvaditi codyam / parihāramāha / sarvadharmā nirvikārasamā itītyādi / nirvikāro dharmadhātustena samāḥ sarvadharmā nābhāvamātreṇa / dharmadhātuścālambyamāna āryadharmāṇāṃ heturbhavati / ata eva dharmadhāturitucyate / tatkuto vaiphalyam?
body.translated_text: Henceforth, the objections are to be inferred by oneself; but the resolutions are to be stated. 'If the <s>pāramitās</s> are of the nature of non-existence and are cultivated, then their cultivation would be fruitless, like the cultivation of a horse's horn' — this is the objection. He states the resolution: 'All <s>dharmas</s> are equal in being without transformation' and so forth. The <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of dharmas) is without transformation; all <s>dharmas</s> are equal with it — not merely through non-existence. And the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, when taken as an object, becomes the cause of the noble <s>dharmas</s>. For that very reason it is called the '<s>dharmadhātu</s>' (element/cause of <s>dharmas</s>). Then whence [comes] fruitlessness?

body.text: nanu pratyātmavedya ātmā vijñaptiśca / ataḥ sati grāhake grāhyamapyastīti na yuktaḥ sarvadharmāṇāmabhāva iti codyam / parihāramāha / sarvadharmāṇāmamanātmavijñaptitaḥ prajñānubodhanata ityādi / anātmavijñaptita ityātmavilakṣaṇatvādanātmākāreṇa grāhyagrāhakavaidhuryādavijñaptyākāreṇa ca /
body.translated_text: Now, the objection is: the self is known individually (<s>pratyātmavedya</s>), and <s>vijñapti</s> (representation) also exists. Therefore, if the apprehender (<s>grāhaka</s>) exists, the apprehended (<s>grāhya</s>) must also exist — hence the non-existence of all <s>dharmas</s> is not established. To address this objection, he states: "from the non-self-representation of all <s>dharmas</s>, from the awakening by <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom)" and so forth. "Non-self-representation" (<s>anātmavijñaptitaḥ</s>) means: because it is different from the self, it has the aspect of non-self (<s>anātmākāra</s>); and because of the absence of the duality of apprehended and apprehender (<s>grāhyagrāhakavaidhurya</s>), it has the aspect of non-representation (<s>avijñaptyākāra</s>).

body.text: prajñānubodhanata iti pramāṇena pratīteḥ / ātmā hi nityaikarūpo jñātā na ca skandhādaya ithambhūtāḥ / tasmādanātmatvena siddhāḥ / grāhyagrāhakavaidhuryācca / ata eva ca vijñaptyākāreṇāpi siddhāḥ / grāhakalakṣaṇatvāttasyāḥ / grāhakābhāvādgrāhyamapi nāstīti siddhaḥ sarvadharmāṇāmabhāvaḥ /
body.translated_text: "From the awakening by <s>prajñā</s>" means: because it is ascertained by a valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>). For the self (<s>ātman</s>) is a knower that is eternal and of a single form, but the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) and so forth are not of such nature. Therefore they are established as non-self (<s>anātman</s>). And because of the absence of the duality of apprehended and apprehender. For this very reason, they are also established as having the aspect of non-representation (<s>avijñaptyākāra</s>), since that [representation] has the characteristic of an apprehender. Since there is no apprehender, the apprehended also does not exist — thus the non-existence of all <s>dharmas</s> is established.

body.text: rūpādiśabdairyebhilapyante ta eva rūpādayaḥ / asti ca loke taisteṣāmabhilāpaḥ / śrotṝṇāṃ vyavahāraḥ saṃvādaśca / tatkuto 'bhāvaḥ sarvadharmāṇāmiti codyam / parihāramāha / nāmamātreṇetyādinā / arthaśūnyaṃ nāma nāmamātram / tena te sarvadharmā abhilapyante / na hi buddhyākāra eṣāmartho bāhyatvena prati [ya]te, bāhye ca pravṛtteḥ / nāpi bāhya evārthaḥ, asatyapi bāhye śabdādarthagateḥ / buddhireva bāhyarūpeṇa śabdārtha iti cet / na caitasyā artho rūpaṃ, atyantabhedāt / abhede vā na visaṃvādaḥ syāt / buddhimantaścārthavantā bhaveyuḥ / tasmādarthābhāvānnāmamātreṇa vyavahāramātreṇābhilapyante / vyavahārastāvadastīti cedāha / vyavahāraścetyādi / na kvacidityarthābhāvat / na kutaściditi vācakābhāvāt / nāpi kaściditi na vāciko na ca kāyiko nāpi mānasaḥ / vācyavācakayorabhāvāt / sarvadharmā ityādinopasaṃhāraḥ / avyavahārā avyāhārā iti teṣu tayorabhāvāt / ata eva cāvyāhṛtāḥ /
body.translated_text: Those that are designated by words such as "form" (<s>rūpa</s>) and so forth are indeed <s>rūpa</s> and the rest. And in the world, there is designation of them by those [words]. Listeners have conventional usage and agreement. So the objection is: how can all <s>dharmas</s> be non-existent? To address this, he states "by mere name" and so forth. A name devoid of a real object is a mere name (<s>nāmamātra</s>). By that, all those <s>dharmas</s> are designated. For the mental image (<s>buddhyākāra</s>) is not their object as something external, since [words] function with reference to external [objects]. Nor is the external thing itself the object, since the meaning of words is apprehended even when no external [object] exists. If one says that cognition itself in the form of an external [object] is the meaning of the word — no, that is not its object or form, because of their utter difference. Or if they were non-different, there would be no error. And those possessing cognition would [always] possess real objects. Therefore, due to the absence of a [real] object, [things] are designated by mere name, by mere convention. If one says "at least convention exists," he states "and convention" and so forth. "Not anywhere" — because of the absence of a [real] object. "Not from anything" — because of the absence of a signifier. "Nor is there any" — neither verbal, nor bodily, nor mental, because of the absence of both the signified and the signifier. "All <s>dharmas</s>" and so forth is the conclusion. They are "without convention" (<s>avyavahāra</s>) and "without utterance" (<s>avyāhāra</s>), because both [signified and signifier] are absent in them. And for this very reason they are "unuttered" (<s>avyāhṛta</s>).

body.text: nanu rūpādīnāṃ pramāṇavattvāt tacchūnyatā api pramāṇavatya iti tadālambanā prajñāpāramitā pramāṇavatī syāt / na ceṣyata iti codyam / parihāramāha / sarvadharmāṇāṃ apramāṇata iti / apramāṇatvāt / tathā hi sarvadharmāṇāṃ nāsti pramāṇamabhāvalakṣaṇatvāt / ākāśasyeva rūpābhāvalakṣaṇasya, tatastacchūnyatānāmapi nāsti pramāṇamavacchedakābhāvāt / tataḥ prajñāpāramitāyā apyālambanābhedāt /
body.translated_text: Now, the objection is: since <s>rūpa</s> and the rest possess valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>), their emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) also possesses valid means of knowledge, so <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> which takes that as its object should possess valid means of knowledge — and this is not accepted. To address this, he states: "from the non-validity of all <s>dharmas</s>." Because they lack valid means of knowledge. For indeed, all <s>dharmas</s> have no <s>pramāṇa</s>, since their nature is non-existence — just as space (<s>ākāśa</s>), whose nature is the absence of form. Therefore their emptiness also has no <s>pramāṇa</s>, because there is no delimiting factor (<s>avacchedaka</s>). Hence, for <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> as well, because there is no difference in its object.

body.text: yadi tarhi rūpādayo na santi kaitya(kimiti) nīlādayaḥ prakhyānti / dharmanimittānyetāni na dharmavastūni / ekānekasvabhāvavirahāt, aprakāśātmanaḥ prakāśāyogācca / dharmanimittāni tu dharmabhrāntīnāmākārāḥ / tā hi prakāśarūpatvāt prakāśamānāstairasabhdirapi rūpaiḥ prakhyānti / asatkhyātilakṣaṇatvāda bhrāntīnām / yadyeva, na siddhayati prajñāpāramitā / sā khalvabhrāntā sākārā tu buddhirbhrāntaiva / na ca nirākārā buddhiḥ svapnepyanubhūyata iti codyam / parihāramāha / sarvadharmānimittata ityādinā / sarvadharmeṣvānimittaṃ nimittāstamayājjñānasya nirābhāsatā nirākāratā / tataḥ prajñāpāramitā veditavyā / ākāraparivarjanādārūpyasamāpattivaditi bhāvaḥ /
body.translated_text: If, then, <s>rūpa</s> and the rest do not exist, why do blue and other [colors] appear? These are <s>dharma</s>-signs (<s>dharmanimitta</s>), not <s>dharma</s>-realities (<s>dharmavastu</s>). Because they lack both singular and plural essential nature, and because that which is non-luminous by nature cannot be luminous. But <s>dharma</s>-signs are the aspects (<s>ākāra</s>) of <s>dharma</s>-delusions (<s>dharmabhrānti</s>). For those [delusions], being luminous in nature, appear as luminous even through those unreal forms. Because delusions have the characteristic of apprehending what is non-existent (<s>asatkhyāti</s>). If that is so, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is not established. For it is non-deluded, yet a cognition with aspects (<s>sākāra</s>) is indeed deluded. And a cognition without aspects (<s>nirākāra</s>) is never experienced even in dreams — this is the objection. To address this, he states "from the signlessness of all <s>dharmas</s>" and so forth. Signlessness (<s>ānimitta</s>) with respect to all <s>dharmas</s> means the absence of images (<s>nirābhāsatā</s>), the absence of aspects (<s>nirākāratā</s>) of knowledge, due to the setting of signs. From that, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is to be understood. The meaning is: through the abandonment of aspects, like the formless attainments (<s>ārūpyasamāpatti</s>).

body.text: nanvayaṃ vikalpanimittānāṃ parivarjanāddharmadhātoḥ samyaṅmanasikāro na punaḥ prajñāpāramiteti codyam / parihāramāha sarvadharmanirvedhata ityādi /
body.translated_text: Now, the objection is: this is merely right attention (<s>samyaṅmanasikāra</s>) to the <s>dharmadhātu</s> through the abandonment of conceptual signs (<s>vikalpanimitta</s>), not <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. To address this, he states "from the penetration of all <s>dharmas</s>" and so forth.

body.text: nirvedhaśabdenātra prativedha uktaḥ / sarvadharmāṇāṃ pariniṣpannena rūpeṇa prativedho jñānasākṣātkriyā sa teṣāṃ nirvedhaḥ / tata iti tena lakṣaṇena prajñāpāramitā ityarthaḥ / pūrvatra hetau tṛtīyā / tadantāttam / tathā hi tasyaiva samyaṅmanasikārasya śrutacintābhāvanānvayādanābhogato 'nabhisaṃskārataḥ sarvadharmatathatāyā niṣprapañcajñānamutpadyate / sa tasyāḥ prativedhaḥ / atha ko 'rthaḥ prajñāpāramitā(ta)yā śuddhiḥ? naitadyuktam / tathā hi / kastayā śuddhyati? nātmā tasyāniṣṭeḥ, na cittaṃ pratikṣaṇabhedāt / atha cittasantānaḥ / sopyaśuddhaḥ śuddho vā prakṛtyā bhavet / pūrvasmin pakṣe na tasya śuddhiraṅgārasyeva ghṛṣyamāna(ṇa)sya / dvitīyapakṣe vaiyarthyam / atha cittadharmatā tayā śuddhyati / tadapyayuktaṃ nirvikāratvāttasyā iti codyam / parihāramāha / sarvadharmaprakṛtipariśuddhita ityādi / sarvadharmāṇāṃ prakṛtistasyāḥ pariśuddhistatastena prayojanena prajñāpāramitānugantavyā / anuṣṭhātavyetyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: By the word <s>nirvedha</s>, <s>prativedha</s> (penetration) is meant here. The penetration of all <s>dharmas</s> in their perfected form (<s>pariniṣpanna</s>), the direct realization (<s>sākṣātkriyā</s>) through knowledge — that is their <s>nirvedha</s>. "From that" means: by that characteristic, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> — this is the meaning. In the preceding [compounds], the instrumental case is used in a causal sense. That ends with that. For indeed, from that very right attention (<s>samyaṅmanasikāra</s>), through the sequence of hearing, reflection, and meditation (<s>śrutacintābhāvanā</s>), spontaneously (<s>anābhogataḥ</s>) and without fabrication (<s>anabhisaṃskārataḥ</s>), there arises non-conceptual knowledge (<s>niṣprapañcajñāna</s>) of the <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) of all <s>dharmas</s>. That is its penetration. Now, what is the purpose? Purification (<s>śuddhi</s>) through <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>? This is not correct. For who is purified by it? Not the self (<s>ātman</s>), since that is not accepted. Not the mind (<s>citta</s>), because it perishes at every moment. Then perhaps the mental continuum (<s>cittasantāna</s>)? That too would be either impure or pure by nature. In the first case, there would be no purification of it, just as a burning coal cannot be [whitened] by rubbing. In the second case, there would be no purpose. Perhaps the nature of mind (<s>cittadharmatā</s>) is purified by it? That too is not correct, because it is immutable — this is the objection. To address this, he states "from the inherent purity of all <s>dharmas</s>" and so forth. The nature (<s>prakṛti</s>) of all <s>dharmas</s>, its purity (<s>pariśuddhi</s>) — from that, for that purpose, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is to be pursued. The meaning is: it is to be practiced.

body.text: nanūktaṃ tadapyayuktaṃ nirvikāratvāttasyā iti / uktametatkintu na yuktam / hetoranaikāntikatvāt / sā hi prakṛtyaiva pariśuddhā atanmayatvāt, āgantukenāvaraṇamalairmalinīkriyate nabha ivātra tamastuhinādibhiḥ / paścātprajñāpāramitayaiva teṣāṃ nirāsāddhiśuddhayati pavanādibhirabhrādimocanādiva nabhaḥ /
body.translated_text: Now, it was said "that too is not correct, because it is immutable." This has been stated, but it is not correct, because the reason is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>). For it [the nature of mind] is inherently pure, because it is not of the nature [of defilements]; it is made impure by adventitious (<s>āgantuka</s>) obscuring defilements — just as the sky [is obscured] by darkness, frost, and the like. Afterwards, through <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> itself, by the removal of those [defilements], it becomes pure — just as the sky [becomes clear] through wind and the like removing clouds and so forth.

body.text: nanu prajñāpāramitāpi bhagavataiva deśitā / deśanā ca sanimittameva jñānamutpādayati / tataḥ prajñāpāramitāpi nirmimittā na yukteti codyam / parihāramāha / sarvadharmāvacanata ityādinā / sarvadharmāṇāmavacanāt / vācāsvarūpamaprakāśya kevalaṃ sūcanāt / paramārthadarśanāya prajñāpāramitānugantavyā /
body.translated_text: Now, the objection is: <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> too was taught by the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) himself. And teaching produces only knowledge that has signs (<s>sanimitta</s>). Therefore, it is not correct that <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is signless (<s>nirmimitta</s>). To address this, he states "from the non-verbal nature of all <s>dharmas</s>" and so forth. Because all <s>dharmas</s> are without verbal expression — [teaching] merely indicates (<s>sūcanā</s>) without revealing the essential nature through speech. For the sake of seeing the ultimate reality (<s>paramārthadarśana</s>), <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is to be pursued.

body.text: nanu keyaṃ viśuddhiḥ? klaiśapakṣa (kṣaya) iti cet / punarbhavaḥ syādeva / atha hetukṣayājjanmāpi kṣīyate tadā pariśiṣṭā saṃskārā yāvadāyuravasthāya svayameva nirudhyante / iti śrāvakabodhireva syānnānuttarā samyaksambodhiḥ / satyāṃ vā viśeṣo vaktavya iti codyam / parihāramāha tribhirvākyaiḥ / sarvadharmāṇāmanirodhata iti / anāśravāṇāṃ dharmāṇāmakṣayāt prajñāpāramitānugantavyā / kathamanirodhaḥ? prahāṇasamatayā / nirdeśatvena prahāṇādaviśeṣāt / sarvadharmāṇāmiti sāṃkleśikānāṃ sarvadharmāṇāṃ nirvāṇaprāptitaḥ prajñāpāramitānugantavyā / yathā teṣāṃ tathatā tathaiva ta iti jñānaṃ tathatāsamatā / tayā kathaṃ tathatāsamatetyāha / sarvadharmā ityādi / nāgacchantyanāgatādadhvanaḥ, na gacchantyatītamadhvānaṃ, yata āgantavyaṃ yatra ca gantavyaṃ tayorasattvāt / yataśca ajānānāḥ svasaṃvinmātre 'dhvanāmajñānāt / jñānapūrvakatvācca gatyāgamanayoḥ / tasmāt ajātā atyantājātita iti //
body.translated_text: Now, what is this purification? If it is the destruction of the affliction-side (<s>kleśapakṣa</s>), then there would still be rebirth. If, due to the destruction of causes, birth too is destroyed, then the remaining <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) would naturally cease upon lasting until the end of life. Thus it would only be the awakening of the <s>Śrāvaka</s> (hearer), not the unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). Or, if it [the unsurpassed awakening] does exist, the distinction should be stated — this is the objection. He addresses this with three statements. "From the non-cessation of all <s>dharmas</s>": because the undefiled (<s>anāśrava</s>) <s>dharmas</s> do not decay, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is to be pursued. How is there non-cessation? Through the equality of abandonment (<s>prahāṇasamatā</s>). Because abandonment is by way of pointing out, there is no distinction. "Of all <s>dharmas</s>" means: from the attainment of <s>nirvāṇa</s> of all defiled <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is to be pursued. Just as their <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) is, so is the knowledge that they are thus — that is equality with <s>tathatā</s> (<s>tathatāsamatā</s>). How is there equality with <s>tathatā</s>? He states "all <s>dharmas</s>" and so forth. They do not come from the future time-period, nor do they go to the past time-period, because both — that from which one should come and that to which one should go — are non-existent. And because, not knowing, in mere self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvid</s>), there is no cognition of time-periods. And because coming and going are preceded by knowledge. Therefore, they are unborn, utterly unborn.

body.text: iyatā bodhisattvānāṃ svārthasampat prasādhitā / astu nāmaiṣāṃ svārthasampatsvārthasya loke prakṛtyaiva priyatvāttadartha duṣkarasyāpi vyavasāyāt /
body.translated_text: By this much, the accomplishment of self-benefit (<s>svārthasampat</s>) of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> has been established. Let this self-benefit be [granted], since one's own benefit is naturally dear in the world, and one makes efforts even in difficult tasks for its sake.

body.text: parārthastu duṣkaratvānāmānantyāt paratvādvipratipattiḥ bahulatvāditi codyam / parihāramāha ātmetyādinā / ātmā para iti yo ca bheda [:] tasyādarśanātsarvasattvānāmātmasamatādarśanādityarthaḥ / tathā coktamāryavimalakīrtinirdeśe "sumerusamāṃ satkāyadṛṣṭimutpādya bodhicittamutpādyate / tataḥ sarvadharmā virohanti" iti /
body.translated_text: But regarding the benefit of others (<s>parārtha</s>), there is disagreement because of the infinity of difficulties, the otherness [of those to be helped], and the prevalence [of obstacles] — this is the objection. To address this, he states "self" and so forth. The distinction between self and other — from not seeing that [distinction], from seeing the equality of self with all sentient beings — this is the meaning. And thus it is stated in the <s>Āryavimalakīrtinirdeśa</s>: "Having generated the view of the self-existence-body (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) as great as <s>Sumeru</s>, one generates <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening). From that, all <s>dharmas</s> spring forth."

body.text: ita ūrdhvaṃ duṣkarasaṃjñāpratipakṣeṇa yathā yathā pravekṣaṇīyaṃ tadāha samudraśabdādarvāk / tatrādau sattvānāmarhattvadiṣu duṣkara saṃjñānirāsārthamāha / sarvadharmāḥ sattvavyahāraviṣayāḥ / āryārhantaḥ yataḥ prakṛtipariśuddha / dharmatāmātratvāt / bhārānāropaṇatayeti niḥsvabhāvatvāt bhāvasya / sattvavinayāya daśadigbuddhakṣetragamanena duṣkarasaṃjñānirāsāyāha / sarvadharmāṇāṃ adeśāpradeśata iti / adeśatvācca prakṛtisvabhāvata iti / rūpādīnāṃ pratistasyāḥ svabhāvataḥ / na hi tasyādeśo 'patanadharmatvāt / nāpi pradeśo niraṃśatvādākāśavat / saṃsārasukhe dustyajasaṃjñānirāsāyāha / sarvadharmāṇāṃ sāṃsārikāṇāṃ nirodhe prahalādanatvaṃ sukhasaṃjñotpādanatvaṃ tataḥ prajñāpāramitānugantavyā /
body.translated_text: From here onward, he states how one should progressively enter by means of the antidote to the perception of difficulty (<s>duṣkarasaṃjñā</s>), up to the word "ocean" (<s>samudra</s>). First, in order to remove the perception of difficulty regarding the <s>Arhatship</s> and other [attainments] of sentient beings, he states: all <s>dharmas</s> are the domain of the conventional dealings of sentient beings. Noble <s>Arhats</s> are inherently pure, because [things] are mere <s>dharmatā</s> (nature of reality). "By way of placing a burden" means: because entities lack intrinsic nature (<s>niḥsvabhāva</s>). In order to remove the perception of difficulty through going to the <s>Buddha</s>-fields in the ten directions for the discipline of sentient beings, he states: "from the non-locality and non-partiality of all <s>dharmas</s>." Because they have no location, and because of their natural essential nature (<s>prakṛtisvabhāva</s>). [That nature] of <s>rūpa</s> and the rest, from its very essence — it has no fixed location, because it is subject to decay; nor does it have parts, because it is partless, like space (<s>ākāśa</s>). In order to remove the perception of difficulty in abandoning the pleasures of <s>saṃsāra</s>, he states: from the delight in the cessation (<s>nirodha</s>) of all <s>saṃsāric</s> <s>dharmas</s>, from generating the perception of happiness — from that, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is to be pursued.

children.translated_text: "Impermanent indeed are <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations), having the nature of arising and passing away;

children.text: utpadya hi nirudhyante teṣāṃ vyupaśamaḥ sukhamiti //"
children.translated_text: Having arisen, they cease — their pacification is happiness."

body.text: itiśabdaḥ śrāvakavinayanasamāptyarthaḥ / bodhisattvavinayanamadhikṛtyāha / aratyaviratita iti / ratiratyantamutkaṇṭhā nirvāṇe / tadabhāvo bodhisattvānāṃ aratiḥ / viratiratyantamudvegaḥ saṃsāre / tadabhāvo bodhisattvānāmarati / tābhyāṃ prajñāpāramitā / iti saṃsāranirvāṇāpratiṣṭhānāya pratyavekṣā / araktāviraktatayetyādinā vairāgyāya pratyavekṣā / sarvadharmā aśa(sa)ktā ityanabhiniviṣṭāḥ / saṅgāsaṅgā saṅgatatpratipakṣau / tadvigatāstayoranupalambhāditi vikalpaprahāṇāya pratyavekṣā / sarvadharmāḥ sarvamārgāḥ saptābhisamayāḥ / ta eva bodhiḥ / bodhiprāpakatvāt / ata evāha / bodhiḥ / buddhajñānāvabodhanatayeti / avabodhana prāpaṇa iti bodhiḥ / sulabhāvabodhanāya pratyavekṣā / sarvadharmāsvalakṣaṇadhāraṇāt / te śūnyānimittāpraṇihitā vijñānamātratvenārthavirahāt sarvanimittāstamayāt / bhrāntiśarīre traidhātukapraṇidhānābhāvācca yathākramam / iti mārgasaṃkṣepaḥ /
body.translated_text: The word "thus" (<s>iti</s>) indicates the completion of the disciplining of <s>Śrāvakas</s>. With reference to the disciplining of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, he states: "from non-delight and non-aversion." Delight (<s>rati</s>) is extreme longing for <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Its absence in <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is non-delight (<s>arati</s>). Aversion (<s>virati</s>) is extreme revulsion toward <s>saṃsāra</s>. Its absence in <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is non-aversion (<s>avirati</s>). Through these two, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> [is characterized]. Thus, this is the examination for non-abiding in either <s>saṃsāra</s> or <s>nirvāṇa</s>. "From being neither attached nor detached" and so forth is the examination for dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>). All <s>dharmas</s> are "unattached" (<s>asakta</s>), meaning without clinging (<s>anabhiniviṣṭa</s>). Attachment and non-attachment (<s>saṅgāsaṅga</s>) are attachment and its antidote. Being free from both of those, from the non-apprehension of either — this is the examination for the abandonment of conceptual proliferation (<s>vikalpa</s>). All <s>dharmas</s> are all the paths, the seven <s>abhisamayas</s> (clear realizations). They themselves are <s>bodhi</s> (awakening), because they lead to awakening. Therefore he says: "<s>bodhi</s>." This is the examination for awakening to <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge. [And] the examination for awakening that is easily attainable. From the bearing of the own-characteristics of all <s>dharmas</s>: they are empty (<s>śūnya</s>), signless (<s>ānimitta</s>), and wishless (<s>apraṇihita</s>) — empty because they are devoid of objects as mere representation (<s>vijñānamātra</s>); signless because all signs have set; and wishless because there is no aspiration for the three realms in the body of delusion — respectively. Thus, this is the summary of the path.

body.text: yadi vimokṣamukhānyapi teṣāṃ mārgastadā tāni bhāvayanto hīnabodhau pateyuḥ / ityata āha / sarvatyādi / sarvadharmāḥ sarvabodhisattvamārgāḥ / bhaiṣajyamiti hīnayānaspṛhāmahāvyādhiharāḥ / kuta ityāha / maitrīpūrvaṅgamatayeti / yato maitrī teṣāṃ puraḥsarī / api ca / sarvacaturbhirapramāṇaiḥ saha viharaṇāt matrīvihāriṇaḥ / brahmabhūtā iti brahmaṇā tulyāḥ / tadvadeva doṣānutpādanādityuddeśaḥ / sarvadoṣānutpādanata iti nirdeśaḥ / sarvadoṣā maitryādīnāṃ vipakṣo yathākramaṃ vyāpādo vihiṃsā aratiḥ pratighānunayau ca / apraṇihitata iti nirvānotkaṇṭhāvirahāt / apratihatita iti saṃsāre atyantānudvegāt / iti trayodaśavidho 'pūrvābhisamayaḥ sānuṣaṅgaḥ //
body.translated_text: If the doors of liberation (<s>vimokṣamukha</s>) are also their path, then those cultivating them would fall into the inferior awakening. Therefore he states: "all" and so forth. All <s>dharmas</s> are all the <s>Bodhisattva</s> paths. They are "medicine" (<s>bhaiṣajya</s>), meaning they cure the great disease of craving for the lesser vehicle (<s>hīnayāna</s>). How? He states: "because <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) is their forerunner." Since <s>maitrī</s> is their precursor. Moreover, through dwelling together with all four immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>), they are dwellers in <s>maitrī</s>. "Having become <s>Brahma</s>" means equal to <s>Brahmā</s>. Just as he [<s>Brahmā</s>] does not produce faults — this is the indication. "From the non-production of all faults" is the detailed exposition. All faults are the adversaries of <s>maitrī</s> and the rest, respectively: malice (<s>vyāpāda</s>), harmfulness (<s>vihiṃsā</s>), discontent (<s>arati</s>), and aversion and attachment (<s>pratigha</s> and <s>anunaya</s>). "From wishlessness" (<s>apraṇihita</s>): because of the absence of longing for <s>nirvāṇa</s>. "From unobstructedness" (<s>apratihata</s>): because of utter freedom from revulsion toward <s>saṃsāra</s>. Thus, this is the thirteen-fold unprecedented clear realization (<s>apūrvābhisamaya</s>) together with its auxiliaries.

body.text: ekakṣaṇābhisamayo vaktavyāḥ /
body.translated_text: The single-moment clear realization (<s>ekakṣaṇābhisamaya</s>) is to be stated.

body.text: ekakṣaṇābhisambodho lakṣaṇena caturvidhaḥ // 1-16 //
body.translated_text: The single-moment clear awakening (<s>ekakṣaṇābhisambodha</s>) is fourfold by its characteristics. [Verse 1-16]

body.text: iti yaḥ pūrvamuddiṣṭaḥ sa kathaṃ caturvidhaḥ? sarvānāśravadharmaikacittakṣaṇābhisamayaḥ / vipākajasarvasāśravānāśravadharmaikacittakṣaṇābhisamayaḥ / alakṣaṇasarvadharmaikacittakṣaṇābhisamayaḥ / advayasarvadharmaikacittakṣaṇābhisamayaśceti //
body.translated_text: Thus, that which was previously indicated — how is it fourfold? [It is:] (1) the single-moment realization of all undefiled <s>dharmas</s> (<s>sarvānāśravadharmaikacittakṣaṇābhisamaya</s>); (2) the single-moment realization of all defiled and undefiled <s>dharmas</s> born of ripening (<s>vipākajasarvasāśravānāśravadharmaikacittakṣaṇābhisamaya</s>); (3) the single-moment realization of all <s>dharmas</s> as without characteristics (<s>alakṣaṇasarvadharmaikacittakṣaṇābhisamaya</s>); and (4) the single-moment realization of all <s>dharmas</s> as non-dual (<s>advayasarvadharmaikacittakṣaṇābhisamaya</s>).

body.text: tatra prathamamadhikṛtya śāstram-
body.translated_text: With regard to the first, the treatise [states]:

children.translated_text: "Because even by a single [moment] of giving and the like, the sage comprehends all undefiled [<s>dharmas</s>],
this should be known as the single-moment realization." // 7-1 //
"Just as even a single bucket-chain link, set in motion by a person,
moves the entire [chain] at once, so too does knowledge in a single moment." // 7-2 //

body.text: prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carato bodhisattvasya 'ekaikenāpi dānādinā' cittakṣaṇena pravṛttena 'sarveṣāṃ' anāśravāṇāṃ dharmāṇāṃ 'saṅgrahāt' ākṣepāt 'ekṣaṇāvabodhaḥ' ekacittakṣaṇābhisamayaḥ / 'ayaṃ' iti prathamaḥ / tathā hi 'yathaikāpi pari(da)kā' 'puruṣapreritā sarvamaraghaṭaṃ(ṭṭaṃ) sakṛccalayati' tathaikapadamapi dānādicittaṃ prayuktaṃ sarvamanāśravadharmasandohaṃ sakṛdevākarṣayatītyarthaḥ / ataḥ sūtraṃ samudrāparyantatayā prajñāpāramitāparyantatānugantavyeti / atra prajñāpāramitā parigṛhītatvāt, sarvākārajñatā manasikārāvirahitatvācca / gambhīrodāra ekaiko dānādicittakṣaṇaḥ
body.translated_text: For the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who practices in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, "because of the comprehension" (<s>saṅgraha</s>), the drawing in (<s>ākṣepa</s>), "of all" undefiled <s>dharmas</s>, "by even a single" mind-moment engaged in giving and the like, [there is] "single-moment realization" — the single-mind-moment realization (<s>ekacittakṣaṇābhisamaya</s>). "This" refers to the first. For thus: "just as even a single bucket-chain link" (<s>parikā/padikā</s>), "set in motion by a person, moves the entire bucket-chain at once" — so too even a single step of mind engaged in giving and the like, when applied, draws in the entire collection of undefiled <s>dharmas</s> at once — this is the meaning. Therefore the <s>sūtra</s> [says]: "By the boundlessness of the ocean, the boundlessness of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be understood." Here, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is so because of being embraced [by wisdom], and <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience in all aspects) because of not being separated from mental attention. Each profound and noble mind-moment of giving and the like

body.text: prajñāpāramitetyucyate / tasyāparyantatā anāśravadharmākarṣakatvam / teṣāmanyonyasambandhasya cirapariśīlitatvāt sānugantavyā veditavyā / kathamityāha / samudrāparyantatayeti / gambhīrodārasya samudrasyāparyantatā sakṛdaparyantanimnagājalākarṣakatvam / tāsāṃ parasparasaṃsargāt / tayā samudrāparyantatayā upamayā / tadvadityarthaḥ / iti sarvānāśravadharmaikacittakṣaṇābhisamayaḥ //
body.translated_text: is called "<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>." Its boundlessness is its capacity to draw in undefiled <s>dharmas</s>. Because the mutual connection of those [<s>dharmas</s>] has been long cultivated, that [boundlessness] "should be understood." How? He says: "By the boundlessness of the ocean" — the boundlessness of the profound and noble ocean is its capacity to draw in at once the waters of boundless rivers. Because of their mutual intermingling. By that analogy of the ocean's boundlessness — "likewise" is the meaning. Thus, the single-moment realization of all undefiled <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: dvitīyamadhikṛtya śāstram-
body.translated_text: With regard to the second, the treatise [states]:

children.translated_text: "When the state of the nature of ripening-born [<s>dharmas</s>], consisting entirely of the wholesome,
has become <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, then knowledge [arises] in a single moment." // 7-3 //

body.text: vipākajo dharmo vipākadharmastabhdāvastattāsāṃ 'avasthā' asyā iti yathoktā prajñāpāramitā / 'sarvaśuklamayī' iti sarve kuśalā dharmāḥ sāśravā anāśravāḥ / ye purvamanena niḥsvabhāvatayā bhāvitāste paścādvipākajāḥ / ataḥ prakṛtyaiva teṣāṃ naiḥsvābhāvyasaṃvedinī / tasmātsarvaśuklamayī / īdṛśī sā yadā 'jātā' sampannā 'tadā' 'jñānaṃ' cittaṃ 'ekakṣaṇe ' teṣu sarveṣvanābhogena / anāśraveṣu sarveṣu sābhogaḥ prathamaḥ / ayaṃ tu dvitīyaḥ sāśravānāśravanirābhogaśca / ataḥ sūtram / gaganāparyantatayā prajñāpāramitāparyantatānugantavyeti / prajñāpāramitāyāḥ vipākadharmatāvasthā sarvaśuklamayī ca / ata evāparyantatā / teṣu sarveṣu bhāvābhāvaikarasā / nirābhogaśca vipākajatvāt / tasyā aparyantatā veditavyā / kathamityāha / gaganāparyantatayā dṛṣṭānteneti / gaganamākāśam / tacca rūpidravyābhāvaikarasamaparyantaṃ nirābhogaṃ ca parispandābhāvāt / ata ubhayorapi aparyantatā sadṛśīti vipākajasarvaśukladharmaikacittakṣaṇābhisamayo dvitīyaḥ //
body.translated_text: A <s>dharma</s> born of ripening (<s>vipāka</s>) is a "ripening-<s>dharma</s>" (<s>vipākadharma</s>); the "state" (<s>avasthā</s>) of those [constituting] its condition — that is the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> as described. "Consisting entirely of the wholesome" — all wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, both defiled (<s>sāśrava</s>) and undefiled (<s>anāśrava</s>). Those that were previously cultivated by him through [the understanding of their] essencelessness become ripening-born afterward. Therefore, she is by nature the awareness of the essencelessness of those [<s>dharmas</s>]. Hence, "consisting entirely of the wholesome." When such a [<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>] has "arisen" — been accomplished — "then" "knowledge" — the mind — "in a single moment" [comprehends] all those [<s>dharmas</s>] without deliberate effort. In the first [realization], the [comprehension of] all undefiled [<s>dharmas</s>] was with deliberate effort. But this second [realization comprehends both] defiled and undefiled without deliberate effort. Therefore the <s>sūtra</s> [says]: "By the boundlessness of space, the boundlessness of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be understood." <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is in the state of the nature of ripening-<s>dharmas</s> and consists entirely of the wholesome. Hence her boundlessness — she is of one flavor in all of them, in [both] existence and non-existence. And she is without deliberate effort, because of being born of ripening. Her boundlessness should be understood. How? He says: "By the boundlessness of space" — as an analogy. Space (<s>gagana</s>) is the sky (<s>ākāśa</s>). And that is of one flavor with the absence of material substance, boundless, and without deliberate effort because of the absence of movement. Therefore, the boundlessness of both is alike — thus, the single-moment realization of all wholesome <s>dharmas</s> born of ripening is the second.

body.text: tṛtīyamadhikṛtya śāstram-
body.translated_text: With regard to the third, the treatise [states]:

children.translated_text: "Having abided in <s>dharmas</s> that are like dreams, [and] being foremost in giving and the like,
one realizes the characteristiclessness of <s>dharmas</s> in a single moment." // 7-4 //

body.text: 'svapnopameṣu dhāvadgandharvanagaropameṣu" iti mahatyorbhagavatyoḥ paṭhyate / śāstre tvekameva padaṃ sarveṣāmekārthatvāt / sa punarartho vicitrairapi lakṣaṇaiḥ pratibhāsamānānāmeṣāṃ yathālakṣaṇamasattvādalakṣaṇatā / tato māyopamatvādalakṣaṇeṣu sarvadharmeṣu 'sthitvā' ṣaṭpāramitāḥ paripūrayan 'sarvadharmāṇāmalakṣaṇatvamekakakṣaṇenaiva 'vindati' jānāti / dhātūnāmekārthatvena vindaterjñānavṛtteḥ / etadāha / meruvicitrayā prajñāpāramitāvicitratānugantavyeti / māyopameṣu
body.translated_text: "In <s>dharmas</s> that are like dreams, like a running <s>Gandharva</s> city" — thus it is read in the two great <s>Bhagavatīs</s>. But in the treatise, only one term [is used], because all have the same meaning. And that meaning is: although they appear with diverse characteristics, because they do not exist according to their [imagined] characteristics, they are without characteristics (<s>alakṣaṇatā</s>). Therefore, "having abided" in all <s>dharmas</s> that are without characteristics because of being like illusions, fulfilling the six <s>pāramitās</s>, "one realizes" — knows — "the characteristiclessness of all <s>dharmas</s> in a single moment." Because of the single meaning of the <s>dhātus</s> (elements), "realizes" (<s>vindati</s>) is used in the sense of knowledge. This he states: "By the variegatedness of <s>Meru</s>, the variegatedness of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be understood." In <s>dharmas</s> that are like illusions

body.text: sarvadharmeṣvalakṣaṇatvena yadekarasaṃ jñānaṃ seha prajñāpāramitā / atastasyā ekarasatvepi māyopamaiḥ sarvadharmapratibhāsairyā vicitratā sā meruvicitratayā dṛṣṭāntena veditavyā / yathā hyākāśasya nīrūpatvādasatī meruṇā vicitratāvabhāti / merupārśvānāṃ caturvarṇānāṃ dikṣu tatsarvavarṇatayā prakhyānāt / tathā tasyā ityalakṣaṇasarvadharmaikacittakṣaṇābhisamayastṛtīyaḥ //
body.translated_text: , the knowledge that is of one flavor through the characteristiclessness of all <s>dharmas</s> — that is here <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Therefore, even though she is of one flavor, the variegatedness [that arises] through the appearances of all <s>dharmas</s> that are like illusions — that should be understood by the analogy of the variegatedness of <s>Meru</s>. For just as space, being formless, nevertheless appears variegated through <s>Meru</s> — because the four colors of the sides of <s>Meru</s> are reflected in the [corresponding] directions as having all those colors — so too of her [<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>]. Thus, the single-moment realization of all <s>dharmas</s> as without characteristics is the third.

body.text: caturthamadhikṛtya śāstram-
body.translated_text: With regard to the fourth, the treatise [states]:

children.translated_text: "The dream and its perceiver — because of the application of duality, [there is] the non-seer;
one sees the non-dual reality of <s>dharmas</s> in a single moment." // 7-5 //

body.text: 'snanaṃ taddarśinaṃ caiva' iti kudyoge kathaṃ dvitīyā? kartavyo 'tra yatnaḥ / athavā / anīkṣiteti tṛn paṭhitavyaḥ / tṛtīye sarvadharmāṇāṃ svapnamāyopamairākārairvicitraḥ pratibhāsaḥ / caturthe tu teṣāmastamayāccharanmadhyānhagaganasamo vigatasamastaviplavaḥ / tatra svapnadṛśyaṃ narakacittaraṅgādisvapnaḥ / taddarśī ātmaiva tayorastamayāt / yastau vikṛte(tau) 'yogena' [a]bhedena so 'dvayaṃ' grāhyagrāhakaśūnyaṃ 'dharmāṇāṃ tattva' paramārthaṃ 'ekakṣaṇenaiva paśyati' / enamāha / rūpāparyantatayetyādinā / iha caturtha ekakṣaṇābhisamayaḥ / prajñāpāramitā tasyā aparyantatā / sarvadharmaparamārthasya kevalasya kevalavimalanabhonibhasya tena saṃvedanāt / sā veditavyā / kathamityāha / rūpādīnāmaparyantayeti / kathaṃ teṣāmaparyantatā? dvayapratibhāsāstamayāt / yāvatkhalu dvayaṃ tāvatparyantaḥ parimitatvāt /
body.translated_text: "The dream and its perceiver" — in an incorrect reading, how is there a second? Effort must be made here. Or alternatively, "<s>anīkṣita</s>" should be read with the <s>tṛn</s> [suffix]. In the third [realization], there is a variegated appearance of all <s>dharmas</s> through forms like dreams and illusions. But in the fourth, through their cessation, [the mind is] like an autumn midday sky, free from all disturbance. There, the dream-seen — the waves of hell-mind and so on — is the dream. Its seer is the self itself. Through the cessation of both, whoever [perceives] those two by their "application" — [that is,] non-duality — that "non-dual" [reality], empty of grasped and grasper, the "reality" (<s>tattva</s>), the ultimate (<s>paramārtha</s>) of <s>dharmas</s>, "one sees in a single moment." This he states: "By the boundlessness of form" and so on. Here, the fourth single-moment realization. <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>; her boundlessness — because of the awareness of the ultimate of all <s>dharmas</s> alone, which is purely immaculate, resembling the sky — that should be understood. How? He says: "By the boundlessness of form and the rest." How is there boundlessness of those? Because of the cessation of the appearance of duality. For as long as there is duality, there is limitation, because of being bounded.

body.text: nanu rūpatadgrāhakayorastamayenāpi paryantatā? ka āha rūpasyaiveti? kintarhi? rūpasya yāvadvijñānasya / nanu tathāpi grāhakasyāstamayo nokta iti cet / na tasyāpi skandhaireva saṃgrahāt / aprakāśātmano grāhakatvāyogāditi sarvadharmādvayatattvaikacittakṣaṇābhisamayaścaturthaḥ //
body.translated_text: "But surely, even by the cessation of form and its grasper, there would be limitation?" Who says [it is] only of form? What then? Of form up to consciousness. "But even so, the cessation of the grasper has not been stated" — if so, no, because it too is included in the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates). Because what is non-luminous by nature is not fit to be a grasper. Thus, the single-moment realization of the non-dual reality of all <s>dharmas</s> is the fourth.

body.text: ekakṣaṇābhisamayaḥ saptamo 'bhisamayaḥ //
body.translated_text: The single-moment realization (<s>ekakṣaṇābhisamaya</s>) is the seventh <s>abhisamaya</s> (realization).

body.text: aṣṭamo 'bhisamayo dharmakāyaḥ / tasya catvāri vastūni / trayaḥ kāyāḥ kāritraṃ ca / tathāhi pūrvamuddeśaḥ kṛtaḥ-
body.translated_text: The eighth <s>abhisamaya</s> is the <s>Dharmakāya</s> (truth-body). Its four constituents are: the three bodies (<s>kāyas</s>) and [their] activity (<s>kāritra</s>). For previously the summary was stated:

children.translated_text: "The <s>Svābhāvika</s> (essential), the <s>Sāṃbhogika</s> (enjoyment), and the <s>Nairmāṇika</s> (emanation) — thus threefold,
the <s>Dharmakāya</s> together with its activity is declared to be fourfold." // 1-17 //

body.text: iti // dharmo mārgaḥ / sa ceha prakarṣagateḥ prakaraṇācca saptābhisamayalakṣaṇo gṛhyate / dharmalabhyaḥ kāyo 'dharmakāyaḥ' / kāyaḥ śarīram / trīṇi śarīrāṇi buddhānāṃ trayaḥ kāyāḥ / uktaṃ hi mahatyorbhagavatyoḥ- "sarvākārapariśuddhānāmanāśravāṇāṃ sarvadharmāṇāṃ yā prakṛtiḥ sa tathāgato 'rhansamyaksambuddho veditavyaḥ // punaraparaṃ teṣāmeva dharmāṇāmadhigamādanuttarāṃ samyaksambodhimabhisambudhya dvātriṃśatā lakṣaṇairaśītyānuvyañjanairalaṅkṛtakāyastathāgato 'rhansamyaksambuddho bodhisattvānāṃ paramaṃ mahāyānadharmamanuttararatiprītiprāmodyasukhopabhogāya deśayati // punaraparaṃ teṣāmeva sarvadharmāṇāmadhigamādanuttarāṃ samyaksambodhimabhisambudhya tathāgato 'rhansamyaksambuddho daśasu dikṣvanantāparyanteṣu lokadhātuṣu sarvakālaṃ nānānirmāṇameghena sarvasattvānāmarthaṃ karoti" iti // uktaṃ ca sūtrālaṃkāre-
body.translated_text: "<s>Dharma</s>" is the path. And that here, because of [its] going to the highest degree and because of the subject-matter, is taken as characterized by the seven <s>abhisamayas</s> (realizations). The body (<s>kāya</s>) obtained through <s>dharma</s> is the "<s>Dharmakāya</s>." "Body" (<s>kāya</s>) means form (<s>śarīra</s>). The three forms of the <s>Buddhas</s> are the three bodies. For it is said in the two great <s>Bhagavatīs</s>: "The nature of all those undefiled <s>dharmas</s> that are purified in all aspects — that is to be known as the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One. Furthermore, having realized unsurpassed perfect awakening through the attainment of those very <s>dharmas</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, with a body adorned by the thirty-two marks and eighty minor signs, teaches the supreme <s>Mahāyāna dharma</s> to the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> for the enjoyment of unsurpassed delight, joy, gladness, and happiness. Furthermore, having realized unsurpassed perfect awakening through the attainment of all those very <s>dharmas</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, accomplishes the benefit of all beings at all times in the boundless and limitless world-realms in the ten directions through clouds of diverse emanations." And it is said in the <s>Sūtrālaṅkāra</s>:

children.translated_text: "The collection of the bodies of the <s>Buddhas</s> should be known through three bodies;
this, together with its support, [serving] one's own and others' benefit, is shown through three bodies."

body.text: iti /
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: tasmāt tribhireva kāyaiḥ kāritreṇa ca paricchedena caturdhā dharmakāya uktaḥ /
body.translated_text: Therefore, by the three bodies alone and by [their] activity, the <s>Dharmakāya</s> is said to be fourfold, through [this] division.

body.text: tatra svabhāvaḥ prakṛtiḥ / svabhāva eva 'svābhāvikaḥ' / vinayādibhyaṣṭhagiti svārthe ṭhak / athavā tasminneva svabhāve bhavo viśuddhaḥ paraḥ prakarṣaḥ svābhāvikaḥ kāyaḥ / sambhogāya prabhavatīti 'sāmbhogikaḥ' / nirmāṇa nirmitiḥ / tena nirvṛttaḥ kāyo 'nairmāṇikaḥ' /
body.translated_text: Among these, "nature" (<s>svabhāva</s>) is the essential nature (<s>prakṛti</s>). That which is the nature itself is the "<s>Svābhāvika</s>" (essential [body]). The <s>ṭhak</s> suffix is in the reflexive sense, from [the roots] <s>vinaya</s> and the like. Or alternatively, that which is born in that very nature, [and is] pure, supreme, most excellent — that is the <s>Svābhāvika</s> body. That which is efficacious for enjoyment (<s>sambhoga</s>) is the "<s>Sāṃbhogika</s>" (enjoyment [body]). "Emanation" (<s>nirmāṇa</s>) is creation (<s>nirmiti</s>). The body produced by that is the "<s>Nairmāṇika</s>" (emanation [body]).

body.text: tatra svābhāvikamadhikṛtya śāstram-
body.translated_text: With regard to the <s>Svābhāvika</s> (essential body), the treatise [states]:

children.text: sarvākārāṃ viśuddhiṃ ye prāptā dharmā nirāśravāḥ /
children.translated_text: "The undefiled <s>dharmas</s> that have attained purification in all aspects —
their essential-nature characteristic is considered the <s>Svābhāvika</s> body." // 8-1 //

body.text: teṣāṃ prakṛtidharmatā dharmadhātuḥ / nanu na dharmadhātustathāgato 'tiprasaṅgāt / kiṃ tarhi? dharmadhātuviśuddhiḥ / tathā coktamārya buddhabhūmisūtre- "pañcabhirākāraiḥ susamuditabuddhabhūmeḥ saṅgraho veditavyaḥ / katamaiḥ pañcabhiḥ? dharmadhātuviśuddhayā ādarśajñānena samatājñānena pratyavekṣaṇājñānena kṛtyānuṣṭhānajñānena ca" iti /
body.translated_text: Their essential <s>dharmatā</s> (nature of reality) is the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of phenomena). "But surely the <s>dharmadhātu</s> is not the <s>Tathāgata</s>, because of overextension." What then? The purification of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>. Thus it is said in the Noble <s>Buddhabhūmi Sūtra</s>: "The collection of the well-accomplished <s>Buddhabhūmi</s> (Buddha-stage) should be understood through five aspects. Which five? Through the purification of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, through mirror-like knowledge (<s>ādarśajñāna</s>), through the knowledge of equality (<s>samatājñāna</s>), through the knowledge of discrimination (<s>pratyavekṣaṇājñāna</s>), and through the knowledge of accomplishing activities (<s>kṛtyānuṣṭhānajñāna</s>)."

body.text: dharmadhātuviśuddhiḥ suviśuddho dharmadhātuḥ / suviśuddhānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ dharmateti nārthabhedaḥ kaścit / ataḥ sūtram / sūryaraśmimaṇḍalāparyantāvabhāsanatayā prajñāpāramitāparyantāvabhāsanatānugantavyeti / sarva eva trāsādidoṣarahitāḥ sphāṭikāḥ śuddhāḥ / tatra candrasūryābhyāmanye śrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ vimuktikāyasyopamāḥ / sūryācandramasāvapi śuddhasphāṭikau / tayoretadadhikaṃ yattau daśadigvyāpiraśmijālaṃ janayataḥ / tatastāvanantajñeyaviṣayamanantaṃ jñānamutpādayato buddhānāṃ vimuktikāyasyopamāne / ata evāsau dharmakāya ityabhidhīyate / anantadharmāśrayatvāt / tadiha dharmadhātuviśuddhijamanantaṃ jñānaṃ prajñāpāramitā / tasyā aparyantajñeyāvabhāsanatā veditavyā sūryaraśmimaṇḍalāparyantāvabhāsanatayā dṛṣṭāntena / tathā hi buddhadharmāṇāṃ suviśuddho dharmadhātuḥ sūryavat / tajjā prajñā prajñapāramitā sūryaraśmiṇḍalavat / tayā yadaparyantāvabhāsanaṃ tadraviraśmimaṇḍalenāparyantāvabhāsanavat / tadanena buddhānāṃ suviśuddho dharmadhātuḥ svābhāvikaḥ kāyastasya ca sarvatra jñeye jñānavaśitā darśitā /
body.translated_text: The "purification of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>" is the thoroughly purified <s>dharmadhātu</s>. "The <s>dharmatā</s> of thoroughly purified <s>dharmas</s>" — there is no difference in meaning whatsoever [between the two expressions]. Therefore the <s>sūtra</s> [says]: "By the boundlessness of the illumination of the disk of the sun's rays, the boundlessness of the illumination of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be understood." All [those <s>dharmas</s>] are crystal-pure, free from the faults of fear and the like. Among them, [those] other than the sun and moon are analogies for the liberation-body (<s>vimuktikāya</s>) of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. The sun and moon too are pure crystals. But they have this additional [quality]: that they produce a net of rays pervading the ten directions. Therefore they are the analogies for the liberation-body of the <s>Buddhas</s>, who produce boundless knowledge with a boundless field of knowables. Hence that is called the <s>Dharmakāya</s> — because of being the support of infinite <s>dharmas</s>. Here then, the infinite knowledge born from the purification of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Her boundless illumination of knowables should be understood by the analogy of the boundless illumination of the disk of the sun's rays. For thus: the thoroughly purified <s>dharmadhātu</s> of the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> is like the sun. The wisdom born from it — <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> — is like the disk of the sun's rays. Its boundless illumination is like the boundless illumination by the disk of the sun's rays. By this, the thoroughly purified <s>dharmadhātu</s> of the <s>Buddhas</s> — the <s>Svābhāvika</s> body — and its mastery of knowledge over all knowables have been shown.

body.text: tasyaiva sattvārthavaśitāṃ vyāpinityatvaṃ cādhikṛtya śāstram-
body.translated_text: With regard to its mastery over the benefit of beings — its pervasiveness and permanence — the treatise [states]:

children.text: paripākaṃ gate hetau yasya yasya yadā yadā /
children.translated_text: "Whenever and wherever the cause has reached maturation,

children.text: hitaṃ bhavati kartavyaṃ prathate tasya tasya saḥ // 8-9 //
children.translated_text: for that being and at that time, it manifests as the benefit that is to be accomplished." // 8-9 //
"For even though the rain-cloud pours down rain, the seedless does not sprout;
even upon the arising of <s>Buddhas</s>, the unfit one does not partake of good fortune." // 9-10 //
'Thus, because of the abundance of conduct, the <s>Buddha</s> is called all-pervading.
And because of the very inexhaustibility of that [conduct], he is also said to be eternal.' // 8-11 //

body.text: 'saḥ' iti svābhāvikaḥ kāyaḥ / 'prathate ' nirmāṇaprathanāt / tadā tadeti gamyate 'yadā yadā' iti vacanāt / tasya hitasya karaṇāyetyarthādgamyate / tasmāttadā tadaivetyata āha / 'varṣatyapi' ityādi / 'iti' ityādi / 'kāritravaipulyaṃ' sarvabhavyeṣu kāritram / tasyaiva' iti kāritrasya / iti svābhāvikaḥ kāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: '<s>Saḥ</s>' (he) refers to the <s>svābhāvika-kāya</s> (essential body). '<s>Prathate</s>' (extends) — because of the extension of emanations (<s>nirmāṇa</s>). 'Then that' is understood from the statement 'whenever.' 'For the sake of accomplishing benefit' — this is understood from the meaning. Therefore, 'then and there itself' — to this he says '<s>varṣati api</s>' (even rains) and so on. '<s>Iti</s>' and so on: '<s>kāritravaipulya</s>' (abundance of conduct) is conduct toward all trainable beings. '<s>Tasyaiva</s>' (of that very) refers to the conduct. Thus [this describes] the <s>svābhāvika-kāya</s> (essential body).

body.text: sāmbhogikasya kāyasya bahuvaktavyam / tatra sambhogamadhikṛtyāha / sarvaśabdāparyantatayā prajñāpāramitāpayantatānugantavyeti / śāsturdeśayataḥ śrṛṇvatāṃ ca bodhisattvānāṃ yaḥ paramamahāyānadharmasaṃbodhaḥ sā prajñāpāramitā / sa eva sambhogaḥ sambhogakāraṇatvāt / yaḥ punastajjānāṃ mṛdumadhyādhimātrasaumanasyalakṣaṇānāṃ ratiprītiprāmodyānāṃ sukhasya cānubhavaḥ sa mukhyaḥ sambhogaḥ / tasyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyā aparyantatā veditavyā / kathamityāha / sarvaśabdāpayantatayeti /
body.translated_text: Much is to be said about the <s>sāmbhogika-kāya</s> (enjoyment body). Therein, with reference to enjoyment (<s>sambhoga</s>), he says: 'By the boundlessness of all words, the boundlessness of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> should be understood.' The supreme awakening to the great <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>Dharma</s> that the Teacher teaches and that the <s>bodhisattvas</s> hear — that is <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>. That itself is the enjoyment, because it is the cause of enjoyment. The actual experience of happiness characterized by delight, joy, and gladness — of mild, moderate, and intense pleasant feeling — of those who are born from it: that is the primary enjoyment. The boundlessness of that <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> should be known. How? — he says: 'By the boundlessness of all words.'

body.text: hetau tṛtīyā / yatastayoḥ sambodhayoryathākramamaparyantā deśanāḥ śabdajanyā janakāśca te kathaṃ sarve? nānā vineyānurūpaiḥ sarvairākāraiḥ prathanāt / kathamaparyantāḥ? anidhanena tena kāyena deśanāyā niravadhikatvāt / tāthāgatasyāpi sambodhasyāparyantatā / kuta ityāha / savabuddhadharmasamudāgamāparyantatayā prajñāpāramitāparyantatā / yathoktaḥ śāstureva mahāyānadharmasambodha iha prajñāpāramitā / tasyā aparyantatā / tatkāraṇasya sarvabuddhadharmāṇāṃ samudāgamasyāparyantatayetyarthaḥ / te punardharmā mahatyobhagavatyoḥ paṭhyante / saptatriṃśabdodhipakṣyā dharmāḥ / aṣṭau vimokṣāḥ / navānupūrvavihārasamāpattayaḥ / daśa kṛtsnāyatanāni / aṣṭavabhibhvāyatanāni / araṇā samādhiḥ / praṇidhijñānam / catasraḥ pratisamvidaḥ / sarvākārāścatasraḥ pariśuddhayaḥ / daśa vaśitāḥ / daśa balāni / catvāri vaiśāradyāni / trīṇyarakṣyāṇi / trīṇi smṛtyupasthānāni / asaṃmoṣadharmatā / vāsanāsamudghātaḥ / mahākaruṇā / aṣṭādaśāveṇikāḥ buddhadharmāḥ / sarvākārajñatā ceti // ataḥ śāstram-
body.translated_text: The third case [is used] in the sense of cause. Because the teachings, produced by and productive of the two types of awakening (<s>sambodha</s>) respectively in their order, are boundless — how [are they] 'all'? Through extension in all modes conforming to the various types of trainees. How are they boundless? Because of the unlimitedness of teaching by that imperishable body. The boundlessness of the <s>Tathāgata's</s> awakening too [follows]. How so? — he says: 'By the boundlessness of the complete acquisition of all <s>Buddha</s>-qualities, the boundlessness of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> [is established].' As stated, the Teacher's own awakening to the <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>Dharma</s> is here <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>. Its boundlessness — [follows] from the boundlessness of the complete acquisition of all <s>Buddha</s>-qualities, which is its cause — this is the meaning. Those qualities are read in the two great [texts, i.e., the <s>Mahāprajñāpāramitā</s> and the <s>Bhagavatī</s>]: the thirty-seven <s>bodhipakṣya dharmas</s> (factors of awakening); eight <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations); nine successive attainments of absorption (<s>anupūrvavihāra-samāpattis</s>); ten <s>kṛtsnāyatanas</s> (totality bases); eight <s>abhibhvāyatanas</s> (bases of mastery); the <s>araṇā-samādhi</s> (concentration of non-conflict); <s>praṇidhi-jñāna</s> (aspiration-knowledge); four <s>pratisaṃvids</s> (analytical knowledges); all-aspect fourfold purifications; ten <s>vaśitās</s> (masteries); ten <s>balas</s> (powers); four <s>vaiśāradyas</s> (fearlessnesses); three <s>arakṣyas</s> (things not requiring guarding); three <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (applications of mindfulness); <s>asammoṣa-dharmatā</s> (nature of non-forgetfulness); <s>vāsanā-samudghāta</s> (destruction of latent impressions); <s>mahākaruṇā</s> (great compassion); eighteen <s>āveṇika buddha-dharmas</s> (unique Buddha-qualities); and <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience in all aspects). Therefore the treatise [states] —

children.translated_text: 'The factors of awakening, the immeasurables, the liberations, and in sequence,
the ninefold attainment, the tenfold totality,' // 8-2 //
'the bases of mastery of eight kinds in [their] divisions,
the concentration of non-conflict, aspiration-knowledge, the superknowledges, the analytical knowledges,' // 8-3 //
'all-aspect, the four purifications, the ten masteries,
the ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, the [three things] not requiring guarding,' // 8-4 //
'the threefold application of mindfulness, the threefold nature of non-forgetfulness,
the destruction of latent impressions, and great compassion for beings,' // 8-5 //
'the qualities unique to the Sage alone, which are declared as eighteen,
and omniscience in all aspects — [all this] is called the <s>dharmakāya</s> (dharma-body).' // 8-6 //

body.text:
bodhipakṣyāścāpramāṇānīti dvandvaḥ / 'anupūrvaśa' iti / anupūrva pareṇa saṃbadhyate / 'arakṣaṇa' ityakaraṇīyarakṣaṇam / arakṣyamityarthaḥ / tat trividham / 'dharmakāya' iti / anāśravo buddhānāṃ dharmarāśiḥ / yathāvasaramasmābhirbahavo vyākhyātāḥ / śeṣāniha vyācakṣīmahi /
'aṣṭau vimokṣā' iti / rūpī rūpāṇi paśyati suvarṇadurvarṇāni nīlapītalohitāvadātānīti prathamo vimokṣaḥ / adhyātmamarūpasaṃjñī rūpāṇi paśyati pūrvavaditi
body.translated_text:
'<s>Bodhipakṣyāḥ</s> (factors of awakening) and the immeasurables' — this is a <s>dvandva</s> (copulative compound). '<s>Anupūrvaśaḥ</s>' (in sequence) — '<s>anupūrva</s>' connects with the following [verse]. '<s>Arakṣaṇa</s>' means 'the guarding of that which need not be guarded' — meaning '<s>arakṣya</s>' (not requiring guarding). That is threefold. '<s>Dharmakāya</s>' — the uncontaminated aggregate of qualities of the <s>Buddhas</s>. Many of these have been explained by us elsewhere. We shall explain the remaining ones here.
'The eight <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations)' — 'Having form, one sees forms — golden, ugly, blue, yellow, red, and white' — this is the first liberation. 'Not having the perception of form internally, one sees forms externally, as before' — this is

body.text: dvitīyaḥ / śubhaṃ vimokṣaṃ kāyena sākṣātkṛtvopasampadya viharatīti tṛtīyaḥ / ākāśānantyāyatanādivimokṣāścatvāraḥ / saṃjñāveditanirodho 'ṣṭamaḥ /
body.translated_text: the second. 'Having directly realized the beautiful liberation with the body, one dwells having attained it' — this is the third.
