The four liberations beginning with the sphere of infinite space (<s>ākāśānantyāyatana</s>) and so on. The cessation of perception and feeling (<s>saṃjñāvedita-nirodha</s>) is the eighth.

body.text: āvaraṇādvimucyanta ebhiriti vimokṣāḥ / tatra trayo nirmāṇāvaraṇavimokṣāḥ / śeṣāḥ śāntavihārasamāpattyāvaraṇavimokṣāḥ / trayo rūpiṇaḥ / pañcārūpiṇaḥ / paramapraśānto 'ṣṭamaḥ / rūpīti ātmani rūpasaṃjñī / paśyatīti adhimokṣanirmitāni manasā paśyati / adhyātmamarūpasaṃjñī / ātmani nāmasaṃjñī / śubho vimokṣaḥ / śubhāśubhāni rūpāṇi nirmāya teṣvekatarasaṃjñālābhāt / yathākramamābhogaprātikūlyaprahāṇāya / saṃjñāveditānirodho 'sthāvarāṇāṃ cittacaitasikānāṃ kliṣṭamanaḥsaṃgṛhītānāṃ ca nirodhaḥ prāg vyutthānāt //
body.translated_text: 'They are liberated from obscurations through these' — hence '<s>vimokṣas</s>' (liberations). Therein, three are liberations from the obscuration to emanation. The rest are liberations from the obscuration to peaceful abiding and attainment. Three have form. Five are formless. The eighth is supremely peaceful. '<s>Rūpī</s>' (having form) — having the perception of form in oneself. 'Sees' — sees with the mind the objects created through resolve (<s>adhimokṣa</s>). '<s>Adhyātmam arūpasaṃjñī</s>' — having the perception of name (not form) in oneself. 'The beautiful liberation' — having created beautiful and ugly forms, through attaining the perception of one or the other — for the purpose of abandoning, respectively, aversion to deliberate effort and to what is disagreeable. The cessation of perception and feeling (<s>saṃjñāvedita-nirodha</s>) — is the cessation of unstable mental and mental-factor [states], including those comprised by the afflicted mind (<s>kliṣṭa-manas</s>), prior to re-emergence.

body.text: aṣṭāvabhibhvāyatanāni / ālambanābhibhavanādabhibhūtāni āyatanāni cittasthitayo 'bhibhvāyatanānyaṣṭau / tatra prathamādvimokṣāt dve abhinirhriyete / dvitāyādapi dve / tṛtīyāccatvāri / adhyātmaṃ rūpasaṃjñī bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyati parīttāni suvarṇadurvarṇāni hīnapraṇītāni / tāni khalu rūpāṇyabhibhūya jānāti, abhibhūya paśyati, tathā saṃjñī ca bhavatīti prathamam / adhyātmaṃ rūpasaṃjñī bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyatyadhimātrāṇi suvarṇadurvarṇāni yāvattathāsaṃjñī ca bhavatīti dvitīyam / adhyātmamarūpasaṃjñī ca bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyati parīttānītyādi tṛtīyam / adhyātmamarūpasaṃjñī bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyatyadhimātrāṇītyādi caturtham / tṛtīyādvimokṣāccatvāryabhinirhriyante / adhyātmamarūpasaṃjñī bahirdhā rūpāṇī paśyati nīlāni nīlavarṇāni nīlanidarśanāni nīlanirbhāsāni / tadyathā umakāpuṣpaṃ sampannaṃ vārāṇaseyakaṃ vastraṃ nīlaṃ nīlavarṇaṃ nīlanidarśanaṃ nilanirbhāsam / tāni ca rūpāṇyabhibhūya jānāti, abhibhūya paśyati, tathāsaṃjñī ca bhavatīti pañcamam / evaṃ pītānītyādi / tadyathā karṇikārapuṣpamityadikaṃ ṣaṣṭham / evaṃ lohitānityādi / tadyathā bandhujīvapuṣpamityādi saptamam / evamavadātānītyādi / tadyathā uṣasi tārakārūpamityādi cāṣṭamam //
body.translated_text: The eight <s>abhibhvāyatanas</s> (bases of mastery). Because of mastering the objects, the mastered mental states are the bases of mastery — eight [in number]. Therein, from the first liberation, two are extracted. From the second also, two. From the third, four. 'Having the perception of form internally, one sees forms externally — limited, golden or ugly, inferior or excellent. Having mastered those forms, one knows, having mastered them one sees, and one has such a perception' — this is the first. 'Having the perception of form internally, one sees forms externally — extensive, golden or ugly, and so on, and one has such a perception' — this is the second. 'Not having the perception of form internally, one sees forms externally — limited' and so on — this is the third. 'Not having the perception of form internally, one sees forms externally — extensive' and so on — this is the fourth. From the third liberation, four are extracted. 'Not having the perception of form internally, one sees forms externally — blue, of blue color, of blue appearance, of blue radiance. Just as the <s>umaka</s> flower in full bloom, or a cloth of <s>Vārāṇasī</s> that is blue, of blue color, of blue appearance, of blue radiance. Having mastered those forms, one knows, having mastered them one sees, and one has such a perception' — this is the fifth. Similarly 'yellow' and so on — just as the <s>karṇikāra</s> flower and so on — this is the sixth. Similarly 'red' and so on — just as the <s>bandhujīva</s> flower and so on — this is the seventh. Similarly 'white' and so on — just as the form of stars at dawn and so on — this is the eighth.

body.text: tatra parīttāni sattvasakhyātāni svalpapramāṇatvāt / suvarṇadurvarṇāni śubhāśubhatvāt / hīnapraṇītāni bhaumadivyatvāt / tāni vimokṣairadhimucyābhibhvāyatanairabhibhavati / punaḥ punarantarddhāpya darśanāt / abhibhūya jānāti śamathena paśyati vipaśyanayā tathāsaṃjñī bhavati nirabhimānatvāt / adhimātrāṇīti / asattvasaṃkhyātāni gṛhavimānaparvatādīni mahāpramāṇatvāt / nīlānīti uddeśaḥ / śeṣairnirdeśaḥ / nīlavarṇānīti svābhāvikena varṇena / nīlanidarśanānīti sāṃyogikena varṇena / nīlanirbhāsānīti / ubhayathāpi bhāsvaratvāt / umakātaśī(sī?) / karṇikāraḥ prasiddhaḥ / bandhujīvo bandhūkaḥ / uṣā rātrerantaḥ //
body.translated_text: Therein, 'limited' — reckoned among sentient beings, because of their small measure. 'Golden and ugly' — because of being beautiful and ugly. 'Inferior and excellent' — because of being earthly and divine. Those are resolved by the <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations) and mastered by the <s>abhibhvāyatanas</s> (bases of mastery) — through repeatedly causing [them] to appear and disappear from within. 'Having mastered, one knows' — through <s>śamatha</s> (calm). 'One sees' — through <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight). 'One has such a perception' — because of being free from conceit. 'Extensive' — reckoned among non-sentient things such as houses, palaces, mountains, and the like, because of their great measure. 'Blue' — this is the outline. The rest is the detailed exposition. 'Of blue color' — by its natural color. 'Of blue appearance' — by its adventitious color. 'Of blue radiance' — because of being luminous in both ways. '<s>Umakā</s>' is a [type of flax flower]. '<s>Karṇikāra</s>' is well known. '<s>Bandhujīva</s>' is the <s>bandhūka</s> [flower]. '<s>Uṣā</s>' is the end of night.

body.text: 'kṛtsnaṃ' daśavidhātmakaṃ' iti / abhibhvāyatanairabhibhūya pṛthivyādīnāṃ kṛtsnaṃ samantādibhiḥ sapharaṇātkṛtsnānyucyante / kadācittānyevāyatanānīti kṛtsnāyatanānyucyante / kadācittu pṛthivyādibhirviśiṣya nirdiśyante / pṛthivīkṛtsnaṃ apkṛtsnaṃ tejaḥkṛtsnaṃ vāyuḥkṛtsnaṃ nīlakṛtsnaṃ pītakṛtsnaṃ lohitakṛtsnaṃ avadātakṛtsnaṃ ākāśānantyāyatanakṛtsnaṃ vijñānānantyāyatanakṛtsnaṃ ceti //
body.translated_text: 'The tenfold totality (<s>kṛtsna</s>)' — having mastered [objects] through the <s>abhibhvāyatanas</s>, the <s>kṛtsnas</s> (totalities) of earth and so on are called '<s>kṛtsnas</s>' because of pervasion in all directions. Sometimes those very [mental] bases are called '<s>kṛtsnāyatanas</s>' (totality-bases). Sometimes they are specified by earth and so on: the earth-totality, water-totality, fire-totality, wind-totality, blue-totality, yellow-totality, red-totality, white-totality, infinite-space-sphere-totality, and infinite-consciousness-sphere-totality.

body.text: 'sarvākārāścatasraḥ pariśuddhaya' iti / āśrayapariśuddhirālambanapariśuddhiścittapariśuddhirjñānapariśuddhiśca /
body.translated_text: 'The all-aspect fourfold purifications' — purification of the basis (<s>āśraya</s>), purification of the object (<s>ālambana</s>), purification of mind (<s>citta</s>), and purification of knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>).

body.text: tatra savāsanānāṃ sarvakleśapakṣāṇāṃ daurbalyānāmāśrayādatyantoparamaḥ svasyacātmabhāvasya yathecchamādānasthānacyavaneṣu vaśavartitā sarvākārā āśrayapariśuddhiḥ / sarvālambanānāṃ nirmāṇapariṇāmasaṃprakhyāneṣu vaśavartitā sarvākārā ālambanapariśuddhiḥ / pūrvavatsarvacittadauṣṭhulyāpagamaścitte ca sarvākārakuśalamūlopacayaḥ sarvākārāṃ cittapariśuddhiḥ / pūrvavatsarvāvidyāpakṣadauṣṭhulyāpagamaḥ sarvajñeyajñāne ca vaśavartitā sarvākārā jñānapariśuddhiḥ //
body.translated_text: Therein, the all-aspect purification of the basis is: the complete cessation of all classes of affliction together with their latent impressions and weaknesses from the basis; and mastery over the assumption, maintenance, and leaving of one's own embodiment at will. The all-aspect purification of the object is: mastery over the emanation, transformation, and manifestation of all objects. The all-aspect purification of mind is, as before: the removal of all unsuitability of mind, and the accumulation of wholesome roots of all aspects in the mind. The all-aspect purification of knowledge is, as before: the removal of all unsuitability belonging to the class of ignorance, and mastery over the knowledge of all that is to be known.

body.text: 'vaśitā daśa' iti / daśa vaśitāḥ / ayurvaśitā yathecchamāyuṣasthāpanāt tyajanācca / cittavaśitā yathecchadhyānādisamāpatteḥ / pariṣkāravaśitā yathecchamupakaraṇapratyupasthānāt / karmavaśitā yathecchaṃ kāyavākkarmasiddheḥ / upapattivaśitā sarvopapattyāyataneṣu yathecchamupapatteḥ / ṛddhivaśitā yathecchamabhijñāḥ / praṇidhānavaśitā sarvapraṇidhānasamṛddheḥ / adhimuktivaśitā yadyathādhimucyate tattathaiva bhavati / jñānavaśitā yadeva jñātumicchati tadeva jānāti / dharmavaśitā sūtrādidharmavyavasthāneṣu kauśalam //
body.translated_text: 'The ten masteries (<s>vaśitās</s>)' — the ten masteries are: mastery over lifespan, through establishing and relinquishing the life-force at will; mastery over mind, through entering <s>dhyāna</s> and other attainments at will; mastery over requisites, through the appearance of provisions at will; mastery over action, through the accomplishment of bodily and verbal action at will; mastery over birth, through being born at will in all places of rebirth; mastery over <s>ṛddhi</s> (supernatural power), through [exercising] the superknowledges at will; mastery over aspiration, through the fulfillment of all aspirations; mastery over resolve (<s>adhimukti</s>), [whereby] whatever one resolves upon, that very thing comes to be; mastery over knowledge, [whereby] whatever one wishes to know, that very thing one knows; mastery over <s>Dharma</s>, skill in establishing the <s>Dharma</s> as <s>sūtras</s> and so on.

body.text: 'trīṇyarakṣyāṇi' iti / pariśuddhakāyasamudācārastathāgato nāsti tasyāpariśuddhakāyasamudācāratā yāṃ tathāgataḥ praticchādayitavyāṃ manyeta kaccitpare na jānīyurityetatprathamamarakṣyam evaṃ vākkarma dvitīyam / evaṃ manaḥkarma tṛtīyam //
body.translated_text: 'The three things not requiring guarding (<s>arakṣyas</s>)' — The <s>Tathāgata</s> has pure bodily conduct; there is no impure bodily conduct of his that the <s>Tathāgata</s> would think should be concealed, [wondering] 'perhaps others might find out' — this is the first thing not requiring guarding. Similarly, verbal action is the second. Similarly, mental action is the third.

body.text: 'trīṇi smṛtyupasthānāni' yathāpāṭham- "tathāgatasya dharma deśayata ekatyāḥ śuśrūṣante / śrotramavadadhati / ājñācittamupasthāpayanti pratipadyante dharmasyānudharmam / na tena tathāgatasya nandī bhavati na saumanasyaṃ na cetasa utplāvitatvam / apare na śuśrūṣante / na śrotramavadadhatītyādi / na tena tathāgatasyāghāto nākṣāntirnāpratyayaḥ na cetaso 'nabhirāddhiḥ / ekatyāḥ śuśrūṣante / ekatyā na suśrūṣante / na tena tathāgatasya dvayaṃ bhavati nandī āghātaśca / sarvatropekṣako viharati smṛtimāna samprajānan" iti //
body.translated_text: 'The three applications of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthānas</s>)' — according to the reading: 'When the <s>Tathāgata</s> teaches the <s>Dharma</s>, some listen, lend ear, generate the mind of understanding, and practice in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s> — the <s>Tathāgata</s> has no delight, no pleasant feeling, no mental elation on that account. Others do not listen, do not lend ear, and so on — the <s>Tathāgata</s> has no resentment, no impatience, no displeasure, no mental dissatisfaction on that account. Some listen and some do not listen — the <s>Tathāgata</s> has neither of the two on that account, neither delight nor resentment. In all cases he abides equanimous, mindful and clearly comprehending.'

body.text: 'asammoṣadharmatā' sattvārthakriyākālānatikramādbuddhānām / ata evaiṣā lakṣaṇavidhānatopapannā bhavati //
body.translated_text: 'The nature of non-forgetfulness (<s>asammoṣa-dharmatā</s>)' — because the <s>Buddhas</s> do not let slip the proper time for acting for the benefit of beings. For this very reason, this [quality] is established through the provision of [the <s>Buddha's</s>] marks.

body.text: 'vāsanāsamuddhāta' iti / prahīṇakleśasyāpi yadaprahīṇakleśasyeva ceṣṭitaṃ sā kleśavāsanā / sāpi tathāgatasyāstaṅgateti samudghātakleśavāsanaḥ sa bhagavānucyate //
body.translated_text: 'The destruction of latent impressions (<s>vāsanā-samudghāta</s>)' — even for one whose afflictions have been abandoned, there is behavior as though afflictions had not been abandoned — that is the latent impression of afflictions (<s>kleśa-vāsanā</s>). Even that has set in the <s>Tathāgata</s> — hence the <s>Bhagavān</s> is said to have destroyed the latent impressions of affliction.

body.text: 'mahākaruṇā' hitāśayatā / yayā bhagavānsarvakālaṃ ṣaṭkṛtvo lokaṃ vyavalokayati "ko hīyata ko varddhata" ityādi //
body.translated_text: '<s>Mahākaruṇā</s>' (great compassion) — the disposition toward benefit. By which the <s>Bhagavān</s> surveys the world at all times, six times [a day]: 'Who is declining? Who is progressing?' and so on.

body.text: 'sarvākārajñatā' iti sarvadharmāṇāṃ svabhāvaviśeṣalakṣaṇaprabhedaparyantajñānamityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: '<s>Sarvākārajñatā</s>' (omniscience in all aspects) — means the knowledge of the own-nature, specific characteristics, divisions, and limits of all <s>dharmas</s> — this is the meaning.

body.text: raṇaṃ vivādakalahādi / iha tu raṇahetuḥ kleśo raṇaḥ / tamālambya raṇamutpādayatīti / yaṃ samādhiṃ samāpadyate, yato vyutthāya grāmādau praviṣṭaṃ tamālambya tatratyānāṃ raṇaṃ notpadyate sā 'araṇā' / sā śrāvakasyāpi bhavati buddhasyāpi / tayoḥ kāritraviśeṣaḥ / tamadhikṛtya śāstram-
body.translated_text: '<s>Raṇa</s>' (conflict) is dispute, quarrel, and the like. But here, the <s>kleśa</s> (affliction) that is the cause of conflict is '<s>raṇa</s>.' 'Relying on that, it produces conflict' — the <s>samādhi</s> that one attains, from which, upon emerging, when one enters a village and the like, relying on that [samādhi], conflict does not arise among the people there — that is '<s>araṇā</s>' (non-quarrel). That exists for a <s>Śrāvaka</s> as well as for a <s>Buddha</s>. The distinction in their function between those two — regarding that, the treatise [states] —

children.translated_text: The <s>araṇā</s> of the <s>Śrāvaka</s> removes the seeing [of afflictions], not the afflictions themselves.
The <s>Jina's</s> (Victor's) <s>araṇā</s> is for cutting off the stream of those afflictions in villages and the like. [8-7]

body.text: śrāvakīyāraṇā kleśahetordarśanasya parihāritā / na sākṣātkleśasya / saugatī tu parakīyakleśasrotasa ucchedāya na darśanasyetyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: The <s>Śrāvaka's</s> <s>araṇā</s> removes the seeing of the cause of afflictions, not the afflictions directly. But the <s>Sugata's</s> (Buddha's) is for the cutting off of the stream of others' afflictions, not of seeing — this is the meaning.

body.text: idaṃ jānīyāmiti praṇidhāya dhyānaṃ samāpannasya lokavṛttāntādau yajjñānamutpadyate tat 'praṇidhijñānaṃ' śrāvakāṇām /
body.translated_text: 'Having resolved "I shall know this," the knowledge that arises for one who has attained <s>dhyāna</s> regarding worldly events and the like' — that is the '<s>praṇidhijñāna</s>' (resolution-knowledge) of the <s>Śrāvakas</s>.

body.text: tathāgatamadhikṛtya śāstram-
body.translated_text: Regarding the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the treatise [states] —

children.translated_text: Without deliberate effort, unobstructed, unimpeded, always abiding,
Removing all questions, and exalted — this is held to be the resolution-knowledge. [8-8]

body.text: 'anābhogaṃ' nirvikalpatvāt / 'anāsaṅgaṃ' nirapekṣatvāt / 'avyāghātaṃ' sarvatrāpratihatatvāt / 'sadā sthitaṃ' ityasamāhite cetasi sthitatvāt / sarvapraśnān chedayatīti 'sarvapraśnāpanut' /
body.translated_text: 'Without deliberate effort' (<s>anābhoga</s>) — because of being non-conceptual. 'Unobstructed' (<s>anāsaṅga</s>) — because of being independent. 'Unimpeded' (<s>avyāghāta</s>) — because of being unhindered everywhere. 'Always abiding' — because of abiding even in a non-concentrated state of mind. 'It removes all questions' — it cuts through all questions — hence '<s>sarvapraśnāpanut</s>.'

body.text: sa ca sambhogakāyaḥ pariśuddhe svabuddhakṣetre jāyate yāvadākāśasthitiravatiṣṭhate / tatkuto buddhakṣetram? prādhānyena tasyaiva tatropapatteḥ /
body.translated_text: And that <s>Saṃbhogakāya</s> (enjoyment body) arises in a purified <s>Buddha-kṣetra</s> (Buddha-field) and abides as long as space endures. Whence is the <s>Buddha-kṣetra</s>? Because of the birth there principally of that very [<s>Saṃbhogakāya</s>].

body.text: lujyate pralujyateti lokaḥ / prajātaṃ bhājanaṃ ca / tasmāt dvidhā lokadhātuḥ sattvaloko bhājanalokaśca / tatra sattvalokapariśuddhimadhikṛtyāha / sarvasattvadhātupuṇyajñānasambhārāparyantatayā prajñāpāramitāpayantatānugatavyeti / yayā bhagavataḥ prajñayā paripācitāḥ sattvāstatra yāvadākāśamutpadyante / utpannāśca yayā bodhaye pariprācyante / seha prajñāpāramitā / tasyā aparyantatānugantavyā / kathamityāha / sarvetyādi / ye kecittatra sattvā utpadyante / sarve te labdhāryabhūmayo bodhisattvāḥ / te sarve / sarvaḥ sattvadhātuḥ sattvarāśiḥ / tasya puṇyajñānasambhāraḥ / tayoraparyantatayā / pṛthivīdhātvaparyantatayā prajñāpāramitāparyantatānugantavyā / evamabdhātutejodhātuvāyudhātvākāśadhātuvijñānadhātvaparyantatayā prajñāpāramitāparyantatānugantavyeti / tathā hi bhājanalokastatra karatalasamaṃ bhūtalam / prāsādodyānavāpīkalpadrumādiparikaraśca sattvāvāsaḥ paramojjvalasaptaratnamayo 'nekalokadhātvantarasphuraṇamahāraśmipramokṣa upariṣṭhācca gaganamanurūpasanirbhāsaṃ ṣaḍdhātukāśca sattvāḥ / "ṣaḍdhāturayaṃ bhikṣo puruṣaḥ" iti vacanāt / atasteṣāmapi kāyaḥ kāntimān prabhāmaṇḍalībhūmyanurūpavarṇasaṃskāraḥ / tatrābhogaparibhogāśca sattvānāṃ sarvadevalokaprativiśiṣṭāḥ / yeṣāmupabhoga ekāntasukha ekāntānavadya ekāntavaśavartī ca / īdṛśī ṣaḍdhātupariśuddhiraparyantā niravadhikatvādativiśālatvācca / atastasyā aparyantayā tatkāraṇabhūtāyā bhagavataḥ prajñāyā aparyantatānugantavyā / tatra cotpannā bodhisattvā anantān lokadhātūn gatvā tatratyānāṃ sattvānāmakuśalaṃ(la)sañcayān hantadhyā(vyā?)na(n) tatpratipakṣāṃśca kuśalasañcayān prajānanti / teṣāmapramāṇatayā tatparicchedikāyāsteṣāṃ prajñāyā apramāṇatā veditavyetyetadāha / kuśalākuśaladhamasañcayāpramāṇatayā prajñāpāramitāpramāṇatā veditavyeti / yāvantaśca te bodhisattvāsteṣāṃ kuśaladharmotpādanāya dharma deśayanti sa sarvaḥ sarvadharmasañcayaḥ / tasyāpramāṇatayā tadvyavasthāpikāyāsteṣāṃ prajñāyā apramāṇatā veditavyetyetadāha / sarvadharmasañcayāpramāṇatayā prajñapāramitāpramāṇatā veditavyeti //
body.translated_text: 'That which perishes and disintegrates' is the world (<s>loka</s>). And that which is born — the container [world]. Therefore the world-realm (<s>lokadhātu</s>) is twofold: the world of sentient beings and the world of the container. Regarding the purification of the world of sentient beings, he says: 'Because of the limitlessness of the accumulations of merit and knowledge of all the <s>sattvadhātu</s> (realm of beings), the limitlessness of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be understood.' The <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) of the <s>Bhagavān</s> by which beings are ripened, [so that] they are born there for as long as space [endures], and by which, once born, they are matured toward awakening — that here is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Its limitlessness should be understood. How? He says beginning with 'All' and so on. Whatever beings are born there — all of them are <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have attained the noble stages. All of them. The entire <s>sattvadhātu</s> is the mass of beings. Their accumulation of merit and knowledge. Because of the limitlessness of those two. Because of the limitlessness of the earth-element, the limitlessness of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be understood. Similarly, because of the limitlessness of the water-element, fire-element, wind-element, space-element, and consciousness-element, the limitlessness of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be understood. For the container world there [has] a level ground smooth as the palm of the hand, and the dwelling of beings [is] with the accoutrements of palaces, gardens, ponds, wish-fulfilling trees, and the like, made of supremely brilliant seven jewels, emitting great rays that radiate through many world-realms; and above, the sky is splendidly luminous in conformity [with the ground]. And the beings are of six elements — because of the statement: 'This person, O <s>bhikṣu</s>, is of six elements.' Therefore their bodies too are radiant, with color, form, and adornment conforming to the luminous ground. And the provisions and enjoyments of beings there surpass even all the heavenly realms — whose enjoyment is exclusively pleasurable, exclusively blameless, and exclusively under one's control. Such purification of the six elements is limitless — because of being unbounded and exceedingly vast. Therefore, because of its limitlessness, the limitlessness of the <s>Bhagavān's</s> <s>prajñā</s>, which is its cause, should be understood. And the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> born there, going to infinite world-realms, know the accumulations of unwholesome [karma] of the beings there — which are to be destroyed — and also the accumulations of wholesome [karma] that are their antidote. Because of the immeasurability of those [beings], the immeasurability of the <s>prajñā</s> that discerns them should be known — this he states: 'Because of the immeasurability of the accumulations of wholesome and unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>, the immeasurability of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be known.' And whatever <s>Dharma</s> those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> teach for the generation of wholesome <s>dharmas</s> in those [beings] — all that is the accumulation of all <s>dharmas</s>. Because of its immeasurability, the immeasurability of the <s>prajñā</s> that establishes them should be known — this he states: 'Because of the immeasurability of the accumulation of all <s>dharmas</s>, the immeasurability of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be known.'

body.text: sarvadharmasamādhyaparyantatayā prajñāpāramitāparyantatānugantavyeti / dharmā dhāraṇyaḥ samādhayaścittasthitayaḥ / dharmāśca samādhayaśca sarve ca te dharmasamādhayaśca / teṣāmaparyantatā / tatpratilambhitā tallābhitā yā tatra bodhisattvānāṃ tayā tajjanikāyā bhagavataḥ prajñayā aparyantatā veditavyetyarthaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Because of the limitlessness of all <s>dharma-samādhis</s>, the limitlessness of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be understood.' '<s>Dharmas</s>' are <s>dhāraṇīs</s> (retentions); '<s>samādhis</s>' are the stabilities of mind. Both <s>dharmas</s> and <s>samādhis</s>, and all of these are '<s>dharmasamādhis</s>.' Their limitlessness. Because of being obtained by them — because of being attained by the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> there — the limitlessness of the <s>Bhagavān's</s> <s>prajñā</s> that produces those [attainments] should be understood — this is the meaning.

body.text: sarvabuddharmāparyantatayā prajñāpāramitāparyantatānugantavyeti / tatra buddhaḥ sambhogakāyaḥ / tasya sarve dharmāḥ sarvabuddhadharmāḥ / dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇānyaśīti
body.translated_text: 'Because of the limitlessness of all <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>, the limitlessness of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be understood.' There, the '<s>Buddha</s>' is the <s>Saṃbhogakāya</s>. All the <s>dharmas</s> (qualities) of that [Buddha] are 'all <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>.' The thirty-two marks of a great person and the eighty

body.text: cānuvyañjanāni / teṣāmaparyantatā aparicchedyatā / kenāparicchedyatā? tulayā / tathāgatādanyasya tādṛśānāmabhāvāt / tayā bhagavataḥ prajñāyāstādṛśyevāparyantatā veditavyā / katamasyāḥ prajñāyāḥ? yayā teṣāṃ samagrāṇi kāraṇāni samyak parijñāya samyaganuṣṭhitāni / ataḥ śāstram-
body.translated_text: secondary marks. Their limitlessness is their being beyond delimitation. By what are they beyond delimitation? By comparison — because of the non-existence of such [marks] in anyone other than the <s>Tathāgata</s>. By that, such limitlessness of the <s>Bhagavān's</s> <s>prajñā</s> should be known. Which <s>prajñā</s>? That by which, having completely understood the aggregate causes of those [marks] correctly, they were correctly practiced. Therefore the treatise [states] —

children.translated_text: The thirty-two marks and eighty secondary marks constitute the <s>Muni's</s> (Sage's)
This body, held to be the <s>Saṃbhogakāya</s> (enjoyment body), because of the enjoyment of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. [8-12]

body.text: caturthena pādena sambhogikatve kāraṇamāha /
body.translated_text: By the fourth quarter [of the verse], he states the reason for its being the <s>Saṃbhogakāya</s>.

body.text: tatrādau pañcabhirindravajrābhirlakṣaṇānyāha /
body.translated_text: Therein, first, by five <s>Indravajrā</s> verses, he states the marks.

children.translated_text: Wheel-marked hands; feet with a [firm] step; tortoise-like feet; web-joined fingers on hands and feet;

children.text: karau sapādau taruṇau mṛdū ca samucchrayaiḥ saptabhirāśrayo 'sya // 8-13 //
children.translated_text: Hands and feet that are youthful and soft; and his body is characterized by seven elevations. [8-13]
Long fingers and a body with extended heels; full, straight, with high-arched feet and upward-growing body hair;
Antelope-like calves; and nimble thighs and arms; sheath-covered, supreme, with concealed private parts. [8-14]
Golden-colored, with fine smooth skin, each hair curling to the right and well-born;
His face marked with the <s>ūrṇā</s> (tuft); lion-like upper body; rounded shoulders, with full inter-shoulder breadth. [8-15]
The inferior taste is renowned; his supreme taste; his body symmetrical like a banyan tree;
<s>Uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown protuberance) on his head; broad and beautiful tongue; <s>Brahmā's</s> voice; lion-like jaw; brilliantly white [teeth]; [8-16]
Equal in measure, not crowded, his teeth; not less in number, four [sets of] ten;
Blue eyes; eyelashes like those of a bull — these indeed are the thirty-two marks. [8-17]

body.text: kramaḥ pādaḥ cakrāṅkau hastau cāsyeti 'cakrāṅkahastakramaḥ' / supratiṣṭhitatvāt kūrmāviva pādāvasyeti 'kūrmāpādaḥ' / sa cāsau sa ceti samāsaḥ / jālāvanaddhāṅgalī pāṇī ca pādau cāsyeti 'jālāvanaddhāṅgalipāṇipādaḥ' / 'karau sapādau taruṇau mṛdū ca' asyeti pareṇa sambandhaḥ / 'samucchrayaiḥ saptabhirāśrayo 'sya' / lakṣaṇe tṛtīyā / āśrayaḥ kāyaḥ saptabhirucchayairlakṣitaḥ kāyo 'syetyarthaḥ / etena pañcalakṣaṇānyuktāni / cakrāṅkitapāṇipādatā supratiṣṭhitapādatā jālapāṇipādatā mṛdutaruṇahastapādatā saptocchrayatā ceti /
body.translated_text: '<s>Krama</s>' (step) is the foot; 'wheel-marked hands and step' [means] the hands and [feet] marked with wheels. 'Because of being well-established, the feet are like tortoises' — hence '<s>kūrmapāda</s>.' 'That one and this one' — thus the compound. 'Whose fingers on hands and feet are joined by webs' — hence '<s>jālāvanaddha-aṅguli-pāṇi-pāda</s>.' 'Hands and feet that are youthful and soft belong to him' — this connects with the following. 'His body with seven elevations.' The instrumental case is for the characteristic. '<s>Āśraya</s>' (support) is the body; the body characterized by seven protuberances belongs to him — this is the meaning. By this, five marks are stated: wheel-marked hands and feet; well-established feet; webbed hands and feet; soft and youthful hands and feet; and the seven protuberances.

children.translated_text: 'Long fingers and a body with extended heels; full, straight, with high-arched feet and upward-growing body hair;
Antelope-like calves; and nimble thighs and arms; sheath-covered, supreme, with concealed private parts.'

body.text: dīrghāṅgulitvaṃ ca āyatapārṣṇiśceti samāhāradvandvaḥ / 'gātraṃ prājyaṃ ṛju' iti bṛhadṛjugātram / ucchaṅkhapādaścāsau 'ūrdhvaromā' ca / uccaiḥ sunigūḍhajānugulphatvāducchaṅkhapāda iti sūtram / ataśca utkarṣanigūḍhārtha ucchabdaḥ / jānugulphāsthivācī śaṅkhaśabdaḥ / urū mūlādadhaśca sarva pāda iti gamyate / vastau guhyaṃ vastuguhyam / kośāvadhānamuttama vastiguhyamasyeti tathoktaḥ / anenāṣṭau lakṣaṇāni / dīrghāṅgulitā / āyatapārṣṇitā / bṛhadujugātratā / ucchaṅkhapādatā / ūrdhvāṅgaromatā / aiṇeyajaṅghatā / paṭūrubāhutā / kośāvahitavastiguhyatā ceti /
body.translated_text: 'Long fingers' and 'extended heels' — this is a collective <s>dvandva</s> compound. 'The body is full and straight' — meaning a large and straight body. 'High-arched feet' and 'upward-growing hair.' '<s>Ucchaṅkhapāda</s>' — the <s>sūtra</s> [reads]: 'Because of the deeply hidden knees and ankles, [he has] high-arched feet.' Therefore the word '<s>uccha</s>-' has the meaning of 'elevated, deeply hidden.' The word '<s>śaṅkha</s>' denotes the bones of the knee and ankle. 'Everything below the upper thighs is the foot' — this is understood. '<s>Vastiguhya</s>' is the private parts of the lower abdomen. '<s>Kośāvadhāna</s>' means 'supreme concealment of the private parts' belongs to him — thus so called. By this, eight marks [are stated]: long fingers; extended heels; large straight body; high-arched feet; upward-growing body hair; antelope-like calves; nimble thighs and arms; and sheath-covered private parts.

children.translated_text: 'Golden-colored, with fine smooth skin, each hair curling to the right and well-born;
His face marked with the <s>ūrṇā</s>; lion-like upper body; rounded shoulders, with full inter-shoulder breadth.'

body.text: hareriva pūrvakāyo 'syeti 'haripūrvakāyaḥ' / 'vṛttau' iti susaṃvṛttau / suśliṣṭaparimaṇḍalagrīvatvāt / asaṃyoraṃtaraṃ uttarāṃsamuraḥ / tadupacitamasyeti 'citāntarāṃsaḥ' / anena saptalakṣaṇāni / suvarṇavarṇatā / ślakṣaṇacchavitā / ekaikapradakṣiṇāvartaromatā / ūrṇāṅkitamukhatā / siṃhapūrvakāyatā / susaṃvṛtaskandhatā / citāntarāṃsatā ceti /
body.translated_text: 'His upper body is like a lion's' — hence '<s>haripūrvakāya</s>.' '<s>Vṛttau</s>' means well-rounded — because of the neck being well-covered and circular. '<s>Antarāṃsa</s>' is the upper chest between the shoulders. 'His [inter-shoulder breadth] is full' — hence '<s>citāntarāṃsa</s>.' By this, seven marks [are stated]: golden color; smooth fine skin; each hair curling to the right; face marked with the <s>ūrṇā</s>; lion-like upper body; well-rounded shoulders; and full inter-shoulder breadth.

body.text: 'hīno rasaḥ khyāti rasottamo 'sya nyagrodhavanmaṇḍalatulyamūrtiḥ /
body.translated_text: 'The inferior taste is renowned; his supreme taste; his body symmetrical like a banyan tree;

body.text: uṣṇīṣamūrdhā pṛthucārujivho brahmasvaraḥ siṃhahanuḥ suśuklāḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Uṣṇīṣa</s> on his head; broad and beautiful tongue; <s>Brahmā's</s> voice; lion-like jaw; brilliantly white [teeth];

children.translated_text: Equal in measure, not crowded, his teeth; not less in number, four [sets of] ten;
Blue eyes; eyelashes like those of a bull — these indeed are the thirty-two marks.'

body.text: anena ślokadvayena dvādaśalakṣaṇānyuktāni / rasarasajñatā / nyagrodhaparimaṇḍalatā / uṣṇīṣaśiraskatā / pṛthutanujivhatā / brahmasvaratā / siṃhahanutā / suśukladantatā / samadantatā / aviraladantatā / samacatvāriṃśaddantatā abhinīlanetratā / gopakṣmanetratā ceti / daśaparimāṇamasyāḥ saṃhateriti 'daśikā' / tāścatasraḥ / catvāriṃśadityarthaḥ / govṛṣau gobalīvardau / athavā 'govṛṣaḥ' puṅgavaḥ / sarvaikatvena 'dvāṃtriśadetāni hi lakṣaṇāni' / eṣāṃ vyākhyānaṃ ca hetuśca pūrvanimittatā ca dharmadāna (?) sūtre /
body.translated_text: By these two verses, twelve marks are stated: the knowledge of supreme taste; banyan-tree-like symmetry; <s>uṣṇīṣa</s>-head; broad and delicate tongue; <s>Brahmā</s>-voice; lion-jaw; brilliantly white teeth; even teeth; uncrowded teeth; forty teeth; deeply blue eyes; and bull-eyelashed eyes. '<s>Daśikā</s>' — a group whose measure is ten — 'of this collection'; and four of those — meaning forty. '<s>Govṛṣa</s>' — a bull (<s>gobalīvarda</s>). Alternatively, '<s>govṛṣa</s>' means the foremost [among cattle]. Together as one, 'these indeed are the thirty-two marks.' The explanation of these, their causes, and their precedent conditions [are found] in the <s>Dharmadāna</s>(?) <s>sūtra</s>.

children.translated_text: Whatever cause here accomplishes whatever mark —
Through the fulfillment of each such [cause], this [body] has the characteristic of accomplishment. [8-18]

body.text: atra
body.translated_text: Here,

children.text: 'yasya yasya lakṣaṇasya yo yo hetuḥ prasādhakaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever cause accomplishes whatever mark —
Through the fulfillment of each such [cause], this [body] has the characteristic of accomplishment.'

body.text: ayaṃ sāmbhogikaḥ kāyaḥ / kasya punaḥ ko heturityāha /
body.translated_text: This is the <s>Sāṃbhogika kāya</s> (enjoyment body). Now, what is the cause of what? — to this he says —

children.translated_text: Following teachers and the like; firmness regarding the vow;
The practice of the means of gathering [beings]; and the gift of excellent material things; [8-19]
The liberation of those condemned to death; undertaking [vows]; and the increase of the wholesome;
And so on — as in the <s>sūtra</s>, the cause that accomplishes the marks. [8-20]

body.text: tatra gurūṇāmanugamanapratyudgamānābhyāṃ dharmaśravaṇamālyopahāracaityānupānaprabhṛtiṣu ca paricāradānāccakrāṅkahastapādatā / dṛḍhasamādānatvāt supratiṣṭhitapādatā / saṃgrahavastūnāmāsevanājjālahastapādatā / praṇītānnapānādidānānmṛdutaruṇahastapādatā
body.translated_text: Therein, through going to meet and escorting teachers, and through the service of offering such as garlands, worship at <s>caityas</s>, and the like — [arises] the mark of wheel-marked hands and feet. Through firmness of undertaking — the mark of well-established feet. Through the practice of the means of gathering [beings] — the mark of webbed hands and feet. Through the gift of excellent food, drink, and the like — the mark of soft and youthful hands and feet.

body.text: saptocchadatā ca / 'vadhyamokṣāḥ' iti bahuvacanāmādyartham / vadhyamokṣaṇājjīvitānugrahakaraṇāt / prāṇātipātavirateścāsevanāddīrghāṅgulitā āyatapārṣṇitā bṛhadṛjugātratā ca / kuśaladharmasamādānasya vivardhanāducchaṃkhapādatā / ūrdhvāṅgiromatā ca / 'ityādika' evamādikaḥ / 'yathāsūtraṃ' iti yathā paṭhiṣyati dharmadāne / mahāpuruṣakāratvāt mahāpuruṣāstathāgatā mahābodhisattvāśca / teṣāṃ dyotakāni mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇāni dvātriṃśat / teṣāmeva śobhākaraṇādaśītyanuvyañjanāni / tānyadhikṛtya dvādaśaślokāḥ-
body.translated_text: And the seven elevations. '<s>Vadhyamokṣāḥ</s>' — the plural is used in the sense of 'and so forth.' Through liberating those condemned to death — through performing the act of saving life — and through the habitual practice of abstaining from killing — [arise] the marks of long fingers, extended heels, and a large straight body. Through the increase of the undertaking of wholesome <s>dharmas</s> — the mark of high-arched feet and upward-growing body hair. '<s>Ityādika</s>' means 'and so on, of such kind.' 'As in the <s>sūtra</s>' means as it will be read in the <s>Dharmadāna</s> [section]. Because of performing the deeds of a great person, the <s>Tathāgatas</s> and great <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are great persons. The thirty-two marks that are their indicators are the marks of a great person. The eighty secondary marks (<s>anuvyañjana</s>) that beautify those very [marks]. Regarding those, twelve verses —

children.text: tāmrāḥ snigdhāśca tuṅgāśca nakhā aṅgulayo muneḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Muni's</s> nails are copper-colored, glossy, and elevated;
His fingers are round, full, gradual; his veins are concealed and without knots. [8-21]

body.text: anenāṣṭāvanuvyañjanānyuktāni / tāmranakhatā snigdhanakhatā tuṅganakhatā ca / vṛttāṅgulitā citāṅgulitā anupūrvāṅgulitā ca gūḍhaśiratā nirgranthiśiratā ceti /
body.translated_text: By this, eight secondary marks are stated: copper-colored nails, glossy nails, elevated nails; round fingers, full fingers, gradual fingers; concealed veins, and knotless veins.

children.translated_text: His ankles are concealed, his feet even; his gait is like a lion's, an elephant's, a bull's, a lord of cattle's;
Majestic, rightward-turning, beautiful — his walk is straight and rounded.

body.text: muṣṭānupūrvate
body.translated_text: Fist-like and gradual —

body.text: iti ṣaḍakṣarādhikena ślokena dvādaśa / gūḍhagulphatā / aviṣamapādatā / siṃhavikrāntagāmitā / haṃsavikrāntagāmitā / vṛṣabhavikrāntagāmitā / pradakṣiṇāvataṃgāmitā / cārūgāmitā / avakragātratā / vṛttagātratā / mṛṣṭagātratā anupūrvagātratā ceti //
body.translated_text: By this verse and six [extra] syllables, twelve [secondary marks]: concealed ankles; even feet; lion-like gait; swan-like gait; bull-like gait; rightward-turning gait; beautiful gait; straight body; rounded body; polished body; gradual body.

children.translated_text: Purity and softness — a clean body;
Complete secondary marks; a beautiful, broad, circular body. [8-23]

body.text: iti ṣaḍiṃvaśatyākṣaraiḥ pañcānuvyañjanāni / śucigātratā mṛdugātratā viśuddhagātratā paripūrṇavyañjanatā cārupṛthumaṇḍalagātratā ceti /
body.translated_text: By twenty-six syllables, five secondary marks: a pure body, a soft body, a very clean body, complete secondary marks, and a beautiful broad circular body.

children.translated_text: Even gait; purity of the eyes; tenderness [of body];
A body not sunken but full; a well-knit and supple body. [8-24]

body.text: anena ṣaṭ / samakramatā viśuddhanetratā sukumāragātratā utsadagātratā susaṃhatanagātratā ceti //
body.translated_text: By this, six [secondary marks]: even gait; pure eyes; tender body; prominent body; well-knit and supple body.

children.translated_text: Well-proportioned limbs; darkness-dispelling, luminous purity;
Round, polished, unwounded, not-emaciated belly; and profundity [of the navel]. [8-25]

body.text: dakṣiṇāvartatā nābheḥ samantāddarśanīyatā /
body.translated_text: Rightward-turning navel; pleasing appearance from all sides;

body.text: anena sārdhaślokena nava / suvibhaktāṅgapratyaṅgatā vitimiraśuddhālokatā mṛṣṭakukṣitā abhagnakukṣitā akṣāmakukṣitā gambhīranābhitā dakṣiṇāvartanābhitā samantaprāsādikatā ceti //
body.translated_text: By this verse-and-a-half, nine [secondary marks]: well-proportioned major and minor limbs; darkness-free luminous purity; polished belly; unbroken belly; not-emaciated belly; deep navel; rightward-turning navel; pleasing from all sides.

body.text: samācāraḥ śuciḥ kālatilakāpagatā tanuḥ // 8-26 //
body.translated_text: Good conduct; purity; a body free from moles and blemishes. [8-26]

children.translated_text: Hands with markings that are cotton-soft, glossy, deep, and extended;
Speech that is not overly long; a face in which reflections arise like images. [8-27]

body.text: bimbānāṃ pratibimbodayo 'sminniti tathoktamāsyaṃ mukhamasyeti 'bimbapratibimbodayāsyaḥ' / anena sārdhaślokenāṣṭau / śucisamācāratā vyapagatatilakagātratā tūlasadṛśasukumārapāṇitā snigdhapāṇilekhatā gambhīrapāṇilekhatā āyatapāṇilekhatā nātyāyatavadanatā bimbapratibimbadarśanavadanatā ceti /
body.translated_text: 'A face (<s>āsya</s>) in which the arising of reflections (<s>pratibimba</s>) of images (<s>bimba</s>) [occurs]' — thus it is so called; the face belongs to him — hence '<s>bimbapratibimbodayāsya</s>.' By this verse-and-a-half, eight [secondary marks]: pure conduct; a body free from moles; cotton-like soft delicate hands; glossy palm-lines; deep palm-lines; extended palm-lines; speech that is not overly long; and a face in which images appear as reflections.

children.text: mṛdvī tanvī ca raktā ca jivhā jīmūtaghoṣatā /
children.translated_text: His tongue is soft, thin, and red; his voice is like a thundercloud;
His speech is lovely, sweet, and melodious; his canines are round, sharp, white, and even;

body.text: anupūrvodagatāstuṅgā nāsikā paramaṃ śuciḥ // 8-28 //
body.translated_text: Elevated and prominent; his nose is supremely pure. [8-28]

body.text: 'paramaṃ' atyantam / anena sārdhaślokena dvādaśa / mṛdujivhatā tanujivhatā raktajivhatā ca / gajagarjitajīmutaghoṣatā / madhuracārumañjusvaratā vṛttadaṃṣṭratā tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭratā śukladaṃṣṭratā samadaṃṣṭratā anupūrvadaṃṣṭratā tuṅganāsikatā śucināsikatā ceti //
body.translated_text: '<s>Parama</s>' means exceedingly. By this verse-and-a-half, twelve [secondary marks]: soft tongue, thin tongue, red tongue; voice like an elephant's trumpet and thundercloud; sweet, lovely, and melodious voice; round canines, sharp canines, white canines, even canines, graduated canines; prominent nose, pure nose.

body.text: viśāle nayane pakṣma cittaṃ padmadalākṣitā // 8-29 //
body.translated_text: Broad eyes; eyelashes; the mind [is serene]; eyes marked like lotus petals. [8-29]

children.translated_text: Eyebrows with hair that is long, smooth, well-glossed, and even; arms
Full and extended; ears that are even and free from defect. [8-30]

body.text: lalāṭamaparimlānaṃ pṛthu pūrnottamāṅgatā /
body.translated_text: A forehead that is unwithered, broad; fullness of the head.

body.text: samarome iti striyāṃ ḍāp / anena ślokadvayena trayodaśa / viśālanayanatā citapakṣmatā sitasitakamaladalanayanatā āyatabhrūtā ślakṣṇabhrūtā snigdhabhrūtā samaromabhrūtā pīnāyatabhujatā samakarṇatā anupahatakarṇatā supariṇāmitalalāṭatā pṛthulalāṭatā paripūrṇottamāṅgatā ceti //
body.translated_text: '<s>Samarome</s>' — in the feminine, the <s>ḍāp</s> suffix [is applied]. By these two verses, thirteen [secondary marks]: broad eyes; thick eyelashes; eyes [marked] like blue-white lotus petals; long eyebrows; smooth eyebrows; glossy eyebrows; even-haired eyebrows; full and extended arms; even ears; uninjured ears; a well-formed forehead; a broad forehead; fullness of the head.

body.text: bhramarābhrāścitāḥ ślakṣṇā asaṃluḍitamūrtayaḥ // 8-31 //
body.translated_text: Hair like bees, thick, smooth; a body of undisturbed form. [8-31]

children.translated_text: Hair that is not rough; [a body] that captivates people by its fragrance;
The <s>Śrīvatsa</s> (auspicious mark) and the <s>Svastika</s> — these are held to be the <s>Buddha's</s> secondary marks. [8-32]

body.text: anena sārdhaślaukena sapta / bhramarasadṛśakeśatā citakeśatā ślakṣṇakeśatā asaṃluḍitakeśatā aparuṣakeśatā śrīvatsasvastikanandyāvartalalitapāṇipādatā ceti //
body.translated_text: By this verse-and-a-half, seven [secondary marks]: bee-like hair; thick hair; smooth hair; undisturbed hair; non-rough hair; hands and feet marked with <s>Śrīvatsa</s>, <s>Svastika</s>, and <s>Nandyāvarta</s> patterns.

body.text: sarvaikatvena buddhānāmaśītiranuvyañjanāni //
body.translated_text: Together as one, these are the eighty secondary marks of the <s>Buddhas</s>.

body.text: iti sāmbhogikaḥ kāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus the <s>Sāṃbhogika kāya</s> (enjoyment body).

body.text: nairmāṇikaṃ kāyamadhikṛtya śāstram-
body.translated_text: Regarding the <s>Nairmāṇika kāya</s> (emanation body), the treatise [states] —

children.text: karoti yena citrāṇi hitāni jagataḥ samam /
children.translated_text: That by which he performs various beneficial [deeds] for the world equally,
Uninterrupted from the [beginning of] existence — that is the <s>Nairmāṇika kāya</s> (emanation body) of the <s>Muni</s>. [8-33]

body.text: tathā karmāpyanucchinnamasyā saṃsāramiṣyate /
body.translated_text: Similarly, the uninterrupted activity of this [<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>] in <s>saṃsāra</s> is declared.

body.text: ataḥ sūtram / sarvadharmāparyantatayā prajñāpāramitāparyantatānugantavyeti / yāvantaḥ sthalajalāntarikṣacarāṇāṃ sthāvarajaṅgamānāṃ sattvānāṃ kāyavāksaṃgṛhītā dharmāḥ sattvānāṃ vinayanāya bhagavatā ananteṣu lokadhātuṣu nirmitāḥ te sarvadharmāsteṣāmaparyantatayā bhagavataḥ prajñāyā aparyantatā veditavyā / katamasyāḥ te nirmitāḥ? śūnyatāparyantatayā prajñāpāramitāparyantatānugantavyeti / yathā tathāgatena nirmitāḥ kāyā anantāstathā teṣāṃ śūnyatāpyanantā / kena śūnyatā? svādhīnaiścicaitasikairmāyāpuruṣavat / atastasyāpi aparyantatayāparyantateti pūrvavat / yathā teṣāṃ kāyavācau nirmite tathā cittacaitasikā api kinna nirmīyante? tadupādānābhāvāt, apūrvasattvāprādurbhāvācca / nanu cittacaitasikanirmāṇamapīṣyate buddhānāṃ /
body.translated_text: Therefore the <s>sūtra</s> [says]: 'Because of the limitlessness of all <s>dharmas</s>, the limitlessness of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be understood.' However many <s>dharmas</s> — comprised of body and speech — of beings moving on land, in water, and in the sky, of stationary and mobile beings, have been emanated by the <s>Bhagavān</s> in infinite world-realms for the disciplining of beings — all those are 'all <s>dharmas</s>'; because of their limitlessness, the limitlessness of the <s>Bhagavān's</s> <s>prajñā</s> should be known. By which [<s>prajñā</s>] are those emanated? 'Because of the limitlessness of emptiness, the limitlessness of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be understood' — just as the bodies emanated by the <s>Tathāgata</s> are infinite, so too their emptiness is infinite. Empty of what? Of mind and mental factors that are self-governed — like a man created by illusion. Therefore, because of its limitlessness, [<s>Prajñāpāramitā's</s>] limitlessness — as before. Just as their bodies and speech are emanated, why are their minds and mental factors not also emanated? Because of the absence of their substratum (<s>upādāna</s>), and because unprecedented beings do not appear. But is not the emanation of mind and mental factors also accepted for the <s>Buddhas</s>?

body.text: "kāyavākcittanirmāṇaprayogopāyakarmakaḥ /"
body.translated_text: 'His activity operates through the means of emanating body, speech, and mind.'

body.text: iti vacanāt / satyamiṣyate / kintu satyupādāne devatādhiṣṭhānena svapnadarśanavat / vācā vāgarthanni(rthani)vedanavacca / ata āha / cittacaritāparyantatayā prajñāpāramitāparyantatānugantavyeti / teṣāṃ ca sattvānāṃ yathā deśitaṃ dharmamālambya prātipakṣikāḥ kuśalā dharmā utpadyante / taiśca teṣāṃ vikṣepakā akuśalā dharmāḥ prahīyante / ata āha / kuśalākuśaladharmāparimāṇatayā prajñāpāramitāparimāṇatānugantavyeti /
body.translated_text: — because of this statement. True, it is accepted. However, it is [only] with the substratum present, through the sustaining power of a deity, like seeing in a dream. And speech too, because of conveying verbal meaning. Therefore he says: 'Because of the limitlessness of the mental conduct [of beings], the limitlessness of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be understood.' And for those beings, as the <s>Dharma</s> is taught, relying on the taught <s>Dharma</s>, antidotal wholesome <s>dharmas</s> arise. And by those, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> that cause their distraction are abandoned. Therefore he says: 'Because of the immeasurability of wholesome and unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>, the immeasurability of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be understood.'

body.text: atha ye nirmitāste kathaṃ bhagavataḥ kāyāḥ? bhagavatā nirmitatvāditi cet / māyākāranirmitā gajādayastarhi māyākārasya kāyāḥ syuḥ, svakāyatvenādhiṣṭhāya tena nirmāṇāt / svakāyavacca gamanavyāhārādiṣu duṣkareṣu vyāpa[ā]raṇāttepi kāyā ityayaṃ bhagavato nairmāṇikaḥ kāyaḥ /
body.translated_text: But if those who are emanated — how are they the bodies of the <s>Bhagavān</s>? If because they are emanated by the <s>Bhagavān</s> — then elephants and the like emanated by a magician would be the bodies of the magician, since he emanates them by projecting his own body. Because, like his own body, they operate in difficult [activities] such as walking, speaking, and the like — those too are [called] bodies. This is the <s>Bhagavān's</s> <s>Nairmāṇika kāya</s> (emanation body).

body.text: uktāstrayaḥ kāyāḥ / kāritramidānīṃ vaktavyam / tatsamāsata āha / siṃhanādanadanatayā prajñāpāramitānugantavyeti / mṛgāṇāmuttamaḥ siṃhaḥ / tatsādharmyāt puruṣottamāḥ puruṣasiṃhā ityucyante / iha tu prakarṣagaterdevamanuṣyādisarvapuruṣottamastathāgataḥ siṃha ityucyate / tasya dharmaḥ sarvāśāparipūraṇatayā sarvaparapravādimṛgabhīṣaṇatayā ca siṃhanāda ityucyate / siṃhadhvajavat / tasya nadano deśakaḥ / tabhdāvastattā / tayā bhagavataḥ prajñā gantavyā pāragamanāt pāramitā veditavyetyarthaḥ / sa punaḥ siṃhanādanadanaḥ saptaviṃśatividhasya kāritradeśanā / sā vistareṇa mahatyorbhagavatyordraṣṭavyā / tāmadhikṛtya śāstram-
body.translated_text: The three bodies have been stated. The function (<s>kāritra</s>) is now to be explained. That he states in summary: 'Because of the lion's roar proclamation, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be understood.' The foremost among animals is the lion. By analogy with that, the foremost among persons are called 'lion among persons.' But here, through the sense of pre-eminence, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, who is the foremost among all persons including gods and humans, is called 'the lion.' His <s>Dharma</s>, because of fulfilling all aspirations and because of frightening all the animals [i.e., proponents] of opposing doctrines, is called 'the lion's roar' — like a lion's banner. Its 'proclamation' (<s>nadana</s>) is the teaching. Its state is its nature. By that, the <s>Bhagavān's</s> <s>prajñā</s> should be understood — [it is] <s>pāramitā</s> because of having gone to the other shore — this is the meaning. And that lion's-roar proclamation is the teaching of the twenty-seven-fold function. That should be seen in detail in the two great <s>Bhagavatīs</s> [texts]. Regarding that, the treatise [states] —

body.text: gatīnāṃ śamanaṃ karma saṃgrahe ca caturvidhe // 8-34 //
body.translated_text: The pacification of the [evil] destinies is the activity; and in the fourfold means of gathering [beings]; [8-34]

children.translated_text: The establishing in [the knowledge of] defilement, in purification, in awakening;
In the true nature of the welfare of beings; and in the six <s>pāramitās</s>; [8-35]
In the <s>Buddha</s>-path; in the natural emptiness; in the destruction of duality;
In conventional designation; in non-apprehension; and in the ripening of embodied beings; [8-36]
In the path of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>; and in the prevention of adherence;
In the attainment of <s>bodhi</s>; in the purification of the <s>Buddha-kṣetra</s> (Buddha-field); regarding certainty; [8-37]
And in the immeasurable welfare of beings; in qualities such as service to the <s>Buddhas</s>;
In the limbs of awakening; in the non-destruction [of wholesome roots]; in the truth-seeing of actions; [8-38]
And in the abandonment of the errors (<s>viparyāsa</s>); in the method of its [the error's] substancelessness;
In purification; in the accumulations; regarding the conditioned and the unconditioned; [8-39]
In the full understanding of the non-differentiation; and in <s>nirvāṇa</s> — the establishing.
This activity of the <s>Dharmakāya</s> is held to be twenty-seven-fold. [8-40]

body.text: bhagavāṃstānvigrahānnirmimīte ye nārakāṇāṃ narakāgninirvāpaṇena dharmadeśanayā ca tathā tiraścāṃ svamāṃsarudhirādidānena tathā pretānāmannapānādidānena dharmadeśanayā ca cittamabhipra sādya tena cābhiprasādena svagatibhyaścyutānāṃ devamanuṣyeṣūpapādayanti / devānapi hīnayānādhimuktikān dharmadeśanayābhiprasādya manuṣyeṣūpapannān yāvacchrāvakabodhau pratyekabodhau ca pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyantīti gatipraśamanakarma //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> emanates those bodies which, for beings in hell, by extinguishing the fires of hell and by teaching the <s>Dharma</s>, and similarly for animals by giving his own flesh, blood, and the like, and similarly for hungry ghosts by giving food, drink, and the like, and by teaching the <s>Dharma</s> — having pleased their minds and through that pleasure, causing those who have fallen from their [evil] destinies to be reborn among gods and humans. Even gods who are inclined toward the lesser vehicle — having pleased them through <s>Dharma</s>-teaching and when they are reborn among humans, they will establish them up to the awakening of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. This is the activity of pacifying the [evil] destinies.

body.text: ye ca manuṣyān bāhyādhyātmikeṣvāmiṣadāneṣu laukikalokotareṣu ca dharmadāneṣu, arthacaryāyāṃ samānārthatāyāṃ ca śikṣayantīti saṅgrahavastuniveśanakarma //
body.translated_text: Those who train humans in external and internal material gifts, and in worldly and supramundane <s>Dharma</s>-gifts, in beneficial conduct, and in the practice of common purpose — this is the activity of establishing [beings] in the [four] means of gathering.

body.text: saṃkleśaḥ kleśāvaraṇaṃ jñeyāvaraṇaṃ ca / vyavadānaṃ tayorastamayaḥ / sa ca pudgaladharmanairātmyajñānāditi saṃvṛtiḥ / paramārthastu [na] dharmadhātoranyadastīti saṃkleśavyavadānajñānaniveśanakarma //
body.translated_text: Defilement (<s>saṃkleśa</s>) is the obscuration of afflictions and the obscuration of the knowable. Purification (<s>vyavadāna</s>) is the subsiding of those two. And that [arises] from the knowledge of the selflessness of the person and of <s>dharmas</s> — this is the conventional [truth]. But the ultimate [truth] is that nothing other than the <s>dharmadhātu</s> exists. This is the activity of establishing [beings] in the knowledge of defilement and purification.

body.text: yathā hi māyākāro vicitrāṇi vastūni yāvabhdakṣyabhojyāni nirmāya lokaṃ toṣayati / sa ca loko na jānāti sarvametadadravyakamiti / yaśca prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carati na sa dharmadhātuvyatiriktaṃ kiñcitpaśyati na sattvaṃ nāpi sattvaprajñaptiṃ dharmāṇāmapi nairātmyāditi sattvārthayāthātmyaniveśanakarma //
body.translated_text: For just as a magician, having created various things including edibles and consumables, gratifies the world — and that world does not know that all this is without substance — so too, one who practices <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> does not see anything apart from the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, neither a being nor even the designation of a being, because of the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s> as well. This is the activity of establishing [beings] in the true nature of the welfare of beings.

body.text: sa ātmanā ca dānaṃ dadāti parāṃśca dāne niyojayati dānasya ca varṇaṃ bhāṣate / ye cānye dānaṃ dadati teṣā ca varṇavādī bhavati samanujñaḥ / evamātmanā ca śīlaṃ rakṣatītyādi vācyamiti ṣaṭpāramitāniveśanakarma //
body.translated_text: He himself practices generosity, and causes others to engage in generosity, and praises the virtues of generosity. And of others who practice generosity, he praises them and approves. Similarly, he himself observes morality, and so on — this should be stated. This is the activity of establishing [beings] in the six <s>pāramitās</s>.

body.text: ātmanā ca daśakuśalān karmapathān samādāya vartate / ātmanā ca pañcaśikṣāpadāni yāvadātmanā ca dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇāśītyanuvyañjanāni niṣpādayatīti vācyamiti buddhamārganiveśanakarma //
body.translated_text: He himself undertakes and abides in the ten wholesome courses of action. He himself [observes] the five training precepts, and so on — he himself accomplishes the thirty-two marks of a great person and the eighty secondary marks — this should be stated. This is the activity of establishing [beings] in the <s>Buddha</s>-path.

body.text: iha bodhisattvaḥ sattvānāṃ pāramitādīn sarvadharmān deśayati / teṣāṃ koṭitrayasya phalasya ca prakṛtiśūnyatāṃ deśayati / te tathā bhāvayanto viśeṣamadhigacchanti /
body.translated_text: Here the <s>Bodhisattva</s> teaches beings all <s>dharmas</s> such as the <s>pāramitās</s> and the like. He teaches them the natural emptiness (<s>prakṛtiśūnyatā</s>) of the three endpoints [beginning, middle, and end] and of their fruit. Those, cultivating thus, attain distinction.

body.text: tataste bhūyasyā mātrayā prakṛtiśūnyatāṃ bhāvayanti yāvadanuttarāṃ samyaksambodhimadhigacchantīti prakṛtiśūnyatāniveśanakarma //
body.translated_text: Then they cultivate natural emptiness to an even greater degree, until they attain unsurpassed perfect awakening. This is the activity of establishing [beings] in natural emptiness.

body.text: prakṛtiśūnyāḥ sarvadharmāḥ na cānyā prakṛtiśūnyatā anye dharmāḥ / kiṃ tarhi? prakṛtiśūnyataiva dharmāḥ / ta eva prakṛtiśūnyatetyadvayadharmaniveśanakarma //
body.translated_text: All <s>dharmas</s> are naturally empty; and natural emptiness is not one thing while <s>dharmas</s> are another. Rather, natural emptiness itself is the <s>dharmas</s>, and those very [<s>dharmas</s>] are natural emptiness. This is the activity of establishing [beings] in the non-dual <s>dharma</s>.

body.text: na samyaksambodhau bhagavatā kaściddharma upalabdhaḥ / yatpunarabhisambudhya dharmā deśitāḥ skandhadhātvādayo vā yāvatsarvākārajñatā vā tatsarvaṃ lokavyavahāreṇeti sāṅketikajñānaniveśanakarma //
body.translated_text: No <s>dharma</s> whatsoever was apprehended by the <s>Bhagavān</s> at [the time of] <s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (perfect awakening). Whatever <s>dharmas</s> were taught after awakening — whether the <s>skandhas</s>, <s>dhātus</s>, and the rest, or up to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects) — all that is by worldly convention. This is the activity of establishing [beings] in conventional knowledge.

body.text: yadi pāramitādiṣu sarvadharmeṣu śikṣate tathāpi samyaksambodhaye na śaknoti / yadi punasteṣveva carati teṣāṃ ca koṭitrayaṃ phalaṃ ca nopalabhate / tadā samyaksambodhaye śaknotītyupalambhaniveśanakarma //
body.translated_text: Even if one trains in all <s>dharmas</s> such as the <s>pāramitās</s> and the rest, one is still unable [to attain] <s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s>. But if one practices those very [<s>dharmas</s>] yet does not apprehend the three endpoints or the fruit of those — then one is able [to attain] <s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s>. This is the activity of establishing [beings] in non-apprehension.

body.text: yadyapi bodhisattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caran sattvaṃ sattvaprajñaptiṃ ca nopalabhate tathāpi saṃvṛtyā paśyati sattvān vastūpalambhena saṃkliṣyamānān / sa tāṃstatprahāṇāya triṣu yāneṣu paripācayatīti sattvaparipākaniveśanakarma //
body.translated_text: Even though the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, does not apprehend a being or the designation of a being, still, conventionally, he sees beings defiled by the apprehension of things as real. He ripens them in the three vehicles for the purpose of their abandoning that [defilement]. This is the activity of establishing [beings] in the ripening of beings.

body.text: sa evamupaparīkṣate / śūnyāḥ sarvadharmāḥ / na ca śūnyatā śūnyatāmabhiniviśate / tasmātsarvadharmeṣvanabhiniviṣṭena bhavitavyam / dānādiṣu caritavyam / na ca teṣu tatphaleṣu vā gantavyamiti sarvābhiniveśaprahāṇaniveśanakarma //
body.translated_text: He examines thus: 'All <s>dharmas</s> are empty. And emptiness does not adhere to emptiness. Therefore, one should abide without adhering to any <s>dharmas</s>. One should practice generosity and the rest, yet one should not cling to them or their fruits.' This is the activity of establishing [beings] in the abandonment of all adherence.

body.text: na mārgeṇa bodhiḥ prāpyate nāmārgeṇa / yato bodhi eva mārgaḥ mārga eva bodhiḥ / bodhisattva eva tarhi buddhaḥ syāditi cet / yadā sarvabuddhadharmān paripūrya vajropamasamādhau sthitvā bodhisattva ekakṣaṇasamāyuktayā prajñayā samyaksambodhimadhigacchati tadā sa eva tathāgataḥ sarvadarśī sarvajña iti nirdiśyata iti bodhiprāptiniveśanakarma //
body.translated_text: <s>Bodhi</s> is not attained by means of the path, nor without the path — because <s>bodhi</s> itself is the path and the path itself is <s>bodhi</s>. 'Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> himself would be a <s>Buddha</s>' — if so [objected], [the answer is]: when, having fulfilled all <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> and standing in the <s>vajropama samādhi</s> (diamond-like concentration), the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, by <s>prajñā</s> unified in a single moment, attains <s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s> — then that very one is designated as '<s>Tathāgata</s>, the all-seeing, the omniscient.' This is the activity of establishing [beings] in the attainment of <s>bodhi</s>.

body.text: sa ātmanaḥ pareṣāṃ ca daśākuśalasaṃgṛhītāni dauḥśīlyāni ṣaṭpāramitāvipakṣāṃśca hīnayānaphalānāṃ ca pañcānāṃ sākṣātkriyāspṛhayoravakāśaṃ, skandhadhātvādisāśravānāśravasarvadharmasaṃjñādauṣṭhulyāni ca nivārya svayaṃ ca pāramitādiṣu sarvakuśaladharmeṣu pratiṣṭhito bhavati parānapi pratiṣṭhāpayati / tacca kuśalamūlaṃ sarvasattvasādhāraṇakṛtvā ātmanaḥ samyaksambodhau ca sarvākārāyāṃ ca svabuddhakṣetrapariśuddhau pariṇāmayati / praṇidhānāni ca buddhakṣetrapariśuddhaye yathā sūtraṃ karotīti buddhakṣetrapariśuddhiniveśanakarma //
body.translated_text: He prevents, for himself and others, the moral failings comprised in the ten unwholesome [courses of action], the adversaries of the six <s>pāramitās</s>, and the opportunity for craving the direct realization of the five [inferior] fruits of the lesser vehicle, as well as the unwholesome tendencies of perception regarding all <s>dharmas</s> — both defiled and undefiled — such as <s>skandhas</s>, <s>dhātus</s>, and the rest. And he himself abides established in all wholesome <s>dharmas</s> such as the <s>pāramitās</s> and the like, and establishes others as well. And having made that wholesome root common to all beings, he dedicates it toward his own <s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s> and toward the complete purification of his own <s>Buddha-kṣetra</s> in all aspects. And he makes vows for the purification of the <s>Buddha-kṣetra</s> according to the <s>sūtra</s>. This is the activity of establishing [beings] in the purification of the <s>Buddha-kṣetra</s>.

body.text: prathamacittotpādika eva bodhisattvaḥ samyaksambodhau niyato bhavati / niyatasya kathamapāyeṣūpapattiriti cet / yaḥ samyaksambodhau cittamutpādya ṣaṭsu pāramitāsu caturṣu vāpramāṇeṣu carati daśa cākuśalān dharmān prahāya tiṣṭhati /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> is determined toward <s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s> from the very first generation of the mind [of awakening]. 'If he is determined, how can there be rebirth in the evil destinies?' — if so [asked]: one who, having generated the mind toward <s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s>, practices the six <s>pāramitās</s> and the four immeasurables, and abides having abandoned the ten unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> —

body.text: aṣṭau tasyākṣaṇā na sambhavanti kiṃ punarapāyopapattiḥ / kathaṃ tarhi tiryagyonau jātakāni? tāni sāśravānāśravasarvakuśaladharmasamanvāgatasya sattvārthā(rtha) vaśitayā saṃcintyopapattayo na ca tiryagduḥkhavedanāḥ / tadyathā tathāgataḥ paramavaśitvalābhātsarvalokadhātuṣu yugapadanantānātmabhāvān parārthāya nirmimīta iti samyaksambodhiniyataniveśanakarma //
body.translated_text: For him the eight inopportune states do not occur — how much less rebirth in the evil destinies? 'How then are there birth-stories (<s>Jātakas</s>) in the animal realm?' Those are deliberate rebirths, for the welfare of beings, by one who possesses all defiled and undefiled wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, through mastery — and they do not involve the experience of animal suffering. Just as the <s>Tathāgata</s>, through the attainment of supreme mastery, simultaneously emanates infinite bodies in all world-realms for the welfare of others. This is the activity of establishing [beings] in the certainty of <s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s>.

body.text: sa hi prajñāpāramitāyāṃ sthitvā daśasu dikṣu gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu sattvānāmartha karoti na ca lipyate / tathā hi yaḥ spṛśet, yena spṛśet, yaṃ ca spṛśet, trīnimāndharmānasau nopalabhate śūnyatāyāṃ ca sthitaḥ sarvaśukladharmeṣu sthito bhavati / tayaiva teṣāṃ saṅgrāt / tathāhi sarvadharmāḥ sarvadharmaiḥ śūnyāḥ / tataḥ śūnyatāyāmantarbhūtā ityaprameyasattvārthaniveśanakarma //
body.translated_text: For he, abiding in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, works for the welfare of beings in the ten directions, [as numerous as] the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, yet is not tainted. For he does not apprehend these three <s>dharmas</s>: the one who touches, that by which he touches, and that which is touched. And abiding in emptiness, he abides in all wholesome <s>dharmas</s> — because of their inclusion within that very [emptiness]. For all <s>dharmas</s> are empty of all <s>dharmas</s>; therefore they are contained within emptiness. This is the activity of establishing [beings] in the immeasurable welfare of beings.

body.text: sa evaṃ nirūpayati / ye te daśasu dikṣu gaṅgānadīvālukopamā lokadhātavo ye ca teṣu tathāgatāḥ sarve te svabhāvena śūnyāḥ kevalaṃ nāmasaṅketena prajñapyate / sāpi prajñaptiḥ svabhāvena śūnyā / yadi tu kasyacicchūnyatā na syāt prādeśikī syāt / yatastu na pradeśikī tataḥ sarvadharmāḥ sarvadharmaśūnyā iti / sa evaṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ sthitvā ṣaḍabhijñā abhinirharati / yāsu sthitvā daśadiksarvatathāgatānupasaṃkrāmati paryupāste tebhyaśca dharma śṛṇoti teṣu ca kuśalamūlānyavaropayatyanabhiniviṣṭaḥ / na hi śūnyatāṃ śūnyatāyāmabhiniviśate / sa divyena cakṣuṣā daśadiglokadhātuṣu sattvān dṛṣṭvā sadyo 'bhijñayā tatra gatvā tebhyo dharmaṃ deśayati / divyena śrotradhātunā daśadiksarvabuddhānāṃ dharmadeśanāṃ śrutvodgṛhya sattvebhyo deśayati / cetaḥparyāyajñānena sattvānāṃ cittāni viditvā yathācittamebhyo dharma deśayati / so 'nekavidhaṃ pūrvanivāsamātmanaḥ pareṣāṃ cānusmarati / pūrvatathāgatadeśitāṃśca dharmānanusmṛtyatadvineyebhyaḥ sattvebhyo deśayati / sa āśravakṣayajñānena sattvānāmanurūpaṃ dharmaṃ deśayati / sa tābhirabhijñābhiryaṃ yamevākāṃkṣatyātmabhāvaṃ sattvānāmarthāya pratigrahītuṃ taṃ tameva pratigṛṇhāti / na ca tatra sukhaduḥkhānunayapratighairūpalipyata iti daśadigbuddhopāsanādiniveśanakarma //
body.translated_text: He investigates thus: 'Whatever world-realms in the ten directions are as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, and whatever <s>Tathāgatas</s> are in them — all of those are empty by nature. They are designated merely by conventional name. And even that designation is empty by nature. But if the emptiness of anything were absent, it would be partial. Since, however, it is not partial, all <s>dharmas</s> are empty of all <s>dharmas</s>.' He, thus abiding in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, brings forth the six <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges). Established in those, he approaches all <s>Tathāgatas</s> in the ten directions, attends upon them, hears the <s>Dharma</s> from them, and plants wholesome roots in their presence — without adhering. For emptiness does not adhere to emptiness. With the divine eye, seeing beings in the world-realms of the ten directions, he instantly goes there by supernatural power and teaches them the <s>Dharma</s>. With the divine ear-element, having heard the <s>Dharma</s>-teaching of all <s>Buddhas</s> in the ten directions and having grasped it, he teaches it to beings. With the knowledge of others' minds, knowing the minds of beings, he teaches them the <s>Dharma</s> according to their minds. He recollects many kinds of previous lives, both his own and others'. And recollecting the <s>dharmas</s> taught by previous <s>Tathāgatas</s>, he teaches them to beings who are to be disciplined by those [teachings]. With the knowledge of the destruction of the outflows, he teaches beings the appropriate <s>Dharma</s>. With those superknowledges, whatever form of existence he wishes to assume for the welfare of beings — that very one he assumes. And he is not tainted there by attraction or aversion toward pleasure and suffering. This is the activity of establishing [beings] in the service of the <s>Buddhas</s> of the ten directions and the like.

body.text: kāni punarbodhisattvasya bodhyaṅgāni? ṣaṭpāramitāścatvāri dhyānāni yāvadāveṇikā buddhadharmāḥ / yadi teṣu carati koṭitrayaṃ ca teṣāṃ nopalabhate / yadi cātmanaḥ samyaksambodhaye sarvasattvānāṃ cāgratāyai tān samyakpariṇāmayati / yadyamī bodhisattvadharmāḥ katame tarhi buddhadharmāḥ? eta eva / yadyobhaḥ sarvākārajñatāmabhisambudhyate prahīṇasarvavāsanānusandhiśca bhavati, ekakṣaṇasamāyuktayā ca prajñayā sarvabuddhadharmānabhisambudhyate / na caivaṃ bodhisattva iti bodhyaṅganiveśanakarma //
body.translated_text: What then are the limbs of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅgas</s>) of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>? The six <s>pāramitās</s>, the four <s>dhyānas</s>, up to the distinctive <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>. If he practices those and does not apprehend the three endpoints of those — and if he rightly dedicates them toward his own <s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s> and toward being foremost among all beings — if these are <s>Bodhisattva</s>-dharmas, then which are <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>? These very same. When one fully awakens to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects) and has the continuity of all latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) severed, and by <s>prajñā</s> unified in a single moment fully awakens to all <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> — but a <s>Bodhisattva</s> is not like that. This is the activity of establishing [beings] in the limbs of awakening.

body.text: yadyapi svalakṣaṇaśūnyāḥ sarvadharmāstathāpyasti karma, asti teṣāṃ phalam / na hi sattvāḥ svalakṣaṇaśūnyān dharmān jānanti / ajānantaḥ pudgalaṃ dharmāṃśca kalpayantaḥ karmābhisaṃskurvanti sucaritaṃ duścaritaṃ vā / duścaritena triṣvapāyeṣu patanti / sucaritairdevamanuṣyeṣūpapadyante / kecitpunaḥ pudgalanairātmyaṃ parijñāya sugatidurgatīḥ prahāya nirvāṇamadhigacchanti / bodhisattvāḥ pāramitādīn kuśalān dharmānparipūrayantaḥ krameṇa daśabhūmīnadhigamyaikakṣaṇasamāyuktayā prajñāyā sarvadharmānabhisambudhya buddhā bhagavanto bhavantīti karmaphalasambandhāvipraṇāśananiveśanakarma //
body.translated_text: Even though all <s>dharmas</s> are empty of their own characteristics, nevertheless there is action (<s>karma</s>) and there is the fruit of those [actions]. For beings do not know <s>dharmas</s> that are empty of their own characteristics. Not knowing, they imagine a person and <s>dharmas</s>, and produce karmic formations — either good conduct or bad conduct. Through bad conduct they fall into the three evil destinies. Through good conduct they are reborn among gods and humans. And some, having fully understood the selflessness of the person, abandon the happy and unhappy destinies and attain <s>nirvāṇa</s>. <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, fulfilling wholesome <s>dharmas</s> such as the <s>pāramitās</s>, gradually realize the ten stages, and by <s>prajñā</s> unified in a single moment, having fully awakened to all <s>dharmas</s>, become <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bhagavāns</s>. This is the activity of establishing [beings] in the non-destruction of the connection between action and fruit.

body.text: na bodhisattvaḥ satyaiḥ satyajñānairvā nirvāti / kintarhi? catuḥsatyasamatayā / yā teṣāṃ samatā tathatā niḥsvabhāvatā sā na kaściddharmamupalabhate satyaparyāpannamanyaṃ vā / tataḥ sarvadharmāḥ śūnyā iti paśyanniyāyamamavakramya gotrabhūmau sthito bhavati dhyānānyutpādayatyapramāṇānyārūpyasamāpattīśca / sa iha śamathabhūmau sthitvā duḥkhaṃ parijānāti samudayaṃ prajahāti nirodhaṃ sākṣātkaroti mārgaṃ bhāvayati / na ca satyārambaṇaṃ cittamutpādayati / kevalaṃ bodhinimnena cittena svalakṣaṇaśūnyānsarvadharmān paśyati / so 'nayā vipaśyanayā sarvadharmaśūnyatāṃ paśyati / upāyakauśalyena ca dharmaṃ deśayatīti catuḥsatyadarśananiveśanakarma //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not attain <s>nirvāṇa</s> through the truths or through the knowledge of the truths. Rather, through the equality of the four truths. That equality of those — <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), lack of intrinsic nature — that does not apprehend any <s>dharma</s> included in the truths or otherwise. Therefore, seeing that all <s>dharmas</s> are empty, abiding on the <s>gotra-bhūmi</s> (lineage-stage) without entering the fixed course [of the <s>Śrāvakas</s>], he generates the <s>dhyānas</s>, the immeasurables, and the formless attainments. Standing on this ground of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding), he fully understands suffering, abandons the origin, directly realizes cessation, and cultivates the path. Yet he does not generate a mind that takes the truths as its object. Rather, with a mind inclined toward awakening, he sees all <s>dharmas</s> as empty of their own characteristics. With this <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight), he sees the emptiness of all <s>dharmas</s>. And through skill in means, he teaches the <s>Dharma</s>. This is the activity of establishing [beings] in the seeing of the four truths.

body.text: "maitreya āha / yadi bhagavannabhāvasvabhāvāḥ sarvadharmā kathaṃ bodhisattvena rūpādau śikṣitavyaṃ yāvadbuddhadharmeṣu? bhagavānāha / nāmamātratayā / āha / saṃskāranimittena vastunā avastukaṃ nāmakathanaṃ nāmamātram / saṃskāro vikalpaḥ / tasya nimittaṃ viṣayaḥ / yatraivaṃ bhavati / idaṃ rūpamiyaṃ vedanā yāvadamī buddhadharmā iti bhāvaḥ // bhagavānāha // āgantukametannāmadheyamatra prakṣiptam / idaṃ rūpaṃ yāvadamī buddhadharmā iti / nāmābhedena nāmā ca (? nāmyartha)pratīteḥ / tasmādalīkaḥ śabdārtho vyavahāramātraṃ na vastu // āha // vyavahāramātratāpi rūpasya svabhāva eveti / rūpasvabhāva upalabdha eva bhavati / bhagavānāha / na rūpasya svabhāva eveti / rūpasvabhāva upalabdha eva bhavati / bhagavānāha / na tasyotpādanirodhau tato na sa svabhāvaḥ // āha // kiṃ punarbhagavan sarvaśaḥ svalakṣaṇena na santyeva rūpādayo yāvadbuddhadharmāḥ? bhagavānāha / santi lokasaṅketavyavahārato na nu paramārthataḥ // āha // yathāhaṃ bhagavato bhāṣitasyārthamājānāmi / anabhilāpya eṣa dhātuḥ paramārthataḥ / sacetsaskāranimittaṃ vastu sa evānabhilāpyo dhāturiti vyāhatametat //
body.translated_text: "<s>Maitreya</s> said: 'If, <s>Bhagavān</s>, all <s>dharmas</s> are without the nature of existence, how should the <s>Bodhisattva</s> train in form and the rest, up to the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'By [understanding them as] mere names.' He said: 'A name-designation of a substanceless [thing] by means of a thing that is a sign of formation — that is a mere name. Formation is conceptualization. Its sign is the object. Where it is thus: "This is form, this is feeling, up to these are <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>" — this is the sense.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'This name is adventitious, cast here — "This is form," up to "these are <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>." Because through non-differentiation of name [and meaning], the meaning of the name is cognized. Therefore the referent of the word is false — it is mere convention, not a [real] thing.' He said: 'But even being-mere-convention is the very nature of form. [Then] the nature of form would be apprehended indeed.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'There is no arising or cessation of that; therefore it is not a [real] nature.' He said: 'But, <s>Bhagavān</s>, do form and the rest up to <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> not exist at all in every respect by their own characteristics?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'They exist by worldly conventional usage, but not ultimately.' He said: 'As I understand the meaning of the <s>Bhagavān's</s> statement, this element (<s>dhātu</s>) is ultimately inexpressible. If the thing that is the sign of formation is itself the inexpressible element, this is contradictory.'

body.text: bhagavānāha // yadāte 'nabhilāpye dhātau prajñāpracāro bhavatyupalabhase / tadā saṃskāranimittaṃ vastu / āha / nohīti // bhagavānāha // ata eva na tattasmādanyannāpyananyata / adyanyat kutastadā vinaṣṭam / athānanyat kuto nopalabhyate / api ca / yadyasau saṃskāranimittādanyaḥ syādapīdānī sarvabālapṛthagjanāḥ parinirvāyuḥ samyaksambodhiṃ
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'When you have the operation of <s>prajñā</s> in the inexpressible element, do you apprehend [anything]? When there is a thing that is the sign of formation —' He said: 'No indeed.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Precisely for this reason, that is neither different from it, nor is it also non-different. If it were different, then even now all foolish ordinary persons would attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> and <s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s>.

body.text:
cābhisambudhyeran / athānanyaḥ syādapīdānīṃ tadapi nimittaṃ nopalabhyeta // āha // anabhilāpyadhātūpanibaddhe prajñāpracāre vartamāne yadi saṃskāranimittaṃ nopalabhyate tatkimasannopalabhyate sadvā? bhagavānāha / yadi vikalpato grahaṇameti na vikalpeṣvapagateṣu tadā parikalpamātraṃ taditi na tasya sattvamasattvaṃ vā / āha / katibhirākārairbhagavan dharmāṇāṃ prajñaptiḥ? tribhirmaitreya / yaduta parikalpitaṃ rūpaṃ vikalpitaṃ rūpaṃ dharmatā rūpam / yāvatparikalpitā buddhadharmāḥ / vikalpitā buddhadharmāḥ / dharmatā buddhadharmā iti / tatra yā saṃskāranimitte vastuni rūpamiti nāmasaṅketavyavahāraṃ niśritya rūpasvabhāvatayā parikalpanā tatparikalpitaṃ rūpam / yattasya saṃskāranimittasya vikalpamātratāyāmavasthānaṃ tadvikalpitaṃ rūpam / yā punastena parikalpitena rūpeṇa tasya vikalpitarūpasya nityakālaṃ niḥsvabhāvatā nairātmyaṃ tathatā bhūtakoṭistaddharmatārūpam / evaṃ yāvatparikalpitavikalpitadharmatākhyā buddhadharmāḥ / tatra parikalpitaṃ rūpamadravyam / vikalpitaṃ sadravyaṃ vikalpitasadravyatayā, na svatantravṛttitaḥ / dharmatārūpaṃ naivādravyaṃ na sadravyaṃ dharmatāprabhāvitam / evaṃ yāvadbuddhadharmāḥ / āha / yaduktaṃ bhagavatā / advayasyaiṣā gaṇanā kṛtā yaduta rūpamiti yāvadbuddhadharmā iti tatkatham? bhagavānāha / yatkalpitaṃ rūpaṃ na tadrūpaṃ niḥsvabhāvatvāt / na cārūpaṃ vyavahārataḥ / yadvikalpitaṃ rūpaṃ na tadrūpaṃ svatantravṛttitaḥ / na cārūpaṃ vikalpitarūpatvāt / yaddharmatārūpaṃ na tadrūpaṃ rūpavivekatvāt / na cārūpaṃ rūpaparamārthatvāt / tasmādadvayasyaiṣā gaṇanā rūpamiti yāvadbuddhadharmā iti // āha // evamantadvayaṃ prahāya madhyamāpratipadaṃ pratipannasya rūpe yāvadbuddhadharmeṣu kathaṃ lakṣaṇaparijñā lakṣaṇaprahāṇa lakṣaṇasākṣātkriyā lakṣaṇabhāvanā ca? bhagavānāha // rūpasya yanna parijñānaṃ nāparijñānaṃ tadevāsya parijñānam
/ evaṃ yāvadyā bhāvanā nābhāvanā saiva bhāvanā / evaṃ yāvadbuddhadharmāṇām // āha // evaṃ parijñādisamanvāgatasya bodhisattvasya katamannirvāṇam? bhagavānāha / gambhīrameṣāṃ nirvāṇaṃ yato na tannirvāṇaṃ nānirvāṇam / tatkatham? yataḥ parānārabhya saṃsārāparityāga eṣāṃ na nirvāṇam / ātmānamārabhya nirvāṇāparityāga eṣāṃ nirvāṇam / ekātyāga itaratyāgādayukta ubhayoratyāga iti cet / ubhayoravikalpanādubhābhyāṃ nodvijate / tato yukta ubhayoratyāgaḥ / sa tarhi saṃsarati nirvāti ceti na yuktam? yadvodhisattvasya cittavaśitāprāptasyopāyakauśalyena saṃsārasaṃdarśanaṃ so 'sya saṃsārāparityāgaḥ / yā śūnyatā yā cānupalambhapratiṣṭhānatā so 'sya nirvāṇāparityāgaḥ // āha // avikalpanāyāḥ samastaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ katamat? bhagavānāha / ye ca rūpādayaḥ sarvadharmāḥ / yā ca teṣāṃ śūnyatā / yā ca teṣāṃ tasyāśca bhāvābhāvādvayatā / yā cāprapañcanā /
body.translated_text: would also realize. Or if it were other [than the cause], even so, the cause (<s>nimitta</s>) would not be apprehended. // He asks: // When the activity of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) proceeds in connection with the inexpressible element (<s>anabhilāpyadhātu</s>), if the cause characterized by <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) is not apprehended — is it that it is apprehended as non-existent, or as existent? The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: If the apprehension comes through conceptualization, then when conceptualizations have ceased, it is mere imagination — therefore there is neither its existence nor non-existence. // He asks: // In how many modes, <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the designation (<s>prajñapti</s>) of <s>dharmas</s>? In three, <s>Maitreya</s>: namely, imagined form (<s>parikalpita rūpa</s>), conceptualized form (<s>vikalpita rūpa</s>), and the form of <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature). Up to: imagined <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>, conceptualized <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>, and <s>dharmatā Buddha-dharmas</s>. Therein, the imagination of something as having the nature of form, based on the conventional usage of the name 'form' with respect to a thing that serves as a cause of <s>saṃskāras</s> — that is 'imagined form.' That which is the abiding of that <s>saṃskāra</s>-cause in the state of being mere conceptualization — that is 'conceptualized form.'
