And that which is the eternal naturelessness, selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>), suchness (<s>tathatā</s>), reality-limit (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>) of that conceptualized form through that imagined form — that is the 'form of <s>dharmatā</s>.' Thus up to: <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> designated as imagined, conceptualized, and <s>dharmatā</s>. Therein, imagined form is without substance (<s>adravya</s>). Conceptualized [form] has substance insofar as it is a conceptualized substance, not through independent existence. The form of <s>dharmatā</s> is neither without substance nor with substance — it is empowered by <s>dharmatā</s>. Thus up to <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>. // He asks: // What was said by the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'This enumeration of the non-dual has been made — namely, form, up to <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>' — how is that? The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: What is imagined form is not [truly] form, because of naturelessness; nor is it non-form, from the standpoint of conventional usage. What is conceptualized form is not [truly] form, from the standpoint of independent existence; nor is it non-form, because of being conceptualized form. What is <s>dharmatā</s>-form is not [truly] form, because of being the differentiation of form [from its true nature]; nor is it non-form, because of being the ultimate reality of form. Therefore, this enumeration of the non-dual [is established] — 'form, up to <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>.' // He asks: // For one who has thus abandoned both extremes and entered the middle path without [fixed] position — how is there, with respect to form up to <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>, full knowledge of the characteristic, abandonment of the characteristic, direct realization of the characteristic, and cultivation of the characteristic? The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: // That which is neither full knowledge nor non-full-knowledge of form — that itself is its full knowledge. Thus up to: that which is neither cultivation nor non-cultivation — that itself is cultivation. Thus up to <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>. // He asks: // For a <s>bodhisattva</s> thus endowed with full knowledge and the rest, what is <s>nirvāṇa</s>? The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: Profound is the <s>nirvāṇa</s> of these [bodhisattvas], for it is neither <s>nirvāṇa</s> nor non-<s>nirvāṇa</s>. How so? Because their non-abandonment of <s>saṃsāra</s> for the sake of others is [their] non-<s>nirvāṇa</s>; their non-abandonment of <s>nirvāṇa</s> for their own sake is [their] <s>nirvāṇa</s>. If [one objects:] 'the abandonment of one [entails] the abandonment of the other — therefore the abandonment of both is impossible' — because of non-conceptualization of both, one is not distressed by either; therefore the abandonment of both is justified. [Objection:] 'Then it is not justified that he both transmigrates and attains <s>nirvāṇa</s>?' When a <s>bodhisattva</s> who has attained mastery of mind shows the appearance of <s>saṃsāra</s> through skillful means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>) — that is his non-abandonment of <s>saṃsāra</s>. Whatever is emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) and whatever is the stance of non-apprehension — that is his non-abandonment of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. // He asks: // What is the complete characteristic of non-conceptualization? The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: Whatever are the <s>dharmas</s> beginning with form; whatever is their emptiness; whatever is the non-duality of existence and non-existence of them and of that [emptiness]; and whatever is [their] freedom from conceptual elaboration —

body.text:
idamavikalpanāyāḥ samastaṃ lakṣaṇam // āha // kinnu bhagavan sarveṣāṃ śrāvakāṇāmekāntena nirvāṇapratiṣṭhā bhavati? bhagavānāha / nānādhātuke loke nānābhūtāḥ sattvā nānāgotraprakṛutayaḥ / asti sā gotrajātiryā ādita eva praṇītaṃ viśeṣaṃ prārthayate / tamevādhigacchati / asti yā hīnaṃ viśeṣaṃ prārthayate / tamevādhigacchati / tenaiva santuṣyati / sa śamaikāyanaḥ śrāvakaḥ / asti yo hīnaṃ viśeṣa prārthayate / tamevādhigacchati na ca tāvatā santuṣyati / uttaripraṇītaṃ viśeṣaṃ prārthayate / sa bodhipariṇatikaḥ śrāvakaḥ / so 'rhattva prāpya cireṇa samyaksambodhiṃ prāpnoti / tasya tatprāptaye yā upapattayo na tāḥ karmakleśavaśena / api tvacintyāṃ nirvāṇapāragāminīmarhato 'pyupapattiṃ prajñapayāmi yā prathamā gotrajātiḥ sā bodhisattvānām // āha // āścaryaṃ bhagavan yāvadudārāśayā bodhisattvā māhātmyāśayāśca // bhagavānāha // yadamī śakratvalokapālatvacakravartitvādibhiḥ sarvalokasampattibhiranarthino 'nuttarāyāṃ bodhau kuśalaṃ pariṇāmayanti / tāsu ca niḥsaṅgatā niravagrahatā ca / iyameṣānudārāśayatā / yatpunastadaśa(sa)ktisukhamanavagrahasukhaṃ nirvṛtisukhaṃ ca tatsarva sarvasattvasādhāraṇamicchanto 'nuttarāyāṃ bodhau kuśalamūlaṃ pariṇāmayanti saṃsārāparityāgatayā / iyameṣāṃ māhātmyāśayatā // āha // āścaryādbhūtā bhagavan bodhisattvadharmāḥ / tān prāptukāmairanuttarāyāṃ samyaksambodhau cittamutpādayitavyam / ita ūrdhvam // subhūtirāha // abhāvasvabhāveṣu sarvadharmeṣu kathaṃ karmaphalavyavastheti // bhagavānāha // dharmāṇāmabhāvasvabhāvamajānantaḥ sattvā viparyāsasamutthitairvikalpaiḥ karmāṇi kṛtvā yathākarmaphalāni prāpnuvanti / " tatra catvāro viparyāsāḥ pudlanairātmyavipakṣaḥ / bhāveṣvabhiniveśo dharmanairātmyavipakṣaḥ / atra ca maitreyapraśnottarairvahavo viparyāsā nirastāḥ
/ subhūtipraśnottaraiḥ katicit / iti viparyāsaprahāṇaniveśanakarma //
body.translated_text: this is the complete characteristic of non-conceptualization. // He asks: // Is it the case, <s>Bhagavān</s>, that all <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers) invariably abide in <s>nirvāṇa</s>? The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: In a world of diverse elements, beings are of diverse natures and diverse dispositions (<s>gotra</s>). There is that class of disposition which from the very beginning aspires to an exalted distinction — and attains it. There is [a class] which aspires to a lesser distinction — and attains it; and is satisfied with that alone. That one, whose sole path is tranquility, is a <s>śrāvaka</s>. There is one who aspires to a lesser distinction and attains it, but is not satisfied with that alone — [and] aspires to a further, more exalted distinction. That one is a <s>śrāvaka</s> destined for awakening (<s>bodhipariṇātika</s>). He, having attained <s>arhatship</s>, in due course attains perfect complete awakening (<s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). And those rebirths of his that lead to that attainment are not due to the force of <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions); rather, I designate an inconceivable rebirth that leads beyond <s>nirvāṇa</s>, even for an <s>arhat</s>. That first class of disposition belongs to the <s>bodhisattvas</s>. // He asks: // Wonderful, <s>Bhagavān</s>, how exalted are the aspirations of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, and how great their aspirations! // The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: // That these [bodhisattvas], not desiring all worldly prosperities such as the status of <s>Śakra</s>, world-guardianship, universal sovereignty, and the like, dedicate their wholesome [roots] to unsurpassed awakening — and have non-attachment and non-grasping toward those [prosperities] — this is their exalted aspiration. And that they, desiring that all the happiness of non-attachment, non-grasping, and cessation be shared equally by all beings, dedicate their roots of wholesome [merit] to unsurpassed awakening through non-abandonment of <s>saṃsāra</s> — this is their great aspiration. // He asks: // Wonderful and marvelous, <s>Bhagavān</s>, are the qualities of <s>bodhisattvas</s>! Those who wish to attain them should generate the thought of unsurpassed perfect awakening. From this point onward: // <s>Subhūti</s> asks: // In all <s>dharmas</s> whose nature is non-existence, how is the determination of <s>karma</s> and its result [possible]? // The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: // Beings who do not know the nature of non-existence of <s>dharmas</s>, performing <s>karmas</s> through conceptualizations arisen from distortion (<s>viparyāsa</s>), obtain results according to their <s>karmas</s>. Therein, the four distortions are: [1] clinging to persons — the opponent of <s>pudgalanairātmya</s> (selflessness of persons); [2] clinging to [the reality of] entities — the opponent of <s>dharmanairātmya</s> (selflessness of phenomena). And here, by the questions and answers of <s>Maitreya</s>, many distortions have been eliminated; by the questions and answers of <s>Subhūti</s>, some [more]. Thus [ends] the action of eliminating and establishing distortion. //

body.text: viparyāsena sattvāḥ karmābhisaṃskurvanti / tataḥ saṃkliśyante ca lokavyavahāreṇa na paramārthataḥ / na hi kiñcidvastvasti vālāgrakoṭīnikṣepamātrakamapi yatra sthitvā karma kuryuḥ / tadyathā svapnamāyādiṣviti viparyāsanirvastukatājñānaniveśanakarma //
body.translated_text: Through distortion, beings fashion <s>karmas</s> (actions); from that they are defiled — conventionally, not in ultimate reality. For there is not the slightest thing, not even to the extent of the tip of a hair, wherein standing they might perform <s>karma</s>. Just as in dreams, illusions, and the like — thus [ends] the action of establishing the insubstantiality of distortion and ignorance. //

body.text: yā sarvadharmāṇāṃ samatā tathatā bhūtakoṭistanirvāṇam / tacca lokavyavahāreṇa vyavahriyate na paramārthato 'nabhilāpyatvāditi vyavadānaniveśanakarma //
body.translated_text: The equality of all <s>dharmas</s>, <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), the reality-limit (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>) — that is their <s>nirvāṇa</s>. And that is spoken of conventionally, not in ultimate reality, because of its inexpressibility — thus [ends] the action of establishing purification (<s>vyavadāna</s>). //

body.text: yadyapi svapnamāyopamāḥ sarvadharmā nirvastukāstathāpi tadajānantaḥ sattvā vastvabhiniveśena karmāṇi kṛtvā sugatidurgati gacchanti / atasteṣāṃ viparyāsaprahāṇāya bodhisattvo bodhau cittamutpādya saṃsāre carati / yāvadabhisambudhya sattvān parimocayatīti vyavadānasambhāraniveśanakarma //
body.translated_text: Although all <s>dharmas</s> are like dreams and illusions, insubstantial, nevertheless beings who do not know this, having performed <s>karmas</s> through clinging to [their] substantiality, go to fortunate or unfortunate rebirths. Therefore, for the elimination of their distortion, the <s>bodhisattva</s>, having generated the thought of awakening, moves through <s>saṃsāra</s> — until, having fully awakened, he liberates beings. Thus [ends] the action of establishing the equipment for purification (<s>vyavadāna-sambhāra</s>). //

body.text: "bhagavānāha // na dvayenābhisamayo nādvayena ! eṣa evātrābhisamayo yatra na dvayaṃ nādvayam // tatkasya hetoḥ? prapañco eṣa yo 'yameṣāmabhisamayaḥ / na ca dharmasamatāyāṃ prapañcosti / niṣprapañcā dharmasamatā / saiva sarvadharmāḥ / saiva sarvapṛthagjanāryapudgalāḥ / saiva buddharatnaṃ saṃgharatnaṃ ca / samatā hi dharmatā / na ca dharmatāyā nānātvamasti // subhūtirāha / kiṃ dharmatā saṃskṛtā kiṃ asaṃskṛtā // bhagavānāha // na saṃskṛtā nāsaṃskṛtā / yaśca saṃskṛto dhāturyaścāsaṃskṛta ubhāvetau na saṃyuktau na visaṃyuktau na rūpiṇau anidarśanāvapratighāvekalakṣaṇau yadutālakṣaṇau" iti saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtāvyatibhedena jñānaniveśanakarma //
body.translated_text: "The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: // Realization (<s>abhisamaya</s>) is neither through duality nor through non-duality. This very realization is that in which there is neither duality nor non-duality. // For what reason? Conceptual elaboration (<s>prapañca</s>) is this — namely, their realization [if posited as dual or non-dual]. And in the equality of <s>dharmas</s> there is no conceptual elaboration. The equality of <s>dharmas</s> is free from elaboration. That itself is all <s>dharmas</s>. That itself is all ordinary persons and noble individuals. That itself is the <s>Buddha-jewel</s> and the <s>Saṅgha-jewel</s>. For equality is <s>dharmatā</s> (the true nature); and of <s>dharmatā</s> there is no plurality." // <s>Subhūti</s> asks: Is <s>dharmatā</s> conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>) or unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>)? // The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: // Neither conditioned nor unconditioned. And whatever is the conditioned element and whatever is the unconditioned element — these two are neither conjoined nor disjoined, formless, non-demonstrable, without resistance, of one characteristic — namely, characteristiclessness." Thus [ends] the action of knowledge through the non-differentiation of conditioned and unconditioned. //

body.text: "bhagavānāha // sarvadharmāḥ subhūte svabhāvena śūnyāḥ / te na śrāvakairna pratyekabuddhairna tathāgataiḥ kṛtāḥ / yā ca svabhāvaśūnyatā tannirvāṇaṃ" iti nirvāṇaniveśanakarma //
body.translated_text: "The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: // All <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, are empty by nature. They are not made by <s>śrāvakas</s>, nor by <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, nor by <s>Tathāgatas</s>. And that which is emptiness of own-nature — that is their <s>nirvāṇa</s>." Thus [ends] the action of establishing <s>nirvāṇa</s>. //

body.text: kāritrasyaiva vyāpitvaṃ darśayitumāha / sarvadharmākopyatayā prajñāpāramitākopyatānugantavyeti / kāritramācāraḥ / ācāro dharmaḥ / "nyāyo hi sācāro dharmaḥ svabhāvaśca dharmākhyaḥ" iti vacanāt / sarvo dharmaḥ saptaviṃśatividhaṃ kāritram / tasyākopyatā avadhyatā / daśadiksarvalokadhātusthiteṣu sarvasattveṣu sarvairākāraiḥ yathā bhājanamavicchedena yāvadākāśaṃ pravṛttiḥ / tayā tajjanikayā bhagavataḥ prajñāpāramitāyā akopyatā tādṛśyeva veditavyā / ityuktaṃ dharmakāyasya kāritram //
body.translated_text: In order to show that practice (<s>kāritra</s>) itself is all-pervading, he says: '<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is to be followed through the imperturbability of all <s>dharmas</s>.' <s>Kāritra</s> (practice) is conduct (<s>ācāra</s>). Conduct is <s>dharma</s>. As stated: 'For <s>dharma</s> is indeed conduct according to principle, and the nature [of things] is [itself] called <s>dharma</s>.' All <s>dharma</s> is practice of twenty-seven kinds. Its imperturbability is its inviolability — in all beings situated in all world-realms in the ten directions, through all modes, just as a vessel without interruption as far as space extends. By that which produces it, the imperturbability of the <s>Bhagavān's</s> <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be understood as being just like that. Thus has been stated the practice of the <s>Dharmakāya</s>. //

body.text: samudrāparyantatāvākyādibhirakopyatāvākyaparyantaiḥ prajñāpāramitāyā ye viśeṣā uktāsteṣāṃ pāramārthikaṃ jñānamānupūrvyā darśayitukāmaḥ pṛcchati tatkasya hetoriti / ekakṣaṇābhisamayadharmakāyasambandhibhiranugamavākyairyaduktaṃ tatsarvaṃ kasya hetoḥ kena kāraṇenetyarthaḥ / rūpaṃ hītyādikamuttaram / iha samudro 'paryantaḥ śūnyatāmātratvāt / tasyāśca pramāṇābhāt / evaṃ rūpādayopi pañcaskandhāḥ samudrasamāḥ / tadvatprajñāpāramitāpi / tathā hi ye ca rūpādayo yā ca teṣāṃ śūnyatā yā ca prajñāpāramitā sarva ete na saṃyuktā na visaṃyuktā arūpiṇo 'nidarśanā ekalakṣaṇā yadutālakṣaṇā iti bhāvaḥ / evaṃ gaganasamatādayopi jñātavyāḥ / yāvadanupalabdhiriti / akliṣṭamajñānam / evaṃ hītyādi / evaṃ hīti / yathaite 'ṣṭāvabhisamayāḥ saparicchadā nirdiṣṭastathaivetyarthaḥ / anugantavyeti anusartavyā / tataḥ kiṃ karaṇīyamityāha yadetyādi / anugamiṣyatīti vyañjanakāyena śroṣyati /
body.translated_text: Wishing to show in sequence the ultimate knowledge of those special qualities of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> that were stated through the statements on the boundlessness of the ocean and so on, up to the statements on imperturbability, he asks: 'For what reason?' The meaning is: whatever was stated through the statements on realization in a single instant connected with the <s>Dharmakāya</s> — all of that, for what reason, by what cause? The answer is: 'For form...' and so on. Here, the ocean is boundless because of being mere emptiness, and because of the absence of a measure for that [emptiness]. Similarly, the five aggregates beginning with form are also equal to the ocean. Likewise <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. For whatever are form and the rest, whatever is their emptiness, and whatever is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> — all these are neither conjoined nor disjoined, formless, non-demonstrable, of one characteristic — namely, characteristiclessness. This is the meaning. Similarly, 'by the equality of space' and the rest should also be understood — up to 'non-apprehension.' '<s>Akliṣṭam ajñānam</s>' means undefiled ignorance. 'Thus indeed' — just as these eight <s>abhisamayas</s> (realizations) with their accessories have been taught, so it is — this is the meaning. 'Is to be followed' means is to be pursued. Then what is to be done? — to this he says 'whatever' and so on. 'Will follow' means will hear through the body of words.

body.text:
vyavacārayiṣyatītyarthaśarīreṇa jñāsyati / avatariṣyatīti śraddhāsyati / avabhotsyata iti prajñāsyati / cintayiṣyatīti catasṛbhirvicāraṇāyuktibhiścintayiṣyati vicārayiṣyati / evamevaitannānyatheti / yāni punaḥ sthānāni cintayan bālaḥ śaktikṣayāt khinna unmādyet mūrcchet maraṇaṃ vā nigacchet tāni sthānānyacintyāni teṣu tulayiṣyati / yathaitāni bhagavatā paramayogīśvareṇa dṛṣṭāni tathaiva nirdiṣṭāni / asmākametānyacintā(ntyā)ni tarkāgocaratvāditi upaparīkṣiṣyata iti / etāvataiva sarvasaṃśayānāṃ chedanādavadhārayiṣyatyevamevaitaditi / evamatīva cchinneṣu saṃśayeṣu bhavanāyā adhikāraḥ / ata āha / bhāvayiṣyatīti / caturvidhā bhāvanā / śamatho vipaśyanā śamathavipaśyane śamathavipaśyanābhiratiśca / kīdṛśairmanasikārairityāha / sarvamāyetyādi / ahamiti mameti rūpamiti vedanetyevamādikaḥ sarvābhiniveśaḥ sarvamanyanā / manyāśabdāṇṇijantādyac manyanā / sarvaparapravādibhirmārādibhiḥ kleśaiśca yāḥ kampanāḥ tāḥ sarveñjanāḥ / tadā nāsya durlabhetyādi / sarvaguṇānāmiti bodhisattvaguṇānām / buddhakṣetrasyeti guṇānāṃ paripūririti
vartate / śeṣaṃ sugamam //
body.translated_text: 'will investigate' — he will know by means of the body of meaning. 'Will enter' — he will have faith (<s>śraddhā</s>). 'Will comprehend' — he will have wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>). 'Will reflect' — he will reflect and investigate by means of the four reasoning methods of investigation. 'It is exactly thus, not otherwise.' But those topics which a foolish person, reflecting upon, might go mad, faint, or even die from exhaustion of his faculties — those topics are inconceivable; regarding them he will weigh [thus]: 'Just as these were seen by the Bhagavān, the supreme lord of yogins, so too were they taught. For us these are inconceivable, because they are beyond the range of reasoning' — thus 'he will examine.' By just this much, from the cutting of all doubts, 'he will ascertain: it is exactly thus.' When doubts have been thus completely cut, there is eligibility for meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>). Therefore he says: 'he will meditate.' Meditation is fourfold: <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding), <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight), <s>śamatha-vipaśyanā</s> (both combined), and delight in <s>śamatha-vipaśyanā</s>. 'With what kind of mental engagements?' — he says 'all is illusion' and so on. 'I,' 'mine,' 'form,' 'feeling' — all such attachment is all 'thinking' (<s>manyanā</s>). The word <s>manyā</s> with the <s>ṇij</s> suffix and <s>ac</s> ending [yields] <s>manyanā</s>. All the agitations caused by all rival proponents, by <s>Māra</s> and the like, and by the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) — those are all 'disturbances.' 'Then for him nothing is hard to attain' and so on. 'Of all qualities' means of the <s>bodhisattva</s> qualities. 'Of the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field)' — 'the fulfillment of qualities' is to be supplied. The rest is easily understood.

body.text: sūtrasyārtho 'ṣṭavabhisamayāḥ śāstre prathamamuddiṣṭāḥ / ta iyatā vistareṇa nirdiṣṭāḥ / punaḥ śāstram-
body.translated_text: The meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is the eight <s>abhisamayas</s> (clear realizations); in the <s>śāstra</s> (treatise) they were first enumerated. They have been explained in this much detail. Again, the <s>śāstra</s> [says]:

children.translated_text: 'The characteristic, its application, its excellence, its sequence,
its culmination, and its fruition — this is the other sixfold summary of meaning.'

body.text: athavā ṣaḍarthāḥ sūtrasya / sarvākārajñatā mārgajñatā sarvajñatā ceti trayametallakṣaṇaṃ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ / yatastrividhaiva sā / caturthaḥ sarvākārābhisambodhiḥ / so 'syāṃ prayogaḥ / caryetyarthaḥ / pañcamo mūrdhābhisamayaḥ / so 'syāṃ prayogaprakarṣaḥ / ṣaṣṭho 'nupūrvābhisamayaḥ so 'syāṃ prayogānukramaḥ / anupūrvaprayoga ityarthaḥ / saptama ekakṣaṇābhisamayaḥ / so 'syāṃ prayoganiṣṭhāḥ / aṣṭamo dharmakāyaḥ / so 'syāṃ vipākaḥ / pradhānaphalamityarthaḥ / punaḥ śāstram-
body.translated_text: Alternatively, there are six meanings of the <s>sūtra</s>. <s>Sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience in all aspects), <s>mārgajñatā</s> (path-knowledge), and <s>sarvajñatā</s> (all-knowledge) — these three constitute the characteristic (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>. Because it is indeed threefold. The fourth is <s>sarvākārābhisambodhi</s> (awakening to all aspects). That is its application (<s>prayoga</s>) — meaning its practice (<s>caryā</s>). The fifth is <s>mūrdhābhisamaya</s> (peak realization). That is its excellence of application (<s>prayogaprakarṣa</s>). The sixth is <s>anupūrvābhisamaya</s> (sequential realization); that is its sequence of application (<s>prayogānukrama</s>) — meaning sequential practice. The seventh is <s>ekakṣaṇābhisamaya</s> (single-moment realization). That is its culmination of application (<s>prayoganiṣṭhā</s>). The eighth is <s>dharmakāya</s>. That is its fruition (<s>vipāka</s>) — meaning the principal result. Again, the <s>śāstra</s> [says]:

children.translated_text: 'The threefold object, the cause, the fourfold application,
the <s>dharmakāya</s>, the fruit, and action — this is the other threefold summary of meaning.'

body.text: athavā trayorthāḥ sutrasya / hetuḥ prayogaḥ phalaṃ ca / tatra trividhaḥ prayogaviṣayo hetuḥ / sarvākārajñatā mārgajñatā sarvajñatā ca / catvāro 'rthāḥ prayogaḥ prayogasāmānyāt / sarvākārābhisambodho mūrdhābhisamayo 'nupūrvābhisamaya ekakṣaṇābhisambodhaśceti /
body.translated_text: Alternatively, there are three meanings of the <s>sūtra</s>: cause, application, and fruit. Therein, the threefold object of application is the cause: <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>, <s>mārgajñatā</s>, and <s>sarvajñatā</s>. The four topics [constitute] the application, because of being the general [category of] application: <s>sarvākārābhisambodha</s> (awakening to all aspects), <s>mūrdhābhisamaya</s> (peak realization), <s>anupūrvābhisamaya</s> (sequential realization), and <s>ekakṣaṇābhisambodha</s> (single-moment awakening).

body.text: phalaṃ dharmakāyaḥ karma ca / vināpi tenārthagateḥ / arthasaṃgrahaḥ sakalasūtrārthasya saṃkṣepaḥ / tatra prathamo 'ṣṭadhā / dvitīyaḥ ṣoḍhā / tṛtīyastredhā //
body.translated_text: The fruit is <s>dharmakāya</s> and action as well — even without that, because the meaning is arrived at. 'Summary of meaning' (<s>arthasaṃgraha</s>) is the condensation of the entire meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>. Therein, the first [summary] is eightfold; the second is sixfold; the third is threefold.

body.text: anugamasya vācakaḥ parivarto 'nugamaparivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: The chapter that expresses the 'following along' (<s>anugama</s>) is the <s>Anugama-parivarta</s> (Chapter on Following Along).

body.text: āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ sāratamānāmni pañjikāyāṃ ratnākaraśāntiviracitāyā ekonatriṃśattamaḥ parivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: In the <s>Pañjikā</s> commentary named <s>Sāratamā</s>, composed by <s>Ratnākaraśānti</s>, on the noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s> — this is the twenty-ninth chapter.

body.text: 30. sadāpraruditaparivarto nāma triṃśattamaḥ /
body.translated_text: 30. The thirtieth [chapter] is named the '<s>Sadāprarudita-parivarta</s>' (Chapter of Ever-Weeping).

body.text: aṣṭābhirabhisamayairbhagavatī nirdiṣṭā / sā yathā veditavyā tannoktam / atastabhdagavān vica(va)kṣurāha punaraparamityādinā / paryeṣṭavyeti icchateḥ prayogaḥ / paryeṣitā paryeṣamāṇeneti / eṣṛ ityasya bhauvādikasya prayogaḥ / kāyaklamathādimanasikārāṇāṃ pratiṣedho vīryātiśayārthaḥ / mā ca kvacidityādinā vikṣepapratiṣedhaḥ / mā praṇidhā iti mā niveśaya / kvacita ityuddeśaḥ / adhyātmaṃ bahirdhā veti nirdeśaḥ / adhiśabdo 'dhikaraṇārthaḥ / tato vitarkyārthe 'vyayībhāvaḥ / ana ityac samāsāntaḥ ṭilopaḥ / bahirdheti bahirityarthaḥ / mā gā iti sambandhaḥ / māṅi luṅ, iṇo gā luṅi, gātisthetyādinā sico luk / na māṅyoga ityaḍāgamapratiṣedhaḥ / vāmena dakṣiṇeneti pārśveneti bhāvaḥ / pūrveṇetyādinā diśāṃ nirdeśaḥ / anuvidiśamiti vidiśām / anuśabdo vīpsāyām / vidiśi vidiśītyanuvidiśam / avyayībhāve śaratprabhṛtibhya ityac samāsāntaḥ / tathā ca kulaputretyādinā atattvamanasikārāṇāṃ pratiṣedhaḥ / nātmato na satkāyata iti / sīdatīti sat / rāśitvātkāyaḥ / anityo rūpādirāśiḥ satkāya ityucyate / satkāye pudgalaḥ prajñapyate / ataśca nātmato na satkāyataścalasīti / na dravyasatā pudgalarūpeṇa nāpi prajñaptisatā / ubhayoranupalambhādityarthaḥ / na rūpataścetyādi / nāpi rūpādibhiḥ skandhaiḥ / dharmāṇāmapyanupalabdheriti bhāvaḥ / ataścalatīti ebhiścalati / eṣāṃ samāropeṇa vitiṣṭhat iti nivartate / śeṣaṃ sugamam /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavatī</s> has been expounded through the eight <s>abhisamayas</s>. How she is to be understood — that has not been stated. Therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the all-seeing one, says 'furthermore' and so on. '<s>Paryeṣṭavyā</s>' (is to be sought) — the conjugational form of <s>iś</s> (to desire). '<s>Paryeṣitā paryeṣamāṇena</s>' — the conjugational form of the <s>bhvādi</s> root <s>eṣṛ</s>. The negation of mental engagements such as bodily fatigue and the like is for the purpose of [expressing] extraordinary effort. By 'and may he not anywhere' and so on — the negation of distraction. '<s>Mā praṇidhā</s>' means 'do not place.' '<s>Kvacit</s>' (anywhere) is the enumeration. 'Internally [and] externally' is the detailed exposition. The prefix '<s>adhi</s>' has the sense of location; from that, the <s>avyayībhāva</s> compound in the sense of consideration. '<s>Ana</s>' is the <s>ac</s> compound-final with <s>ṭi</s>-deletion. '<s>Bahirdhā</s>' means 'externally.' '<s>Mā gāḥ</s>' — this is the connection. <s>Māṅ</s> with <s>luṅ</s>; the root <s>iṇ</s> [becomes] <s>gā</s> in <s>luṅ</s>, by '<s>gātisthe</s>' and so on, [there is] <s>sic-luk</s>. 'No <s>aḍ-āgama</s> in connection with <s>māṅ</s>' — this is the prohibition of the augment. 'By the left, by the right' — 'by the side' is the import. By 'from the east' and so on — the enumeration of the directions. '<s>Anuvidiśam</s>' means 'in the intermediate directions.' The prefix '<s>anu</s>' is in the sense of distributiveness. 'In each intermediate direction' — [this is] <s>anuvidiśam</s>. The <s>ac</s> compound-final [applies] by '<s>śaratprabhṛtibhyaḥ</s>' in <s>avyayībhāva</s>. Similarly, by 'O son of good family' and so on — the negation of mental engagements that are not in accordance with reality. '<s>Na ātmataḥ na satkāyataḥ</s>' — '<s>sat</s>' because it subsides; '<s>kāya</s>' because of being a group. The impermanent group of form etc. is called <s>satkāya</s>. In <s>satkāya</s>, a <s>pudgala</s> (person) is designated. Therefore: 'Do not move from the self, not from the <s>satkāya</s>' — not in the form of a person that is substantially real, nor as [merely] nominally real; because neither is apprehended — this is the meaning. 'Not from form' and so on — nor by the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) of form etc.; because <s>dharmas</s> too are non-apprehensible — this is the import. 'Therefore he moves' — he moves by these; 'abiding in their superimposition' — this is what is negated. The rest is easily understood.

body.text: vaiśabdo 'vadhāraṇe / evamevetyarthaḥ / ālokamiti mokṣamārgasya deśanām / samudānetukāma iti / ātmani samyagutpādayitukāmaḥ / adhimuktimiti / evamevaitadityavadhāraṇam / kva? sarvadharmeṣu / kīdṛśeṣu? śūnyānimittāpraṇihiteṣu / yathāpratibhāsamarthābhāvācchūnyeṣu / tasya ca pratibhāsasya bhrāntinimittasya prakṛtinirodhādanimitteṣu /
body.translated_text: The word '<s>vai</s>' is in the sense of emphasis. The meaning is 'exactly thus.' '<s>Ālokam</s>' means the teaching of the path of liberation. '<s>Samudānetukāmaḥ</s>' — wishing to properly generate within oneself. '<s>Adhimukti</s>' (conviction) — the ascertainment 'it is exactly thus.' Where? In all <s>dharmas</s>. Of what kind? Those that are empty (<s>śūnya</s>), signless (<s>animitta</s>), and wishless (<s>apraṇihita</s>). Empty of what? Of [both] appearance and own-nature — because of the absence of meaning as it appears. And because of the natural cessation of that appearance which is the cause of error — signless.

body.text: ataśca bhrāntimātratayā dṛṣṭe traidhātuke praṇidhānābhāvādapraṇihiteṣu / śūnyatāśabdaḥ kvacitpaṭhyate / tatra svārthe tal / nimittaparivarjitenetyuddeśaḥ / bhrāntinimittayorvastvabhiniveśastadiha nimittam / tatparivarjitena bhāvaparivarjitena sattvadṛṣṭiparivarjitena ceti nirdeśaḥ / bhāvo dharmadṛṣṭi sattvadṛṣṭirātmadṛṣṭiḥ / tābhyāṃ parivarjitenetyarthaḥ / yānītyādi / yāni dharma deśayantīti sambandhaḥ / śūnyānimittāpraṇihitāḥ pūrvavat / niḥsvabhāvasya notpādo na jātirna nirodhaḥ / yasya notpādanirodhau so 'bhāvaḥ / tasmād anutpādā ajātā anirodhā abhāvāḥ sarvadharmā ityevaṃ yāni dharmaṃ deśayanti tāni kalyāṇamitrāṇi / arthādgamyate tadviparītaṃ dharma yāni deśayanti tāni pāpamitrāṇi / pratipadyamāno anutiṣṭhan / kṛtajña śrutajñānāt / kṛtavedī śrutaphalajñānāt / paritulayamāneneti cintayatā / lokāmiṣaṃ annapānavastrādi / tena pratisaṃyuktā tadabhilāṣiṇī / anubaddhavyo 'nugantavyaḥ / asti hīti / asti khalvetat / sevitumityādeḥ padatrayasya paribhoktumityarthaḥ / abhibhūyeti nirdoṣīkṛtya / sattvavinayeneti sattvānāṃ cittarakṣārtham / parigrahamupādāyeti parigrahārtham / saṅgastṛṣṇā / ārambaṇamupalambhaḥ / bhūtanaya paramārthaprabhedaḥ / saṃkleśābhāvād asaṃkleśāḥ / vyavadānābhāvād avyavadānāḥ / niḥsattvādipadaiḥ pudgalanairātmyamāha / māyopamādipadairdharmanairātmyam / prativāṇiḥ prativacanam / aniviṇṇamakhinnam /
body.translated_text: And therefore, because the three realms are seen as mere error, due to the absence of aspiration — wishless. The word '<s>śūnyatā</s>' is sometimes read [in place of <s>śūnya</s>]. There, the <s>tal</s> suffix is in the reflexive sense. 'By that which is free from signs' — this is the enumeration. The sign of error — attachment to the reality of things — that is the 'sign' here. 'Free from that' — 'free from [attachment to] existence,' 'free from the view of beings' — this is the detailed exposition. 'Existence' (<s>bhāva</s>) is the view of <s>dharmas</s>; 'the view of beings' is the view of self. 'Free from both' — this is the meaning. 'Which' and so on — 'which teach the <s>Dharma</s>' is the connection. Empty, signless, wishless — as before. 'Of that which is without own-nature, there is no arising, no birth, no cessation.' That which has no arising and no cessation is a non-entity (<s>abhāva</s>). Therefore, 'non-arising, unborn, non-ceasing, non-entities are all <s>dharmas</s>' — those who teach the <s>Dharma</s> thus are the spiritual friends (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>). By implication, those who teach the <s>Dharma</s> in the opposite way are evil friends (<s>pāpamitra</s>). '<s>Pratipadyamānaḥ</s>' — practicing. '<s>Kṛtajña</s>' — from knowledge of what was heard. '<s>Kṛtavedī</s>' — from knowledge of the fruit of what was heard. '<s>Paritulayamānena</s>' — by one who reflects. '<s>Lokāmiṣa</s>' — food, drink, clothing, etc. '<s>Tena pratisaṃyuktā</s>' — desirous of that. '<s>Anubaddhavyaḥ</s>' — to be followed. '<s>Asti hi</s>' — indeed this exists. The triad of words beginning with '<s>sevitum</s>' (to serve) has the meaning 'to enjoy.' '<s>Abhibhūya</s>' — having purified. '<s>Sattvavinayena</s>' — for the purpose of protecting the minds of beings. '<s>Parigraham upādāya</s>' — for the purpose of possession. '<s>Saṅga</s>' is craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>). '<s>Ārambaṇa</s>' is apprehension (<s>upalambha</s>). '<s>Bhūtanaya</s>' is the classification of ultimate reality (<s>paramārtha</s>). Because of the absence of defilement, 'undefiled.' Because of the absence of purification, 'unpurified.' By the words '<s>niḥsattva</s>' etc., he states the selflessness of persons (<s>pudgalanairātmya</s>). By the words '<s>māyopama</s>' (illusion-like) etc., [he states] the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmanairātmya</s>). '<s>Prativāṇi</s>' is a reply. '<s>Aniviṇṇam</s>' means unwearied.

body.text: anuśāsanī upadeśaḥ / auṇādiko 'nirdharaṇīvat / rudan aśrupātena / krandan dīnasvaraiḥ / śocan utkaṇṭhamānaḥ / paridevamāno vilapan anubaddha iti samanvitaḥ / kvacillyapaḥ pāṭhaḥ / tasyāpi pūrvādikkarma / anuparikṣiptā pariveṣṭitā / parikhāḥ khātayaḥ / ṛddhā dhanasampattyā / sphītā gṛhodyānādiśobhayā / kṣemā nirupadravatvāt / subhikṣā sulabhānnapānatvāt / ākīrṇo vistīrṇaḥ / bahu nānāvidho janaḥ parivāro yeṣāṃ te tathā / tādṛśā manuṣyā yasyāṃ sā tathā / antarasyāntare āpaṇaḥ krayavikrayasthānam / tasmin vithīśatāni / taiḥ pañcabhiḥ nirviddhā niḥśeṣaṃ viddhā / vithīnāmā prakārāntamubhayato gamanāt / ālekhyena vicitrāṇi ca tāni citrāṇi cādbhūtatvāt / sadṛśāni ca purānurūpatvāt / taiḥ anutpīḍamasaṃbādhaṃ janayugyayānānāṃ saṃkramasthānāni saṃbhūya gamanasthānāni vistīrṇarathyāḥ / teṣāṃ sthāpitāni sthāpanāni / bhāve ktaḥ / taiḥ sumāpitā suracitā / tatra janaḥ padikādilokāḥ /
body.translated_text: '<s>Anuśāsanī</s>' is instruction. It is an <s>auṇādika</s> [formation], like '<s>nirdharaṇī</s>.' '<s>Rudan</s>' — with tears. '<s>Krandan</s>' — with piteous cries. '<s>Śocan</s>' — yearning. '<s>Paridevamānaḥ</s>' — lamenting. '<s>Anubaddha</s>' means possessed of. In some readings, [there is] <s>lyap</s>. Its [construction] too has the previous as the first action. '<s>Anuparikṣiptā</s>' means surrounded. '<s>Parikhāḥ</s>' are moats. '<s>Ṛddhā</s>' — by abundance of wealth. '<s>Sphītā</s>' — by the splendor of houses and gardens. '<s>Kṣemā</s>' — because of being free from calamity. '<s>Subhikṣā</s>' — because of food and drink being easily available. '<s>Ākīrṇaḥ</s>' means extensive. 'Many diverse people are the retinue of whom — they are thus'; 'such people are in which [city] — it is thus.' '<s>Antara</s>' is 'in between'; '<s>āpaṇa</s>' is a place of buying and selling. In that [market], hundreds of lanes. 'Pervaded by those five' means completely pervaded. '<s>Vithī</s>' [has the character] of reaching the end of a row on both sides [for walking]. 'And paintings — those that are variegated and wonderful because of their marvel'; 'and similar — because of conformity with the city.' 'By those, without crushing, without crowding' — [there are] crossroads, places for going together, [suitable] for people-and-yoked-vehicles — broad streets. 'Their establishments' — places; the <s>kta</s> suffix is in the sense of the abstract noun. 'Well-constructed by those' — well-fashioned. 'People there' — pedestrians and such folk.

body.text:
yugyāni vāhanāni / yānāni rathāḥ / anantaratvātparasparatulyatvācca samasamaiḥ / khoḍakaśīrṣāṇi kramaśīrṣāṇi / upodgatānīti prākārādativistīrṇāt kiñcinnirgatyodgatāni / pramāṇavantīti pṛthūni tuṅgāni ca / nānāvicitrarityanyathānyathā vicitraiḥ / sarvataśca khoḍakavṛkṣānnirgatā vṛkṣāntaram / yathābhavati tathāvasaktam / sarvamasyāmastīti sarvāvanī / kiṅkiṇījāleneti catuṣprākārakhoḍakavṛkṣāvasaktamaṇisūtracatuṣṭayāvavaddhānekamaṇisūtravalambinā / valguḥ / śrotrasukhatvāt / rañjanīyo manoharatvāt / pañcāṅgāni vīṇāvaṃśādīni / gandharvā gāyanāḥ / krīḍanti śrotreṇa, ramante manasā, paricārayanti kāyavākparispandaiḥ / parikhāḥ khātayaḥ / anusārivārivāhinya iti vātādyanusāriṇā jalapravāheṇa yuktāḥ / padmaṃ raktakamalam / puṇḍarīkaṃ sitapadmam / abhijātābhijātariti praṇītapraṇītaiḥ / sugandhaśabdaḥ surabhiparyāyaḥ / tatpuṣkariṇīnāmityudyānapuṣkariṇīnāṃ pramāṇam / samantāditi sarvapārśveṣu / krośaḥ krośa iti vīpsā / nīlādipadāni prāgvyākhyātāni / upanikūjitā buddhanetrī prajñāpāramitā / tasyā citrīkāraḥ paraḥ prasādaḥ / tenānugataṃ sugatebhyaḥ śrutacittaṃ yeṣāṃ te tathā / teṣāṃ madhye śrṛṅgāṭakasyeti
sambandhaḥ / samantāditi pratipārśvam / gṛhaparibhoga iti gṛhasya pariveṣṭaḥ / kimarthamityāha / upabhogaribhogāyeti / upabhogaḥ phalapuṣpādīnām / paribhogaḥ sākalyena bhogo vanavihārādinā / vivaraṃ sandhiḥ / tasminnantaraṃ avakāśaḥ / samarpitaḥ saṅgamitaḥ / tairavakāśaguṇaiḥ / sarvendriyāṇāmanugrahaḥ samanvaṅgaḥ / tadyogāt samanvaṅgī krīḍati vācā / ramate manasā / paricārayati kāyena / tāvatkālamiti parimitakālam / tata iti krīḍādikālādūrdhvam / trikālamiti prāṇhamadhyānhāparānheṣu / āsanasya viśeṣaṇaṃ suvarṇapādakamityādi / ardhakrośamuccastveneti yāvat / tūlikayā vā āstīrṇaṃ goṇikayā vā garbholikācīnāṃśukapratyāstaraṇam / upari sā asyeti uparigarbholikama / kāśikavastraṃ vārāṇaseyakaṃ divyaṃ vā / tat pratyāstaraṇamasyeti tathoktam / samaṃ yathā bhavati na viṣamaṃ tathā dhārayanti pramāṇavabhdiḥ stambhaiḥ / sahitāḥ samagrāḥ / niratāḥ sāvadhānāḥ / kathamityāha / kimayaṃ saṃsthita iti / kuta ityāha / susaṃsthitetyādi / muktāvicitritaṃ paryanteṣu hārārddhahārāṇāṃ pralambanāt, madhye ca sthūlamuktākalāpasya / abhyavakiranti purastāt / prakaranti triṣu pārśveṣu / saṃpravikiranti punaścaturṣvapi
body.translated_text: '<s>Yugyāni</s>' (yoke-animals) are draught animals. '<s>Yānāni</s>' (vehicles) are chariots. 'Of equal quality' — because of being contiguous and mutually equal. '<s>Khoḍakaśīrṣāṇi</s>' means pinnacles in sequence. '<s>Upodgatāni</s>' — having emerged slightly beyond the very wide rampart and risen up. '<s>Pramāṇavanti</s>' means broad and tall. '<s>Nānāvicitrair</s>' means with various ornaments, differing in one way or another. 'And from the pinnacle-trees on all sides, emerging to another tree' — as is appropriate, attached. '<s>Sarvāvanī</s>' — 'all of it is therein.' 'With a net of bells' — attached to the four rampart pinnacle-trees, suspended from four strings of jewels tied together, with many jewel-strings hanging [from them]. 'Charming' — because of being pleasant to the ears. 'Delightful' — because of being captivating to the mind. 'Five-limbed [instruments]' are the <s>vīṇā</s> (lute), flute, and the like. '<s>Gandharvas</s>' are singers. 'They play' — through the ears; 'they delight' — through the mind; 'they amuse themselves' — through bodily and vocal movements. '<s>Parikhā</s>' are moats. 'With flowing water that follows along' — provided with a water-current that flows following the wind and the like. '<s>Padma</s>' (lotus) is a red lotus. '<s>Puṇḍarīka</s>' is a white lotus. '<s>Abhijātābhijātar</s>' means with increasingly excellent [lotuses]. The word '<s>sugandha</s>' (fragrant) is a synonym for '<s>surabhi</s>' (sweet-scented). 'The measure of those lotus-ponds' — of the garden lotus-ponds. '<s>Samantāt</s>' means on all sides. '<s>Krośaḥ krośaḥ</s>' — the repetition indicates distribution. The terms '<s>nīla</s>' (blue) and the rest have been explained previously. 'Serenaded' — the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the guide of the <s>Buddhas</s>. Its '<s>citrīkāra</s>' (wonderment) is supreme faith. Those whose minds, having heard from the <s>Sugatas</s> (well-gone ones), are accompanied by that — they are so described. 'In their midst, of the crossroads' — this is the syntactic connection. '<s>Samantāt</s>' means on each side. '<s>Gṛhaparibhoga</s>' means the enclosure of the house. 'For what purpose?' — he says: 'for enjoyment and use.' 'Enjoyment' is of fruits, flowers, and the like. 'Use' is complete enjoyment through forest recreation and the like. '<s>Vivara</s>' (gap) is a joint. In that, '<s>antara</s>' is space. '<s>Samarpita</s>' means joined together. With those qualities of space. '<s>Samanvaṅga</s>' is the gratification of all the senses. Through connection with that, 'the one having gratification plays' — with speech; 'delights' — with the mind; 'amuses' — with the body. 'For that period' means for a limited time. 'After that' means after the time of play. 'At the three times' — in the morning, midday, and afternoon. The qualifications of the seat are 'having golden legs' and the rest. 'Half a <s>krośa</s> in height' — up to that extent. 'Spread with a mattress or a <s>goṇikā</s>' — a covering of <s>garbholī</s> cloth and Chinese silk. 'Having that on top' — having the <s>garbholī</s> on top. '<s>Kāśika</s>-cloth' is cloth from <s>Vārāṇasī</s> or divine [cloth]. 'Having that as a covering' — thus it is so called. 'So that it is even and not uneven' — they hold it with pillars of proper measure. '<s>Sahita</s>' means complete. '<s>Nirata</s>' means attentive. 'How?' — he says: 'Whether this one is well-established.' 'From what?' — he says: 'well-established' and so forth. 'Adorned with pearls' — because of the hanging of strings and half-strings [of pearls] on the edges, and of a thick pearl garland in the middle. 'They strew [flowers] in front'; 'they scatter on three sides'; 'they sprinkle again on all four

body.text: pārśveṣu / dharmāśayaviśuddhyeti dharme yā teṣāṃ śraddhācchandayoḥ śuddhiḥ / dharmāya gauravaṃ kalyāṇamitratvāt / sanniśrayatā bhājanatā / śraddhārhe yā śraddhadhānatā tayā / vinipāto durgatigamanam / aviṣṭitaṃ avicchinnam / tuṣṭa iti prītaḥ / udagra iti tayā prītyā unnatapūrvakāyaḥ / tadekatānatvāt āttamanaskaḥ / prīterutkarṣāt pramuditaḥ / prītisahagataḥ prasādaḥ prītisaumanasyam / tajjātamasyeti tathoktaḥ / tasya śrṛṇoti smeti sambandhavivakṣayāpādāne ṣaṣṭhī /
body.translated_text: sides.' 'By the purity of their disposition toward the <s>Dharma</s>' — that which is the purity of their faith and desire in the <s>Dharma</s>. 'Reverence toward the <s>Dharma</s>' — because of being a spiritual friend. '<s>Sanniśrayatā</s>' (reliance) is receptivity. 'Through placing faith in what is worthy of faith.' '<s>Vinipāta</s>' (downfall) is going to the evil destinies. '<s>Aviṣṭita</s>' means uninterrupted. '<s>Tuṣṭa</s>' (satisfied) means pleased. '<s>Udagra</s>' (elated) means with the upper body raised due to that joy. Because of single-pointed [focus] on that — '<s>āttamanaska</s>' (overjoyed). Because of the intensification of joy — '<s>pramudita</s>' (delighted). Faith accompanied by joy is '<s>prītisaumanasya</s>' (joyful elation). 'Born of that' — hence it is so called. 'He hears of that one' — the sixth case (genitive) is used in the sense of a purposive connection.

body.text: sarvadharmeṣvaniśritasaṃjñāmiti / yathaitarhi me dharmodgatadeśanayā pratibhāsaḥ sanidhā(dā)namanāśritaḥ / evaṃ hetuniyamamanāśritāḥ sarvadharmā ityenāṃ saṃjñāmatyantasamāhitām / asyāḥ saṃjñāyāḥ prabhāvātkimabhūdityāha / tasyetyādi / samādhaya eva mukhāni mahopāyatvāt / sarvadharmāṇāṃ svabhāvāḥ svalakṣaṇāni / teṣāṃ vyavalokano draṣṭā / teṣāṃ anupalabdhirasattāniścayaḥ / sarvadharmāṇāṃ nirnānātvaṃ samatā svalakṣaṇānāmabhāvāt / tadālambanaḥ samādhistathoktaḥ / sā ca samatā tathatā / tayā nirvikārānsarvadharmān paśyatīti sarvadhamanirvikāradarśī / evaṃ yāvatsarvatathāgatadarśī samādhirveditavyaḥ / eṣu samādhiṣviti krameṇa sarveṣu sthitaḥ san / daśadiśo 'sminniti daśadiglokaḥ sarvalokadhātava ityarthaḥ / tatra buddhān bhagavato 'prameyāsaṃkhyeyān paśyati sma / naikasmin kāle 'nekastathāgata ekasyaiva sarvasattvārthakriyāsu śakteriti cet / nityameka eva buddhastasyaivānantamāyuradhiṣṭhātuṃ śakteriti kinneṣyate? hetubalādanyepi bhavantīti cet / hetubalādeva tarhi yugapadananteṣu lokadhātuṣvanantāstathāgatā jāyanta iti ko virodhaḥ? yathā buddhau cakravartinau sakṛdekatra caturdvīpake lokadhātau notpadyete niḥsapatnakarmakāritvāt tathā tathāgatau trisāhasre lokadhātāviti mahārathaiḥ kṣuṇṇametat /
body.translated_text: 'The perception of non-reliance on all <s>dharmas</s>' — 'just as now, through the teaching of <s>Dharmodgata</s>, this appearance to me [arises] with a basis, not without reliance — in the same way, all <s>dharmas</s>, not relying on the determination of a cause, are [characterized by] this perception of being utterly concentrated.' 'Through the power of this perception, what occurred?' — he says 'of that' and so forth. The <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations) themselves are the gateways, because of being the great means. The self-natures of all <s>dharmas</s> are their own characteristics. The 'beholder' of those is the one who sees. The 'non-apprehension' of those is the ascertainment of non-existence. 'The non-differentiation of all <s>dharmas</s>' is equality — because of the non-existence of their own characteristics. The <s>samādhi</s> having that as its object is so called. And that equality is <s>tathatā</s> (suchness). Through that, he sees all <s>dharmas</s> as without transformation — hence 'the seer of the non-transformation of all <s>dharmas</s>.' Similarly, up to 'the seer of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>' — the <s>samādhi</s> should be understood. 'In those <s>samādhis</s>' — having established [himself] in all of them sequentially. 'The ten-directional [world]' — 'in which the ten directions [exist]' — meaning all world-realms. Therein, he sees immeasurable and incalculable <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>. If [one objects:] 'Not at one time could many <s>Tathāgatas</s> [appear], since a single one alone has the power for all the welfare-activities of beings' — [we reply:] why not accept that there is always just one <s>Buddha</s>, who alone has the power to sustain his infinite lifespan? If [one responds:] 'Others also arise through the force of causes' — then what contradiction is there in saying that, through the force of causes, infinite <s>Tathāgatas</s> are simultaneously born in infinite world-realms? Just as two <s>Buddhas</s> and two <s>Cakravartins</s> (universal monarchs) do not arise simultaneously in one four-continent world-realm — because of performing the function without a rival — so too [not] two <s>Tathāgatas</s> in one three-thousandfold world-realm — this has been thoroughly examined by the great scholars.

body.text: gatiṃ gatā iti / gatirapratidyātaḥ / tāṃ prāptāḥ / śikṣāpita iti śikṣāṃ prāpitaḥ / tatkṛtamiti / yadeva tena purva kṛtam / dhārayitavyaṃ cetasi na vismartavyam / celaṃ vastram / tasya uṇḍukaḥ śiraśāṭaka ityarthaḥ / utkaṇṭhā śokaḥ / paritasanaṃ duḥkhāsikā / kāṣṭhāgatā prītiḥ prema / guṇavatsu cetaso 'kāluṣyaṃ prasādaḥ / tadguṇeṣu vismayaḥ citrīkāraḥ / arbhyahaṇaṃ gauravam / katamaṃ śabdamityata āha / ghoṣamityādi / katamaṃ bhoṣamiṃtyāha / kaḥ pureṣeṇetyādi / atikrāmayiṣyatīti mitāṃ hrasvo na bhavati / "vā cittavirāge"
body.translated_text: 'Gone to the state' — '<s>gati</s>' (state) means that which is beyond obstruction; 'having attained that.' '<s>Śikṣāpita</s>' means made to train. 'That which was done by him' — that which he previously did. 'Should be retained' — should not be forgotten in the mind. '<s>Cela</s>' is cloth. Its '<s>uṇḍuka</s>' means a head-covering — this is the meaning. '<s>Utkaṇṭhā</s>' is sorrow. '<s>Paritasana</s>' is distressing agitation. '<s>Kāṣṭhāgatā prītiḥ</s>' is love [that has reached its] culmination. '<s>Prasāda</s>' (serene faith) is the non-turbidity of the mind toward those possessing qualities. '<s>Citrīkāra</s>' (wonderment) is astonishment at their qualities. '<s>Arghyahaṇa</s>' is reverence. 'What word?' — to this he says '<s>ghoṣa</s>' (sound) and so forth. 'What sound?' — he says 'who is the searcher' and so forth. '<s>Atikrāmayiṣyati</s>' means 'the measured [time] does not become short.'

body.text: ityato vāśabdānuvṛttervyavasthitavibhāṣā / vijñānācca / atiśabdaścātra apaśabdārthe vartate / ataḥ pañcamī yuktā bhavati / yannuśabdastasmādarthe / paryutthāpayāmāseti vyagrīkṛtavān / yatheti yataḥ / asthimajjayāśceti / majjanśabdasya liṅgavyatyayena striyāṃ ḍāp sīmāvat / kalyacitta iti tenaiva harṣeṇa karmaṇyacittaḥ / tataśca dviguṇībhūtaharṣatvāt pramuditacittaḥ / guṇajātiḥ manuṣyasāmānyo guṇaḥ / viśeṣastu manuṣyātikrānto guṇaḥ / kṣamante ceti svayaṃ kartavyatayāpi rocanāt / viṣayiteti śaktiḥ /
body.translated_text: Because of the continuation of the word '<s>vā</s>' (or) from [the rule] 'or in the dispassion of mind,' it is an optionally prescribed rule. And because of [the support of] cognition. The word '<s>ati</s>' here is used in the sense of a faulty term. Therefore the fifth case (ablative) is justified. The word '<s>yannuḥ</s>' is in that meaning. '<s>Paryutthāpayāmāsa</s>' means made agitated. '<s>Yathā</s>' means 'because.' 'And of bone and marrow' — through gender-change of the word '<s>majjan</s>' (marrow), the <s>ḍāp</s> suffix [applies] in the feminine, like '<s>sīmā</s>.' '<s>Kalyacitta</s>' (light-hearted) means having a mind fit for action through that very joy. And therefore, because of the doubling of joy, '<s>pramuditacitta</s>' (delighted mind). '<s>Guṇajāti</s>' (quality by birth) is a quality common to humans. But the special [quality] is a quality surpassing the human. '<s>Kṣamante</s>' means they approve — because of inclination [even] as something to be done by oneself. '<s>Viṣayitā</s>' is capacity.

body.text: viditābhiprāya āha / alpotsuka ityādi / utsuka autsukyam / yattat kṣaṇaṃ lavamapi tat / tanmuhūrtamapi tat / trayāṇāmupādānaṃ tu śrotṛṇāṃ śraddhabhedāt / niṣpratibhāna ityuddeśaḥ / sadāpraruditasyetyādinirdeśaḥ / uttara iti uttaranimiuttam / apratipadyamāno 'labhamānaḥ / daddhvamiti dad dāne / vādyaprakṛtayo vādyaprakārāḥ / prabhūtāḥ prakārabāhulyāt / vipulāḥ pratiprakāramānantyāt / bhogā arthāḥ / sarvalokaviśiṣṭā iti sarvalokātikrāntāḥ /
body.translated_text: Knowing his intention, he says '<s>alpotsuka</s>' (of little eagerness) and so forth. '<s>Utsuka</s>' is eagerness. 'That which [is] a moment' — 'even a <s>lava</s>' — that. 'Even a <s>muhūrta</s>' — that. The taking up of the three [terms] is because of the difference in the faith of the listeners. '<s>Niṣpratibhāna</s>' (without eloquence) is the general statement. 'Of <s>Sadāprarudita</s>' and so forth is the detailed exposition. '<s>Uttara</s>' means on account of a superior. '<s>Apratipadyamāna</s>' means not obtaining. '<s>Daddhvam</s>' — the root '<s>dad</s>' is in the sense of giving. '<s>Vādyaprakṛtayaḥ</s>' means types of musical instruments. '<s>Prabhūtāḥ</s>' (abundant) — because of the multiplicity of types. '<s>Vipulāḥ</s>' (vast) — because of the infinitude within each type. '<s>Bhogāḥ</s>' are possessions. '<s>Sarvalokaviśiṣṭāḥ</s>' means surpassing the entire world.

body.text: upariṣṭānmūrdhna iti upari śirasaḥ / prātiṣṭhata iti praśabdaḥ praterarthe / vihāyasītyantarikṣe / prāñco 'ñjalayaḥ prāñjalayaḥ / sphuṭa iti prāptaḥ / sahadarśanāditi darśanātkāraṇāddarśanena sahaivaityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'From above, from the head' — from the top of the head. '<s>Prātiṣṭhata</s>' — the prefix '<s>pra</s>' is in the sense of '<s>prati</s>' (toward). '<s>Vihāyasā</s>' means in the sky. '<s>Prāñco'ñjalayaḥ</s>' — those whose <s>añjalis</s> (joined palms) are directed forward — hence '<s>prāñjalayaḥ</s>.' '<s>Sphuṭa</s>' means attained. '<s>Sahadarśanāt</s>' means from the very cause of seeing — meaning 'simultaneously with the seeing itself.'

body.text: sadāpraruditopalakṣitaḥ parivartastatparivartaḥ // āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ sāratamānāmni pañjikāyāṃ ratnākaraśāntiviracitāyāṃ triśattamaḥ parivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: The chapter characterized by <s>Sadāprarudita</s> is that chapter. In the <s>Pañjikā</s> commentary named <s>Sāratama</s>, composed by <s>Ratnākaraśānti</s>, on the noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s> — this is the thirtieth chapter.

body.text: 31. dharmodgataparivarto nāmaikatriśattamaḥ /
body.translated_text: 31. The thirty-first [chapter] is named the '<s>Dharmodgata-parivarta</s>' (Chapter of <s>Dharmodgata</s>).

body.text: evamukta ityādi / na khalvityādi pratijñā / acalitā hi tathateti hetuḥ / tathāgatānāṃ kimāgatamiti cedāha / yā cetyādi / evamuttarepi hetavaḥ sasamarthanā veditavyāḥ / sarve caite hetavaḥ śūnyatāparyāyā nimittabhedāttu bhedaḥ / ākāśadhāturākāśasādharmyāttathataiva / nanu dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇāśītyanuvyañjanavirājitavigrahastathāgato na punastathatādaya ityata āha / na hi kulaputrānyatretyādi / tathataiva suviśuddhā tathāgata iti bhāvaḥ / sa hi teṣāṃ svābhāvikaḥ kāya iti nyāyaḥ / evaṃ tathatāditathāgatayorabhedamuktvātyantābhedaṃ darśayitumāha / yā cetyādi / eṣāmeva dharmāṇāmiti tathatādīnāṃ tathateti parikalpitarūpaśūnyatā / yā ca sarvadharmāṇāmiti skandhadhātvādīnāṃ yā ca tathāgatasya / ekaivetyādiruddeśaḥ / punarekaivetyādi nirdeśaḥ / hetumāha / yadutāsattvāditi / adravyatvānna
body.translated_text: 'Thus spoken' and so forth. 'Not indeed' and so forth is the thesis. 'For <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) is immovable' — this is the reason. 'What, then, has come of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>?' — to this he says 'whatever' and so forth. Similarly, in the remaining [arguments] too, the reasons together with their justifications should be understood. All these reasons are synonyms of emptiness; the difference is only due to the difference in [conceptual] signs. '<s>Ākāśadhātu</s>' (space-element) — because of its likeness to space, [it is] <s>tathatā</s> itself. 'But surely the <s>Tathāgata</s> is [a being] adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great person and the eighty secondary marks — not <s>tathatā</s> and the like' — to this he says 'not indeed, O son of good family, apart from [that]' and so forth. The meaning is: <s>tathatā</s> itself, perfectly purified, is the <s>Tathāgata</s>. For that is, according to logic, their natural body (<s>svābhāvikakāya</s>). Having thus stated the non-difference of <s>tathatā</s> and the like with the <s>Tathāgata</s>, in order to show their absolute non-difference, he says 'whatever' and so forth. 'Of these very <s>dharmas</s>' means of <s>tathatā</s> and the like. '<s>Tathatā</s>' means the emptiness of imagined form. 'And of all <s>dharmas</s>' means of the aggregates, elements, and the like. 'And of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.' 'One and the same' and so forth is the general statement. 'Again, one and the same' and so forth is the detailed exposition. He states the reason: 'namely, because of non-being-ness' — because of non-substantiality, not

body.text: punaryathālakṣaṇamabhāvāditi bhāvaḥ / punastathāgatānāmagatigatyorabhāvaṃ yathākalpanamasattvāt / bhāvakalpanā tu saṃjñāviparyāsāditi dṛṣṭāntaiḥ pratipādayitumāha / tadyathāpītyādi / madhyānhakālasamaya iti / madhyānhaścāsau kālaśca / tasya samayaḥ / āgamanaṃ yathā ca grāmaṃ praviṣṭa iti viśaterarthasya gativiśeṣatvāt kartari ktaḥ / tathehāpi tathāgatam abhiniviṣṭā iti / dharmākāyā iti dharmatākāyāḥ / hastikāyasyetyādau kāyaḥ samūhaḥ / pariniṣpattiriti bhūtatvam / muṣāvādastatsādharmyān vañcaka ityarthaḥ / ata evāha abhūta iti / amoghaṃ dāyakasya mahāphalahetutvāt / ata eva dakṣiṇīyāḥ /
body.translated_text: furthermore, because of non-existence as characterized — this is the meaning. Furthermore, to demonstrate through examples the non-existence of coming and going of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, as they are imagined, because of non-being-ness — but the conceptualization of existence is due to the distortion of perception — he says 'just as, for example' and so forth. '<s>Madhyānhakālasamaya</s>' — midday is that, and it is a time; and the occasion of that. 'Arrival' — 'just as having entered the village' — because the meaning of the root '<s>viś</s>' (enter) is a specific kind of going, the <s>kta</s> suffix is in the agent sense. Similarly here too, 'those attached to the <s>Tathāgata</s>.' '<s>Dharmakāyāḥ</s>' means those whose body is <s>dharmatā</s> (the true nature of reality). '<s>Hastikāyasya</s>' and the like — '<s>kāya</s>' means a group. '<s>Pariniṣpatti</s>' means true existence. '<s>Mṛṣāvāda</s>' (falsehood) — because of the similarity [with actual beings], 'deceptive' — this is the meaning. For that very reason he says '<s>abhūta</s>' (unreal). '<s>Amogha</s>' (not vain) — because of being a cause of great fruit for the donor. Therefore indeed they are worthy of offerings (<s>dakṣiṇīya</s>).

body.text: prabhāvyante upalabhyante / kāyapariniṣpattiḥ caramabhavasaṃgṛhītā / nāpi kvacidgacchatīti parinirvāṇakāle / na kvacidastīti parinirvāya yatra gacchati / hetarūpādānakāraṇaṃ pratyayāḥ sahakāriṇaḥ / tatra śabdasyopādānaṃ śabdaparamāṇava ityeke / vāyuparamāṇava ityapare / tatra upadhānī tantrīveṣṭanaṃ cakulikā / upavāṇyo apradhānatantrayaḥ / ādyantayoḥ na śabdo niścaratīti vacanaṃ madhye sarvatra sambandhanārtham / nirhetukāśabdāt svārthe 'ṇa nairhetukī /
body.translated_text: 'They become manifest' means they are perceived. 'The perfection of the body' is that which pertains to the final existence. 'Nor does it go anywhere' — at the time of <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final cessation). 'Nor does it exist anywhere' — having attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, where it goes. '<s>Hetu</s>' (cause) is the substantial cause (<s>upādānakāraṇa</s>). '<s>Pratyaya</s>' (condition) is the auxiliary condition. Therein, the substantial cause of sound, according to some, is the atoms of sound. According to others, the atoms of air. Therein, '<s>upadhānī</s>' is the winding of the string on the lute. '<s>Upavāṇya</s>' is the non-principal strings. 'No sound issues forth at the beginning or end' — this statement is for the purpose of connecting [the argument] to the middle [point, namely] everywhere. '<s>Nairhetukī</s>' — from '<s>nirhetuka</s>' (without cause), the <s>aṇ</s> suffix in the reflexive sense — [yielding] '<s>nairhetukī</s>.' (being without cause).

body.text: saṃkṣobhitāni saṃpracalitāni / jihmībhūtāni naṣṭacchāyāni / utsṛjanti smeti muñcanti sma / vihāyasamiti ākāśam / svakena kāyena dharmodgatamabhicchādayati smeti tasyāgrataḥ sarvakāyena bhūmau patati smetyarthaḥ / kiyantaṃ kālamityata āha saptavarṣāṇīti / avakrāmaṇaṃ praveśanam / yadvayamiti yadā vayam / anuvartamānā ityanukurvatyaḥ / divyamityākāśabhavam / cittasyānyathātva pṛthivīsekavaimukhyam / iti pratisaṃkhyāyeti evaṃ nirūpya sarvāṇi tānīti dārikāśatāni / tāni tānīti śastraviśeṣaṇam / avatāramavakāśaḥ / adhyatiṣṭhadityakarot / gandhamityatra adhyatiṣṭhaditi cakāreṇānukṛṣyate / parīṣṭiḥ paryeṣaṇā /
body.translated_text: '<s>Saṃkṣobhitāni</s>' means 'shaken.' '<s>Saṃpracalitāni</s>' means 'trembling.' '<s>Jihmībhūtāni</s>' means 'having lost their luster.' '<s>Utsṛjanti sma</s>' means 'they released.' '<s>Vihāyasam</s>' means 'the sky.' 'With his own body he covered <s>Dharmodgata</s>' means 'before him, he fell to the ground with his entire body' — this is the meaning. 'For how long?' — to this he says 'Seven years.' '<s>Avakrāmaṇa</s>' means 'entry.' '<s>Yadvayam</s>' means 'when we.' '<s>Anuvartamānāḥ</s>' means 'imitating.' '<s>Divyam</s>' means 'celestial, [produced] from the sky.' '<s>Cittasyānyathātva</s>' — the turning away from sprinkling the ground. '<s>Iti pratisaṃkhyāya</s>' means 'having thus reflected.' '<s>Sarvāṇi tāni</s>' — the hundreds of maidens. '<s>Tāni tāni</s>' — this is an adjective for weapons. '<s>Avatāra</s>' means 'opportunity.' '<s>Adhyatiṣṭhat</s>' means 'he performed.' '<s>Gandham</s>' — here '<s>adhyatiṣṭhat</s>' is drawn in by the particle '<s>ca</s>.' '<s>Parīṣṭi</s>' means 'seeking.'

body.text: kīdṛśī tatrāryasya dharmodgatasya dharmadeśanābhūdityata āha / tatreyaṃ dharmodgatasyetyādi sugamam / yadutaśabdaḥ sāmānyenoddiṣṭasya viśeṣaṃ dyotayati / ebhistriṃśatā ākārairityarthaḥ / ata evāsyāḥ śrutabalenotpannā /
body.translated_text: 'What was the nature of noble <s>Dharmodgata's</s> <s>Dharma</s>-teaching there?' — to this he says 'Here was <s>Dharmodgata's</s>' and so on — this is easily understood. The word '<s>yaduta</s>' specifies the particular within what has been stated in general. 'By these thirty aspects' — this is the meaning. For precisely this reason, [the samādhis] arose through the power of what was heard.

body.text: ebhireva triṃśatākāraiḥ sadāpraruditasya bodhisattvasyotpannāstriṃśatsamādhayaḥ paṭhiṣyante / prajñāpāramitāyāḥ samatā sarvadharmeṣu / kutaḥ? sarvadharmasamatayā / sā hi dharmadhātvālambanā / sa ca samānaḥ sarvadharmeṣu / prajñāpāramitāyā viviktatā / kutaḥ? sarvadharmaviviktatayā / yataḥ sarvadharmāḥ svalakṣaṇairviviktāḥ / ataḥ sāpi viviktā svalakṣaṇapratibhāsaiḥ / sā kadācidasmādvivekāccalatīti cedāha / prajñāpāramitāyā acalanatā / kutaḥ? sarvadharmācalanatayā / yataḥ sarvadharmā na vivekāccalanti / tataḥ sāpi na vivekāccalati / mananāccalatīti cedāha / prajñāpāramitāyā amananatā / kutaḥ? sarvadharmāmananatayā / amananā hi sarvadharmāḥ / na te kiñcinmanyante niḥsvabhāvatvāt / tataḥ sāpyamananā / kimasau kenāpi stambhitā yato na calatīti cedāha / prajñāpāramitāyā astambhitatā / kutaḥ? sarvadharmāstambhitatayā / na hi vivekāccalanti sarvadharmāḥ kenāpi stambhitāḥ / kiṃ tarhi? prakṛtyaiva viveke sthirāstataḥ prajñāpāramitāpi sthirā / ādau samatāmātramuktaṃ naikarasatā / tāmapyāha / prajñāpāramitāyā ekarasatā sarvadharmeṣu / kutaḥ? sarvadharmāṇāmekarasatayā tathataikarasā hi sarvadharmāḥ svalakṣaṇānāmabhāvāt / tadvatprajñāpāramitāpi svalakṣaṇānāmapratibhāsāt / prajñāpāramitāyā aparyantatā / kutaḥ? sarvadharmāṇāmaparyantatayā / tathā hi dvau paryantau pūrvā ca koṭiraparā ca / tau ca na staḥ sarvadharmāṇām / atītānagatayorasattvāt / tasmādaparyantāḥ sarvadharmāḥ / tadvatprajñāpāramitāpi / prajñāpāramitāyā anutpādatā / kutaḥ? sarvadharmānutpādatayā / tathāhi niḥsvabhāvāḥ sarvadharmāḥ / tasmānnotpadyante kharaviṣāṇavat / tasmādanutpādāḥ / tadvatprajñāpāramitāpi / anirodhā prajñāpāramitā / kutaḥ? sarvadharmāṇāmanirodhatayā / na hyamī nirudhyante 'sattvāt kharaviṣāṇavat / tadvatprajñāpāramitāpi / prajñāpāramitāyā aparyantatā / kenopamānena? gaganāparyantatayā / tathāhi gaganasya nāsti paryanto daśasu dikṣu triṣu cādhveṣu / evaṃ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ / [yā] daśadiktraiyadhvikā sarvadharmatathatāmātraprathanāt / samudrāparyantatayā prajñāpāramitāparyantateti / yathā hyākāśasya nāstyantastathaiva daśadiglokadhātūnāṃ kimpunarananteṣu lokadhātuṣu samudrāṇām / tataḥ siddhā samudrāparyantatā / tadvatprajñāpāramitāyāḥ / tathā hi yā teṣāṃ samudrāṇāṃ tathatā yā ca sarvadharmāṇāṃ yā ca prajñāpāramitāyāḥ, ekaivaiṣā tathatā / tathatālambanā ca prajñāpāramitā / tasmātsamudrāparyantatayā prajñāpāramitāparyantateti siddham /
body.translated_text: By these very thirty aspects, thirty <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations) arose for the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Sadāprarudita</s> (Ever-Weeping) — [these] will be recited. The equality of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> in all <s>dharmas</s> — why? Because of the equality of all <s>dharmas</s>. For it takes <s>dharmadhātu</s> (the realm of dharmas) as its object, and that is equal in all <s>dharmas</s>. The detachment of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> — why? Because of the detachment of all <s>dharmas</s>. Since all <s>dharmas</s> are detached from their own characteristics, therefore it too is detached from the appearances of own-characteristics. If [one objects] that it sometimes moves away from this detachment — to this he says: the non-wavering of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> — why? Because of the non-wavering of all <s>dharmas</s>. Since all <s>dharmas</s> do not waver from detachment, therefore it too does not waver from detachment. If [one objects] that it wavers through thinking — to this he says: the non-thinking of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> — why? Because of the non-thinking of all <s>dharmas</s>. For all <s>dharmas</s> are non-thinking; they do not think anything, because they are devoid of own-nature. Therefore it too is non-thinking. If [one objects:] 'Is it then propped up by something, such that it does not waver?' — to this he says: the unpropped nature of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> — why? Because of the unpropped nature of all <s>dharmas</s>. For all <s>dharmas</s> do not waver from detachment, propped up by anything. Rather, by their very nature they are stable in detachment — therefore <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> too is stable. At first, mere equality was stated, not single-taste. That too he states: the single-taste of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> in all <s>dharmas</s> — why? Because of the single-taste of all <s>dharmas</s>. For all <s>dharmas</s> are of the single taste of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), because of the absence of their own characteristics. Likewise <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> too, because of the non-appearance of own-characteristics. The boundlessness of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> — why? Because of the boundlessness of all <s>dharmas</s>. For there are two boundaries: the prior limit and the posterior limit. And those do not exist for all <s>dharmas</s>, because of the non-existence of the past and the future. Therefore all <s>dharmas</s> are boundless; likewise <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>. The non-arising of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> — why? Because of the non-arising of all <s>dharmas</s>. For all <s>dharmas</s> are devoid of own-nature; therefore they do not arise, like the horn of a hare. Therefore they are non-arising; likewise <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>. <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is non-ceasing — why? Because of the non-ceasing of all <s>dharmas</s>. For these do not cease, because they are non-existent, like the horn of a hare; likewise <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>. The boundlessness of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> — by what analogy? By the boundlessness of space. For space has no boundary in the ten directions and in the three times. Similarly with <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, because it extends as nothing but the <s>tathatā</s> of all <s>dharmas</s> in the ten directions and three times. The boundlessness of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> by the boundlessness of the ocean — for just as space has no end, so too of the world-realms in the ten directions, and how much more of the oceans in infinite world-realms. Therefore the boundlessness of the ocean is established; likewise of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>. For the <s>tathatā</s> of those oceans, the <s>tathatā</s> of all <s>dharmas</s>, and the <s>tathatā</s> of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> — this is one and the same <s>tathatā</s>. And <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> takes <s>tathatā</s> as its object. Therefore, the boundlessness of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> through the boundlessness of the ocean is established.

body.text: nanu svapnopamatayāpi jñānaṃ prajñāpāramitā gaganopamatayāpi / tatra pūrvā vicitrapratibhāsā uttarā nirābhāsā / kathamanayorekārthatetyata āha / meruvicitratayā prajñāpāramitāvicitrateti / yathā hyekarasamākāśaṃ prakṛtyā tathāpi
body.translated_text: Objection: By its dream-like nature, [one type of] knowledge is <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>; by its space-like nature, another [is]. Therein, the former has variegated appearances while the latter is appearance-free. How can these two have the same meaning? — to this he says: 'By the variegation of <s>Meru</s>, the variegation of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>' — just as space is of a single taste by nature, yet

body.text: merupārśvānāṃ vicitrāṇāmādhipatyāttadvadeva vicitraṃ khyāti / evamekarasaiva tathatā na vicitrā / tathatālambanā ca prajñāpāramitā / yastu svapnopamādijñāne vicitrapratibhāsaḥ so 'bhūtaparikalpadharmaḥ / tasmātsvapnopamamāyopamādijñānaṃ saṃvṛtiḥ / nirābhāse yā ca parimārthike jñāne sattvanāmavatāraṇāya nirdiśyate, nirābhāsapṛṣṭhabhāvī cāvikalpoyaṃ tadanubhūtaniścayārthaḥ / tasmātsiddhamidaṃ meruvicitratayā prajñāpāramitāvicitrateti /
body.translated_text: due to the dominance of the variegated flanks of <s>Meru</s>, that very [space] appears variegated — so too <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) is of a single taste alone, not variegated. And <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> takes <s>tathatā</s> as its object. But the variegated appearance in dream-like and other [mundane] knowledge — that belongs to the domain of false imagination (<s>abhūtaparikalpa</s>). Therefore, dream-like, illusion-like, and other knowledge is conventional (<s>saṃvṛti</s>). That which is taught regarding appearance-free, ultimate knowledge for the purpose of introducing beings to it — and the non-conceptual [knowledge] that follows upon the appearance-free [knowledge], [which serves] for the purpose of certainty regarding what was experienced [in meditation] — therefore it is established that 'by the variegation of <s>Meru</s>, the variegation of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.'

body.text: nanu saiva nirābhāsā prajñāpāramitā svayamanubhūyamānaṃ paramārthamitthaṃ niścinoti niḥsvabhāvāḥ sarvadharmā iti / tatkathamasau nirvikalpetyata āha / gaganākalpanatayā prajñāpāramitākalpanateti / prajñāpāramitāyā yākalpanatā na sā kiñcidvikalpayati vikalpapāragatatvāt / tadyathā gaganaṃ na kiñcidvikalpayati jaḍatvāt / ajaḍā prajñāpāramitā kinna vikalpayatīti cet / uktamatra / vikalpaśca bhrāntirabhrāntā ca sā / tasmānna vikalpayatīti siddham /
body.translated_text: Objection: That very appearance-free <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> determines the ultimate as directly experienced — 'all <s>dharmas</s> are devoid of own-nature.' Then how is it non-conceptual? — to this he says: 'By the non-conceptualization of space, the non-conceptualization of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.' The non-conceptualization that is <s>prajñāpāramitā's</s> does not conceptualize anything, because it has gone beyond conceptualization. Just as space does not conceptualize anything, because of its insentience. If [one objects:] '<s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is not insentient, so why does it not conceptualize?' — this has been addressed: conceptualization is error, and it is non-erroneous. Therefore, that it does not conceptualize is established.

body.text: rūpāparyantatayā prajñāpāramitāparyantateti / yathā hyākāśamaparyantaṃ tathārūpaskandhopi / yatrānyadrūpaṃ nāsti tatrāvaśyaṃ tamaḥ prakāśo vāsti / tadvattadīyatathatāpratibhāsinī prajñāpāramitāpyaparyantatā / yathaiva samudrāparyantatayā prajñāpāramitāparyantatāsmābhirvyākhyātā tathaiva sattvānāmānantyāt vedanāparyantatayāpi saṃskāraparyantatayāpi vijñānāparyantatayāpi pṛthivīdhātvaparyantatayāpi apdhātvaparyantatayāpi tejodhātvaparyantatayāpi vāyudhātvaparyantatayāpi ākāśadhātvaparyantatayāpi vijñānadhātvaparyantatayāpi vyākhyātavyā / atha yā vijñānaskandhāparyantatayā yā ca vijñānadhātvaparyantatayā tayoḥ ko viśeṣaḥ? skandhadhātuśabdābhyāṃ prayogakṛtaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'By the boundlessness of form, the boundlessness of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>' — for just as space is boundless, so too is the <s>rūpa-skandha</s> (aggregate of form). Where there is no other form, there must be either darkness or light. Likewise, <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, which manifests the <s>tathatā</s> of those [forms], is also boundless. Just as we explained the boundlessness of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> through the boundlessness of the ocean, similarly, because of the infinity of beings, it should be explained through the boundlessness of feeling, through the boundlessness of formations, through the boundlessness of consciousness, through the boundlessness of the earth element, through the boundlessness of the water element, through the boundlessness of the fire element, through the boundlessness of the wind element, through the boundlessness of the space element, and through the boundlessness of the consciousness element. Now, what is the difference between the boundlessness through the consciousness aggregate and the boundlessness through the consciousness element? The difference is made by the words '<s>skandha</s>' (aggregate) and '<s>dhātu</s>' (element), due to their different applications.

body.text: vajropamadharmasamatayā prajñāpāramitāsamateti / cittadhāraṇāddharmaḥ samādhiḥ / tasya yā sarvadharmeṣu samatā tayomānena prajñāpāramitāyāḥ samatā sarvadharmeṣu sarvadharmāsambhedanatayā prajñāpāramitāsambhedanateti sarvadharmāṇāmasambhedo abhedaḥ / bhedakānāṃ svalakṣaṇānāmabhāvāt / tadvatprajñāpāramitāyā api na bhedaḥ / samvedyamānenaiva rūpeṇa teṣāṃ tasyāmabhāvāt / sarvadharmānupalabdhitayā prajñāpāramitānupalabdhiteti / sarvadharmā na kiñcidupalabhante / rūpasya jaḍatvāt / śeṣāṇāmapyātmani paratra vā grāhakatvāyogāt / nāpyupalabhyante grāhakābhāvāt / tadvatprajñāpāramitāpi nopalabhate nāpyupalabhyate / tasmātteṣāṃ tasyāścānupalabdhitā / sarvadharmāvibhāvanāsamatayā prajñāpāramitāvibhāvanāsamateti / vibhāvanāṃ parebhyo
body.translated_text: 'By the equality of the vajra-like dharma, the equality of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>' — '<s>dharma</s>' [here means] <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), because it sustains (<s>dhāraṇa</s>) the mind. Its equality in all <s>dharmas</s> — by that measure, the equality of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> in all <s>dharmas</s>. 'By the non-splitting of all <s>dharmas</s>, the non-splitting of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>' — the non-splitting of all <s>dharmas</s> is their non-differentiation, because of the absence of own-characteristics that would differentiate [them]. Likewise, <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> too has no differentiation, because of the absence of their being experienced with those very forms [i.e., as differentiated] in it. 'By the non-apprehension of all <s>dharmas</s>, the non-apprehension of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>' — all <s>dharmas</s> do not apprehend anything — because of the insentience of form; and because the remaining [dharmas] are also incapable of being a grasper of either themselves or of others. Nor are they apprehended, because of the absence of a grasper. Likewise, <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> neither apprehends nor is apprehended. Therefore, [there is] the non-apprehension of those and of it. 'By the equality of the non-exposition of all <s>dharmas</s>, the equality of the non-exposition of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>' — '<s>vibhāvanā</s>' (exposition) is teaching to others

body.text: vācā deśanā / sā sarvadharmāṇāṃ na vidyate tasmādavibhāvanayā samatā teṣām / tadvatsarvālambaneṣu prajñāpāramitāyā avibhāvanāsamatā / sarvadharmaniśceṣṭatayā prajñāpāramitāniśceṣṭateti / ceṣṭā īhāvyāpāraḥ / avyāpāraḥ sarvadharmāḥ / kathaṃ tarhi kaścitkutaścidutpadyate? idaṃpratyayamātreṇa / asmin satīdaṃ bhavati, asati na bhavatītyetāvatā hetuphalabhāvaḥ / tasmādamī niśceṣṭāḥ tadvatprajñāpāramitāpi / sarvadharmācintyatayāpi prajñāpāramitācintyateti / yathā hi dharmāḥ parebhyo na deśyante nirviṣayatvādvācaḥ / tathā svayamapi na cintyante na nirūpyante vāgvikalpayorekārthatvāt / tadvatprajñāpāramitāpyacintyā / veditavyetyante yat paṭhyate tatsarvadharmasamatādivākyeṣu sarveṣu sambadhyate 'ntardīpakatvāt /
body.translated_text: through speech. That does not exist for all <s>dharmas</s>; therefore, through non-exposition, their equality [is established]. Likewise, the equality of <s>prajñāpāramitā's</s> non-exposition with regard to all objects. 'By the inactivity of all <s>dharmas</s>, the inactivity of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>' — '<s>ceṣṭā</s>' (activity) is purposive effort. All <s>dharmas</s> are without purposive effort. Then how does something arise from something? Merely by conditionality: 'When this exists, that exists; when this does not exist, that does not exist' — by just this much, the relation of cause and effect [is established]. Therefore these are inactive; likewise <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>. 'By the inconceivability of all <s>dharmas</s>, the inconceivability of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>' — for just as <s>dharmas</s> cannot be taught to others, because speech is without a real object, so too they cannot be thought of or examined by oneself, because speech and conceptualization have the same object. Likewise <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is inconceivable. The word '<s>veditavya</s>' (should be understood) that is read at the end connects with all the sentences beginning with 'the equality of all <s>dharmas</s>' and so on, because it functions as an internal connective.

body.text: atha khalvityādi / atheti deśanāparisamāptau / tathā niṣaṇṇasvaṃveti śrutāsanādanutthitasya / athetyuddeśaḥ / kṛtaḥ / tasyaiva nirdeśaḥ tasyāṃ velāyāmiti / yenaiva krameṇa yairevākāraiḥ prajñāpāramitā deśitā tenaiva krameṇa tairevākāraistriṃśatsamādhaya utpannā iti samudāyārthaḥ / tatra sarvadharmasamatādyākāratvātsamādhayastathā vyapadiśyante / kathamamī ākārāḥ? ebhi prakārairvastujñānāt / yathoktam-
body.translated_text: 'Now then' and so on. '<s>Atha</s>' — at the conclusion of the teaching. '<s>Tathā niṣaṇṇasya</s>' — of one who had not risen from the seat of listening. '<s>Atha</s>' — this is the outline. It has been done. The detailed exposition of that very [outline is] 'at that very time.' In the very same sequence and by the very same aspects by which <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> was taught, in that very sequence and by those very aspects, thirty <s>samādhis</s> arose — this is the collective meaning. Therein, because of having the aspects of the equality of all <s>dharmas</s> and so on, the <s>samādhis</s> are designated accordingly. How are these 'aspects'? Through knowing things in these modes. As it has been stated —

body.text: vastujñānaprakārāṇāmākāra iti lakṣaṇam /
body.translated_text: 'The characteristic of an aspect is [that it represents] the modes of knowing things.'

body.text: iti / kiṃ tarhyālambanam? tadeva vastu yathāsvam / athavā sarvadharmasamatādirevālambanam / tadālambanatvātsamādhayastathoktāḥ / vastūnyadhiṣṭhāni / ākāro yathāsvaṃ nirnimittatādiḥ / evaṃ pramukhānīti triṃśatsamādhipramukhāni / kathameṣāṃ pramukhatvam? ebhiravaśeṣāṇāmākṣepāt / śatasahasrāṇīti lakṣāṇi //
body.translated_text: What then is their object? Each respective thing itself. Alternatively, the equality of all <s>dharmas</s> and so on is itself the object. Because of having those as objects, the <s>samādhis</s> are so designated. The things are their bases. The aspect in each case is their signlessness and so on. '<s>Evaṃ pramukhāni</s>' means 'beginning with the thirty <s>samādhis</s>.' How are they 'foremost' (<s>pramukha</s>)? Because by these, all the remaining [samādhis] are implied. '<s>Śatasahasrāṇi</s>' means 'hundreds of thousands' [i.e., <s>lakṣas</s>].

body.text: dharmodgatena lakṣitaḥ parivartastatparivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: The chapter marked by <s>Dharmodgata</s> — hence that chapter [bears that name].

body.text: āryāṣṭasāhasrikāyāḥ prajñāpāramitāyāḥ sāratamānāmni pañjikāyāṃ ratnākaraśāntiviracitāyāmekatriṃśattamaḥ parivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: In the <s>Pañjikā</s> commentary named <s>Sāratamā</s>, composed by <s>Ratnākaraśānti</s>, on the noble <s>Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s> — this is the thirty-first chapter.

body.text: 32. parīnandanāparivarto nāma dvātriṃśattamaḥ /
body.translated_text: 32. The chapter named '<s>Parīnandanā-parivarta</s>' (Chapter on Rejoicing) is the thirty-second.

body.text: sahapratilabdhānāmityādi / anena labdhānāṃ samādhīnāṃ tatkālajamanuśaṃsamāha / ata eva sahaśabdaḥ samānakālatārthaḥ / pratilabdhānāmiti
body.translated_text: 'Of those simultaneously obtained' and so on. By this he states the benefit, arising at that time, of the <s>samādhis</s> that were obtained. For precisely this reason, the word '<s>saha</s>' has the meaning of simultaneity. '<s>Pratilabdhānām</s>' means

body.text: pratilabdheṣu satsu / ebhireva nayeriti yathoktavastubhiraṣṭābhirabhisamayaiḥ / ebhireva nāmabhiriti sarvākārajñatādibhiḥ / sarvāsu ca jātiṣu na jātu buddhavirahito 'bhūdityuddeśaḥ / asya nirdeśa uttaro granthaḥ svapnāntaragatopīti yāvat /
body.translated_text: 'when they have been obtained.' 'By these very methods' means through the eight <s>abhisamayas</s> (clear realizations) [related to] the things described. 'By these very names' means by '<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>' (omniscience in all aspects) and so on. 'And in all births he was never without a <s>Buddha</s>' — this is the outline. The detailed exposition of this is the subsequent text, up to 'even while in a dream.'

body.text: tatra khalvityādirupodghātaḥ parīndanāyāḥ / tadanenāpi paryāyeṇaiti sadāpraruditavṛttāntenāpi / tasmāttarhītyādinā anuśāsanīśabdaparyantena prathamā parīndanā / atra ca tathāgatādhiṣṭhāneneti vacanaṃ kimartham? mahārthatvābhdagavatī bavhantarāyā ca vinā buddhādhiṣṭhānena likhitumapi [na] śakyeti pradarśanārtham / iyamasmākamanuśāsanītīyamasmākaṃ parīndanā / yathā asyāḥ śravaṇādikaṃ na vicchidyate tathā tvayā kartavyamityarthaḥ / tatkasya hetoriti / tatparīndanaṃ kena prayojanenetyarthaḥ / ata āha / atra hītyādi /
body.translated_text: There, "now then" and so on is the introduction to the entrustment (<s>parīndanā</s>). "By this method too" means also by the account of <s>Sadāprarudita</s> (Ever-Weeping). "Therefore then" and so on, up to the word "instruction" (<s>anuśāsanī</s>), is the first entrustment. And what is the purpose of the statement "by the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s empowerment" here?
