To demonstrate that, because the <s>Bhagavatī</s> is of great purpose and has many obstacles, it is impossible even to write [her] without the empowerment of the <s>Buddha</s>. "This is our instruction" — this is our entrustment. "You must act such that the hearing and the like of this [<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>] is not interrupted" — this is the meaning. "For what reason?" — "for what purpose is that entrustment?" — this is the meaning. Therefore he says: "for herein" and so on.

body.text: tatkathamityādinā dvītīyaparīndanāyā upodghātaḥ / asmin mama samucchaya iti mama śarīre / tathataditi / etatpremādikam / etenopādghātena dve parīndane / yata āha dvirapi trirapīti / parīndāmīti samarpayāmi / anuparīndamītyānukūlyaṃ samarpayāmi / kathaṃ parīndanetyata āha yatheyamityādi / anyaḥ puruṣa ityabhaktaḥ / kasmādasyāmetāvadgauravamityata āha / yāvadityādi bahuvidhāśca pūjābhiriti yāvat /
body.translated_text: "How then" and so on is the introduction to the second entrustment. "In this my aggregate" means "in my body." "Thus and thus" — this love and the like. By this introduction, there are two entrustments. Therefore he says: "twice, even thrice." "I entrust" (<s>parīndāmi</s>) means "I hand over." "I entrust again" (<s>anuparīndāmi</s>) means "I hand over with further assent." "How does he entrust?" — to this he says: "just as this" and so on. "Another person" means an unfaithful one. "Why such great reverence for this [<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>]?" — to this he says: "as long as" and so on — meaning "with many kinds of worships."

body.text: bhagavatyāḥ parisamāptimudyotayan saṅgītikāra āha / idamavocadityādi / idamiti prajñāpāramitāsūtram / avocaditi bhāṣitavān / bhagavāniti śāstā / parārtharasikāstathāgatāḥ / parārtha ca parārthakriyā bhagavatyā deśanā / tata āha / āttamanā iti / niruttaradharmadeśanayā prītaḥ sannityarthaḥ / śrotāraḥ kimukurvannityāha / bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandanniti / abhipūrvo nandiḥ sakarmakaḥ / sa kadācidabhilāṣe vartate / kadācitprītau / yadā prītau tadā tadālambanamevāsya karma bhavati / tatpunaḥ karma bhagavato bhāṣitam / eṣaiva deśanā / ke punaste śrotāra ityāha / te cetyādi / lokaḥ sattvasamūhaḥ / sa ca śrotṝṇāṃ rājagṛhasya ca prakṛtatvānmanuṣyasamūha eva kevalo gamyeta / tathā mā bhūditi viśeṣaṇaṃ kriyate / sadevamānuṣāsuragandharvaśceti / te ca bodhisattvādayaḥ sadevādiśca loka iti samuccayaḥ //
body.translated_text: Illuminating the conclusion of the <s>Bhagavatī</s>, the compiler (<s>saṅgītikāra</s>) says: "this he spoke" and so on. "This" refers to the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> <s>sūtra</s>. "He spoke" means he expounded. "The <s>Bhagavān</s>" is the Teacher. The <s>Tathāgatas</s> are devoted to the welfare of others. And the welfare of others, the activity for others' benefit, is the teaching of the <s>Bhagavatī</s>. Therefore he says: "delighted" (<s>āttamanā</s>) — meaning "being pleased by the unsurpassed <s>Dharma</s>-teaching." "What did the listeners do?" — he says: "they rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words" (<s>bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan</s>). The root <s>nand</s> with the prefix <s>abhi</s> is transitive. It sometimes occurs in the sense of desire, sometimes in the sense of delight. When [it is] in the sense of delight, then the very object of that [delight] becomes its grammatical object. And that object is the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s utterance — this very teaching. "Who then are those listeners?" — he says: "they" and so on. "The world" (<s>loka</s>) is the assembly of beings. And since the listeners and <s>Rājagṛha</s> are the established [context], only the human assembly would be understood. "Lest that be so," a qualifier is added: "together with the gods, humans, <s>asuras</s>, and <s>gandharvas</s>." And the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and the others, together with the world including gods and the rest — this is a cumulative conjunction.

body.text: parīndanābhidhāyī parivartaḥ parīndanāparivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: The chapter that expresses the entrustment is the "Entrustment Chapter" (<s>Parīndanā-parivarta</s>).

children.translated_text: Through the departure of all the stains of diverse errors, what is ungraspable and without a grasper,
shines forth in this [<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>] as having the nature of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), of one flavor — the entire universe.
<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the boat for crossing over conceptualization — she is the wisdom of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>;
by the steadfast, she herself is called the "<s>Tāthāgatī</s>" (the quality of the <s>Tathāgata</s>) in crossing to the far shore of purification.
The eight <s>abhisamayas</s> (realizations) that truly [constitute] this [text], and the eight thousand [verses] —

children.text: sūtraṃ tatte bhagavati mayā yaśca labdho vibhajya //
children.translated_text: that <s>sūtra</s> of yours, O <s>Bhagavatī</s>, and whatever mass of merit has been obtained by me through analyzing [it] —

children.text: puṇyaskandhaḥ phalatu sa yathā yuktimuktiṃ prajānām /
children.translated_text: may that bear fruit such that beings, who are boundless, [attain] liberation through reasoning,
and may I [attain] mastery in the activities for the welfare of all.
Polished with incomparable qualities, possessing stainless and complete virtues,
the speech of <s>Gautama</s> steals away your attachment to worldly existence;
there arises in the great and compassion-filled mind of beings
the inner light — for the purpose of its transmission.
Of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, which is measured by eight hundred [verses multiplied by] ten,
this <s>Pañjikā</s> (commentary) called <s>Sāratama</s> on the <s>Abhisamaya</s> is my clear and dense [work].

children.text: ye dharmā hetuprabhavā hetuṃ teṣāṃ tathāgato hyavadat /
children.translated_text: Those <s>dharmas</s> that arise from causes — the <s>Tathāgata</s> has declared their cause,

children.text: teṣāṃ ca yo nirodha evaṃvādī mahāśramaṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: and that which is their cessation — thus teaches the great ascetic.

children.text: ?(?) samvat ā to rājñaḥ śrīharṣadevarājye śrīgaṇḍigulmaviṣaye /
children.translated_text: (?) In the year ... of the reign of King <s>Śrī Harṣadeva</s>, in the district of <s>Śrī Gaṇḍigulma</s>,
[this is] the manuscript of the family scribe (or: of the learned) <s>Śrī Jīvandhara Siṃha</s>, the <s>Paṇḍita</s>. // 0 //
